We are looking for a database engineer who has dealt with large-scale search infrastructure and is not afraid to recommend tearing something down and rebuilding it when the situation calls for it. Context: Our Elasticsearch cluster indexes over two million legal documents across three languages. Search response times have degraded significantly as the corpus grew, and we need someone who can diagnose the architecture, propose a credible path forward and help us execute it without unacceptable downtime. Day-to-day responsibilities:
— Profiling query performance and identifying bottlenecks in our current Elasticsearch setup
— Designing and prototyping an improved indexing architecture, which may or may not remain Elasticsearch-based
— Evaluating vector search and hybrid retrieval approaches for multilingual legal text
— Coordinating with our backend engineers (Python, PostgreSQL) to maintain API compatibility during any migration
— Documenting infrastructure changes clearly enough that the team can maintain them without you in the room Required background:
— Strong hands-on experience with Elasticsearch or an equivalent large-scale search system
— Familiarity with vector databases or semantic search pipelines is a significant advantage
— Experience planning zero-downtime or near-zero-downtime migrations
— Comfort working on a team of two engineers where you will need to make calls independently Nice to have:
— Experience with on-premises Kubernetes deployments
— Any background in legal or document-heavy domains This role is based at NTP Novi Sad. Some remote work is possible after the first three months. Apply with a CV to [email removed] and mention 'DB Engineer' in the subject line.

C006/website/2024-01-15/What PravniPilot.id: C006/website/2024-01-15/What PravniPilot Does — Platform and Services Overview
C006/website/2024-01-15/What PravniPilot.title: What PravniPilot Does — Platform and Services Overview
C006/website/2024-01-15/What PravniPilot.text: PravniPilot gives lawyers faster access to the decisions and arguments that matter to their case. Our platform holds over two million court decisions from Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Every document is parsed, indexed and linked to related cases so you can find relevant precedent in seconds rather than hours. Keyword search, Boolean filters, court-level filters and date ranges are all available from a single interface. No installation required — the platform runs in any modern browser. The case-outcome prediction module analyzes the facts you enter and compares them against historical decisions in the same legal area. It returns a probability distribution across outcome categories, along with the decisions that influenced that estimate. The module currently covers commercial disputes, labor claims and property litigation. Prediction results include the number of supporting cases so you know how much data sits behind any estimate. For firms that process high volumes of documents, our document annotation tool generates structured summaries of uploaded filings, extracts cited statutes and precedents, and flags arguments the opposing side has used in similar past cases. Enterprise customers — insurers, banks and larger litigation practices — can access our full dataset through a bulk-export API. We also license cleaned, structured legal datasets to third parties under a separate data agreement. All customer data is stored on our own infrastructure inside Serbia. We do not use customer documents or queries to train or update our models without explicit written consent. For pricing, onboarding timelines or a demonstration, contact our sales team in Subotica or visit our development office at NTP Novi Sad.

C007.title: Suncokret Eko d.o.o.
C007.text:
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. (C007): Cleantech — biomass and organic waste valorisation, Novi Sad, 31 employees, founded 2017.
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. was founded in 2017 in Novi Sad by a small group of agricultural engineers and process technicians who wanted to do something practical with the mountains of sunflower husks and maize cobs left behind every harvest season in Vojvodina. We started with a single pellet press in a rented hall near the Danube and now operate a full processing line at the NTP Novi Sad campus with 31 people on staff. We buy agricultural residues directly from farms and food-processing plants across the region, dry and sort them, and convert them into two main products: pressed pellet fuel sold to district heating operators and private households, and biochar used as a soil amendment and carbon-sequestration material. Our domestic heating customers include several municipal utility companies in Serbia and a growing number of commercial greenhouse operators in Hungary and Romania. On the biochar side we are working toward export sales in Germany and the Netherlands. What separates us from larger biomass processors is that we stay close to the feedstock supply chain. Our head of procurement, Milica Vranić, maintains direct contracts with fourteen farms, which gives us visibility on quality before material arrives at the gate. Our process lead, Dragan Ostojić, has run more than two hundred pyrolysis batches and keeps detailed logs that we use to tune every run. We are not the biggest operation in the region, but we know our material well.
Products: Wood-free biomass pellets (ENplus-equivalent grade) from sunflower husks and maize cobs; Agricultural biochar for soil amendment and carbon sequestration; Custom pelletising service for third-party agricultural waste streams; Bulk biochar supply for industrial composting and land reclamation projects; Carbon removal documentation support package for biochar buyers seeking credit eligibility.
Tech: Rotary drum drying for feedstock moisture control; Hammer-mill particle-size reduction and screening; Flat-die and ring-die pellet presses; Slow-pyrolysis reactor (batch, 400–700 °C operating range); Proximate and ultimate analysis of biochar (fixed carbon, ash, volatile matter); Feedstock moisture monitoring with in-line NIR sensors; Mass-balance and carbon-yield tracking spreadsheets (internally developed); ISO 17225 pellet quality testing protocols.
Plans: Suncokret Eko is expanding pyrolysis capacity with a second batch reactor expected to be operational by mid-2026, targeting a combined biochar output of 400 tonnes per year. We are also exploring co-processing of food-industry digestate with our existing agricultural residue streams to diversify feedstock supply.
R&D capacity: We have two technically trained staff who can run controlled production trials and maintain detailed process logs, but we do not have dedicated research personnel or laboratory equipment beyond basic moisture and proximate-analysis tools.
Past collaborations: We completed a six-month feedstock characterisation project in 2022 with the Institute for Food Technology in Novi Sad (FINS) to benchmark the energy content of regional sunflower husk varieties.

C007-CH1.title: Our biochar product tests at around 55% fixed carbon but customers in Germany need at least 70% for soil-amendment certification; we've tried raising pyrolysis temperature but that cuts yield by nearly a third and makes the economics fall apart.
C007-CH1.text:
Our biochar product tests at around 55% fixed carbon but customers in Germany need at least 70% for soil-amendment certification; we've tried raising pyrolysis temperature but that cuts yield by nearly a third and makes the economics fall apart.

Our biochar consistently comes out with around 55% fixed carbon when we run the pyrolyser at 500–520 °C, which is where our yield is commercially acceptable. Buyers in Germany and the Netherlands need at least 70% fixed carbon to qualify under soil-amendment certification schemes. We have pushed the temperature up to 650 °C and beyond in trials, and we do hit the 70% threshold, but the mass yield drops from roughly 28% to under 20%, which means we need about 40% more raw material to fill the same order. At current feedstock and energy costs that wipes out the price premium we get for certified biochar. We have also tried extending the hold time at lower temperatures rather than raising the peak, but the gains in fixed carbon are modest. We have two years of batch logs covering temperature profiles, feedstock moisture, particle size and output quality that we can share. We need a way to improve fixed-carbon content without either wrecking yield or requiring capital we do not have for a new reactor. A good outcome would be a process adjustment we can test on our existing equipment within six months.

C007-CH2.title: We want to enrol our biochar in the European Biochar Certificate scheme to sell carbon removal credits but the documentation requirements are in German and English and keep changing; we've already spent six months on paperwork without submitting a complete application.
C007-CH2.text:
We want to enrol our biochar in the European Biochar Certificate scheme to sell carbon removal credits but the documentation requirements are in German and English and keep changing; we've already spent six months on paperwork without submitting a complete application.

The European Biochar Certificate is the main route for us to register carbon removal credits and charge a premium to buyers who need documented carbon sequestration. We have been trying to prepare an application for almost a year. The scheme requires detailed chain-of-custody records, feedstock declarations, specific lab analyses, and a written quality management description that maps to their framework document, which is updated periodically. Our team speaks Serbian and we have one colleague, Jovana Filipović, who handles correspondence in English, but the technical language in the EBC framework is not straightforward even for native speakers. We have collected most of the required lab data and we have roughly 18 months of production records. What we are missing is someone who can read the current framework critically, identify exactly what gaps we still have in our documentation, and help us write the quality management section in a way that satisfies the auditors. We have a small budget set aside for this, around 4,000 EUR, and we would like to submit a complete application before the end of the year.

C007-CH3.title: Our pellet press breaks down about once a month because the sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size coming from different suppliers; downtime costs us roughly 15,000 EUR per incident when we have delivery commitments.
C007-CH3.text:
Our pellet press breaks down about once a month because the sunflower husk feedstock has inconsistent moisture and particle size coming from different suppliers; downtime costs us roughly 15,000 EUR per incident when we have delivery commitments.

Our pellet press line goes down roughly once a month. The root cause is almost always the same: sunflower husk material arriving with moisture content or particle size outside the range the press can handle. When moisture is above 14% the dies clog; when there is too much fine dust mixed with coarser pieces the compression is uneven and we get bearing failures. Different suppliers deliver material that can vary from 8% to 22% moisture and from fine powder to chunks over 15 mm in the same delivery. Our current process is to check a sample at intake and reject loads that look bad, but our in-line NIR sensor only covers moisture and is not reliable below 10% or above 18%, and we have no automated particle-size check at all. Each breakdown costs us around 15,000 EUR in lost production, emergency maintenance and contract penalties. We have looked at pre-conditioning equipment, specifically a secondary hammer mill and a conditioning mixer, but we have not been able to confirm whether the spec we are considering would actually stabilise output enough to prevent failures. We need a clearer picture of what incoming feedstock variance is acceptable and what pre-processing steps would bring our current suppliers' material inside that range.

C007/blog/2024-05-30/What We Learned at.id: C007/blog/2024-05-30/What We Learned at BioenergyEurope Showcase 2024 in Vienna
C007/blog/2024-05-30/What We Learned at.title: What We Learned at BioenergyEurope Showcase 2024 in Vienna
C007/blog/2024-05-30/What We Learned at.text: Four of us from Suncokret Eko attended the BioenergyEurope Showcase in Vienna at the beginning of May. It was the first time we had taken a stand at an international trade event rather than just walking the floor, and it was worth the effort. The conversations that were most useful were not with the large equipment suppliers or the established pellet producers. They were with two groups of buyers we had not had direct contact with before. The first were German agricultural input distributors who are looking for biochar they can blend into soil conditioner products. Three of them asked about our production capacity and our quality documentation. Two of those three specifically asked about European Biochar Certificate registration, which confirmed for us that this certification is becoming a practical requirement for that market, not just a nice-to-have. The second group was buyers from the Netherlands running commercial greenhouse operations. They are interested in biochar as a growing medium component. Their fixed-carbon requirements were similar to the German buyers, and one of them was willing to discuss a pilot purchase even before full certification, on the condition that we could provide detailed lab analysis and a signed declaration of production method. We also spent time at a session on feedstock pre-conditioning for pellet producers. A presenter from Slovakia described a system they use to homogenise cereal straw from multiple suppliers before it enters the press. The approach was not identical to our situation but some of the ideas were directly relevant to the sunflower husk consistency problems we have been dealing with. We came back with a list of follow-up contacts and a clearer sense that the biochar market in Germany and the Netherlands is real and moving faster than the domestic Serbian market. Getting our certification documentation finished is no longer a background task — it is the main commercial bottleneck on that side of our business.

C007/job/2024-02-05/Process Technician —.id: C007/job/2024-02-05/Process Technician — Pelletising and Drying Line
C007/job/2024-02-05/Process Technician —.title: Process Technician — Pelletising and Drying Line
C007/job/2024-02-05/Process Technician —.text:
Suncokret Eko d.o.o. is looking for an experienced process technician to join our production team at NTP Novi Sad. We run a biomass processing line that includes rotary drum drying, hammer-mill size reduction, and flat-die and ring-die pellet presses. The role reports to our process lead, Dragan Ostojić. What the job involves:
— Operating and monitoring the drying and pelletising line during scheduled shifts
— Conducting incoming feedstock checks (moisture, particle size, visual inspection) and recording results
— Performing first-level maintenance on press dies, rollers, and bearings according to our maintenance schedule
— Logging process parameters for every production run using our internal tracking sheets
— Flagging feedstock quality issues to the procurement team before they reach the press
— Assisting with trials when we test process adjustments What we need:
— At least three years of hands-on experience with pellet presses or similar mechanical processing equipment
— Comfort working with NIR moisture sensors and basic measurement instruments
— Methodical record-keeping habits — our process logs are the main tool we use to diagnose problems
— Willingness to work a rotating shift pattern Useful but not required:
— Experience with biomass or agricultural material handling
— Familiarity with ISO 17225 pellet quality standards
— Basic knowledge of preventive maintenance planning We offer a permanent contract, competitive pay for the sector, and a straightforward working environment where the problems are real and the fixes are visible. Send a CV and a short note about your maintenance experience to [email removed]. We will arrange interviews on a rolling basis.

C007/news/2024-04-18/Suncokret Eko Secur.id: C007/news/2024-04-18/Suncokret Eko Secures Supply Agreement with Toplana Zrenjanin
C007/news/2024-04-18/Suncokret Eko Secur.title: Suncokret Eko Secures Supply Agreement with Toplana Zrenjanin
C007/news/2024-04-18/Suncokret Eko Secur.text: We are pleased to confirm that Suncokret Eko has signed a two-year pellet supply agreement with Toplana Zrenjanin, a municipal district heating operator serving approximately 8,400 households. Deliveries under the agreement will begin in September 2024 ahead of the winter heating season. The contract covers 1,200 tonnes of biomass pellets per year. Toplana Zrenjanin was looking for a locally produced, wood-free fuel that could be introduced gradually into their existing combustion system alongside their current fuel mix. Our sunflower husk pellets met their calorific value and ash-content requirements and the short transport distance from our facility in Novi Sad was a factor in their decision. For us this is the largest single supply contract we have signed to date. It also creates a clear forward load on our pellet press line for the next two years, which affects how we plan maintenance and feedstock procurement. Our procurement manager, Milica Vranić, has already begun discussions with three additional farms in the Zrenjanin area to secure enough husk material to cover the increased volume without putting pressure on our existing suppliers. Dragan Ostojić noted that running at higher sustained throughput will also give us better data on how our line performs over longer uninterrupted runs, which feeds directly into the work we are doing to reduce press downtime. We thank the team at Toplana Zrenjanin for a straightforward and practical negotiation process. Questions about pellet supply availability can be directed to [email removed].

C008.title: Elekron Sistemi a.d.
C008.text:
Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008): IoT and electronics hardware, Subotica, 117 employees, founded 1987.
Elekron Sistemi a.d. was founded in 1987 in Subotica by the Vukičević family, who started by building custom relay control panels for local factories. Over the following decades the company grew into a recognised supplier of ruggedised electronic control panels and remote terminal units for municipal water, heating, and waste-water operators across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. In 2014 the founding family transferred ownership to an employee trust, and today the 117 people who work here are also the owners. That structure suits us: decisions are made by people who understand the hardware and stand behind every unit that leaves Subotica. Our sheet-metal workshop bends and welds roughly 2,400 panels a year entirely in-house. Our RTU product line communicates over licensed radio, GSM, and, since 2021, LoRaWAN — a direction we are pushing hard because municipal clients need affordable ways to connect meters that were installed before wireless was an option. We hold framework contracts with seven municipal utilities and work through regional integrators in Sarajevo and Skopje. Quality certification to IEC 61439 and a service team that can reach most Western Balkans sites within 24 hours are what clients mention most when they explain why they keep reordering.
Products: Ruggedised electronic control panels for water and district-heating substations; Remote terminal units (RTUs) for SCADA integration over licensed radio and GSM; LoRaWAN collar retrofit kits for legacy water and heat meters; Custom sheet-metal enclosures and powder-coated housing fabricated in-house; Field maintenance and remote diagnostics service contracts.
Tech: LoRaWAN (Class A and Class C devices, custom network server integration); Embedded C firmware on STM32 and NXP Kinetis microcontrollers; IEC 61131-3 ladder logic for panel PLC configuration; Modbus RTU and DNP3 communication protocols; In-house MIG welding and CNC press-brake sheet-metal fabrication; Epoxy primer and polyester powder-coat finishing line; JTAG and SWD-based hardware debugging toolchains; GIT-based firmware version control with Jenkins CI.
Plans: Elekron Sistemi intends to release a second-generation LoRaWAN collar with an integrated signal-boost relay option and to qualify the product line for sale in Romania and Bulgaria by the end of 2026. We are also evaluating whether to bring a small electronics assembly line in-house to reduce dependence on contract PCB assemblers in Novi Sad.
R&D capacity: We have four engineers who can dedicate part of their time to a development collaboration, plus access to our production hardware, field-test sites at three municipal utilities, and a small lab in Subotica with oscilloscopes, protocol analysers, and environmental test chambers.
Past collaborations: We completed a two-year product-development agreement with Integra Automatika d.o.o. from Novi Sad between 2019 and 2021 covering firmware portability across two RTU hardware revisions.

C008-CH1.title: We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty clauses after six months of missed SLA.
C008-CH1.text:
We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty clauses after six months of missed SLA.

We are fitting our LoRaWAN collar device onto existing water and heat meters in basement plant rooms for three municipal clients — two in Bosnia and one in North Macedonia. The problem is signal. Measured RSSI inside these rooms runs between -120 and -125 dBm, right at the edge of what our gateways can reliably decode. We are using SF12 already, which is the slowest spreading factor and gives us the best link budget, but we are still losing around 9% of daily readings. The SLA we signed requires 99% daily read success, so we are in breach and have been for six months. We have tried repositioning gateway antennas on rooftops and adding one repeater node per building with limited improvement. We do not have budget for a full gateway infrastructure overhaul — the contracts are fixed-price. What we need is either a way to recover more packets from weak signals, a smarter retransmission scheme that fits within the duty-cycle limits, or a low-cost way to extend coverage into these specific rooms. A good outcome is getting missed reads below 1% without replacing the gateways or re-running cables.

C008-CH2.title: Our sheet-metal enclosure workshop in Subotica produces around 2,400 panels a year; we bend and weld everything in-house but we are seeing a 6% rework rate on powder-coated parts because weld spatter creates surface defects that only appear after coating — we lose roughly 140,000 dinars per month in rework labour and materials.
C008-CH2.text:
Our sheet-metal enclosure workshop in Subotica produces around 2,400 panels a year; we bend and weld everything in-house but we are seeing a 6% rework rate on powder-coated parts because weld spatter creates surface defects that only appear after coating — we lose roughly 140,000 dinars per month in rework labour and materials.

Our panel enclosures go through MIG welding before powder coating, and we have a persistent rework problem. Weld spatter — tiny metal balls that stick to the sheet surface — is not always visible before the part goes into the coating oven. After coating the spatter shows up as raised bumps or pinholes and the part has to be stripped, re-ground, re-primed, and re-coated. We track rework per batch and the rate has sat at around 6% for three years. That translates to roughly 140,000 dinars a month in extra labour and materials, not counting the scheduling delays when a batch comes back. We have tried tightening welding parameters, switching to an anti-spatter spray, and adding a manual inspection step before priming, but the manual check catches maybe half the defective parts. Our workshop supervisor, Branimir Talić, thinks the real issue is inconsistency between welders on different shifts. We have no automated inspection equipment. We are open to any approach — sensor-based, vision-based, process change — as long as it fits in a workshop that runs two shifts and cannot afford long production stoppages for installation. Cutting the rework rate to under 1.5% would recover most of the cost.

C008-CH3.title: We want to expand into Romania and Bulgaria but our sales team of five people has no experience with public procurement rules there — we have lost two tenders already because we submitted the wrong notarial documents and missed a local-content clause we did not know existed.
C008-CH3.text:
We want to expand into Romania and Bulgaria but our sales team of five people has no experience with public procurement rules there — we have lost two tenders already because we submitted the wrong notarial documents and missed a local-content clause we did not know existed.

We want to sell our RTU and control panel products directly to municipal utilities in Romania and Bulgaria rather than through local resellers who take a large margin. Both countries run public tenders through their national e-procurement portals. We have a sales team of five, all experienced with Serbian and regional procurement under UNCITRAL-style rules, but Romanian and Bulgarian tender documents use different notarial certification formats, translated attestation requirements, and, in two tenders we entered, local-content or EU-origin documentation we were not aware of. We lost both tenders on administrative grounds before technical evaluation even started. We do not have a local legal partner in either country yet. We have budget for a short consultancy engagement and we are willing to pay a success fee on a first contract win. What we need is either a structured guide to the documentation requirements for each country, or a contact who can review our tender packs before submission. A realistic target is winning one contract in Romania or Bulgaria within 18 months.

C008-CH4.title: The RTU firmware we ship has grown to 340,000 lines of C code over 20 years and nobody on the team fully understands the interrupt-handling layer anymore — we had two field failures in the last year caused by race conditions that took an average of 11 weeks each to reproduce and fix, which is unacceptable for critical infrastructure clients.
C008-CH4.text:
The RTU firmware we ship has grown to 340,000 lines of C code over 20 years and nobody on the team fully understands the interrupt-handling layer anymore — we had two field failures in the last year caused by race conditions that took an average of 11 weeks each to reproduce and fix, which is unacceptable for critical infrastructure clients.

Our main RTU firmware is a C codebase that has been added to by many different engineers since 2003. It now runs to about 340,000 lines and the interrupt-handling layer was written by two engineers who have since retired. We had two separate field failures last year — both traced back to race conditions where an interrupt fired during a flash-write operation and corrupted a register. Each one took an average of 11 weeks to reproduce in the lab because the fault only appeared under specific timing conditions with real hardware attached. That is unacceptable for clients running water or heating distribution. We have no formal concurrency model documented, no static analysis in the CI pipeline, and our current team is not confident modifying the interrupt layer. We are not in a position to rewrite the firmware from scratch — the product is in active production and we have contractual obligations. What we need is a method or toolset to find latent race conditions without a full rewrite, and some kind of structured documentation of the existing interrupt behaviour so future engineers can work on it safely. Budget is limited but the risk of another field failure is the bigger concern.

C008/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware En.id: C008/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware Engineer — RTU and LoRaWAN Products
C008/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware En.title: Embedded Firmware Engineer — RTU and LoRaWAN Products
C008/job/2024-02-05/Embedded Firmware En.text:
Elekron Sistemi a.d. is looking for an embedded firmware engineer to join our development team in Subotica. We make remote terminal units and LoRaWAN metering devices for municipal water and heating clients, and our firmware runs on STM32 and NXP Kinetis microcontrollers in safety-relevant field environments. What you will work on:
- Maintaining and extending our ES-RTU firmware (C, approximately 340,000 lines, bare-metal with a lightweight RTOS layer)
- Developing new features for our LoRaWAN collar device, including adaptive data-rate logic and retransmission schemes for weak-signal environments
- Writing and running hardware-in-the-loop tests using our bench rigs and JTAG/SWD toolchains
- Participating in field failure investigations — we expect honesty about what went wrong, not cover-ups What we are looking for:
- Solid knowledge of C for embedded targets; assembly reading ability is a plus
- Familiarity with interrupt-driven architectures and an understanding of concurrency hazards in bare-metal code
- Experience with at least one of: Modbus RTU, DNP3, LoRaWAN stack integration
- Ability to read a schematic and work alongside hardware engineers
- Any experience with static analysis tools (PC-lint, Polyspace, Cppcheck, or similar) would be valued What we offer:
- Permanent employment, employee share scheme after two years
- A real codebase with real consequences — not a demo project
- A team of 12 engineers who have been building this product family for years
- Competitive salary aligned with Subotica engineering market rates, negotiable based on experience Send a CV and a short note about a firmware problem you have debugged to [email removed]. We do not require a cover letter but we do read the notes carefully.

C008/job/2024-03-10/Process Engineer — S.id: C008/job/2024-03-10/Process Engineer — Sheet-Metal Fabrication and Surface Finishing
C008/job/2024-03-10/Process Engineer — S.title: Process Engineer — Sheet-Metal Fabrication and Surface Finishing
C008/job/2024-03-10/Process Engineer — S.text:
Our Subotica workshop produces around 2,400 steel enclosures per year for our own panel and RTU product lines. We run CNC press-brakes, MIG welding stations, and a powder-coat finishing line. We are hiring a process engineer to help us reduce defect rates and improve consistency across shifts. The role:
You will be responsible for analysing our current welding and pre-coating inspection workflow, identifying where surface defects originate, and implementing measurable improvements. This is a hands-on position — you will spend time on the workshop floor, not just in front of a spreadsheet. Our workshop supervisor Branimir Talić will be your closest collaborator. Specific priorities for the first six months:
- Characterise the weld-spatter defect pattern across our three welding stations and two shifts
- Evaluate options for pre-coating inspection, including any sensor or imaging approaches that can be integrated into our existing conveyor flow
- Propose and pilot at least one process change with measurable before-and-after data Background we are looking for:
- Degree or apprenticeship in mechanical or manufacturing engineering, or equivalent practical experience
- Direct experience with MIG welding processes or powder-coat surface preparation
- Comfortable working with data — even basic analysis of defect logs is sufficient
- Knowledge of any machine-vision or sensor-based inspection systems is a plus but not required We are open to candidates who are early in their career if they have the right practical instincts. This is a full-time permanent position based in Subotica. Salary is negotiable. Write to [email removed] with a short description of a quality problem you have worked on.

C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Rec.id: C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research
C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Rec.title: Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research
C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Rec.text: Elekron Sistemi a.d. has been awarded a grant of 4.2 million dinars from the Vojvodina Development Fund's 2024 innovation support programme. The grant will part-fund a 14-month applied research project aimed at improving LoRaWAN read reliability in obstructed urban environments, specifically basement meter rooms with thick reinforced-concrete walls. The project, internally called ReachRate, will combine antenna configuration testing, adaptive spreading-factor firmware logic, and evaluation of low-power mesh relay approaches. We are conducting the work with our own engineering team and are in early discussions with the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad about additional technical support for the signal propagation and firmware analysis components. The grant covers approximately 55% of projected project costs. The remainder will be funded from our own operating budget. Project lead is our senior RF engineer Dragan Fekete, who has been with Elekron Sistemi for nine years and led the original LoRaWAN collar development. We set a clear target for the project: reduce daily missed readings at our existing deployments from the current 9% to below 1% without replacing installed gateways. We have three live municipal sites in Bosnia and North Macedonia where we can test changes under real conditions, which is a significant practical advantage compared with laboratory-only research. If the project produces firmware or hardware changes that meet the target, we will roll them out to existing collar deployments as an over-the-air firmware update and incorporate them into new production units from mid-2025 onward. We thank the Vojvodina Development Fund for the support. Detailed project reporting will be submitted at the six-month and final milestones as required by the grant terms.

R0016.title: Ivona Matić
R0016.text:
Ivona Matić (R0016): Full Professor, Department of Energy and Process Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Energy Engineering; Industrial Process Engineering; Power Systems and Power Quality; Electrochemical and Electromechanical Manufacturing.
Keywords: energy audit; demand-side management; power quality; peak-demand tariff; load shifting; electrochemical manufacturing; energy-flow mapping; harmonic distortion; variable-speed drives; submetering.
Bio: Ivona Matić received her Dipl.Ing. degree in Industrial Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2001, and her PhD in Energy Engineering from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on power-quality disturbances in electroplating facilities. She joined the Department of Energy and Process Engineering as an assistant professor in 2009 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on energy auditing and demand-side management for manufacturing plants that operate large electrochemical and electromechanical loads, including electrolytic coating lines, electric-arc and induction furnaces, and variable-speed drive systems. The group uses portable power-quality analysers, submetering loggers, and thermal-imaging cameras housed in the department's Industrial Energy Diagnostics Laboratory. She teaches Industrial Energy Management and Power Systems Quality at undergraduate and master level.
Open to: contract research: energy audits and demand-side management studies for manufacturing companies; consulting on peak-demand tariff reduction and power-quality compliance; joint project proposals (Interreg, Science Fund of Serbia) with companies operating electrochemical or electromechanical processes; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; equipment access: power-quality analysers, portable submetering loggers, thermal-imaging cameras available on a cost-sharing basis; student internships for energy engineering and electrical engineering students.
Industry experience: Matić has conducted paid energy audits and demand-side management studies at more than thirty manufacturing companies in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia since 2010, several under direct contracts with Vojvodina-based exporters in the automotive supply chain. She served as a technical expert on the Serbian Ministry of Mining and Energy working group that drafted the national guidelines for industrial energy audits (2017–2018).
Notes: Matić has a strong preference for projects where measurement campaigns and verified savings are part of the scope; she is less interested in purely simulation-based or policy-analysis work without an empirical component. Her laboratory's portable instrumentation can typically be mobilised within two weeks of contract signing. She is not seeking new long-term academic partnerships at present but is actively looking for NTP-based industry partners for a planned follow-on project application to the Science Fund of Serbia in 2026.

R0030.title: Vladana Vojnović
R0030.text:
Vladana Vojnović (R0030): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Machine Learning and Data Mining; Distributed Systems and Infrastructure Monitoring; Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Data Stream Processing.
Keywords: anomaly detection; log analysis; unsupervised learning; event correlation; high-velocity data streams; clustering; intrusion detection; time-series analysis; Apache Kafka; SIEM.
Bio: Vladana Vojnović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2008 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2013, with a dissertation on unsupervised clustering methods for distributed system log analysis. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an Assistant Professor in 2014 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on real-time anomaly detection, event correlation across heterogeneous log sources, and streaming data pipelines. She teaches courses in operating systems, distributed systems monitoring, and applied machine learning. The group operates the StreamLab facility, equipped with a small on-premises Kafka-based testbed, GPU workstations for model training, and access to the university HPC cluster.
Open to: joint projects with companies generating high-volume operational or security logs; contract research on anomaly detection pipeline design and deployment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from NTP Novi Sad companies; student internships (master's level) focused on log analysis tooling; consulting on SIEM tuning and alert fatigue reduction; equipment access to StreamLab Kafka testbed for short-term experiments.
Industry experience: Vojnović spent four months in 2020 as a visiting researcher at Sinteza IT d.o.o. in Novi Sad, where she assisted in designing a log collection and triage pipeline for a managed security service offering. She has since maintained an informal advisory relationship with the company.
Notes: Vojnović is currently co-supervising three PhD students and has limited capacity for new large commitments until mid-2026. She prefers industry partnerships that include access to real operational log datasets, even under NDA, as benchmark data remains a bottleneck for the group's research. She is particularly interested in contact with companies in manufacturing, utilities, and telecommunications operating in the region.

R0041.title: Stefan Ostojić
R0041.text:
Stefan Ostojić (R0041): Full Professor, Department of Graphic Engineering and Design, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Graphic and Visual Communication Design; Environmental and Wayfinding Design; Ergonomics and Human Factors; Healthcare Facility Design.
Keywords: wayfinding sign systems; information architecture; symbol legibility; contrast sensitivity; low-luminance conditions; healthcare environments; older adults; pictogram design; directional signage; typography in signage.
Bio: Stefan Ostojić received his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Graphic Engineering and Design from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2001 and 2004 respectively, and his PhD from the same institution in 2009, with a dissertation on legibility of directional signage in complex built environments. He has been a Full Professor in the Department of Graphic Engineering and Design since 2019. His research group investigates information architecture, wayfinding sign system design, and visual communication in healthcare and institutional buildings, with particular emphasis on symbol–text legibility under low-luminance conditions and for older adult populations with reduced contrast sensitivity. He teaches courses in visual communication, typography, and environmental graphic design. The group operates a dedicated legibility testing laboratory equipped with a calibrated light-tight chamber, a contrast sensitivity measurement rig, and an eye-tracking system used for reading and scanning behaviour studies.
Open to: contract research on sign system design and legibility testing for healthcare or infrastructure clients; consulting on wayfinding system specification and evaluation; joint grant applications with companies developing digital or physical signage products for public buildings; student internships in legibility testing and environmental graphic design; access to legibility testing laboratory and contrast sensitivity measurement equipment for collaborative studies.
Industry experience: Ostojić has provided paid consulting services to two hospital facility management organisations in Vojvodina during the design and procurement of new wayfinding sign systems, contributing to technical specifications and conducting pre-installation legibility verification tests. He has also served as an expert reviewer on a public tender for wayfinding signage at a newly constructed clinical building in Novi Sad.
Notes: Ostojić is particularly interested in partnerships with companies that produce physical or digital signage products for healthcare or public sector buildings and are willing to share prototype materials for structured laboratory testing. He is not seeking purely theoretical collaborations and prefers projects with a concrete deliverable such as a tested design specification or a field-implemented prototype.

R0057.title: Lazar Šarić
R0057.text:
Lazar Šarić (R0057): Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Signal Processing; Data Compression and Coding; Biomedical Informatics; Machine Learning.
Keywords: signal compression; physiological time series; quasi-periodic redundancy; entropy coding; ECG compression; wavelet transform; learned compression; lossless coding; sparse representation; beat segmentation.
Bio: Lazar Šarić completed his undergraduate and master's studies in mathematics and computer science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2010 and 2012 respectively. He received his PhD from the same faculty in 2017, with a dissertation on adaptive transform coding of quasi-periodic biomedical signals. Following a postdoctoral stay at the Technical University of Graz (2017–2019), he returned to Novi Sad as an assistant professor. His group focuses on lossless and near-lossless compression of physiological time series—ECG, PPG, and EEG—using discrete cosine and wavelet transforms, sparse coding, and, more recently, learned entropy models based on small recurrent networks. Teaching covers data structures, information theory, and signal processing. The group uses a shared Linux cluster in the Faculty computing lab and collaborates with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina for annotated signal datasets.
Open to: joint projects on embedded or real-time biomedical signal compression; contract research on codec design and evaluation for medical device manufacturers; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a signal processing or machine learning background; consulting on compression standard compliance (SCP-ECG, HL7 FHIR waveforms); student internships for final-year or master's students from partner faculties.
Industry experience: Šarić carried out a short consultancy engagement in 2022 with Mediconn d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based medical device startup, advising on the selection and parameter tuning of an ECG compression module for their Holter recorder firmware.
Notes: Šarić has expressed interest in collaborating with companies at NTP Novi Sad working on wearable health devices or remote patient monitoring platforms, particularly where real-time or near-real-time compression on constrained hardware is a bottleneck. He is not seeking purely data-science or AI engagements unrelated to signal compression.

R0071.title: Olivera Rakić
R0071.text:
Olivera Rakić (R0071): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Machine Learning and Data Mining; Signal and Time-Series Analysis; Industrial Fault Detection and Diagnostics; Pattern Recognition.
Keywords: anomaly detection; imbalanced learning; semi-supervised classification; concept drift; time-series; high-dimensional data; oversampling; real-time inference; fault detection; ensemble methods.
Bio: Olivera Rakić received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a dissertation on semi-supervised detection of rare fault events in industrial sensor streams. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Zagreb from 2018 to 2020 before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor. Her group focuses on anomaly detection and classification in high-dimensional, heavily imbalanced time-series data, including methods for handling concept drift and label scarcity. She teaches courses on machine learning and data mining at undergraduate and master level. The group makes regular use of the Faculty's data analytics cluster and has access to a small edge-computing testbed for real-time inference experiments.
Open to: joint projects with companies on anomaly detection in industrial sensor data; contract research on imbalanced classification and concept drift adaptation; industrial PhD supervision (co-supervision with company mentor); student internships for master students working on real company datasets; consulting on evaluation methodology and validation protocol design for ML-based monitoring systems.
Industry experience: During her postdoctoral period at the University of Zagreb, Rakić participated in a six-month consulting engagement with a regional utility company to audit the evaluation practices of their existing predictive maintenance classifier, resulting in a revised validation protocol. She has no other formal industry employment.
Notes: Rakić is currently co-supervising two PhD students under DRIFTGUARD and has limited capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2025. She is particularly interested in partners who can provide access to real labelled or partially labelled sensor datasets, which are the main bottleneck for her research. She prefers collaborations where the company has an internal technical contact who can validate domain assumptions.

R0104.title: Aleksandra Matić
R0104.text:
Aleksandra Matić (R0104): Associate Professor, Department of Industrial Engineering and Management, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Industrial Engineering and Management; Quality Management; Organisational Performance Measurement; Operations Management.
Keywords: balanced scorecard; KPI aggregation; ISO 9001; performance measurement; manufacturing SMEs; composite index; AHP weighting; quality management systems; process improvement; transition readiness.
Bio: Aleksandra Matić received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Industrial Engineering and Management from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2008 respectively, and completed her Ph.D. at the same institution in 2013 with a dissertation on composite performance index construction for Serbian manufacturing SMEs. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on organisational performance measurement, balanced scorecard adaptation for mid-sized manufacturers, KPI aggregation and weighting techniques, and quality management system transitions, particularly ISO 9001. She teaches courses in Quality Management Systems, Business Process Modelling, and Performance Measurement at both undergraduate and master's level. The group regularly uses SPSS, SmartPLS, and MS Project in its empirical studies, and collaborates with the Faculty of Organizational Sciences in Belgrade and partners in Slovenia and Hungary.
Open to: joint projects with companies implementing or upgrading ISO 9001 systems; contract research on performance measurement system design; consulting on balanced scorecard adaptation for manufacturing clients; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from technology park companies; student internships in quality management and data collection roles.
Industry experience: Matić has worked as an external quality management consultant for three mid-sized metal processing companies in Novi Sad and Zrenjanin between 2015 and 2019, supporting ISO 9001 implementation and balanced scorecard design. She has delivered in-house training workshops for quality teams at two food manufacturing enterprises in the region.
Notes: Matić is currently PI on the active QMSEVAL project and prefers new collaborations that align with its longitudinal data collection activities or extend its findings. She is particularly interested in companies at the NTP Novi Sad that are planning ISO 9001 certification or that produce measurement or process management software applicable to manufacturing contexts. She is not seeking equipment access partnerships.

R0127.title: Emilija Tešić
R0127.text:
Emilija Tešić (R0127): Full Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Artificial Intelligence; Natural Language Processing; Machine Learning; Knowledge Representation and Reasoning.
Keywords: explainable AI; hallucination detection; large language models; retrieval-augmented generation; citation grounding; fact verification; faithfulness evaluation; saliency methods; natural language inference; benchmark construction.
Bio: Emilija Tešić received her BSc and MSc degrees in Mathematics and Computer Science from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and 2004, respectively, and completed her PhD at the same institution in 2009 with a dissertation on formal verification methods for inference systems. She joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on explainability frameworks for machine learning models, automated detection of factual inconsistencies in large language model outputs, and grounding mechanisms that link generated text to verifiable source documents in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. She teaches courses in logic programming, knowledge representation, and applied machine learning. The group regularly uses the Faculty's GPU cluster and maintains shared annotation infrastructure for benchmarking hallucination detection datasets.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing document automation or compliance tools; contract research on hallucination detection and citation verification for RAG systems; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on NLP or XAI in applied settings; consulting on evaluation methodology for AI-generated text quality; student internships related to annotation tool development and benchmark construction.
Industry experience: Tešić collaborated with a regional legal information provider during the VERIFAI-RS project, advising on requirements and evaluating a prototype verification module against real workflows. She has provided informal consulting to two software companies in Novi Sad on explainability reporting requirements under EU AI regulations.
Notes: Tešić is on a reduced teaching load in the 2025–2026 academic year following her term as vice-dean, which gives her more time for research collaborations than in the previous two years. She has a preference for collaborations that involve concrete evaluation datasets and measurable technical deliverables rather than purely exploratory engagements.

R0135.title: Veljko Savić
R0135.text:
Veljko Savić (R0135): Associate Professor, Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Production and Industrial Engineering; Maintenance Engineering and Reliability; Biomass Processing Technology; Applied Statistics and Stochastic Modelling.
Keywords: biomass densification; pellet mill reliability; condition-based maintenance; feedstock variability; Weibull failure analysis; die wear; vibration monitoring; stochastic degradation models; briquetting press; fault detection.
Bio: Veljko Savić completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Production Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2004 and 2007 respectively. He earned his PhD in 2013 from the same faculty, with a dissertation on stochastic failure modelling for pellet press drive systems. He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His group focuses on condition-based and predictive maintenance frameworks for biomass densification equipment—pellet mills, briquetting presses, and ring-die extruders—with particular attention to how fluctuating feedstock moisture, particle size, and ash content accelerate component degradation. The group operates a small instrumented pilot pellet press and collaborates with the Laboratory for Quality and Reliability at FTN. He teaches courses in Industrial Maintenance Management and Reliability Engineering.
Open to: joint projects with companies operating pellet or briquetting production lines; contract research on maintenance scheduling and condition monitoring; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from biomass processing or agricultural machinery companies; student internships involving data collection or simulation work at partner facilities; consulting on maintenance programme development for biomass densification facilities; equipment access to pilot pellet press and vibration instrumentation.
Industry experience: Savić has provided consulting services to two agricultural cooperatives in Vojvodina on maintenance programme restructuring for their pellet production lines, and collaborated with Bioenergo d.o.o. as an industry partner in the RELIODENSE project, including on-site instrumentation of their ring-die press.
Notes: Savić is primarily interested in industry collaborations that can provide access to operational failure data or instrumented field equipment; he is less available for short-term feasibility studies without a clear path to joint publication or a follow-on project.

R0151.title: Lidija Radić
R0151.text:
Lidija Radić (R0151): Associate Professor, Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Pharmaceutical solid-state chemistry; Crystal engineering; Materials characterisation; Applied chemistry.
Keywords: co-crystals; polymorphism; powder X-ray diffraction; differential scanning calorimetry; Raman mapping; dissolution rate; active pharmaceutical ingredients; crystal engineering; solid-state characterisation; hot-stage microscopy.
Bio: Lidija Radić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2003 and 2005 respectively, followed by a PhD in Pharmaceutical Solid-State Chemistry at the same institution in 2010. She joined the Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry as a teaching assistant in 2006 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2018. Her research group investigates the solid-state landscape of active pharmaceutical ingredients, with particular focus on co-crystal screening, polymorph identification, and crystal engineering strategies to enhance dissolution rate and bioavailability. She teaches courses in Physical Chemistry of Materials and Instrumental Methods of Analysis. The group routinely operates a powder X-ray diffractometer (Bragg-Brentano geometry), a DSC-TGA platform, and a confocal Raman mapping system acquired in 2017.
Open to: contract research on co-crystal and polymorph screening for pharmaceutical companies; equipment access (PXRD, DSC-TGA, confocal Raman mapping) for external academic or industrial users; industrial PhD supervision in collaboration with NTP Novi Sad tenant companies; student internships (master and PhD level); consulting on solid-form selection and regulatory characterisation packages.
Industry experience: From 2020 to 2023, she collaborated with Farmaceutski Zavod Vojvodina d.o.o. under a research services agreement for solid-form screening of two developmental APIs, resulting in co-crystal candidates that entered pre-formulation evaluation. She has also provided ad hoc analytical consultancy to two smaller regional generic manufacturers.
Notes: Radić has expressed interest in longer-term engagement with companies at NTP Novi Sad, particularly those working in generic pharmaceutical development or nutraceutical formulation. Her laboratory has some remaining instrument capacity on the Raman mapping system on Fridays and can accommodate external samples with reasonable lead time. She is not planning a sabbatical in the near term.

R0206.title: Vesna Knežević
R0206.text:
Vesna Knežević (R0206): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Signal Processing; Machine Learning for Edge Devices; Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnostics.
Keywords: vibration signal compression; edge inference; adaptive sampling; microcontroller deployment; neural network quantisation; rotating machinery diagnostics; compressive sensing; real-time DSP; fault detection; hardware-software co-design.
Bio: Vesna Knežević received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on adaptive data reduction for vibration monitoring in rotating machinery. She joined the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications as a Teaching Assistant in 2013 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2019. Her group focuses on resource-constrained signal processing: compressing high-frequency vibration streams on microcontroller-class hardware, deploying quantised neural networks for fault detection without cloud offloading, and designing adaptive sampling schemes that meet latency and power budgets. She teaches courses on digital signal processing and embedded systems. The group regularly uses a Kistler piezoelectric sensor array, an oscilloscope bench with 200 MHz bandwidth, and STM32- and RISC-V-based development platforms.
Open to: joint projects with companies needing embedded condition monitoring solutions; contract research on microcontroller-based signal processing and TinyML deployment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with embedded systems background; student internships on firmware development and sensor node prototyping; consulting on neural network quantisation and edge inference optimisation; equipment access (bearing test rigs, Kistler sensor array, STM32 and RISC-V development platforms).
Industry experience: Vesna Knežević has collaborated with two small companies at NTP Novi Sad on pilot deployments of vibration sensor nodes for conveyor and CNC applications within the EDGEVIB project, including firmware integration and on-site calibration work.
Notes: She is currently finalising the EDGEVIB project (ending late 2025) and would be well positioned to take on a new industry contract or Horizon Europe work package starting from mid-2026. She has expressed a preference for collaborations where the company can provide labelled operational data from real machinery, as the group's existing datasets are all from controlled laboratory rigs.

R0207.title: Danijela Fejsa
R0207.text:
Danijela Fejsa (R0207): Full Professor, Department of Educational Technology, Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Educational Technology; Inclusive Education; Learning Sciences; Human–Computer Interaction.
Keywords: universal design for learning; specific learning differences; dyslexia; digital instructional materials; accessible e-learning; text-to-speech; eye-tracking in education; UDL framework; formative assessment adaptation; inclusive digital pedagogy.
Open to: joint projects with edtech companies on accessible content authoring tools; contract research on accessibility auditing of digital learning platforms; consulting on UDL implementation for organisations developing educational software; student internships for computer science or education students working on accessible e-learning; industrial PhD supervision in collaboration with companies developing adaptive learning systems.
Industry experience: Fejsa served as an external accessibility consultant for a Novi Sad-based e-learning content company during 2019–2020, reviewing and recommending revisions to a suite of primary-school digital textbook prototypes prior to their submission for ministerial approval.
Notes: Fejsa is particularly interested in connecting with companies that develop or maintain learning management systems or digital textbook platforms, where her audit framework and teacher professional development materials could be practically tested and refined at scale. She is not currently on sabbatical and has capacity for one new collaboration starting in 2025 or 2026.

R0217.title: Andrea Malešević
R0217.text:
Andrea Malešević (R0217): Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Distributed Systems and Databases; Algorithms and Data Structures; Network Security and PKI; Computer Science Theory.
Keywords: distributed database optimisation; OCSP query resolution; scalable data structures; certificate status protocol; high-throughput systems; B-tree variants; consistent hashing; public key infrastructure; real-time query processing; LSM-tree.
Bio: Andrea Malešević diplomirala je matematiku na Prirodno-matematičkom fakultetu Univerziteta u Novom Sadu 2012. godine, a doktorsku disertaciju iz oblasti distribuiranih baza podataka odbranila je 2019. godine na istom fakultetu. Od 2020. radi kao asistent s doktoratom, a od 2023. kao docent na Departmanu za matematiku i informatiku. Njena istraživačka grupa bavi se optimizacijom upita u visokopropusnim distribuiranim sistemima, projektovanjem skalabilnih struktura podataka i efikasnim rešavanjem OCSP upita u infrastrukturama javnih ključeva. Izvodi nastavu iz predmeta Baze podataka i Algoritmi i strukture podataka. U radu koristi klaster od 24 čvora u Laboratoriji za distribuirane sisteme PMF-a, kao i testna okruženja zasnovana na Apache Cassandri i PostgreSQL-u.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing PKI or certificate management infrastructure; contract research on distributed database performance evaluation; student internships in database engineering and systems programming; consulting on OCSP infrastructure design and scaling; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on secure data infrastructure.
Industry experience: Tokom 2020–2021. godine sarađivala je s lokalnom firmom za razvoj softvera iz Novog Sada na proceni arhitekture sistema za upravljanje sertifikatima, u okviru konsultantskog angažmana trajanja šest meseci. Nema stalnog zaposlenja u privredi.
Notes: Preferira saradnju s kompanijama koje imaju konkretan tehnički problem i mogućnost pristupa realnim skupovima podataka; nije zainteresovana za opšte konsultacije bez jasno definisanog istraživačkog pitanja. Tokom 2026. godine ima povećano nastavno opterećenje zbog odsustva kolege, što može uticati na dostupnost za nove projekte do kraja akademske godine.

R0233.title: Valentina Stojanović
R0233.text:
Valentina Stojanović (R0233): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering and Testing; Embedded Systems; Formal Methods; Computing and Control Engineering.
Keywords: model-based testing; mutation testing; embedded firmware; automated regression testing; formal specification; test case generation; state machine models; hardware-in-the-loop testing; test adequacy criteria; control software verification.
Bio: Valentina Stojanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2004 and 2007 respectively, and her Ph.D. in 2012 from the same institution with a dissertation on mutation-based adequacy criteria for embedded control software. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2013 and Associate Professor in 2018. Her group focuses on formal specification languages for firmware behaviour, automated generation of test suites from state-machine and contract-based models, and regression testing strategies for resource-constrained embedded systems. She teaches courses on software testing, formal methods, and embedded systems at both undergraduate and graduate levels. The group uses a lab equipped with JTAG debuggers, hardware-in-the-loop rigs, and several microcontroller development platforms for validation experiments.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing or testing embedded firmware; contract research on automated testing toolchain development; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from technology companies; consulting on test process improvement for embedded software teams; student internships in the testing and formal methods lab.
Industry experience: Stojanović conducted a two-year action research collaboration with a regional industrial electronics firm producing programmable logic controllers, contributing to the introduction of formal specification practices in their firmware development workflow. She has provided short-term consulting to two additional companies in the automotive electronics sector on test adequacy assessment.
Notes: Stojanović has a preference for collaborations where research access to real firmware codebases or development histories is possible; anonymised datasets are acceptable. The lab has hardware-in-the-loop rigs available for collaborative experiments. She is not seeking pure consulting arrangements but is open to industry contracts that include a research output component.

R0248.title: Darko Zarić
R0248.text:
Darko Zarić (R0248): Assistant Professor, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and Firmware Engineering; Agricultural Automation and Precision Farming; Industrial Communication Networks; Real-Time Systems.
Keywords: ISOBUS; ISO 11783; CANopen; protocol adaptation; embedded firmware; CAN bus; agricultural ECU; gateway design; real-time scheduling; fieldbus interoperability.
Bio: Darko Zarić completed his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Mechatronics at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2011 respectively, and defended his doctoral dissertation on ISOBUS gateway architectures for mixed-generation tractor fleets in 2017 at the same institution. He joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation as a Teaching Assistant in 2012 and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2018. His group focuses on embedded firmware design, protocol translation layers, and real-time scheduling for CAN-based fieldbus networks in agricultural machinery. He teaches courses on embedded systems programming and industrial communication protocols. The group operates a dedicated agricultural electronics laboratory equipped with Vector CANalyzer hardware, ISOBUS virtual terminal emulators, Kvaser interfaces, and a set of test ECUs from decommissioned combines and sprayers.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing agricultural ECUs or precision-farming hardware; contract research on ISOBUS or CANopen firmware development and validation; consulting on CAN network design and fieldbus conformance testing; student internships for embedded systems or electronics engineering students; equipment access to CAN bus analysis laboratory for external partners; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with embedded firmware backgrounds.
Industry experience: Zarić completed a six-month engagement with Agroelektronika d.o.o. (fictional, Subotica) in 2020 as a technical consultant on ISOBUS task-controller firmware, contributing to the specification and bench validation of their first TC-BAS compliant product line.
Notes: Zarić prefers collaborations with a concrete firmware or hardware component rather than pure data-analysis partnerships. His laboratory equipment is available to NTP companies on a scheduled basis; advance coordination is required due to student course use during the academic semester.

R0261.title: Pavol Struhár
R0261.text:
Pavol Struhár (R0261): Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Statistics and Probability; Data Science and Machine Learning; Actuarial and Risk Modelling; Internet of Things.
Keywords: time-series feature extraction; Bayesian inference; high-frequency sensor data; probabilistic risk modelling; actuarial pricing; IoT; change-point detection; extreme-value theory; predictive maintenance; streaming data.
Bio: Pavol Struhár completed his undergraduate studies in Mathematics at the University of Novi Sad in 2008 and received his PhD in Applied Mathematics from the same institution in 2014, with a dissertation on Bayesian change-point detection in non-stationary time series. He held a postdoctoral position at the University of Ljubljana (2015–2017) before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics and Informatics. His group works on statistical methods for high-frequency IoT sensor data, covering feature extraction pipelines, extreme-value theory for rare failure events, and Bayesian models for individualised actuarial pricing in insurance and maintenance contexts. He teaches probability theory, stochastic processes, and statistical computing. The group uses a small cluster of GPU workstations and has access to streaming data infrastructure shared with the Faculty of Technical Sciences.
Open to: joint projects with companies generating high-frequency sensor or telematics data; contract research on probabilistic risk and pricing models; industrial PhD supervision; consulting on Bayesian model design and validation; student internships for data science and statistics students.
Industry experience: During 2019–2020, Struhár provided statistical consulting to a regional property insurer on the design of a sensor-based premium adjustment scheme for commercial fire risk, covering model specification, data pipeline requirements, and regulatory documentation. He has also collaborated informally with an automotive components supplier in the context of a feature extraction benchmarking study.
Notes: Struhár is currently supervising two PhD students and has capacity for one further industrial PhD candidate starting from the 2025–2026 academic year. He prefers collaborations where data-sharing agreements can be established formally; his department has a standard template for this. He is not on sabbatical and has no planned leave through 2027.

R0277.title: Martin Hriešik
R0277.text:
Martin Hriešik (R0277): Associate Professor, Department of Environmental Engineering and Occupational Safety, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Environmental Engineering; Industrial Ecology and Life-Cycle Assessment; Environmental Management Systems; Occupational Safety and Regulatory Compliance.
Keywords: ISO 14001; life-cycle inventory; polymer processing; industrial effluent characterization; environmental management systems; regulatory compliance auditing; material flow analysis; wastewater treatment; thermoplastic manufacturing; eco-profile.
Bio: Martin Hriešik received his Dipl.Ing. in Environmental Engineering from the University of Novi Sad (2003) and his PhD from the same institution (2009), with a doctoral thesis on material flow analysis in thermoplastic extrusion plants. He joined the Department of Environmental Engineering and Occupational Safety as an Assistant Professor in 2010 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2016. His research group focuses on environmental management system design, life-cycle inventory construction for polymer processing facilities, industrial effluent characterization, and ISO 14001 compliance auditing. He teaches courses on industrial ecology, environmental legislation, and occupational risk assessment. The group operates a laboratory for wastewater analysis and uses SimaPro and GaBi for LCA modelling, along with portable field instruments for on-site effluent sampling at partner facilities.
Open to: contract research on environmental management system design and ISO 14001 implementation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from polymer processing or waste management companies; compliance auditing consulting for manufacturing facilities; joint project applications in the Interreg IPA or Horizon Europe LIFE programme; student internships at partner industrial facilities; equipment access for effluent characterization and on-site air quality monitoring.
Industry experience: Hriešik has served as an external ISO 14001 compliance auditor for three polymer processing companies in Serbia and one in Bosnia and Herzegovina between 2014 and 2023. He has also provided regulatory mapping consultancy to a packaging film producer preparing its integrated environmental permit renewal application.
Notes: Hriešik is actively looking for industry partners in the NTP Novi Sad ecosystem who generate primary production data that could feed into the RECYCLCA dataset or future EPD programmes. He prefers project roles that involve direct facility access for measurement campaigns rather than purely desk-based work.

R0280.title: Ivana Novaković
R0280.text:
Ivana Novaković (R0280): Research Associate, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: High-Voltage Engineering; Electrical Power Systems; Signal Processing; Non-Destructive Testing.
Keywords: partial discharge; power transformers; piezoelectric acoustic emission; impedance spectroscopy; time-frequency analysis; insulation diagnostics; wavelet transform; sensor array localisation; transformer condition monitoring; oil-paper insulation.
Bio: Ivana Novaković received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2012 and 2015 respectively, and completed her Ph.D. at the same institution in 2021, with a dissertation on piezoelectric acoustic emission sensing combined with impedance spectroscopy for partial discharge localisation in oil-filled power transformers. She has held a Research Associate position in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2022. Her group investigates insulation degradation mechanisms in high-voltage apparatus, focusing on time-frequency signal decomposition methods applied to acoustic and electrical partial discharge signatures. She teaches laboratory courses in high-voltage engineering and electrical measurements. Her experimental work is carried out in the High Voltage Laboratory at the Faculty, equipped with a 200 kV AC test system, calibrated PD measurement bridge, and a multi-channel piezoelectric sensor array.
Open to: contract research on transformer insulation diagnostics; joint projects with manufacturers of HV equipment or monitoring systems; consulting on acoustic PD measurement procedures and interpretation; equipment access (High Voltage Laboratory, piezoelectric sensor array, impedance analyser); student internships for master-level students; industrial PhD supervision.
Industry experience: Ivana Novaković collaborated with JP Elektrovojvodina on two field measurement campaigns at 110 kV substations in Vojvodina as part of the ACODIAG project, and has provided informal technical advice to the utility's maintenance team on interpreting acoustic PD survey results.
Notes: She is particularly interested in connecting with companies developing embedded monitoring hardware or data acquisition systems for HV assets, as her current work is limited by the availability of compact multi-channel synchronised acquisition platforms suitable for permanent installation.

R0283.title: Ana Mamužić
R0283.text:
Ana Mamužić (R0283): Associate Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Power Electronics; Electromagnetic Compatibility; Electrical Drives; Signal Processing.
Keywords: conducted EMI; variable-speed drives; EMC filter design; harmonic spectrum analysis; IEC 61800-3; common-mode noise; differential-mode noise; PWM inverters; impedance mismatch; EMI mitigation.
Bio: Ana Mamužić received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2003 and 2006 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2012. She has been an Associate Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2019. Her research group focuses on conducted electromagnetic interference in variable-speed drive systems, covering harmonic spectrum characterisation, common-mode and differential-mode noise separation, and EMC filter design and validation against IEC 61800-3. The group routinely uses a Rohde & Schwarz EMI test receiver, a two-line impedance stabilisation network, and a custom-built differential-mode insertion-loss test bench housed in the laboratory for power electronics and EMC at the Faculty.
