She teaches courses on power electronics and electromagnetic compatibility at both undergraduate and postgraduate level.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; consulting; equipment access; student internships; industrial PhD supervision.
Industry experience: Mamužić has provided consulting to two domestic manufacturers of industrial control panels on EMC filter selection and IEC 61800-3 pre-compliance testing procedures. She has also participated in a short-term industry contract with a regional drive assembler to audit an existing product line for Category C2 compliance.
Notes: Mamužić is co-supervising two PhD students expected to defend in 2026–2027, which limits availability for new PhD co-supervision until 2027. She is particularly interested in collaboration with companies that manufacture or integrate variable-speed drives, frequency converters, or industrial automation equipment and face IEC 61800-3 compliance challenges. Access to the Faculty's EMI test receiver and LISN setup can be arranged for collaborative projects under a formal agreement.

R0286.title: Ana Rajić
R0286.text:
Ana Rajić (R0286): Full Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Телекомуникације и бежичне мреже; Безбедност уграђених система; Индустријска информатика и теlemетрија; Криптографски протоколи.
Keywords: firmware update protocols; LPWAN; industrial telemetry; authenticated firmware delivery; intermittent wireless links; low-bandwidth networks; SCADA security; LoRaWAN; delta patching; cryptographic authentication.
Bio: Ана Рајић је редовни професор на Катедри за енергетику, електронику и телекомуникације Факултета техничких наука Универзитета у Новом Саду. Дипломирала је 2001. и докторирала 2009. године на истом факултету, са тезом о протоколима за безбедну дистрибуцију фирмвера у индустријским мрежама са ограниченим пропусним опсегом. Њена истраживачка група бави се аутентификацијом и интегритетом фирмвера у телеметријским системима са прекидном бежичном везом, укључујући LPWAN технологије и индустријске SCADA окружења. Предаје курсеве из безбедности уграђених система и протокола бежичних мрежа. Лабораторија располаже опремом за емулацију деградираних канала, LoRaWAN и Zigbee развојним платформама, као и алатима за формалну верификацију криптографских протокола.
Open to: joint projects with industry on firmware security for industrial IoT deployments; contract research on protocol design and evaluation for OTA update systems; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with embedded systems background; consulting on IEC 62443 firmware security compliance; equipment access: LoRaWAN testbed, Zigbee development platforms, channel emulator.
Industry experience: Сарађивала је са домаћим произвођачем система за даљинско очитавање бројила (AMI) на пројекту испоруке фирмвера преко PLC-а и бежичних веза у дистрибутивној мрежи у периоду 2016–2018. године. Поред тога, учествовала је као технички саветник у пројекту надоградње SCADA телеметријског система за водопривредно предузеће.
Notes: Тренутно надгледа четири докторанда и активно тражи индустријске партнере за примену резултата пројекта SAFELINK. Заинтересована искључиво за сарадњу у домену индустријске безбедности уграђених система; не прихвата консалтинг изван овог домена.

R0292.title: Đurđica Kuzmanović
R0292.text:
Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292): Associate Professor, Department of Serbian Language and Linguistics, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Computational Linguistics; Natural Language Processing; Corpus Linguistics; Slavic and Finno-Ugric Language Studies.
Keywords: cross-lingual transfer learning; morphologically rich languages; corpus annotation; South Slavic languages; Finno-Ugric languages; part-of-speech tagging; dependency parsing; multilingual NLP; Serbian language technology; low-resource NLP.
Bio: Đurđica Kuzmanović completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Serbian language and linguistics at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, and defended her doctoral dissertation on cross-lingual morphological tagging in 2013 at the same institution. She was appointed Assistant Professor in 2014 and promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on building annotated corpora and computational resources for morphologically rich languages, particularly Serbian, Croatian, Hungarian, and Finnish, with an emphasis on transfer learning across typologically distant language families. She teaches courses in corpus linguistics, computational morphology, and natural language processing at both undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group works primarily within the Laboratory for Language Technologies at the Faculty of Philosophy, making use of shared HPC resources through the Academic Network of Serbia.
Open to: joint projects; contract research on corpus annotation and data preparation for Serbian and regional languages; consulting on NLP pipeline development for South Slavic or Finno-Ugric language inputs; student internships (linguistics or computer science background welcome); industrial PhD supervision in multilingual text processing.
Industry experience: Kuzmanović served as a linguistic consultant for a Novi Sad-based software localisation company during 2017–2018, advising on Serbian morphological analysis requirements for a terminology management system. She has otherwise worked exclusively in academic and publicly funded research settings.
Notes: Kuzmanović is on leave until September 2024 but continues to supervise doctoral students and manage VoiLaRes remotely at reduced capacity. She has expressed a preference for collaborations that involve genuine linguistic analysis tasks rather than purely engineering-focused engagements, and is particularly interested in partners working on document processing, legal or medical text analysis, or multilingual customer-facing applications in the regional language context.

R0308.title: Jovan Bogićević
R0308.text:
Jovan Bogićević (R0308): Associate Professor, Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Manufacturing Engineering; Structural and Computational Mechanics; Control Engineering; Materials Processing.
Keywords: springback prediction; sheet-metal forming; press-brake bending; finite element analysis; adaptive control; high-strength steel; advanced high-strength steel; closed-loop CNC control; material characterisation; forming limit.
Bio: Jovan Bogićević received his Dipl.-Ing. degree in Production Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2004, followed by his M.Sc. in 2007 and Ph.D. in 2013, with a doctoral thesis on analytical springback models for high-strength steel sheets bent on CNC press-brakes. He joined the Department of Production Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2006 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His research group focuses on springback prediction using both closed-form analytical methods and finite-element simulation, and on adaptive control strategies for press-brake bending that compensate for springback in real time. He teaches courses in Sheet-Metal Technology, Manufacturing Processes, and Computer-Aided Manufacturing. The group operates a CNC hydraulic press-brake instrumented with angle-measurement sensors, a tensile-testing machine, and access to the faculty's ABAQUS and PAM-STAMP FEM licences.
Open to: joint projects with sheet-metal fabricators and tooling manufacturers; contract research on springback characterisation and FEM model calibration; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; student internships (M.Sc. level) on press-brake instrumentation and digital twin topics; consulting on CNC press-brake setup, tooling selection, and forming process qualification; equipment access to instrumented press-brake and FEM simulation licences for external collaborators.
Industry experience: Bogićević has carried out two short-term consulting engagements with sheet-metal fabrication companies in Vojvodina, advising on CNC press-brake tooling selection and bending-sequence optimisation for structural steel components. He has also participated in a bilateral industry contract with a local HVAC enclosure manufacturer to develop bending correction tables for galvanised and pre-painted steel.
Notes: Bogićević is currently co-supervising three doctoral students, two of whom are on the FORMTWIN project, so capacity for new long-term commitments is limited until mid-2026. He is particularly interested in connecting with NTP companies that operate press-brakes or laser-cutting lines and face tolerance problems with AHSS or aluminium alloys. He has no planned sabbatical in the near term.

R0312.title: Branislava Dragišić
R0312.text:
Branislava Dragišić (R0312): Research Associate, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering; Mobile Computing; Software Testing and Quality Assurance.
Keywords: Android fragmentation; cross-version compatibility; automated regression testing; API deprecation; test suite generation; mobile software quality; platform-specific defects; continuous integration; UI compatibility testing; static analysis.
Bio: Branislava Dragišić completed her Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Computer Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012, respectively, and defended her PhD in 2018 on automated detection of Android platform fragmentation defects. She has been a Research Associate in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering since 2019. Her group focuses on software testing methodologies, mobile platform compatibility, and continuous integration pipelines for heterogeneous device ecosystems. She teaches courses in Software Quality Assurance and Mobile Application Development at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The group maintains a device testing laboratory with approximately 40 physical Android devices spanning API levels 19 through 35, supplemented by cloud-based emulator farms used in empirical studies.
Open to: joint projects with mobile software development companies; contract research on Android compatibility testing and CI pipeline setup; student internships for companies needing hands-on testing support; consulting on mobile QA process improvement; equipment access to the physical Android device testing laboratory; co-supervision of industrial PhD candidates in software testing.
Industry experience: Dragišić collaborated with Droidforge Solutions d.o.o. on a six-month contract engagement in 2020–2021 to audit and restructure their Android regression testing pipeline, resulting in a reduction of post-release compatibility bug reports. She has maintained an ongoing advisory relationship with the same company since then.
Notes: Dragišić is currently supervising two PhD students whose theses are embedded in the COMPAT-RS project; she prefers that any new industry engagements align with or complement that project's scope to avoid overcommitment. She is particularly interested in working with companies that have existing mobile products and a willingness to share anonymised defect data for research purposes.

R0322.title: Emilija Zec
R0322.text:
Emilija Zec (R0322): Full Professor, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Educational Psychology; Psychometrics and Measurement; Cognitive Science; Human–Computer Interaction.
Keywords: item response theory; knowledge tracing; cognitive skill acquisition; Bayesian inference; hidden Markov models; clickstream analysis; technology-enhanced learning; response time modelling; latent class analysis; formative assessment.
Bio: Emilija Zec completed her undergraduate and master's degrees in psychology at the University of Novi Sad (2001, 2004) and her doctorate at the University of Ljubljana in 2009, with a dissertation on latent class models of arithmetic skill progression in primary-school children. She joined the Department of Psychology at the Faculty of Philosophy in Novi Sad in 2010 and was promoted to Full Professor in 2021. Her group develops and validates psychometric models—primarily item response theory variants, Bayesian knowledge-tracing extensions, and hidden Markov approaches—for inferring learners' cognitive states from clickstream and response-time data generated within digital learning platforms. She teaches psychometrics, research methods, and cognitive psychology at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The group operates a behavioural data laboratory equipped with eye-tracking hardware, response-time collection software, and access to a university computing cluster for large-scale model estimation.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing adaptive learning or HR assessment platforms; contract research on psychometric model development and validation; consulting on assessment design and trace-data analysis pipelines; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on learning analytics or psychometric software; student internships related to data analysis and educational platform evaluation.
Industry experience: Emilija Zec provided consulting to a Novi Sad-based e-learning startup (Edukos d.o.o.) in 2019–2020 on the psychometric calibration of their adaptive quiz engine, including item bank design and ability score reporting. She has since maintained informal contact with several NTP-based software companies interested in assessment functionality.
Notes: Emilija Zec is particularly interested in collaborations where real interaction-log data from a learning or HR platform are available; she has found that data-sharing agreements are often the bottleneck and prefers to address these early. She is on reduced administrative load in 2025–2026 following completion of her departmental headship, making this a good period for new project engagement.

R0349.title: Stefan Dragić
R0349.text:
Stefan Dragić (R0349): Full Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Information Retrieval; Natural Language Processing; Text Mining; Computational Linguistics.
Keywords: information retrieval; script normalization; transliteration; Serbian text; mixed-script indexing; Cyrillic-Latin; inverted index; query expansion; morphological analysis; corpus linguistics.
Bio: Stefan Dragić je diplomirao matematiku na Prirodno-matematičkom fakultetu Univerziteta u Novom Sadu 2001. godine, a doktorirao je 2008. na istom fakultetu, s tezom o indeksiranju višeskriptnih tekstualnih korpusa. Nakon postdoktorskog boravka na Univerzitetu u Beču (2009–2010), vratio se na Departman za matematiku i informatiku, gde je 2019. izabran u zvanje redovnog profesora. Njegova istraživačka grupa bavi se pronalaženjem informacija u dokumentima koji sadrže mešovito ćirilično-latinično srpsko pismo, normalizacijom skripte, transliteracijom kao korakom u pretprocesiranju i izgradnjom invertovanih indeksa otpornih na varijacije pisma. Predaje kurseve iz upravljanja bazama podataka i rudarenja teksta. Laboratorija koristi sopstvene korpuse pravnih i novinarskih tekstova.
Open to: joint projects with companies that manage large Serbian-language document collections; contract research on internal search engine customization; consulting on script normalization and multilingual indexing; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a software background; student internships (master's level) focused on NLP pipeline development.
Industry experience: U periodu 2022–2023. sarađivao je s jednim novosadskim startapom iz oblasti legaltech-a na prilagođavanju pretražnog modula za srpske sudske odluke, u okviru ugovornog istraživanja trajanja 18 meseci.
Notes: Dragić preferira saradnju s kompanijama koje imaju jasno definisan i dovoljno veliki tekstualni korpus na srpskom jeziku; nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente. Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.

R0356.title: Darko Ninkov
R0356.text:
Darko Ninkov (R0356): Senior Research Associate, Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechatronics and Embedded Systems; Automotive Electronics and ECU Testing; Real-Time and FPGA-Based Control; Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation.
Keywords: hardware-in-the-loop; ECU validation; FPGA I/O emulation; real-time simulation; open-source real-time target; CAN bus; automotive embedded systems; fault injection; rapid control prototyping; low-cost test bench.
Bio: Darko Ninkov received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Mechatronics Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2005 and 2008 respectively, and his Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the same institution in 2013. He joined the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation as a Research Associate in 2013 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2019. His group focuses on hardware-in-the-loop simulation, real-time control platforms, and FPGA-based I/O emulation primarily for automotive ECU testing. He teaches courses on embedded systems and real-time programming at undergraduate and master levels. The laboratory operates several open-source real-time targets based on ARM and x86 architectures, a suite of Xilinx-family FPGA boards, CAN/LIN/FlexRay bus interfaces, and bench-level power supply and fault-injection hardware.
Open to: contract research on ECU test bench development; joint projects with automotive ECU suppliers or Tier-1 companies; industrial PhD supervision in real-time systems and FPGA-based I/O emulation; student internships on FPGA board bring-up and Linux real-time configuration; equipment access for FPGA development boards and CAN/FlexRay bus analysers; consulting on selecting and configuring open-source real-time platforms.
Industry experience: Ninkov collaborated with two regional automotive ECU suppliers under non-disclosure agreements during the HILVOP project, providing bench design support and test case development. He has also delivered short technical training sessions for engineering teams at a Novi Sad-based electronics manufacturing company.
Notes: Prefers projects where at least part of the results can be published; willing to negotiate publication embargoes of up to 18 months for industry contracts. Currently supervising two doctoral students, so capacity for new long-term commitments is limited until mid-2027.

R0364.title: Žarko Pejić
R0364.text:
Žarko Pejić (R0364): Research Associate, Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Remote Sensing and Earth Observation; Hydrometeorology and Climatology; Agricultural Risk and Insurance; Spatial Statistics and GIS.
Keywords: spatial downscaling; satellite precipitation estimation; geostatistical interpolation; index insurance; rainfall variability; NDVI; Vojvodina; kriging with external drift; field-level weather indices; bias correction.
Bio: Žarko Pejić completed his BSc in Geography at the University of Novi Sad in 2011 and his MSc in Remote Sensing and Environmental Monitoring at the same institution in 2014. He received his PhD from the University of Novi Sad in 2020, with a dissertation on geostatistical downscaling of satellite precipitation estimates for agricultural applications in the Vojvodina plain. Since 2021 he has held a Research Associate position within the Remote Sensing and GIS Group at BioSense Institute, where the group focuses on Earth observation data processing, land-use mapping, and precision agriculture. He participates in undergraduate fieldwork courses and co-supervises MSc students. His primary laboratory work involves QGIS, R, and Python environments running on the institute's high-performance computing cluster, alongside access to meteorological station networks maintained by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia.
Open to: joint projects on spatial weather data products for agri-insurance or precision agriculture; contract research involving satellite precipitation downscaling or geostatistical interpolation; consulting for insurers or reinsurers designing rainfall index products for the Pannonian region; student internships for MSc students working on spatial data science or hydrometeorology; equipment access to the group's dense gauge network for short deployment campaigns.
Industry experience: Pejić provided technical consultancy to Agroprotekta d.o.o., a regional agricultural insurance intermediary based in Novi Sad, in 2023, advising on spatial resolution requirements for parametric rainfall products covering Vojvodina. He has participated in one workshop organised by a Vienna-based reinsurance analytics firm evaluating satellite rainfall data quality for Eastern European agricultural portfolios.
Notes: Pejić is particularly interested in partnerships with companies that process or distribute agronomic data, operate IoT sensor networks in fields, or develop insurance technology platforms, as these could complement his group's remote sensing data streams. He is not currently on sabbatical and supervises one PhD student whose topic overlaps directly with this specialty.

R0365.title: Bojan Erić
R0365.text:
Bojan Erić (R0365): Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Materials Science and Structural Integrity; Computational Mechanics; Manufacturing and Joining Technology.
Keywords: fatigue crack growth; fracture mechanics; welded steel joints; residual stress; finite element simulation; low-temperature fatigue; thermal cycling; stress intensity factor; structural steel; variable-amplitude loading.
Bio: Bojan Erić received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2003, and his PhD from the same institution in 2010, with a dissertation on fatigue crack propagation in multipass fillet welds under variable-amplitude loading. He joined the Department of Mechanical Engineering as an assistant in 2004 and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on fatigue and fracture mechanics of welded structural steel joints subjected to combined cyclic mechanical loading and low-temperature thermal excursions, residual-stress redistribution, and finite-element simulation of crack driving forces. He teaches courses in Machine Elements, Fracture Mechanics, and Welded Structures. The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models built in Abaqus for residual-stress and fracture-mechanics analyses.
Open to: contract research on fatigue and fracture testing of welded steel components; consulting on structural integrity assessment and fitness-for-service evaluation; joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions; industrial PhD supervision for companies dealing with steel structures, cranes, or pressure equipment; equipment access (servo-hydraulic fatigue machine, climate chamber to −60 °C, DIC setup); student internships related to experimental mechanics or FE simulation of welds.
Industry experience: Erić has carried out two consultancy engagements for regional steel fabricators on fatigue assessment of crane runway girders and has collaborated informally with a Vojvodina-based metalworking company during the crane girder monitoring campaign reported in his 2020 conference paper.
Notes: Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination. He is particularly interested in partnering with companies that manufacture steel structures operating outdoors in cold environments, such as cranes, storage tanks, or pipeline supports.

R0375.title: Stefan Kostić
R0375.text:
Stefan Kostić (R0375): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Formal Methods and Verification; Embedded and Real-Time Systems; Software Engineering; Computer Science.
Keywords: formal verification; static program analysis; model checking; safety-critical software; SMT solvers; counterexample generation; coverage metrics; MISRA-C; real-time systems; bounded model checking.
Bio: Stefan Kostić completed his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Computer Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2012 respectively, followed by a PhD in 2018 on bounded model checking for real-time embedded controllers. After a two-year postdoctoral stay at the University of Ljubljana, he returned to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor in 2020. His research group focuses on formal verification, static program analysis, and model-based testing of safety-critical software, with particular attention to MISRA-C compliance checking, coverage metrics for control-flow and data-flow criteria, and automated counterexample generation using SMT solvers. He teaches courses in software verification, embedded systems programming, and formal methods. The group regularly uses the UPPAAL model checker, CBMC, and Frama-C on a dedicated embedded systems laboratory bench.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing safety-critical embedded or PLC-based software; contract research on MISRA-C compliance tooling and static analysis integration into CI pipelines; industrial PhD supervision for engineers working on formal verification or software testing; consulting on IEC 61508 / ISO 26262 software verification processes; student internships involving Frama-C, CBMC, or UPPAAL.
Industry experience: During the VERITAS project, Kostić worked directly with a Serbian automation equipment manufacturer on integrating Frama-C analysis into their firmware review process, resulting in a signed cooperation agreement for follow-on work. He has also delivered in-company formal methods training to engineers at two Novi Sad-based software companies.
Notes: Kostić is actively looking for industry partners whose embedded software teams would benefit from static analysis tooling or coverage-based testing. He is particularly interested in companies operating under functional safety standards (IEC 61508, ISO 26262, EN 50128) where formal verification evidence is required or incentivised. His laboratory has licensed access to UPPAAL and maintains a workstation cluster for SMT solver experiments.

R0399.title: Sara Nedeljković
R0399.text:
Sara Nedeljković (R0399): Senior Research Associate, Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Structural Mechanics; Dynamics and Vibration; Fatigue and Fracture Mechanics.
Keywords: vibration analysis; structural fatigue; frequency-domain FEM; rotating machinery; modal analysis; fatigue life prediction; harmonic response; power spectral density; gear dynamics; welded joints.
Bio: Sara Nedeljković completed her Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Mechanical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2007 and 2009 respectively, and defended her PhD thesis on fatigue life prediction of gear assemblies under variable-amplitude loading in 2014 at the same institution. She joined the Department of Machine Design and Mechanics as a Research Associate in 2015 and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. Her research group focuses on vibration diagnostics, high-cycle and low-cycle structural fatigue, and frequency-domain finite-element methods applied to rotating machinery, power transmission components, and cyclically loaded welded structures. She teaches undergraduate courses in Machine Elements and graduate courses in Structural Dynamics. The group operates a structural vibration laboratory equipped with LMS SCADAS modal analysis hardware, servo-hydraulic fatigue testing frames, and access to ANSYS Mechanical and MSC Nastran licences.
Open to: contract research; joint projects; consulting on vibration fatigue assessment and structural dynamics; equipment access (fatigue test frames, modal analysis hardware); industrial PhD co-supervision; student internships.
Industry experience: Nedeljković carried out a six-month engagement as a technical consultant for Agrotech Solutions d.o.o. during 2022–2023, supporting fatigue life assessment of welded chassis components and advising on sensor placement for in-service load measurement campaigns.
Notes: Prefers applied collaborative projects where physical testing and simulation are both feasible; the group has limited bandwidth for purely computational studies without experimental validation. Equipment booking should be arranged at least four weeks in advance due to shared laboratory scheduling.

R0413.title: Branislava Lekić
R0413.text:
Branislava Lekić (R0413): Associate Professor, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Health Psychology; Persuasion and Communication Research; Behavioural Science; Public Health.
Keywords: health behaviour change; message framing; motivational interviewing; self-determination theory; gain-loss framing; narrative persuasion; smoking cessation; physical activity promotion; intervention design; autonomy support.
Bio: Branislava Lekić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in psychology at the University of Novi Sad (2003, 2006) and defended her doctoral dissertation at the same institution in 2012, with a research stay at the University of Ljubljana during 2010–2011. She has been an Associate Professor in the Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, since 2019. Her group investigates how message framing, narrative structures, and self-determination principles can be applied in health communication campaigns, particularly for chronic disease self-management, physical activity promotion, and smoking cessation. She teaches courses on health psychology and persuasion theory at undergraduate and postgraduate levels. The group regularly uses online survey platforms, physiological arousal measures (skin conductance, heart rate), and eye-tracking equipment shared with the Cognitive Neuroscience Laboratory at the Faculty.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; consulting; student internships; industrial PhD supervision.
Industry experience: Lekić has provided consulting advice to two health technology companies on the behavioural science underpinnings of their patient engagement features, including message tone, framing, and notification design. She has also delivered communication training workshops to occupational health teams in companies in Vojvodina.
Notes: Lekić has particular interest in collaborating with companies developing digital health tools, mobile apps, or workplace wellbeing platforms where behaviour change communication design is a core product concern. She is willing to support user research, message testing, and evidence-based content development. Available for new collaborations from autumn 2025 onward; currently finalising the MOTIVOJNA project reporting.

R0416.title: Ksenija Hadžić
R0416.text:
Ksenija Hadžić (R0416): Associate Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Theoretical Computer Science; Formal Language Theory; Machine Learning and Inference; Network Protocol Analysis.
Keywords: automata theory; grammatical inference; regular grammars; passive learning; protocol inference; finite state machines; L* algorithm; RPNI algorithm; formal verification; network trace analysis.
Bio: Ksenija Hadžić completed her undergraduate and master's studies in mathematics and computer science at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. She received her PhD in 2013 from the same institution, with a dissertation on passive inference of finite automata from labelled example strings. After a postdoctoral stay at the University of Ljubljana (2014–2015), she returned to Novi Sad as an assistant professor and was promoted to associate professor in 2020. Her group works on grammatical inference of regular and context-free languages, with a particular focus on deriving communication protocol models from network traces. She teaches courses on formal languages, automata theory, and algorithms. The group uses a small cluster of eight nodes for symbolic learning experiments and maintains an open corpus of protocol trace datasets.
Open to: joint projects with companies on protocol analysis or network security; contract research on automaton-based behavioural modelling; student internships for master's or final-year undergraduate students; consulting on formal specification and verification of communication protocols; co-supervision of industrial PhD candidates working on network security or IoT.
Industry experience: Hadžić collaborated with BEZ Systems d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based embedded systems company, on an anomaly detection pilot for SCADA protocol traffic between 2018 and 2020, contributing inference algorithms and evaluation methodology.
Notes: Hadžić is particularly interested in working with companies that generate large volumes of network or protocol logs and need structured behavioural models for testing, monitoring, or certification purposes. She prefers project engagements where there is a defined research question rather than pure development work. The GInferLib library is freely available and can serve as a starting point for feasibility discussions.

R0422.title: Attila Bálint
R0422.text:
Attila Bálint (R0422): Full Professor, Department of Finance and Banking, Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Quantitative Finance and Risk Management; Operational Risk and Insurance Mathematics; Information Security Economics; Applied Statistics and Econometrics.
Keywords: operational risk; loss distribution approach; information security incidents; cyber risk quantification; extreme value theory; compound Poisson process; Basel framework; Monte Carlo simulation; severity modelling; frequency estimation.
Bio: Attila Bálint received his BSc and MSc in Economics from the Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 1998 and 2001 respectively, and completed his PhD at the same institution in 2007 with a dissertation on loss distribution approaches for operational risk under Basel II requirements. He joined the Department of Finance and Banking as an assistant professor in 2008 and was promoted to full professor in 2019. His research group focuses on statistical modelling of low-frequency, high-severity operational loss events, with particular emphasis on information security incidents, cyber insurance pricing, and frequency–severity decomposition methods. He teaches courses in financial risk management and quantitative methods at undergraduate and postgraduate level. The group uses actuarial simulation software, R, and Python environments hosted on departmental computing infrastructure.
Open to: joint research projects on cyber risk quantification with companies holding internal incident data; contract research on actuarial modelling of information security losses; consulting on operational risk model development and validation for financial institutions and insurers; industrial PhD supervision for candidates combining data science and financial risk backgrounds; student internships focused on loss data analysis and statistical modelling.
Industry experience: Between 2004 and 2007, Bálint served as a part-time quantitative risk analyst at a Novi Sad-based commercial bank, where he contributed to the development of the institution's first AMA-compliant operational risk model. He has since conducted several short-term consulting engagements with insurance firms on cyber product pricing.
Notes: Bálint is particularly interested in collaborations with technology companies at NTP Novi Sad that generate or handle internal incident data, as access to real-world loss records is the binding constraint in his current research programme. He is cautious about projects requiring significant software engineering effort and prefers partners who can provide data and domain knowledge while his group contributes statistical methodology. His teaching load is highest in the autumn semester; project meetings are easier to schedule in spring.

R0484.title: Jovan Puzović
R0484.text:
Jovan Puzović (R0484): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Machine Learning; Natural Language Processing; Legal Informatics; Data Engineering.
Keywords: imbalanced datasets; data augmentation; transfer learning; legal text classification; judicial decision prediction; SMOTE variants; small sample learning; sequence modelling; synthetic data generation; Serbian legal corpus.
Bio: Jovan Puzović received his BSc and MSc degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2013 respectively, and completed his PhD at the same institution in 2019, with a thesis on transfer learning strategies for imbalanced legal corpora. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2014 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2020. His research group focuses on machine learning methods suited to small and structurally imbalanced datasets, with a particular emphasis on judicial decision sequences, legal text classification, and synthetic data generation. He teaches courses in machine learning fundamentals and data engineering. The group works primarily with Python-based ML frameworks and uses the Faculty's shared GPU cluster for model training experiments.
Open to: joint projects with companies handling structured or textual legal and compliance data; contract research on document classification and outcome prediction for small proprietary datasets; student internships in machine learning and NLP; consulting on imbalanced dataset strategy and evaluation design; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on document intelligence or legal tech.
Industry experience: Puzović completed a three-month consulting engagement in 2022 with a Novi Sad-based software company developing a contract review tool, advising on classifier design for a dataset of approximately 800 annotated commercial agreements. He has no other formal industry positions.
Notes: Puzović is co-supervising two PhD students whose dissertations are expected in 2026–2027, which limits availability for large new commitments until mid-2026. He is particularly interested in partnerships where the company can provide access to proprietary labelled datasets, as public Serbian legal corpora are a recurring bottleneck in his research.

R0503.title: Milica Nikolić
R0503.text:
Milica Nikolić (R0503): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Cryptography and Information Security; Embedded Systems and Hardware Engineering; Computer Engineering.
Keywords: post-quantum cryptography; lattice-based signatures; hardware security modules; resource-constrained devices; performance benchmarking; side-channel analysis; CRYSTALS-Dilithium; NTRU; microcontroller implementation; memory optimisation.
Bio: Milica Nikolić completed her undergraduate and master's studies at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, and received her PhD in computer engineering from the same institution in 2009, with a dissertation on side-channel resistance in symmetric cipher implementations. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. Her research group focuses on implementing and benchmarking post-quantum cryptographic primitives—particularly lattice-based schemes—on microcontrollers, smart cards, and dedicated hardware security modules with tight memory and power budgets. She teaches courses in applied cryptography, embedded systems security, and secure software design. The group maintains a laboratory equipped with oscilloscopes, electromagnetic probes, and a collection of ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V development boards used for power and timing analysis.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing HSMs, IoT security firmware, or industrial control system security; contract research on PQC migration assessment and implementation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad member companies; student internships for embedded security firmware development; consulting on NIST post-quantum standard adoption timelines and compliance.
Industry experience: Milica Nikolić collaborated with Informatika d.o.o. (Novi Sad) on a six-month applied research contract in 2022 covering PQC readiness assessment for their smart metering gateway product line. She has also served as a technical reviewer for two Serbian national certification procedures involving cryptographic modules.
Notes: Prefers collaborative arrangements that involve real hardware and measurable deliverables rather than purely theoretical work. The lab has limited availability of the Infineon SLE97 evaluation kits (two units); industrial partners providing additional hardware would accelerate shared projects. Currently co-supervising four PhD students; capacity for a fifth industrial PhD exists from late 2025 onward.

R0524.title: Mónika Papp
R0524.text:
Mónika Papp (R0524): Senior Research Associate, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Natural Language Processing; Computational Linguistics; Machine Learning; Information Retrieval.
Keywords: cross-lingual semantic similarity; named-entity alignment; multilingual transformers; structured document reconciliation; sentence embeddings; low-resource languages; legal NLP; entity linking; parallel corpora; document matching.
Bio: Mónika Papp completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. She earned her PhD in 2013 with a dissertation on cross-lingual sentence alignment in multilingual legal corpora. After a postdoctoral stay at the University of Ljubljana (2014–2015), she returned to Novi Sad as a Research Associate and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. Her group focuses on multilingual natural language processing, with particular emphasis on transformer-based semantic similarity, named-entity alignment, and structured document reconciliation across typologically diverse languages. She teaches courses in computational linguistics and machine learning for text data. The group uses GPU-equipped workstations and accesses HPC resources through the Institute of Mathematics of the Serbian Academy of Sciences.
Open to: joint projects; contract research on document matching and data reconciliation; consulting on multilingual NLP system design; student internships; industrial PhD supervision.
Industry experience: Papp carried out a six-month applied research engagement with a regional insurance company (2018–2019) focused on automated cross-lingual matching of damage-claim documents submitted in Serbian and Hungarian. The engagement resulted in a prototype system deployed internally by the company.
Notes: Papp is currently at full teaching load and can take on new projects only from late 2025 onward. She has a strong preference for projects with a clearly defined applied component and real multilingual document data rather than purely benchmark-oriented work.

R0528.title: Goran Radović
R0528.text:
Goran Radović (R0528): Teaching Assistant, Department of Graphic Engineering and Design, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Graphic and typographic engineering; Computational design and parametric modelling; Digital typography and font technology; Localisation and script encoding.
Keywords: generative typeface design; parametric glyph interpolation; OpenType feature engineering; Southern Slavic diacritics; minority script systems; variable fonts; Cyrillic typography; Rusyn orthography; prepress rendering; glyph contour optimisation.
Bio: Goran Radović completed his Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Graphic Engineering and Design at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, graduating with a Master's thesis on parametric construction of Cyrillic letterforms in 2022. He joined the Department of Graphic Engineering and Design as a Teaching Assistant in 2023 and is currently enrolled in doctoral studies under the supervision of Associate Professor Milena Vukčević. His research focuses on generative methods for designing typefaces that support minority script systems of the southern Slavic region, including Rusyn and Bunjevac orthographies, and on engineering OpenType features for correct rendering of Southern Slavic diacritics in both screen and print workflows. He teaches courses in typography, prepress technology, and digital typeface production. He regularly uses the department's type-proofing laboratory and has access to a variable-font testing rig running cross-platform rendering benchmarks.
Open to: joint projects with companies requiring multilingual font development; contract research on OpenType feature engineering for specialised character sets; student internships in type design or prepress quality assurance; consulting on Southern Slavic diacritics rendering in publishing and web software.
Industry experience: Radović completed a three-month internship in 2022 with Štamparija Futura d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based print production house, where he audited their prepress font pipeline for Cyrillic rendering failures in imposition software. He has since provided informal consulting to the same company on font substitution issues in PDF/X workflows.
Notes: Radović is in the early phase of his doctoral studies and cannot independently supervise PhD candidates. His supervisor Milena Vukčević should be included in any collaboration discussions that imply sustained project leadership. He is particularly interested in connections with software companies developing text-rendering engines, publishing platforms, or localisation tools that need tested Southern Slavic OpenType support.

R0567.title: Zorica Jovanović
R0567.text:
Zorica Jovanović (R0567): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Power Electronics; Electrical Drives and Motor Control; Power Quality and Harmonics; Industrial Automation.
Keywords: multi-level inverters; selective harmonic elimination; pulse-width modulation; medium-voltage drives; cascaded H-bridge; neutral-point-clamped inverter; total harmonic distortion; motor drive control; power quality; switching frequency optimization.
Bio: Zorica Jovanović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2007 and 2010 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2016. She has been an Assistant Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications since 2018. Her research group focuses on pulse-width modulation strategies for multi-level inverter topologies, selective harmonic elimination techniques, and power quality improvement in medium-voltage motor drive systems for industrial applications. She teaches undergraduate courses in Power Electronics and graduate courses in Motor Drive Control. The group regularly uses a laboratory-scale 5-level cascaded H-bridge inverter testbed, a dSPACE DS1104 real-time control platform, a Yokogawa power analyser, and simulation tools including MATLAB/Simulink and PLECS.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing or integrating medium-voltage variable-speed drives; contract research on harmonic measurement, analysis, and filter design for industrial installations; consulting on power quality compliance for medium-voltage motor drive systems; student internships in power electronics laboratory work; equipment access (5-level CHB testbed, Yokogawa power analyser, dSPACE DS1104).
Industry experience: Zorica Jovanović conducted a six-month applied research engagement with a regional electrical switchgear manufacturer in 2019–2020, providing technical analysis of harmonic emissions in their medium-voltage variable-frequency drive product line. She has also participated in two measurement campaigns at industrial sites in Vojvodina as part of the HARMIND project.
Notes: Zorica Jovanović is particularly interested in collaboration with companies facing IEC harmonic compliance issues in existing installations, as her team has both simulation and on-site measurement capabilities. She currently supervises two doctoral students and can take on one more in the near term.

R0571.title: Mirjana Malešević
R0571.text:
Mirjana Malešević (R0571): Research Associate, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Data Engineering; Software Quality Assurance; Distributed Systems; Applied Machine Learning.
Keywords: data quality monitoring; anomaly detection; schema drift; real-time data pipelines; API data integration; event-driven architecture; cross-source consistency; streaming data; business rule validation; data observability.
Bio: Mirjana Malešević received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2011 and 2014 respectively, and defended her Ph.D. thesis on automated schema-drift detection in event-driven data pipelines at the same institution in 2019. She has held a Research Associate position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering since 2020. Her group focuses on data quality assurance in distributed and real-time systems, with particular attention to API-mediated data flows, cross-source consistency validation, and anomaly detection under schema evolution. She teaches courses on data engineering and software quality assurance at undergraduate and master level. Her laboratory work relies on a self-hosted Apache Kafka cluster, a PostgreSQL-based data observatory, and shared computing infrastructure maintained by the faculty.
Open to: joint projects with companies operating API-based data integrations; contract research on data quality tooling and pipeline monitoring; student internships in data engineering and quality assurance; consulting on schema governance and anomaly detection system design; industrial Ph.D. co-supervision.
Industry experience: Mirjana worked as a software engineer at a regional IT services company in Novi Sad from 2014 to 2016, where she was involved in integration projects connecting ERP systems via REST APIs. This experience directly motivated her research focus on practical pipeline reliability.
Notes: Mirjana is particularly interested in collaborating with companies at NTP Novi Sad that handle data from multiple external API sources and face reliability or consistency problems. She prefers project engagements that include access to real anonymised operational data. Her current teaching load is moderate, leaving time for one additional collaboration in 2025–2026.

R0593.title: Đuro Simić
R0593.text:
Đuro Simić (R0593): Assistant Professor, Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Manufacturing and Production Engineering; Welding Technology; Surface Engineering and Coatings; Quality Control and Metrology.
Keywords: MIG/MAG welding; spatter reduction; thin sheet welding; weld process optimisation; pre-weld surface preparation; electrostatic powder coating; pre-treatment quality control; phosphating; coating adhesion; mild steel.
Bio: Đuro Simić received his B.Eng. and M.Eng. degrees in Production Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2008 and 2011 respectively, and defended his PhD thesis on low-spatter MIG/MAG parameter optimisation for thin mild-steel sheet in 2017 at the same institution. He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2018. His research group focuses on arc welding process control, pre-weld surface preparation, and quality assurance methodology for electrostatic powder coating pre-treatment lines, with particular interest in correlating surface chemistry measurements with coating adhesion outcomes. He teaches undergraduate courses in Manufacturing Processes and Welding Technology and a graduate course in Surface Engineering. The group regularly uses the department's inverter MIG/MAG welding station, profilometry bench, and salt-spray cabinet, as well as XRF and SEM-EDS equipment shared with the Materials Testing Laboratory.
Open to: contract research on weld process qualification and parameter optimisation; consulting on pre-treatment line quality control and SPC implementation; joint projects with companies operating powder coating or welding production lines; student internships in welding technology or surface treatment quality; equipment access (MIG/MAG welding station, profilometry, salt-spray cabinet).
Industry experience: Between 2011 and 2013, Simić worked part-time as a process engineer at Termometal d.o.o., Novi Sad, supporting qualification of weld procedures for thin-wall HVAC components. He has since carried out two short consulting engagements with powder coating contractors in Vojvodina on pre-treatment bath management.
Notes: Simić has expressed a preference for collaborations with companies that can provide real production-line access for measurement campaigns, as opposed to purely laboratory-based contracts. He is not currently on sabbatical and has moderate teaching load in the spring semester.

R0611.title: Danijela Ninkov
R0611.text:
Danijela Ninkov (R0611): Full Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Electromagnetic Compatibility; Power Electronics; Power Systems and Power Quality; Signal Processing in Electrical Engineering.
Keywords: electromagnetic compatibility; conducted emissions; time-domain modelling; low-voltage power networks; power electronic loads; harmonic distortion; line impedance stabilisation network; grid-connected inverters; power quality; conducted disturbance propagation.
Bio: Danijela Ninkov received her Dipl.Ing. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 1998 and 2003 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2008. She has held a Full Professor position since 2019 in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications. Her research group focuses on electromagnetic compatibility in low-voltage distribution networks, with particular attention to time-domain modelling of conducted disturbances, harmonic propagation, and the interaction between power electronic loads and grid regulation equipment. She teaches undergraduate and postgraduate courses in electromagnetic compatibility and power quality. The group operates a dedicated EMC measurement laboratory equipped with a line impedance stabilisation network, conducted emission analysers calibrated to CISPR standards, and a real-time power network emulator.
Open to: contract research on EMC characterisation of industrial or consumer power electronic equipment; consulting on conducted emission compliance and power quality assessment; joint projects on supraharmonic emissions and smart grid EMC; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from companies with relevant measurement or simulation needs; equipment access: LISN-based conducted emission measurement, power quality class A monitoring, network impedance characterisation up to 30 MHz; student internships in the EMC laboratory.
Industry experience: Danijela Ninkov has provided technical consulting to a regional distribution system operator on power quality measurement methodology and has assisted two domestic equipment manufacturers with pre-compliance conducted emission testing. She has no long-term industrial employment.
Notes: Prefers projects with a clear measurement component rather than purely theoretical work. The EMC laboratory is shared with two other research groups and access scheduling should be discussed early in any collaboration. Available for new project commitments from early 2026 onward.

R0627.title: Nikola Ranković
R0627.text:
Nikola Ranković (R0627): Full Professor, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Psychometrics and psychological assessment; Cognitive psychology; Developmental psychology; Educational measurement.
Keywords: psychometrics; cognitive ability testing; computerised adaptive testing; test norming; item response theory; working memory; fluid intelligence; Serbian children; differential item functioning; standardisation.
Bio: Nikola Ranković completed his undergraduate and master's degrees in psychology at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Philosophy, graduating in 2001 and 2004 respectively. He received his doctorate from the University of Belgrade in 2009, with a dissertation on latent structure models in intelligence testing. He joined the Department of Psychology in Novi Sad as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group focuses on psychometric test development, item response theory applications, and standardisation of cognitive and scholastic ability measures for Serbian-speaking children and adolescents. He teaches undergraduate courses in psychological measurement and statistics, and postgraduate seminars on structural equation modelling. The group uses the department's psychophysiology laboratory and maintains a norming database covering approximately 4,200 children aged 6–16 collected across Vojvodina schools.
Open to: joint projects on digital assessment and adaptive testing platforms; contract research for test development or norming studies; consulting on psychometric instrument validation and standardisation; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on educational technology or HR assessment; student internships in data collection, scoring software testing, or norm table development.
Industry experience: Ranković has provided consulting to two educational publishers in Serbia on the revision of existing cognitive test norms and the reporting of psychometric properties in technical manuals. He has also advised a regional HR services firm on the validation of a reasoning test used in graduate recruitment, reviewing item fit statistics and group fairness analyses.
Notes: Ranković is receptive to collaboration with software and edtech companies working on assessment delivery platforms, particularly those interested in embedding adaptive testing logic or automatic norm-referenced scoring. He prefers projects where the psychometric work is substantive rather than purely advisory. He is currently supervising three doctoral students and has limited capacity for large new commitments until mid-2026.

R0641.title: Branislav Stojanović
R0641.text:
Branislav Stojanović (R0641): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Signal Processing; Data Compression; Computer Engineering.
Keywords: edge computing; lossy compression; adaptive sampling; anomaly detection; resource-constrained devices; IoT sensor nodes; on-device processing; microcontroller; vibration monitoring; energy-efficient algorithms.
Bio: Branislav Stojanović received his Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad in 2001, followed by an M.Sc. in 2004 and a Ph.D. in 2009 from the same institution. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group focuses on signal processing algorithms designed to operate within the severe memory, compute, and energy budgets of microcontroller-class hardware, with particular emphasis on lossy compression schemes that preserve anomaly signatures in sensor streams. He teaches courses on embedded systems, digital signal processing, and real-time operating systems. The group maintains a laboratory equipped with mixed-signal oscilloscopes, logic analysers, a range of ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V development boards, and a small anechoic test chamber for acoustic sensing experiments.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; industrial PhD supervision; consulting; equipment access; student internships.
Industry experience: Stojanović served as a technical consultant to StruktoSens d.o.o. between 2022 and 2024, advising on embedded firmware architecture for their wireless structural monitoring product line. He has also provided paid consultancy on LoRaWAN payload optimisation to two regional agricultural technology startups.
Notes: Stojanović is particularly interested in collaboration with companies working on predictive maintenance, structural monitoring, precision agriculture, or wearable health devices where embedded data reduction is a bottleneck. He is open to co-supervising engineering students placed at NTP companies. His laboratory has spare board-bring-up capacity and can run short contracted benchmarking studies on new microcontroller families.

R0664.title: Jasmina Arsić
R0664.text:
Jasmina Arsić (R0664): Full Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Probability and Mathematical Statistics; Extreme Value Theory; Environmental and Hydrological Risk Analysis; Computational Statistics.
Keywords: copula models; tail dependence; multivariate extreme value theory; quantile estimation; environmental hazards; river discharge; precipitation extremes; risk analysis; vine copulas; threshold exceedance.
Bio: Jasmina Arsić received her BSc and MSc degrees in Mathematics from the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, in 1998 and 2001 respectively, and her PhD in Probability and Statistics from the same institution in 2006, with a dissertation on tail dependence structures in bivariate hydrometeorological series. She joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as an Assistant Professor in 2007, was promoted to Associate Professor in 2013, and to Full Professor in 2019. Her research group focuses on copula families for modelling dependence in correlated environmental hazard variables — precipitation, river discharge, wind speed, temperature extremes — and on multivariate extreme quantile estimation for risk assessment. She teaches Probability Theory, Mathematical Statistics, and Extreme Value Theory at undergraduate and graduate levels. The group makes regular use of the high-performance computing cluster at the Faculty of Sciences and accesses meteorological and hydrological archives maintained by the Hydrometeorological Service of Vojvodina.
Open to: joint projects with companies processing environmental sensor data or operating hydrological infrastructure; contract research on statistical risk modelling for insurance or reinsurance applications; consulting on multivariate return period analysis for engineering design; industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a strong mathematics background; student internships in applied statistics and data analysis.
Industry experience: Arsić carried out a six-month consulting engagement with a regional reinsurance analytics firm in 2020, developing copula-based aggregate loss models for weather-related claims portfolios in the Adriatic–Pannonian region. She has occasionally advised engineering consultancies on the statistical assumptions underlying flood return period calculations for bridge and embankment design submissions.
Notes: Arsić is particularly interested in collaborations that bring access to high-frequency sensor data (IoT weather stations, SCADA systems on water infrastructure) which her group currently lacks. She prefers project partnerships where the mathematical methodology remains within the scope of her group rather than pure data-processing service roles.

R0666.title: Jelena Jokić
R0666.text:
Jelena Jokić (R0666): Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Technical Faculty "Mihajlo Pupin" Zrenjanin, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mechanical Engineering; Structural Health Monitoring; Experimental Mechanics; Non-Destructive Testing.
Keywords: structural health monitoring; modal analysis; welded steel frames; vibration-based damage detection; natural frequency; mode shape; damping ratio; operational modal analysis; weld fatigue; non-destructive evaluation.
Bio: Jelena Jokić received her Diploma in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2005 and her PhD from the same institution in 2012, with a dissertation on modal parameter identification in welded steel structures under operational conditions. She joined the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Technical Faculty 'Mihajlo Pupin' Zrenjanin in 2008 as a teaching assistant and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2018. Her research focuses on vibration-based structural health monitoring, with particular attention to damage detection in welded steel frames through changes in natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping ratios. The group uses a servo-hydraulic testing frame, multichannel data acquisition hardware, and laser vibrometry equipment shared with the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad. She teaches courses in Machine Dynamics and Technical Diagnostics.
Open to: contract research on SHM system deployment and interpretation for industrial clients; consulting on vibration testing and modal analysis of steel structures; equipment access (multichannel DAQ, impact hammer kits, limited SLDV access via Faculty of Technical Sciences); student internships for MSc-level mechanical or civil engineering students; joint project proposals in the area of industrial structural monitoring.
Industry experience: Jokić has carried out two paid measurement campaigns for metalworking companies in the Zrenjanin area, one involving baseline modal testing of a crane girder and one involving post-repair verification of a welded storage frame. She has also provided informal consulting to a fabrication company regarding vibration-related quality control of welded assemblies.
Notes: The faculty is located in Zrenjanin (about 70 km from Novi Sad), so in-person meetings at NTP Novi Sad require advance scheduling. Jokić is open to hosting company representatives at the Zrenjanin lab for demonstrations. She is currently supervising two PhD students and has capacity for one additional collaboration.

R0700.title: Darko Tošić
R0700.text:
Darko Tošić (R0700): Principal Research Fellow, Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Даљинска детекција и ГИС; Хидрометеорологија; Геостатистика; Картографија хазарда.
Keywords: конвективне падавине; фузија података даљинске детекције; радарска метеорологија; геостатистичка интерполација; картирање хазарда; просторно-временска анализа; поплавни ризик; метеоролошки радар; МХСС производи; екстремне падавине.
Bio: Дарко Тошић дипломирао је на Департману за географију, туризам и хотелијерство Универзитета у Новом Саду 2004. године, а докторат из геоинформатике одбранио је на Универзитету у Бечу 2011. године. Од 2012. године запослен је у Истраживачкој групи за даљинску детекцију и ГИС Института БиоСенс, где је 2021. унапређен у звање вишег научног сарадника. Група се бави просторно-временском анализом екстремних метеоролошких догађаја, фузијом вишеизворних података даљинске детекције и геостатистичком интерполацијом падавина. Тошић користи радарске, сателитске и плувиометријске мреже за картирање конвективних олуја високе резолуције. Изводи наставу на мастер студијама БиоСенса и менторише докторанде. Редовно користи опрему лабораторија за обраду хиперспектралних и радарских снимака.
Open to: заједнички пројекти са компанијама из области агро-осигурања и управљања ризиком; уговорна истраживања — QPE производи и картирање хазарда на захтев; консалтинг за процену хазарда екстремних падавина; приступ лабораторијској и теренској опреми (X-band радар, мрежа дистрометара); менторство индустријских докторандуса; студентске праксе у области даљинске детекције и хидрометеорологије.
Industry experience: У периоду 2017–2019. сарађивао је са осигуравајућом кућом Агропрот д.о.о. из Новог Сада на пројекту зонирања премија за градобитно осигурање усева, у оквиру кога су коришћени радарски производи за процену учесталости и интензитета туче на нивоу катастарских парцела.
Notes: Тошић у академској 2025/2026. години има смањено наставно оптерећење због руковођења теренским мерним кампањама у оквиру пројекта FLOODWISE-IPA; доступан је за нове сарадње, али са почетком рада не пре септембра 2025. Посебно заинтересован за сарадњу са компанијама које раде у области прецизне пољопривреде или управљања критичном инфраструктуром, где постоји конкретна потреба за просторним производима падавина.

R0710.title: Uroš Kecman
R0710.text:
Uroš Kecman (R0710): Research Associate, Department of Geography, Tourism and Hotel Management, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: climatology; GIS.
Keywords: drought indices; climate data; spatial analysis.
Bio: Uroš Kecman is a Research Associate at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, affiliated with the Department of Geography, Tourism and Hotel Management. His research focuses on climatology and geographic information systems, with particular emphasis on drought monitoring, climate variability, and spatial analysis of meteorological data across the Pannonian Plain and the broader Balkans region. He works extensively with standardized drought indices and applies GIS-based methodologies to assess long-term climatic trends. Kecman has contributed to regional climate assessments and has collaborated with meteorological institutions across the former Yugoslav space. He is actively seeking opportunities for industrial PhD supervision and joint projects with technology-oriented partners, particularly those involved in environmental monitoring, precision agriculture, or geospatial data services.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0719.title: Miloš Ivanović
R0719.text:
Miloš Ivanović (R0719): PhD student, Department of Materials Engineering, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Materials Science and Engineering; Corrosion Science; Mechanical Testing of Metals; Fractography and Failure Analysis.
Keywords: stress corrosion cracking; hydrogen embrittlement; high-strength fastener steels; slow strain rate testing; fractographic analysis; atmospheric corrosion; hydrogen uptake; grade 10.9 bolts; SCC susceptibility index; industrial environments.
Bio: Miloš Ivanović is a PhD student in the Department of Materials Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, where he enrolled in the doctoral programme in 2022 after completing his master's degree at the same institution. His research focuses on stress corrosion cracking and hydrogen embrittlement of high-strength fastener steels exposed to atmospheric industrial environments, with particular emphasis on slow strain rate testing and post-fracture surface analysis. He works within the Corrosion and Surface Engineering group led by his supervisor, contributing to studies on hydrogen uptake mechanisms and crack initiation in grades 10.9 and 12.9 bolts. He assists in undergraduate laboratory courses on materials testing and corrosion protection. His experimental work is carried out using the group's slow strain rate testing machine, scanning electron microscopy facility, and electrochemical measurement equipment.
Open to: contract research on corrosion testing and failure analysis; equipment access (slow strain rate testing, SEM-EDS, electrochemical permeation); student internships in materials testing and corrosion assessment; joint projects with fastener manufacturers or industrial plant operators.
Industry experience: Ivanović completed a three-month placement at Kovačnica Vojvodina d.o.o. in Zrenjanin in 2023, where he observed production quality control procedures for high-strength bolt steels and collected service-exposed fastener samples for laboratory analysis.
Notes: Currently in the middle stage of his PhD; availability for longer collaborative engagements may depend on thesis submission timeline expected in late 2026. Prefers collaborations that can supply real service-failed fastener samples for comparative fractographic study.

R0727.title: Milutin Đukić
R0727.text:
Milutin Đukić (R0727): Principal Research Fellow, Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Remote Sensing and Earth Observation; Climatology and Agroclimatology; Geographic Information Science; Environmental Modelling.
Keywords: spatial downscaling; geostatistical interpolation; agroclimatic indices; land surface temperature; MODIS; Sentinel-2; kriging; vegetation phenology; crop stress mapping; high-resolution climate grids.
Bio: Milutin Đukić received his BSc in Geography (2003) and MSc in Climatology (2006) from the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, followed by a PhD in Remote Sensing and Environmental Modelling from the same institution in 2012. He joined the BioSense Institute in 2013 as a research associate and was promoted to Principal Research Fellow in 2020. His group focuses on satellite-derived land surface variables, spatial interpolation of climate data, and precision agriculture applications. Đukić teaches a doctoral course on geostatistical methods at the Faculty of Sciences and supervises MSc students. His laboratory work relies on workstations running ENVI and QGIS pipelines, access to Copernicus data infrastructure, and a small cluster used for Monte Carlo cross-validation runs.
Open to: joint projects with agri-tech or precision agriculture companies needing high-resolution climate data products; contract research for spatial downscaling and agroclimatic index derivation; consulting on geostatistical interpolation workflows and sensor network design; student internships (MSc and doctoral level) in remote sensing data processing; equipment and data infrastructure access for external researchers requiring Copernicus-based processing.
Industry experience: Đukić provided a short consultancy engagement in 2021 to a regional irrigation management company advising on the suitability of satellite-derived ET₀ grids as input to their field-level water scheduling tool. He has no extended industry employment history.
Notes: Đukić is open to collaboration involving agronomic end-users but prefers that methodological rigour and publication rights be explicitly agreed before project start. He is not seeking additional administrative coordination roles in the near term, having completed two consecutive coordinator positions.

R0728.title: Anna Čániová
R0728.text:
Anna Čániová (R0728): Research Associate, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Formal Methods; Computer Science Theory; Concurrent and Distributed Systems; Software Engineering.
Keywords: model checking; temporal logic; LTL; CTL; concurrent systems; formal verification; SPIN; Promela; state-space explosion; compositional verification.
Bio: Anna Čániová completed her BSc and MSc in Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2009 and 2011 respectively. She earned her PhD in 2017 from the same institution with a dissertation on compositional model checking of shared-memory concurrent systems. Since 2018 she has held a Research Associate position in the Department of Mathematics and Informatics, where her group focuses on formal methods for verifying correctness properties of concurrent and distributed software, with particular interest in temporal logic specification and automated state-space exploration. She teaches courses in logic for computer science and software verification at undergraduate and master's level. Her group works primarily with SPIN, NuSMV, and the UPPAAL toolchain, and has access to a departmental computing cluster used for large state-space analyses.
Open to: joint research projects with companies developing safety-critical or concurrent software; contract research on formal specification and verification of embedded or industrial control software; student internships for software engineering or computer science students with interest in formal methods; consulting on tool selection and verification workflow design; industrial PhD co-supervision.
Industry experience: During the SAFE-ICS project Čániová worked directly with engineers at two manufacturing SMEs to translate informal safety requirements into verifiable temporal logic specifications, gaining practical experience with PLC programming environments and industrial safety standards. She has also informally advised a Novi Sad-based startup on testing strategy for a concurrent messaging library.
Notes: Čániová is currently supervising two PhD students funded by CONVER, which limits her availability for large new commitments until mid-2025. She has expressed interest in collaborations specifically involving embedded controllers, communication protocols, or any domain where correctness of concurrent behaviour has economic or safety consequences. She prefers engagements that include some research component rather than pure consulting.

R0741.title: Snežana Todorović
R0741.text:
Snežana Todorović (R0741): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Information Retrieval; Distributed Systems; Data Engineering; Machine Learning.
Keywords: full-text indexing; approximate nearest-neighbour search; distributed inverted index; vector search; hybrid retrieval; large-scale document collections; multilingual IR; HNSW; query latency optimisation; index partitioning.
Bio: Snežana Todorović received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2011 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2017, with a thesis on distributed inverted-index structures for heterogeneous document corpora. She held a postdoctoral position at the University of Ljubljana between 2018 and 2019 before returning to Novi Sad as an Assistant Professor. Her group focuses on scalable full-text retrieval, approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search over dense vector embeddings, and hybrid sparse–dense index architectures suited for multilingual and multi-modal document collections. She teaches courses on database systems and information retrieval. The group operates within the Laboratory for Intelligent Data Systems at FTN, where they maintain a small GPU cluster and access shared HPC resources through the PARADOX-IV system.
