Open to: joint projects with companies building internal search or document management systems; contract research on index architecture, ANN search tuning, or hybrid retrieval pipelines; industrial PhD supervision for candidates working on search infrastructure problems; student internships for final-year or master's students; consulting on search system scalability and evaluation methodology.
Industry experience: Between 2011 and 2013, Todorović worked part-time as a backend engineer at a Novi Sad software house building a document archiving platform, where she was responsible for search indexing components. She has since collaborated informally with two local companies on search performance evaluations.
Notes: Todorović is comfortable with projects that require access to sensitive or non-public document collections under appropriate data-sharing agreements. She prefers collaborations where the research question is clearly defined before contracts are signed, and is cautious about engagements that would limit publication rights.

R0750.title: István Lukács
R0750.text:
István Lukács (R0750): Teaching Assistant, Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Industrial and Production Engineering; Operations Research and Optimisation; Supply Chain Management; Decision Analysis under Uncertainty.
Keywords: multi-criteria decision making; supplier selection; supply chain risk; stochastic optimisation; robust optimisation; demand uncertainty; AHP; TOPSIS; Monte Carlo simulation; procurement.
Bio: István Lukács completed his undergraduate studies in Industrial Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2019, followed by a master's degree in Production and Industrial Engineering at the same institution in 2021. He joined the Department of Production Engineering as a Teaching Assistant in 2022, where he is currently pursuing his doctoral research under the supervision of Associate Professor Jelena Borozan. His research focuses on supplier evaluation and selection under demand uncertainty, combining stochastic optimisation models with robust multi-criteria decision-making frameworks to quantify and manage supply chain risk. He contributes to courses in operations management, production planning, and quantitative methods. In his work, he uses standard simulation and optimisation software including MATLAB, Python, and AnyLogic.
Open to: joint projects with companies on supplier evaluation and procurement optimisation; contract research on supply chain risk modelling; student internships involving data collection from industrial partners; consulting on quantitative procurement decision support.
Industry experience: During his master's studies, Lukács completed a four-month internship in the logistics and procurement department of a Novi Sad-based food packaging manufacturer, where he assisted with supplier performance data collection and reporting. He has also conducted structured interviews and data collection at eight Vojvodina SMEs as part of the RISKCHAIN-VS project.
Notes: Lukács is in the second year of his doctoral programme and his availability for external activities is moderate; involvement in larger projects would need to be coordinated with his supervisor. He is particularly interested in collaborations that can provide real industrial datasets for his dissertation work.

R0754.title: Žarko Jakovljević
R0754.text:
Žarko Jakovljević (R0754): Research Associate, Sensors and Microsystems Group, BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems and IoT; Wireless Sensor Networks; Signal Processing and Data Quality; Telecommunications.
Keywords: fault-tolerant sensor nodes; edge diagnostics; low-power wide-area networks; data quality; heterogeneous cellular networks; sensor degradation detection; NB-IoT; remote monitoring; energy harvesting; embedded firmware.
Bio: Žarko Jakovljević received his B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2011 and his Ph.D. in Technical Sciences from the same university in 2018, with a dissertation on fault detection architectures for resource-constrained wireless sensor nodes. Since 2019 he has been a Research Associate in the Sensors and Microsystems Group at the BioSense Institute, where the group develops precision sensing systems for agricultural, environmental, and infrastructure monitoring. His work focuses on hardware and firmware strategies for maintaining data integrity in IoT deployments subject to intermittent cellular connectivity, power fluctuations, and sensor degradation. He contributes to practical courses in embedded systems at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. His primary laboratory tools include network emulation rigs, low-power microcontroller evaluation boards, vector network analysers, and a multi-channel climate chamber for accelerated sensor ageing tests.
Open to: joint projects; contract research; consulting; student internships; equipment access (climate chamber, network emulation rig).
Industry experience: Jakovljević completed a three-month technical secondment in 2022 at Telemetrija d.o.o., a Novi Sad-based company producing remote water-level monitoring systems, where he assisted with NB-IoT modem integration and on-device diagnostic firmware. He has also provided informal consulting to two agricultural technology startups on sensor selection and data validation pipelines.
Notes: Currently principal investigator on an active PROMIS project (DIAQUAL, ending 2026), so capacity for entirely new large-scale commitments is limited until mid-2026; smaller consulting engagements and student co-supervision are feasible. Has expressed interest in working with companies that have existing IoT hardware deployments generating data quality problems, particularly in utilities or infrastructure monitoring, where his diagnostic methods could be adapted beyond agriculture.

R0779.title: Ivona Ostojić
R0779.text:
Ivona Ostojić (R0779): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Mobile and Edge Computing; Internet of Things; Wireless Communications; Energy-Efficient Embedded Systems.
Keywords: mobile edge computing; task offloading; energy harvesting; congestion control; IoT scheduling; dense wireless deployments; latency-energy tradeoff; Lyapunov optimization; heterogeneous networks; resource allocation.
Bio: Ivona Ostojić received her B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2011 and 2013 respectively, and her Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on energy-constrained task scheduling at mobile edge nodes. She spent six months as a visiting researcher at the University of Ljubljana in 2017. Since 2019 she has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. Her group works on task offloading decisions, radio-aware scheduling, and energy harvesting integration for IoT gateway devices in dense deployments. She teaches courses on embedded systems, wireless sensor networks, and real-time operating systems. The group uses a testbed of 40-plus heterogeneous IoT nodes, USRP software-defined radios, and access to the Faculty's edge server cluster.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing IoT gateways or edge inference hardware; contract research on scheduling firmware for energy-harvesting devices; student internships involving embedded systems programming and testbed experiments; consulting on radio-frequency interference assessment for dense sensor deployments; equipment access to IoT testbed and USRP software-defined radio platform.
Industry experience: Between 2013 and 2015, Ostojić worked part-time as an embedded software developer at a Novi Sad-based startup building wireless environmental monitoring equipment, where she implemented MAC-layer duty-cycling firmware for IEEE 802.15.4 nodes.
Notes: Ostojić is currently supervising two Ph.D. students and has limited capacity for entirely new project coordination roles before 2027. She is interested in collaborations with NTP Novi Sad tenants working on smart manufacturing, building automation, or precision agriculture who can provide real deployment environments for testbed-to-field validation studies.

R0837.title: Vukica Arsić
R0837.text:
Vukica Arsić (R0837): Full Professor, Department of Educational Technology, Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Educational Technology; Cognitive Development; Mathematics Education; Learning Sciences.
Keywords: game-based learning; mathematical cognition; late childhood; digital-physical hybrid; quasi-experimental design; arithmetic fluency; educational games; cognitive load; primary school mathematics; intervention evaluation.
Bio: Vukica Arsić completed her undergraduate and master's degrees in pedagogy at the Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2001 and 2004 respectively. She earned her PhD in educational psychology from the University of Novi Sad in 2011, with a dissertation examining arithmetic fluency outcomes under game-mediated instruction. She joined the Faculty of Education in Sombor as an assistant professor in 2012 and was promoted to full professor in 2022. Her research group focuses on experimental and quasi-experimental studies measuring how digital-physical hybrid games affect mathematical cognition in children aged eight to twelve. She teaches courses in educational technology and research methods. The group uses eye-tracking equipment, tablet-based assessment software, and a small instrumented classroom at the Faculty.
Open to: joint projects on learning analytics for educational game platforms; contract research evaluating game-based learning products for school-age children; consulting on experimental design and outcome measurement for educational software companies; student internships for software or game-design students seeking school-based evaluation experience; industrial PhD supervision on adaptive game mechanics and embedded assessment.
Industry experience: Arsić served as an external evaluator for a regional educational publisher developing a tablet-based arithmetic game series in 2020–2021, assessing learning outcomes and recommending revisions to game mechanics based on classroom data.
Notes: Arsić has an established network of primary school contacts in Vojvodina and can facilitate school-based study recruitment relatively quickly. She is particularly interested in collaborating with companies that have a working prototype requiring independent evaluation rather than partners seeking only endorsement. She is not interested in purely software-development roles without an empirical research component.

R0842.title: Péter Szabó
R0842.text:
Péter Szabó (R0842): Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Probability and Mathematical Statistics; Actuarial and Financial Mathematics; Computational Statistics and Bayesian Inference.
Keywords: extreme-value theory; Bayesian actuarial modelling; credibility theory; small-sample inference; heavy-tailed distributions; low-frequency high-severity risk; generalised Pareto distribution; hierarchical Bayesian models; non-life insurance; sparse loss data.
Bio: Péter Szabó studied mathematics at the University of Novi Sad, where he received his BSc in 2007 and MSc in 2009. He completed his PhD at the University of Ljubljana in 2014, with a dissertation on Bayesian credibility models for sparse actuarial loss data. After a postdoctoral year at the University of Debrecen, he returned to Novi Sad in 2016 as a teaching assistant and was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019. His research focuses on extreme-value theory applied to low-frequency, high-severity losses, small-sample Bayesian inference in non-life insurance, and credibility theory. He teaches probability, mathematical statistics, and actuarial mathematics. His group uses the R and Stan computing environments; no dedicated laboratory infrastructure is required.
Open to: contract research on tail risk quantification and extreme-loss modelling; consulting for insurance or reinsurance companies on Bayesian reserving and capital modelling; industrial PhD supervision for candidates placed at NTP companies with actuarial or risk analytics activities; joint grant applications in applied statistics and insurance mathematics; student internships for data science or actuarial-track students.
Industry experience: Szabó provided consultancy to a regional reinsurance brokerage in Novi Sad during 2018–2019, assisting with internal model validation under Solvency II for a small non-life insurer. He has no ongoing commercial positions.
Notes: Szabó reads and writes Serbian, Hungarian, English, and Slovenian. He is interested in problems from companies dealing with low-frequency operational or environmental risk, not only insurance firms. He has moderate teaching and administrative load and can commit meaningful time to a new collaboration.

R0859.title: Milan Sabo
R0859.text:
Milan Sabo (R0859): Assistant Professor, Department of Industrial Engineering and Management, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Industrial Engineering; Environmental Engineering; Life-Cycle Assessment; Sustainable Manufacturing.
Keywords: life-cycle assessment; carbon footprint; ISO 14064; ISO 14067; discrete manufacturing; energy intensity; environmental performance reporting; product carbon footprint; greenhouse gas accounting; eco-efficiency.
Bio: Milan Sabo received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Industrial Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2011 respectively, and completed his Ph.D. at the same institution in 2017 with a thesis on carbon footprint quantification methods for metal-forming processes. He was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019. His research group focuses on life-cycle assessment of discrete manufacturing systems, energy-intensity benchmarking, and environmental performance reporting aligned with ISO 14064 and product carbon footprint standards such as PAS 2050 and ISO 14067. He teaches courses in Environmental Management Systems and Industrial Ecology. The group uses a dedicated LCA workstation suite (SimaPro licence, ecoinvent database), energy monitoring hardware deployed on production lines, and the faculty's material testing laboratory for process data collection.
Open to: joint projects with NTP Novi Sad companies requiring carbon footprint quantification or ISO 14064/14067 compliance support; contract research for LCA studies and GHG inventory development; industry PhD supervision for candidates employed at manufacturing companies; consulting on CBAM reporting and supplier emission data collection; student internships in companies willing to host LCA data collection work; access to SimaPro/ecoinvent licences and energy monitoring hardware for collaborative measurement campaigns.
Industry experience: Between 2017 and 2019 Sabo worked part-time as an environmental consultant for a Novi Sad-based engineering services firm, conducting ISO 14001 gap analyses and initial GHG inventories for four manufacturing clients. He has since maintained informal advisory relationships with two of those clients.
Notes: Sabo is the primary SimaPro licence administrator for the department; companies collaborating with his group can access the software under a shared-use agreement. He prefers projects where primary production-floor data collection is feasible, rather than studies relying entirely on generic database factors.

R0905.title: Filip Mijatović
R0905.text:
Filip Mijatović (R0905): Assistant Professor, Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Microelectronics and mixed-signal circuit design; Wireless sensor networks and embedded systems; Biomedical instrumentation; Low-power communication protocols.
Keywords: ultra-low-power design; body-area networks; mixed-signal CMOS; biopotential acquisition; duty-cycled MAC; energy harvesting; sub-threshold circuits; wireless health monitoring; impedance spectroscopy; biomedical sampling constraints.
Bio: Filip Mijatović received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Electronics and Telecommunications from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2009 and 2012 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2018, with a thesis on duty-cycled MAC protocols for implantable sensor nodes. He spent fourteen months as a visiting researcher at the Graz University of Technology between 2016 and 2017. Since 2019 he has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications. His group focuses on mixed-signal front-end circuits operating below 1 µA average current, low-noise amplifier topologies for biopotential acquisition, and link-layer scheduling algorithms that respect biomedical sampling timing constraints. He teaches undergraduate analogue electronics and graduate wireless sensor systems. The group uses a Cadence Virtuoso IC design suite, a Keysight parametric analyser, and a small anechoic chamber shared with the antenna laboratory.
Open to: joint projects with medical device companies; contract research on mixed-signal front-end design; industrial PhD supervision; student internships (M.Sc. level, hardware-oriented); consulting on BLE and 802.15.4 protocol configuration for biomedical products; access to Cadence Virtuoso design suite for short collaborative visits.
Industry experience: Between 2012 and 2014, Mijatović worked part-time as a hardware design consultant for a Novi Sad-based startup developing Bluetooth-connected pulse oximetry accessories, contributing to the analogue signal chain and firmware of their first product revision.
Notes: Mijatović is currently supervising two doctoral candidates and has limited bandwidth for large new commitments before mid-2025. He has expressed interest in applied problems from companies developing wearable or implantable devices, particularly where circuit-level co-design with protocol optimisation is relevant. He is cautious about projects requiring significant regulatory or clinical-trial management, which is outside his team's expertise.

R0906.title: Maja Popović
R0906.text:
Maja Popović (R0906): Associate Professor, Department of Biomedical Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: biomedical signal processing; wearables.
Keywords: ECG; atrial fibrillation; arrhythmia detection; false alarms; accelerometer.
Bio: Maja Popović is an Associate Professor in the Department of Biomedical Engineering at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. Her research focuses on biomedical signal processing and wearable sensing systems, with a particular emphasis on cardiac monitoring, arrhythmia detection, and the reduction of false alarms in ambulatory ECG devices. She develops embedded signal-processing algorithms suitable for deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers and wearable patch sensors. Professor Popović leads the HEARTWATCH project, which investigates remote cardiac monitoring solutions for long-term atrial fibrillation screening. She has authored multiple peer-reviewed publications on ECG classification, motion-artifact suppression, and accelerometer-based activity recognition. She is actively seeking industrial PhD co-supervision arrangements and joint applied research projects with technology companies.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0920.title: Filip Urošević
R0920.text:
Filip Urošević (R0920): Full Professor, Department of Production Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Manufacturing and Machining Technology; Tribology and Surface Engineering; Materials Characterisation; Production Engineering.
Keywords: PVD coatings; cemented carbide; cutting insert wear; dry turning; TiAlN coating; flank wear; crater wear; high-speed machining; tribology; SEM/EDS wear analysis.
Bio: Filip Urošević received his Dipl.Ing. degree in Production Engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and his PhD from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on adhesive and abrasive wear in coated carbide tooling. He was appointed Full Professor in 2019. His research group focuses on tribological characterisation of PVD-coated cutting inserts—primarily TiAlN, TiSiN, and CrAlN variants—tested under high-speed dry turning of hardened steels and cast irons. Ongoing work examines coating delamination mechanisms, crater and flank wear progression, and the role of substrate surface preparation on coating adhesion. Teaching covers manufacturing technology, machining processes, and tribology at both undergraduate and master level. The group operates a tribometer laboratory and a metallographic preparation suite, with access to SEM/EDS and XRD facilities within the Faculty.
Open to: contract research on coating selection and wear testing for industrial cutting tool applications; joint projects with tool manufacturers or automotive component producers; consulting on PVD coating specification and tribological qualification testing; equipment access (tribometer, SEM/EDS, profilometry) for industrial partners; industrial PhD supervision on wear characterisation topics; student internships in machining and surface characterisation laboratory.
Industry experience: Urošević has conducted contract wear testing and coating evaluation for two regional cutting tool distributors and one automotive castings manufacturer over the past six years, with results reported as confidential technical reports.
Notes: Prefers long-term engagements over single one-off tests; the tribometer and SEM are shared with two other research groups so scheduling lead time is typically four to six weeks. No sabbatical planned before 2027.

R0925.title: Milan Petrović
R0925.text:
Milan Petrović (R0925): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: natural language processing; machine learning.
Keywords: transformer models; Serbian language; retrieval; embeddings; question answering.
Bio: Milan Petrović is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad. His research focuses on natural language processing and machine learning, with a particular emphasis on transformer-based language models and low-resource NLP for Serbian. He works on building open language resources for Serbian, including pre-trained models, annotated corpora, and evaluation benchmarks. His recent work addresses dense retrieval, question answering, and the challenges of processing text in both Latin and Cyrillic scripts within a unified embedding space. He collaborates with regional and international partners and is actively involved in the SRB-NLP initiative under the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia. He is open to industrial PhD supervision and joint research projects with companies seeking NLP solutions.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R0992.title: Đorđe Vukelić
R0992.text:
Đorđe Vukelić (R0992): Associate Professor, Department of Applied and Engineering Chemistry, Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Chemical and Process Engineering; Biomass and Bioenergy; Materials Characterisation; Agricultural and Environmental Chemistry.
Keywords: pyrolysis kinetics; lignocellulosic biomass; biochar characterisation; thermogravimetric analysis; temperature–residence-time optimisation; agricultural residues; thermochemical conversion; biochar agronomic certification; activation energy; fixed-bed reactor.
Bio: Đorđe Vukelić completed his undergraduate and master's studies in Chemical Engineering at the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. He received his PhD in 2012 from the same institution, with a dissertation on pyrolysis kinetics of agricultural residues common to Vojvodina. After a postdoctoral period at the University of Ljubljana (2013–2014), he returned to Novi Sad as Assistant Professor and was promoted to Associate Professor in 2019. His group focuses on thermochemical conversion of lignocellulosic biomass—particularly sunflower husks, corn stover, and wheat straw—studying pyrolysis kinetics, reactor temperature–residence-time optimisation, and physicochemical characterisation of biochar for agronomic use. He teaches courses in physical chemistry and industrial thermochemistry. The laboratory is equipped with a TGA-DSC coupled analyser, a fixed-bed tube furnace reactor (up to 1100 °C), BET surface area apparatus, and FTIR and Raman spectrometers.
Open to: contract research on biochar production optimisation and characterisation; consulting on pyrolysis process design and biochar quality assurance; equipment access (TGA-DSC, fixed-bed reactor, BET, FTIR, Raman); joint project applications (industry or EU funding); industrial PhD supervision; student internships.
Industry experience: Vukelić has worked on a short-term industry contract with Agrokompleks Vojvodine d.o.o. to evaluate the technical feasibility of integrating a small-scale pyrolysis unit into their sunflower processing facility. He has also provided informal consulting to two smaller agricultural cooperatives in Bačka on biochar procurement criteria.
Notes: Vukelić is currently committed at roughly 0.8 FTE research capacity due to PYROLINK obligations and a full teaching load; prospective partners should plan accordingly. He prefers collaborations with a concrete experimental component and is cautious about engagements that are primarily desktop or regulatory in nature. His PhD student graduating in 2026 may be available for direct hire by an industrial partner thereafter.

R0995.title: Veljko Pantelić
R0995.text:
Veljko Pantelić (R0995): Assistant Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Software Engineering; Industrial Automation; Model-Driven Engineering; Programming Languages and Compilers.
Keywords: IEC 61131-3; model-driven engineering; software product lines; domain-specific languages; code generation; PLC programming; metamodeling; feature models; model transformation; Structured Text.
Bio: Veljko Pantelić received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computing and Control Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2010 and 2013 respectively, and his Ph.D. from the same institution in 2019. His doctoral work focused on metamodel-driven code generation pipelines targeting IEC 61131-3 Structured Text for programmable logic controllers. Since 2020 he has held an Assistant Professor position in the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. His research group investigates domain-specific language design, model transformation chains, and software product-line variability management for industrial automation software. He teaches courses in software engineering, formal languages, and industrial programming. The group uses Eclipse Modeling Framework, Xtext, Sirius, and a small PLC laboratory equipped with several Wago and Beckhoff controllers for validation experiments.
Open to: joint projects with automation software companies; contract research on PLC code generation tooling; industrial PhD supervision; student internships in PLC software tooling development; consulting on DSL design for industrial automation; equipment access to PLC laboratory for partner validation experiments.
Industry experience: During 2013–2015 Pantelić worked part-time as a software engineer at a Novi Sad-based automation integrator, where he developed IEC 61131-3 programs for conveyor and palletiser systems; this experience directly motivated his research focus on maintainability and variability in PLC codebases.
Notes: Pantelić is particularly interested in partnerships with NTP companies developing configurable or product-line-structured automation equipment, especially where legacy code migration is a concern. He has limited availability for consulting engagements during the spring semester due to teaching load but is flexible in summer and autumn.

R1006.title: Danilo Mitrović
R1006.text:
Danilo Mitrović (R1006): Assistant Professor, Department of Mathematics and Informatics, Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Educational Data Mining; Learning Analytics; Applied Statistics; Machine Learning.
Keywords: clickstream analysis; longitudinal data modelling; competency prediction; learning management systems; survival analysis; hidden Markov models; sequence mining; student performance; Moodle log data; feature engineering.
Bio: Danilo Mitrović completed his BSc and MSc in Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Novi Sad (2006, 2009), followed by a PhD in Applied Mathematics with a focus on statistical learning models at the same institution (2015). He joined the Department of Mathematics and Informatics as a Teaching Assistant in 2010 and was promoted to Assistant Professor in 2016. His research centres on educational data mining and learning analytics, with particular emphasis on modelling longitudinal clickstream sequences from learning management systems to predict student competency outcomes. The group regularly analyses event-log datasets from the university's Moodle deployment and collaborates with the department's Statistical Computing Laboratory, which maintains standard HPC cluster access. He teaches courses in probability, statistics, and data analysis at undergraduate and graduate level.
Open to: joint projects with companies using internal learning or training data; contract research on employee skill-gap analysis or workforce competency tracking; consulting on statistical model design for HR analytics or e-learning platforms; student internships involving data engineering or analysis on LMS log data; co-supervision of industrial PhD candidates working on applied learning analytics.
Industry experience: Mitrović completed a four-month consultancy engagement in 2022 with an e-learning content provider based in Novi Sad, advising on the design of a learner progress scoring system for their corporate training platform. He has no other sustained industry roles.
Notes: Mitrović is on a reduced teaching load in the 2025–2026 academic year due to the active CROSSLEARN project obligations, which leaves limited capacity for additional large commitments before mid-2026. He has expressed interest in problems involving sparse or irregularly sampled longitudinal data, which are common in industrial training contexts but underrepresented in academic educational data mining literature.

R1008.title: Krisztina Kiss
R1008.text:
Krisztina Kiss (R1008): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Industrial cybersecurity; Network traffic analysis; Machine learning and statistical modelling; Industrial control systems.
Keywords: anomaly detection; one-class classification; industrial control systems; SCADA security; statistical baseline modelling; Modbus; DNP3; unsupervised learning; network intrusion detection; protocol traffic analysis.
Bio: Krisztina Kiss received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and her PhD in electrical and computer engineering from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on statistical traffic profiling in industrial Ethernet networks. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2009 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for industrial control system protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling, kernel methods, and lightweight online learning algorithms suited to constrained embedded environments. She teaches courses on network security, operating systems, and industrial communication protocols. The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
Open to: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions; contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment; industrial PhD supervision for candidates from companies in automation and critical infrastructure; student internships on ICS testbed experiments and dataset collection; consulting on detector calibration, evaluation methodology, and deployment architecture for industrial networks; access to ICS testbed and long-term traffic capture infrastructure for collaborative experiments.
Industry experience: Kiss has collaborated with a regional energy distributor and a water utility as monitoring data partners on two funded projects, providing practical validation of research methods on operational infrastructure. She has carried out paid consulting for a mid-size automation integrator on specifying anomaly detection requirements for a SCADA upgrade project.
Notes: Kiss prefers applied collaborations that result in deployment on real infrastructure rather than purely synthetic experiments. Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement. She is particularly interested in partners dealing with proprietary or undocumented ICS protocols, which represent a gap in her current work.

R1015.title: Vuk Đukić
R1015.text:
Vuk Đukić (R1015): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: cybersecurity; network security.
Keywords: intrusion detection; industrial control systems; anomaly detection; IoT security; threat modelling.
Bio: Vuk Đukić is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, within the Department of Computing and Control Engineering. His research focuses on cybersecurity and network security, with particular emphasis on intrusion detection, anomaly detection in industrial control systems, IoT security, and threat modelling. He has led and contributed to multiple national and international research initiatives aimed at securing critical infrastructure and smart environments. Professor Đukić has published in reputable journals and conferences and is actively involved in interdisciplinary collaboration with industry. He is open to supervising industrial PhD students and engaging in joint research projects with technology companies seeking expertise in operational technology security and advanced threat analysis.
Open to: industrial PhD supervision; joint projects.

R1020.title: Predrag Nedić
R1020.text:
Predrag Nedić (R1020): Full Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Distributed Systems; Data Engineering; Parallel and High-Performance Computing; Cloud Computing.
Keywords: stream processing; distributed join algorithms; real-time data reconciliation; Apache Flink; cloud-native infrastructure; latency optimisation; multi-source data fusion; backpressure management; event-time windowing; data parallelism.
Bio: Predrag Nedić received his Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 1999, followed by his M.Sc. in 2003 and Ph.D. in 2009 from the same institution, with a doctoral thesis on partitioned stream join scheduling under variable data arrival rates. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2010 and was promoted to full professor in 2021. His research group focuses on distributed stream processing systems, parallel join algorithms, latency-sensitive data pipelines, and cloud-native deployment of real-time analytics workloads. He teaches courses on distributed systems, database internals, and parallel computing. The group operates a local cluster of 24 nodes running Apache Flink and Kafka workloads and maintains access to cloud testbeds through institutional agreements.
Open to: joint research projects with companies processing high-volume event or sensor data; contract research on stream pipeline architecture and performance tuning; industrial PhD supervision for candidates employed at NTP Novi Sad companies; student internships involving hands-on work with Flink or Kafka deployments; consulting on cloud-native data infrastructure design and latency diagnostics; equipment access to the group's 24-node Flink/Kafka cluster for joint experiments.
Industry experience: Nedić provided technical consultancy to a regional logistics software company between 2016 and 2018, advising on the migration of their batch reconciliation workflows to a near-real-time Kafka-based pipeline. He has also delivered internal training workshops on stream processing fundamentals for engineering teams at two technology companies in Novi Sad.
Notes: Nedić is particularly interested in partnerships with companies that have concrete latency or throughput problems in existing data pipelines rather than greenfield platform builds. He prefers collaborations that include access to real (anonymised) operational data for benchmarking. He is not currently on sabbatical and carries a moderate teaching load of two courses per semester.

R1022.title: Milutin Paunović
R1022.text:
Milutin Paunović (R1022): Associate Professor, Department of Computing and Control Engineering, Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
Fields: Embedded Systems Software Engineering; Formal Methods and Verification; Real-Time and Concurrent Systems; Software Maintenance and Refactoring.
Keywords: interrupt-driven firmware; model checking; static analysis; data race detection; real-time systems; safety-critical software; legacy C code refactoring; resource-constrained microcontrollers; concurrent embedded software; formal verification.
Bio: Milutin Paunović received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in Computing and Control Engineering from the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, in 2003 and 2006 respectively, and his Ph.D. in 2012 from the same institution, with a thesis on static data-race detection in interrupt-driven embedded firmware. He joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2013 and was promoted to associate professor in 2018. His research group focuses on formal verification of real-time firmware, static and dynamic analysis of concurrent embedded software, and refactoring techniques for safety-relevant C codebases on microcontrollers with severe memory and timing constraints. He teaches courses in embedded systems programming, software verification, and real-time operating systems. The group operates a laboratory equipped with ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V development boards, JTAG trace units, and licensed model-checking toolchains.
Open to: joint projects with companies developing safety-relevant embedded firmware; contract research on static analysis tooling and MISRA-C compliance; industrial PhD supervision for engineers working on embedded software verification; consulting on firmware refactoring and formal verification methodology; student internships for final-year and master's students in embedded software; equipment access (ARM Cortex-M and RISC-V development boards, JTAG trace units).
Industry experience: Paunović collaborated with a Novi Sad-based automotive electronics supplier during the SAFE-MIGRATE project, providing hands-on refactoring support for a production motor-controller firmware codebase. He has given two invited technical training sessions for embedded-software engineers at companies in the Science Technology Park Novi Sad.
Notes: Paunović is particularly interested in collaborations where access to real production firmware codebases is possible, even under NDA; academic benchmark firmware is a poor substitute for evaluating refactoring and verification tools. He is not seeking collaborations primarily oriented toward hardware design. Teaching load is moderate and he can accommodate one new PhD student starting in 2026.

SYN-PAT-009.title: Method and Device for Anomaly-Preserving Adaptive Bit Allocation in Compressed Sensor Data Streams
SYN-PAT-009.text:
Method and Device for Anomaly-Preserving Adaptive Bit Allocation in Compressed Sensor Data Streams (2023, pending).
Inventors: Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
A method for compressing sensor data streams on resource-constrained embedded processors wherein a CUSUM-based detector flags anomalous signal segments in real time and a bit allocator redistributes the saved bits from normal segments to flagged segments within a fixed per-frame bit budget. The device comprises a microcontroller executing the detector and allocator in under 15 CPU cycles per sample and a non-volatile memory unit storing compressed output. The method preserves signal peaks associated with mechanical fault events at compression ratios where conventional uniform-bit-rate coders suppress such peaks below detection threshold.

SYN-PAT-013.title: Embedded Gateway Device for Bidirectional Protocol Translation Between ISO 11783 and CANopen Networks with Run-Time Configurable Mapping Tables
SYN-PAT-013.text:
Embedded Gateway Device for Bidirectional Protocol Translation Between ISO 11783 and CANopen Networks with Run-Time Configurable Mapping Tables (2023, pending).
Inventors: Darko Zarić (R0248).
The device is a dual-CAN embedded module containing firmware that translates process-data objects between an ISO 11783 ISOBUS network and a CANopen DS4xx device network. Mapping tables defining the correspondence between ISOBUS DDIs and CANopen object dictionary indices are stored in non-volatile flash and can be updated over the ISOBUS virtual terminal interface without reflashing the device. The architecture supports simultaneous operation on both networks at different baud rates and provides a watchdog-supervised fail-safe state that places the ISOBUS segment in a passive listening mode if the CANopen side loses heartbeat continuity. Filed with the Intellectual Property Office of the Republic of Serbia.

SYN-PAT-018.title: Circuit and method for electrode-offset cancellation in a capacitively coupled biopotential amplifier with sub-nanoampere DC servo current
SYN-PAT-018.text:
Circuit and method for electrode-offset cancellation in a capacitively coupled biopotential amplifier with sub-nanoampere DC servo current (2022, granted).
Inventors: Filip Mijatović (R0905).
The invention covers a DC servo loop architecture for use in capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifiers intended for wearable biopotential acquisition. The loop uses a switched-capacitor integrator clocked at 8 Hz to sense residual offset at the output and apply a correction current at the input through a high-impedance current DAC, keeping total servo current below 20 nA. The approach tolerates electrode polarisation offsets up to ±400 mV without saturating the main amplifier chain. The patent was filed in Serbia through the Intellectual Property Office and subsequently extended via PCT.

SYN-PAT-033.title: Process for producing certified-grade biochar from sunflower husk by controlled slow pyrolysis with integrated temperature–residence-time feedback
SYN-PAT-033.text:
Process for producing certified-grade biochar from sunflower husk by controlled slow pyrolysis with integrated temperature–residence-time feedback (2021, granted).
Inventors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992).
A process for producing biochar from sunflower husk feedstock meeting European Biochar Certificate Basic grade specifications. The process comprises pre-drying to below 10 wt% moisture, staged heating at 8–12 K min⁻¹ to a final temperature of 580–640 °C in a fixed-bed tube reactor under inert gas, and an isothermal holding step of 55–80 minutes controlled by a thermocouple-feedback loop. Biochar discharged from the reactor is passivated by controlled air admission. The specification covers reactor geometry constraints and acceptable feedstock particle size range (0.3–1.2 mm). Assigned to the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.

SYN-PAT-034.title: Method and circuit arrangement for tiered watchdog supervision of multi-peripheral embedded sensor nodes
SYN-PAT-034.text:
Method and circuit arrangement for tiered watchdog supervision of multi-peripheral embedded sensor nodes (2021, granted).
Inventors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754).
A hardware and firmware arrangement for supervising the operational state of embedded sensor nodes carrying multiple independent peripheral subsystems. The arrangement uses three independently clocked watchdog timers assigned to distinct supervision layers: the main application scheduler, the wireless communication driver, and the analog measurement front-end. Each timer triggers a graduated recovery response specific to its layer, avoiding a full device reset unless lower-tier recovery fails within a defined window. The arrangement reduces unnecessary measurement gaps caused by full resets and is suitable for implementation on standard microcontroller platforms without additional external components. Granted by the Intellectual Property Office of the Republic of Serbia.

SYN-PAT-040.title: Passive EMC Input Filter Assembly with Temperature-Compensated Y-Capacitor Array for Variable-Speed Drive Applications
SYN-PAT-040.text:
Passive EMC Input Filter Assembly with Temperature-Compensated Y-Capacitor Array for Variable-Speed Drive Applications (2020, granted).
Inventors: Ana Mamužić (R0283).
An EMC input filter assembly for three-phase variable-speed drives incorporates a Y-capacitor array in which each capacitor cell is paired with a negative-temperature-coefficient compensation network. The compensation network maintains effective CM capacitance within ±5% of nominal across the operating temperature range −10 °C to +85 °C, preventing the insertion-loss degradation observed in standard film capacitor designs at elevated cabinet temperatures. The assembly is rated for 400 V AC, 32 A continuous, and fits within the footprint of a standard 15 kW drive input terminal block. Patent granted by the Intellectual Property Office of the Republic of Serbia.

SYN-PAT-043.title: Reconfigurable Fault Injection Board for Automotive ECU I/O Lines with Solid-State Relay Matrix and Microcontroller Interface
SYN-PAT-043.text:
Reconfigurable Fault Injection Board for Automotive ECU I/O Lines with Solid-State Relay Matrix and Microcontroller Interface (2020, granted).
Inventors: Darko Ninkov (R0356).
A hardware board comprising a matrix of solid-state relays arranged to selectively connect any of up to 32 ECU I/O lines to open-circuit, battery voltage, or ground conditions under software control. A microcontroller receives fault commands over a standard serial interface and drives the relay gates within a guaranteed 2 ms switching latency. The board includes overcurrent protection on each channel and a watchdog that returns all channels to a safe default state if the host controller fails to send a heartbeat within a configurable timeout. The design targets low-cost laboratory HiL bench applications.

SYN-PAT-044.title: Method and Circuit Arrangement for Adaptive Threshold-Triggered Vibration Data Acquisition on Low-Power Microcontroller Platforms
SYN-PAT-044.text:
Method and Circuit Arrangement for Adaptive Threshold-Triggered Vibration Data Acquisition on Low-Power Microcontroller Platforms (2022, granted).
Inventors: Vesna Knežević (R0206).
The patent covers a hardware-software method in which an analogue comparator on a microcontroller's input pin monitors a running RMS estimate of an accelerometer signal and triggers a DMA burst acquisition only when the estimate exceeds a configurable threshold stored in non-volatile memory. The threshold may be updated by a host application over UART or BLE without reflashing firmware. The arrangement reduces idle current draw by 55–70% compared to continuous DMA acquisition in laboratory measurements on an STM32L4 platform. The patent is assigned to the University of Novi Sad.

SYN-PAT-055.title: Method and Device for In-Process Springback Compensation in CNC Press-Brake Bending by Iterative Punch Re-Strike with Optical Angle Feedback
SYN-PAT-055.text:
Method and Device for In-Process Springback Compensation in CNC Press-Brake Bending by Iterative Punch Re-Strike with Optical Angle Feedback (2022, granted).
Inventors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308).
The invention relates to a method for compensating springback in air-bending operations performed on a CNC hydraulic press-brake. An optical angle sensor measures the bend angle at the moment of punch retraction. If the measured angle deviates from the target by more than a preset threshold, the controller calculates a corrective punch-depth increment using a preloaded surrogate model and executes one or more re-strike sub-strokes within the same machine cycle. The device includes a sensor mounting bracket compatible with standard European V-die tooling systems and a controller interface module. The method is claimed for ferrous and non-ferrous sheet materials in the thickness range 0.5 mm to 6.0 mm.

SYN-PRJ-0009.title: SRB-NLP: open language resources for Serbian
SYN-PRJ-0009.text:
SRB-NLP: open language resources for Serbian (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0925 researcher.
The SRB-NLP project aims to build a comprehensive suite of open language resources for Serbian, addressing a long-standing gap in the NLP ecosystem for South Slavic languages. The project encompasses the creation of large pre-training corpora, fine-tuning datasets for core NLP tasks including named entity recognition, question answering, semantic similarity, and intent detection, as well as the training and public release of transformer-based language models tailored to Serbian. A central objective is ensuring that all resources support both Latin and Cyrillic scripts on equal footing. The project also includes the design and dissemination of standardised evaluation benchmarks to enable reproducible comparison of future Serbian NLP systems. Running from 2023 to 2026 with funding from the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, the project involves collaboration between linguists and computer scientists and is committed to open science through the public release of all data, model weights, and code.

SYN-PRJ-0011.title: VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs
SYN-PRJ-0011.text:
VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs (Innovation Fund, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0548 academic partner.
VISIONQC aims to bring AI-powered quality control capabilities within reach of small and medium enterprises that lack the data infrastructure and machine learning expertise of large manufacturers. The project develops a modular inspection platform combining few-shot defect detection, synthetic data augmentation, and edge-deployable quantized models, enabling SMEs to configure reliable inspection pipelines with minimal labeled data and without cloud dependency. As academic partner, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation, ensuring that research outputs are translated into production-ready components. Pilot deployments are conducted at two regional manufacturing SMEs producing metal and polymer components, with key performance indicators targeting detection accuracy above 90% and setup time under two working days per new product type. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund (synthetic) program.

SYN-PRJ-0014.title: HEARTWATCH: remote cardiac monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0014.text:
HEARTWATCH: remote cardiac monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0906 principal investigator.
HEARTWATCH is a three-year research project funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, running from 2022 to 2025, with Associate Professor Maja Popović serving as principal investigator. The project addresses the clinical need for reliable, long-term remote cardiac monitoring outside hospital settings, targeting particularly the early detection of atrial fibrillation in high-risk populations. The core technical objective is the development of a complete algorithmic stack—spanning signal quality assessment, motion-artifact suppression, real-time arrhythmia classification, and adaptive false-alarm reduction—capable of executing on a low-power wearable ECG patch. A secondary objective is the creation of a clinically annotated benchmark dataset in partnership with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. By project completion, HEARTWATCH aims to deliver open-source firmware validated in a prospective pilot study involving at least 120 participants, providing a translational foundation for commercialization through collaboration with medical device companies.

SYN-PRJ-0017.title: SECURE-ICS: security monitoring for factories
SYN-PRJ-0017.text:
SECURE-ICS: security monitoring for factories (Innovation Fund, 2023–2025).
Participants: R1015 academic partner.
SECURE-ICS addresses the growing need for robust cybersecurity monitoring in industrial manufacturing environments. The project develops an integrated security monitoring platform tailored specifically to factory automation systems, encompassing network traffic analysis, anomaly detection, and real-time alerting for operational technology networks. As academic partner, the University of Novi Sad team led by Professor Đukić contributes expertise in intrusion detection algorithm design, threat modelling for ICS environments, and evaluation methodology. The platform targets Modbus, PROFINET, and EtherNet/IP protocol stacks commonly found in Serbian manufacturing facilities. Deliverables include a deployable monitoring agent, a validated anomaly detection model trained on representative factory traffic, and a set of security assessment guidelines for small and medium enterprises in the industrial sector. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund programme.

SYN-PRJ-0038.title: Vibration Fatigue Assessment Framework for Welded Structures in Agricultural Machinery
SYN-PRJ-0038.text:
VIBROAG: Vibration Fatigue Assessment Framework for Welded Structures in Agricultural Machinery (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0399 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac; Agrotech Solutions d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project developed and experimentally validated a standardised frequency-domain fatigue assessment framework for welded steel structures used in agricultural machinery, where vibration loading from field operation is the dominant fatigue driver. The work involved field measurement campaigns on operating combine harvesters and balers, laboratory fatigue testing of welded specimens under stationary and non-stationary random loading, and implementation of the assessment procedure in a semi-automated Python toolchain interfacing with commercial FE solvers. A database of in-service PSD profiles for four machinery classes was compiled. The framework was demonstrated on three industrial case-study structures, with predicted lives compared against fleet service data. Two Master's theses and one PhD thesis are being completed within the project.

SYN-PRJ-0039.title: Dynamic Characterisation of Bolted and Press-Fit Joints in Power Transmission Systems
SYN-PRJ-0039.text:
DYNOJOINT: Dynamic Characterisation of Bolted and Press-Fit Joints in Power Transmission Systems (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2019–2021).
Participants: R0399 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
This project investigated the dynamic properties—stiffness, damping, and nonlinear force–displacement behaviour—of bolted flange connections and interference-fit assemblies encountered in industrial gearboxes and shafts. Experimental characterisation was carried out on purpose-built test rigs allowing independent control of preload and interface surface finish. Measured joint properties were incorporated into reduced-order finite-element models. The effect of joint property uncertainties on predicted resonance frequencies and vibration fatigue lives was quantified by Monte Carlo simulation. The project produced a set of experimentally grounded joint modelling recommendations for use in frequency-domain structural analyses.

SYN-PRJ-0045.title: Multilingual Document Reconciliation for Cross-Border Administrative Interoperability in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0045.text:
MULTIREC: Multilingual Document Reconciliation for Cross-Border Administrative Interoperability in the Western Balkans (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0524 principal investigator.
Partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences; West University of Timișoara, Department of Computer Science; University of Debrecen, Faculty of Informatics; Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina.
MULTIREC addresses the practical problem of reconciling structured administrative documents exchanged between Serbian public institutions and their counterparts in Hungary and Romania, where records are maintained in different languages and schema vocabularies. The project builds on transformer-based cross-lingual semantic similarity to develop automated field-mapping and value-reconciliation tools. Activities include corpus construction (legal, cadastral, and civil registration document pairs), development and evaluation of the DocAlign-ML framework, and a pilot deployment in cooperation with a regional administrative body. The project involves four partners across three countries and has produced six peer-reviewed publications, two open-source software libraries, and training materials for public-sector data managers.

SYN-PRJ-0046.title: NLP Tools for Multilingual e-Government Document Exchange in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0046.text:
NLPADMIN-IPA: NLP Tools for Multilingual e-Government Document Exchange in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0524 work package leader.
Partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences; University of Pécs, Department of Linguistics; Municipality of Subotica; Csongrád-Csanád County Government; Chamber of Commerce of Southern Transdanubia.
This Interreg project targets the digitisation and linguistic harmonisation of administrative document workflows in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border area, where a large Hungarian-speaking minority creates demand for bilingual public services. The University of Novi Sad team leads the NLP tools development work package, which covers named-entity alignment, form-field translation, and automated consistency checking for bilingual document pairs. The project partners include municipalities, a regional chamber of commerce, and two universities. Deliverables include a web-based bilingual document assistant, a shared terminological database covering civil administration and land registry domains, and a report on user acceptance among public servants.

SYN-PRJ-0076.title: Diagnostic Inference from Behavioural Trace Data in Digital Learning Environments
SYN-PRJ-0076.text:
DIAGTRACE: Diagnostic Inference from Behavioural Trace Data in Digital Learning Environments (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0322 principal investigator.
Partners: Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade, Serbia; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia.
The project developed and validated psychometric and statistical methods for inferring cognitive skill states from the behavioural trace data produced by digital learning platforms, specifically focusing on contexts where traditional item-level ground-truth labels are unavailable or unreliable. Research activities included simulation studies of model identifiability, empirical calibration studies in Serbian primary and secondary schools, and the development of an open-source R package for label-free knowledge tracing. A pilot deployment in six schools in Vojvodina tested the pipeline end-to-end. The project involved collaboration with the Institute for Educational Research in Belgrade and the Faculty of Technical Sciences in Novi Sad, and produced eight peer-reviewed outputs and one publicly released software toolkit.

SYN-PRJ-0077.title: Cognitive Flexibility Assessment and Cross-Cultural Comparability in South-East European Adolescents
SYN-PRJ-0077.text:
COGFLEX-SEE: Cognitive Flexibility Assessment and Cross-Cultural Comparability in South-East European Adolescents (Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0322 work package leader; R0755 team member; R0074 team member.
Partners: Babeș-Bolyai University, Cluj-Napoca, Romania; Provincial Institute for the Evaluation of Education Quality, Novi Sad, Serbia.
This cross-border project designed, calibrated, and administered a computer-based cognitive flexibility assessment battery to adolescent samples in Serbia and Romania, with the goal of establishing measurement comparability across the two educational systems. Emilija Zec led the psychometric calibration and measurement invariance work package, overseeing IRT item banking and multi-group confirmatory factor analyses. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian/Romanian) assessment instrument, a joint data repository shared between the two partner universities, and a report submitted to educational authorities in both countries. A three-day methodological workshop on IRT and invariance testing was delivered to school psychologists in Timișoara and Novi Sad.

SYN-PRJ-0078.title: Inclusive Digital Learning Environments for Students with Attention and Processing Differences in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0078.text:
INCLUDE-AP: Inclusive Digital Learning Environments for Students with Attention and Processing Differences in the Western Balkans (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0207 principal investigator; R1043 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad; Pedagogical Institute of Vojvodina; Primary School Đura Daničić, Novi Sad.
This project investigated barriers to and enablers of UDL implementation in inclusive primary and secondary schools in Serbia, focusing specifically on students with attention-related and auditory/visual processing differences. The project combined a large-scale survey of 620 teachers across 38 schools, three school-based design-and-test cycles for UDL-adapted digital materials, and the development of an open-access audit toolkit for school teams. A teacher professional development model was piloted in 12 schools in Vojvodina and validated through pre/post measurement and independent observer evaluation. Final deliverables include the audit toolkit, a freely downloadable material template library, and a policy brief submitted to the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Serbia.

SYN-PRJ-0079.title: Accessible Digital Learning across the Adriatic–Danube Region: Framework Development and Pilot Validation
SYN-PRJ-0079.text:
ADRIADL: Accessible Digital Learning across the Adriatic–Danube Region: Framework Development and Pilot Validation (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0207 work package leader; R1043 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad; University of Pécs, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary; Faculty of Teacher Education, University of Rijeka, Croatia; National Institute of Education Research, Budapest, Hungary.
ADRIADL brought together educational research institutions in Serbia, Hungary, and Croatia to develop a shared framework for assessing and improving the accessibility of digital instructional materials in primary education. Fejsa led the work package responsible for empirical validation of the framework across Serbian pilot schools, coordinating a team of four researchers who conducted classroom observations, student assessments, and teacher interviews in 14 schools. The project produced a trilingual framework document, a validated teacher self-assessment instrument available in Serbian, Hungarian, and Croatian, and a series of open-access training videos. Findings were disseminated through national teacher in-service training networks in all three partner countries.

SYN-PRJ-0100.title: Sensor-Driven Probabilistic Risk Models for SME Asset Management
SYN-PRJ-0100.text:
SENSORISK: Sensor-Driven Probabilistic Risk Models for SME Asset Management (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0261 principal investigator; R0901 team member; R0476 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research, Novi Sad; Vojvodina SME Development Agency (fictional).
The project developed a modular software pipeline for ingesting high-frequency IoT sensor streams, extracting interpretable statistical features, and fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models suitable for small and medium enterprises that lack dedicated data science teams. Use cases were developed in collaboration with three SMEs in Vojvodina operating in food processing, cold-chain logistics, and metal fabrication. A reference implementation was released as open-source software. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed outputs. A key output was a calibration protocol that allows a new site to obtain reliable risk scores after as little as 60 days of sensor history by borrowing strength from previously observed sites via the hierarchical model structure.

SYN-PRJ-0103.title: Cross-Border Flash Flood Early Warning System for the Sava and Tisa Catchments
SYN-PRJ-0103.text:
FLOODWISE-IPA: Cross-Border Flash Flood Early Warning System for the Sava and Tisa Catchments (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0700 work package leader.
Partners: Универзитет Сечени Иштван, Ђер, Мађарска; Покрајински секретаријат за пољопривреду, водопривреду и шумарство АП Војводине; Управа за ванредне ситуације, Подручна јединица Нови Сад.
Интеррег IPA пројекат окупља партнере из Србије и Мађарске у циљу развоја прекограничног система раног упозорења на изненадне поплаве у сливовима Саве и Тисе. Тошић руководи радним пакетом задуженим за QPE производе и просторну интерполацију падавина. Систем у реалном времену преузима оперативне радарске производе обеју земаља, меша их са плувиометријским подацима и прослеђује хидролошком моделу који управља мађарски партнерски универзитет. Крајњи корисници система су локалне самоуправе и ватрогасно-спасилачке службе у Бачкој и Барањи. Планирано је да систем буде у пилот-оперативном режиму до краја 2025. године.

SYN-PRJ-0105.title: Cloud-Edge Data Stream Processing for Cross-Border Industrial Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0105.text:
CEDS-BRIDGE: Cloud-Edge Data Stream Processing for Cross-Border Industrial Monitoring (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R1020 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary; Regional Development Agency of Vojvodina; Pannonia Industrial Automation Kft. (fictional).
CEDS-BRIDGE was a cross-border cooperation project addressing real-time monitoring of industrial processes that span manufacturing sites in northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The project developed a shared cloud-edge data platform capable of ingesting sensor data streams from both sides of the border, applying configurable reconciliation and alerting logic, and presenting unified dashboards to operators at both sites. Nedić's work package covered the stream processing core: operator placement across edge and cloud nodes, latency characterisation under cross-border WAN conditions, and the adaptation of open-source tooling for deployment in resource-constrained edge environments. Field trials were conducted at a pilot water treatment facility and a logistics sorting centre.

SYN-PRJ-0113.title: Cross-Border Agricultural Data Infrastructure for Climate Risk Management in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0113.text:
AGRIDATA-CROSS: Cross-Border Agricultural Data Infrastructure for Climate Risk Management in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0364 work package leader.
Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Institute of Geography and Earth Sciences, University of Miskolc, Hungary; Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Water Economy and Forestry, Vojvodina; South Transdanubian Regional Development Agency, Hungary.
AGRIDATA-CROSS builds a shared meteorological data infrastructure and climate risk assessment platform serving agricultural stakeholders in the Hungary–Serbia border region. Žarko Pejić leads the work package responsible for harmonising national meteorological station records, generating consistent cross-border gridded precipitation climatologies, and providing spatial input layers to a joint drought monitoring dashboard. The project links national hydrometeorological services, regional agricultural extension offices, and university research groups on both sides of the border. Outputs include a web-accessible map viewer, an annual climate risk bulletin, and training workshops for farmers and insurance intermediaries on interpreting spatial weather data.

SYN-PRJ-0114.title: Data Quality Assurance in Cross-Organisational Real-Time Streaming Integrations
SYN-PRJ-0114.text:
DAQSTREAM: Data Quality Assurance in Cross-Organisational Real-Time Streaming Integrations (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0571 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; LogiFlow d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner).
DAQSTREAM addressed the gap between theoretical data quality frameworks and the operational realities of streaming API integrations shared by multiple organisations. The project developed monitoring components for schema drift detection, cross-source consistency validation, and anomaly alerting, targeting Kafka-based pipeline architectures. Pilot deployments were conducted with two partner organisations in logistics and retail sectors in Vojvodina. The project produced a reference architecture, an open-source monitoring toolkit, and a set of evaluation datasets released publicly. Four journal papers and three conference contributions were produced. The project also supported the doctoral work of two Ph.D. students at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0115.title: Automated Pipeline Integrity Monitoring for API-Mediated Business Data Exchange
SYN-PRJ-0115.text:
APIGUARD: Automated Pipeline Integrity Monitoring for API-Mediated Business Data Exchange (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0571 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad.
APIGUARD is a smaller regionally funded project focused specifically on integrating data quality monitoring components directly into existing API gateway infrastructure used by small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina. The project develops lightweight agents deployable alongside standard API management tools, requiring no modification to existing service code. Activities include requirement analysis with five SME participants, prototyping, and a controlled usability evaluation. The project also supports a master thesis programme in which students implement and test specific monitoring modules. Results are intended to be transferable to companies at NTP Novi Sad that operate API-based integrations with partners or public registries.

SYN-PRJ-0117.title: Catastrophe Modelling Tools for Small Non-Life Insurers in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0117.text:
CATTOOL: Catastrophe Modelling Tools for Small Non-Life Insurers in the Western Balkans (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2022).
Participants: R0842 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; University of Debrecen, Faculty of Economics and Business; Balkans Insurance Analytics d.o.o., Novi Sad; PannonRe Consulting Kft., Debrecen.
A cross-border applied research project that produced an open decision-support toolkit for underwriting and reserving departments of small non-life insurance companies operating in Hungary and Serbia. Péter Szabó led the work package on statistical methodology, overseeing implementation of GPD-based tail models and Bayesian updating routines in a user-facing R Shiny application. The toolkit was piloted with two regional insurers. The project also delivered two training workshops for actuarial staff and a technical manual translated into Serbian and Hungarian. Total budget for the Serbian side was approximately 180,000 EUR.

SYN-PRJ-0118.title: Drift-Aware Semi-Supervised Monitoring for Low-Label Industrial Environments
SYN-PRJ-0118.text:
DRIFTGUARD: Drift-Aware Semi-Supervised Monitoring for Low-Label Industrial Environments (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0071 principal investigator; R0030 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research of Serbia (fictional); Termovent Energetika d.o.o. (fictional).
DRIFTGUARD addresses the combined challenge of label scarcity and concept drift in industrial condition monitoring. The project develops a unified framework in which a semi-supervised classifier is coupled with a lightweight drift detector; when drift is flagged, the system selects a small targeted query set using active learning rather than retraining from scratch on all historical data. The framework is validated on sensor streams from two partner facilities: a food-processing conveyor line and a district heating pump station. Expected outcomes include an open benchmark dataset with documented drift events, a reference software implementation, and design guidelines for practitioners. The project funds one PhD student and two master student thesis positions at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.

SYN-PRJ-0119.title: Edge-Deployable Streaming Analytics for Smart Manufacturing in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0119.text:
STREAMWISE: Edge-Deployable Streaming Analytics for Smart Manufacturing in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0071 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Bay Zoltán Alkalmazott Kutatási Közhasznú Nonprofit Kft. (fictional); Precizna Automatika d.o.o. Subotica (fictional); Pannon Ipar Klaszter (fictional); NTP Novi Sad – Science Technology Park Novi Sad (fictional).
STREAMWISE is a cross-border cooperation project targeting the deployment of data stream analytics in small and medium enterprises in the Hungarian–Serbian border region. Olivera Rakić leads the work package on model compression and edge deployment, responsible for adapting anomaly detection and classification pipelines to resource-constrained hardware installed in partner SME facilities. The work package produces deployment-ready software containers, an evaluation report comparing accuracy–latency trade-offs across hardware tiers, and a training curriculum for engineers at partner companies. The project is coordinated by the Hungarian partner and involves three Serbian and two Hungarian organisations.

SYN-PRJ-0151.title: Edge Processing and Compressed Sensing for Precision Agriculture IoT Deployments in Cross-Border Regions
SYN-PRJ-0151.text:
IOTEDGE-AG: Edge Processing and Compressed Sensing for Precision Agriculture IoT Deployments in Cross-Border Regions (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0641 work package leader.
Partners: University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering, Hungary; BioSense Institute, Novi Sad; Vojvodinašume JP, Petrovaradin.
A cross-border cooperation project aiming to deploy low-cost LoRaWAN-connected soil and microclimate sensor nodes across agricultural holdings in Bács-Kiskun County (Hungary) and South Bačka District (Serbia). Stojanović led the work package on on-device data reduction, contributing dictionary coding and adaptive sampling methods validated in the field. The project produced a common hardware reference design and an open-source firmware library for payload compression. Field trials involved 140 sensor nodes over two growing seasons monitoring maize, sunflower, and soybean plots. The project also organised two joint student workshops on embedded IoT programming attended by 34 students from both countries.

SYN-PRJ-0154.title: Cross-Border Network for Mobile Application Testing Methodologies in SME Software Development
SYN-PRJ-0154.text:
MOBTESTNET: Cross-Border Network for Mobile Application Testing Methodologies in SME Software Development (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0312 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen; Syntara Solutions d.o.o., Subotica; Kodalab Kft., Pécs; Droidforge Solutions d.o.o., Novi Sad.
MOBTESTNET brought together two universities and three SME software development companies from the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region to document and transfer mobile application testing practices suited to small development teams. Dragišić led the work package responsible for assembling a shared device testing infrastructure accessible remotely by partner organisations, and for developing a training curriculum on multi-version Android compatibility testing delivered to 42 developers across four workshops. The project produced an open testing guideline document and a reusable CI pipeline template adopted by two of the three company partners within the project period.

SYN-PRJ-0155.title: Automated Compatibility Assurance for Android Applications in the Serbian Mobile Market
SYN-PRJ-0155.text:
COMPAT-RS: Automated Compatibility Assurance for Android Applications in the Serbian Mobile Market (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R0312 principal investigator; R0363 team member; R0106 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Droidforge Solutions d.o.o., Novi Sad; Mobilix Technologies d.o.o., Belgrade.
COMPAT-RS addresses the practical gap between academic compatibility testing research and the capacity of Serbian SME mobile developers to apply such methods. The project is building an open-source toolkit, CompatKit, combining static analysis, differential UI testing, and a risk prediction module trained on Serbian and regional application datasets. The toolkit targets API levels 26 through the current release and is being validated with six industry partner applications. Secondary objectives include maintaining a public dataset of Android compatibility defects sourced from the region and publishing practitioner-oriented guidance documents.
