Dragišić leads the project with a team of two PhD students and one research assistant.

SYN-PRJ-0174.title: Interoperable Communication Middleware for Heterogeneous Agricultural Vehicle Networks
SYN-PRJ-0174.text:
AGRILINK: Interoperable Communication Middleware for Heterogeneous Agricultural Vehicle Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0248 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad; Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops Novi Sad; Agroelektronika d.o.o. Subotica (fictional company).
AGRILINK addressed the practical interoperability gap between ISOBUS and CANopen subsystems on small and medium farm machinery common in the Western Balkans, where operators maintain mixed fleets spanning multiple decades of production. The project developed a configurable middleware layer running on a dual-CAN embedded platform that dynamically maps process-data between the two protocol worlds, with a focus on minimal latency and flash footprint suitable for low-cost ECUs. A reference implementation was validated on two commercially sourced implements supplied by a regional agricultural machinery dealer. The project also produced an open test harness and a set of training materials for Serbian agricultural engineering students.

SYN-PRJ-0213.title: Physiological Signal Compression for Low-Power Telemetry in Remote Patient Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0213.text:
PHYCOMP: Physiological Signal Compression for Low-Power Telemetry in Remote Patient Monitoring (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0057 principal investigator.
Partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
The project investigates compression algorithms suitable for deployment on low-power microcontrollers in wearable and implantable patient monitoring devices. Work packages cover beat-synchronous transform coding, sparse dictionary methods, and lightweight learned entropy models with a shared emphasis on keeping encoder complexity below 10 mJ per minute of single-lead ECG. The project includes a clinical validation component in collaboration with the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, where compressed and reconstructed signals are assessed for diagnostic equivalence by cardiologists. A reference software library with documented APIs is being developed for use by regional medical-device developers. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher.

SYN-PRJ-0214.title: Cross-Border Telemedicine Data Infrastructure for Cardiac Monitoring
SYN-PRJ-0214.text:
CROTIMED: Cross-Border Telemedicine Data Infrastructure for Cardiac Monitoring (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0057 work package leader; R0653 team member; R0019 team member.
Partners: Somogy County Health Authority, Kaposvár; General Hospital Subotica; Mediconn d.o.o., Novi Sad.
A cross-border infrastructure project aiming to establish shared telemedicine data pipelines between partner hospitals in southern Hungary and the Vojvodina region. Šarić leads the work package on signal compression and transmission standards, contributing ECG and PPG codec implementations compliant with the SCP-ECG data standard. The work package also produces interoperability guidelines for compressed signal exchange between different hospital information systems used on the two sides of the border. Deliverables include a compression middleware component integrated into the project's shared telemedicine platform and a joint training session for clinical IT staff at both partner sites.

SYN-PRJ-0271.title: Cross-Institutional Learning Trace Data Harmonisation for Comparative Analytics
SYN-PRJ-0271.text:
CROSSLEARN: Cross-Institutional Learning Trace Data Harmonisation for Comparative Analytics (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R1006 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen, Hungary; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Subotica Tech – College of Applied Sciences, Subotica.
CROSSLEARN addresses the lack of interoperability between learning management system log formats at universities on both sides of the Hungary–Serbia border, which prevents comparative analytics research. The project is producing a shared data schema and an open-source transformation pipeline covering Moodle, Canvas, and one proprietary system used by a Hungarian partner. Mitrović leads the work package on statistical harmonisation, which develops procedures for aligning feature distributions across institutions before joint model training. An ongoing longitudinal study tracks 2,600 students across four partner universities from enrolment through first degree, with annual data extracts. Outputs include a harmonised benchmark dataset and two cross-border student mobility analytics pilots.

SYN-PRJ-0281.title: Hybrid Game Interventions for Mathematical Cognition in Primary Education: A Cross-National Evaluation
SYN-PRJ-0281.text:
HYBRIMATH: Hybrid Game Interventions for Mathematical Cognition in Primary Education: A Cross-National Evaluation (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0837 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Education in Sombor, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade; BioSens Institute, University of Novi Sad.
HYBRIMATH investigated whether digital-physical hybrid game interventions produce superior arithmetic and fraction outcomes compared to digital-only and conventional instruction across diverse primary school contexts. The project coordinated data collection in 24 schools in Serbia, developed and validated a battery of mathematics cognition instruments calibrated for grades three through five, and produced open-access intervention materials including teacher facilitation guides. A secondary strand examined log data from tablet sessions to identify behavioural predictors of learning gain. The project produced seven journal articles, two conference papers, and one open dataset. It also supported two doctoral students at the Faculty of Education in Sombor.

SYN-PRJ-0297.title: Conducted Disturbance Characterisation and Unified Time-domain Simulation for Low-Voltage Smart Grids
SYN-PRJ-0297.text:
CONDUCTS: Conducted Disturbance Characterisation and Unified Time-domain Simulation for Low-Voltage Smart Grids (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0611 principal investigator; R0637 team member; R0028 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Elektrotehnički fakultet, University of Belgrade; Elektrodistribucija Srbije d.o.o. – Regional Centre Novi Sad.
The project builds a validated simulation and measurement infrastructure for analysing conducted disturbances in low-voltage distribution networks with high penetration of power electronic loads. Key activities include: extended characterisation of emission sources (EV chargers, PV inverters, smart meters, LED drivers) using LISN measurements and Norton equivalent extraction; development of a time-domain feeder simulation library in MATLAB/Simulink with open-licence distribution; a 12-month field monitoring campaign on two suburban feeders; and a probabilistic compliance assessment tool. Results feed into a position paper on Serbian national transposition of IEC 61000-3 limits for aggregated loads.

SYN-PRJ-0331.title: Optimisation of Biochar Production from Vojvodina Agricultural Residues for Soil Amendment and Carbon Sequestration
SYN-PRJ-0331.text:
BIOCHAR-VJ: Optimisation of Biochar Production from Vojvodina Agricultural Residues for Soil Amendment and Carbon Sequestration (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0992 principal investigator; R0151 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad; Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad; Agrokompleks Vojvodine d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project systematically mapped the pyrolysis parameter space—temperature, residence time, and feedstock type—for the three dominant agricultural residues of Vojvodina: sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover. Over 200 biochar samples were produced and fully characterised against European Biochar Certificate criteria. A decision-support matrix was developed to guide producers in selecting process conditions based on intended agronomic use (soil amendment versus carbon sequestration credit). Field verification was conducted through a two-season pot experiment in collaboration with the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops. Results fed directly into four journal publications and one conference paper.

SYN-PRJ-0333.title: Condition-Based Maintenance Protocols for Small-Scale Biomass Densification Facilities in the Pannonian Region
SYN-PRJ-0333.text:
BIOMAINT: Condition-Based Maintenance Protocols for Small-Scale Biomass Densification Facilities in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0135 coordinator; R0744 team member.
Partners: University of Miskolc, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Hungary; Agricultural Cooperative Zlatna Njiva, Subotica, Serbia; Regional Energy Agency of Southern Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary.
The project addressed the widespread absence of structured maintenance practice in small- and medium-scale biomass pellet and briquette facilities operating across the Vojvodina–Southern Hungary border region. Partners inventoried 34 facilities, documented failure histories, and collected feedstock quality records over 18 months. The Novi Sad team developed condition monitoring protocols calibrated to the variable feedstock profiles of the region; the Miskolc team contributed failure database infrastructure. A set of maintenance planning tools—including a moisture-adjusted bearing replacement nomogram and a simplified RBD-based availability calculator—was packaged into a freely distributable spreadsheet toolkit distributed to cooperatives and processing companies in the cross-border region.

SYN-PRJ-0334.title: Reliability-Centred Operation of Biomass Densification Systems under Variable Feedstock Quality
SYN-PRJ-0334.text:
RELIODENSE: Reliability-Centred Operation of Biomass Densification Systems under Variable Feedstock Quality (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0135 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Food Technology, Novi Sad; Bioenergo d.o.o., Vrbas, Serbia.
RELIODENSE addresses the gap between laboratory degradation models and field-deployable maintenance decision tools for biomass densification equipment. The project integrates on-line NIR feedstock sensing, low-cost MEMS vibration loggers, and Bayesian degradation models into a prototype decision support system tested at two commercial pellet facilities in Vojvodina. Research tasks include calibration of NIR regression models for mixed agricultural residues, development of the particle-filtering RUL estimator, discrete-event simulation of full production lines, and a field validation campaign. The project supports one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher. The primary output is a validated software prototype and an open dataset of bearing vibration and feedstock quality records from the two field sites.

SYN-PRJ-0341.title: Distributed In-situ Data Quality Assurance for Low-Power Environmental Monitoring Networks
SYN-PRJ-0341.text:
DIAQUAL: Distributed In-situ Data Quality Assurance for Low-Power Environmental Monitoring Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R0754 principal investigator.
Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
DIAQUAL addresses the absence of standardised data quality assurance methods for resource-constrained IoT nodes used in environmental monitoring. The project is developing a layered diagnostic framework in which lightweight statistical tests execute at node level, aggregation logic runs at gateway level, and a calibration traceability module operates at the cloud backend. The framework targets NB-IoT and LTE-M deployments and is being validated on soil, water-level, and air-quality sensor networks operated by project partners. The project employs two research assistants based at BioSense Institute and includes a measurement campaign at ten instrumented sites across the Fruška Gora protected area. A hardware reference design and open-source firmware library are planned deliverables.

SYN-PRJ-0381.title: Process Monitoring and Control Tools for Small-Scale Electrostatic Powder Coating Pre-Treatment Lines
SYN-PRJ-0381.text:
COATLINE: Process Monitoring and Control Tools for Small-Scale Electrostatic Powder Coating Pre-Treatment Lines (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2020–2021).
Participants: R0593 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association.
This project addressed the lack of structured process monitoring in small powder coating operations in Vojvodina. Activities included a baseline survey of bath chemistry management practices at seven local contractors, instrument calibration audits, and a pilot SPC deployment at two volunteer companies. The project produced a bilingual (Serbian/English) SPC implementation guide for pre-treatment lines, freely distributed to members of the Vojvodina Coating Contractors Association. Results from the pilot companies were subsequently published in peer-reviewed form. Total funding was 1.2 million RSD.

SYN-PRJ-0382.title: Scalable Formal Verification Methods for Interrupt-Driven Firmware in Industrial Embedded Systems
SYN-PRJ-0382.text:
FIRMVER: Scalable Formal Verification Methods for Interrupt-Driven Firmware in Industrial Embedded Systems (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R1022 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Czech Technical University in Prague, Czech Republic.
FIRMVER investigated compositional and incremental model-checking techniques to make formal verification of real-time interrupt-driven firmware feasible for industrial-scale codebases. The project developed the MisraFix automated repair tool, the incremental Promela extraction pipeline, and a library of verified component stubs for common peripheral driver patterns on ARM Cortex-M devices. Three Ph.D. students were supported. Deliverables include a publicly available toolchain prototype, five peer-reviewed journal publications, and a technical report on integration with the CMake build system. The project collaborated with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and with Czech Technical University in Prague for external validation of the methodology on independently developed firmware.

SYN-PRJ-0390.title: Product-Line Code Generation Infrastructure for Configurable PLC Software
SYN-PRJ-0390.text:
PLCGEN: Product-Line Code Generation Infrastructure for Configurable PLC Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0995 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania.
The PLCGEN project developed an end-to-end toolchain for model-driven software product-line engineering targeting IEC 61131-3 Structured Text. Work packages covered metamodel design, feature model integration, incremental generation, and round-trip recovery of variation points from legacy code. The project delivered an Eclipse-based IDE plugin, a library of reusable transformation modules, and the benchmark suite reported in the 2026 journal paper. Two Ph.D. students were funded through the project. Industry validation was carried out with one automation equipment manufacturer in Novi Sad and one in Subotica under non-disclosure agreements. The project produced nine peer-reviewed publications and one master thesis.

SYN-PRJ-0391.title: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software
SYN-PRJ-0391.text:
SAFEPLL: Safety-Aware Product-Line Modelling for Certified Automation Software (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0995 work package leader; R0749 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary; Automatika-Pro d.o.o., Novi Sad; RoboSystems Kft., Pécs, Hungary.
SAFEPLL addressed the integration of functional safety requirements into model-driven PLC product-line workflows, targeting IEC 62061 SIL 1 and SIL 2 certified applications. The project brought together researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest with two SME automation integrators. Veljko Pantelić led the work package on traceability from HAZOP artefacts to generated code, contributing the SysML parametric diagram transformation described in the 2021 conference paper. The project produced a methodology document adopted by both industrial partners as an internal development guideline, and delivered training workshops for engineering staff at both companies.

SYN-PRJ-0392.title: EMC Characterisation and Filter Validation Methods for SiC-Based Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Environments
SYN-PRJ-0392.text:
EMCDRIVE: EMC Characterisation and Filter Validation Methods for SiC-Based Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Environments (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0283 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Institute for Power Engineering and Automation, Subotica.
The project addressed the gap between laboratory IEC 61800-3 compliance and field performance of EMC filters for SiC MOSFET motor drives. The work covered three main activities: systematic conducted emission characterisation of SiC drives from 2.2 kW to 22 kW, development of a measurement uncertainty budget specific to high-di/dt inverter systems, and design and experimental validation of filter topologies robust to realistic PE impedance variation encountered in Serbian industrial installations. Forty-seven sites were surveyed for PE impedance. Deliverables included a filter design procedure, a dataset of emission spectra and PE impedance profiles made publicly available, and two validated simulation models. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed publications.

SYN-PRJ-0412.title: Thermal State Estimation and Adaptive Parameter Control for Robotic Arc Welding
SYN-PRJ-0412.text:
THERMARC: Thermal State Estimation and Adaptive Parameter Control for Robotic Arc Welding (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0445 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac; Metalprodukt Inženjering d.o.o., Novi Sad.
THERMARC addressed the problem of unknown and varying thermal boundary conditions in robotic GMAW production cells. The project developed sensor fusion methods combining infrared pool imaging with arc electrical signals to estimate workpiece thermal state in real time, and built closed-loop controllers that use these estimates to adjust process parameters. Work was conducted on a dedicated robotic GMAW cell at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Outcomes included validated observer algorithms, a dataset of 600 annotated welding runs, three journal publications, and a technology demonstrator evaluated with an industrial partner manufacturing structural steel subassemblies in Novi Sad. Two PhD students were funded through the project.

SYN-PRJ-0414.title: Verification and Runtime Analysis for Safety-Critical Embedded Control Software
SYN-PRJ-0414.text:
VERITAS: Verification and Runtime Analysis for Safety-Critical Embedded Control Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0375 principal investigator; R1045 team member; R0363 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš; Politehnica University of Timișoara, Romania.
VERITAS addressed two interrelated problems in safety-critical embedded software engineering: the cost of exhaustive formal verification and the limited coverage of runtime assertion checking. The project developed lightweight static pre-filters that reduce the verification search space before handing off to model checkers, and a runtime monitor generator that instruments binaries with safety properties at the machine-code level without modifying source code. Verification experiments were conducted on firmware from the automotive and building-automation domains. The project produced six peer-reviewed publications, an open-source Frama-C plugin for incremental MISRA-C checking, and a cooperation agreement with one Serbian automation equipment manufacturer for follow-on contract research. Two MSc students and one PhD candidate were funded through the project.

SYN-PRJ-0415.title: Formal Methods Training and Tool Integration for Small Embedded Software Teams in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0415.text:
FORMBASE: Formal Methods Training and Tool Integration for Small Embedded Software Teams in the Western Balkans (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2024).
Participants: R0375 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Vojvodina ICT Cluster, Novi Sad; Pécs Engineering and Innovation Centre, Hungary.
FORMBASE aimed to lower the barrier to formal methods adoption in small software teams developing embedded control systems in Hungary and Serbia. Stefan Kostić led the work package responsible for curriculum development and tool-integration workshops. The project produced a three-day training course covering CBMC, Frama-C, and UPPAAL, delivered to 68 engineers from 11 companies across the two countries. A companion open-access textbook of 180 pages was written in Serbian and Hungarian. The project also ran a tool evaluation study comparing six open-source formal verification tools on a shared benchmark of embedded firmware, with results published as a technical report. Two pilot adoptions in participating companies were documented as case studies.

SYN-PRJ-0427.title: Energy-Efficient Edge Vibration Monitoring for Smart Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-0427.text:
EDGEVIB: Energy-Efficient Edge Vibration Monitoring for Smart Manufacturing (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0206 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Automat d.o.o. Novi Sad (fictional industrial partner); SensoraTech d.o.o. Novi Sad (fictional industrial partner).
EDGEVIB focuses on the integration of adaptive sampling, lightweight data compression, and on-device neural inference within a single firmware stack targeting coin-cell-powered BLE sensor nodes. The project collaborates with two companies at NTP Novi Sad for pilot deployments on conveyor drive motors and CNC spindle units. Key research questions concern the trade-off between inference duty cycle and battery longevity, the robustness of int8 models after incremental over-the-air updates, and the minimum sensor bandwidth needed to detect early-stage bearing faults. A secondary outcome is a teaching module on TinyML incorporated into the embedded systems curriculum at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0498.title: Adaptive Anomaly Detection Frameworks for High-Velocity Industrial Log Streams
SYN-PRJ-0498.text:
STREAMGUARD: Adaptive Anomaly Detection Frameworks for High-Velocity Industrial Log Streams (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0030 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Automatika d.o.o., Novi Sad.
STREAMGUARD investigates adaptive unsupervised methods for detecting anomalies in log streams generated by industrial control and IT infrastructure, with a focus on handling concept drift and heterogeneous log sources in real time. The project funds two PhD students and one postdoctoral researcher. Work packages cover log parsing standardisation, streaming algorithm design, EVT-based threshold adaptation, and evaluation on datasets from regional industrial partners. Hardware procured under the project includes two GPU workstations and an expansion of the Kafka testbed. Results are being transferred to two regional companies through technology-transfer agreements negotiated in the final project year.

SYN-PRJ-0499.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Log Analytics for Cross-Organisational Threat Intelligence
SYN-PRJ-0499.text:
LOGFED: Privacy-Preserving Federated Log Analytics for Cross-Organisational Threat Intelligence (Horizon Europe, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0030 work package leader.
Partners: Technical University of Graz, Austria (coordinator); University of Bologna, Italy; Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest, Hungary; CyberShield Analytics GmbH, Berlin, Germany; NetVigilance S.R.L., Cluj-Napoca, Romania; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Sinteza IT d.o.o., Novi Sad; Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași, Romania.
LOGFED brings together eight partners from five countries to develop federated machine learning infrastructure for shared threat detection without raw log exchange. Vojnović leads the work package on federated model architecture and aggregation robustness. The Novi Sad team is responsible for the heterogeneous-log simulation environment and for benchmarking aggregation strategies under adversarial participant conditions. The project targets GDPR-compliant deployment scenarios in healthcare, utilities, and financial sectors. An open-source toolkit for federated log anomaly detection is planned for release in the final project year.

SYN-PRJ-0502.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Hardware Security Modules in Critical Infrastructure
SYN-PRJ-0502.text:
PQHSM: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Hardware Security Modules in Critical Infrastructure (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0503 principal investigator.
Partners: RT-RK Institute for Computer Based Systems, Novi Sad; Faculty of Electrical Engineering, University of East Sarajevo; Informatika d.o.o., Novi Sad.
The project investigates the performance and security constraints of deploying post-quantum cryptographic algorithms on hardware security modules used in Serbian energy and transport infrastructure. Work packages cover algorithm selection and adaptation, FPGA and secure microcontroller implementation, side-channel and fault-injection evaluation, and a migration roadmap document targeting IEC 62443 compliance. The team collaborates with the RT-RK Institute in Novi Sad for industrial system integration testing. Outputs include an open benchmarking dataset, two software libraries released under an open-source licence, and a technical report delivered to the Serbian Ministry of Information and Telecommunications.

SYN-PRJ-0503.title: Securing Embedded Controllers in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems Against Quantum-Capable Adversaries
SYN-PRJ-0503.text:
SECURED-ICS: Securing Embedded Controllers in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems Against Quantum-Capable Adversaries (Horizon Europe, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0503 work package leader; R0641 team member.
Partners: TU Dresden, Germany; Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania; VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland; Axiom Technologies S.A., Brussels; RT-RK Institute for Computer Based Systems, Novi Sad; Cybersecurity Research Institute, Zagreb; SINTEF Digital, Oslo.
SECURED-ICS is a 3-year Horizon Europe project bringing together eight partners from six countries to develop and validate a reference architecture for quantum-resistant security in industrial cyber-physical systems. Milica Nikolić leads Work Package 3, which covers hardware-level implementation and benchmarking of NIST-standardised post-quantum schemes on programmable logic controllers and remote terminal units. The work package produces a common evaluation board, a porting guide for firmware engineers, and a set of test vectors and timing datasets. Results feed into Work Package 5 on certification methodology. The project targets IEC 62443 and the forthcoming ETSI EN 303 645 annex on quantum-resistant requirements.

SYN-PRJ-0504.title: Scalable Real-Time Certificate Status Query Resolution for High-Volume Distributed Environments
SYN-PRJ-0504.text:
SCALOCSP: Scalable Real-Time Certificate Status Query Resolution for High-Volume Distributed Environments (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0217 principal investigator.
Partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu; Faculty of Automatic Control and Computers, Politehnica University of Bucharest, Romania.
Projekat SCALOCSP bavi se projektovanjem i evaluacijom arhitektura distribuiranih baza podataka prilagođenih zahtevima OCSP sistema koji opslužuju infrastrukture s više od pet miliona aktivnih sertifikata. Istraživanje obuhvata razvoj skalabilnih struktura podataka, strategija keširanja s formalnim granicama zastarelosti i tehnika particionisanja prilagođenih promenljivim stopama izdavanja sertifikata. Planiran je razvoj otvorenog referentnog okruženja za merenje performansi koje će biti dostupno istraživačkoj zajednici. Projekat uključuje partnerske institucije iz Srbije i Rumunije i predviđa obuku dva doktoranda.

SYN-PRJ-0505.title: Cross-Border Data Infrastructure for Trusted Digital Services in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0505.text:
CROSSDATA: Cross-Border Data Infrastructure for Trusted Digital Services in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0217 work package leader.
Partners: Departman za matematiku i informatiku, PMF, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu; Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs, Hungary; Naučno-tehnološki park Novi Sad.
CROSSDATA ima za cilj uspostavljanje zajedničke istraživačke infrastrukture za testiranje distribuiranih sistema za upravljanje digitalnim identitetom i statusom sertifikata u prekograničnom kontekstu između Srbije i Mađarske. Andrea Malešević vodi radni paket posvećen dizajnu i evaluaciji baza podataka, uključujući WAN testiranje latencije i razvoj zajedničkih protokola za merenje performansi. Projekat predviđa organizaciju dve zajedničke letnje škole i razvoj otvorenih obrazovnih materijala na srpskom, mađarskom i engleskom jeziku.

SYN-PRJ-0511.title: Incremental and Calibrated Anomaly Recognition for Operational SCADA Systems
SYN-PRJ-0511.text:
ICAROS: Incremental and Calibrated Anomaly Recognition for Operational SCADA Systems (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R1008 principal investigator; R0564 team member; R0043 team member.
Partners: Elektrodistribucija Bačka d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional energy distributor); Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš.
ICAROS addressed the calibration and incremental update of unsupervised anomaly detectors deployed on live SCADA networks. The project developed threshold calibration procedures for detectors operating without labelled attack data, incremental Gaussian mixture and autoencoder update algorithms suited to concept drift induced by planned process changes, and a set of evaluation protocols for comparing detectors across different ICS protocol environments. A labelled Modbus/TCP and DNP3 benchmark dataset was produced and released. Partners included a regional energy distributor that provided controlled access to a monitoring mirror port on an operational substation network, enabling validation under real traffic conditions. The project supported two doctoral candidates and produced nine peer-reviewed publications.

SYN-PRJ-0512.title: Federated Anomaly Detection Across Distributed Industrial Control System Sites
SYN-PRJ-0512.text:
FEDICS: Federated Anomaly Detection Across Distributed Industrial Control System Sites (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R1008 coordinator.
Partners: Department of Automation and Applied Informatics, Budapest University of Technology; Faculty of Informatics, University of Debrecen; Vodovod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional regional water utility).
FEDICS developed federated learning protocols enabling anomaly detection models trained at geographically distributed ICS sites to be aggregated without exchanging raw network traffic. The project addressed privacy constraints common in critical infrastructure contexts and evaluated ensemble aggregation strategies for combining site-level one-class classifiers. Pilot deployments were conducted at two water utility control centres and two district heating substations across the Hungarian–Serbian border region. The project also produced a joint curriculum module on ICS cybersecurity delivered at partner universities. Key deliverables included open-source federated aggregation software, two datasets, and six joint publications by the consortium.

SYN-PRJ-0513.title: Secure and Authenticated Firmware Lifecycle Management for Low-Power Industrial Wireless Networks
SYN-PRJ-0513.text:
SAFELINK: Secure and Authenticated Firmware Lifecycle Management for Low-Power Industrial Wireless Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0286 principal investigator.
Partners: Електротехнички факултет, Универзитет у Београду; Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, University of Zagreb.
Пројекат SAFELINK бави се дизајном, формалном анализом и практичном имплементацијом протокола за управљање животним циклусом фирмвера у индустријским бежичним мрежама са малом потрошњом енергије. Обухвата три главна правца: развој протокола за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера усклађених са ограничењима LPWAN технологија, процену примењивости пост-квантних потписних схема на уређајима класе 1 и класе 2, и методологију за верификацију усклађености са индустријским безбедносним стандардима. Пројекат укључује лабораторијско тестирање на тестбеду са 40 чворова и сарадњу са два партнерска универзитета из региона. Планирани резултати укључују шест журналских радова, отворени репозиторијум имплементације протокола и нацрт техничке препоруке за индустријске кориснике.

SYN-PRJ-0515.title: Quantitative Cyber Risk Models for Financial Institutions in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-0515.text:
CYQUAN: Quantitative Cyber Risk Models for Financial Institutions in the Western Balkans (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2023).
Participants: R0422 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Economics, University of Kragujevac; Vojvođanska bančarska asocijacija (fictional banking association, Novi Sad).
The project developed a suite of calibrated frequency–severity models for cyber operational risk specific to the Western Balkans financial sector, where publicly available loss data are scarce and internal bank databases are small. Activities included collection of anonymised loss data from six participating banks under a data-sharing protocol approved by the National Bank of Serbia, development of a Bayesian LDA toolbox implemented in R, and delivery of three training workshops for bank risk managers. The project produced six journal papers, two conference contributions, and an open-access R package (CyLDA) deposited on GitHub. A policy brief was submitted to the National Bank of Serbia recommending adoption of a standardised loss data taxonomy compatible with ORX and the forthcoming DORA framework.

SYN-PRJ-0516.title: Cross-Border Operational Risk Data Infrastructure for SMEs in the Subotica–Pécs Corridor
SYN-PRJ-0516.text:
RISKDATA-HU-RS: Cross-Border Operational Risk Data Infrastructure for SMEs in the Subotica–Pécs Corridor (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0422 work package leader; R0120 team member; R0543 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs, Hungary; Regional Chamber of Commerce Subotica (fictional); Pécs Innovation and Enterprise Centre (fictional).
This cross-border cooperation project builds a shared operational risk data collection infrastructure for SMEs in the Subotica–Pécs corridor. The project collects standardised cyber and fraud incident reports from approximately 200 SMEs on both sides of the border, develops a joint anonymisation and pooling protocol, and constructs baseline actuarial models for frequency and severity by sector. Bálint leads Work Package 3, responsible for statistical model development and validation. Outputs include a bilingual (Hungarian–Serbian) self-assessment tool for SME cyber risk, a joint academic report, and a prototype data portal accessible to registered SME participants. The project addresses the absence of credible loss data for non-financial SMEs, which is the primary barrier to affordable cyber insurance in the region.

SYN-PRJ-0544.title: Vojvodina Language Resources: Computational Infrastructure for Minority Languages in a Multilingual Region
SYN-PRJ-0544.text:
VoiLaRes: Vojvodina Language Resources: Computational Infrastructure for Minority Languages in a Multilingual Region (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0292 principal investigator; R0309 team member; R0383 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad; Department of Rusyn Studies, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Slovak Language and Culture, Bačský Petrovec; Faculty of Letters, West University of Timișoara.
VoiLaRes aims to build a coordinated set of computational language resources—lexicons, annotated corpora, and baseline NLP tools—for the four official minority languages of Vojvodina: Hungarian, Slovak, Pannonian Rusyn, and Romanian. The project involves linguists from three Novi Sad institutions and one partner from Timișoara. Core outputs include morphological lexicons for Rusyn and Slovak adapted for computational use, a 250,000-token multi-genre corpus for each language with part-of-speech annotation, and a publicly accessible web interface for corpus search. The project also develops annotation guidelines that are deliberately cross-compatible with those used for Serbian, allowing future cross-lingual experiments. All resources are deposited in the CLARIN infrastructure under open licences.

SYN-PRJ-0545.title: Morphology as a Bridge: Transfer Learning Across South Slavic and Finno-Ugric Language Families
SYN-PRJ-0545.text:
MorphBridge: Morphology as a Bridge: Transfer Learning Across South Slavic and Finno-Ugric Language Families (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0292 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad; Research Institute for Linguistics, Budapest; Eötvös Loránd University, Budapest; Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, Novi Sad.
MorphBridge is a cross-border research and capacity-building project bringing together linguists and NLP researchers from Novi Sad and Budapest to study whether shared morphological feature spaces can systematically improve transfer learning between Serbian and Hungarian. The project constructs parallel annotated data sets in both languages across three domains (legal, medical, and news), runs a series of controlled transfer learning experiments comparing feature-based and representation-based transfer methods, and organises two joint summer schools for doctoral students from both sides of the border. Đurđica Kuzmanović leads the work package on data collection and annotation methodology. Project outputs include shared model checkpoints, a jointly authored technical report for language policy stakeholders, and course materials for the summer schools.

SYN-PRJ-0546.title: Mixed-Script Information Retrieval for South Slavic Administrative and Legal Documents
SYN-PRJ-0546.text:
MixIR: Mixed-Script Information Retrieval for South Slavic Administrative and Legal Documents (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0349 principal investigator.
Partners: Pravni fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu; Opštinska uprava Novi Sad — Služba za informatiku; Viši sud u Novom Sadu.
Projekat MixIR bavio se izgradnjom pretražnih sistema prilagođenih srpskim administrativnim i pravnim dokumentima koji sadrže mešovito pismo. Cilj je bio razvoj metodoloških osnova i softverskih alata za normalizaciju pisma, transliteraciju i rangiranje koji se mogu primeniti u javnom sektoru. U okviru projekta izgrađen je anotiran korpus od 150 000 dokumenata, razvijen je open-source modul za normalizaciju pisma kompatibilan s popularnim okvirima za pretragu, i sprovedene su tri pilot implementacije u saradnji s jednom opštinskom upravom i jednim regionalnim sudom. Rezultati su objavljeni u sedam naučnih radova i prezentovani na tri međunarodne konferencije.

SYN-PRJ-0554.title: Legal Text Classification for Under-Resourced Balkan Languages
SYN-PRJ-0554.text:
LEXICO: Legal Text Classification for Under-Resourced Balkan Languages (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2023).
Participants: R0484 principal investigator; R0039 team member; R1030 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad; School of Computing, Union University, Belgrade.
LEXICO addressed the absence of annotated legal corpora and pretrained language models tailored to Balkan languages with limited digital legal resources. The project assembled a multilingual corpus covering Serbian, Macedonian, and Bosnian court decisions (approximately 18,000 documents in total), established annotation guidelines for outcome and procedural-stage labels, and trained lightweight transformer models suitable for deployment on modest hardware. Deliverables included two publicly released datasets, three peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype web interface for case outcome screening used in a demonstration with a Belgrade-based legal aid organisation. The project was carried out entirely within Serbian institutions, with informal advisory input from collaborators at Masaryk University.

SYN-PRJ-0556.title: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains
SYN-PRJ-0556.text:
VERIFAI-RS: Verification and Explanation of AI-Generated Text in High-Stakes Domains (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0127 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade; Department of Computer Science, University of Pécs; Regional Legal Information Centre Novi Sad (observer partner).
The project investigated automated fact verification and explanation methods for AI-generated text with a focus on legal, medical, and financial documents in Serbian and English. The team built annotated corpora for hallucination detection, developed lightweight NLI models fine-tuned on domain-specific data, and designed a modular verification pipeline applicable to retrieval-augmented generation architectures. The project funded two PhD students and supported collaboration with the Faculty of Organisational Sciences, University of Belgrade, and the University of Pécs. Outputs include three datasets released under open licences, seven peer-reviewed publications, and a prototype verification module tested with a regional legal information provider.

SYN-PRJ-0558.title: Efficient Vector Search Infrastructures for Multilingual Document Repositories
SYN-PRJ-0558.text:
VECSEARCH: Efficient Vector Search Infrastructures for Multilingual Document Repositories (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0741 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research and Development of Serbia; Faculty of Law, University of Novi Sad.
The project investigates the co-design of approximate nearest-neighbour index structures and multilingual text encoders for document retrieval in public-sector repositories. Work packages cover: (1) encoder fine-tuning for South Slavic languages with limited supervision, (2) quantisation-aware index construction balancing recall and storage, and (3) a prototype retrieval service validated on a 10-million-document legal and administrative corpus provided by a partner institution. The project funds two PhD students and covers compute costs on the PARADOX-IV HPC cluster. An open benchmark dataset covering Serbian and Croatian legal documents is a planned deliverable.

SYN-PRJ-0559.title: Cross-Lingual Document Discovery in Regional Public Administration Archives
SYN-PRJ-0559.text:
CROSSDOC: Cross-Lingual Document Discovery in Regional Public Administration Archives (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0741 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; University of Debrecen, Faculty of Informatics, Hungary; City Archive of Subotica; Municipal Document Centre of Pécs, Hungary.
CROSSDOC aims to improve access to administrative documents held by Hungarian and Serbian public bodies by building a shared cross-lingual retrieval layer. The Serbian technical team, led by Todorović, is responsible for the index infrastructure work package, including the design of a federated index architecture that allows each national partner to retain custody of its documents while exposing a unified query interface. The system will be piloted with two municipal archives containing approximately 400,000 documents each. Hungarian-language tokenisation and transliteration components are contributed by the University of Debrecen partner.

SYN-PRJ-0568.title: Carbon Footprint Management Tools for Manufacturing SMEs in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0568.text:
CARBMAN: Carbon Footprint Management Tools for Manufacturing SMEs in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2021–2023).
Participants: R0859 work package leader.
Partners: Regional Development Agency of South Transdanubia, Pécs, Hungary; Vojvodina Development Agency, Novi Sad, Serbia; Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary.
CARBMAN aimed to develop and pilot a freely available carbon footprint calculation toolkit tailored to the data constraints of manufacturing SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region. The project produced a web-based data entry interface pre-loaded with regional emission factors, a report generator aligned with ISO 14067, and a training curriculum delivered through four workshops across Novi Sad, Subotica, and Pécs. Milan Sabo led the work package responsible for methodology development and tool validation, coordinating testing at five Serbian pilot companies. The project trained 68 company representatives. The toolkit was handed over to the Vojvodina Development Agency for ongoing maintenance after project closure.

SYN-PRJ-0583.title: Peak-Demand Reduction Strategies for Electrochemical Manufacturing Under Evolving Tariff Structures in Serbia
SYN-PRJ-0583.text:
PEAKSHIFT: Peak-Demand Reduction Strategies for Electrochemical Manufacturing Under Evolving Tariff Structures in Serbia (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0016 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Energy Research and Development, Belgrade.
The project investigated how changes in Serbian electricity tariff regulation affect the feasibility and design of load-shifting programmes at electrochemical manufacturing facilities. Research activities included: longitudinal monitoring of fourteen metal-finishing SMEs over three years; development and validation of a linear programming scheduling tool parameterised by process constraints and real-time metering; tariff sensitivity analysis covering four regulatory scenarios; and a comparative study of sites that had and had not implemented structured energy management. The project produced verified evidence that schedule optimisation under the 2021 revised tariff structure is economically attractive for a broader set of process configurations than under the previous structure. A freely available scheduling tool and user documentation were released under an open-source licence at project close.

SYN-PRJ-0591.title: Digital Twin Architectures for Sheet-Metal Forming Machines in SME Environments
SYN-PRJ-0591.text:
FORMTWIN: Digital Twin Architectures for Sheet-Metal Forming Machines in SME Environments (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2023–2026).
Participants: R0308 work package leader; R0377 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Kragujevac; Department of Manufacturing Science and Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Institute for Logistics and Production Systems, University of Miskolc; Metaloform d.o.o., Novi Sad; Acélszerkezet Kft., Győr; Lemezipari Zrt., Debrecen.
FORMTWIN brings together two Serbian and two Hungarian academic institutions with three SME partners operating sheet-metal job shops to develop practically deployable digital twin prototypes for press-brake and stamping machines. Bogićević leads Work Package 3, covering press-brake digital twin design, sensor integration, and FEM-based state estimation. The work package is producing a reference instrumentation kit (sensor selection, mounting guidelines, data-acquisition hardware) that the SME partners are piloting on their production machines. Deliverables include a software framework released under an open licence, two joint journal publications, and a training workshop held at the Science Technology Park Novi Sad. The project runs until mid-2026.

SYN-PRJ-0598.title: Environmental Performance Benchmarking and Compliance Support for Polymer Processors in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
SYN-PRJ-0598.text:
POLYENV: Environmental Performance Benchmarking and Compliance Support for Polymer Processors in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0277 coordinator; R0075 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering, University of Szeged; Regional Development Agency Vojvodina (RDEV); West Pannon Regional and Economic Development Public Nonprofit Ltd., Győr.
The project developed a shared environmental performance benchmarking toolkit for small and medium polymer processors operating in the Serbia–Hungary cross-border region. Activities included primary data collection at twenty-two facilities, construction of sector-specific environmental performance indicator sets, delivery of four compliance workshops attended by a total of 187 company representatives, and publication of a freely accessible online benchmarking platform. The Serbian side, coordinated by the University of Novi Sad team, focused on regulatory mapping and effluent characterisation, while the Hungarian partner contributed process energy monitoring data and LCI datasets. The project produced a multilingual guidance document on ISO 14001 implementation aligned with current Serbian and Hungarian permit requirements.

SYN-PRJ-0599.title: Life-Cycle Assessment Database for Mechanically Recycled Plastics from Southeast European Post-Consumer Streams
SYN-PRJ-0599.text:
RECYCLCA: Life-Cycle Assessment Database for Mechanically Recycled Plastics from Southeast European Post-Consumer Streams (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0277 principal investigator; R0055 team member; R0242 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Serbian Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA).
RECYCLCA aims to close a critical data gap in LCA practice by constructing verified, primary-data-based life-cycle inventory datasets for five categories of mechanically recycled plastics sourced from Serbian and regional post-consumer collection systems: HDPE bottles, PET bottles, PP packaging, mixed polyolefin film, and EPS. The project combines on-site measurement campaigns at three Serbian recycling facilities with uncertainty quantification and pedigree-matrix-based data quality assessment. Datasets are formatted for ecoinvent 3.x integration and will be made available under an open licence. A secondary objective is to train a cohort of twelve industry practitioners in LCA methodology through a structured workshop series delivered at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0631.title: Motivational Communication Strategies for Chronic Disease Prevention in Primary Care Settings in Vojvodina
SYN-PRJ-0631.text:
MOTIVOJNA: Motivational Communication Strategies for Chronic Disease Prevention in Primary Care Settings in Vojvodina (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0413 principal investigator.
Partners: Institute of Public Health Vojvodina, Novi Sad; Department of Family Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad; Health Centre Zrenjanin.
This project investigated the translation of laboratory-tested motivational communication principles into scalable brief interventions delivered in primary care consultations. The project trained 45 general practitioners and nurses in autonomy-supportive communication, developed and validated a Serbian-language motivational communication fidelity coding scheme, and conducted a stepped-wedge cluster trial across 12 primary care centres in Vojvodina targeting physical inactivity and poor dietary behaviour in adults with elevated cardiometabolic risk. The trial enrolled 680 patients followed over 18 months. Secondary objectives included identifying patient-level moderators of intervention response and producing a freely accessible practitioner training manual in Serbian.

SYN-PRJ-0699.title: Harmonic Mitigation Strategies for Multi-Level Inverter-Fed Industrial Drives in Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks
SYN-PRJ-0699.text:
HARMIND: Harmonic Mitigation Strategies for Multi-Level Inverter-Fed Industrial Drives in Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0567 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia; Faculty of Electronic Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia; Agroind Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin, Serbia.
The project investigated harmonic emission and mitigation strategies for cascaded H-bridge and neutral-point-clamped inverter drives connected to 6 kV and 10 kV industrial distribution networks. Work packages covered reformulated SHE-PWM methods, passive and hybrid active filter design, network-level harmonic interaction modelling in PSCAD, and a measurement campaign at two industrial sites in Vojvodina. The project involved collaboration with the Faculty of Electronic Engineering in Niš and a local industrial partner from the food processing sector. Results included improved SHE-PWM formulations tolerant to DC-link imbalance, validated filter design procedures, and a publicly available measurement dataset from the industrial sites.

SYN-PRJ-0727.title: Sensor Fixture Standardisation and Calibration Protocols for Acoustic Partial Discharge Monitoring in Distribution Transformers
SYN-PRJ-0727.text:
TRANSENSE: Sensor Fixture Standardisation and Calibration Protocols for Acoustic Partial Discharge Monitoring in Distribution Transformers (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0280 principal investigator; R1026 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia; JP Elektrovojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia.
This project addresses the lack of standardised procedures for mounting and calibrating piezoelectric acoustic emission sensors on power transformer tanks during field partial discharge measurements. The study produces engineering guidelines covering sensor type selection, minimum clamping force, coupling agent requirements, and reference signal verification procedures applicable to distribution transformers rated 35 kV and below. Laboratory experiments on a steel tank mockup and two decommissioned 10 MVA transformers provide the empirical basis. A draft protocol document suitable for adoption by distribution companies is one of the main deliverables. The project is conducted in cooperation with a regional distribution utility that provides access to out-of-service equipment and engineering input on practical constraints.

SYN-PRJ-0826.title: Quantitative Risk Assessment Methods for Regional Supply Chains in Vojvodina
SYN-PRJ-0826.text:
RISKCHAIN-VS: Quantitative Risk Assessment Methods for Regional Supply Chains in Vojvodina (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2024–2025).
Participants: R0750 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Regional Chamber of Commerce Novi Sad; Institute for Industrial Systems, Novi Sad.
This project develops quantitative tools for supply chain risk assessment tailored to small and medium-sized manufacturers operating in the Vojvodina region. The team combines Monte Carlo simulation, fault tree analysis, and multi-criteria scoring to produce a practical risk assessment toolkit that can be applied without specialised optimisation software. The project involves fieldwork with eight SMEs across the food processing and light manufacturing sectors in Vojvodina, collecting disruption event histories and procurement cost data. Deliverables include a documented methodology, a spreadsheet-based tool for risk scoring, and a set of case study reports. Lukács is responsible for the stochastic simulation component and co-authors the case study reports.

SYN-PRJ-0837.title: Bilateral Cooperation on Multilayer PVD Coating Architecture and Wear Performance in Interrupted Cutting
SYN-PRJ-0837.text:
CARBWEAR: Bilateral Cooperation on Multilayer PVD Coating Architecture and Wear Performance in Interrupted Cutting (bilateral, 2019–2021).
Participants: R0920 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Poland.
A two-year bilateral collaboration between the University of Novi Sad and Wrocław University of Science and Technology focused on multilayer TiAlN/TiN and TiAlN/CrN coatings for interrupted cutting conditions. Each side contributed deposition and characterisation capabilities; Wrocław provided coatings via their magnetron sputtering system and Novi Sad performed all turning tests and SEM/XRD analysis. Outcomes included two joint journal publications and a joint workshop held in Novi Sad in 2020. The collaboration provided foundational data for the bilayer period investigation published in Wear in 2022.

SYN-PRJ-0849.title: Performance Measurement Frameworks for ISO-Transitioning SMEs in the Danube Region
SYN-PRJ-0849.text:
PERFMAP: Performance Measurement Frameworks for ISO-Transitioning SMEs in the Danube Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0104 coordinator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Engineering, University of Miskolc; Regional Development Agency Vojvodina Nord, Subotica; Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Bács-Kiskun County, Kecskemét.
PERFMAP aimed to develop and disseminate practical performance measurement toolkits tailored to manufacturing SMEs in cross-border regions of Hungary and Serbia undergoing ISO 9001 transitions. The project combined empirical survey research across 140 companies, participatory tool development workshops in Novi Sad and Subotica, and a 12-month pilot in 18 volunteer companies. Outputs included a validated short-form BSC instrument, a pre-certification readiness checklist, and a freely accessible web-based self-assessment platform developed by the Hungarian partner. The project also supported four joint training events attended by approximately 200 quality managers and consultants. Two peer-reviewed journal publications and five conference papers were produced during the project period.

SYN-PRJ-0850.title: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness of Quality Management System Implementations in Serbian Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-0850.text:
QMSEVAL: Evaluating Long-Term Effectiveness of Quality Management System Implementations in Serbian Manufacturing (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0104 principal investigator; R0035 team member; R0988 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade; Serbian Chamber of Commerce – Association of Manufacturers.
QMSEVAL is a longitudinal study tracking operational and financial performance outcomes in 60 Serbian manufacturing SMEs across three years following ISO 9001 certification or recertification. The project applies a repeated-measures design with annual data collection combining company records, structured manager interviews, and external audit documentation. Analysis focuses on identifying factors that sustain post-certification performance gains versus those associated with performance drift. Secondary objectives include the development of a predictive model for post-certification performance and the validation of a composite performance index against independent financial audit data. The project supports one doctoral student and collaborates with the Faculty of Organizational Sciences, Belgrade, on survey design and data analysis.

SYN-PRJ-0857.title: Adaptive Statistical Process Control for Non-Normal Manufacturing Processes in the Western Balkans Plastics Industry
SYN-PRJ-0857.text:
ADAPTSPC: Adaptive Statistical Process Control for Non-Normal Manufacturing Processes in the Western Balkans Plastics Industry (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0048 principal investigator; R0859 team member; R0104 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia; PlastSerb d.o.o., Novi Sad, Serbia; Polymold Inženjering d.o.o., Subotica, Serbia.
The project develops a framework of adaptive CUSUM and EWMA monitoring schemes tailored to non-normal quality characteristics arising in injection moulding and extrusion. The work includes derivation of exact and approximate control limits for gamma, log-normal, and Burr XII process models, development of economic-statistical design procedures incorporating variable sampling intervals, and validation on process data collected from three Serbian plastics manufacturers. Software tools implementing the designed charts as add-ins to standard statistical packages are produced. The project also provides training workshops for quality engineers at partner companies and contributes to doctoral training at the Faculty of Technical Sciences.

SYN-PRJ-0986.title: Digital Typography Infrastructure for the Minority Languages of Vojvodina
SYN-PRJ-0986.text:
VOJVOTYPE: Digital Typography Infrastructure for the Minority Languages of Vojvodina (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2024–2026).
Participants: R0528 team member; R0438 team member; R0500 team member.
Partners: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad; Provincial Secretariat for Culture and Information, Vojvodina; Secondary School of Design Novi Sad (Srednja škola za dizajn Novi Sad).
The project addresses the absence of professionally engineered OpenType fonts for the six officially recognised minority languages of Vojvodina: Hungarian, Slovak, Romanian, Rusyn, Bunjevac, and Romani. The work plan covers character set analysis, encoding decisions, parametric master design, OpenType feature engineering, and release under open licences. Goran Radović is responsible for the Rusyn and Bunjevac workstreams, building directly on his doctoral research. The project also includes a teacher-training module for secondary-school graphic design programmes in Vojvodina, providing educators with structured materials for teaching multilingual desktop publishing. Deliverables include six font families, a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat, and a public web repository.

SYN-PRJ-0992.title: Legibility Standards for Age-Inclusive Hospital Signage in Cross-Border Healthcare Facilities
SYN-PRJ-0992.text:
SIGN-AGE: Legibility Standards for Age-Inclusive Hospital Signage in Cross-Border Healthcare Facilities (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2020–2023).
Participants: R0041 coordinator.
Partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad, Serbia; County Hospital Bács-Kiskun, Kecskemét, Hungary; University of Pécs, Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, Hungary.
The project addressed the lack of harmonised age-inclusive wayfinding standards in cross-border healthcare contexts between Serbia and Hungary. Activities included legibility testing of symbol–text combinations with older adult participants at partner hospitals on both sides of the border, development of a shared design specification document, and production of a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) signage template package. The project also delivered training workshops for facilities managers at four hospitals. The University of Novi Sad team led the perceptual testing work package and coordinated production of the final guideline document. The project resulted in a tested and piloted sign system implemented in one hospital facility in each country.

SYN-PRJ-0993.title: Towards a National Guideline for Wayfinding Sign Systems in Serbian Public Healthcare Facilities
SYN-PRJ-0993.text:
WAYFIND-RS: Towards a National Guideline for Wayfinding Sign Systems in Serbian Public Healthcare Facilities (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2022–2025).
Participants: R0041 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Oncology of Vojvodina, Sremska Kamenica; Institute for Standardisation of Serbia, Belgrade.
This project compiles empirical legibility data across a range of target user groups, lighting conditions, and sign configurations encountered in Serbian public hospitals, with the goal of generating evidence-based minimum requirements for a national guideline. The research programme includes field audits of 20 hospital facilities, controlled laboratory experiments on type size, symbol design, colour contrast, and material reflectance, and an extended consultation process with the Serbian Chamber of Engineers and the Ministry of Health. A draft guideline document is under preparation for submission to the Institute for Standardisation of Serbia as a basis for a national pre-standard.

SYN-PRJ-1024.title: Compositional Verification Techniques for Concurrent Industrial Software
SYN-PRJ-1024.text:
CONVER: Compositional Verification Techniques for Concurrent Industrial Software (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0728 principal investigator.
Partners: Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad; School of Electrical Engineering, University of Belgrade; Faculty of Automation and Computers, Politehnica University of Timișoara.
CONVER investigates compositional and modular model-checking methods that scale to the sizes of concurrent software found in industrial settings, particularly embedded control systems and communication middleware. The project develops assume-guarantee proof rules for timed systems, implements them as extensions to existing open-source tools, and evaluates them against benchmarks drawn from partner companies. A secondary objective is training: the project funds two PhD students and organises an annual two-day workshop on formal methods for regional practitioners. The project budget is approximately 4.8 million RSD. Deliverables include tool extensions, the VeriBench-C benchmark suite, and five peer-reviewed publications.

SYN-PRJ-1025.title: Formal Safety Analysis for Industrial Control Systems in Cross-Border Manufacturing
SYN-PRJ-1025.text:
SAFE-ICS: Formal Safety Analysis for Industrial Control Systems in Cross-Border Manufacturing (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0728 work package leader; R0134 team member; R0057 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Informatics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics; Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad; Termopack d.o.o., Novi Sad (fictional); Dunamenti Automatika Kft., Pécs (fictional).
SAFE-ICS is a cross-border cooperation project between Serbian and Hungarian academic partners and two small manufacturing companies. The project applies model checking and formal hazard analysis to programmable logic controllers used in food-processing and packaging equipment manufactured in the Vojvodina and Southern Transdanubia regions. Čániová leads the work package responsible for formal specification of safety requirements in timed CTL and their automated verification using UPPAAL. The project also develops training materials for control engineers with no prior formal-methods background. Expected outputs include three verified PLC case studies, a translated safety specification guideline, and a joint patent application currently under preparation.

SYN-PRJ-1056.title: Formal Models for IoT Device Behaviour Verification in Smart Infrastructure
SYN-PRJ-1056.text:
FORMIOT: Formal Models for IoT Device Behaviour Verification in Smart Infrastructure (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0416 coordinator.
Partners: Elektromont d.o.o., Novi Sad; Department of Mathematics and Informatics, University of Novi Sad.
FORMIOT investigates the application of formally inferred finite automaton models to the problem of verifying expected behaviour of IoT devices deployed in smart-building and smart-city infrastructure. The project establishes a testbed of 30 representative consumer and industrial IoT devices, collects long-term traffic datasets under normal and fault-injected conditions, and evaluates multiple inference algorithms on their ability to produce accurate and compact behavioural models. A particular focus is on encrypted-traffic scenarios where only metadata is available. Results are intended to inform procurement guidelines for IoT devices in public-sector infrastructure in Vojvodina. The project involves a local engineering company as an industry partner providing device access and domain expertise.

SYN-PRJ-1057.title: Danube Extreme Event Dependence: Multivariate Statistical Methods for Trans-boundary Flood and Drought Risk
SYN-PRJ-1057.text:
DANEX: Danube Extreme Event Dependence: Multivariate Statistical Methods for Trans-boundary Flood and Drought Risk (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2019–2022).
Participants: R0664 coordinator.
Partners: University of Pécs, Faculty of Sciences, Hungary; Directorate for Water Management Vojvodina, Novi Sad; North Transdanubian Water Directorate, Győr, Hungary.
DANEX addressed the lack of harmonised multivariate statistical tools for assessing compound flood and drought risk across the Hungarian–Serbian border reach of the Danube and its tributaries. The project assembled a shared archive of daily hydrometeorological records from 38 stations in the two countries, developed copula-based joint return period models calibrated on the pooled dataset, and produced risk maps at 1:25 000 scale for municipalities in the Bačka and Baranya regions. Training workshops were held in Novi Sad and Pécs for staff at regional water directorates. Open-source software implementing the statistical methods was released under an MIT licence. The project delivered three peer-reviewed publications and one technical standard recommendation submitted to the International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River.

SYN-PRJ-1058.title: Compound Hazard Probability Assessment for Serbian Critical Infrastructure
SYN-PRJ-1058.text:
COMPAS: Compound Hazard Probability Assessment for Serbian Critical Infrastructure (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0664 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Belgrade; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for the Development of Water Resources Jaroslav Černi, Belgrade.
COMPAS developed a probabilistic framework for quantifying compound hydrometeorological hazard at locations hosting critical infrastructure — water treatment plants, road bridges, electricity substations — in Serbia. The core methodological contribution was a vine copula model for simultaneous extreme discharge, extreme wind speed and extreme ice loading, with parameters estimated from heterogeneous observational records of differing lengths using a censored composite likelihood. Risk metrics including annual failure probability and 50-year maximum expected loss were computed for 27 infrastructure sites identified in consultation with the Ministry of Construction, Transport and Infrastructure. The project ran five stakeholder workshops and produced a publicly available hazard atlas covering Serbia at county resolution. Two graduate students completed their doctoral research within the project.

SYN-PRJ-1349.title: Corrosion Failure Mechanisms of High-Strength Fasteners in Aggressive Industrial Atmospheres
SYN-PRJ-1349.text:
FASTEN-COR: Corrosion Failure Mechanisms of High-Strength Fasteners in Aggressive Industrial Atmospheres (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2023–2026).
Participants: R0719 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade; Kovačnica Vojvodina d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project investigates the conditions under which high-strength structural fasteners fail by stress corrosion cracking or hydrogen embrittlement when exposed to polluted industrial atmospheric environments typical of petrochemical and power-generation facilities in the Vojvodina region. Research activities include laboratory simulation of atmospheric condensate chemistries, slow strain rate testing of candidate steel grades, electrochemical hydrogen permeation measurements, and post-fracture microscopic characterisation. Miloš Ivanović is responsible for the SSRT experimental programme and fractographic documentation tasks. The project consortium includes partners from the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad, the Institute for Testing of Materials Belgrade, and an industrial observer from the fastener manufacturing sector.

SYN-PRJ-1392.title: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows
SYN-PRJ-1392.text:
SOLIDFORM: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0151 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade; Farmaceutski Zavod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner).
The project established a tiered screening workflow integrating computational co-former selection (hydrogen-bond propensity and complementary functionality scoring) with experimental LAG, solution, and spray-drying screening for five poorly soluble APIs provided by a local formulation company. Characterisation relied on in-house PXRD, DSC-TGA, and Raman mapping, supplemented by access to solid-state NMR at a partner facility. Successful co-crystals were scaled to 50–100 g by twin-screw extrusion and assessed for dissolution improvement and physical stability under ICH storage conditions. The project trained two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed papers and three conference contributions.

SYN-PRJ-1710.title: Weld Condition Monitoring in Industrial Steel Structures Using Low-Cost Sensor Networks
SYN-PRJ-1710.text:
WELDMON: Weld Condition Monitoring in Industrial Steel Structures Using Low-Cost Sensor Networks (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0666 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Institute for Testing of Materials, Belgrade; Kovinarstvo Petrović d.o.o., Zrenjanin.
The project aimed to develop and field-test a practical SHM system specifically targeting weld fatigue damage in industrial steel structures. Activities included laboratory fatigue testing of representative weld joint geometries, development of automated OMA routines for edge-computing hardware, and 18-month deployments on two real industrial structures (a crane girder and a mezzanine frame) in Vojvodina. The project produced sensor placement guidelines, an open-source data processing pipeline, and a damage detection threshold framework accounting for temperature and operational load variability. Four journal papers, one conference paper, and a technical guideline document were produced. Two MSc students completed their theses within the project.

SYN-PRJ-1729.title: Evidence-Based Screencast Design Standards for Vocational Curricula in the Western Balkans
SYN-PRJ-1729.text:
VOCSCREEN: Evidence-Based Screencast Design Standards for Vocational Curricula in the Western Balkans (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0600 principal investigator; R0837 team member.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; Centre for Vocational and Adult Education, Belgrade; Secondary Vocational School Mihajlo Pupin, Kula; Technical School Nikola Tesla, Zrenjanin.
The project aimed to establish an empirically grounded set of design standards for screencasts used in Serbian secondary vocational education across six subject domains. The core activities included a large corpus study of 240 teacher-produced screencasts, three experimental studies with vocational students, development and validation of the SQR-Voc rubric, and a professional development module for vocational teachers. Partner schools were recruited across Vojvodina and the Belgrade region. The project produced 8 peer-reviewed outputs, trained 64 teachers through a pilot development programme, and delivered rubric materials freely available to vocational school curriculum coordinators. Total budget was approximately 3.2 million RSD.

SYN-PRJ-1747.title: Multi-Source Satellite Monitoring of Flood Dynamics and Wetland Hydroperiods in the Pannonian Plain
SYN-PRJ-1747.text:
PANNFLOOD: Multi-Source Satellite Monitoring of Flood Dynamics and Wetland Hydroperiods in the Pannonian Plain (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2021–2024).
Participants: R0424 principal investigator; R0700 team member; R1014 team member.
