Partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad; Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation, Novi Sad; Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad.
PANNFLOOD aimed to produce the first systematic, SAR-based hydroperiod climatology for wetland complexes in the Serbian portion of the Pannonian Plain. The project generated a continuous Sentinel-1 inundation record spanning 2015–2024, validated against in-situ canal gauge data, drone surveys, and field campaigns at six representative wetland sites. A coupled SAR–hydrological modelling component was developed to handle shallow inundation under dense canopy, building on the water-cloud model inversion methods developed in Zorić's earlier work. Outputs include open-access raster datasets, a technical report submitted to the Provincial Secretariat for Nature Protection, and peer-reviewed publications. The project employed one postdoctoral researcher and two PhD students.

SYN-PRJ-1810.title: National Normative Database for Cognitive and Scholastic Ability Tests in Serbian School-Age Children
SYN-PRJ-1810.text:
NORMSRB: National Normative Database for Cognitive and Scholastic Ability Tests in Serbian School-Age Children (Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma), 2020–2023).
Participants: R0627 principal investigator.
Partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Belgrade; Institute for Educational Research, Belgrade; Faculty of Education, University of Kragujevac.
This project aimed to collect a nationally representative normative dataset for three cognitive and two scholastic ability instruments, covering children aged 6–16 across all four Serbian statistical regions. Data collection involved 42 primary schools and 6,800 children, with stratification by region, settlement size, school type, and parental education. The project produced continuous norming tables using the cNORM methodology, developed open-access scoring software for school psychologists, and created a reusable anonymised dataset deposited with the Institute for Educational Research. A secondary aim was to document socioeconomic and regional variation in ability profiles to inform educational policy.

SYN-PRJ-1811.title: Adaptive Cognitive Screening for Early Educational Intervention in Vojvodina Schools
SYN-PRJ-1811.text:
ADAPTIVOED: Adaptive Cognitive Screening for Early Educational Intervention in Vojvodina Schools (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0627 coordinator.
Partners: Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad; Primary School Consortium of the South Bačka District; Centre for Applied Psychology, Novi Sad.
The project is developing and piloting a web-based adaptive cognitive screening platform for children aged 7–10 intended for use by school psychologists in Vojvodina. The platform draws on a pre-calibrated item bank of 120 items and applies a maximum information CAT algorithm with Sympson–Hetter exposure control. A feasibility trial in 12 Vojvodina schools (approximately 480 children) will evaluate usability, administration time, data quality, and school psychologist acceptance. The project includes a training component for educational practitioners and will produce open documentation for potential extension to other Serbian regions.

SYN-PUB-00168.title: Power-Quality Disturbances in Industrial Electroplating Baths: Field Measurements and Source Identification
SYN-PUB-00168.text:
Power-Quality Disturbances in Industrial Electroplating Baths: Field Measurements and Source Identification (2010, journal, Journal of Industrial Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: power quality; harmonics; electroplating; rectifier; THD.
Chromium and nickel electroplating rectifiers generate significant harmonic currents that propagate into the medium-voltage supply network and distort voltage waveforms across neighbouring loads. This study presents field measurements taken at three electroplating facilities in the Vojvodina region over a six-month period using calibrated power analysers at the point of common coupling and at individual rectifier cabinets. Total harmonic distortion of current (THDi) reached 28–41% at the rectifier terminals, with dominant fifth and seventh harmonics accounting for 70–75% of harmonic content. Voltage THD at the busbar exceeded the EN 50160 limit of 8% during peak-production shifts at two of the three sites. Passive LC filters tuned to the fifth harmonic were evaluated through simulation and on-site trials; measured THDi dropped to 9–12% post-installation. The paper discusses the correlation between production scheduling patterns and harmonic injection levels, and proposes a simplified screening method for rapid site classification based on installed rectifier capacity and shift timing.

SYN-PUB-00169.title: Energy-Flow Mapping Methodology for Batch Electrochemical Processing Lines
SYN-PUB-00169.text:
Energy-Flow Mapping Methodology for Batch Electrochemical Processing Lines (2012, journal, Energy and Process Engineering Review).
Authors: Ivona Matić (R0016); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Tibor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy-flow mapping; Sankey diagram; electrochemical processing; submetering; energy audit.
Batch electrochemical lines — including anodising, electroforming, and electrolytic degreasing — follow cyclical current and thermal profiles that complicate standard metering-based energy accounting. This paper develops a systematic energy-flow mapping methodology adapted for batch processes, combining continuous submetering of rectifier DC output, bath heating elements, ventilation, and effluent treatment units with material-balance cross-checks. The methodology was applied to two aluminium anodising lines at an automotive component supplier in Novi Sad. Sankey diagrams constructed from twelve weeks of logged data show that electrolytic heating accounted for 52–58% of total site electricity, while ventilation contributed 18–22%, figures substantially different from operator estimates. The procedure identifies a set of standardised measurement points sufficient to reconstruct full-site energy flows without permanently installed instrumentation on every sub-circuit, reducing audit preparation time by approximately 35% compared to a conventional audit protocol tested at the same facility.

SYN-PUB-00171.title: Thermal Imaging as a Supplementary Tool in Industrial Energy Audits of Electromechanical Equipment
SYN-PUB-00171.text:
Thermal Imaging as a Supplementary Tool in Industrial Energy Audits of Electromechanical Equipment (2015, journal, Journal of Industrial Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: thermography; energy audit; motor losses; power quality; electromechanical systems.
Infrared thermography is routinely used for predictive maintenance but is less commonly integrated into energy audits. This study examines how thermal imaging of motors, switchgear, and bus ducts can improve loss quantification during audits. At a Vojvodina-based electric motor rewinding and testing facility, thermographic surveys were conducted in parallel with power-quality logging at forty-two measurement points across two production shifts. Temperature anomalies on motor housings and cable terminations were correlated with measured copper and iron losses calculated from current and voltage waveforms. The combined approach identified six motors with winding insulation degradation whose measured electrical losses were 11–23% above nameplate expectations; replacing these with IEC IE3-class units was estimated to save 47 MWh per year. The paper presents a reproducible integration protocol and discusses the minimum qualification requirements for thermographers participating in energy audits at sites with live electrical equipment.

SYN-PUB-00173.title: Automated Submetering Architecture for Continuous Energy Monitoring in Electroplating Facilities
SYN-PUB-00173.text:
Automated Submetering Architecture for Continuous Energy Monitoring in Electroplating Facilities (2017, journal, Energy Monitoring and Control Systems).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Martin Zahorec (R0807); Mina Kecman (R0588); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: submetering; continuous monitoring; electroplating; data acquisition; energy management system.
Continuous energy monitoring in electroplating plants is complicated by the co-existence of high-current DC rectifier circuits, three-phase AC motor drives, and resistive heating loads on shared busbars. This paper describes a submetering architecture deployed at a zinc–nickel plating facility in Subotica, Serbia, consisting of twenty-four current-transformer-based sensors, a Modbus RTU data concentrator, and a cloud-accessible time-series database sampled at ten-second intervals. The system was validated against utility interval meters over a three-month commissioning period; discrepancy was below 1.2%. After twelve months of operation, the continuous data stream enabled identification of two systematic energy anomalies — a heating-bath thermostat hunting pattern adding 6.8 MWh per month, and an idle-run pattern on the rinsing-tank agitation motors consuming 3.1 MWh per month — neither of which had been visible in periodic audit snapshots. The paper discusses sensor selection criteria, installation challenges in corrosive environments, and data-management requirements for long-term monitoring.

SYN-PUB-00174.title: Demand-Side Management for Induction Furnace Operations: Scheduling Model and Industrial Trial
SYN-PUB-00174.text:
Demand-Side Management for Induction Furnace Operations: Scheduling Model and Industrial Trial (2018, conference, Proceedings of the South-East European Industrial Energy Conference).
Authors: Bojan Radovanović (outside co-author); Tibor Fekete (outside co-author); Valentina Russo (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: induction furnace; demand-side management; scheduling; peak demand; foundry.
Induction furnaces for aluminium scrap remelting draw power in distinct melt-and-hold cycles that produce sharp demand spikes. This study develops a mixed-integer scheduling model for a foundry operating three medium-frequency induction furnaces, with the objective of minimising monthly peak demand while satisfying production volume and delivery-deadline constraints. The model was parameterised using two months of measured power profiles and production logs from a Novi Sad foundry. Trial implementation of the derived schedule over a subsequent four-month period reduced measured monthly peak demand by 18.3% on average, compared with the operator's prior heuristic scheduling. The reduction corresponded to a verified tariff saving of approximately 4,200 EUR per month. The paper discusses the sensitivity of the schedule to scrap-charge variability and furnace downtime, and identifies the minimum telemetry needed to run the model in near-real-time using current meter readings as input.

SYN-PUB-00175.title: Energy Auditing of Electrochemical and Electromechanical Manufacturing: Methods and Case Studies
SYN-PUB-00175.text:
Energy Auditing of Electrochemical and Electromechanical Manufacturing: Methods and Case Studies (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Industrial Energy Management in South-East Europe (edited volume, University of Novi Sad Press)).
Authors: Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: energy audit; ISO 50001; electrochemical manufacturing; electromechanical manufacturing; case studies.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-00176.title: Reactive Power Compensation Planning for a Multi-Process Manufacturing Site with Dominant Rectifier and VSD Loads
SYN-PUB-00176.text:
Reactive Power Compensation Planning for a Multi-Process Manufacturing Site with Dominant Rectifier and VSD Loads (2020, journal, Journal of Industrial Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author); Martin Zahorec (R0807); Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Lars Brandt (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: reactive power compensation; power factor; harmonic resonance; active filter; manufacturing.
Manufacturing sites combining large rectifier installations and variable-speed drives present a reactive power compensation problem that static capacitor banks alone cannot solve reliably, owing to harmonic resonance risk. This paper reports a compensation planning study for a Vojvodina-based manufacturer of electric motors, where measured power-factor values ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 across shifts and monthly reactive energy penalties represented 8.3% of the total electricity bill. A combination of passive detuned capacitor banks and a 200 kVAr active filter was evaluated through simulation calibrated against six months of power-quality measurements. The selected solution — two detuned banks at 7% tuned to 189 Hz, plus the active filter on the rectifier feeder — achieved a simulated power factor of 0.968 under peak-load conditions. Post-installation measurements over three months confirmed a power factor of 0.952–0.971 and a 91% reduction in harmonic voltage distortion at the point of common coupling. Reactive energy penalty costs dropped by 87% relative to the pre-installation baseline.

SYN-PUB-00177.title: Baseline Setting and Measurement and Verification for Load-Shifting Interventions in Electrochemical Plants
SYN-PUB-00177.text:
Baseline Setting and Measurement and Verification for Load-Shifting Interventions in Electrochemical Plants (2021, journal, Energy Efficiency in Industry).
Authors: Bojan Radovanović (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Ildikó Tóth (R0927); Valentina Russo (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: measurement and verification; IPMVP; load shifting; electrochemical plant; baseline.
Measurement and verification (M&V) of demand-side management interventions in electrochemical manufacturing is complicated by process variability: bath temperature, electrolyte concentration, and substrate geometry all influence electrical load independently of scheduling decisions. This paper proposes an M&V protocol for load-shifting projects at electrochemical plants, adapted from the IPMVP Option B framework, with explicit correction procedures for three primary non-routine adjustment variables: production volume, bath-electrolyte conductivity, and ambient temperature. The protocol was applied retrospectively to data from load-shifting trials at five plating and anodising facilities. Corrected savings estimates differed from uncorrected estimates by between −11% and +19%, illustrating the importance of adjustment. The paper provides worked examples of the correction calculations and discusses the minimum monitoring requirements needed to apply the protocol at a new site, including which variables can be proxied from process-control logs rather than dedicated instrumentation.

SYN-PUB-00178.title: Impact of Time-of-Use Tariff Reform on Optimal Load-Scheduling in Serbian Metal Finishing SMEs
SYN-PUB-00178.text:
Impact of Time-of-Use Tariff Reform on Optimal Load-Scheduling in Serbian Metal Finishing SMEs (2022, journal, Energy Policy and Management Journal).
Authors: Jelena Ostojić (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: time-of-use tariff; load scheduling; metal finishing; SME; demand charge.
A revision to Serbian distribution tariff regulation in 2021 changed the red-zone window definitions and increased the demand charge coefficient, altering the economics of load-shifting for small and medium manufacturing enterprises. This paper analyses the impact of the tariff change on fourteen metal-finishing SMEs that had previously implemented schedule-based load-shifting recommendations. For each site, the pre-reform load schedules were re-optimised under the new tariff structure using a linear programming model driven by fifteen-minute interval meter data. In eleven of fourteen cases the optimal schedule window shifted by 60–90 minutes, and the achievable tariff saving increased by 4–14 percentage points relative to the pre-reform potential, because the new red-zone windows align better with natural gaps in surface-treatment process cycles. Three sites showed diminished benefit due to customer-driven delivery constraints that prevented schedule modification. The paper discusses implications for policy design and for the timing of investment in smart-metering infrastructure at SME level.

SYN-PUB-00179.title: On-Site Renewable Integration and Its Effect on Peak-Demand Management at an Electromechanical Assembly Plant: A Measured Case Study
SYN-PUB-00179.text:
On-Site Renewable Integration and Its Effect on Peak-Demand Management at an Electromechanical Assembly Plant: A Measured Case Study (2023, journal, Renewable and Industrial Energy Systems).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Christoph Huber (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: photovoltaic; peak-demand management; net metering; load shifting; electromechanical assembly.
Rooftop photovoltaic systems are increasingly installed at manufacturing sites in Serbia under net-metering arrangements, but their interaction with active peak-demand management programmes has received limited attention. This paper presents measured data from a 480 kWp rooftop PV installation at an electromechanical assembly plant in Novi Sad, combining twelve months of fifteen-minute PV generation and site demand data with tariff modelling. The analysis shows that PV generation reduces peak demand during summer afternoon hours by 60–130 kW on clear days, but introduces scheduling conflicts on overcast winter days when the coincidence of PV generation with the red-zone window is low. An adjusted load-shifting schedule that explicitly accounts for PV generation forecast uncertainty was developed and back-tested against the measured year; it reduced monthly peak demand by a further 8.3% on average compared with a schedule that ignores PV variability. The paper discusses practical forecasting approaches suitable for plant-level implementation without specialist meteorological expertise.

SYN-PUB-00180.title: Energy Intensity Indicators for Electrochemical Surface Treatment: Definition, Measurement Protocol, and Sector Benchmarks for the Western Balkans
SYN-PUB-00180.text:
Energy Intensity Indicators for Electrochemical Surface Treatment: Definition, Measurement Protocol, and Sector Benchmarks for the Western Balkans (2024, journal, Journal of Cleaner Production Processes).
Authors: Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Sanja Vidović (outside co-author); Marjan Petković (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: energy intensity; benchmarking; surface treatment; electroplating; Western Balkans.
Energy intensity metrics for electrochemical surface-treatment processes are not standardised, making it difficult to compare audit findings across facilities or to set evidence-based improvement targets. This paper proposes a set of process-level energy intensity indicators (EIIs) for five common surface-treatment technologies — zinc electroplating, chromium hard-plating, nickel plating, aluminium anodising, and electrolytic phosphating — each expressed per unit of treated surface area and per unit of coating thickness where applicable. The indicators were derived from measurements at twenty-two facilities across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia collected between 2019 and 2023. Sector benchmark distributions are reported as 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile values for each technology. The paper also describes a simplified measurement protocol for calculating site-level EIIs using only production records and monthly energy bills, enabling rapid self-assessment without a full instrument-based audit. Comparison of self-assessed EIIs against instrument-verified values at eight sites showed agreement within ±9%.

SYN-PUB-00181.title: Data-Driven Detection of Abnormal Energy Consumption Patterns in Continuous Electroforming Lines Using Statistical Process Control Charts
SYN-PUB-00181.text:
Data-Driven Detection of Abnormal Energy Consumption Patterns in Continuous Electroforming Lines Using Statistical Process Control Charts (2026, preprint, engrXiv preprint server).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author); Ivona Matić (R0016).
Keywords: statistical process control; CUSUM; EWMA; electroforming; anomaly detection.
Continuous electroforming lines for copper foil and nickel mesh production run at near-constant current density for days or weeks at a time, making gradual efficiency degradation difficult to detect from periodic audits. This preprint describes the application of statistical process control (SPC) methods — specifically CUSUM and EWMA charts — to time-series energy data from two continuous electroforming lines in Serbia and one in Romania, logged at one-minute resolution over eight and eleven months respectively. Chart parameters were tuned using three months of baseline data collected immediately after a confirmed maintenance overhaul. The charts correctly flagged three anode degradation events and one electrolyte-temperature drift event across the monitoring periods, each confirmed retrospectively by maintenance logs. Average detection lag was 4.2 hours, compared with an estimated 60–180 hours for detection by operator observation alone. The preprint discusses the sensitivity-specificity trade-off under different chart parameterisations and provides guidance on adapting the approach to other constant-rate electrochemical processes.

SYN-PUB-00208.title: Cyber Insurance Pricing for SMEs Using Credibility Theory: Evidence from Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-00208.text:
Cyber Insurance Pricing for SMEs Using Credibility Theory: Evidence from Vojvodina (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Regional Conference on Insurance and Actuarial Science, Ljubljana).
Authors: Petra Horváth (outside co-author); Ivana Lukić (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422); Lidija Ranković (R0018).
Keywords: credibility theory; cyber insurance; SME; Bühlmann–Straub; Vojvodina.
This paper applies Bühlmann–Straub credibility theory to cyber insurance pricing for small and medium enterprises, using a dataset of 127 SMEs in the Vojvodina region that participated in a voluntary risk disclosure programme between 2019 and 2022. Each firm reports annual cyber incident counts and aggregate losses; the dataset yields 381 firm–year observations. Credibility weights are computed per firm size class (micro, small, medium) and per industry sector. The resulting credibility-weighted frequency and severity parameters are compared to class-mean priors; the average credibility weight across firms is 0.41, reflecting the limited length of individual histories. Simulated insurance premiums based on the credibility model differ from those based on class-mean parameters by up to 23% for individual firms. The paper discusses how technology parks and business incubators could facilitate the data pooling arrangements needed to expand such credibility datasets.

SYN-PUB-00225.title: Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata
SYN-PUB-00225.text:
Uticaj morfološke redukcije na preciznost pretrage srpskih višeskriptnih dokumenata (2013, journal, Infoteka: Časopis za informatiku i bibliotekarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Petar Hadžić (R0019).
Keywords: morfološka analiza; stemovanje; višeskriptni tekst; srpski jezik; rangiranje.
Srpski jezik je morfološki bogat, što znači da ista leksema može imati nekoliko desetina flektivnih oblika. U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa. Koristimo tri stemera dostupna za srpski jezik — dva pravilo-zasnovana i jedan statistički — i kombinujemo ih s fonemskim kanonizacionim korakom opisanim u prethodnim radovima. Evaluacija je sprovedena na podskupu CLEF 2012 kolekcije koji sadrži dokumente u oba pisma. Rezultati pokazuju da redosled operacija (stemovanje pre ili posle normalizacije skripte) utiče na odziv, pri čemu stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije (poboljšanje od 4 do 9 procentnih poena u MAP). Rad daje i analizu grešaka za 50 ručno pregledanih upita.

SYN-PUB-00336.title: Quantisation Effects on Convolutional Neural Networks for Vibration-Based Fault Detection Deployed on Cortex-M7
SYN-PUB-00336.text:
Quantisation Effects on Convolutional Neural Networks for Vibration-Based Fault Detection Deployed on Cortex-M7 (2020, journal, Microprocessors and Embedded Computing).
Authors: Vesna Knežević (R0206); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Olivera Kuzmanović (R0028); Claudia Bauer (outside co-author).
Keywords: post-training quantisation; 1-D CNN; Cortex-M7; fault detection; mixed precision.
Post-training quantisation (PTQ) of floating-point convolutional neural networks to 8-bit fixed-point is a standard step for microcontroller deployment, but its effect on detection sensitivity for subtle bearing faults is not well characterised. This paper trains a small five-layer 1-D CNN on 30000 vibration segments (2048 samples each, 25.6 kHz) covering five fault categories and a healthy class, then applies symmetric and asymmetric per-layer and per-channel PTQ schemes. Accuracy degradation from float32 to int8 ranged from 0.4% (per-channel asymmetric) to 3.8% (per-layer symmetric) on the test set. Flash footprint dropped from 187 kB to 51 kB, and inference on an STM32H743 at 480 MHz required 4.1 ms, fitting comfortably within a 10 ms real-time budget. An ablation study shows that quantisation of the first convolutional layer accounts for 60–70% of total accuracy loss, suggesting a mixed-precision strategy where only that layer remains in float16.

SYN-PUB-00345.title: Comparing Autoencoder Architectures for Anomaly Scoring in Web Server Access Logs
SYN-PUB-00345.text:
Comparing Autoencoder Architectures for Anomaly Scoring in Web Server Access Logs (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Machine Learning Systems (CEWMS)).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Tamás Fekete (outside co-author); Jovana Milinković (outside co-author).
Keywords: autoencoder; web server logs; anomaly scoring; AUROC; reconstruction error.
We evaluate four autoencoder designs—shallow, deep, variational, and denoising—for scoring anomalies in Apache access logs gathered from three production web services over 90 days. Input features include request method, status code, payload size, inter-arrival time, and URI path hash. Each architecture is trained on a 70-day clean baseline and tested on 20 days containing 1,247 manually labelled anomalies spanning DDoS precursors, crawler bursts, and authentication brute-force sequences. The denoising autoencoder achieves the highest AUROC of 0.91, while the variational model offers better calibration of reconstruction-error thresholds. We find that log volume spikes caused by legitimate marketing campaigns substantially raise false-positive rates unless a session-level normalisation step is applied. Processing latency for the best model is 18 ms per 10,000 requests on a single GPU, making online deployment feasible. Code and anonymised dataset excerpts are released.

SYN-PUB-00346.title: Temporal Pattern Mining in Multi-Source Event Logs Using Frequent Episode Discovery
SYN-PUB-00346.text:
Temporal Pattern Mining in Multi-Source Event Logs Using Frequent Episode Discovery (2016, journal, Expert Systems with Applications in Network Engineering).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Bogdan Cvetković (outside co-author); Árpád Nagy (R0564); Renata Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: episode mining; event correlation; multi-source logs; SNMP; hierarchical clustering.
Frequent episode discovery is applied to correlated event sequences drawn simultaneously from OS syslogs, application logs, and SNMP traps in a mid-sized enterprise network. The study covers a 14-month trace comprising events from 120 devices. Episodes are mined at three temporal granularities (1 s, 10 s, 60 s) and ranked by a lift-based interestingness measure. Results show that 83% of confirmed incidents correspond to at least one high-lift episode identified at the 10-second granularity, while per-source mining misses 41% of the same incidents. A post-processing step uses agglomerative hierarchical clustering to group structurally similar episodes, reducing the analyst's review set from ~9,000 raw episodes to 214 episode families. The paper also discusses the computational cost of episode mining as event rates grow, reporting quadratic scaling behaviour beyond roughly 50,000 events per second on commodity hardware.

SYN-PUB-00347.title: Benchmarking Stream Processing Engines for Real-Time Log Anomaly Detection Pipelines
SYN-PUB-00347.text:
Benchmarking Stream Processing Engines for Real-Time Log Anomaly Detection Pipelines (2017, conference, Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Distributed Computing and Data Streams (DCDS)).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Stefan Radović (outside co-author); Ioana Popa (outside co-author).
Keywords: Apache Flink; stream processing; isolation forest; one-class SVM; throughput benchmarking.
This study compares Apache Flink, Apache Storm, and a custom lightweight engine for deploying log anomaly detection models in a streaming context. Three detection algorithms—isolation forest, one-class SVM, and a sliding-window statistical method—are embedded into each engine and evaluated on synthetic log streams injected at rates from 10,000 to 500,000 events per second. Metrics collected include end-to-end latency, throughput, CPU and memory footprint, and detection recall under backpressure conditions. Flink exhibits the most stable latency (median 7 ms at 200 k events/s) and the lowest performance degradation when detection model inference time increases. The one-class SVM degrades most severely under high throughput, dropping recall from 0.88 to 0.61 at 400 k events/s due to feature computation bottlenecks. Recommendations for practitioners on engine and algorithm pairing are provided.

SYN-PUB-00348.title: Log Parsing at Scale: Evaluating Drain, Spell, and AEL on Industrial SCADA Event Logs
SYN-PUB-00348.text:
Log Parsing at Scale: Evaluating Drain, Spell, and AEL on Industrial SCADA Event Logs (2018, journal, Computers in Industry — Eastern European Special Edition).
Authors: Nikola Štrbac (outside co-author); Vladana Vojnović (R0030).
Keywords: log parsing; SCADA; Drain; event templates; OT logs.
Log parsing is a prerequisite for machine learning on unstructured log data, yet most parsing benchmarks use IT rather than operational technology (OT) logs. This paper evaluates three representative parsers—Drain, Spell, and Abstracting Event Log (AEL)—on logs collected from two SCADA systems in a regional water treatment facility and a district heating network, totalling 22 million lines across eight months. Evaluation uses grouping accuracy against a manually annotated ground truth of 310 distinct event templates. Drain achieves 94.1% grouping accuracy on water-treatment logs but drops to 81.7% on heating-network logs, where message formats are less regular. A hybrid pre-processing step combining domain-specific token masking with Drain raises accuracy to 97.4% on both corpora. Parser throughput, sensitivity to depth and similarity-threshold hyperparameters, and degradation under firmware update events are also analysed in detail.

SYN-PUB-00349.title: Correlated Anomaly Detection Across Microservice Traces and Infrastructure Logs Using Graph-Based Clustering
SYN-PUB-00349.text:
Correlated Anomaly Detection Across Microservice Traces and Infrastructure Logs Using Graph-Based Clustering (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management).
Authors: Predrag Antonić (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484); Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Markus Brandl (outside co-author); Jovana Milinković (outside co-author).
Keywords: microservices; Kubernetes; graph clustering; Louvain; distributed tracing.
Modern applications generate interleaved traces from dozens of microservices alongside infrastructure logs from the underlying Kubernetes nodes. This paper proposes representing concurrent events as nodes in a time-attributed multigraph, where edges encode causal or temporal co-occurrence within a configurable window. Community detection via the Louvain algorithm is then applied to identify correlated anomaly clusters. Experiments are conducted on a synthetic microservice benchmark (8 services, 14 days, 4.3 billion events) with injected faults covering latency spikes, pod crashes, and network partitions. The graph-based approach achieves a macro-averaged F1 of 0.84 for fault-type classification, compared to 0.71 for an independent per-log isolation forest baseline. Memory consumption grows linearly with the number of active trace IDs, reaching 6.2 GB at peak load in the test environment. A pruning strategy based on trace-completion events reduces memory usage by 38%.

SYN-PUB-00350.title: Self-Tuning Threshold Selection for Streaming Anomaly Detectors Under Non-Stationary Log Distributions
SYN-PUB-00350.text:
Self-Tuning Threshold Selection for Streaming Anomaly Detectors Under Non-Stationary Log Distributions (2021, journal, Journal of Network and Systems Management).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Cosmin Alupoaei (outside co-author).
Keywords: extreme value theory; adaptive thresholding; distribution shift; autoencoder; streaming.
Fixed reconstruction-error thresholds for autoencoder-based anomaly detectors become unreliable when log distributions shift due to application updates, workload changes, or seasonal traffic patterns. This paper introduces a threshold adaptation scheme based on extreme value theory (EVT), specifically fitting a generalised Pareto distribution to the tail of recent reconstruction errors in a sliding window of configurable width. The scheme is evaluated on four real-world log datasets with documented distribution shifts: a university web portal (50 days), an e-commerce backend (90 days), a CI/CD pipeline (120 days), and a virtualised telecom switching platform (60 days). Compared to static thresholds and a simple percentile-based method, the EVT approach reduces false-positive rates by between 22% and 47% depending on dataset, while maintaining recall above 0.87 in all four cases. Computational overhead of threshold updates is under 2 ms per window step.

SYN-PUB-00351.title: Unsupervised Detection of Lateral Movement in Enterprise Networks via Windows Event Log Correlation
SYN-PUB-00351.text:
Unsupervised Detection of Lateral Movement in Enterprise Networks via Windows Event Log Correlation (2022, conference, Proceedings of the 18th European Symposium on Research in Cybersecurity (ESRC)).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Aleksa Đorđević (outside co-author); Tamás Fekete (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233).
Keywords: lateral movement; Windows event logs; graph autoencoder; MITRE ATT&CK; enterprise security.
Lateral movement by adversaries typically produces subtle, distributed signals across Windows Security Event Logs on multiple hosts. This study constructs user-host access graphs from Security Event IDs 4624, 4648, 4768, and 4769 collected over 30 days from a 600-host enterprise test environment, with synthetic lateral movement sequences injected following MITRE ATT&CK patterns. Node embeddings derived from a graph autoencoder are clustered with k-means; cluster membership deviation is used as an anomaly score. The method detects 19 of 24 injected lateral movement chains with a false-positive rate of 3.2 per day—substantially below the 11.7 per day produced by a signature-based SIEM rule set. A user-facing triage interface ranks suspicious chains by graph anomaly score. Limitations around encrypted Kerberos traffic and pass-the-hash variants that bypass standard logging are discussed.

SYN-PUB-00352.title: Log-Based Predictive Maintenance for Conveyor Belt Controllers: A Case Study from a Food-Processing Plant
SYN-PUB-00352.text:
Log-Based Predictive Maintenance for Conveyor Belt Controllers: A Case Study from a Food-Processing Plant (2023, journal, Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Milica Labus (outside co-author); Zoran Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: predictive maintenance; PLC logs; isolation forest; industrial IoT; Vojvodina.
Predictive maintenance using log data from industrial programmable logic controllers (PLCs) is explored in a food-processing facility in Vojvodina operating 14 conveyor belt lines. PLC diagnostic logs recording motor current deviations, sensor timeouts, and safety interlock triggers were collected over 18 months, yielding approximately 9.4 million log entries and 38 confirmed maintenance events. A combination of sliding-window frequency features and an isolation forest classifier trained on normal operating periods is used to flag degradation precursors. Leave-one-out cross-validation across the 38 events yields a mean warning lead time of 4.3 hours before failure with a precision of 0.79 and recall of 0.87. The paper describes practical challenges including irregular maintenance windows that contaminate normal-operation labels and proprietary log formats that required manual template construction.

SYN-PUB-00353.title: Dimension Reduction Strategies for Log Embeddings in High-Throughput Anomaly Detection: UMAP, PCA, and Random Projections Compared
SYN-PUB-00353.text:
Dimension Reduction Strategies for Log Embeddings in High-Throughput Anomaly Detection: UMAP, PCA, and Random Projections Compared (2024, journal, ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data).
Authors: Predrag Antonić (outside co-author); Rastko Zorić (R0148); Nora Varga (outside co-author); Vladana Vojnović (R0030).
Keywords: UMAP; PCA; random projections; log embeddings; dimension reduction.
Log embedding vectors derived from transformer-based language models are high-dimensional (768–1024 dimensions) and expensive to process at stream-processing speeds. This paper systematically compares three dimension-reduction strategies—PCA, random projections, and UMAP—for use in downstream anomaly detection on log streams, evaluating trade-offs between compression ratio, anomaly detection accuracy, and reduction latency. Experiments use four publicly available log datasets augmented with two proprietary datasets from partners, covering syslog, HDFS, BGL supercomputer logs, and application logs from a regional ISP. At a 32-dimensional target, UMAP preserves anomaly structure best (AUROC 0.89 averaged across datasets) but requires 14× more time to fit than PCA. Random projections at 64 dimensions achieve AUROC 0.84 with negligible fitting overhead, making them preferable in continuously retraining deployments. Interaction effects between reduction method and downstream detector type are analysed with a factorial experimental design.

SYN-PUB-00354.title: Federated Anomaly Detection on Distributed Log Streams Without Raw Data Sharing
SYN-PUB-00354.text:
Federated Anomaly Detection on Distributed Log Streams Without Raw Data Sharing (2025, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Machine Learning for Networked Systems (MLNS)).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Aleksa Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: federated learning; privacy-preserving; distributed logs; federated averaging; autoencoder.
Many organisations are willing to participate in shared anomaly detection initiatives but cannot transfer raw logs off-premises due to regulatory or competitive concerns. This paper proposes a federated learning framework in which each participant trains a local autoencoder on its own log streams and shares only model parameter gradients with a central aggregator. Experiments involve five simulated organisations with heterogeneous log formats (web, database, VPN, mail, and DNS servers) and deliberately asynchronous update schedules. Federated averaging and two robust aggregation strategies (coordinate-wise median and trimmed mean) are compared. The federated model achieves AUROC within 0.04 of a centrally trained oracle model on anomalies present across multiple participants, though performance degrades for organisation-specific anomaly types unique to a single participant. Communication overhead per round is under 12 MB per participant.

SYN-PUB-00355.title: Temporal Causality Inference Between Correlated Log Events Using Granger-Inspired Tests on Count Time Series
SYN-PUB-00355.text:
Temporal Causality Inference Between Correlated Log Events Using Granger-Inspired Tests on Count Time Series (2026, journal, Knowledge and Information Systems).
Authors: Vladana Vojnović (R0030); Milica Labus (outside co-author); Cosmin Alupoaei (outside co-author); Markus Brandl (outside co-author).
Keywords: Granger causality; count time series; event correlation; root cause analysis; ERP logs.
Distinguishing genuine causal relationships between event types from spurious temporal correlations is a persistent challenge in multi-source log analysis. This paper adapts Granger causality testing to discrete-valued count time series formed by bucketing log event occurrences at 1-second resolution. A negative binomial regression model accounts for overdispersion common in log count data. The approach is validated on a synthetic dataset of 50 known causal pairs injected into background traffic and on a real 90-day production log corpus from a cloud-hosted ERP system. On the synthetic data, the method recovers 46 of 50 causal pairs at a 5% false-discovery-rate threshold; on the production corpus, six previously unknown causal pairs are identified that collectively explain a recurring five-minute service degradation whose root cause had been unresolved for over a year. Sensitivity to bucket width and minimum event frequency is characterised.

SYN-PUB-00403.title: Firmware Architecture for Bridging CANopen DS401 and ISO 11783 in Retrofit Sensor Modules
SYN-PUB-00403.text:
Firmware Architecture for Bridging CANopen DS401 and ISO 11783 in Retrofit Sensor Modules (2015, journal, Journal of Agricultural Mechatronics and Control Systems).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Miroslav Đurić (outside co-author); Žarko Gavrilović (R0033); Aneta Vukić (outside co-author); László Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: CANopen DS401; ISOBUS gateway; STM32F4; PDO mapping; protocol bridging.
Many older agricultural implements carry CANopen-based sensors that cannot communicate directly with ISOBUS task controllers. This work describes a firmware architecture for a compact gateway ECU that translates CANopen DS401 digital and analogue I/O process-data objects (PDOs) into ISO 11783 process data messages, enabling legacy sensors to participate in precision-farming data flows without hardware replacement. The gateway is built around an STM32F4 microcontroller and uses two independent CAN controllers operating at 250 kbit/s and 500 kbit/s. Mapping tables are stored in flash and configurable through an ISOBUS virtual terminal menu. Field trials on a 120-hectare test plot with a John Agro tractor (fictional) and a three-section sprayer boom demonstrated 99.6% message delivery over six-hour continuous sessions. Object dictionary alignment issues introduced by vendor-specific CANopen profiles are discussed and a resolution strategy using sub-index remapping is presented.

SYN-PUB-00405.title: Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform
SYN-PUB-00405.text:
Calibration of a Battery Cell Emulator for BMS ECU Validation on a Low-Cost HiL Platform (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 15th European Conference on Power Electronics and Embedded Control (EPEC)).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author); Žarko Gavrilović (R0033); Cristian Morariu (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: battery cell emulator; BMS ECU; Zynq SoC; impedance emulation; HiL calibration.
Battery management system (BMS) ECUs require accurate emulation of cell voltages, temperatures, and internal impedances during validation testing. This paper describes the design and calibration of a 12-cell emulator board built from precision voltage references, operational amplifier buffers, and a digitally programmable resistor network to model ohmic and diffusion impedances. The board interfaces to a Zynq-7020 SoC running the simulation host and updates cell parameters at 10 ms intervals via SPI. Calibration was performed against a reference Keithley source-measure unit across the 2.5–4.2 V operating range; voltage accuracy after calibration was ±2.1 mV at 25 °C and ±4.8 mV over the −20 °C to 60 °C range. A lithium iron phosphate cell model with 18 parameters was validated against 12 published drive-cycle datasets. A commercial BMS ECU was tested using 88 scripted test cases including cell balancing activation, state-of-charge estimation accuracy, and over-voltage protection response time. The total bill of materials for the emulator board was 280 EUR.

SYN-PUB-00478.title: Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data
SYN-PUB-00478.text:
Co-crystal formation between furosemide and three pyridine derivatives: structural inference from PXRD and Raman spectroscopy in the absence of single-crystal data (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 6th Central European Symposium on Pharmaceutical Technology).
Authors: Marija Petrović (outside co-author); Vasilije Ivković (R0038); Vesna Ilić (outside co-author); Lidija Radić (R0151).
Keywords: furosemide; co-crystal; Raman spectroscopy; PXRD indexing; FaSSIF.
Three co-crystals of furosemide (a poorly soluble loop diuretic) with 2-aminopyridine, 3-hydroxypyridine, and 4,4′-bipyridine were prepared by LAG with acetonitrile and characterised entirely in polycrystalline form. Single crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction could not be grown from any of the nine solvent systems attempted. Structural inference relied on indexing of PXRD patterns (DICVOL06 and TREOR90 algorithms), lattice parameter comparison with Cambridge Structural Database entries, and Raman band shifts. The carbonyl stretch of furosemide at 1678 cm⁻¹ shifted to 1663 cm⁻¹ in the 2-aminopyridine co-crystal, consistent with N–H···O hydrogen bonding. Quantitative phase analysis of DSC data confirmed 1:1 stoichiometry for all three co-crystals by molar enthalpy comparison. Dissolution experiments in simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF) at 37 °C showed 1.5-, 1.9-, and 1.3-fold increases in maximum dissolved concentration for the three co-crystals, respectively. The 3-hydroxypyridine co-crystal showed a spring-and-parachute effect with maximum concentration maintained for 120 minutes.

SYN-PUB-00488.title: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware
SYN-PUB-00488.text:
Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbour Retrieval for Embedding-Based Recommenders: A Benchmark on Commodity Hardware (2024, journal, Information Retrieval Journal).
Authors: Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Anita Bošnjak (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: approximate nearest neighbour; HNSW; embedding retrieval; two-stage recommendation; scalability.
Two-stage recommenders use approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search to retrieve candidate items from a learned embedding space before a more expensive ranking model re-scores them. We benchmark five ANN index structures—HNSW, IVF-Flat, IVF-PQ, ScaNN, and a flat exact baseline—on three embedding spaces of different dimensionalities (64, 128, 256) and catalogue sizes (50K, 500K, 5M items) using recall@100 and query latency at fixed memory budgets on a single server with 64 GB RAM and no GPU. HNSW achieves the best recall–latency trade-off for catalogues up to 500K items; IVF-PQ becomes competitive at 5M items under 16 GB memory constraints. We also measure how ANN retrieval recall translates to end-to-end NDCG@10 degradation and find that recall@100 above 0.92 causes less than 1% NDCG loss relative to exact retrieval. A practical configuration guide is included.

SYN-PUB-00492.title: Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams
SYN-PUB-00492.text:
Incremental Gaussian Mixture Models for Online Anomaly Detection in Continuous ICS Traffic Streams (2018, journal, Control Engineering Practice).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Ivković (R0039); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: incremental learning; Gaussian mixture model; online detection; concept drift; district heating.
This paper proposes an incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic without the need for periodic full retraining. The algorithm maintains a fixed number of Gaussian components (K = 5 to 20 evaluated) and uses a Bayesian update rule to adjust component means, covariances, and weights with each arriving window of observations. Feature vectors are 32-dimensional, derived from 10-second traffic windows. The method was evaluated on a 180-day Modbus/TCP capture from a district heating control network and compared with a static GMM retrained every 24 hours. The iGMM maintained an F1 score within 0.03 of the periodically retrained model while reducing retraining compute cost by 94%. Concept drift induced by a planned process reconfiguration was detected as a persistent anomaly episode; a supervised reset mechanism based on operator acknowledgement was proposed and tested. Memory footprint per detector instance was under 120 KB.

SYN-PUB-00509.title: Legibility thresholds of directional arrows in hospital corridor signage: a controlled viewing-distance study
SYN-PUB-00509.text:
Legibility thresholds of directional arrows in hospital corridor signage: a controlled viewing-distance study (2010, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Milena Vranić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Milica Ostojić (R0290).
Keywords: directional arrows; legibility distance; stroke width; illuminance; hospital signage.
This study measured the critical viewing distance at which 42 adult participants could correctly identify seven directional arrow variants used in Serbian public hospital signage. Stimuli were printed on matte substrates and presented under three illuminance levels (50 lx, 150 lx, and 500 lx) in a light-tight chamber. Arrow width-to-height ratio, stroke width, and arrowhead angle were varied systematically across 21 design conditions. Participants identified the direction of travel indicated by each arrow from distances ranging from 1 m to 18 m in 0.5 m increments. Results showed that reducing stroke width below 12% of symbol height caused identification accuracy to drop below 90% at distances exceeding 8 m even at 500 lx. Arrowhead angles between 40° and 55° yielded the highest identification rates across all illuminance levels. Recommendations for minimum stroke width and arrowhead geometry are proposed for standardisation within hospital wayfinding guidelines in Serbia.

SYN-PUB-00510.title: Pictogram comprehension across age groups in a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-00510.text:
Pictogram comprehension across age groups in a tertiary care hospital in Vojvodina (2012, journal, Applied Ergonomics and Design).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Marija Čolić (R0325); Katalin Fehér (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: pictogram comprehension; age groups; ISO 7001; healthcare pictograms; text–symbol pairing.
The study assessed comprehension rates of 30 ISO 7001 transport and healthcare-related pictograms among three age groups (18–35, 36–59, 60–79 years; n = 180 total, 60 per group) recruited in the waiting areas of a large regional hospital. Participants were shown each pictogram individually on a calibrated tablet display at a standardised ambient luminance of 200 cd/m² and asked to state its meaning without any contextual cues. A second session introduced a bilingual Serbian–Hungarian text label beneath the symbol. Comprehension scores without labels averaged 58% for the 60–79 age group compared to 79% for the 18–35 group. Adding text labels raised overall comprehension to 91% but reduced the benefit specifically for pictograms with ambiguous spatial relationships. Sixteen pictograms fell below the ISO-recommended 67% comprehension threshold when tested without labels in the oldest group. The findings support mandatory text pairing in wayfinding applications targeting mixed-age hospital populations.

SYN-PUB-00511.title: Colour contrast ratios in existing hospital wayfinding systems: an audit of twelve facilities in Serbia and Croatia
SYN-PUB-00511.text:
Colour contrast ratios in existing hospital wayfinding systems: an audit of twelve facilities in Serbia and Croatia (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Environmental Graphic Design, Zagreb).
Authors: Tomislav Knežević (outside co-author); Branislav Jović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: colour contrast; wayfinding audit; hospital facilities; WCAG contrast ratio; reflective surfaces.
An observational audit was conducted across twelve hospital facilities in Serbia (eight) and Croatia (four), recording foreground–background colour contrast ratios of 684 installed wayfinding signs. Measurements were taken using a calibrated spectrophotometer under prevailing ambient conditions, and contrast ratios were computed according to the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula adapted for reflective surfaces. Fifty-three percent of measured signs fell below a contrast ratio of 3:1, and 31% below 2:1. Facilities built before 1985 had a significantly higher proportion of non-conforming signs than those built after 2000. Common failure modes included yellow text on cream backgrounds, dark-grey symbols on mid-grey substrate panels, and colour-coded zone maps with insufficient inter-zone differentiation. The audit instrument and scoring rubric developed for this study are described in detail and are available for replication in other Central and Eastern European healthcare facility audits.

SYN-PUB-00512.title: Contrast sensitivity and sign character recognition in adults aged 65 and older: implications for minimum type size in healthcare wayfinding
SYN-PUB-00512.text:
Contrast sensitivity and sign character recognition in adults aged 65 and older: implications for minimum type size in healthcare wayfinding (2015, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Vesna Petrović (outside co-author); Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Marina Stevanović (R0862).
Keywords: contrast sensitivity; type size; mesopic conditions; older adults; sans-serif legibility.
Contrast sensitivity functions (CSFs) were measured for 68 adults aged 65–84 using a sinusoidal grating test under photopic (300 lx) and mesopic (5 lx) conditions. The same participants then completed a character recognition task with uppercase sans-serif text (Helvetica Neue LT Pro 55 Roman and 75 Bold weights) at sizes ranging from 12 mm to 80 mm cap height, presented on matte white signage-grade substrate at contrast ratios of 4.5:1 and 8:1. CSF peak sensitivity at mesopic luminance was on average 0.41 log units lower than at photopic luminance across the group. A type size of 40 mm cap height at 8:1 contrast achieved 95% correct identification at a 5 m viewing distance under mesopic conditions. Below 25 mm at 4.5:1 contrast, accuracy dropped below 80% even at 3 m. Recommendations are formulated for minimum type sizes in hospital corridor and lift-lobby signage where night-time lighting is reduced.

SYN-PUB-00513.title: Wayfinding strategy differences between first-time and repeat visitors in a multi-building hospital campus: an observational study
SYN-PUB-00513.text:
Wayfinding strategy differences between first-time and repeat visitors in a multi-building hospital campus: an observational study (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 9th European Symposium on Wayfinding Research, Vienna).
Authors: Ivana Zdravković (outside co-author); Gerhard Strobl (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: navigational behaviour; hospital campus; first-time visitors; directional signs; landmark cues.
Forty-eight participants (24 first-time visitors, 24 repeat visitors) were recruited at the entrance of a multi-building regional hospital campus in Vojvodina and asked to navigate to four pre-specified destinations. Participants wore a chest-mounted camera and a GPS tracker; post-task interviews were conducted using a think-aloud recall protocol. First-time visitors spent on average 4.2 minutes longer per route and consulted printed directory signs 3.1 times more frequently than repeat visitors. Errors were categorised as wrong-turn, backtracking, and sign-missed; wrong-turn errors clustered at two T-junction nodes where sign placement was blocked by a temporary construction screen. Repeat visitors relied primarily on landmark cues rather than directional signs, suggesting that sign systems must remain functional for orientation even when environmental landmarks are temporarily altered. The study identifies five specific sign locations that account for 67% of all navigational errors.

SYN-PUB-00514.title: Symbol–text spatial arrangement and reading order in bilingual hospital signage: Serbian and Hungarian side-by-side layouts
SYN-PUB-00514.text:
Symbol–text spatial arrangement and reading order in bilingual hospital signage: Serbian and Hungarian side-by-side layouts (2017, journal, Information Design Journal).
Authors: Annamária Szűcs (outside co-author); Milena Vranić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: bilingual signage; symbol placement; eye tracking; Serbian; Hungarian; reading order.
Healthcare facilities in the Vojvodina region of Serbia are legally required to provide bilingual signage in Serbian and Hungarian in municipalities where the Hungarian community exceeds 15% of the population. This study examined how the spatial arrangement of a pictogram relative to bilingual text blocks affects reading speed and comprehension. Forty subjects with Serbian as their first language and 40 with Hungarian as their first language completed timed reading tasks for six layout configurations varying the symbol position (left, right, above text) and the ordering of the two language text blocks. Eye-tracking data were collected using a remote eye tracker at 60 Hz. Symbol-left placement with Serbian text on top produced the fastest mean fixation-to-decision time (1.8 s) for Serbian-dominant readers, while Hungarian-dominant readers showed no statistically significant preference for language ordering. Results inform a bilingual signage template for healthcare facilities in the region.

SYN-PUB-00515.title: Retroreflective materials for emergency egress signage: luminance uniformity measurements in reduced-power lighting scenarios
SYN-PUB-00515.text:
Retroreflective materials for emergency egress signage: luminance uniformity measurements in reduced-power lighting scenarios (2018, journal, Lighting Research and Building Science).
Authors: Đorđe Milovanović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: retroreflective materials; emergency signage; luminance uniformity; egress signs; low illuminance.
Emergency egress signs in hospitals are required to remain readable during power failures when only battery-backed emergency lighting operates, typically reducing corridor illuminance to 1–5 lx. This study evaluated four commercially available retroreflective substrate materials (two glass-bead and two microprismatic types) as potential replacements for internally illuminated plastic sign panels. Luminance uniformity and minimum–maximum luminance ratios were measured across each substrate at five incidence angles (0°, 10°, 20°, 30°, 45°) under a 2 lx emergency lighting simulation using a standardised LED emergency luminaire. Microprismatic materials maintained luminance uniformity ratios above 0.65 at incidence angles up to 20°, while glass-bead materials dropped below 0.40 beyond 10°. A practical assessment protocol using portable luminance meters is described, enabling facilities managers to evaluate installed retroreflective signs without laboratory equipment. Limitations related to specular reflections from polished floor surfaces are discussed.

SYN-PUB-00516.title: Information hierarchy and sign density at decision points in hospital wayfinding: a subjective workload study
SYN-PUB-00516.text:
Information hierarchy and sign density at decision points in hospital wayfinding: a subjective workload study (2019, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Information Design, Novi Sad).
Authors: Branislav Jović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Petra Hanáková (outside co-author).
Keywords: information hierarchy; sign density; decision points; NASA-TLX; virtual environment simulation.
Excessive sign density at navigational decision points has been identified anecdotally as a source of confusion, but empirical data on information load thresholds remain sparse. Sixty participants navigated a hospital corridor simulation rendered in a 3-D virtual environment displayed on a large-format monitor. Sign panels at simulated T-junctions contained between 2 and 10 destination entries, with sub-experiments varying font size, colour-coding, and arrow orientation. NASA-TLX subscale scores for mental demand and frustration increased significantly when entry count exceeded six (p < 0.01) regardless of colour-coding condition. Response time to select the correct destination increased by an average of 0.32 s per additional entry beyond six. A hierarchical categorisation of destinations into three display tiers (immediate clinical areas, support services, building exits) is proposed as a practical method for managing information density within the six-entry threshold.

SYN-PUB-00517.title: A field evaluation of redesigned wayfinding signs in an oncology centre: before-and-after navigation performance and user satisfaction
SYN-PUB-00517.text:
A field evaluation of redesigned wayfinding signs in an oncology centre: before-and-after navigation performance and user satisfaction (2020, journal, Health Environments Research and Design).
Authors: Ivana Zdravković (outside co-author); Nataša Todorović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: field evaluation; sign system redesign; oncology centre; navigation performance; user satisfaction.
A complete wayfinding sign system was redesigned and installed in a 380-bed oncology centre following a structured design process that incorporated legibility testing and staff consultation. Pre-installation data were collected over three weeks (n = 94 unassisted navigation observations) and post-installation data over three weeks six months after installation (n = 98 observations). The primary outcome was successful unassisted navigation, defined as reaching the stated destination without asking staff for directions or making more than one corrective backtrack. Successful navigation increased from 61% pre-installation to 84% post-installation. Staff reported a 43% reduction in wayfinding-related questions from patients and visitors based on a structured log kept by reception personnel. Patient satisfaction survey scores related to ease of finding one's way increased by 1.4 points on a 7-point Likert scale. The study describes the design process, testing methodology, and implementation logistics.

SYN-PUB-00518.title: Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights
SYN-PUB-00518.text:
Floor-level and ceiling-level wayfinding cues: visibility from wheelchair and walking-frame user eye heights (2021, journal, Universal Access in the Built Environment).
Authors: Tatjana Spasojević Brkić (outside co-author); Ana Todorović (R0760); Ildikó Papp (R0626); Jelena Korać (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: wheelchair users; sign installation height; universal access; detection distance; mobility aids.
Standard-height wall-mounted signage is designed for standing adult eye heights (approximately 1.55–1.70 m) and may be partially or fully outside the useful visual field of wheelchair users (eye height approximately 1.20 m) and walking-frame users who adopt a forward-inclined posture (functional eye height approximately 0.95–1.10 m). This study measured detection and identification distances for wall-mounted signs at three installation heights (1.0 m, 1.5 m, 2.1 m) for 22 wheelchair users and 18 walking-frame users recruited at rehabilitation and geriatric wards. Detection distance for signs at 1.0 m was significantly greater for wheelchair users than for walking-frame users (p = 0.008). Floor-applied vinyl wayfinding strips were also tested; identification of the destination label was not possible beyond 2.5 m for any participant group due to perspective distortion. Dual-height mounting at 1.0 m and 1.5 m is recommended for facilities serving high proportions of mobility-impaired users.

SYN-PUB-00519.title: Typeface weight and stroke modulation effects on character recognition under simulated cataract contrast reduction
SYN-PUB-00519.text:
Typeface weight and stroke modulation effects on character recognition under simulated cataract contrast reduction (2022, journal, Journal of Visual Communication and Information Design).
Authors: Maja Grubić (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041); Laura Bennetti (outside co-author).
Keywords: typeface selection; stroke modulation; cataract simulation; contrast sensitivity loss; character recognition.
Cataract-related vision impairment reduces contrast sensitivity rather than acuity, making it a useful model for testing signage under age-related conditions. Using a cataract simulation filter (Neuro-Vision CatSim 2 goggles, calibrated to approximately 0.3 log unit loss at 3 cycles/degree), 55 participants aged 22–40 with normal acuity completed character identification tasks for eight typefaces varying in stroke weight (thin, regular, medium, bold, extrabold) and modulation (low-modulation grotesks versus high-modulation humanist sans-serifs). Text was presented at a fixed cap height of 35 mm at 5 m on matte-white signage substrate at 180 lx. Bold and extrabold weight variants of low-modulation grotesks achieved identification accuracy above 93% under the cataract filter; thin and regular weights of high-modulation humanist faces fell below 75%. The results suggest that stroke modulation is a more critical parameter than weight alone for users with contrast sensitivity deficits.

SYN-PUB-00520.title: Standardisation gaps in hospital wayfinding sign systems in the Western Balkans: a comparative policy review
SYN-PUB-00520.text:
Standardisation gaps in hospital wayfinding sign systems in the Western Balkans: a comparative policy review (2023, journal, Design Policy and Regulation Studies).
Authors: Emina Hadžimuratović (outside co-author); Branislav Jović (outside co-author); Vesna Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: wayfinding standards; Western Balkans; healthcare regulation; ISO 7001; policy comparison.
This paper reviews existing technical standards, building regulations, and national guidelines governing hospital wayfinding signage in six Western Balkan countries (Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania). Regulatory documents were collected through national standards institutes and ministry of health websites; interviews were conducted with eight hospital facility managers across the region. No country in the survey has a dedicated national standard for healthcare wayfinding; applicable requirements are scattered across fire safety codes, accessibility legislation, and voluntary quality frameworks. The ISO 7001 pictogram standard has been formally adopted in Serbia and Croatia but not in the remaining four countries. Significant variation exists in minimum contrast, type size, and symbol size requirements across the jurisdictions that do specify such values. The paper identifies the most consequential gaps and discusses pathways toward a regional harmonised guideline, drawing on comparisons with German DIN and UK NHS wayfinding standards.

SYN-PUB-00521.title: Dynamic digital wayfinding displays in hospital entrance lobbies: update frequency and motion effects on older adult legibility
SYN-PUB-00521.text:
Dynamic digital wayfinding displays in hospital entrance lobbies: update frequency and motion effects on older adult legibility (2024, journal, Applied Ergonomics and Design).
Authors: Jelena Korać (outside co-author); Ralf Schindler (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: digital displays; dynamic content; older adults; legibility; dwell time; hospital lobby.
Digital display panels are increasingly used as directory boards in hospital lobbies, with content cycling through multiple screens or using scrolling text. This study examined how content update frequency (static, 5 s cycle, 3 s cycle, continuous scroll at 40 px/s) affected legibility and task completion for 44 adults aged 65–80 and 44 adults aged 25–40. Participants were asked to locate a named destination on a digital directory panel at a standardised distance of 3.5 m. Task completion rate for older adults fell from 91% on static displays to 54% on 3-second cycled displays and to 29% on continuously scrolled content. Younger adults showed no significant difference across cycle frequencies but performed below 80% on continuous scroll. Fixation duration data from remote eye tracking showed that older adults required at least 4.2 s of stable display time to complete a single read. Recommendations for minimum dwell times and motion-free zones in digital hospital directory design are proposed.

SYN-PUB-00522.title: Colour-zone coding systems in hospital wayfinding: memorability and navigation efficiency in a multi-storey building simulation
SYN-PUB-00522.text:
Colour-zone coding systems in hospital wayfinding: memorability and navigation efficiency in a multi-storey building simulation (2025, conference, Proceedings of the 15th European Symposium on Wayfinding Research, Ljubljana).
Authors: Ivana Zdravković (outside co-author); Annamária Szűcs (outside co-author); Đorđe Milovanović (outside co-author); Stefan Ostojić (R0041).
Keywords: colour-zone coding; wayfinding; multi-storey hospital; colour vision deficiency; redundant coding.
Colour-zone coding assigns a distinct colour to each functional zone or floor of a hospital, aiming to reduce cognitive load during navigation. This study tested whether participants could correctly associate six colour codes with their corresponding zones after a single briefing exposure, and whether this association aided navigation in a multi-storey virtual building simulation. Seventy-two participants were divided into a colour-coded sign condition and a text-only sign condition. In the virtual building, navigation to six targets was timed and error-counted over three consecutive trials. After three trials, colour-coded condition participants committed fewer wrong-floor errors (mean 0.8 vs. 2.1 per participant) and showed steeper learning curves. However, 18 participants reported colour vision deficiency or difficulty; post-hoc analysis showed their error rates were equivalent across conditions, indicating that colour coding without secondary coding (shape or pattern) provides no benefit for this group. Revised guidelines integrating redundant coding are discussed.

SYN-PUB-00637.title: Monitoring melt viscosity indices in recycled polymer injection moulding using EWMA charts with estimated parameters under non-normality
SYN-PUB-00637.text:
Monitoring melt viscosity indices in recycled polymer injection moulding using EWMA charts with estimated parameters under non-normality (2024, journal, Journal of Polymer Processing Quality Control).
Authors: Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Sonja Ilić (outside co-author); Andrei Popescu (outside co-author); Marija Tadić (R0048); Milan Sabo (R0859); Milana Lekić (R0161).
Keywords: EWMA; recycled polymers; melt flow index; parameter estimation; bootstrap.
The growing use of recycled polymers in injection moulding introduces additional variability in melt viscosity, which is an in-process quality indicator correlated with final part properties. Melt flow index (MFI) measurements of recycled polypropylene batches exhibit pronounced right skewness (skewness coefficient 1.8–2.4) and batch-to-batch parameter drift. This study applies an EWMA chart with parameters estimated from a rolling Phase I window of the 60 most recent subgroups to monitor MFI in real time. The chart is designed to achieve a steady-state ARL of 150 at the target MFI, with control limits adjusted for parameter estimation uncertainty using a bootstrap correction derived from 10,000 resamples of the Phase I data. Data were collected from a production line processing post-consumer PP flake over 22 weeks, producing 1,840 subgroup observations of size 3. The rolling-estimation EWMA detected seven assignable causes confirmed by operator inspection, with two false alarms, against four detections and six false alarms for a fixed-parameter chart designed under normality.

SYN-PUB-00708.title: Queue-Aware Offloading Decisions for Battery-Constrained IoT Gateways Under Variable Channel Conditions
SYN-PUB-00708.text:
Queue-Aware Offloading Decisions for Battery-Constrained IoT Gateways Under Variable Channel Conditions (2019, journal, Journal of Wireless Networks and Distributed Computing).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Dragana Uzelac (R0053); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Lyapunov optimization; task offloading; IoT gateway; channel-aware scheduling.
This paper examines task offloading at IoT gateway devices operating under time-varying wireless channels and limited battery capacity. A discrete-time queuing model is constructed in which computational tasks arrive according to a Poisson process with mean rate 8 tasks per second. A Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty framework is applied to derive an online policy that jointly controls the offloading fraction and transmission power without requiring future channel state information. Experiments are conducted on a testbed of 12 Raspberry Pi 4 nodes connected over a 2.4 GHz IEEE 802.11n link with artificially injected congestion. The proposed policy reduces average task latency by 34% compared to a greedy offloading baseline while keeping battery depletion events below 2 per hour per node under a 50 mW solar harvesting input. Sensitivity analysis shows robustness to arrival rate fluctuations of up to ±40%.

SYN-PUB-00722.title: Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles
SYN-PUB-00722.text:
Detecting Stealthy Coil-Write Injection in Modbus Networks Using Temporal Autoencoder Ensembles (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Nina Dimitrijević (R0054).
Keywords: stealthy attacks; autoencoder ensemble; coil-write injection; Modbus; temporal features.
Stealthy coil-write injection attacks modify a small number of PLC output coils at irregular intervals designed to evade detectors sensitive only to rate or volume changes. This paper evaluates temporal autoencoder ensembles—ten autoencoders trained on temporally shuffled subsets of a 60-day Modbus/TCP capture—for detecting such attacks. Each autoencoder receives a 30-dimensional feature vector derived from 5-second windows including coil change frequency, write-to-read ratio per coil address, and inter-write interval statistics. Anomaly scores from ensemble members are aggregated by the maximum rule. Against 240 injected stealthy attack episodes of varying intensity (1 to 8 modified coils per window), the ensemble achieved recall of 0.89 at a false positive rate of 0.8 per hour, compared with 0.64 for a single autoencoder and 0.58 for a static threshold detector. Computational cost of the ensemble was 2.3× that of a single autoencoder, remaining feasible on edge hardware.

SYN-PUB-00754.title: Piecewise-Linear Approximation of ECG Signals Using Adaptive Breakpoint Selection
SYN-PUB-00754.text:
Piecewise-Linear Approximation of ECG Signals Using Adaptive Breakpoint Selection (2013, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Lazar Šarić (R0057); Pavol Struhár (R0261); Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Dragan Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: ECG compression; piecewise-linear approximation; dynamic programming; wearable.
This paper examines piecewise-linear approximation as a preprocessing stage for ECG compression. A dynamic-programming algorithm selects breakpoints by minimising the sum of squared residuals subject to a maximum reconstruction error bound of 10 µV. Experiments were conducted on 30 records from the PhysioNet MIT-BIH arrhythmia database resampled to 360 Hz. The method achieves an average compression ratio of 4.1:1 at a per-sample root-mean-square error below 8 µV, outperforming fixed-window linear interpolation by approximately 18% in bit rate under identical distortion constraints. Computational cost is O(N log N) per record, making the approach suitable for microcontroller deployment in wearable monitors. The study also evaluates how premature ventricular contractions, which deviate from normal quasi-periodic morphology, affect the breakpoint density and proposes a beat-classification pre-filter that reduces the density penalty for irregular beats by 23%.

SYN-PUB-00755.title: Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings
SYN-PUB-00755.text:
Beat-Synchronous DCT Coding of Long-Term ECG Recordings (2015, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Biomedical Engineering and Medical Informatics (SBEMI)).
Authors: Milena Vuković (outside co-author); Lazar Šarić (R0057); Ana Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Holter ECG; DCT; beat segmentation; compression ratio; PRD.
Long-term (Holter) ECG recordings present compression challenges because gradual heart-rate drift shifts beat boundaries relative to fixed analysis windows. This work proposes a beat-synchronous discrete cosine transform (DCT) coder in which each beat is individually segmented using a Pan-Tompkins R-peak detector, zero-padded or truncated to a uniform 512-sample frame, and transformed to the DCT domain. Coefficient quantisation thresholds are derived per lead from a short training segment of the same recording, adapting to inter-patient variability.
