This study reports personal and area air monitoring results from purging operations at four injection moulding facilities in Serbia, covering polystyrene, ABS, and polyamide 6 materials. Sampling was conducted using NIOSH-validated methods over forty-eight production shifts. Formaldehyde concentrations during ABS purging reached 0.24 mg/m³ as a shift average, exceeding the Serbian occupational exposure limit of 0.12 mg/m³ in two of twelve measured events. Acrolein peaks during PS purging reached 0.09 mg/m³. PM2.5 concentrations at the machine operator position ranged from 18 to 74 µg/m³ depending on ventilation conditions. The study identifies ventilation adequacy, purging temperature settings, and purge compound selection as primary determinants of worker exposure. Practical control measures are recommended, including local exhaust ventilation specifications and revised standard operating procedures.

SYN-PUB-02734.title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom
SYN-PUB-02734.text:
Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom (2022, journal, Informatika i sistemi: Časopis za informacione tehnologije i računarstvo).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Mónika Papp (R0524).
Keywords: pretraga u realnom vremenu; tok vesti; inkrementalni indeks; skalabilnost.
Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

SYN-PUB-02735.title: Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval
SYN-PUB-02735.text:
Evaluating Pretrained Multilingual Embeddings for Mixed-Script Serbian Document Retrieval (2023, journal, Information Processing and Management).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author); Željko Đurić (R0213); Miroslav Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: multilingual embeddings; transformer; dense retrieval; mixed-script; fine-tuning.
Pretrained multilingual transformer models encode text at the subword level and might be expected to handle script variation implicitly, since their vocabularies cover both Serbian scripts. This paper measures to what extent this expectation holds in practice. We fine-tuned three publicly available multilingual models of different sizes on SrMIR-1, the mixed-script Serbian retrieval benchmark, and compared their nDCG@10 scores against a script-normalizing BM25 baseline and a hybrid model. Without fine-tuning, the multilingual models rank below the BM25 baseline on mixed-script queries. After fine-tuning on 12 000 query–passage pairs, the best model reaches nDCG@10 of 0.601, above the hybrid BM25 baseline of 0.587. However, for queries and documents that mix scripts within a single sentence, fine-tuned models underperform by up to 9 percentage points relative to their performance on single-script inputs, indicating that subword tokenization does not fully resolve the alignment problem. We release the fine-tuning splits and evaluation scripts.

SYN-PUB-02736.title: A Benchmark Suite for Model Checkers Applied to Industrial-Scale Concurrent C Code
SYN-PUB-02736.text:
A Benchmark Suite for Model Checkers Applied to Industrial-Scale Concurrent C Code (2025, journal, Journal of Automated Reasoning and Formal Methods (JARFM)).
Authors: Tobias Frenzel (outside co-author); Zlata Malešević (R0810); Anna Čániová (R0728); Željko Đurić (R0213); Nemanja Ostojić (outside co-author); Dušan Grujić (outside co-author); Sara Lindqvist (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark suite; model checker comparison; SPIN; CBMC; CPAchecker; C verification.
Evaluating model checkers in a reproducible way requires benchmarks that reflect the scale and structure of real industrial code rather than toy examples. We present VeriBench-C, a suite of 40 verification tasks derived from open-licensed industrial C codebases in the domains of automotive firmware, PLC controllers, and network protocol stacks. Each task is accompanied by a formal property in LTL and a ground-truth verdict established by at least two independent tools. We run five model checkers — SPIN 6.5, CBMC 5.12, CPAchecker 2.2, Seahorn, and ESBMC — on the full suite and report verification time, memory consumption, and verdict accuracy. SPIN solves 28 of 40 tasks within a 4 GB / 3600 s budget; CBMC solves 35 but produces two incorrect verdicts. We analyse the sources of divergence and provide all models, property files, and analysis scripts in a public repository. The suite is intended as a living resource for future comparisons.

SYN-PUB-02765.title: Efikasnost B+-stabla nasuprot LSM-stablu u okruženjima s intenzivnim čitanjem: empirijska analiza
SYN-PUB-02765.text:
Efikasnost B+-stabla nasuprot LSM-stablu u okruženjima s intenzivnim čitanjem: empirijska analiza (2014, journal, Journal of Data Engineering and Distributed Systems).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Dragan Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: B+-tree; LSM-tree; read-heavy workload; benchmarking.
Rad poredi performanse B+-stabla i LSM-stabla (Log-Structured Merge-tree) u scenarijima u kojima dominiraju operacije čitanja, što je tipično za sisteme za proveru statusa sertifikata. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na skupu podataka od 50 miliona sintetički generisanih X.509 sertifikata raspoređenih na klasteru od osam čvorova. Merene su latencija tačkastih upita, propusnost pri 10.000 zahteva u sekundi i zauzeće memorije tokom šestočasovnih opterećenja. Rezultati pokazuju da B+-stablo ostvaruje za 18% nižu medijanu latencije pri čistim radnim opterećenjima čitanja, dok LSM-stablo pokazuje prednost u scenarijima s mešovitim operacijama čitanja i pisanja u omeru 70:30. Rad identifikuje prag od oko 40% pisanja kao tačku u kojoj LSM-stablo postaje povoljniji izbor za datu klasu aplikacija.

SYN-PUB-02766.title: Consistent Hashing with Bounded Load for Certificate Revocation List Distribution
SYN-PUB-02766.text:
Consistent Hashing with Bounded Load for Certificate Revocation List Distribution (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Symposium on Distributed Computing (CESDC)).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Miroslav Janković (outside co-author); Petra Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: consistent hashing; bounded load; CRL distribution; PKI; load balancing.
Certificate revocation list (CRL) distribution in large-scale PKI deployments creates uneven load across serving nodes when naive hashing schemes are used. This paper applies a bounded-load variant of consistent hashing to a simulated CRL distribution network of 32 nodes serving up to 80,000 requests per second. We define a load imbalance coefficient and show that the bounded scheme keeps it below 1.12 across all tested configurations, compared with values up to 2.4 under standard consistent hashing. The evaluation uses trace data from a regional government PKI deployment anonymised for research purposes, comprising approximately 12 million certificate entries. We also characterise the overhead introduced by the bounding mechanism, which amounts to an average of 3.1 additional hash lookups per request. The approach is shown to be practical within the constraints of commodity hardware.

SYN-PUB-02767.title: Particionisanje podataka o statusu sertifikata u Apache Cassandra klasterima: strategije i kompromisi
SYN-PUB-02767.text:
Particionisanje podataka o statusu sertifikata u Apache Cassandra klasterima: strategije i kompromisi (2017, conference, Zbornik radova 24. telekomunikacionog foruma TELFOR).
Authors: Sanja Filipović (outside co-author); Andrea Malešević (R0217); Ljubomir Malešević (R0489).
Keywords: Apache Cassandra; data partitioning; certificate status; NoSQL.
Ovaj rad istražuje tri strategije particionisanja podataka o statusu sertifikata u Apache Cassandra klasteru: particionisanje po serijskom broju, po vremenskom periodu isteka i po izdavačkom autoritetu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na klasteru od 12 čvorova sa skupovima podataka veličine između 5 i 200 miliona zapisa. Strategija particionisanja po serijskom broju pokazala je najravnomerniju distribuciju podataka, ali najlošije karakteristike lokalnosti upita pri pretrazi po izdavačkom autoritetu. Particionisanje po isteku pogoduje scenarijima masovnog brisanja isteklih zapisa i smanjuje amplifikaciju pisanja za 22%. Rad pruža preporuke za odabir strategije na osnovu profila opterećenja i nudi analitički model za procenu veličine particije pri različitim stopama rasta sertifikata.

SYN-PUB-02768.title: Reducing OCSP Responder Latency Through Probabilistic Caching with Staleness Bounds
SYN-PUB-02768.text:
Reducing OCSP Responder Latency Through Probabilistic Caching with Staleness Bounds (2019, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC)).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Dragan Kovačević (outside co-author); Luca Martinelli (outside co-author); Nemanja Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: OCSP; probabilistic caching; Bloom filter; LRU; TLS.
Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responders in high-traffic deployments frequently become bottlenecks due to repeated identical queries. This paper proposes a probabilistic caching layer that serves cached responses while providing a configurable staleness bound expressed in seconds. The cache uses a counting Bloom filter to track query frequency and promotes entries to a fixed-size LRU tier above a frequency threshold. We evaluate the design against a synthetic query workload modelled on TLS handshake patterns, reaching peak loads of 45,000 queries per second. The cache achieves an 87% hit rate at a staleness bound of 30 seconds, reducing mean responder latency from 14.2 ms to 2.1 ms. We formally characterise the probability that a served response misrepresents true certificate status, showing it remains below 10^-5 at the tested revocation rates. The implementation is available as an open-source Java library.

SYN-PUB-02770.title: Distributed OCSP Responder Architecture for National-Scale PKI: A Case Study in Deployment Design
SYN-PUB-02770.text:
Distributed OCSP Responder Architecture for National-Scale PKI: A Case Study in Deployment Design (2023, book chapter, Distributed Security Infrastructures: Architectures and Protocols (edited volume, IOS Press)).
Authors: Dragan Kovačević (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author); Andrea Malešević (R0217); Miroslav Janković (outside co-author).
Keywords: OCSP; PKI architecture; distributed systems; sharding; consistency.
This book chapter describes the architectural considerations involved in designing a distributed OCSP responder system intended to serve a national-scale PKI with an estimated 8 million active certificates and peak query rates of 120,000 requests per second. The chapter covers the selection of a sharding strategy based on issuer DN hash, the placement of read replicas across three geographic regions, and the consistency model chosen — eventual consistency with a maximum staleness window of 60 seconds. Failure modes analysed include responder node loss, network partition between regions, and upstream CA unavailability. The chapter also discusses monitoring instrumentation using time-series metrics at one-second resolution and describes an alerting policy calibrated to detect latency regressions within 90 seconds. The described architecture was developed as a reference design during a joint research engagement and has not been deployed in production.

SYN-PUB-02771.title: Merenje uticaja veličine Bloom filtera na stopu lažno pozitivnih odgovora u OCSP keš slojevima
SYN-PUB-02771.text:
Merenje uticaja veličine Bloom filtera na stopu lažno pozitivnih odgovora u OCSP keš slojevima (2024, journal, Novi Sad Journal of Mathematics and Computing).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Tamara Bošnjak (outside co-author).
Keywords: Bloom filter; false positive rate; OCSP cache; memory footprint.
Bloom filteri se često koriste u OCSP keš slojevima za brzo odbacivanje upita za sertifikate koji sigurno nisu u kešu, ali veza između dimenzionisanja filtera i operativnih performansi nije detaljno dokumentovana u kontekstu OCSP sistema. Ovaj rad sistematski meri stopu lažno pozitivnih odgovora za Bloom filtere veličina od 1 do 64 bita po elementu, pri populacijama od 100.000 do 10 miliona zapisa o statusu sertifikata. Eksperimenti potvrđuju teorijsku krivu lažno pozitivnih odgovora u okviru 2% pri svim testiranim veličinama i pokazuju da 8 bita po elementu pruža prihvatljiv kompromis između memorijskog zauzeća i stope lažno pozitivnih od ispod 2,2% pri 10 miliona elemenata. Rad opisuje i merenu cenu osvežavanja filtera pri inkrementalnim ažuriranjima statusa i predlaže prag za planiranje potpune rekonstrukcije filtera.

SYN-PUB-02772.title: Benchmarking Query Latency in Multi-Region Certificate Status Databases Under Simulated WAN Conditions
SYN-PUB-02772.text:
Benchmarking Query Latency in Multi-Region Certificate Status Databases Under Simulated WAN Conditions (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Databases and Security Systems (EWDSS)).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Stefan Vuković (outside co-author); Ioana Constantin (outside co-author); Marina Bošković (R0235); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: distributed database; WAN latency; OCSP; benchmarking; replication.
Cross-region replication of certificate status data introduces variable latency that is difficult to characterise from first principles alone. This paper presents a controlled benchmark of four distributed database systems — Apache Cassandra, CockroachDB, YugabyteDB, and a custom single-purpose store — under simulated wide-area network conditions with round-trip delays between 20 ms and 120 ms and packet loss rates of 0%, 0.1%, and 0.5%. The workload consists exclusively of OCSP-style point lookups and bounded-range scans over serial number ranges. We report 50th, 95th, and 99th percentile latencies at throughputs of 5,000, 20,000, and 60,000 queries per second per region. CockroachDB shows the most stable p99 latency under packet loss, while the custom store achieves the lowest p50 at 60,000 QPS under zero-loss conditions. Results include confidence intervals derived from ten independent runs per configuration. All benchmark scripts and dataset generation code are published under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-02773.title: Adaptivno particionisanje vremenskih serija u bazama podataka za revokaciju sertifikata sa promenljivim stopama izdavanja
SYN-PUB-02773.text:
Adaptivno particionisanje vremenskih serija u bazama podataka za revokaciju sertifikata sa promenljivim stopama izdavanja (2026, journal, Journal of Data Engineering and Distributed Systems).
Authors: Andrea Malešević (R0217); Tamara Bošnjak (outside co-author); Nemanja Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: adaptive partitioning; time series; certificate revocation; Apache Cassandra; dynamic sharding.
Sistemi za revokaciju sertifikata u savremenim mrežama suočavaju se s visokim i neravnomernim stopama izdavanja koje otežavaju statičke strategije particionisanja. Ovaj rad predlaže shemu adaptivnog particionisanja zasnovanog na praćenju gustine zapisa po vremenskom prozoru i automatskom deljenju particija kada gustina premaši konfigurabilni prag. Implementacija je realizovana kao proširenje iznad Apache Cassandre i evaluirana je na sintetičkim skupovima podataka koji modeluju rast od 1.000 do 50.000 novih sertifikata na dan tokom perioda od godinu dana. Mereni su vreme upita, balans particija i troškovi reparticionisanja. Adaptivna shema smanjuje maksimalno odstupanje veličine particija sa 340% na 28% u poređenju sa statičkim mesečnim particionisanjem, uz prosečni troškak reparticionisanja od 1,4 sekunde po operaciji deljenja na testnom klasteru. Rad takođe analizira ponašanje sheme pri naglim skokovima broja vydatih sertifikata.

SYN-PUB-02944.title: Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software
SYN-PUB-02944.text:
Mutation Operators for Finite State Machine Specifications of Embedded Control Software (2011, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Software Engineering and Testing (CEWSET)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: mutation testing; finite state machines; embedded software; test adequacy; mutation operators.
This paper defines a catalogue of 18 mutation operators tailored to finite state machine (FSM) specifications commonly used in embedded control firmware. Operators cover state deletion, transition guard modification, action substitution, and reset-condition negation. An experiment was conducted on four open-source microcontroller firmware projects totalling approximately 14,000 lines of C code. Mutants were seeded automatically using a custom Python tool, and an existing hand-written test suite was used as the baseline oracle. Mutation scores ranged from 41% to 67% across the four subjects, revealing systematic gaps in transition coverage. The paper reports the proportion of equivalent mutants identified through static analysis (approximately 12% of all seeded mutants) and discusses the effort required for manual equivalence classification. The results motivate the need for specification-driven test generation rather than ad hoc test suite growth.

SYN-PUB-02945.title: Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies
SYN-PUB-02945.text:
Deriving Test Suites from UML Statecharts: A Comparison of Three Path-Selection Strategies (2013, journal, Software Testing and Verification Journal).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Pavol Čáni (R0371).
Keywords: UML statecharts; model-based testing; path selection; test generation; embedded systems.
Model-based test generation from UML statecharts can follow different path-selection criteria, each yielding test suites of different size and fault-detection capability. This study compares all-transitions, all-transition-pairs, and boundary-interior path selection applied to a set of seven industrial-scale statechart models provided by a regional automotive supplier. Models ranged from 12 to 89 states and 18 to 204 transitions. Test cases were generated automatically and executed against seeded mutation faults. All-transition-pairs coverage detected 14% more mutants on average compared with all-transitions, while increasing test suite size by a factor of 3.1. Boundary-interior selection offered a middle ground but showed inconsistent results across subjects. Execution times on target hardware were measured to assess whether suite sizes remain feasible under real-time constraints. The paper recommends a hybrid strategy that applies all-transition-pairs only to safety-critical subsystems and all-transitions elsewhere.

SYN-PUB-02946.title: Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes
SYN-PUB-02946.text:
Automated Regression Test Selection for Firmware After Incremental Source Changes (2015, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Control).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: regression test selection; change-impact analysis; binary instrumentation; firmware; continuous integration.
Regression testing of embedded firmware is expensive because full test suite execution on hardware targets can take hours. This paper presents a lightweight change-impact analysis technique that identifies which tests in an existing suite are affected by a given firmware patch without requiring full re-execution. The method instruments the firmware binary at basic-block granularity to record coverage during an initial full run, then uses static call-graph differencing to predict which blocks are reachable from changed functions. On a dataset of 120 patches drawn from the version history of three open-source firmware projects, the technique retained on average 31% of the original test suite while missing 2.1% of fault-detecting tests. False negative rates are characterised per patch type. The implementation is released as a set of scripts wrapping GCC and a custom binary instrumentation tool. Practical integration into a continuous integration pipeline is described.

SYN-PUB-02947.title: Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation
SYN-PUB-02947.text:
Contract-Based Specification of Interrupt-Driven Firmware for Model-Based Test Generation (2016, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Formal Techniques for Embedded Systems (FTES)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: contract-based specification; interrupt-driven firmware; ISR testing; model-based test generation; ARM Cortex-M.
Interrupt-driven firmware presents challenges for model-based testing because interleaving of interrupt service routines (ISRs) with the main execution thread produces combinatorial state spaces. This paper proposes a contract language, IFContract, that allows engineers to annotate ISR entry and exit conditions, shared-variable invariants, and timing constraints using a syntax embedded in C comments. A parser translates annotations into an extended FSM representation. Test cases covering pairwise ISR–main-thread interactions are generated from this model. The approach was evaluated on firmware for a battery management unit implemented on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The generated suite comprised 147 test cases and detected all 38 manually seeded interface faults. Compared with a randomly generated suite of the same size, the model-based suite found 23% more faults. Annotation effort was measured at 2.3 lines of contract per 10 lines of ISR code on average.

SYN-PUB-02948.title: Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments
SYN-PUB-02948.text:
Weak Mutation vs. Strong Mutation for Assessing Test Suite Quality in Resource-Constrained Environments (2017, journal, Software Testing and Verification Journal).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: weak mutation; strong mutation; mutation score; embedded testing; test quality.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-02949.title: Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems
SYN-PUB-02949.text:
Model-Based Testing for Embedded Systems (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Software Testing Methods for Embedded and Cyber-Physical Systems, Springer).
Authors: Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Katarina Knežević (R0982); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; embedded systems; test generation; timed automata; coverage criteria.
This book chapter surveys the state of practice in model-based testing (MBT) as applied to embedded and cyber-physical systems. It covers modelling notations including UML statecharts, extended finite automata, and timed automata, and maps them to corresponding test generation algorithms. Coverage criteria are categorised into structural, fault-based, and requirements-based families. A discussion of toolchain integration addresses challenges specific to embedded targets: cross-compilation, hardware-in-the-loop execution, and limited observability. Two worked examples illustrate applying MBT to an automotive body control module and an industrial motor controller. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems including scalability to large state spaces, handling of real-time constraints, and the lack of standardised interfaces between modelling and test execution tools.

SYN-PUB-02950.title: Measuring the Cost of Test Suite Maintenance Over Multiple Firmware Releases
SYN-PUB-02950.text:
Measuring the Cost of Test Suite Maintenance Over Multiple Firmware Releases (2020, conference, Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement Conference (ESEM) Proceedings).
Authors: Anita Kovačević (outside co-author); Benedek Horváth (outside co-author); Aleksa Lazić (R0318); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233).
Keywords: test suite maintenance; regression testing; empirical study; model-based testing; firmware evolution.
Automated test suites generated from formal models must be updated as firmware specifications evolve, yet the maintenance cost of model-based suites is rarely quantified empirically. This study tracks five firmware products through 8 to 14 release cycles, recording the time engineers spent updating model specifications, regenerating test cases, and resolving obsolete test oracles. On average, model update effort represented 18% of total release testing effort, compared with 27% for manually maintained suites managing the same products in a parallel control group. The study also records the number of regression faults detected per release and finds that model-based suites detected faults 1.4 releases earlier on average. Threats to validity related to the single-organisation setting and self-reported effort data are discussed. The dataset, anonymised, is made available for further analysis.

SYN-PUB-02951.title: Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic
SYN-PUB-02951.text:
Automating Oracle Construction for Hardware-in-the-Loop Firmware Tests Using Signal Temporal Logic (2021, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Marco Ferreira (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Popović (outside co-author).
Keywords: test oracle; signal temporal logic; hardware-in-the-loop; automated testing; firmware verification.
Specifying correct output behaviour for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) firmware tests is labour intensive because engineers must manually define acceptable signal ranges and timing windows for each scenario. This paper investigates the use of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) formulas as automatically checkable test oracles in HIL test environments. STL formulas are mined from a set of passing execution traces using a template-guided parameter synthesis procedure. The synthesised formulas are then used as oracles for new test runs. The approach was evaluated on a DC motor control firmware and a temperature regulation firmware, each executed on physical target hardware. Oracle construction time dropped from a median of 47 minutes per scenario (manual) to under 4 minutes (automated). False positive and false negative rates of synthesised oracles were 3.1% and 1.8% respectively across 310 test scenarios. Limitations related to non-deterministic hardware timing are discussed.

SYN-PUB-02952.title: Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm
SYN-PUB-02952.text:
Integration of Formal Specification Review into the Firmware Development Workflow: A Case Study at a Serbian Industrial Electronics Firm (2022, journal, Information and Software Technology).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Igor Starčević (R0738); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Nataša Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: formal specification; industrial case study; firmware development; communicating automata; defect reduction.
Adopting formal specification practices in industry requires integrating review steps into existing development workflows without excessive overhead. This paper reports a two-year action research study conducted with a Serbian firm that develops programmable logic controllers. The study introduced a lightweight formalism based on communicating extended finite automata (CEFA) for specifying firmware modules, along with a peer-review checklist and a set of automated consistency checks. Defect data were collected for 34 firmware modules developed before and after adoption. Post-adoption modules showed a 29% reduction in defects found during system integration testing. Developer survey data indicate that engineers found the notation acceptable after a two-day training course. Barriers including tool fragmentation and version control of model artefacts are documented. The paper provides a replication package containing the checklist, consistency check scripts, and anonymised defect logs.

SYN-PUB-02953.title: SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models
SYN-PUB-02953.text:
SpecMutate: A Framework for Specification-Level Mutation Testing of Extended Finite Automata Models (2023, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Software Testing and Analysis (ECSTA)).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author); Emilija Vranješ (R0749).
Keywords: mutation testing; extended finite automata; specification-level faults; model fidelity; test generation framework.
Most mutation testing tools operate at the source code level, but for model-based testing workflows it is useful to seed faults into the formal model rather than the implementation. SpecMutate is a framework that applies 23 mutation operators directly to extended finite automata (EFA) models serialised in an XML interchange format. Operators include guard weakening, output-action swapping, state-merge, and variable initialisation faults. The framework integrates with an open-source model-based test generator and reports the model mutation score alongside the implementation mutation score. An experiment on six firmware EFA models with a combined 312 states found that model mutation scores and code mutation scores diverged significantly for three of the subjects, indicating that the model had lower fidelity than assumed. Runtime for model mutation analysis was under two minutes per model on a standard workstation, making it suitable for pre-commit checks.

SYN-PUB-02954.title: Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data
SYN-PUB-02954.text:
Regression Test Prioritisation for Firmware Using Historical Fault Localisation Data (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering).
Authors: Srđan Popović (outside co-author); Elena Varga (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Luca Bianchi (outside co-author).
Keywords: test prioritisation; regression testing; fault localisation; APFD; history-based testing.
Test prioritisation orders a regression suite so that fault-detecting tests execute earlier, reducing feedback latency. This paper proposes a history-based prioritisation strategy that weights tests by the fault-localisation entropy of the code regions they cover across previous test campaigns. Coverage and fault data from nine firmware projects with histories spanning 12 to 31 releases were used to train and evaluate the strategy. The proposed approach achieved an average percentage of faults detected (APFD) of 0.78, compared with 0.61 for random ordering and 0.71 for a coverage-based baseline. Computational overhead of computing prioritisation order was below 90 seconds for all subjects. The paper also analyses how quickly the historical model degrades after a major refactoring event and proposes a simple reset heuristic triggered by structural change thresholds.

SYN-PUB-02955.title: Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios
SYN-PUB-02955.text:
Combining Model-Based Test Generation with Large Language Model Suggestions for Uncovered Firmware Scenarios (2025, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.XXXXX).
Authors: Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tomáš Blažej (outside co-author).
Keywords: model-based testing; large language models; specification gaps; firmware testing; test scenario generation.
Model-based test generation is constrained by the completeness of the formal model: scenarios not captured in the specification are not tested. This preprint explores a workflow where an LLM is prompted with natural-language firmware documentation and existing EFA models to suggest additional test scenarios that may correspond to specification gaps. Suggested scenarios are reviewed by engineers and, if accepted, formalised as model extensions. The approach was piloted on three firmware modules from an industrial PLC project. Engineers accepted 41% of LLM suggestions after review; of those, 17 were formalised and added to the model. Subsequent mutation analysis showed an increase in model mutation score of 6.3 percentage points on average. The paper does not claim that LLM suggestions are reliable in general but characterises conditions under which they are useful as a complement to structured specification review.

SYN-PUB-02956.title: Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs
SYN-PUB-02956.text:
Automated Generation of Compatibility Test Cases from Android Permission Change Logs (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Software Engineering (CECSE)).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author); Olivera Tomić (R0327).
Keywords: permission model; test case generation; Android; JUnit; automated testing.
Android's permission model underwent significant restructuring between API levels 22 and 23 with the introduction of runtime permissions, causing widespread behavioural incompatibilities in deployed applications. This paper presents PermGen, a tool that parses Android SDK change logs and permission usage declarations in application manifests to automatically generate JUnit-based test cases targeting permission-related execution paths. The tool was evaluated on 45 applications from the Google Play Store's productivity category, generating on average 17.3 test cases per application. Execution of generated suites on a physical device pool covering API levels 21 through 27 revealed 83 previously undocumented permission-handling defects across 31 applications. Compared to manually authored test suites covering the same permission scenarios, PermGen achieved 78% of the fault detection rate at 12% of the authoring effort, measured in developer-hours. Limitations regarding obfuscated code and dynamically requested permissions are discussed.

SYN-PUB-02957.title: Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data
SYN-PUB-02957.text:
Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Small Wind Turbines Using Gradient-Boosted Survival Models on Vibration and SCADA Data (2024, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Predictive Maintenance in Energy Infrastructure (EWPMEI)).
Authors: Igor Starčević (R0738); Valentina Stojanović (R0233); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Srđan Kovačević (outside co-author); Petra Horáková (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: survival analysis; wind turbine; vibration; SCADA; maintenance scheduling.
Small wind turbines installed on agricultural and industrial premises in Serbia are often maintained reactively due to the absence of dedicated condition monitoring. This paper fits gradient-boosted survival models—specifically, a discrete-time hazard model and a random survival forest—to a combined dataset of SCADA telemetry and tower-mounted accelerometer readings from 17 turbines over five years. Predictors include nacelle vibration root-mean-square in three frequency bands, rotor speed deviation, and nacelle temperature differential. The discrete-time hazard model achieved a concordance index of 0.73 on a held-out cohort, outperforming a Cox baseline at 0.65. Predicted 30-day failure probability was used to generate ranked maintenance schedules, which were evaluated in a retrospective simulation against actual maintenance logs, showing an estimated 22 % reduction in unscheduled downtime hours.

SYN-PUB-02958.title: Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration
SYN-PUB-02958.text:
Incremental Model-to-Text Generation for PLC Software: Handling Configuration Changes Without Full Regeneration (2022, journal, Journal of Automation Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Valentina Stojanović (R0233).
Keywords: incremental generation; model-to-text; Xtend; PLC; software product lines; model differencing.
Full regeneration of PLC source code from a configuration model is straightforward but can be impractical in projects where manually authored customisation sections exist alongside generated code. This paper presents an incremental generation strategy that identifies which model elements have changed between two configuration revisions and regenerates only the affected Structured Text compilation units, preserving protected regions in unaffected units. Change detection is implemented as a model differencing step operating on XMI serialisations of feature model configurations, producing a delta structure that drives selective Xtend template invocation. The strategy was evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 50 configuration pairs derived from a packaging-machine product line model with 41 features. Regeneration time was reduced by a mean of 74% compared to full regeneration, with no instances of incorrect code produced across 1,200 generated file revisions as verified by a regression test suite. The paper formalises the notion of generation dependency to characterise when incremental regeneration is sound.

SYN-PUB-03139.title: Timing Analysis of ISO 11783 Message Scheduling on Low-Cost ARM Cortex-M3 Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-03139.text:
Timing Analysis of ISO 11783 Message Scheduling on Low-Cost ARM Cortex-M3 Microcontrollers (2013, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Embedded and Distributed Systems (ISEDS), Bratislava).
Authors: Miroslav Đurić (outside co-author); Tibor Kovač (outside co-author); Darko Zarić (R0248).
Keywords: ISO 11783; CAN scheduling; ARM Cortex-M3; FreeRTOS; timing analysis.
This paper examines the timing behaviour of the ISO 11783 transport protocol (TP) and working-set maintenance messages when implemented on an ARM Cortex-M3 microcontroller running at 72 MHz with a bare-metal scheduler. Measurements were conducted using a custom CAN bus test bench consisting of three ECU nodes and a CANalyzer logging unit. Worst-case response times for address-claim procedures, process-data objects, and ETP multi-packet frames were recorded over 10 000 bus cycles under simulated load from a virtual terminal and a task controller. Results show that address-claim collisions increase worst-case latency by up to 38% compared to uncontested scenarios, and that standard FreeRTOS priority assignment does not meet all timing constraints under simultaneous TP and ETP traffic. A revised priority mapping scheme is proposed and validated experimentally, reducing deadline misses from 4.1% to 0.3% in the test configuration.

SYN-PUB-03140.title: Comparative Evaluation of ISOBUS Conformance Test Suites for Aftermarket Task Controllers
SYN-PUB-03140.text:
Comparative Evaluation of ISOBUS Conformance Test Suites for Aftermarket Task Controllers (2016, journal, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture Systems).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Tibor Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: ISOBUS conformance; task controller; AEF; test coverage; TC-GEO.
ISO 11783 conformance testing is carried out by accredited laboratories using proprietary test suites, but aftermarket ECU developers frequently rely on open-source or self-developed tools whose coverage is incomplete. This paper documents a structured comparison of three freely available ISOBUS test frameworks against the official AEF conformance test specification version 3.2, focusing on the task controller (TC-BAS, TC-SC, TC-GEO) server functionality. Each framework was applied to the same firmware image running on a prototype TC ECU, and discrepancies in test outcomes were logged across 247 individual test cases. The open-source tools missed 31 to 59 failure conditions identified by the reference suite, primarily in section 9 multi-section control and DDOP version negotiation. The analysis highlights specific gaps and proposes a supplementary test script library written in Python and distributed under an MIT licence that closes 24 of the identified gaps.

SYN-PUB-03141.title: Gateway Architectures for Mixed ISO 11783 and SAE J1939 Networks in Multi-Implement Tractor Configurations
SYN-PUB-03141.text:
Gateway Architectures for Mixed ISO 11783 and SAE J1939 Networks in Multi-Implement Tractor Configurations (2017, book chapter, Embedded Communication in Agricultural Machinery — Selected Doctoral Research, University of Novi Sad Press).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248).
Keywords: SAE J1939; ISO 11783; gateway topology; hardware-in-the-loop; CAN bridge.
Modern tractors often expose both an ISOBUS (ISO 11783) connector and a diagnostic SAE J1939 backbone, and integrating implements that assume one standard with a tractor that exposes only the other is a recurring problem for fleet operators. This dissertation chapter surveys five gateway topologies — transparent bridge, selective filtering, protocol translation, store-and-forward, and hybrid — and evaluates them against criteria of latency, bus load, configurability, and failure isolation. Experimental data were collected using a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test bench comprising a dSPACE MicroAutoBox (fictional equivalent: TechSim RapidECU) and three CAN channels. Results indicate that selective-filtering gateways provide the best latency profile (median 1.4 ms end-to-end) but require per-installation configuration, whereas store-and-forward designs tolerate baud-rate mismatches at the cost of a 6–12 ms additional delay. A decision matrix is offered to guide implementation choices based on application requirements.

SYN-PUB-03142.title: Object Dictionary Management Across Multiple CANopen Device Profiles in Distributed Seeding Machines
SYN-PUB-03142.text:
Object Dictionary Management Across Multiple CANopen Device Profiles in Distributed Seeding Machines (2019, journal, International Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Nemanja Perić (outside co-author); Gregor Mlakar (outside co-author).
Keywords: CANopen; object dictionary; DS406; DS408; multi-profile management; seed drill.
Pneumatic seed drills for row crops increasingly carry sensors and actuators from multiple vendors, each conforming to different CANopen device profiles (DS406 encoders, DS408 drives, DS401 I/O). Managing the resulting heterogeneous object dictionary landscape on a central master node is a non-trivial firmware engineering problem. This paper presents a dynamic object dictionary framework implemented on an STM32H7 master node that loads device-specific sub-dictionaries at run-time from CRC-verified flash partitions. The framework was validated on a 24-row seed drill with 72 CANopen nodes operating at 1 Mbit/s over a 6-metre cable harness. SDO access times remained below 3 ms for 98.7% of read operations across 48 hours of bench testing. The paper also reports on node guarding and heartbeat event timing under conditions where three or more nodes are simultaneously reinitialised, which is common during headland turns.

SYN-PUB-03143.title: Latency Profiling of ISOBUS Virtual Terminal Sessions over Extended CAN Harnesses Using Differential Probing
SYN-PUB-03143.text:
Latency Profiling of ISOBUS Virtual Terminal Sessions over Extended CAN Harnesses Using Differential Probing (2020, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Agricultural Engineering Systems (EuCAES), Zagreb).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Tibor Kovač (outside co-author); Raluca Ionescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: ISOBUS VT; CAN signal integrity; harness design; latency; eye diagram.
ISOBUS virtual terminal (VT) responsiveness degrades measurably on long cable runs typical in articulated combine harvesters and road-train configurations. This paper reports a systematic profiling study in which a VT client ECU communicating with a server was tested over harness lengths from 1 m to 40 m at 250 kbit/s, with termination resistance varied between 100 Ω and 130 Ω. Differential voltage probing at seven bus positions provided eye-diagram data alongside software-layer timing logs captured with microsecond resolution. Softkey and numeric-input response latencies increased by 18–34 ms on the 40 m harness compared to 1 m baselines, primarily attributable to ACK-bit timing margin erosion causing retransmissions. Improvements achieved by replacing standard 0.35 mm² twisted pair with 0.5 mm² screened cable and repositioning terminators to within 2 m of end nodes are quantified. The study provides guidance for harness design in large-format machinery.

SYN-PUB-03144.title: A Lightweight ISOBUS Task Controller Client Stack for Microcontrollers with 64 kB Flash
SYN-PUB-03144.text:
A Lightweight ISOBUS Task Controller Client Stack for Microcontrollers with 64 kB Flash (2022, journal, Microprocessors and Microsystems — Embedded Hardware Design).
Authors: Nemanja Perić (outside co-author); Ivana Bogdanović (outside co-author); Darko Zarić (R0248).
Keywords: TC client; ISOBUS; Cortex-M0+; flash-constrained; DDOP; section control.
Most open-source ISOBUS TC client implementations target MCUs with at least 256 kB of flash, which excludes a large class of low-cost sensor ECUs used on small farm implements in developing or budget-constrained markets. This paper describes the design and verification of a TC-BAS client stack written in C99 that compiles to 47.2 kB on a Cortex-M0+ target at -Os optimisation, leaving adequate space for application code. Design decisions including static DDOP allocation, integer-only arithmetic for device-descriptor encoding, and a two-state process-data pump are detailed. The stack was integrated into a prototype section-control module for a 6 m boom sprayer and tested against four commercial task controllers using the AEF plugfest procedure. Interoperability was confirmed with all four controllers for TC-BAS functionality; two edge cases in setpoint handling were identified and resolved during testing. Code is available on a public repository.

SYN-PUB-03145.title: Evaluation of FD-CAN for High-Speed Sensor Aggregation in ISOBUS-Connected Implements
SYN-PUB-03145.text:
Evaluation of FD-CAN for High-Speed Sensor Aggregation in ISOBUS-Connected Implements (2024, journal, Journal of Agricultural Mechatronics and Control Systems).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Ivana Bogdanović (outside co-author); Martin Hruška (outside co-author); Gregor Mlakar (outside co-author).
Keywords: CAN FD; ISOBUS; sensor aggregation; RH850; bus utilisation; precision farming.
CAN FD (flexible data rate) has been standardised but is not yet part of ISO 11783, leaving implement designers who require high sensor data throughput with an interoperability gap. This paper evaluates a hybrid architecture in which an implement-internal FD-CAN backbone at 2 Mbit/s data phase aggregates data from 18 soil-sensing nodes, while a translation ECU presents the aggregated values to the ISOBUS backbone at 250 kbit/s in standard-frame format. The translation ECU uses a Renesas RH850-based prototype board. Round-trip delay from sensor sampling to task-controller reception was measured at 4.7 ms median and 11.2 ms at the 99th percentile under full network load. Bus utilisation on the ISOBUS segment remained below 38% even during simultaneous VT and TC sessions. Limitations due to DDOP element count restrictions in TC-BAS profiles when representing 18 sensors are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03146.title: Interoperability Testing Methodology for ISOBUS AUX-N Function Assignments Across Implement Generations
SYN-PUB-03146.text:
Interoperability Testing Methodology for ISOBUS AUX-N Function Assignments Across Implement Generations (2025, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded Agricultural Systems (ICEAS), Novi Sad).
Authors: Darko Zarić (R0248); Nemanja Perić (outside co-author); Aleksandra Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: ISOBUS AUX-N; auxiliary control; interoperability; VT; ISO 11783-6; UID management.
The ISOBUS Auxiliary Control (AUX-N) service allows operators to assign joystick or button inputs from one ECU to functions on another. In mixed fleets combining implements manufactured over a decade-long span, AUX-N assignment tables stored in VT memory frequently produce mismatches after ECU replacement or firmware updates. This paper presents a structured testing methodology for AUX-N interoperability using a scripted test harness that replays 320 assignment sequences across four VT server implementations and six auxiliary-input-unit firmware versions. The study found that 41% of tested pairings produced at least one incorrect preferred-assignment restore after a power cycle, and that the root cause in most cases was differing interpretations of the AUX-N object UID persistence rules in the standard. Recommended firmware practices for UID management are described and an errata proposal for ISO 11783-6 is outlined.

SYN-PUB-03147.title: FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing
SYN-PUB-03147.text:
FPGA-Based Analog Front-End Emulation for Knock Sensor Signal Generation in Engine HiL Testing (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Control (Regional Edition)).
Authors: Milica Stanković (outside co-author); Darko Zarić (R0248); Andrej Hanus (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: knock sensor emulation; FPGA waveform generation; DAC; engine HiL; signal synthesis.
Knock sensors produce broadband vibration signals in the 5–15 kHz range that engine ECUs process through bandpass filters and envelope detectors to identify combustion knock events. Emulating these signals accurately on a HiL bench requires waveform generation with sufficient bandwidth and amplitude resolution. This work presents an FPGA-based waveform generator implemented on an Artix-7 device that produces synthetic knock and non-knock signals based on parameterised cylinder pressure traces from a four-cylinder naturally aspirated engine model. The generator uses a 16-bit DAC at 250 kS/s per channel and a lookup-table synthesis approach with four independently configurable channels. Signal quality was assessed by comparing spectra from the emulated output against recordings taken from a motored engine on a dynamometer test bench. Spectral flatness error within the 5–15 kHz band was below 1.8 dB. An ECU under test correctly classified knock events in 97.3% of 600 injected test cases. The paper details the fixed-point filter coefficients, DAC interface timing, and calibration procedure.

SYN-PUB-03183.title: Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes
SYN-PUB-03183.text:
Embedded Wavelet Lifting for ECG Compression on Wearable Cortex-M0 Nodes (2015, journal, Biomedical Engineering: Applications, Basis and Communications).
Authors: Slobodan Dražić (outside co-author); Ivana Horvatić (outside co-author); Tibor Takács (R0251); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Christoph Fiedler (outside co-author).
Keywords: ECG compression; wavelet lifting; wearable; Cortex-M0; BLE; PRD.
Electrocardiogram data transmitted from chest-patch wearables place a disproportionate load on BLE bandwidth. We ported a fixed-point integer lifting-scheme wavelet transform (5/3 Le Gall filter) to an ARM Cortex-M0 running at 48 MHz and paired it with a simple threshold quantiser and arithmetic coder. The implementation stores all intermediate coefficients in 12 kB of SRAM, fitting within the budget of low-cost microcontrollers. Compression was evaluated on 30-minute, two-lead recordings from 18 subjects sampled at 500 Hz. The scheme achieved a mean compression ratio of 9.4:1 at a percent root-mean-square difference (PRD) of 2.7%, which is within the clinically acceptable range for rhythm monitoring. QRS peak locations in reconstructed signals deviated by a mean of 1.2 ms from reference annotations. Runtime was 1.8 ms per 500-sample frame, leaving the processor idle for 64% of each sampling period. Power consumption during active compression was 3.1 mW.

SYN-PUB-03206.title: Passive Inference of Regular Tree Languages from XML Document Corpora
SYN-PUB-03206.text:
Passive Inference of Regular Tree Languages from XML Document Corpora (2018, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Applications of Formal Languages (SAFL)).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Slađana Paunović (R0253); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author).
Keywords: tree automata; regular tree languages; XML schema inference; RPNI; structured data.
Finite tree automata generalise string automata to tree-structured inputs. This paper extends the RPNI state-merging strategy to infer regular tree automata from corpora of XML documents treated as ordered labelled trees. We evaluate the approach on three real-world XML corpora: a collection of 9,400 bibliographic records, a set of 4,200 configuration files, and a corpus of 7,800 scientific article metadata documents. Ground-truth schemas expressed as Document Type Definitions (DTDs) are used as reference models. The inferred tree automata correctly accepted 96–99% of held-out valid documents and rejected 88–93% of artificially corrupted counterexamples across the three corpora. Merging order heuristics modelled on EDSM are shown to reduce the size of the inferred automaton by 15–30% compared to canonical RPNI ordering. Running times remain below two minutes on a commodity workstation for all corpora tested.

SYN-PUB-03207.title: Spatial copula modelling of extreme precipitation fields over the Carpathian–Pannonian region using max-stable processes
SYN-PUB-03207.text:
Spatial copula modelling of extreme precipitation fields over the Carpathian–Pannonian region using max-stable processes (2018, journal, Journal of Hydrometeorology).
Authors: Éva Molnár (outside co-author); Slađana Paunović (R0253); Radu Cojocaru (outside co-author); Nevena Kecman (R0408); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: max-stable processes; Brown–Resnick model; spatial extremes; composite likelihood; areal reduction factor.
Spatial risk assessment of extreme precipitation requires models that capture both the marginal behaviour at individual sites and the spatial dependence structure across the region. Max-stable processes provide a coherent framework for this task. Daily precipitation records from 62 stations in Hungary, Romania, Croatia and Serbia for the period 1971–2015 were obtained from national meteorological services. Marginal generalised extreme value parameters were estimated at each station, and three max-stable models — Smith, Schlather and Brown–Resnick — were fitted by pairwise composite likelihood. The Brown–Resnick model with an empirically estimated variogram was selected by the composite likelihood information criterion. Extremal coefficients between station pairs indicate that stations separated by more than 180 km are effectively independent for annual maximum daily precipitation. Areal reduction factors derived from the fitted model differ by up to 25 percent from those currently used in regional design guidelines.

SYN-PUB-03295.title: Bayesian Change-Point Detection in Non-Stationary Industrial Time Series
SYN-PUB-03295.text:
Bayesian Change-Point Detection in Non-Stationary Industrial Time Series (2014, journal, Journal of Applied Statistical Methods).
Authors: Pavol Struhár (R0261); Miroslava Kováčová (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: change-point detection; Bayesian online learning; particle filter; industrial time series.
This paper addresses the identification of abrupt structural changes in time series generated by industrial sensors operating at sampling rates between 10 Hz and 100 Hz. A Bayesian online algorithm based on a product-partition model is adapted to handle autocorrelated noise and missing observations, which are common in factory-floor deployments. The method was evaluated on 14 months of vibration data from three manufacturing sites in central Serbia, comprising approximately 2.1 billion data points. Posterior inference was carried out using a Rao–Blackwellised particle filter, with run-time profiling showing the algorithm processes a 100 Hz stream in under 8 milliseconds per sample on standard server hardware. Against a ground-truth log of 47 documented equipment incidents, the approach achieved a detection rate of 91.5% with a median latency of 1.3 seconds. A comparison with CUSUM and PELT baselines shows consistent improvement in false-positive rate at fixed recall. Model hyperparameters were set via empirical Bayes using an initial 30-day warm-up period.

SYN-PUB-03297.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Models for Failure Rate Heterogeneity Across Machine Populations
SYN-PUB-03297.text:
Hierarchical Bayesian Models for Failure Rate Heterogeneity Across Machine Populations (2018, journal, Reliability Engineering and Statistical Practice).
Authors: Miroslava Kováčová (outside co-author); Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261).
Keywords: hierarchical Bayesian model; failure rate; Poisson–Gamma; MCMC; predictive maintenance.
Industrial fleets of nominally identical machines exhibit substantial heterogeneity in failure rates even after controlling for operating conditions. This paper develops a hierarchical Bayesian Poisson–Gamma model for failure counts observed over irregular inspection intervals, allowing partial pooling of information across 312 compressor units monitored over three years at a natural gas distribution company. A Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler (No-U-Turn) was used for posterior estimation; convergence was verified via Gelman–Rubin diagnostics on 4 independent chains. Unit-level posterior failure rate estimates had a coefficient of variation of 0.34, confirming meaningful heterogeneity. Predictive posterior distributions for time to next failure were used to rank units by expected residual life, and a field trial showed that prioritising the bottom 20% of units by posterior mean life reduced unplanned outages by 31% compared to the previous calendar-based schedule. The sensitivity of results to prior hyperparameter choice is discussed, and a weakly informative default prior is recommended.

SYN-PUB-03298.title: Extreme-Value Modelling of Pressure Spike Amplitudes in Water Distribution Networks
SYN-PUB-03298.text:
Extreme-Value Modelling of Pressure Spike Amplitudes in Water Distribution Networks (2019, journal, Journal of Hydraulic Statistics and Risk Analysis).
Authors: Pavol Struhár (R0261); Maja Filipović (outside co-author); Nebojša Jovanović (R0282); Zoltán Varga (outside co-author); Gordana Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: extreme-value theory; GEV distribution; water distribution; IoT sensor; return levels.
Transient pressure spikes in water distribution networks can cause pipe fatigue and burst failures. This study fits generalised extreme-value (GEV) distributions to block maxima of pressure readings collected at 4 Hz from 28 monitoring nodes across the Novi Sad municipal network over 26 months. Block sizes of one week and one month are compared; likelihood ratio tests favour weekly blocks for this dataset. Maximum likelihood estimates indicate heavy-tailed behaviour (shape parameter ξ̂ ranging from 0.11 to 0.29 across nodes) that is inconsistent with Gaussian or exponential tail assumptions used in standard hydraulic standards. Return-level estimates at 10-year and 50-year periods are reported with 95% profile-likelihood confidence intervals. A spatial analysis using a max-stable process model reveals a correlation range of approximately 2.1 km, meaning that simultaneous extreme events at nodes within this distance must be treated as dependent. The results inform updated inspection intervals recommended to the municipal utility.

SYN-PUB-03299.title: Individualised Actuarial Pricing Using Telematics Features: A Credibility Theory Perspective
SYN-PUB-03299.text:
Individualised Actuarial Pricing Using Telematics Features: A Credibility Theory Perspective (2020, journal, European Actuarial Journal).
Authors: Radovan Nesić (outside co-author); Petra Zemanová (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261).
Keywords: actuarial pricing; credibility theory; telematics; Bayesian linear model; usage-based insurance.
Usage-based insurance pricing has shifted from simple mileage adjustments to models that incorporate behavioural features extracted from vehicle telematics. This paper re-examines the problem through the lens of Bühlmann–Straub credibility theory, showing that classic credibility estimators can be embedded in a Bayesian linear model with conjugate normal–inverse-gamma priors. Trip-level feature vectors (hard-braking rate, speed percentiles, time-of-day distribution, cornering events) were derived from 1 Hz GPS and accelerometer streams of 4,200 policyholders over 12 months, yielding approximately 18 million trip records. The credibility-weighted premium estimator reduced the mean squared prediction error of claim costs by 14.2% relative to a market-segment flat rate and by 6.8% relative to a generalised linear model with the same features but no credibility adjustment. The paper discusses regulatory constraints on feature selection under Serbian and EU insurance law and outlines a procedure for updating the model quarterly as new data arrive.

SYN-PUB-03300.title: Online Variational Inference for Streaming Sensor Anomaly Detection
SYN-PUB-03300.text:
Online Variational Inference for Streaming Sensor Anomaly Detection (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Danube Conference on Probabilistic Computing and Inference).
Authors: Siniša Đorđević (outside co-author); Ágnes Molnár (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261).
Keywords: variational inference; Dirichlet process; anomaly detection; streaming data; edge computing.
Batch Bayesian inference is impractical when sensor streams arrive continuously and model parameters must be updated in near real time. This paper investigates stochastic variational inference (SVI) as an online alternative, using a Gaussian mixture likelihood with a Dirichlet process prior to model the multimodal distribution of normal operating states. The algorithm processes mini-batches of 500 observations drawn from four temperature and humidity sensors on a cold-chain logistics platform, with one parameter update per second. On a 90-day evaluation dataset with 63 labelled anomaly episodes (ranging from 4 minutes to 11 hours), the SVI approach reached an area under the ROC curve of 0.93, compared to 0.89 for a static trained model retrained nightly. Memory footprint was 12 MB for the variational parameters, making the method deployable on edge devices with modest RAM. Drift in the variational posterior over time is characterised and a forgetting factor mechanism is proposed to prevent stale components from dominating.

SYN-PUB-03301.title: Risk Scoring for Agricultural IoT Networks Under Sparse and Irregular Sampling
SYN-PUB-03301.text:
Risk Scoring for Agricultural IoT Networks Under Sparse and Irregular Sampling (2022, journal, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture Statistics Supplement).
Authors: Maja Filipović (outside co-author); Branko Todorović (outside co-author); Kristína Polláková (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261).
Keywords: Gaussian process; irregular sampling; agricultural IoT; risk scoring; disease prediction.
Soil moisture, leaf wetness, and microclimate sensors deployed across vineyards in Fruška Gora are sampled irregularly owing to energy-harvesting constraints, yielding gaps that can span several days. This paper adapts a Gaussian process regression framework to reconstruct latent continuous processes from irregular observations and derives a composite risk score for fungal disease onset. The GP kernel is chosen by leave-one-vineyard-out cross-validation among Matérn 3/2, squared-exponential, and rational-quadratic families; Matérn 3/2 was selected in 11 of 14 vineyard sites. Risk score thresholds calibrated to achieve 85% sensitivity for disease onset predicted spray interventions 2.1 days earlier on average than the standard phenological calendar used by local agronomists, over three growing seasons across 14 sites. A cost-benefit analysis using spray cost and expected yield loss figures from local agricultural records shows a mean saving of approximately 310 EUR per hectare per season under the model-guided schedule.

SYN-PUB-03302.title: Probabilistic Load Forecasting for Small Industrial Consumers Using Meter Data and Bayesian Quantile Regression
SYN-PUB-03302.text:
Probabilistic Load Forecasting for Small Industrial Consumers Using Meter Data and Bayesian Quantile Regression (2023, journal, Statistical Methods in Energy Research).
Authors: Radovan Nesić (outside co-author); Pavol Struhár (R0261); Ivana Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: load forecasting; Bayesian quantile regression; smart meters; probabilistic forecasting; SME energy.
Short-term electricity load forecasting for small and medium industrial consumers is more difficult than for large sites owing to high variability relative to mean demand. This study uses 15-minute smart meter readings from 87 SME customers of a regional distribution company in Vojvodina, covering 28 months. A Bayesian quantile regression model is fitted for each customer, with temperature, hour-of-day, day-of-week, and a 5-lag autoregressive component as covariates. Posterior predictive intervals at the 10th, 50th, and 90th quantiles are evaluated using the pinball loss and empirical coverage. Compared to a pooled point-forecast baseline, the per-customer Bayesian model reduces pinball loss by a median of 18% and achieves nominal coverage within 2 percentage points for 81 of 87 customers. The paper discusses practical aspects of deploying the model in a metering data management system, including re-estimation frequency and handling of customers with fewer than six months of history.

SYN-PUB-03304.title: Sequential Bayesian Updating of Remaining Useful Life Distributions Under Concept Drift
SYN-PUB-03304.text:
Sequential Bayesian Updating of Remaining Useful Life Distributions Under Concept Drift (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.XXXXX).
Authors: Pavol Struhár (R0261); Siniša Đorđević (outside co-author); Ágnes Molnár (outside co-author); Sofija Đukić (R0785); Marco Ciotti (outside co-author).
Keywords: remaining useful life; sequential Bayesian updating; concept drift; importance weighting; predictive maintenance.
Remaining useful life (RUL) models for rotating equipment are typically trained once and then applied statically, but operating conditions and load profiles drift over months or years, causing predictive accuracy to degrade. This preprint proposes a sequential Bayesian updating scheme in which the posterior over RUL model parameters is revised each time a failure or censoring event is recorded, using an importance-weighted likelihood that down-weights observations older than a tunable half-life τ. The method is evaluated on three datasets: a benchmark turbofan engine simulation, a set of 41 conveyor belt drives monitored over 31 months, and compressor units from a previous study by the same group. Choosing τ by cross-validation over a held-out cohort reduced mean absolute RUL error by 22% compared to the static model and by 9% compared to periodic full re-fitting on a 90-day rolling window. Computational overhead relative to a static model is approximately 3% per update cycle.

SYN-PUB-03365.title: Autonomy-supportive versus controlling language in motivational texts for increasing walking behaviour: a two-week diary study
SYN-PUB-03365.text:
Autonomy-supportive versus controlling language in motivational texts for increasing walking behaviour: a two-week diary study (2015, journal, Balkan Journal of Applied Psychology).
Authors: Branislava Lekić (R0413); Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Katarina Simić (outside co-author); Katarina Nedeljković (R0297); Filip Todić (R0267).
Keywords: self-determination theory; autonomy support; physical activity; SMS intervention; accelerometry.
Grounded in self-determination theory, this experiment examined whether daily motivational text messages framed with autonomy-supportive language (emphasising choice and personal relevance) differed from controlling language (emphasising obligation and external expectations) in promoting daily step counts and intrinsic motivation for walking. Eighty-four sedentary adults from Novi Sad were randomised to one of three conditions: autonomy-supportive SMS, controlling SMS, or no-message control. Step counts were logged via a wrist-worn accelerometer over 14 days. Participants receiving autonomy-supportive messages accumulated on average 1,240 more steps per day than the control group (95% CI: 490–1,990) and reported higher autonomous motivation on a post-study questionnaire. The controlling message group did not differ significantly from the control. Autonomous motivation at day 7 partially mediated the effect on day-14 step counts (indirect effect β = 0.18, bootstrapped CI: 0.06–0.33). Findings support applying autonomy-supportive communication principles when designing brief mobile health nudges.

SYN-PUB-03470.title: Material Flow Analysis in a Thermoplastic Extrusion Plant: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
SYN-PUB-03470.text:
Material Flow Analysis in a Thermoplastic Extrusion Plant: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region (2010, journal, Journal of Cleaner Production and Process Engineering).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Vesna Todorov (outside co-author); Ladislav Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: material flow analysis; thermoplastic extrusion; mass balance; polyethylene; Vojvodina.
This study applies material flow analysis (MFA) to a medium-sized thermoplastic extrusion facility in Vojvodina, Serbia, processing approximately 4,200 tonnes of polyethylene and polypropylene annually. System boundaries were drawn from raw pellet delivery to finished pipe dispatch. Mass balances were compiled for twelve input and output streams, including resin, pigment masterbatch, process cooling water, and solid scrap. Field measurements over six months revealed that 6.3% of input polymer leaves the process as off-specification product or trim waste, while cooling water circuits contributed to 18% of total site water consumption. A Sankey diagram representation was constructed and cross-checked against utility invoices. Discrepancies between metered and calculated values were below 5% for energy carriers and below 9% for water streams. Results were used to identify three priority areas for environmental improvement: lubricant oil management, die-cleaning solvent recovery, and edge-trim recycling. The methodology is presented in a format compatible with ISO 14001 planning requirements.

SYN-PUB-03473.title: Life-Cycle Inventory Dataset for Polypropylene Injection Moulding in Southeast European Manufacturing Conditions
SYN-PUB-03473.text:
Life-Cycle Inventory Dataset for Polypropylene Injection Moulding in Southeast European Manufacturing Conditions (2015, journal, International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment and Sustainability).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Annett Kröger (outside co-author); Ladislav Fekete (outside co-author); Gábor Németh (outside co-author).
Keywords: life-cycle inventory; polypropylene; injection moulding; ecoinvent; Southeast Europe.
Existing commercial LCA databases contain life-cycle inventory (LCI) data predominantly derived from Western European manufacturing conditions, which may introduce systematic errors when applied to assessments in Southeast Europe. This study constructs a foreground LCI dataset for polypropylene injection moulding based on primary data collected from five facilities in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Hungary. Data collection covered electricity consumption (average 2.31 kWh/kg product), natural gas for mould heating, cooling water makeup, hydraulic oil losses, mould-release agent, and solid waste streams. Electricity grid mixes specific to each country were applied. The resulting dataset covers seventeen elementary flow categories and is formatted for compatibility with ecoinvent 3.x conventions. Unit process outputs per functional unit (one kilogram of moulded PP part) are reported with uncertainty ranges estimated via pedigree matrix. The dataset is compared against the ecoinvent 'injection moulding' proxy, revealing a 14–22% underestimation of GWP when the proxy is applied to Serbian grid conditions.

SYN-PUB-03474.title: Comparative Eco-Profile of Recycled and Virgin Granulate in Pipe Extrusion: An LCA Perspective
SYN-PUB-03474.text:
Comparative Eco-Profile of Recycled and Virgin Granulate in Pipe Extrusion: An LCA Perspective (2018, journal, Resources, Conservation and Industrial Ecology).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Radu Ionescu (outside co-author); Mirjana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: life-cycle assessment; recycled HDPE; pipe extrusion; eco-profile; circular economy.
Post-consumer and post-industrial recycled polymer granulate is increasingly used in non-pressure pipe extrusion as a partial substitute for virgin resin. This study presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of pipe production using three material compositions: 100% virgin HDPE, a 30% recycled/70% virgin blend, and a 50% recycled/50% virgin blend. Primary LCI data were collected at a pipe extrusion plant in Serbia; recycled granulate supply chain data were sourced from two regional collection and reprocessing facilities in Serbia and Romania. Impact categories assessed include global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, water depletion, and urban land occupation. Results show that substituting 30% virgin HDPE with post-industrial recyclate reduces GWP by 19% per linear metre of DN110 pipe, while the 50% blend achieves a 31% reduction. Energy demand reductions are partially offset by higher scrap rates and increased sorting energy at the recycler. Sensitivity analysis was performed on transport distance assumptions and electricity grid mix.

SYN-PUB-03475.title: Integration of Environmental Aspect Register with EMAS Reporting in a Polymer Recycling Facility
SYN-PUB-03475.text:
Integration of Environmental Aspect Register with EMAS Reporting in a Polymer Recycling Facility (2021, journal, Journal of Environmental Management and Compliance).
Authors: Ladislav Fekete (outside co-author); Martin Hriešik (R0277).
Keywords: EMAS; environmental aspect register; polymer recycling; ISO 14001; environmental performance indicators.
This paper describes the construction and integration of a structured environmental aspect register at a polymer mechanical recycling facility in Vojvodina that sought EMAS registration. The facility processes mixed post-consumer polyolefin waste at approximately 6,500 tonnes per year through sorting, granulation, and compounding lines. The aspect register was built following ISO 14001:2015 clause 6.1.2, covering thirty-one identified aspects across four process areas. Significance criteria applied were regulatory sensitivity, frequency of occurrence, severity of potential impact, and stakeholder concern. Eight aspects were rated significant, including cooling water discharge, granulator dust emissions, solvent use in quality testing, and noise from outdoor shredding. The environmental performance indicators (EPIs) derived from the register were mapped to EMAS Annex IV core indicators. Baseline performance data for three consecutive years (2017–2019) are reported. The paper discusses practical difficulties encountered in quantifying diffuse dust emissions and in aligning aspect significance rankings with operator safety risk assessments.

SYN-PUB-03476.title: Effluent Treatment Options for Cooling Tower Blowdown in Polymer Processing: Technical and Cost Comparison
SYN-PUB-03476.text:
Effluent Treatment Options for Cooling Tower Blowdown in Polymer Processing: Technical and Cost Comparison (2022, journal, Water and Process Engineering Review).
Authors: Mirjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Neven Brkić (outside co-author); Martin Hriešik (R0277); Marija Stojanović (R0618); Annett Kröger (outside co-author).
Keywords: cooling tower blowdown; electrocoagulation; membrane filtration; biocide removal; polymer processing.
Cooling tower blowdown in polymer processing facilities contains biocides, corrosion inhibitors, and scale-control agents that complicate discharge to municipal sewer systems. This paper evaluates four treatment configurations for blowdown streams at two facilities in Serbia: direct discharge with pH correction only, coagulation–flocculation followed by sand filtration, electrocoagulation, and membrane filtration (ultrafiltration + reverse osmosis). Assessment criteria were removal efficiency for key parameters (COD, conductivity, total hardness, biocide residues), capital and operating cost per cubic metre treated, and sludge generation. Electrocoagulation achieved 87% COD removal and 94% biocide removal at a treatment cost of approximately 1.8 EUR/m³, compared with 3.4 EUR/m³ for the membrane option, which produced superior effluent quality but generated a concentrated reject stream requiring separate management. A decision matrix weighted for regulatory compliance probability, operating complexity, and total cost is presented to guide facility selection of appropriate treatment technology.

SYN-PUB-03477.title: Carbon Footprint Scope 3 Estimation for a Serbian Plastics Converter: Data Quality Challenges and Methodological Choices
SYN-PUB-03477.text:
Carbon Footprint Scope 3 Estimation for a Serbian Plastics Converter: Data Quality Challenges and Methodological Choices (2023, journal, Central European Journal of Environmental Management).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Tamara Bjelopavlić (outside co-author); Gábor Németh (outside co-author).
Keywords: Scope 3 emissions; GHG Protocol; carbon footprint; plastics converter; value chain.
Scope 3 greenhouse gas accounting is increasingly expected of manufacturing companies seeking environmental certification or responding to supply chain due diligence requirements. This paper documents a Scope 3 inventory developed for a Serbian plastics converter producing packaging components, with annual turnover of approximately 12 million EUR.
