Following GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain Standard categories, the study covers upstream raw material extraction and transport, waste disposal, employee commuting, and downstream transport to customers. Primary data were available for seven of fifteen relevant categories; spend-based and average-data methods were applied for the remainder. Total Scope 3 emissions were estimated at 8,240 tCO2e per year, with upstream polymer production accounting for 74% of that total. The paper identifies five categories where data quality is insufficient for confident reporting and proposes a prioritised data collection roadmap. Sensitivity of total Scope 3 to polymer granulate emission factor choice is demonstrated through a ±15% scenario analysis.

SYN-PUB-03478.title: Mapping Environmental Legal Obligations for Polymer Processors Under the Updated Serbian Environmental Protection Act: A Practitioner's Analysis
SYN-PUB-03478.text:
Mapping Environmental Legal Obligations for Polymer Processors Under the Updated Serbian Environmental Protection Act: A Practitioner's Analysis (2024, journal, Environmental Law and Industry Practice).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Vesna Todorov (outside co-author); Jelena Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: environmental legislation; Serbia; integrated permit; BAT; VOC regulation.
Serbia amended its core Environmental Protection Act and associated by-laws in 2021–2022 in the process of aligning national legislation with the EU acquis. This paper analyses the implications of these changes for polymer processing facilities subject to integrated environmental permits (operators above threshold emission values) and those covered only by the simplified permit regime. Key changes examined include revised best available technique (BAT) applicability criteria for the plastics sector, updated emission limit values for volatile organic compounds, new requirements for soil and groundwater monitoring at industrial sites, and expanded environmental liability provisions. The analysis is based on review of primary legal texts, comparison with the corresponding EU Industrial Emissions Directive articles, and structured interviews with twelve compliance officers at Serbian polymer processing companies. The paper identifies seven compliance gaps that are commonly observed in current facility permit conditions and are likely to trigger corrective requirements during the next permit review cycle.

SYN-PUB-03479.title: Dynamic LCI Modelling for Polymer Processing Facilities: Accounting for Production Rate Variability and Seasonal Grid Mix
SYN-PUB-03479.text:
Dynamic LCI Modelling for Polymer Processing Facilities: Accounting for Production Rate Variability and Seasonal Grid Mix (2026, preprint, EarthArXiv).
Authors: Martin Hriešik (R0277); Ladislav Fekete (outside co-author); Annett Kröger (outside co-author); Boris Lalić (R0644); Aleksandar Ristić (R0473); Dávid Pataki (outside co-author).
Keywords: dynamic LCA; life-cycle inventory; production variability; marginal electricity; cast film extrusion.
Standard life-cycle inventory modelling assumes static production conditions, but polymer processing facilities operate at variable production rates and are supplied by electricity grids whose carbon intensity changes seasonally and hour-by-hour. This preprint presents a dynamic LCI framework in which production rate data (sampled at fifteen-minute intervals from SCADA logs at a cast film extrusion facility over twelve months) are combined with hourly marginal electricity emission factors derived from the Serbian transmission operator's dispatch data. Results show that the GWP of one kilogram of produced film varies by a factor of 1.7 between high-output summer shifts and low-output winter weekend periods, driven primarily by electricity carbon intensity variability. A simplified annual average LCI underestimates peak-period GWP by up to 34%. The framework is implemented in a Python workflow interfacing with SimaPro via CSV import, and the code is deposited in a public repository. Implications for EPD verification and environmental benchmarking programmes are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03494.title: Acoustic Emission Detection of Partial Discharges in Oil-Filled Model Transformers Using PVDF Sensors
SYN-PUB-03494.text:
Acoustic Emission Detection of Partial Discharges in Oil-Filled Model Transformers Using PVDF Sensors (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 19th International Symposium on High Voltage Engineering (ISH Balkans), Novi Sad).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Bojan Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: PVDF sensor; PZT sensor; partial discharge; acoustic emission; time-difference-of-arrival.
This paper presents a comparative study of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and PZT piezoelectric sensors for detecting partial discharge (PD) events in a laboratory-scale oil-filled transformer model. A needle-to-sphere electrode arrangement was used to generate controlled PD activity at three voltage levels (25, 40, and 55 kV rms). Six PVDF sensors and four PZT sensors were mounted on the tank surface. Acoustic signals were recorded at a sampling rate of 5 MHz and compared against simultaneous IEC 60270 electrical PD measurements. PVDF sensors exhibited a flatter frequency response between 50 and 300 kHz, while PZT sensors showed higher sensitivity in the 100–250 kHz band. Localisation errors using time-difference-of-arrival on the PVDF array averaged 18 mm, compared with 31 mm for the PZT array under the same conditions. Signal attenuation through transformer oil was characterised as a function of temperature between 20 and 80 °C. Results suggest that PVDF arrays offer a practical advantage for wideband acquisition in compact tank geometries.

SYN-PUB-03495.title: Influence of Oil Temperature on Acoustic Propagation Velocity and Partial Discharge Localisation Accuracy in Power Transformers
SYN-PUB-03495.text:
Influence of Oil Temperature on Acoustic Propagation Velocity and Partial Discharge Localisation Accuracy in Power Transformers (2018, journal, IET High Voltage).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: acoustic propagation velocity; transformer oil; thermal ageing; localisation correction; time-difference-of-arrival.
Accurate source localisation of partial discharges via acoustic emission methods depends on a reliable estimate of sound propagation velocity in transformer oil, which varies with temperature and oil ageing. This study measured acoustic propagation velocity in new and thermally aged mineral insulating oil samples at temperatures ranging from 15 to 85 °C using a pulse-echo technique at 150 kHz. Velocity decreased from 1430 m/s at 15 °C to 1280 m/s at 85 °C in new oil, with aged samples showing velocities approximately 2–4% lower across the same range. A correction algorithm was derived from polynomial regression on the measured data and integrated into a four-sensor time-difference-of-arrival localisation routine. Experimental validation in a 100 kVA model transformer showed that applying the temperature correction reduced mean localisation error from 27 mm to 11 mm when oil temperature shifted from 20 to 70 °C during a measurement session. The correction coefficients are provided in tabulated form for direct implementation.

SYN-PUB-03496.title: Wavelet Packet Decomposition of Acoustic Partial Discharge Signals for Discharge-Type Discrimination in Transformer Insulation
SYN-PUB-03496.text:
Wavelet Packet Decomposition of Acoustic Partial Discharge Signals for Discharge-Type Discrimination in Transformer Insulation (2019, journal, Electrical Engineering (Archiv für Elektrotechnik)).
Authors: Tamás Varga (outside co-author); Bojan Krstić (outside co-author); Nenad Stanković (outside co-author); Ivana Novaković (R0280).
Keywords: wavelet packet decomposition; discharge-type classification; acoustic emission; k-nearest neighbour; transformer insulation.
Three representative partial discharge source types relevant to power transformer insulation — surface discharge along pressboard barriers, internal void discharge in oil-impregnated paper, and corona from a metallic protrusion — were produced in a controlled test cell and characterised using a six-element piezoelectric sensor array. Acoustic emission signals were processed with a wavelet packet decomposition scheme using a Daubechies-8 mother wavelet at five decomposition levels. Energy distribution across the resulting 32 sub-bands was used as a feature vector for each discharge type. A k-nearest-neighbour classifier trained on 480 labelled waveforms achieved 91.4% classification accuracy on a 120-sample test set, outperforming a threshold-based frequency centroid method that reached 74.2% under the same conditions. Misclassifications occurred primarily between surface and internal void sources when signal-to-noise ratio fell below 12 dB. The paper also examines the effect of sensor coupling agent (silicone grease versus epoxy) on sub-band energy reproducibility across repeated mounting cycles.

SYN-PUB-03497.title: Frequency-Selective Impedance Measurement as an Indirect Indicator of Partial Discharge Onset Voltage in Oil-Paper Insulation
SYN-PUB-03497.text:
Frequency-Selective Impedance Measurement as an Indirect Indicator of Partial Discharge Onset Voltage in Oil-Paper Insulation (2020, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dielectrics and Electrical Insulation).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Katarzyna Walczak (outside co-author).
Keywords: impedance spectroscopy; oil-paper insulation; partial discharge inception; thermal ageing; dielectric diagnostics.
This study investigates whether changes in the complex impedance spectrum of oil-paper insulation at frequencies between 1 Hz and 1 MHz can serve as a precursor to partial discharge inception, measured by conventional IEC 60270 methods. Flat test cells consisting of three layers of thermally aged kraft paper impregnated with mineral oil were subjected to a step-ramp voltage protocol while simultaneous impedance spectra were recorded with a four-terminal impedance analyser at 50 V signal amplitude. For cells aged at 110 °C for periods of 0, 250, 500, and 1000 hours, the partial discharge inception voltage decreased from 12.1 kV to 7.4 kV while the loss tangent at 1 kHz increased from 0.0031 to 0.019. A peak in the derivative of the imaginary impedance component with respect to voltage, observable at frequencies above 10 kHz, consistently preceded electrical PD inception by 3–8% of the inception voltage in all 27 tested specimens. The method is proposed as a non-disruptive complement to acoustic PD monitoring during field transformer inspections.

SYN-PUB-03498.title: Combined Acoustic–Electrical Partial Discharge Measurement System for On-Site Power Transformer Diagnostics: Design and Field Evaluation
SYN-PUB-03498.text:
Combined Acoustic–Electrical Partial Discharge Measurement System for On-Site Power Transformer Diagnostics: Design and Field Evaluation (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnosys), Pilsen).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Nenad Stanković (outside co-author); Radovan Popović (outside co-author); Tamás Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: on-site measurement; acoustic-electrical correlation; FPGA acquisition; transformer diagnostics; GPS synchronisation.
A portable measurement system combining an eight-channel piezoelectric acoustic emission array with a synchronised electrical partial discharge acquisition channel compliant with IEC 60270 was designed and evaluated at three 110/35 kV transformers in substations in Vojvodina. The system uses a compact field-programmable gate array data acquisition unit with 10 MHz sampling on each acoustic channel and 30 MHz on the electrical channel, synchronised via GPS pulse-per-second signal to permit time correlation of acoustic and electrical events. On-site measurements at each transformer spanned six hours under normal service voltage. At one unit, consistent acoustic events were detected correlating with electrical PD charges of 180–420 pC, and the three-dimensional source position was estimated at 340 mm from the HV lead-out bushing, which aligned with findings from subsequent internal inspection. The paper describes the hardware architecture, shielding approach for the electrical channel in the substation electromagnetic environment, and the semi-automatic event correlation procedure used in data post-processing.

SYN-PUB-03499.title: Short-Time Fractional Fourier Transform Applied to Partial Discharge Acoustic Emission Signals in Power Transformers
SYN-PUB-03499.text:
Short-Time Fractional Fourier Transform Applied to Partial Discharge Acoustic Emission Signals in Power Transformers (2023, journal, Signal Processing (Elsevier)).
Authors: Ivana Novaković (R0280); Aleksandra Pejović (outside co-author); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: fractional Fourier transform; time-frequency analysis; acoustic emission; partial discharge; dispersive propagation.
Standard time-frequency representations such as the short-time Fourier transform and continuous wavelet transform have known limitations when applied to dispersive acoustic signals recorded on transformer tank walls, where multiple propagation modes arrive at different times with different frequency contents. This paper examines the short-time fractional Fourier transform (STFrFT) as an alternative representation, evaluating its ability to concentrate energy for chirp-like acoustic PD signals generated by needle-plate discharges in a 630 kVA transformer model. The optimal rotation angle in the fractional Fourier domain was estimated from the chirp rate extracted from Wigner–Ville distributions of reference signals, yielding rotation angles between 0.81π and 0.94π for the discharge configurations tested. STFrFT representations improved energy concentration by 23–38% compared with the standard STFT as measured by the Rényi entropy criterion, and the improved localisation of impulse energy in the joint domain reduced the uncertainty in time-of-arrival estimation by approximately 1.2 µs on average. Computation time on a standard workstation was 340 ms per waveform at 5 MHz sampling, which is discussed in the context of practical implementation.

SYN-PUB-03500.title: Effect of Mechanical Clamping Pressure on Piezoelectric Sensor Sensitivity and Repeatability in Acoustic Partial Discharge Measurements
SYN-PUB-03500.text:
Effect of Mechanical Clamping Pressure on Piezoelectric Sensor Sensitivity and Repeatability in Acoustic Partial Discharge Measurements (2024, journal, NDT & E International).
Authors: Bojan Krstić (outside co-author); Ivana Novaković (R0280).
Keywords: piezoelectric sensor; clamping force; acoustic coupling; measurement repeatability; sensor fixture.
Attachment consistency of piezoelectric sensors to transformer tank walls is rarely controlled in practice and may contribute substantially to inter-measurement variability in acoustic PD diagnostics. This paper reports a systematic study in which six PZT-5A disc sensors were attached to a 100 mm thick steel plate using a spring-loaded clamping fixture allowing controlled normal forces between 5 and 80 N, with and without silicone coupling gel. Frequency response functions were measured by pencil-lead break excitation at a fixed point, with 30 repeated attachment–detachment cycles at each force level. Sensitivity at 150 kHz varied by up to 8.4 dB across the 5–80 N range, with a plateau of stable response above 35 N. Cycle-to-cycle reproducibility, expressed as standard deviation of the peak sensitivity, was 0.9 dB above 35 N and 2.6 dB below 20 N. A minimum clamping force of 40 N with coupling gel is recommended for field measurements where quantitative comparison between sessions is required. These findings are directly relevant to the design of permanent or semi-permanent sensor fixtures for continuous monitoring systems.

SYN-PUB-03501.title: Impedance-Acoustic Joint Feature Extraction for Ageing-Condition Classification of 110 kV Power Transformers: A Data Collection Study
SYN-PUB-03501.text:
Impedance-Acoustic Joint Feature Extraction for Ageing-Condition Classification of 110 kV Power Transformers: A Data Collection Study (2026, preprint, arXiv (eess.SP)).
Authors: Nenad Stanković (outside co-author); Radovan Popović (outside co-author); Ivana Novaković (R0280); Lucija Horvat (outside co-author); Aleksandra Pejović (outside co-author).
Keywords: transformer ageing; joint feature extraction; impedance spectrum; dissolved gas analysis; clustering.
This preprint describes a field data collection campaign carried out at 18 power transformers of the same series (110/10 kV, 40 MVA) operated by a regional distribution company in Vojvodina, spanning installation dates from 1987 to 2009. For each unit, the following data were collected during planned outages: broadband impedance spectra (1 Hz–1 MHz, four-terminal), dissolved gas analysis results, degree of polymerisation from oil furfural content, and a one-hour acoustic PD survey under induced voltage at 1.05 pu. A feature vector of 38 parameters extracted from impedance spectra and acoustic PD pulse descriptors was computed for each transformer. Hierarchical clustering on the feature matrix suggested three groups broadly corresponding to low, moderate, and high insulation degradation as judged by the furfural-based DP estimates. Within-group variance was dominated by acoustic features in the 100–200 kHz band and by the imaginary impedance slope between 10 and 100 kHz. The dataset (anonymised) is made available as a supplement to encourage independent analysis. A follow-up study with a larger sample is planned.

SYN-PUB-03505.title: Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations
SYN-PUB-03505.text:
Towards a Unified Security Profile for Over-the-Air Firmware Update in IEC 62443 Compliant Industrial Installations (2026, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Ivana Novaković (R0280); Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 62443; firmware update; industrial security standards; security level; OTA compliance.
IEC 62443 defines security levels and component requirements for industrial automation and control systems but provides limited normative guidance on firmware update mechanisms. This paper analyses firmware update security requirements implied by IEC 62443-3-3 and IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Levels 1 through 3, identifying 23 specific requirements that a compliant OTA firmware update subsystem must satisfy. For each requirement, the paper maps existing technical mechanisms — from HMAC-based integrity checking to certificate-based authentication and monotonic rollback counters — and identifies three areas where current practice does not clearly satisfy the standard's intent: cryptographic agility, update transaction atomicity across power loss events, and audit logging on Class 1 devices. A reference architecture for a compliant firmware update service is outlined, and the paper estimates implementation effort in person-months for each architectural component at three device capability tiers. The analysis is illustrated using data from two anonymised industrial deployments reviewed during the study.

SYN-PUB-03532.title: Bivariate tail dependence in simultaneous flood peaks on tributaries of the Danube in the Vojvodina region
SYN-PUB-03532.text:
Bivariate tail dependence in simultaneous flood peaks on tributaries of the Danube in the Vojvodina region (2008, journal, Journal of Stochastic Hydrology and Water Management).
Authors: Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Milan Sekulić (R0990); Nebojša Jovanović (R0282); Svetlana Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: tail dependence; Archimedean copulas; flood frequency; Danube tributaries; joint exceedance probability.
Simultaneous high-discharge events on adjacent tributaries of the Danube present a compound flood risk that univariate frequency analysis cannot capture. Daily mean discharge records from six gauging stations in Vojvodina for the period 1961–2005 were assembled from the Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. Pairwise tail dependence coefficients were estimated using the non-parametric rank-based estimator of Coles, Heffernan and Tawn, and three Archimedean copula families — Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard and Frank — were fitted by maximum likelihood. The Gumbel–Hougaard copula consistently gave the best fit according to the Cramér–von Mises goodness-of-fit statistic for the upper tail. Estimated upper tail dependence coefficients ranged from 0.18 to 0.47 depending on the station pair, indicating moderate but non-negligible co-occurrence risk. Joint exceedance probabilities for the 100-year marginal quantile were computed and compared with those implied by the independence assumption; the independence assumption underestimated joint exceedance probability by up to 31 percent. Implications for levee design standards under simultaneous loading are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03535.title: A Lumped-Parameter EMI Source Model for Three-Phase PWM Drives: Parameter Extraction and Frequency-Range Validation
SYN-PUB-03535.text:
A Lumped-Parameter EMI Source Model for Three-Phase PWM Drives: Parameter Extraction and Frequency-Range Validation (2016, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Miroslav Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: EMI model; parameter extraction; vector network analyser; CM/DM separation; three-phase drive.
Accurate EMI source models are needed to reduce reliance on full-system measurements during filter development. This work describes a parameter extraction procedure for a lumped CM and DM source model of a three-phase 7.5 kW drive. Impedance parameters were extracted from open- and short-circuit measurements at the drive AC terminals using a vector network analyser across 100 kHz–30 MHz. The resulting model comprises eight passive elements representing the inverter module, gate-drive supply, motor cable, and chassis coupling capacitances. Model predictions of conducted emission spectra were compared against LISN measurements at three load points (25%, 50%, and 100% rated torque), yielding a root-mean-square spectral error of 2.1 dB for CM and 2.8 dB for DM components. The extraction procedure is repeatable and requires less than two hours of bench time, making it practical for production-variant characterisation in industrial settings.

SYN-PUB-03536.title: Passive EMC Filter Sizing for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 Compliance: A Design Procedure Based on Attenuation Margin Analysis
SYN-PUB-03536.text:
Passive EMC Filter Sizing for IEC 61800-3 Category C2 Compliance: A Design Procedure Based on Attenuation Margin Analysis (2017, journal, European Transactions on Electrical Power Systems).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Predrag Stanojević (outside co-author).
Keywords: EMC filter design; IEC 61800-3; attenuation margin; nanocrystalline core; insertion loss.
This paper presents a structured procedure for dimensioning passive EMC input filters for variable-speed drives to meet IEC 61800-3 Category C2 quasi-peak limits. The procedure uses measured CM and DM source impedances and a target attenuation profile derived from the gap between unfiltered emission spectra and the regulatory limit line, with a 6 dB safety margin applied throughout. Filter topologies (LC, LCL, and CL stages) are compared for a 15 kW test drive, and component values are selected to avoid resonances within the 150 kHz–2 MHz band that could cause limit exceedances at intermediate frequencies. Prototype filters were wound on nanocrystalline toroidal cores and verified by insertion-loss measurement per IEC 60939-3 before integration. Final compliance measurements confirmed that all quasi-peak and average readings were at least 5 dB below the Category C2 limit across the full 150 kHz–30 MHz range. Total filter volume was 0.38 litres and mass 0.61 kg for the 15 kW case.

SYN-PUB-03537.title: Effect of Motor Cable Length on Common-Mode Conducted Emissions in Variable-Speed Drive Systems
SYN-PUB-03537.text:
Effect of Motor Cable Length on Common-Mode Conducted Emissions in Variable-Speed Drive Systems (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives (PEMD-CEE)).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Thomas Berger (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author).
Keywords: motor cable; cable capacitance; cable shielding; CM emissions; transmission-line model.
Long motor cables are common in industrial installations and amplify common-mode conducted disturbances by adding distributed capacitance to ground. This experimental study quantifies the effect for shielded and unshielded cables of lengths 5 m, 20 m, and 50 m connected to a 5.5 kW drive. CM conducted emission levels at the drive input were measured for each combination. Unshielded 50 m cables increased broadband CM noise by 10–14 dB relative to the 5 m reference below 1 MHz, primarily due to cable-to-ground capacitance estimated at 3.4 nF for the 50 m case. Shield grounding at both ends reduced CM emissions by 5–9 dB across 150 kHz–5 MHz for the 20 m cable. A transmission-line model incorporating per-unit-length parameters measured by time-domain reflectometry reproduced the resonant structure of the emission spectrum within ±3 dB. Practical wiring recommendations derived from the data are summarised for installation engineers.

SYN-PUB-03539.title: EMC Filter Design for SiC MOSFET-Based Motor Drives: Comparison with IGBT Baseline at 150 kHz–30 MHz
SYN-PUB-03539.text:
EMC Filter Design for SiC MOSFET-Based Motor Drives: Comparison with IGBT Baseline at 150 kHz–30 MHz (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd European Conference on Power Electronics and Applications (EPE-ECCE Europe)).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thomas Berger (outside co-author).
Keywords: SiC MOSFET; IGBT comparison; rise time; high-frequency EMI; four-stage filter.
Silicon carbide MOSFET inverters switch at voltages and currents with rise times below 50 ns, generating significantly higher high-frequency conducted emissions than conventional IGBT-based drives of equivalent power rating. This work compares the conducted emission spectra of a 7.5 kW SiC MOSFET drive (switching at 50 kHz) and an IGBT baseline (switching at 8 kHz) under the same load, and documents the additional filter attenuation required to achieve IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance for the SiC case. The SiC drive exceeded the Category C2 quasi-peak limit by up to 22 dB in the 5–30 MHz band compared to 9 dB for the IGBT. An optimised four-stage LC filter reduced the worst-case exceedance to within the 6 dB safety margin, at the cost of a 40% increase in filter volume relative to the IGBT design. Measured and simulated spectra agree within ±3 dB across the full range.

SYN-PUB-03540.title: Measurement Uncertainty in Conducted EMI Testing of Variable-Speed Drives: Contributions from LISN, Cable Routing, and Receiver Settings
SYN-PUB-03540.text:
Measurement Uncertainty in Conducted EMI Testing of Variable-Speed Drives: Contributions from LISN, Cable Routing, and Receiver Settings (2022, journal, Metrology and Measurement Systems).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283); Vera Knežević (R0320); Zoran Mihajlović (outside co-author); Radomir Bogdanović (R0344).
Keywords: measurement uncertainty; GUM; LISN; cable routing; CISPR 16.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-03541.title: EMC Considerations for Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Automation
SYN-PUB-03541.text:
EMC Considerations for Variable-Speed Drives in Industrial Automation (2023, book chapter, Industrial Power Electronics: Systems, Devices and Applications (Springer, edited volume)).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Dragan Vučković (outside co-author); Nataša Milošević (R0530); Tihomir Urošević (R0800).
Keywords: IEC 61800-3; PWM inverter; filter design; installation practice; industrial automation.
This book chapter provides a self-contained treatment of EMC requirements and mitigation strategies for variable-speed drive systems in industrial automation contexts. It covers the regulatory framework (IEC 61800-3, IEC 61000-6-2, and IEC 61000-6-4), the physical origins of conducted and radiated disturbances in PWM inverter drives, and practical filter and shielding design methods. Worked examples are based on measurement data from 2.2 kW to 55 kW drive systems. The chapter addresses installation variables including motor cable routing, grounding topology, and proximity to sensitive signal cables, with quantitative guidance on separation distances and screen termination. A section on SiC-based drives discusses how faster switching transitions alter both emission profiles and filter requirements relative to IGBT designs. The chapter is intended for practising engineers and postgraduate students with a background in power electronics.

SYN-PUB-03542.title: Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Ground Impedance Effects on Common-Mode Filter Performance in Drive Systems
SYN-PUB-03542.text:
Frequency-Domain Characterisation of Ground Impedance Effects on Common-Mode Filter Performance in Drive Systems (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Ana Mamužić (R0283); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Ana Horvat (outside co-author); Marco Trentini (outside co-author); Predrag Stanojević (outside co-author); Dimitrije Puzović (R0343).
Keywords: protective earth impedance; CM filter; Y-capacitor; field installation; insertion loss variability.
The attenuation provided by Y-capacitors in common-mode EMC filters depends on the impedance of the protective earth (PE) connection, which varies substantially between industrial installations. This paper characterises PE impedance at 47 industrial sites across northern Serbia using a vector network analyser, finding that impedance magnitude at 1 MHz ranges from 0.4 Ω to 18 Ω and exhibits significant inductive character above 500 kHz. The measured impedance profiles are used as input to a circuit simulation of a 15 kW drive with a three-stage CM filter, evaluating worst-case degradation in CM insertion loss. CM attenuation at 1 MHz degraded by up to 9 dB between the best and worst PE cases, rendering a filter that passed IEC 61800-3 Category C2 under laboratory conditions non-compliant in 14% of simulated field conditions. A modified filter topology using a split CM choke with partial differential-mode rejection reduces this variability to within ±2 dB.

SYN-PUB-03543.title: Active Common-Mode Voltage Reduction in SiC Inverter Drives Using Predictive PWM with Reduced Switching Vectors
SYN-PUB-03543.text:
Active Common-Mode Voltage Reduction in SiC Inverter Drives Using Predictive PWM with Reduced Switching Vectors (2026, preprint, arXiv (eess.SP)).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thomas Berger (outside co-author); Ana Mamužić (R0283).
Keywords: common-mode voltage; SiC inverter; PWM strategy; zero vector elimination; bearing currents.
Common-mode voltage (CMV) generated by three-phase two-level inverters reaches peak values of Vdc/2 per switching event and is the primary driver of CM conducted emissions and bearing current damage in motor drives. This preprint evaluates a PWM strategy that restricts the active switching vector set to eliminate zero vectors, thereby reducing the peak CMV from Vdc/2 to Vdc/6 with no additional hardware. Implemented on a 7.5 kW SiC inverter drive, the strategy reduced CM conducted emission peaks in the 150–500 kHz band by 8–14 dB compared to standard space-vector PWM at equal fundamental output quality. Total harmonic distortion of the output phase voltage increased from 2.1% to 3.8%, remaining within acceptable limits. CM choke size in a co-designed filter was reduced by 35% for equivalent IEC 61800-3 Category C2 compliance. Thermal measurements confirm no significant change in switch loss distribution.

SYN-PUB-03561.title: A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments
SYN-PUB-03561.text:
A Lightweight Authenticated Bootloader Protocol for Wireless Sensor Nodes in Industrial SCADA Environments (2010, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Communication Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: authenticated bootloader; HMAC; IEEE 802.15.4; SCADA; firmware delivery.
This paper describes the design and evaluation of an authenticated bootloader protocol intended for 8-bit microcontroller-based sensor nodes communicating over IEEE 802.15.4 radio links in industrial SCADA deployments. The protocol uses HMAC-SHA256 for image authentication and a two-phase commit scheme to prevent partial writes during interrupted transmissions. Experimental evaluation was conducted on a testbed of 24 nodes deployed across a simulated substation environment, with artificial packet-loss rates ranging from 5% to 40%. Mean firmware delivery time for a 64 KB image increased from 38 seconds under ideal conditions to 147 seconds at 40% packet loss, while no corrupted images were accepted across 2 400 delivery trials. Code size overhead on the target MCU was 3.2 KB of flash. The paper also discusses replay-attack resistance and the limitations of symmetric key management at scale, proposing a zone-based key hierarchy as a practical mitigation for deployments with up to 500 nodes.

SYN-PUB-03562.title: Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links
SYN-PUB-03562.text:
Delta Patching for Constrained Devices: Reducing Over-the-Air Update Payload on Low-Rate Wireless Links (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Embedded Systems and Industrial Networks (WESIN)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: delta patching; bsdiff; VCDIFF; firmware update; constrained devices.
Firmware images for constrained devices rarely change more than a few percent between successive releases, yet most over-the-air update mechanisms transmit full images. This paper evaluates three binary delta algorithms — bsdiff, VCDIFF, and a purpose-built block-aligned differencer — applied to firmware images from four representative industrial sensor product lines. Patch sizes across 38 consecutive release pairs averaged 11.4% of full image size for bsdiff and 14.7% for the block-aligned approach, with the latter requiring 40% less RAM during reconstruction. Transmission time over a simulated 1.2 kbit/s channel, representative of 868 MHz narrowband industrial radio, was reduced from an average of 4.1 minutes to 28 seconds. Reconstruction failure rates under 10% artificial bit-error conditions were below 0.3% for all schemes when combined with a 16-bit CRC per block. The paper includes a complexity analysis and discusses applicability to devices with less than 8 KB of available RAM.

SYN-PUB-03563.title: Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела
SYN-PUB-03563.text:
Формална верификација протокола за испоруку фирмвера методом провере модела (2013, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Нeнад Ћирић (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: формална верификација; SPIN; Promelamodel checking; firmware protocol; LTL.
У овом раду примењен је алат за проверу модела SPIN на протокол за аутентификовану испоруку фирмвера у бежичним телеметријским мрежама. Протокол је моделован у Прометеловом језику, а верификација је обухватила 14 безбедносних и животних особина формулисаних у линеарној темпоралној логици. Пронађена су три услова у којима поновна репродукција старе поруке може да доведе до инсталације претходне верзије фирмвера ако је монотони бројач секвенце нулиран након ресетовања уређаја. Предложено је проширење протокола са тrajnim бројачем у заштићеном нелетљивом меморијском простору. Исправљени протокол је верификован без кршења постављених особина у простору стања са до 2,1 × 10⁸ стања. Рад такође дискутује ограничења апстракције криптографских примитива у SPIN моделу и предлаже методологију за раздвојено моделовање протоколне логике и криптографских претпоставки.

SYN-PUB-03564.title: Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study
SYN-PUB-03564.text:
Key Distribution Schemes for Large-Scale Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comparative Study (2015, journal, International Journal of Industrial Communication and Control Systems).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Momčilo Nedeljković (R0441); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Tijana Marković (outside co-author); Dragan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: key distribution; wireless sensor networks; industrial security; Blom scheme; 6LoWPAN.
Managing cryptographic keys across hundreds of constrained field devices is a practical bottleneck in industrial wireless deployments. This paper systematically compares five key distribution schemes — pre-shared master key, pairwise key pre-distribution, a Blom matrix scheme, a hierarchical certificate authority approach adapted for 6LoWPAN, and an elliptic-curve Diffie–Hellman bootstrapping protocol — across three criteria: memory footprint on a Cortex-M0 class device, time to complete key establishment after node power-on, and resilience to node capture. Measurements were taken on a physical testbed of 60 nodes. The Blom scheme achieved the best balance for networks under 200 nodes, requiring 1.8 KB RAM and completing key establishment in under 400 ms. The ECC bootstrapping protocol was the only scheme providing forward secrecy but demanded 14 KB RAM and 2.3 seconds for key exchange, making it unsuitable for the lowest-tier devices. Practical recommendations are derived for three deployment tiers based on device capability.

SYN-PUB-03565.title: Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site
SYN-PUB-03565.text:
Firmware Delivery Reliability Over LoRa at Sub-kbit/s Data Rates: Measurement Study in an Urban Industrial Site (2017, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (ISIEA-EU)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Tibor Pásztor (R0590).
Keywords: LoRa; LoRaWAN; firmware OTA; spreading factor; industrial site measurement.
LoRa physical layer spreading factors SF7 through SF12 offer data rates from roughly 250 bit/s to 5.5 kbit/s at the expense of airtime, a constraint with direct implications for over-the-air firmware update feasibility. This paper reports on measurements conducted at a chemical plant in Novi Sad over six weeks using a network of 18 end-devices at distances between 80 m and 1.4 km from a single gateway. Packet delivery ratio at SF12 averaged 91.3% under normal plant operation but dropped to 73.8% during periods of heavy crane and conveyor activity. A store-and-forward segmentation protocol with per-segment HMAC authentication was deployed, and mean time to complete a 32 KB firmware update was measured at 22 minutes at SF12. The paper proposes an adaptive spreading-factor selection policy that reduced average update time to 9.4 minutes while maintaining delivery success above 97% across all trials.

SYN-PUB-03567.title: Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-03567.text:
Integrity Verification of Incremental Firmware Patches Using Merkle Hash Trees on Cortex-M Microcontrollers (2019, journal, Microprocessors and Microsystems: Embedded Hardware Design).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author).
Keywords: Merkle tree; firmware patch; ECDSA; integrity verification; Cortex-M.
Applying binary patches to firmware in the field requires verification mechanisms that can detect partial or corrupted patch delivery without storing the complete expected image. This paper proposes a Merkle hash tree construction adapted for delta patches, where leaf nodes correspond to fixed-size patch chunks and the root hash is authenticated by an ECDSA signature over NIST P-256. The scheme was implemented on an STM32L4 series microcontroller with 64 KB RAM. Hash tree construction over a 16 KB patch (32 leaves) required 210 ms and consumed a peak of 4.1 KB stack space. Verification of a partial delivery — detecting one corrupted chunk among 32 — required fewer than 50 ms. The paper compares this approach against full-image HMAC and rolling-hash alternatives in terms of detection granularity, storage requirements, and recovery strategy. A discussion of the tradeoffs in choosing tree depth is included, with measurements at depths 3, 4, and 5.

SYN-PUB-03568.title: Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model
SYN-PUB-03568.text:
Effect of Duty-Cycle Restrictions on OTA Firmware Update Latency in the 868 MHz ISM Band: An Analytical Model (2020, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: duty cycle; 868 MHz ISM; LoRaWAN; firmware update latency; queuing model.
Regulatory duty-cycle limits in the European 868 MHz ISM band constrain transmission time to 1% in sub-band 1, directly affecting over-the-air firmware update completion times for LPWAN devices. This paper develops a queuing-theory-based analytical model for firmware delivery latency under duty-cycle constraints, accounting for segmentation overhead, retransmission probability, and concurrent traffic from non-update messages. The model is parameterised using empirical measurements from a 30-node LoRaWAN testbed. Analytical predictions of mean delivery time matched measurements within 8% across all tested configurations. The model predicts that for a 64 KB image at SF10, mean delivery time under 1% duty cycle is 4.7 hours in a lightly loaded network and rises to over 18 hours under moderate concurrent telemetry load. A scheduling strategy that prioritises update segments during predicted low-traffic windows is described and shown analytically to reduce mean delivery time by 31%.

SYN-PUB-03569.title: Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee
SYN-PUB-03569.text:
Secure Multicast Firmware Delivery for Co-Located Industrial Sensor Clusters Over Zigbee (2021, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Wireless Sensor Systems and IoT Security (ECWSSIS)).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author).
Keywords: Zigbee; multicast firmware; AES-CCM; industrial IoT; group key management.
When many co-located devices require the same firmware update simultaneously, unicast delivery multiplies airtime linearly with node count. This paper describes a secure multicast delivery scheme for Zigbee-based industrial sensor clusters, using AES-128 CCM* group encryption with individual per-device session key wrapping to prevent one node from decrypting another's update confirmation. The protocol was implemented on CC2530-based nodes and evaluated in a testbed of 8 and 16 node clusters. For a 48 KB image, multicast delivery to a 16-node cluster completed in 6.8 minutes versus 41.3 minutes for sequential unicast, a factor of 6.1 improvement. Delivery success rate was 98.7% at 16 nodes under representative packet loss of 8%. The paper analyses the key management overhead introduced by per-device key wrapping and discusses the session key refresh interval as a function of assumed node compromise rate.

SYN-PUB-03570.title: Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity
SYN-PUB-03570.text:
Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: X.509; offline certificate validation; firmware authentication; constrained devices; public key infrastructure.
Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

SYN-PUB-03571.title: Протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке фирмвера у вишестепеним телеметријским мрежама
SYN-PUB-03571.text:
Протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке фирмвера у вишестепеним телеметријским мрежама (2023, conference, Зборник радова Телекомуникациони форум ТЕЛФОР).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Stefan Bogdanov (outside co-author); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: ланац испоруке фирмвера; вишестепене мреже; потписивање сегмената; LPWAN; индустријска безбедност.
У вишестепеним индустријским мрежама фирмвер може проћи кроз неколико посредничких чворова — концентратора и гетвеја — пре него што стигне до крајњег уређаја. Свaki посреднички чвор представља потенцијалну тачку манипулације. Овај рад предлаже протокол за верификацију ланца испоруке у коме сваки посреднички чвор потписује потврду о пријему и прослеђивању фирмверског сегмента, формирајући верификабилни низ потврда. Коначни уређај верификује цео ланац пре инсталације. Протокол је анализиран у моделу са до четири посреднička нивоа. Поред безбедносне анализе, рад мери додатно кашњење које уносе операције потписивања на различитим класама чворова: 28 ms по потпису на концентратору са Cortex-M4 процесором наспрам 190 ms на Cortex-M0+ чвору. Предложена је хибридна шема у којој само концентраtори потписују ланац, а крajnji уређаји верификују само коренски потпис произвођача, чиме се кашњење своди на прихватљив ниво.

SYN-PUB-03572.title: Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices
SYN-PUB-03572.text:
Benchmarking Post-Quantum Signature Schemes for Firmware Authentication on Class 1 IoT Devices (2024, journal, Journal of Cryptographic Engineering).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Nándor Takács (outside co-author).
Keywords: post-quantum cryptography; Dilithium; Falcon; SPHINCS+; firmware authentication; IoT benchmarking.
Anticipated deployment lifetimes of industrial sensor nodes of 10–20 years motivate evaluation of post-quantum signature algorithms for firmware authentication on severely constrained hardware. This paper benchmarks four NIST post-quantum signature candidates — CRYSTALS-Dilithium2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and a lattice-based scheme submitted to the ongoing standardisation process — on two representative Class 1 IoT platforms: an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 48 MHz with 32 KB RAM and a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz with 256 KB RAM. Metrics collected include signature verification time, public key and signature sizes, and peak RAM consumption. On the Cortex-M0+ platform, Falcon-512 verification completed in 480 ms consuming 28 KB RAM peak, which exceeds available memory, while SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s verified in 1 140 ms with 6.2 KB peak RAM, making it the only scheme feasible on the lower-end device. Dilithium2 was feasible on the Cortex-M4 at 94 ms. The paper discusses the practical tradeoffs for protocol designers choosing between these schemes given device capability distribution in a deployment.

SYN-PUB-03573.title: Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments
SYN-PUB-03573.text:
Adaptive Segmentation and Retransmission Scheduling for Firmware Delivery Over NB-IoT in Deep-Indoor Industrial Environments (2025, journal, Transactions on Industrial Wireless Communications and Networking).
Authors: Ана Рајић (R0286); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Petar Vujanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT; adaptive segmentation; firmware delivery; deep indoor; CQI.
NB-IoT deployment in basement-level and shielded industrial environments produces highly variable signal conditions, with RSRP measurements in one monitored processing facility ranging from −85 dBm to −138 dBm across 22 fixed sensor positions. This paper describes an adaptive firmware delivery protocol that adjusts segment size and retransmission window based on real-time channel quality indicator reports available in the NB-IoT stack. Segment sizes were varied between 64 and 512 bytes; the adaptive scheme selected optimal sizes per device per update session. In a 22-device testbed deployment over four months, the adaptive protocol reduced total update time by 38% compared to a fixed 128-byte segment baseline and reduced the number of incomplete update sessions from 11.4% to 2.1%. Energy consumption per completed update was also measured on battery-powered nodes, with the adaptive scheme consuming 12% less energy due to fewer retransmissions. A lightweight predictor using a 5-point CQI moving average was sufficient to achieve near-optimal segment sizing.

SYN-PUB-03632.title: Sensitivity of deep-knowledge-tracing variants to hyperparameter choices: a systematic benchmarking on three open educational datasets
SYN-PUB-03632.text:
Sensitivity of deep-knowledge-tracing variants to hyperparameter choices: a systematic benchmarking on three open educational datasets (2023, journal, Transactions on Learning Technologies).
Authors: Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Anita Schulze (outside co-author); Zlata Ristić (R0291); Emilija Zec (R0322); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: deep knowledge tracing; benchmarking; hyperparameter sensitivity; hidden Markov; educational data mining.
Deep knowledge tracing (DKT) and two extensions—DKT+ with forgetting regularisation and DKVMN with memory-augmented networks—were systematically benchmarked across three publicly released educational interaction datasets representing algebra tutoring (N ≈ 300,000 events), geometry tutoring (N ≈ 70,000 events), and a reading skills platform (N ≈ 45,000 events). A grid search over 216 hyperparameter combinations per model variant examined hidden-unit counts (32–256), dropout rates (0–0.5), learning-rate schedules, and sequence-length truncation thresholds. AUC for next-item prediction ranged from 0.71 to 0.79 across conditions; variance attributable to hyperparameter choice exceeded variance attributable to model variant for two of three datasets. A comparison with a well-tuned four-state hidden Markov baseline showed that HMM matched DKT AUC within 0.02 on the reading dataset while requiring 40-fold less computation. Recommendations for reproducible DKT evaluation are provided.

SYN-PUB-03633.title: Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus
SYN-PUB-03633.text:
Morphological Disambiguation in Serbian: A Maximum Entropy Approach on a Balanced News Corpus (2011, conference, Proceedings of the South Slavic Language Technology Workshop (SoLaT 2011), Ljubljana).
Authors: Aleksandar Vučković (outside co-author); Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Miroslava Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: morphological disambiguation; Serbian; maximum entropy; corpus annotation; MULTEXT-East.
This paper describes the construction and annotation of a 200,000-token Serbian newspaper corpus and the training of a maximum entropy morphological disambiguator on it. Serbian presents particular challenges for disambiguation due to its free word order, extensive inflectional paradigms, and syncretism across several case forms. The corpus was sampled from three regional dailies covering the period 2005–2009 and annotated manually by two linguists following an adapted MULTEXT-East tagset. Inter-annotator agreement reached κ = 0.87 on the full tagset. The maximum entropy model trained on 80% of the data achieved a per-token accuracy of 91.3% on the held-out test set, outperforming a rule-based baseline by 4.1 percentage points. Error analysis showed that the remaining errors cluster heavily around nominal case syncretism in neuter nouns and verbal aspect ambiguity. The annotated corpus and tagger are made available under a Creative Commons licence.

SYN-PUB-03634.title: Annotation Consistency in Dependency Treebanks: A Case Study on Serbian and Croatian Parallel Texts
SYN-PUB-03634.text:
Annotation Consistency in Dependency Treebanks: A Case Study on Serbian and Croatian Parallel Texts (2013, journal, Journal of Slavic Language Resources).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Tomislav Gregurić (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović Đurđević (outside co-author); Péter Halász (outside co-author).
Keywords: dependency treebank; annotation consistency; Serbian; Croatian; inter-annotator agreement.
Consistent syntactic annotation across closely related language varieties is essential for cross-lingual experiments, yet disagreements between annotation teams are common even when shared guidelines are nominally in use. This study examines annotation consistency in a 50,000-token parallel Serbian–Croatian dependency treebank constructed as part of a bilateral research effort. Five annotators from two institutions independently labelled a common 5,000-token subset, and discrepancies were systematically catalogued and attributed to guideline ambiguity, language-variety differences, or genuine annotator uncertainty. We propose a set of revision criteria for eleven frequently disputed dependency relation categories and demonstrate that applying them retrospectively raises the macro-averaged labelled attachment score (LAS) agreement from 76.4% to 83.1% across the full annotator set. The revised guidelines and the reconciled treebank subset are released alongside the paper. Findings are relevant to any team maintaining parallel treebanks for closely related South Slavic varieties.

SYN-PUB-03635.title: Transferring POS Taggers Across the Slavic–Finno-Ugric Boundary: Experiments with Serbian and Hungarian
SYN-PUB-03635.text:
Transferring POS Taggers Across the Slavic–Finno-Ugric Boundary: Experiments with Serbian and Hungarian (2015, journal, Computational Linguistics and Language Technology (CLaLT), Vol. 8).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Réka Borbély (outside co-author); Đorđe Bošković (R1031); Aleksandar Vučković (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-lingual transfer; POS tagging; Serbian; Hungarian; morphologically rich languages.
This paper investigates how much morphological tagging accuracy can be retained when a tagger trained on Serbian is transferred—without any target-language labelled data—to Hungarian, and vice versa. Despite the typological distance between a South Slavic language and a Finno-Ugric agglutinative language, both exhibit rich morphology, which motivates the comparison. We map the MULTEXT-East tagsets of the two languages onto a reduced shared feature schema covering part of speech, number, and case, then apply three transfer strategies: direct model transfer, feature projection via word alignments, and self-training with a small unlabelled Hungarian/Serbian target corpus. Using Serbian SETimes-derived text and a Hungarian news corpus of comparable size (circa 180,000 tokens each), we find that self-training with 20,000 unlabelled target tokens recovers roughly 60% of the performance gap relative to a fully supervised target-language model. Results suggest shared morphological feature spaces are an effective bridge even across unrelated families.

SYN-PUB-03637.title: Zero-Shot Dependency Parsing of Bosnian Using a Serbian Transition-Based Parser
SYN-PUB-03637.text:
Zero-Shot Dependency Parsing of Bosnian Using a Serbian Transition-Based Parser (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 11th Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation for Slavic Languages (LRESL-11), Brno).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Elvir Huseinović (outside co-author); Nikola Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: dependency parsing; Bosnian; Serbian; Universal Dependencies; zero-shot transfer.
Bosnian and Serbian share the majority of their grammar and lexicon, yet separate standardisation efforts mean that available NLP models almost never target Bosnian explicitly. This paper evaluates whether a transition-based dependency parser trained exclusively on a 90,000-token Serbian treebank can parse Bosnian texts without any adaptation. We test on a newly constructed 8,000-token Bosnian web-text gold standard annotated in Universal Dependencies (UD) format. Unlabelled attachment score (UAS) reaches 81.7% and LAS 74.2%, which we compare against two multilingual baselines (mBERT fine-tuned on Serbian UD data, and a delexicalised cross-lingual parser). We also report results for a shallow domain-adaptation step that replaces Bosnian-specific orthographic conventions and select lexical items, which raises LAS by 2.4 points. The work argues for treating Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian as a resource-sharing cluster within UD rather than as fully independent treebank targets.

SYN-PUB-03638.title: Evaluating Multilingual BERT Representations for Serbian Morphosyntactic Tagging Across Domains
SYN-PUB-03638.text:
Evaluating Multilingual BERT Representations for Serbian Morphosyntactic Tagging Across Domains (2020, journal, Journal of Computational and Quantitative Linguistics in Eastern Europe (CQLEE), Vol. 4, No. 2).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Marija Blagojević (outside co-author); Luca Venturi (outside co-author).
Keywords: mBERT; XLM-RoBERTa; Serbian; morphosyntactic tagging; domain adaptation.
Contextualised word representations from multilingual pretrained transformers have shown strong performance on many NLP tasks, but their behaviour on morphologically complex languages with limited training data in the pretraining corpus is not well understood. We fine-tune multilingual BERT (mBERT) and XLM-RoBERTa on Serbian morphosyntactic tagging across four domains: news, parliamentary proceedings, social media, and legal text, using gold-standard data sets totalling approximately 130,000 tokens. Results show that mBERT fine-tuned on news data drops from 94.1% accuracy on in-domain test data to 87.6% on social media text, with the largest error categories being unknown tokenisation units and non-standard inflected forms. XLM-RoBERTa is more robust across domains, with a 3.2-point smaller drop on social media. We also test both models on a 15,000-token Pannonian Rusyn test set as an extreme low-resource condition and observe that XLM-RoBERTa achieves 71.3% even without any Rusyn fine-tuning data, apparently through transfer from Serbian and Ukrainian subword overlap.

SYN-PUB-03639.title: Annotation of Aspect and Actionality in Serbian Verbal Predicates: Guidelines and a Pilot Corpus
SYN-PUB-03639.text:
Annotation of Aspect and Actionality in Serbian Verbal Predicates: Guidelines and a Pilot Corpus (2021, journal, Slavic Corpus Linguistics Review, Vol. 9, No. 1).
Authors: Tijana Ašić (outside co-author); Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Miroslava Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: verbal aspect; actionality; Aktionsart; Serbian; corpus annotation.
Grammatical aspect in Serbian interacts with lexical actionality (Aktionsart) in ways that create persistent disagreements among annotators and inconsistencies across existing resources. This paper presents a detailed annotation scheme for aspect-actionality combinations in Serbian verbal predicates, developed iteratively over eighteen months through repeated annotation cycles on a pilot corpus of 25,000 tokens drawn from fiction and journalistic prose. The scheme distinguishes five aspectual classes and four primary actionality types, with explicit rules for handling borderline prefixation patterns that shift a verb from imperfective to perfective without clear lexical change. Inter-annotator agreement after guideline stabilisation reached κ = 0.81 for aspect and κ = 0.74 for actionality. We report a frequency distribution of the resulting cross-classifications and show that approximately 12% of verb tokens in our pilot corpus are genuinely ambiguous under context, requiring discourse-level cues for resolution. The annotated pilot corpus and guidelines are released publicly.

SYN-PUB-03640.title: Cross-Lingual Propagation of Named Entity Annotations from Serbian to Macedonian via Bilingual Lexicons
SYN-PUB-03640.text:
Cross-Lingual Propagation of Named Entity Annotations from Serbian to Macedonian via Bilingual Lexicons (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan and South Slavic NLP Symposium (BalNLP 2022), Skopje).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Sonja Gelevska (outside co-author); Marija Blagojević (outside co-author); Ivan Obradović (outside co-author).
Keywords: named entity recognition; Macedonian; cross-lingual projection; low-resource NLP; annotation transfer.
Named entity recognition (NER) for Macedonian is severely constrained by the lack of annotated training data. This paper investigates whether named entity labels from a 95,000-token Serbian NER corpus can be projected onto a parallel Macedonian corpus through automatic word alignment combined with bilingual lexicon filtering, producing usable silver-standard training data. We compare three projection strategies and train a BiLSTM-CRF model on the resulting Macedonian silver data, evaluating on a 3,000-token manually annotated Macedonian gold test set. The best projection strategy yields an F1 of 68.4% for the three-class scheme (PER, ORG, LOC), compared to 51.3% for a naive direct-transfer baseline. We further show that adding 2,000 manually corrected tokens to the silver training set pushes F1 to 76.1%, pointing to a cost-effective data-creation strategy. Macedonian gold test data are released through the CLARIN infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-03641.title: A Morphological Lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn: Construction, Coverage, and Integration into an NLP Pipeline
SYN-PUB-03641.text:
A Morphological Lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn: Construction, Coverage, and Integration into an NLP Pipeline (2023, journal, Language Documentation and Computational Resources, Vol. 2, No. 1).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Mikola Ramač (outside co-author); Kristína Uhrinová (outside co-author).
Keywords: Pannonian Rusyn; morphological lexicon; finite-state transducer; minority language NLP; Vojvodina.
Pannonian Rusyn is a regional language spoken by approximately 15,000 people in Vojvodina, Serbia, and parts of Croatia. It has received almost no computational treatment despite holding official minority language status in Serbia. This paper describes the construction of a morphological lexicon for Pannonian Rusyn containing 28,400 lemmas with full inflection tables generated by a hand-crafted finite-state transducer. Lexicon coverage was evaluated against a 40,000-token web-crawled corpus: the lexicon covers 84.6% of tokens and 61.3% of types, with the largest coverage gap in recent borrowings from Serbian and English. We integrate the lexicon into a simple morphological analysis pipeline and report tagging accuracy of 78.9% on a 2,500-token gold standard. Challenges specific to the language include dialectal spelling variation across the Bačka and Srem sub-varieties and the absence of a stable computational orthography standard. The lexicon is deposited at CLARIN ERIC and licensed under CC BY 4.0.

SYN-PUB-03642.title: Sentence Boundary Detection in Historical Serbian Church-Slavonic Texts: Rule-Based and Statistical Approaches Compared
SYN-PUB-03642.text:
Sentence Boundary Detection in Historical Serbian Church-Slavonic Texts: Rule-Based and Statistical Approaches Compared (2024, journal, Digital Humanities and Historical Linguistics Quarterly, Vol. 6, No. 3).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Bojana Milosavljević (outside co-author); Viorica Enăchescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: sentence boundary detection; Church-Slavonic; historical corpus; OCR post-processing; CRF.
Historical digitisation projects increasingly produce raw OCR output from Serbian Church-Slavonic manuscripts, but standard sentence segmentation tools trained on modern text fail on these materials due to inconsistent punctuation, abbreviation conventions, and interlinear glosses. This paper evaluates three segmentation strategies on a 60,000-character corpus of digitised 18th-century ecclesiastical texts: a rule-based approach built on paleographic knowledge, a CRF model trained on 8,000 manually segmented characters, and a fine-tuned multilingual sentence segmenter. The CRF model achieves the best balance of precision (91.2%) and recall (88.7%), while the rule-based system has higher precision (94.1%) but lower recall (81.3%). We also quantify the downstream effect of segmentation errors on a subsequent keyword-in-context (KWIC) retrieval task, finding that even a 5% boundary error rate reduces KWIC precision by roughly 9 percentage points. The annotated subset and CRF model are shared via the project repository.

SYN-PUB-03643.title: Benchmarking Low-Resource Multilingual Transformers on Four Vojvodina Minority Languages
SYN-PUB-03643.text:
Benchmarking Low-Resource Multilingual Transformers on Four Vojvodina Minority Languages (2025, journal, Transactions on Multilingual Language Processing, Vol. 3).
Authors: Marija Blagojević (outside co-author); Réka Borbély (outside co-author); Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Ján Kvašňák (outside co-author); Andrei Costescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: multilingual transformers; low-resource languages; Vojvodina; benchmark; minority languages.
Vojvodina hosts several small language communities—Hungarian, Slovak, Rusyn, and Romanian—each with official status but minimal NLP resources. This paper constructs a unified benchmark covering three tasks (morphosyntactic tagging, named entity recognition, and sentence-level sentiment classification) for all four languages, using data sets of 10,000–18,000 tokens per language assembled from local newspaper archives and social media under appropriate licences. We evaluate five multilingual transformer models (mBERT, XLM-R base, XLM-R large, a Slavic-focused model, and a model pre-trained on Hungarian) under three data regimes: zero-shot, 500-example few-shot, and full fine-tuning. Results confirm that language family proximity to high-resource languages in the pre-training data is a stronger predictor of zero-shot performance than script similarity. Hungarian achieves the highest zero-shot scores benefiting from the Hungarian-focused model; Rusyn consistently scores lowest across all models and tasks. The benchmark data, evaluation scripts, and all fine-tuned model checkpoints are released publicly.

SYN-PUB-03644.title: Towards a Unified Annotation Scheme for Information Structure in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian Treebanks
SYN-PUB-03644.text:
Towards a Unified Annotation Scheme for Information Structure in Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian Treebanks (2026, preprint, arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.XXXXX).
Authors: Đurđica Kuzmanović (R0292); Tomislav Gregurić (outside co-author); Elvir Huseinović (outside co-author).
Keywords: information structure; Universal Dependencies; topic-focus; South Slavic; annotation scheme.
Information structure—the encoding of topic, focus, and contrast in discourse—is systematically marked in South Slavic languages through word order variation, prosodic prominence, and particle placement, yet no shared annotation scheme currently covers Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian simultaneously. This paper proposes such a scheme, derived from a comparative analysis of 120 ambiguous sentences drawn from parallel news texts in all three varieties. The scheme distinguishes topic span, narrow focus, broad focus, and contrastive topic using a two-tier annotation model compatible with the Universal Dependencies extended relation framework. We report pilot annotation statistics on a 6,000-token shared sample involving annotators from three institutions and discuss the main sources of disagreement, particularly around verum focus and the annotation of cleft-like constructions. A revised annotation manual and the pilot sample are submitted to the UD repository as a discussion document for community feedback.

SYN-PUB-03815.title: Analytical Springback Prediction for Air Bending of Mild Steel Sheets Under Plane-Strain Conditions
SYN-PUB-03815.text:
Analytical Springback Prediction for Air Bending of Mild Steel Sheets Under Plane-Strain Conditions (2010, journal, Journal of Production and Manufacturing Research).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Miroslav Zečević (outside co-author); Valentina Simić (R0445); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: springback; air bending; analytical model; mild steel; bilinear hardening.
This paper presents a closed-form model for springback angle in air bending of mild steel sheets, derived from beam-bending theory with a bilinear elastoplastic material description. Experiments were conducted on a hydraulic press-brake using DC04 mild steel strips of 1.0 mm and 1.5 mm thickness, at punch radii between 2 mm and 8 mm and bending angles from 30° to 150°. The model accounts for neutral-axis shift as a function of punch radius-to-thickness ratio. Predicted springback angles were compared with 120 measured specimens; the mean absolute error was 0.41° across all configurations. A sensitivity study showed that uncertainty in yield stress (±5%) contributed more to prediction error than uncertainty in sheet thickness (±0.05 mm). The model is computationally inexpensive and was implemented in a spreadsheet tool used in the undergraduate laboratory course. Results confirm that the bilinear description is adequate for mild steel but becomes less accurate for bending angles above 130°, where a power-law hardening correction is recommended.

SYN-PUB-03816.title: Influence of Bauschinger Effect on Springback in Repeated-Bending Operations: An Experimental Study
SYN-PUB-03816.text:
Influence of Bauschinger Effect on Springback in Repeated-Bending Operations: An Experimental Study (2012, journal, International Journal of Sheet Metal Technology).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Miroslav Zečević (outside co-author); Tomáš Návrat (outside co-author).
Keywords: Bauschinger effect; cyclic hardening; Chaboche model; DP600; FEM.
Repeated bending-straightening cycles are common in coil-fed press-brake lines and introduce the Bauschinger effect, which reduces the apparent yield stress on load reversal and modifies springback behaviour. This study characterises the Bauschinger effect in three structural steels—S235, S355, and DP600—using cyclic tension-compression tests on flat specimens machined to avoid buckling. The isotropic-kinematic hardening parameters of the Chaboche model were fitted to the cyclic test data. Air-bending experiments with pre-deformed blanks (one to three prior reverse-bending cycles) were then performed on a 40-tonne CNC press-brake. FEM simulations in ABAQUS using the fitted Chaboche parameters reduced springback prediction error from 2.1° (isotropic hardening only) to 0.6° (mixed hardening) for DP600 at a 90° target angle. Practical implications for setting backstop offsets in multi-step bending sequences are discussed. The dataset of 216 cyclic test curves and 144 bending experiments is included as supplementary material.

SYN-PUB-03817.title: FEM-Based Process Window for Springback-Controlled Bending of DP780 Advanced High-Strength Steel
SYN-PUB-03817.text:
FEM-Based Process Window for Springback-Controlled Bending of DP780 Advanced High-Strength Steel (2014, conference, Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Sheet Metal Forming – SheetMet).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Nemanja Radović (outside co-author); Péter Varga (outside co-author); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: DP780; FEM; response surface; process window; CNC press-brake.
Advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) of the dual-phase family are increasingly used in automotive structural parts, but their high yield-to-tensile ratio makes springback prediction and compensation challenging. This paper maps a process window for air bending of DP780 sheets (1.2 mm and 1.5 mm gauges) by running a full-factorial FEM study in PAM-STAMP covering five punch radii (2–10 mm), seven target bending angles (60°–150°), and three friction coefficients (0.05–0.15). In total, 210 simulations were evaluated. Springback angle ranged from 2.3° to 14.8° across the studied parameter space. A response-surface model (second-order polynomial) was fitted to the simulation results with an adjusted R² of 0.971 and validated against 48 physical press-brake experiments, yielding a mean absolute error of 0.72°. The fitted response surface was encoded as a look-up correction table suitable for integration into CNC press-brake controllers. Limits of the approach when material batch variability exceeds ±3% in yield stress are quantified.

SYN-PUB-03818.title: Thickness Strain Distribution in V-Die Bending: Comparison of Hill'48 and Barlat'89 Yield Criteria in FEM Simulations
SYN-PUB-03818.text:
Thickness Strain Distribution in V-Die Bending: Comparison of Hill'48 and Barlat'89 Yield Criteria in FEM Simulations (2015, journal, European Journal of Forming Technology).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Valentina Simić (R0445); Stefan Vuković (R0568); Nemanja Radović (outside co-author); Massimo Tolazzi (outside co-author).
Keywords: yield criterion; Hill'48; Barlat'89; aluminium alloy; thickness strain.
Accurate thickness strain prediction matters for subsequent forming operations and for springback calculation in multi-step sequences. This study compares the Hill'48 and Barlat'89 anisotropic yield criteria in FEM models of V-die bending for three aluminium alloys (AA5754-O, AA6016-T4, AA7075-T6) at 1.0 mm thickness. Lankford r-values and yield loci were determined from uniaxial and biaxial tensile tests. ABAQUS simulations using each yield criterion were run for 45°, 90°, and 135° bending angles at two die widths. Through-thickness strain profiles were extracted and compared with measurements from cross-sectioned and etched specimens using optical microscopy. For AA5754-O, both criteria performed similarly (error < 4%). For AA7075-T6, Barlat'89 reduced maximum thickness-strain error from 9.2% to 3.8% relative to Hill'48. The paper quantifies when the added complexity of Barlat'89 calibration is justified. Springback angle predictions showed smaller sensitivity to criterion choice (< 0.5° difference), consistent with findings from other groups.

SYN-PUB-03819.title: Real-Time Springback Compensation on a CNC Press-Brake Using In-Process Angle Measurement
SYN-PUB-03819.text:
Real-Time Springback Compensation on a CNC Press-Brake Using In-Process Angle Measurement (2017, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Systems and Automation).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Slobodan Tabaković (outside co-author); Miroslav Zečević (outside co-author); Radovan Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: closed-loop control; springback compensation; in-process measurement; CNC press-brake; angle sensor.
This paper describes a closed-loop control scheme implemented on a retrofitted 63-tonne CNC hydraulic press-brake to achieve target bending angles despite springback variability. An optical angle sensor mounted in the die measures the instantaneous bend angle during the downstroke. A proportional-integral controller adjusts the punch penetration depth on the basis of the difference between the measured release angle and the target angle, iterating within a single stroke using incremental re-strikes. The control algorithm was tested on S355 (1.5 mm and 2.0 mm), DP600 (1.2 mm), and AA6016-T4 (1.5 mm) over 500 bending cycles per material grade. Angle accuracy after the closed-loop correction was ±0.3° (2σ) for all materials, compared with ±2.1° (2σ) without compensation. Cycle time increased by an average of 1.8 seconds per part due to re-strike iterations. The system requires no prior knowledge of material properties beyond a first-bend calibration stroke, making it practical for mixed-batch production. Failure modes related to sensor contamination and asymmetric die wear are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03821.title: Effect of Residual Stress from Laser Cutting on Springback in Subsequent Air Bending of S355 Blanks
SYN-PUB-03821.text:
Effect of Residual Stress from Laser Cutting on Springback in Subsequent Air Bending of S355 Blanks (2019, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd International ESAFORM Conference on Material Forming).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Nemanja Radović (outside co-author); Anita Kranjc (outside co-author).
Keywords: residual stress; laser cutting; springback; S355; X-ray diffraction.
Laser-cut blanks carry edge residual stresses that can alter springback behaviour relative to blanks produced by guillotine shearing. This study quantifies the effect by measuring residual stress distributions in S355 steel strips (2.0 mm, 3.0 mm thick) cut by fibre laser at three power/feed combinations using X-ray diffraction at multiple distances from the cut edge (0.1 mm to 10 mm). The stressed strips were subsequently bent at 45°, 90°, and 135° on a V-die press-brake, and springback angles were compared with those of shear-cut reference strips. Springback differences up to 0.9° were observed at 90° for the highest-energy laser setting and 2.0 mm thickness. FEM models incorporating the measured residual stress as an initial condition reproduced the observed differences within 0.25°. The practical conclusion is that, for part tolerances tighter than ±1°, the cutting method and laser parameters should be included in press-brake setup procedures.

SYN-PUB-03822.title: Reduced-Order FEM Surrogate for Springback Prediction in CNC Press-Brake Bending Using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
SYN-PUB-03822.text:
Reduced-Order FEM Surrogate for Springback Prediction in CNC Press-Brake Bending Using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (2021, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Processes).
Authors: Slobodan Tabaković (outside co-author); Andrei Mișcoi (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Radovan Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: surrogate model; POD; FEM; real-time control; springback.
