Full FEM simulations of bending operations are too slow for real-time use inside CNC controllers. This paper constructs a surrogate model using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) applied to a training set of 360 ABAQUS shell-element simulations of air bending across a five-dimensional parameter space: yield stress (200–700 MPa), hardening exponent (0.05–0.30), sheet thickness (0.8–3.0 mm), punch radius (2–12 mm), and target angle (45°–135°). The POD basis retains 99.5% of variance with eight modes. A radial-basis-function interpolant maps parameter vectors to POD coefficients. Springback angle predictions from the surrogate have a mean absolute error of 0.38° against a 60-simulation test set not used in training and execute in under 2 ms on standard industrial PC hardware. The surrogate was embedded in the press-brake controller developed in earlier work and tested with mixed batches of S235, S355, and DP600, maintaining ±0.4° accuracy. Limitations related to extrapolation outside the training domain are characterised.

SYN-PUB-03823.title: Uncertainty Quantification in FEM-Based Springback Prediction: Effect of Material Property Scatter in DP600 and DP780 Coils
SYN-PUB-03823.text:
Uncertainty Quantification in FEM-Based Springback Prediction: Effect of Material Property Scatter in DP600 and DP780 Coils (2022, journal, Journal of Materials Processing and Engineering).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Nemanja Radović (outside co-author); Péter Varga (outside co-author); Katja Brunner (outside co-author).
Keywords: uncertainty quantification; Monte Carlo; DP600; DP780; material variability.
Material properties of advanced high-strength steel coils vary between and within production batches, introducing uncertainty into deterministic springback predictions. This paper applies a Monte Carlo approach to quantify how yield stress, ultimate tensile strength, and normal anisotropy coefficient r—each described by measured statistical distributions drawn from 24 coils of DP600 and 18 coils of DP780 supplied by two European steel producers—propagate to uncertainty in predicted springback angle. Input distributions were characterised from 720 tensile tests. For each steel and three bending configurations (90°, t = 1.2 mm; 90°, t = 1.5 mm; 120°, t = 1.5 mm), 1000 ABAQUS simulations were run using Latin-hypercube-sampled property sets. The 95th-percentile spread in springback angle was 2.4° for DP600 and 3.7° for DP780, with yield stress contributing approximately 65% of the variance in both grades. Results are used to define tolerance bands for adaptive CNC controller targets, replacing single-point predictions with stochastic bounds.

SYN-PUB-03824.title: Characterisation of the Young's Modulus Degradation in Dual-Phase Steels and Its Influence on Springback
SYN-PUB-03824.text:
Characterisation of the Young's Modulus Degradation in Dual-Phase Steels and Its Influence on Springback (2023, journal, European Journal of Forming Technology).
Authors: Slobodan Tabaković (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Katja Brunner (outside co-author).
Keywords: elastic modulus degradation; dual-phase steel; springback; ABAQUS UMAT; tensile test.
The apparent elastic modulus of dual-phase steels decreases with accumulated plastic strain, a phenomenon sometimes called chord-modulus degradation or elastic modulus reduction. This degradation directly affects springback through the elastic-recovery term. The present work measures chord modulus as a function of pre-strain for DP600 and DP800 using loading-unloading tensile tests at seven pre-strain levels from 0% to 16%, with three specimens per level. Modulus values dropped from approximately 205 GPa at zero pre-strain to 178 GPa and 171 GPa at 16% for DP600 and DP800 respectively. A modified exponential degradation law is fitted and incorporated into both an analytical springback model and an ABAQUS user material subroutine. FEM predictions of springback at 90° air bending improved from a mean error of 1.8° with constant modulus to 0.6° with degraded modulus for DP800. The user subroutine is made available via the departmental repository.

SYN-PUB-03825.title: Press-Brake Bending of Aluminium-Lithium Alloy AA2198-T8 for Aerospace Structural Brackets: Springback and Cracking Limits
SYN-PUB-03825.text:
Press-Brake Bending of Aluminium-Lithium Alloy AA2198-T8 for Aerospace Structural Brackets: Springback and Cracking Limits (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Advances in Materials and Processing Technologies – AMPT).
Authors: Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Nemanja Radović (outside co-author); Luca Fratini (outside co-author); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: aluminium-lithium alloy; AA2198; springback; cracking; aerospace.
Aluminium-lithium alloys offer attractive stiffness-to-weight ratios for aerospace brackets but are prone to cracking at small bend radii and exhibit larger springback than conventional aluminium alloys. This study investigates air bending of AA2198-T8 sheet (1.6 mm) on a CNC press-brake, mapping the boundary between acceptable bends and edge cracking as a function of punch radius (2–8 mm) and bending direction relative to rolling direction (0°, 45°, 90°). Forming limit curves and anisotropy coefficients were measured; the minimum safe punch-radius-to-thickness ratio was found to be 2.8 for bends parallel to the rolling direction and 3.5 for transverse bends. Springback angles ranged from 5.2° to 11.4° across the studied parameter space, substantially higher than for AA6016-T4. ABAQUS FEM simulations using a Barlat'89 yield surface and damage indicator reproduced the cracking boundary within one punch-radius increment. Recommended CNC overbend angles for the safe process window are tabulated.

SYN-PUB-03826.title: Digital Twin Framework for an Instrumented Press-Brake: Synchronising FEM State Estimates with Live Sensor Data
SYN-PUB-03826.text:
Digital Twin Framework for an Instrumented Press-Brake: Synchronising FEM State Estimates with Live Sensor Data (2026, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Systems and Automation).
Authors: Slobodan Tabaković (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Radovan Petrović (outside co-author); Andrei Mișcoi (outside co-author); Katja Brunner (outside co-author).
Keywords: digital twin; Kalman filter; press-brake; reduced-order model; in-process identification.
This paper describes a prototype digital twin architecture for a CNC hydraulic press-brake in which a continuously updated FEM state estimate runs in parallel with the physical machine. The physical press-brake is instrumented with four load cells in the bed, a laser angle sensor, two linear encoders on the ram, and a thermocouple array for hydraulic-fluid temperature. Sensor readings at 100 Hz are streamed to a workstation running a reduced-order FEM model (constructed via POD as in prior work) whose material parameters are updated by an unscented Kalman filter using the punch force–displacement curve as the primary observable. The filter converges to within ±2% of tensile-test yield stress values after the first production stroke for S235, S355, and DP600. Springback angle predictions using the filter-updated model achieved 0.31° mean absolute error over a 200-part production run with intentionally mixed material batches. The architecture is described in sufficient detail for replication, and the filter code is released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-03827.title: A Weighted TOPSIS Approach for Supplier Selection in the Automotive Tier-2 Supply Chain: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region
SYN-PUB-03827.text:
A Weighted TOPSIS Approach for Supplier Selection in the Automotive Tier-2 Supply Chain: A Case Study from the Vojvodina Region (2022, journal, Journal of Industrial Engineering and Management (Novi Sad)).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Jovan Bogićević (R0308); Mihály Varga (outside co-author); Đorđe Novaković (R0331).
Keywords: TOPSIS; AHP; supplier selection; automotive supply chain; sensitivity analysis.
This paper applies a weighted Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) model to evaluate and rank a set of 14 candidate suppliers for a Vojvodina-based automotive component manufacturer. Seven criteria were defined through structured interviews with procurement managers, covering price, delivery reliability, quality rejection rate, financial stability, geographic proximity, environmental certification, and responsiveness. Criteria weights were elicited using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with input from five domain experts. The consistency ratio for all pairwise comparison matrices remained below 0.08. Sensitivity analysis was performed by varying the weight of the top two criteria by ±20%. Results show that the final supplier ranking is stable under moderate weight perturbations, with the top three suppliers retaining their positions across all tested scenarios. The paper discusses practical limitations of the model, including the difficulty of obtaining reliable financial data from smaller regional suppliers, and suggests a periodic re-evaluation protocol aligned with annual procurement cycles.

SYN-PUB-03829.title: Quantitative XRD phase analysis of PVD coating cross-sections after high-temperature oxidation and machining exposure
SYN-PUB-03829.text:
Quantitative XRD phase analysis of PVD coating cross-sections after high-temperature oxidation and machining exposure (2020, journal, Surface and Coatings Technology).
Authors: Jana Beranová (outside co-author); Danilo Grujić (R0377); Tamara Vukić (outside co-author); Marko Đurđević (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920); Jovan Bogićević (R0308).
Keywords: Rietveld refinement; XRD; TiAlN oxidation; CrAlN; phase analysis.
TiAlN, CrAlN and TiSiN coatings were subjected to two degradation routes: isothermal furnace oxidation (700 °C, 2 h in air) and actual turning exposure (AISI 4140, 45 HRC, 200 m/min, until VB = 0.3 mm). XRD patterns collected from coating cross-sections prepared by FIB milling were refined by the Rietveld method. After furnace oxidation, TiAlN showed 18 vol% rutile TiO₂ and 9 vol% α-Al₂O₃; CrAlN showed 6 vol% Cr₂O₃ and no alumina phase; TiSiN showed 3 vol% TiO₂. After machining exposure, oxide fractions were systematically lower for all coatings, suggesting that mechanical wear removes oxidised surface layers faster than they form. The retained face-centred cubic phase fraction correlated positively with residual hardness measured by nanoindentation (R² = 0.84). Results provide a quantitative basis for linking XRD phase changes to tribological performance degradation in used cutting inserts.

SYN-PUB-03863.title: Characterising API-Level Incompatibilities in Open-Source Android Applications: An Empirical Survey
SYN-PUB-03863.text:
Characterising API-Level Incompatibilities in Open-Source Android Applications: An Empirical Survey (2015, journal, Journal of Software Engineering Practice).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Olivera Sredojević (R0363); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Jovanka Pejović (outside co-author).
Keywords: Android API; incompatibility classification; static analysis; open-source apps; empirical study.
This study examines the prevalence and distribution of API-level incompatibilities across 320 open-source Android applications drawn from a curated repository of F-Droid projects. Applications were analysed using a combination of static bytecode inspection and dynamic instrumentation across eight Android API levels ranging from level 16 to level 28. Incompatibilities were classified into four categories: deprecated API usage, removed method invocations, permission model changes, and layout inflation failures. Results show that 61% of surveyed applications contain at least one deprecated API call, and 18% exhibit runtime crashes attributable to removed or renamed methods when executed on API levels two or more versions above the target declared in the manifest. The study further correlates repository commit frequency with incompatibility density, finding that applications updated more than twice per year exhibit 34% fewer critical incompatibilities. The classification taxonomy and annotated dataset are released publicly to support further research.

SYN-PUB-03864.title: A Regression Testing Strategy for Android Applications Targeting Multiple API Levels Simultaneously
SYN-PUB-03864.text:
A Regression Testing Strategy for Android Applications Targeting Multiple API Levels Simultaneously (2019, journal, Software Testing International).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Katarina Varga (outside co-author); Radovan Radulović (R0694); Péter Molnár (outside co-author); Jovanka Pejović (outside co-author).
Keywords: regression testing; Espresso; multi-API testing; test tagging; Android.
Maintaining regression test suites that remain valid across a wide span of Android API levels is a practical challenge for small development teams. This paper proposes a layered test architecture in which test cases are tagged with applicability metadata specifying minimum and maximum API levels, deprecation-aware skip conditions, and device-class constraints such as screen density and form factor. The architecture was implemented as an extension to the Espresso UI testing framework and evaluated through a longitudinal case study with three mobile application projects maintained by student teams over two academic semesters. The extended framework reduced the number of false-positive test failures caused by platform differences by 47% compared to unmodified Espresso suites run across the same device pool. The approach added an average overhead of 9% to test execution time. Interviewed developers reported reduced confusion when interpreting test results on mixed-API-level device farms.

SYN-PUB-03865.title: Static Detection of Deprecated API Usage Chains in Android Codebases Using Interprocedural Call Graph Analysis
SYN-PUB-03865.text:
Static Detection of Deprecated API Usage Chains in Android Codebases Using Interprocedural Call Graph Analysis (2020, journal, Journal of Systems and Software Research Letters).
Authors: Dragan Marković (outside co-author); Sonja Bošković (R0923); Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Ana Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: call graph analysis; deprecated APIs; Soot; static analysis; third-party libraries.
Deprecated API calls in Android applications are often not isolated but form chains in which a deprecated method invokes other deprecated or soon-to-be-removed methods across multiple classes and libraries. This paper describes a static analysis approach that constructs interprocedural call graphs from compiled APK files using a modified version of the Soot analysis framework and identifies deprecation chains of length two or more. The technique was applied to 150 applications sampled from five categories on the Google Play Store, each analysed against the API level corresponding to its targetSdkVersion. Deprecation chains were found in 43% of applications, with an average chain length of 2.7 nodes. Chains involving third-party library code accounted for 61% of detected instances, highlighting the role of library update lag in fragmentation risk. A prioritisation score based on chain length and method removal probability is proposed to guide developer remediation efforts.

SYN-PUB-03866.title: Fragmentation Impact on Mobile Application Energy Consumption Across Android Versions
SYN-PUB-03866.text:
Fragmentation Impact on Mobile Application Energy Consumption Across Android Versions (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Symposium on Software Quality (BSSQ)).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Nikola Ostojić (outside co-author); Tobias Wenzel (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy consumption; Android versions; power measurement; Monsoon; non-functional testing.
Platform fragmentation affects not only functional correctness but also non-functional characteristics of Android applications. This study investigates whether energy consumption profiles of Android applications differ systematically across API levels due to changes in system services, scheduling, and I/O subsystems. Twelve applications from diverse categories were instrumented using Monsoon power monitors and executed on eight physical devices running Android 7.1 through 12.0 under controlled workloads. Statistically significant differences in energy consumption between API levels were found for nine of twelve applications, with median differences ranging from 4% to 31% across tested scenarios. Multimedia and background-sync-heavy applications showed the largest variance. The paper presents a lightweight test harness that automates power measurement across a device pool and produces cross-version energy comparison reports, and discusses the implications for battery-sensitive deployment decisions.

SYN-PUB-03867.title: Continuous Integration Pipelines for Multi-Version Android Testing: Configuration Patterns and Failure Analysis
SYN-PUB-03867.text:
Continuous Integration Pipelines for Multi-Version Android Testing: Configuration Patterns and Failure Analysis (2022, book chapter, Advances in Mobile Software Engineering, Springer Verlag Series on Software Quality).
Authors: Katarina Varga (outside co-author); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Branislava Dragišić (R0312).
Keywords: continuous integration; CI pipelines; emulator matrix; flaky tests; Android.
Continuous integration (CI) adoption in Android projects frequently stalls because configuring emulator matrices across multiple API levels is error-prone and time-consuming. This chapter reviews common CI configuration patterns observed in 200 public GitHub repositories hosting Android projects, focusing on how developers specify emulator targets, handle flaky tests attributable to version-specific emulator behaviour, and manage CI execution time budgets. Five recurrent anti-patterns are identified, including hard-coded API level values in CI scripts and the absence of conditional test skipping for deprecated paths. For each anti-pattern, a recommended configuration pattern with concrete YAML examples is provided. Flaky test rates attributable to emulator instability are estimated at 8–14% across the studied repositories, with higher rates on API levels below 24. The chapter closes with a decision guide for teams selecting between physical device clouds and local emulator matrices.

SYN-PUB-03868.title: DroidDelta: A Differential Testing Framework for Identifying Behavioural Changes Between Consecutive Android Releases
SYN-PUB-03868.text:
DroidDelta: A Differential Testing Framework for Identifying Behavioural Changes Between Consecutive Android Releases (2023, journal, Empirical Software Engineering Journal).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Bojana Cvejić (outside co-author); Luca Ferrarese (outside co-author); Ana Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: differential testing; UI comparison; Android releases; DroidDelta; compatibility defects.
Each Android release modifies system behaviour in ways not always reflected in API changelogs, creating latent compatibility defects. DroidDelta is a differential testing framework that automatically executes identical Espresso test scripts on two Android versions side-by-side, captures UI state snapshots at each interaction step, and uses a pixel-cluster comparison algorithm to identify rendering divergences alongside logcat-based behavioural divergence detection. The tool was evaluated comparing Android 12 versus 13 and Android 13 versus 14 release pairs across 30 applications. DroidDelta detected 124 rendering divergences and 41 behavioural divergences not reported in the official release notes. Manual inspection confirmed 87% of rendering divergences as genuine compatibility concerns and 78% of behavioural divergences as developer-relevant. Average per-application analysis time was 22 minutes on a mid-range workstation paired with two physical devices. The framework is designed to integrate as a CI stage triggered by SDK update events.

SYN-PUB-03869.title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Lint-Based Fragmentation Warnings in Reducing Compatibility Defect Density
SYN-PUB-03869.text:
Assessing the Effectiveness of Lint-Based Fragmentation Warnings in Reducing Compatibility Defect Density (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Mobile Software Testing (EWMST)).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Nikola Ostojić (outside co-author); Péter Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: Android Lint; static warnings; compatibility defects; defect density; Kotlin.
Android Lint includes a set of checks for fragmentation-related issues, but their effectiveness in practice has not been systematically evaluated. This study compares compatibility defect densities in 80 Android application projects before and after developers were asked to address all Lint fragmentation warnings in a controlled setting. Projects were drawn from an industry partner pool and ranged from 5,000 to 120,000 lines of Kotlin and Java code. Defects were measured by executing a standardised test suite across API levels 26 through 34 before and after warning remediation. Addressing Lint warnings reduced API-level-attributable defect density by 29% on average, with the largest reductions in projects with higher initial warning counts. However, 54% of defects detected by the test suite had no corresponding Lint warning, indicating substantial gaps in Lint's fragmentation coverage. A supplementary checklist of 18 fragmentation risk patterns not covered by Lint is provided.

SYN-PUB-03870.title: Predicting Compatibility Risk of Android Library Updates Using Dependency Graph Metrics
SYN-PUB-03870.text:
Predicting Compatibility Risk of Android Library Updates Using Dependency Graph Metrics (2026, journal, ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology).
Authors: Branislava Dragišić (R0312); Bojana Cvejić (outside co-author); Marta Kowalczyk (outside co-author); Luca Ferrarese (outside co-author).
Keywords: dependency graph; library updates; compatibility risk; machine learning; Maven.
When Android applications update a third-party library, the new library version may introduce or resolve platform compatibility issues in ways that are difficult to anticipate. This paper presents a predictive model for compatibility risk that uses dependency graph metrics—including fan-in, fan-out, version distance, and deprecation ratio of exported symbols—computed from library release artefacts available on Maven Central. A dataset of 1,140 library update events across 95 applications was constructed retrospectively by replaying version histories and running DroidDelta-based compatibility checks. A gradient-boosted classifier trained on dependency graph metrics achieved an AUC of 0.81 in predicting whether a library update would introduce a new compatibility defect. The model performs best for multimedia and networking libraries and worst for UI component libraries. Integration of the predictor as a pre-merge CI check is described, along with a discussion of threshold selection for different risk tolerances.

SYN-PUB-03940.title: Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances
SYN-PUB-03940.text:
Comparing SMOTE and ADASYN on Short Legal Texts with Fewer Than 500 Training Instances (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Aleksa Lazić (R0318).
Keywords: SMOTE; ADASYN; text resampling; TF-IDF; misdemeanour rulings.
Resampling techniques designed for tabular data are often applied to text feature vectors without assessing whether interpolation in high-dimensional TF-IDF space produces semantically coherent synthetic documents. This paper applies SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and ADASYN to a dataset of 487 Serbian misdemeanour rulings represented as 2,000-dimensional TF-IDF vectors, with minority classes containing as few as 31 samples. Classification performance is assessed using stratified five-fold cross-validation with SVM and gradient boosting classifiers. ADASYN yields the highest macro F1 improvement (from 0.34 to 0.51 for SVM), but manual inspection of 50 synthetic vectors shows that 38% contain feature combinations absent in any real document. The paper proposes a nearest-neighbour coherence filter that removes synthetic points deviating beyond two standard deviations from their class centroid, recovering coherence while retaining 81% of generated samples. This filtered variant outperforms unfiltered ADASYN on two of three evaluation metrics.

SYN-PUB-03969.title: Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework
SYN-PUB-03969.text:
Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework (2022, journal, Energies – Special Issue on Distribution Network Optimisation).
Authors: Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696); Luka Petrović (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Vera Knežević (R0320); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: reactive power dispatch; two-stage optimisation; voltage control; on-load tap changer; distribution system operator.
This paper proposes a two-stage optimisation framework for coordinating reactive power resources in low-voltage distribution networks, combining a day-ahead scheduling stage based on forecast generation and load profiles with a real-time correction stage executed at 15-minute intervals. Reactive power resources considered include smart photovoltaic inverters, a single on-load tap changer at the MV/LV transformer, and a switched capacitor bank at the feeder midpoint. The day-ahead stage minimises total reactive power losses subject to voltage band constraints using a linear programming relaxation of the power flow equations. The correction stage applies a rule-based droop adjustment using local voltage measurements only, requiring no communication infrastructure. The framework is tested on a 52-node low-voltage benchmark network and validated on a real feeder topology from Novi Sad obtained from the distribution system operator. Simulation over a 30-day period shows average voltage deviation reduction of 34 % and reactive energy import reduction of 41 % relative to a no-control baseline. Computational time for the day-ahead stage is under 8 seconds on standard hardware.

SYN-PUB-03983.title: Latent class recovery of arithmetic skill states in primary-school learners: a simulation and empirical study
SYN-PUB-03983.text:
Latent class recovery of arithmetic skill states in primary-school learners: a simulation and empirical study (2010, journal, Journal of Educational Measurement and Assessment).
Authors: Miroslav Kovač (outside co-author); Tanja Horvat (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: latent class analysis; arithmetic skill; primary education; simulation study.
This study evaluated the accuracy of latent class analysis (LCA) for recovering discrete skill states in a sample of 412 third-grade pupils completing a computer-administered arithmetic battery. Three-, four-, and five-class solutions were compared using BIC, AIC, and entropy indices. Simulation conditions varied sample size (100–800), class separation (low, medium, high), and item discrimination. Results showed that four-class solutions with medium-to-high separation were recovered reliably at sample sizes above 250. Applied to the empirical data, a four-class model distinguished non-starters, counting-based solvers, partial-fact retrievers, and fluent retrievers, with class membership predicting end-of-year teacher grades (r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Response latency added incremental classification accuracy beyond accuracy scores alone (ΔBIC = −38). Implications for adaptive routing in primary mathematics software are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03984.title: Fit indices for polytomous Rasch models applied to reading comprehension items in Serbian secondary schools
SYN-PUB-03984.text:
Fit indices for polytomous Rasch models applied to reading comprehension items in Serbian secondary schools (2012, journal, Psihologija u Obrazovanju – Journal of Educational Psychology).
Authors: Emilija Zec (R0322); Dragana Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: partial credit model; item fit; reading comprehension; large-scale assessment.
Polytomous items from a standardised reading comprehension test administered to 1,847 ninth-grade pupils in Serbia were analysed under the partial credit model (PCM) and the generalised partial credit model (GPCM). Item fit was evaluated using infit and outfit mean-square statistics, Q3 residual correlations, and signed chi-square tests. Thirteen of 42 items showed misfit primarily attributable to non-ordered thresholds, a pattern linked to ambiguous intermediate response categories identified through expert review. Reordering category labels improved fit for eight of these items in a validation subsample (n = 623). Person-fit analysis identified approximately 4.2 % of respondents as aberrant responders, concentrated in lower-ability ranges. The study provides normative fit benchmarks for Serbian large-scale educational surveys and recommends threshold disorder checks as a routine step before IRT scaling.

SYN-PUB-03985.title: Response time as a diagnostic signal in adaptive vocabulary tests: evidence from an IRT-based speed–accuracy model
SYN-PUB-03985.text:
Response time as a diagnostic signal in adaptive vocabulary tests: evidence from an IRT-based speed–accuracy model (2015, journal, Language Testing and Assessment Quarterly).
Authors: Vera Petrović (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: response time; speed-accuracy model; adaptive testing; vocabulary assessment.
This study applied a joint speed–accuracy IRT model—specifically a hierarchical version of the van der Linden (2007) framework—to data from an adaptive English vocabulary test taken by 934 university students in Serbia. The test consisted of 60 items drawn from a calibrated bank and was delivered via a browser-based platform that logged response times at millisecond resolution. Separate latent dimensions for ability and speed were estimated; the correlation between person speed and ability was −0.22, indicating that faster responders were not reliably more accurate. Item-level analyses showed that high-frequency vocabulary items elicited shorter and less variable response times, while low-frequency items produced bimodal response-time distributions consistent with dual-process retrieval. A subscore derived from response-time residuals predicted self-reported study habits independently of accuracy-based scores. Implications for adaptive test termination rules are discussed.

SYN-PUB-03986.title: Hidden Markov models for tracking conceptual change in secondary-school physics: a comparison of transition structures
SYN-PUB-03986.text:
Hidden Markov models for tracking conceptual change in secondary-school physics: a comparison of transition structures (2016, journal, Computers & Education Research).
Authors: Ivan Radovanović (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Miroslav Kovač (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: hidden Markov model; conceptual change; physics simulation; knowledge states.
Conceptual change in Newtonian mechanics was modelled as a latent Markov process using interaction logs from a physics simulation environment used by 318 high-school students across eight weeks. Four hidden states—misconception-dominant, transitional, partial-correct, and expert—were hypothesised based on prior qualitative research. Three transition structures (unconstrained, left-to-right, and partially ordered) were compared by marginal likelihood. The partially ordered model, which permitted regression from partial-correct to transitional but not to misconception-dominant, provided the best fit (ΔBIC = 112 versus unconstrained). State residence times averaged 3.1 instructional sessions for the transitional state. Instructional scaffolding events logged by the system were associated with a 2.3-fold increase in forward transition probability. The study provides a template for embedding hidden Markov diagnostics in simulation-based science learning environments.

SYN-PUB-03988.title: Detecting disengaged response patterns in large-scale online assessments using mixture IRT with a non-effortful responder class
SYN-PUB-03988.text:
Detecting disengaged response patterns in large-scale online assessments using mixture IRT with a non-effortful responder class (2018, journal, Educational and Psychological Measurement).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Katarina Vukić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: mixture IRT; disengagement; response time; large-scale assessment; non-effortful responding.
A mixture IRT model was developed to jointly estimate item parameters and classify respondents as effortful or non-effortful, using both accuracy and response-time features. The model was applied to data from a national diagnostic assessment of mathematics delivered online to 11,342 eighth-grade students in Serbia in 2018. The non-effortful class, characterised by near-chance accuracy and response times below 4 seconds, comprised 8.7 % of the sample. Excluding non-effortful respondents shifted item difficulty estimates by up to 0.42 logits for cognitively demanding items and narrowed ability-distribution standard deviation from 1.21 to 1.09. A sensitivity analysis using three alternative time thresholds confirmed stability of class membership above 82 % agreement. The study quantifies the impact of disengagement on population ability estimates and provides a mixture-model framework that can be integrated into operational assessment pipelines.

SYN-PUB-03989.title: Clickstream feature engineering for early prediction of learning outcomes in a university-level statistics MOOC
SYN-PUB-03989.text:
Clickstream feature engineering for early prediction of learning outcomes in a university-level statistics MOOC (2019, journal, Journal of Learning Analytics).
Authors: Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Anita Schulze (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: clickstream analysis; MOOC; dropout prediction; learning analytics; IRT.
Forty-seven clickstream features—covering session frequency, video replay rates, quiz attempt sequences, forum post counts, and time-of-day patterns—were extracted from the activity logs of 2,891 enrolees in a university-level introductory statistics MOOC run over 12 weeks. Feature importance was assessed via gradient-boosted trees and logistic regression; a parsimonious nine-feature model achieved AUC = 0.81 for dropout prediction at week four, compared to AUC = 0.68 for a baseline demographic model. Psychometric analysis using a two-parameter IRT model applied to weekly quiz items showed that estimated ability trajectories up to week three predicted final certificate attainment with r = 0.74. Combining ability trajectories with clickstream features in a stacked model improved AUC to 0.84. The study identifies a minimal feature set suitable for deployment in low-resource learning management systems.

SYN-PUB-03990.title: Estimating knowledge-state transitions without ground-truth labels: an expectation-maximisation approach for unstructured course logs
SYN-PUB-03990.text:
Estimating knowledge-state transitions without ground-truth labels: an expectation-maximisation approach for unstructured course logs (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Educational Data Mining (EDM 2021)).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Nevena Simić (R0755).
Keywords: knowledge tracing; EM algorithm; unstructured logs; corporate learning; label-free estimation.
Most knowledge-tracing studies rely on structured item banks with known correct answers; many real-world e-learning platforms produce unstructured logs where correctness labels are absent or unreliable. This paper develops an EM-based procedure that infers binary correctness proxies from response-time distributions, item co-occurrence patterns, and sequential consistency, without requiring manual item annotation. The procedure was validated on two datasets: a synthetic log generated from a known BKT model (parameter recovery RMSE ≤ 0.06) and an anonymised log of 7,200 learners using a corporate onboarding platform where ground-truth performance ratings were available for a 15 % subsample. On the subsample, inferred correctness correlated r = 0.68 with human ratings. Knowledge-state trajectories estimated from the inferred labels predicted six-month retention test scores (β = 0.41, p < 0.001) after controlling for time on platform. The procedure requires only event-timestamp and item-identifier fields.

SYN-PUB-03991.title: Psychometric calibration of an eye-tracking-based reading fluency diagnostic for early primary grades
SYN-PUB-03991.text:
Psychometric calibration of an eye-tracking-based reading fluency diagnostic for early primary grades (2022, journal, Reading and Writing: An Interdisciplinary Journal).
Authors: Sonja Babić (outside co-author); Ivan Radovanović (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: eye tracking; reading fluency; Rasch model; early literacy; primary education.
An eye-tracking-based reading fluency assessment was developed and calibrated for first- and second-grade children (N = 344, ages 6–8) using a Rasch model applied to fixation-derived accuracy scores and a log-normal response-time model for reading rate. Stimuli consisted of 36 short passages graded by lexical frequency and syntactic complexity. Item calibration indicated good fit (infit MNSQ range: 0.83–1.17) for 31 of 36 passages; five passages were revised after think-aloud protocols revealed ambiguous illustrations. Test information peaked at θ = −0.8, appropriate for the target population. A concurrent validity study against an established teacher-administered oral reading fluency probe yielded r = 0.73. Differential item functioning by gender was absent for 34 of 36 items. The diagnostic was subsequently embedded in a tablet-based assessment application deployed in 12 primary schools in Vojvodina.

SYN-PUB-03992.title: Alignment between formative diagnostic inferences and summative grades: an IRT-based audit across six secondary-school subjects in Serbia
SYN-PUB-03992.text:
Alignment between formative diagnostic inferences and summative grades: an IRT-based audit across six secondary-school subjects in Serbia (2024, journal, Assessment in Education: Principles, Policy & Practice).
Authors: Dragana Milošević (outside co-author); Katarina Vukić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322).
Keywords: formative assessment; summative grades; multidimensional IRT; grade inflation; secondary education.
Data from six secondary-school subjects—mathematics, Serbian language, biology, history, physics, and English—were collected from a digital learning management platform used by 3,412 students in 22 schools across Serbia during one academic year. For each subject, a multidimensional IRT model was estimated from platform quiz responses, and inferred diagnostic ability scores were compared to end-of-year teacher grades using Pearson and Spearman correlations, classification accuracy matrices, and Bland–Altman agreement plots. Correlations ranged from 0.51 (history) to 0.74 (mathematics). Systematic grade inflation relative to diagnostic scores was found in 14 of 22 schools, with a mean offset of 0.4 grade points on a five-point scale. Schools with higher diagnostic–grade alignment also showed lower within-school grade variance. The findings suggest that diagnostic platform scores and teacher grades measure partially overlapping but non-redundant constructs.

SYN-PUB-03993.title: Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach
SYN-PUB-03993.text:
Inferring prerequisite structures among skills from observational response data: a constraint-based graphical modelling approach (2026, journal, Journal of Educational Data Science).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Marco Ferretti (outside co-author); Ognjen Ninkov (R0386); Sonja Babić (outside co-author); Emilija Zec (R0322); Luka Nedić (R0911).
Keywords: prerequisite structures; causal discovery; skill graphs; adaptive learning; mathematics.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-04013.title: Evaluation of PERSIANN-CDR Satellite Precipitation Estimates Against Ground Observations Over the Middle Danube Basin, 2003–2013
SYN-PUB-04013.text:
Evaluation of PERSIANN-CDR Satellite Precipitation Estimates Against Ground Observations Over the Middle Danube Basin, 2003–2013 (2015, journal, International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Remote Sensing Research).
Authors: Žarko Pejić (R0364); Tamás Kovács (outside co-author); Isidora Vranješ (R0981); Danijela Đorđević (R0324); Miroslava Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Halász (outside co-author).
Keywords: PERSIANN-CDR; bias evaluation; Middle Danube Basin; daily precipitation; satellite validation.
Satellite-derived precipitation products are increasingly used in data-sparse regions, but their accuracy must be assessed against independent ground observations before application in agronomic or hydrological models. This study evaluated PERSIANN-CDR daily and monthly precipitation estimates over the Middle Danube Basin covering Serbia, northern Croatia, and southwestern Hungary, comparing them with records from 47 synoptic stations for the period 2003–2013. Statistical metrics including bias ratio, correlation coefficient, probability of detection, and false alarm ratio were computed at both temporal aggregations. At the monthly scale, PERSIANN-CDR showed a mean wet bias of 8.4% over the study area, with overestimation concentrated in the Fruška Gora foothill zone and underestimation over the flat Vojvodina plain. Daily performance was markedly lower, with a probability of detection of 0.61 and a false alarm ratio of 0.34 for events exceeding 10 mm. Systematic biases identified here were used as inputs for a multiplicative bias correction scheme applied in follow-up downscaling work.

SYN-PUB-04014.title: Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of Parametric Crop Insurance
SYN-PUB-04014.text:
Constructing a 25-Year Field-Scale Rainfall Archive for Vojvodina and Its Application to Historical Burn Analysis of Parametric Crop Insurance (2026, journal, Climate Services).
Authors: Ljubica Ristić (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364); Marco Ceriani (outside co-author); Danijela Đorđević (R0324); Stevan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: rainfall archive; burn analysis; parametric insurance; ERA5; TMPA; maize; sunflower.
Actuarially sound index insurance products require long historical records at the spatial resolution at which policies will be written. This paper describes the construction of a daily, 1 km resolution rainfall archive for Vojvodina spanning 1999–2023, produced by applying the KED downscaling framework to a blended ERA5–IMERG covariate and using all available station records (29–48 stations per year depending on network completeness). Archive consistency across the pre-IMERG era was maintained by substituting TMPA 3B42 for years before 2014 after demonstrating statistically equivalent covariate performance. A burn analysis was performed for three parametric products—sowing-period deficit, flowering-period excess, and grain-filling deficit—for maize and sunflower across 1,214 cadastral municipalities. Mean annual payout frequencies under tested trigger calibrations ranged from 14% to 27% depending on product and crop. The archive and analysis scripts are made publicly available. These outputs are intended to support insurers and reinsurers operating in the Pannonian agricultural zone in setting actuarially fair premiums.

SYN-PUB-04195.title: Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array
SYN-PUB-04195.text:
Benchmarking Embedded Lossy Compressors for Structural Health Monitoring on a 32-Node Piezoelectric Sensor Array (2023, journal, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing).
Authors: Ivana Rašković (outside co-author); Milana Bošković (R0341); Marco Bertolini (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: structural health monitoring; piezoelectric array; vector quantisation; guided wave; damage localisation; benchmark.
Structural health monitoring of bridges and tunnels increasingly relies on dense piezoelectric sensor arrays generating sustained data rates of hundreds of kilobytes per second. This paper benchmarks seven embedded lossy compressors — including DPCM, adaptive PLA, Haar filterbank, spectral peak preservation, and three variants of learned vector quantisation — on a 32-node wireless array deployed on a pedestrian footbridge in Novi Sad over four weeks. Evaluation metrics include compression ratio, reconstruction SNR, preservation of guided-wave arrival time picks (used for damage localisation), and energy per sample. The learned vector quantiser with 256-centroid codebook trained offline on historical data achieved the best damage-localisation accuracy (mean error 4.8 cm at 8:1 compression) but required 24 kB of flash for the codebook. Adaptive PLA achieved competitive localisation accuracy (mean error 6.1 cm) with only 2.1 kB of code and data memory. Practical trade-off recommendations are given for deployment scenarios constrained by either memory or localisation precision requirements.

SYN-PUB-04230.title: Implementation of Model Predictive Control for Current Regulation in a Five-Level NPC-Based Medium-Voltage Drive
SYN-PUB-04230.text:
Implementation of Model Predictive Control for Current Regulation in a Five-Level NPC-Based Medium-Voltage Drive (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 20th European Conference on Power Electronics and Drives (ECPED-2018), Warsaw).
Authors: Jelena Komazec (outside co-author); Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Radomir Bogdanović (R0344); Luca Bernardini (outside co-author).
Keywords: FCS-MPC; NPC inverter; synchronous reluctance motor; current control; switching frequency.
Finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) is evaluated as an alternative to conventional PI current regulators for a five-level neutral-point-clamped inverter connected to a 6 kV, 200 kW synchronous reluctance motor. The predictive model includes the motor electrical equations discretised at 50 µs sampling intervals and a capacitor voltage balance term weighted by a tunable factor λ. Two cost function formulations are compared: one penalising only current error and one additionally penalising switching frequency through a transition count term. Experimental validation was performed on a down-scaled 400 V, 7.5 kW laboratory drive using hardware-in-the-loop testing with a dSPACE DS1104 system. The switching-frequency-penalising formulation achieved a 22% reduction in average switching frequency compared to the basic formulation at equivalent current tracking error. Steady-state current THD measured at the motor terminals was 3.2% for the switching-penalised MPC versus 2.9% for PI with conventional space-vector PWM, a trade-off considered acceptable given the reduced thermal stress.

SYN-PUB-04278.title: Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija
SYN-PUB-04278.text:
Izgradnja invertovanog indeksa za srpske tekstove sa mešovitim pismom: osnovna metodologija (2010, conference, Zbornik radova Konferencije o primeni računara i interneta u Srbiji (PRIS 2010)).
Authors: Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349).
Keywords: invertovani indeks; mešovito pismo; normalizacija; srpski jezik.
U radu se opisuje metodologija izgradnje invertovanog indeksa koji istovremeno obrađuje ćirilična i latinična pojavljivanja srpskih reči bez prethodnog potpunog prevođenja u jedno pismo. Predloženi postupak uključuje korak normalizacije tokena kojim se za svaki token generiše kanonska forma zasnovana na fonemskoj reprezentaciji, a zatim se fonemski ključevi koriste kao primarni identifikatori u indeksu. Eksperimenti su sprovedeni na korpusu od 120 000 novinskih članaka preuzetih iz tri srpska dnevna lista u periodu 2000–2008. Mere preciznosti i odziva upoređene su s dva bazična sistema koji koriste isključivo ćirilični, odnosno isključivo latinični indeks. Predloženi sistem postiže F1 vrednost od 0,81 u zadatku ad-hoc pretrage, što je povećanje od 14 procentnih poena u odnosu na bolji od dva bazična sistema. Rad takođe razmatra pitanje memorijskog otiska hibridnog indeksa i predlaže strategiju kompresije rečnika.

SYN-PUB-04279.title: Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification
SYN-PUB-04279.text:
Phoneme-Based Token Canonicalization for Serbian Script Unification (2011, journal, Journal of Language Technology and Computational Linguistics).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author); Radovan Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: phoneme canonicalization; Serbian; script unification; legal text retrieval.
Serbian is officially written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts, and documents frequently contain tokens in both scripts within a single sentence or paragraph. This paper presents a token canonicalization procedure in which each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions, and the resulting phoneme string serves as the canonical form for retrieval purposes. We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions. The phoneme-based canonical form reduced the out-of-vocabulary rate from 9.3% to 2.1% compared with a Latin-only baseline and from 11.7% to 2.4% compared with a Cyrillic-only baseline. Precision at rank 10 improved by 8 percentage points over both baselines. Edge cases involving foreign loanwords and proper nouns are discussed, and a set of override rules is proposed for the 230 most frequent exceptions identified in the corpus.

SYN-PUB-04280.title: Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search
SYN-PUB-04280.text:
Cross-Script Query Expansion Using Transliteration Variants in Serbian Web Search (2014, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Information Retrieval Symposium (CEIRS 2014)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Tomislav Blažević (outside co-author); Milena Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: query expansion; transliteration; web search; Serbian; named entity.
Users searching Serbian-language web content often type queries in one script while relevant documents are stored in the other. This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index. We constructed a test collection of 1 800 queries and 210 000 web pages crawled from .rs domains, with relevance judgments pooled from four assessors. Three expansion strategies were compared: (1) appending the full transliteration variant, (2) appending only tokens whose transliteration differs from the original by more than two characters, and (3) expanding only named entities detected by a rule-based tagger. Strategy 3 achieved the best mean average precision of 0.497, versus 0.431 for no expansion, while reducing index bloat to 6% over the baseline index size. We also report retrieval latency measurements on a commodity server, showing that the overhead introduced by expansion remains under 12 ms at the 95th percentile for queries up to eight tokens.

SYN-PUB-04281.title: Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima
SYN-PUB-04281.text:
Automatska detekcija i korekcija nedoslednosti pisma u srpskim digitalnim arhivima (2015, conference, Zbornik radova 23. Telekomunikacionog foruma TELFOR).
Authors: Bojan Marković (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Ana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: detekcija nedoslednosti pisma; klasifikacija; digitalni arhivi; srpski jezik.
Digitalni arhivi srpskih novina i institucionalnih dokumenata često sadrže nedoslednosti gde je isti dokument delom u ćirilici, a delom u latinici, ponekad zbog grešaka pri skeniranju ili uredničkih intervencija. Ovaj rad predlaže metod automatske detekcije takvih nedoslednosti na nivou rečenice, korišćenjem klasifikatora koji kao atribute uzima raspodelu skriptnih blokova, učestalosti bigrama i morfosintaksičke signale. Klasifikator je treniran na 9 400 ručno označenih rečenica iz arhive jednog novosadskog lista i testiran na 2 100 rečenica iz arhive beogradskog lista. Postiže preciznost od 0,91 i odziv od 0,88 u klasi nedoslednih rečenica. Korak korekcije primenjuje fonemsku transliteraciju na detektovane nedosledne tokene. Eksperiment na donstremu (pretragom dokumenta) pokazuje da korigovana verzija arhive daje veću tačnost od nekorigovane za 7 procentnih poena u prosečnoj preciznosti.

SYN-PUB-04282.title: A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval
SYN-PUB-04282.text:
A Benchmark Corpus for Mixed-Script Serbian Information Retrieval (2017, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference Proceedings (LREC-SE 2017)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark corpus; evaluation; mixed-script; BM25; retrieval models.
Reproducible evaluation of retrieval systems for Serbian requires a shared test collection that explicitly accounts for mixed-script documents. This paper describes the construction of SrMIR-1, a benchmark corpus comprising 95 000 documents from four genres — news, law, literature, and social media — with 600 topics and graded relevance judgments produced by 12 trained assessors following TREC-style pooling at depth 30. Approximately 41% of documents contain tokens in both scripts. Inter-assessor agreement, measured by Cohen's kappa, was 0.73 across all topics. The paper reports baseline results for five retrieval models: BM25, language modelling with Dirichlet smoothing, a transliteration-aware BM25 variant, a neural dense retrieval model fine-tuned on Serbian, and a hybrid sparse–dense model. The transliteration-aware BM25 variant achieves the highest nDCG@10 of 0.531 among sparse models, while the hybrid model reaches 0.587. The corpus is publicly available under a Creative Commons licence.

SYN-PUB-04284.title: Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering
SYN-PUB-04284.text:
Script-Aware Passage Retrieval for Serbian Question Answering (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Workshop on Slavic Natural Language Processing (SlavicNLP 2021)).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: passage retrieval; question answering; BM25; script normalization; Serbian.
Open-domain question answering over Serbian-language document collections requires a passage retrieval component that is robust to the script in which both the question and the passage are written. This paper describes an adaptation of a BM25-based passage retrieval pipeline in which the tokenizer applies script normalization before indexing and at query time. We built an evaluation set of 340 factoid questions with 1 to 4 correct passages each, drawn from a mixed-script encyclopedia-style corpus of 180 000 passages. We compared four configurations: BM25 with no normalization, BM25 with script normalization, a dense bi-encoder model trained on Serbian data, and a hybrid of the latter two. The script-normalized BM25 retrieves at least one correct passage in the top 20 for 72% of questions, a gain of 17 percentage points over unnormalized BM25. The hybrid model reaches 81%. Failure analysis highlights questions containing transliterated foreign proper nouns as the main remaining challenge.

SYN-PUB-04285.title: Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse
SYN-PUB-04285.text:
Normalizacija skripte u kontekstu pretraživača internih dokumenata za mala i srednja preduzeća: iskustva iz prakse (2024, conference, Zbornik radova SYmposium on Informatics and Applied Mathematics (SIAM-Serbia 2024)).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Bojan Marković (outside co-author).
Keywords: interna pretraga; MSP; normalizacija pisma; implementacija; evaluacija.
Mala i srednja preduzeća u Srbiji čuvaju interne dokumente — ugovore, zapisnike, izveštaje — u mešovitom pismu bez konzistentne politike. Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma razvijenim u okviru naše istraživačke grupe. Pilot kompanije imale su kolekcije između 8 000 i 45 000 dokumenata. Merili smo preciznost pretrage pre i posle uvođenja normalizacije, korisnički odaziv i troškove uvođenja. U svim slučajevima normalizacija je poboljšala preciznost za najmanje 11 procentnih poena. Administrativni troškovi uvođenja bili su niski jer je modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema. Rad identifikuje i ograničenja: module treba ažurirati kada kompanija uvede novu terminologiju u jednom pismu, jer inicijalni rečnik sinonima nije potpun.

SYN-PUB-04286.title: SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers
SYN-PUB-04286.text:
SrMIR-2: Extending the Mixed-Script Serbian Retrieval Benchmark to Social Media and Administrative Registers (2025, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems).
Authors: Stefan Dragić (R0349); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Jelena Stanković (outside co-author); Carla Manzoni (outside co-author); Éva Gyöngyössy (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark; social media; administrative text; script mixing; evaluation.
SrMIR-1, released in 2017, covered news, law, literature, and general web content. Since then, social media posts and administrative e-government documents have become important retrieval targets, both exhibiting pronounced script mixing and informal orthography. This paper describes SrMIR-2, which adds two new document registers to the benchmark: 60 000 posts from a Serbian microblogging platform and 28 000 administrative forms and decisions from three municipal e-government portals. We created 280 new topics for these registers with relevance judgments from six trained assessors (kappa = 0.69). Baseline experiments show that script-normalizing BM25 outperforms unnormalized BM25 by a larger margin on social media (22 percentage points in nDCG@10) than on administrative documents (9 points), attributable to the higher rate of informal transliteration in social media. The benchmark is released with code for reproducible evaluation. We also report an ablation study isolating the contribution of named-entity handling in the normalization pipeline.

SYN-PUB-04287.title: Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load
SYN-PUB-04287.text:
Latency–Accuracy Trade-offs in Script-Normalizing Retrieval Pipelines Under Production Load (2026, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Information Retrieval (ECIR 2026)).
Authors: Nikola Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Dragić (R0349); Dejan Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: production retrieval; latency; accuracy; cascaded pipeline; query log analysis.
Deploying script-normalizing retrieval in production requires careful attention to latency, especially when normalization involves neural components. This paper presents a systematic study of trade-offs along the latency–accuracy spectrum for five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer, tested on a simulated production workload derived from query logs of a Serbian news aggregator with peak loads of 340 queries per second. We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes. The deterministic normalizer adds 3 ms median latency with MRR of 0.61. The transformer-based normalizer achieves MRR of 0.68 but adds 47 ms at the 99th percentile. A cascaded configuration — deterministic normalizer with neural fallback triggered only for out-of-vocabulary tokens — reaches MRR of 0.66 with a 99th-percentile latency overhead of only 9 ms. Detailed profiling data and configuration files are provided.

SYN-PUB-04325.title: Colour Space Selection and Feature Extraction for AOI Classification of Tombstoned 0201 Chip Resistors
SYN-PUB-04325.text:
Colour Space Selection and Feature Extraction for AOI Classification of Tombstoned 0201 Chip Resistors (2020, journal, Journal of Electronic Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Nemanja Stanić (outside co-author); Gordana Zorić (R1041); Marko Lazić (outside co-author); Bojana Mijatović (R0352); Dejan Jeremić (R0743).
Keywords: tombstoning; AOI; colour space; feature extraction; SVM.
Tombstoning of 0201 chip resistors is a reflow soldering defect with a low but non-zero occurrence rate that is difficult to classify reliably with AOI systems calibrated primarily on larger components. This study compares classification performance across five colour spaces (RGB, HSV, L*a*b*, YCbCr, greyscale) and three feature extraction strategies (histogram statistics, Haralick texture features, Hu moments) using a labelled dataset of 2 240 images, 340 of which contain tombstone defects, collected from production boards. A linear discriminant classifier and a support vector machine with RBF kernel were applied to each feature-colour combination. The L*a*b* space combined with Haralick features achieved the highest classification accuracy at 97.3% with a false-accept rate of 1.2%. Run-time per image was 54 ms, consistent with in-line deployment on a standard industrial PC. Recommendations for illumination geometry are included.

SYN-PUB-04326.title: Measurement Invariance of AOI Pseudo-Attribute Scores Across Two Inspection Generations at the Same Assembly Site
SYN-PUB-04326.text:
Measurement Invariance of AOI Pseudo-Attribute Scores Across Two Inspection Generations at the Same Assembly Site (2021, journal, Quality Engineering).
Authors: Tatjana Novaković (outside co-author); Valentina Simić (R0445); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Bojana Mijatović (R0352).
Keywords: AOI; measurement invariance; SPC continuity; factor analysis; score equating.
When an AOI system is replaced with a newer generation at an existing assembly site, historical quality data collected on the old system may not be directly comparable to data from the new system, compromising trend analysis and SPC continuity. This paper applies a confirmatory factor analytic framework, adapted from psychometric measurement invariance testing, to sequences of pseudo-attribute scores produced by two successive AOI systems at the same Vojvodina contract manufacturer. Data comprised 8 820 board-level score vectors spanning a 24-month transition period. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance models were fitted and compared by RMSEA, CFI, and chi-square difference tests. Scalar invariance was rejected for three of seven inspection zones, indicating that raw scores in those zones are not on a comparable scale across generations. A post-hoc equating procedure is proposed and validated on holdout data.

SYN-PUB-04328.title: Transfer Learning for AOI Defect Classification in Low-Data PCB Assembly Environments
SYN-PUB-04328.text:
Transfer Learning for AOI Defect Classification in Low-Data PCB Assembly Environments (2023, journal, Computers in Industry).
Authors: Marko Lazić (outside co-author); Dejan Jeremić (R0743); Nemanja Stanić (outside co-author); Ján Kopřiva (outside co-author); Bojana Mijatović (R0352).
Keywords: transfer learning; AOI; defect classification; deep learning; low-data regime.
Deep learning classifiers for AOI typically require thousands of labelled defect images per class, a volume rarely available in low-volume, high-mix PCB assembly where individual product runs are short. This paper evaluates three transfer learning strategies—feature extraction, fine-tuning of the last two convolutional blocks, and progressive unfreezing—applied to a pre-trained compact convolutional backbone retrained on an in-house dataset of 1 870 labelled solder-joint images across seven defect classes. Experiments vary the number of labelled training images per class from 20 to 200. Fine-tuning with progressive unfreezing achieved a macro-averaged F₁ score of 0.884 at 100 images per class, compared with 0.731 for feature extraction only and 0.802 for standard fine-tuning. At 40 images per class, the gap widened to 0.179 in favour of progressive unfreezing. Data augmentation strategies specific to PCB imagery, including simulated lighting variation and pad-rotation augmentation, contributed an additional 3.2 percentage points.

SYN-PUB-04373.title: A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board
SYN-PUB-04373.text:
A PC-Based Real-Time Target for Engine Control Unit Testing Using RTAI-Linux and a Low-Cost DAQ Board (2011, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Branimir Vukić (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356).
Keywords: RTAI-Linux; x86 real-time; engine ECU; CAN bus; low-cost HiL.
This paper describes the construction and validation of a low-cost hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) test bench built around a standard x86 PC running RTAI-Linux 3.8 and a commercially available 16-channel analog/digital acquisition board. The setup was used to emulate the sensor and actuator environment of a diesel engine management ECU supplied by a regional automotive Tier-1 supplier. A mean-value engine model with six state variables was implemented and executed at a fixed step size of 1 ms, achieving worst-case jitter below 35 µs across a 4-hour continuous run. CAN communication between the real-time host and the ECU was handled through a standard USB-to-CAN adapter operating at 500 kbit/s. Forty-two ECU software variants were tested against a library of 180 deterministic test cases covering cold-start, idle, and wide-open-throttle scenarios. The paper reports pass/fail statistics, timing overhead, and the cost breakdown of the bench, which totaled under 1 200 EUR in hardware. Limitations related to I/O bandwidth and USB latency are discussed and partly mitigated through interrupt coalescing.

SYN-PUB-04374.title: Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads
SYN-PUB-04374.text:
Modelling and Real-Time Implementation of a Brushless DC Motor Drive for HiL Emulation of Electric Power Steering Loads (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 10th International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY)).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Svetlana Kovačević (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Tomas Brezina (outside co-author).
Keywords: BLDC motor emulation; FPGA fixed-point; electric power steering; HiL; Spartan-6.
Electric power steering (EPS) systems place demanding requirements on HiL test benches because the steering column torque sensor and motor current feedback must be emulated at update rates below 500 µs. This work presents a BLDC motor model parameterised from bench measurements on a 48 V, 400 W motor taken from a mid-class passenger car. The model captures back-EMF harmonics up to the 7th order and includes a thermal sub-model with two lumped time constants. It was compiled to a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA using a fixed-point arithmetic pipeline operating at 50 MHz, achieving a simulation step of 20 µs. Analog outputs were generated through on-board 16-bit DACs. A comparison between the FPGA model and a reference floating-point Simulink simulation showed RMS current errors below 1.2% over standard SAE J266 steering manoeuvres. The paper also quantifies resource utilisation: 31% of available LUTs and 18% of DSP48 blocks on the target device.

SYN-PUB-04375.title: Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform
SYN-PUB-04375.text:
Fault Injection Framework for Automotive Body Control Module Testing on an Open-Source HiL Platform (2015, journal, International Journal of Automotive Technology and Engineering).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Norbert Feher (outside co-author).
Keywords: fault injection; body control module; ISO 26262; Xenomai; solid-state relay.
Body control modules (BCMs) must tolerate a range of electrical faults including open circuits, shorts to battery and shorts to ground on their I/O lines. Commercial HiL systems provide programmable fault relays, but their cost is prohibitive for small development teams. This paper presents a fault injection board designed around solid-state relay arrays and a microcontroller interface, integrated with a Beaglebone Black running a Xenomai real-time patch as the simulation host. The board supports 32 independent fault channels switchable within 2 ms. A BCM with 28 digital outputs and 14 analog inputs was tested under 96 fault combinations derived from ISO 26262 FMEA tables. The framework detected seven previously unreported software anomalies in the BCM firmware relating to debounce timer behaviour under simultaneous multi-line faults. Replication cost for the fault injection hardware was 340 EUR per board. The design files and driver code are released under a permissive open-source licence.

SYN-PUB-04376.title: Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications
SYN-PUB-04376.text:
Latency Characterisation of Open-Source Real-Time Kernels for Automotive HIL Applications (2016, journal, Real-Time Systems: Theory and Applications).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Zoran Marković (outside co-author); Spasoje Petrović (R0868).
Keywords: RTAI; Xenomai; PREEMPT_RT; latency; real-time Linux; HiL benchmarking.
Several open-source options exist for turning a general-purpose Linux system into a deterministic real-time platform: RTAI, Xenomai 3, and the PREEMPT_RT patch. This paper provides a systematic comparison of all three on two hardware platforms—a standard Intel Core i5 desktop and an ARM Cortex-A9 single-board computer—under automotive HiL workloads. Latency was measured using a hardware timer circuit with 100 ns resolution over 72-hour test windows while simultaneously running a 23-state vehicle dynamics model, a CAN stack, and a UDP telemetry stream. Xenomai 3 with the Cobalt core achieved the lowest worst-case latency on the x86 platform at 18 µs, while PREEMPT_RT showed marginally better throughput at the cost of 47 µs worst-case. On the ARM platform, Xenomai 3 and PREEMPT_RT performed comparably. The paper provides configuration recipes, kernel version numbers, and patch sets used, making the results reproducible. Recommendations are given for selecting a kernel flavour based on step-size and I/O bandwidth requirements.

SYN-PUB-04377.title: Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing
SYN-PUB-04377.text:
Integration of a FlexRay Bus Interface into a Low-Cost FPGA-Based HiL Bench for Chassis Domain ECU Testing (2017, conference, Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Engineering Systems (INES)).
Authors: Milica Stanković (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Péter Galajda (outside co-author); Branimir Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: FlexRay; FPGA VHDL; Artix-7; chassis ECU; ABS ESC testing.
FlexRay is used in safety-critical chassis domains such as active suspension and brake-by-wire. Integrating a FlexRay interface into a low-cost HiL platform is non-trivial because commercially licensed IP cores are expensive. This work documents the integration of an open FlexRay communication controller implemented in VHDL on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with a Linux-based simulation host connected via PCIe. The controller supports static segment scheduling with a cycle time of 5 ms and up to 64 frame slots. Two ABS/ESC ECUs from a regional supplier were used as devices under test. The paper reports successful execution of 214 scheduled test sequences covering wheel speed sensor emulation, hydraulic pressure command injection, and inter-ECU synchronisation checks. Timing accuracy of the FlexRay frames was within ±250 ns of nominal, verified with a dedicated bus analyser. Integration effort and remaining limitations regarding the dynamic segment are also discussed.

SYN-PUB-04378.title: A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases
SYN-PUB-04378.text:
A Semi-Automated Test Case Generation Method for ECU Validation Based on Boundary-Value Analysis of CAN Signal Databases (2018, journal, Journal of Automotive Software Engineering).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Cristian Morariu (outside co-author).
Keywords: test case generation; boundary-value analysis; CAN DBC; ECU validation; test automation.
ECU test suites are typically assembled manually from specification documents, which is time-consuming and incomplete. This paper describes a tool that parses CANdb++ DBC files to extract signal definitions—including physical ranges, factors, offsets, and initial values—and automatically generates boundary-value and equivalence-partition test cases for each signal. The tool was applied to two DBC databases: one covering a powertrain domain (312 signals, 47 message IDs) and one covering a body domain (198 signals, 31 message IDs). Test case counts of 1 847 and 1 203 were produced respectively and executed on the low-cost HiL bench described in earlier work. Execution time per test case averaged 4.3 seconds on the powertrain database. Twelve defects were identified in the body domain ECU firmware that manual testing had not found, including three out-of-range handling errors and two incorrect default value responses. The paper discusses integration with a lightweight Python-based test management framework and export to an XML format compatible with standard reporting tools.

SYN-PUB-04379.title: Power Consumption Profiling of Real-Time Simulation Targets Under Variable ECU Testing Workloads
SYN-PUB-04379.text:
Power Consumption Profiling of Real-Time Simulation Targets Under Variable ECU Testing Workloads (2019, conference, Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Embedded Systems and Real-Time Computing (ESRC)).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Filip Đorđević (R1034); Nikola Bogdanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: power consumption; real-time target; Zynq SoC; HiL workload; energy efficiency.
HiL test benches in embedded development teams often run continuously for extended periods. Understanding their power draw is important for infrastructure planning and for estimating operational costs. This paper presents power measurements taken on four representative real-time targets—an x86 mini-ITX board, a Raspberry Pi 4, a Beaglebone AI, and a Xilinx Zynq-7020 SoC board—while running engine, transmission, and body domain simulation workloads at step sizes of 0.5, 1, and 2 ms. Power was logged at 1 Hz using a calibrated USB power meter and a bench power supply with current monitoring. The x86 platform consumed 38–54 W depending on workload, while the Zynq SoC consumed 4.1–6.8 W for equivalent model complexity. Thermal imaging was used to identify hot spots on each board. The paper also discusses the trade-off between determinism margin and power saving modes, noting that CPU frequency scaling degraded worst-case latency by up to 90 µs on the x86 platform when not properly managed.

SYN-PUB-04380.title: Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms
SYN-PUB-04380.text:
Containerised Deployment of Real-Time ECU Test Environments Using Docker and Xenomai on Embedded Linux Platforms (2022, journal, Software: Practice and Experience in Embedded Systems).
Authors: Darko Ninkov (R0356); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); László Keviczky (outside co-author).
Keywords: Docker; Xenomai; containerisation; ECU test bench; reproducibility.
Reproducing a specific HiL software environment across multiple bench instances and over time is a persistent problem in automotive software development. This paper investigates whether Docker containers can be used to encapsulate the user-space components of a Xenomai 3 real-time application—model binaries, CAN stack configuration, test scripts—while the host kernel retains the Cobalt real-time core. Experiments were conducted on two identical Raspberry Pi 4 platforms running an identical Xenomai-patched kernel. Containerised and native deployments were compared for latency, throughput, and deployment time across three ECU test suites. Worst-case latency overhead introduced by the container runtime was 3 µs in all measured cases, considered acceptable for step sizes of 1 ms and above. Deployment time was reduced from approximately 45 minutes of manual setup to under 6 minutes. The paper also describes a versioning workflow using a private registry and discusses limitations when hardware access to GPIO and CAN interfaces is required inside the container.

SYN-PUB-04381.title: Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment
SYN-PUB-04381.text:
Ethernet-Based Time-Sensitive Networking as a Backbone for Distributed Automotive HiL Benches: Feasibility Assessment (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.SY)).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Darko Ninkov (R0356); Péter Galajda (outside co-author).
Keywords: TSN; IEEE 802.1Qbv; distributed HiL; automotive Ethernet; time synchronisation.
As automotive architectures shift toward Ethernet-based in-vehicle networks, HiL benches must emulate Ethernet traffic alongside classical fieldbuses. This preprint reports preliminary measurements on using IEEE 802.1AS time synchronisation and 802.1Qbv time-aware shaper on a three-node distributed HiL bench where each node hosts a partial vehicle subsystem model. Nodes are connected through a managed switch with TSN support. Clock synchronisation accuracy between nodes was measured at 120 ns RMS over a 48-hour window using a shared GPS-disciplined reference. Model state exchange over scheduled Ethernet frames at 1 ms intervals showed zero missed deadlines in a 24-hour test. The preprint describes the network configuration, measurement methodology, and a preliminary cost comparison against dedicated real-time Ethernet solutions. Limitations include the current absence of a fault simulation capability for the TSN link itself. Full journal submission is planned after completing automotive protocol conformance tests.

SYN-PUB-04457.title: Exploiting Temporal Correlation in Multi-Sensor Nodes: Joint Source Coding Without Inter-Sensor Communication
SYN-PUB-04457.text:
