Counsellors' MI-consistent behaviours, coded from session recordings, were positively associated with participant autonomous motivation at 4 weeks (r = .51). Results justify a fully powered trial and indicate that video-delivered autonomy-supportive counselling is acceptable in this population.

SYN-PUB-04970.title: Message personalisation and perceived relevance in a workplace stress-reduction campaign: evidence from three Serbian companies
SYN-PUB-04970.text:
Message personalisation and perceived relevance in a workplace stress-reduction campaign: evidence from three Serbian companies (2023, journal, Work, Health and Organisational Psychology).
Authors: Branislava Lekić (R0413); Jelena Stojanović (outside co-author); Boris Čanak (outside co-author).
Keywords: message personalisation; workplace health promotion; stress reduction; perceived relevance; occupational psychology.
Workplace mental health campaigns often distribute uniform materials regardless of employee characteristics. This study tested whether personalising stress-reduction messages to employees' reported stress type (work overload, interpersonal conflict, or role ambiguity) increased perceived personal relevance and intention to use provided self-help resources. Employees at three medium-sized companies in Vojvodina (total N = 284) were randomly assigned to receive personalised or generic messaging via their internal e-mail system over three weeks. Perceived relevance was higher in the personalised condition (M = 5.1 vs. 4.3 on a 7-point scale, t(282) = 5.2, p < .001, d = 0.62). Clicks on self-help resource links were 2.3 times more frequent in the personalised group (rate ratio = 2.31, 95% CI: 1.54–3.46). No significant difference was found for self-reported stress levels at three weeks, suggesting that intention and engagement do not immediately translate to symptom reduction. These findings support personalisation as a cost-feasible enhancement to workplace health promotion.

SYN-PUB-04971.title: Fear appeals in anti-sedentary behaviour campaigns: a meta-analysis of experimental studies published 2000–2022
SYN-PUB-04971.text:
Fear appeals in anti-sedentary behaviour campaigns: a meta-analysis of experimental studies published 2000–2022 (2024, journal, Health Communication Research Quarterly).
Authors: Branislava Lekić (R0413); Petra Kováčová (outside co-author); Nevena Simić (R0755); Marko Dimitrijević (outside co-author).
Keywords: fear appeals; sedentary behaviour; meta-analysis; Extended Parallel Process Model; physical activity communication.
Fear appeal interventions aimed at reducing prolonged sitting and sedentary behaviour have accumulated as a distinct literature separate from broader physical activity research. This meta-analysis aggregated 29 experimental and quasi-experimental studies (total N = 6,814) testing fear-based versus non-fear messages on sedentary behaviour outcomes. Random-effects models yielded a pooled effect size of d = 0.22 (95% CI: 0.13–0.31) in favour of fear appeals on behavioural outcomes; effects on intentions were somewhat larger (d = 0.31). Moderator analyses showed that studies including high-efficacy information alongside threat information produced significantly larger effects (Q = 9.4, p = .002), consistent with the Extended Parallel Process Model. Studies relying solely on self-reported sitting time as outcome showed inflated effect estimates relative to device-based measures. Publication bias was detected via Egger's test and trim-and-fill correction reduced the pooled estimate to d = 0.16. The review highlights the importance of pairing threat framing with actionable coping information in campaign design.

SYN-PUB-04972.title: Designing chatbot-delivered behaviour change conversations for smoking cessation: user testing and interaction analysis
SYN-PUB-04972.text:
Designing chatbot-delivered behaviour change conversations for smoking cessation: user testing and interaction analysis (2025, preprint, PsyArXiv).
Authors: Branislava Lekić (R0413); Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Marija Kovačević (outside co-author); Tijana Ranković (outside co-author).
Keywords: chatbot; conversational agent; smoking cessation; motivational enhancement; user testing.
Conversational agents (chatbots) represent a scalable channel for delivering behaviour change support, but evidence on optimal conversational design remains limited. This preprint reports findings from a user-testing phase of a chatbot designed to deliver brief motivational enhancement for smoking cessation. Forty-two smokers (18–55 years) in Novi Sad interacted with a prototype chatbot across two sessions and completed measures of perceived autonomy support, conversational naturalness, and engagement. Think-aloud protocols were recorded during the first session and subjected to thematic analysis. Users responded positively to reflective listening utterances (coded from conversation logs) but found open-ended questioning excessive when not clearly linked to a visible conversational goal. Perceived autonomy support correlated with willingness to continue using the chatbot (r = .58, p < .001). Interaction log analysis identified six recurrent breakdown points where users disengaged or gave minimal responses. The findings are used to revise the chatbot script and interaction logic ahead of a planned randomised evaluation.

SYN-PUB-04995.title: A Comparative Study of RPNI and Evidence-Driven State Merging on Small Labelled Samples
SYN-PUB-04995.text:
A Comparative Study of RPNI and Evidence-Driven State Merging on Small Labelled Samples (2011, journal, Novi Sad Journal of Mathematics and Computing).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Ksenija Hadžić (R0416).
Keywords: RPNI; EDSM; passive automaton learning; benchmarking; state merging.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-04996.title: Inferring Finite Automata for Binary Communication Protocols from Packet Captures
SYN-PUB-04996.text:
Inferring Finite Automata for Binary Communication Protocols from Packet Captures (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Formal Methods and Protocol Engineering (CEFMPE)).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author).
Keywords: protocol inference; packet capture; finite automata; network traces; RPNI.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-04997.title: Active Learning of Network Protocol State Machines Using Membership and Equivalence Queries
SYN-PUB-04997.text:
Active Learning of Network Protocol State Machines Using Membership and Equivalence Queries (2016, journal, Journal of Computer Networks and Distributed Systems).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: L* algorithm; active automaton learning; protocol state machines; membership queries; equivalence queries.
Angluin's L* algorithm learns an unknown regular language by posing membership queries and equivalence queries to a teacher. We adapt this framework to learn state machines of application-layer network protocols, where a live server acts as the membership oracle and conformance testing acts as the approximate equivalence oracle. The approach is applied to four text-based protocols implemented by open-source servers. For each protocol, we measure the number of membership queries required until convergence, the size of the resulting hypothesis automaton, and the number of counterexamples returned during equivalence testing. Across all four protocols, learning converged within 2,100 to 14,700 membership queries and produced automata of 12 to 47 states. We discuss reset costs, timeouts, and non-determinism in server responses as practical obstacles and propose mitigations. The resulting models are validated against independently written RFC-compliant test suites.

SYN-PUB-04998.title: Detecting Anomalous Protocol Behaviour Using Inferred Automaton Models
SYN-PUB-04998.text:
Detecting Anomalous Protocol Behaviour Using Inferred Automaton Models (2019, journal, Journal of Information Security and Networks).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Ivana Đorđević (outside co-author); Florian Herrmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; SCADA; protocol model; inferred automata; intrusion detection.
Once a finite automaton model of a protocol is inferred from normal traffic, it can serve as a baseline for anomaly detection: messages causing transitions absent from the model are flagged. We implement this principle and evaluate it on a dataset of 230,000 sessions from a SCADA communication protocol captured in a test environment, of which 4,800 sessions contain injected anomalies of five types (replay, truncation, out-of-order, field mutation, and session hijack simulation). The inferred DFA correctly flags anomalous sessions with a precision of 0.91 and a recall of 0.87 averaged across anomaly types. Replay and out-of-order anomalies are detected most reliably; field mutation is detected less well because it does not always alter the message-type sequence. We compare performance to a Hidden Markov Model baseline and a rule-based system, finding the automaton approach superior in precision at comparable recall levels.

SYN-PUB-04999.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Passive Learning of Regular Languages with One-Sided Error
SYN-PUB-04999.text:
Sample Complexity Bounds for Passive Learning of Regular Languages with One-Sided Error (2020, journal, Theoretical Computer Science Letters).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Mirjana Vuković (outside co-author); Luka Omerzel (outside co-author).
Keywords: PAC learning; sample complexity; regular languages; VC dimension; one-sided error.
We study the sample complexity of passive learning of regular languages in the PAC framework where learners are permitted only false-negative errors — that is, the hypothesis may reject strings in the target language but must not accept strings outside it. This one-sided error condition arises naturally in safety-critical protocol verification. We derive upper and lower bounds on the number of labelled examples sufficient and necessary for a consistent learner to achieve error at most ε with confidence at least 1 − δ. The upper bound, of order O(k² · n · log(1/δ) / ε), depends on k, the number of states of the minimal DFA, and n, the alphabet size. The lower bound construction uses a family of pairwise distinguishable automata to show that dependence on k is unavoidable. Connections to the VC dimension of DFA hypothesis classes are also established.

SYN-PUB-05000.title: GInferLib: A Python Library for Grammatical Inference of Finite Automata
SYN-PUB-05000.text:
GInferLib: A Python Library for Grammatical Inference of Finite Automata (2021, journal, Journal of Open Research Software in Computer Science).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: grammatical inference; software library; finite automata; open source; benchmarking.
We present GInferLib, an open-source Python library providing implementations of seven grammatical inference algorithms for deterministic and nondeterministic finite automata, including RPNI, EDSM, L*, NL*, and three recent state-merging variants. The library offers a unified API for defining sample sets, running inference, inspecting intermediate hypothesis automata, and exporting results to standard formats including DOT, KISS, and a custom JSON schema. Benchmark results on 500 randomly generated regular languages show running times and accuracy figures consistent with published results in the original algorithm papers, validating the implementations. The library includes utilities for generating random DFAs, sampling strings, and computing standard metrics such as structural accuracy and Jaccard similarity between hypothesis and target. An interactive tutorial built with Jupyter notebooks is included in the repository. The library is intended primarily for researchers and graduate students.

SYN-PUB-05001.title: Learning Automaton Models of IoT Device Behaviour from Encrypted Traffic Metadata
SYN-PUB-05001.text:
Learning Automaton Models of IoT Device Behaviour from Encrypted Traffic Metadata (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Formal Methods in Network Security (FMNS)).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Florian Herrmann (outside co-author); Stefan Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT; encrypted traffic; metadata inference; automaton learning; network security.
End-to-end encryption prevents direct inspection of protocol message content, but metadata features — packet sizes, inter-arrival times, and flow directions — remain observable. We investigate whether finite automaton models of IoT device communication behaviour can be inferred from such metadata alone. Twenty-two consumer IoT device types were placed in a controlled network testbed; traffic was captured over 72-hour periods under scripted usage scenarios. Message sequences were reconstructed from metadata clusters using a k-means procedure with k determined by a silhouette criterion. RPNI was applied to the resulting labelled sequences. The inferred automata reproduce 79–93% of transitions present in models derived from unencrypted reference captures of the same devices. Devices with highly regular behaviour (smart plugs, sensors) yielded better models than devices with irregular patterns (smart cameras during video streaming). The approach is evaluated on its suitability for network anomaly detection in encrypted environments.

SYN-PUB-05002.title: Counterexample-Guided Refinement of Inferred Protocol Automata Using Fuzzing
SYN-PUB-05002.text:
Counterexample-Guided Refinement of Inferred Protocol Automata Using Fuzzing (2024, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Formal Methods and Protocol Engineering (CEFMPE)).
Authors: Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Ivana Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: automaton refinement; fuzzing; counterexample-guided; protocol models; active learning.
An inferred automaton model of a protocol is only as good as the coverage of its training traces. We propose a refinement loop in which a fuzzer generates candidate inputs that drive the live protocol implementation into states not represented in the current hypothesis automaton, collecting new labelled counterexamples that are fed back to the inference algorithm. The process iterates until no new counterexamples are found within a time budget. Applied to four open-source implementations of a file-transfer protocol, the loop produces automata 23–41% larger than those obtained from passive inference alone, with a corresponding increase in structural accuracy of 8–17 percentage points when compared against a manually constructed ground-truth model. Total fuzzing budget across all experiments was 48 CPU-hours. We characterise which protocol features are most likely to be missed by passive inference and most reliably recovered by fuzzing.

SYN-PUB-05003.title: Probably Approximately Correct Identification of Minimal DFAs Under Restricted Query Models
SYN-PUB-05003.text:
Probably Approximately Correct Identification of Minimal DFAs Under Restricted Query Models (2026, journal, Journal of Automata, Languages and Combinatorics).
Authors: Mirjana Vuković (outside co-author); Luka Omerzel (outside co-author); Ksenija Hadžić (R0416); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Ratko Simić (R0790).
Keywords: PAC identification; DFA learning; statistical equivalence; query complexity; sample complexity.
We examine a restricted active learning setting in which equivalence queries are replaced by statistical sampling: the learner draws random strings from a known distribution and observes their membership labels. This weakened query model is relevant when black-box testing of real systems cannot guarantee exact equivalence answers. We show that, for the class of languages accepted by DFAs of at most k states over an alphabet of size n, the number of samples required to achieve PAC identification with parameters (ε, δ) is Θ(k² log(k n / δ) / ε) under the uniform distribution over strings of bounded length. We also show that no consistent learner can do better than Ω(k log k / ε) samples in the worst case regardless of the string distribution. Experimental validation using GInferLib on synthetic targets confirms that empirical sample requirements track the theoretical bounds closely for k ≤ 25.

SYN-PUB-05072.title: Fitting Heavy-Tailed Severity Distributions to Internal Operational Loss Data: A Comparison of Lognormal, Pareto and Weibull Specifications
SYN-PUB-05072.text:
Fitting Heavy-Tailed Severity Distributions to Internal Operational Loss Data: A Comparison of Lognormal, Pareto and Weibull Specifications (2010, journal, Acta Oeconomica Pannonica).
Authors: Mária Kováčová (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: severity distribution; generalised Pareto; operational loss data; Advanced Measurement Approach; goodness-of-fit.
This paper evaluates three parametric families—lognormal, generalised Pareto, and Weibull—for modelling the severity of operational loss events recorded in the internal loss database of a mid-sized Central European bank over 2001–2008. The dataset comprises 1 147 loss observations across six Basel II event-type categories. Parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood and L-moments; goodness-of-fit is assessed via Anderson–Darling and Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics. For the external fraud and internal fraud categories, the generalised Pareto distribution with shape parameter estimated between 0.31 and 0.47 provides the best fit at the 5% significance level. For technology-related events, the lognormal remains competitive. The paper discusses implications for regulatory capital calculation under the Advanced Measurement Approach and recommends a mixed strategy in which the severity model is selected per business-line and event-type cell rather than applied uniformly. Sensitivity of Value-at-Risk at the 99.9% confidence level to distributional choice is shown to be substantial, with differences reaching 34% of the point estimate.

SYN-PUB-05073.title: Poisson versus Negative Binomial Frequency Models for Operational Risk Event Counts: Evidence from a Serbian Banking Panel
SYN-PUB-05073.text:
Poisson versus Negative Binomial Frequency Models for Operational Risk Event Counts: Evidence from a Serbian Banking Panel (2012, journal, South-East European Journal of Finance and Economics).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Bojana Trivunović (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: frequency modelling; negative binomial; overdispersion; operational VaR; bank panel data.
Accurate frequency modelling is a prerequisite for credible operational Value-at-Risk estimation. This study tests whether the Poisson assumption for annual event counts is tenable using a balanced panel of eight Serbian commercial banks observed over 2005–2011, yielding 56 bank–year observations and 4 312 individual loss records obtained under a data-sharing agreement with the National Bank of Serbia. Likelihood-ratio tests and Vuong's statistic consistently reject equidispersion for five of the seven event-type categories examined, favouring the negative binomial specification. Estimated dispersion parameters range from 0.18 to 1.63 across categories. Monte Carlo experiments with 100 000 replications show that using Poisson instead of the negative binomial inflates the 99.9th-percentile aggregate loss estimate by 8–22% depending on severity tail weight. The paper recommends routine overdispersion testing as part of model validation procedures.

SYN-PUB-05074.title: Threshold Selection for Extreme Value Modelling of IT Security Incident Costs in Financial Institutions
SYN-PUB-05074.text:
Threshold Selection for Extreme Value Modelling of IT Security Incident Costs in Financial Institutions (2014, conference, Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Quantitative Methods in Finance and Insurance, Budapest).
Authors: László Farkas (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: extreme value theory; generalised Pareto; threshold selection; IT security costs; bootstrap.
Applying extreme value theory to information security loss data requires a principled choice of threshold above which the generalised Pareto distribution is fitted. This paper compares four threshold selection methods—mean excess plot inspection, the Hill estimator stability plot, the automated metric of Danielsson and de Vries, and a minimum-distance criterion—using a synthetic dataset of 2 000 IT security incident costs constructed to resemble patterns reported in industry loss databases. The distribution of costs follows a mixture with a light-bodied bulk below USD 50 000 and a heavy tail above. Results show that automated methods select thresholds 15–30% higher than graphical inspection, leading to shape parameter estimates that differ by up to 0.12 and to 99th-percentile loss estimates differing by up to 28%. A bootstrap confidence interval procedure for the threshold-conditional GPD fit is proposed and illustrated. The findings have direct relevance for cyber risk capital allocation in small and medium financial institutions.

SYN-PUB-05075.title: Operational Risk Capital Models Under Basel III: A Textbook Treatment with Worked Examples
SYN-PUB-05075.text:
Operational Risk Capital Models Under Basel III: A Textbook Treatment with Worked Examples (2015, book chapter, Quantitative Methods in Banking Regulation, edited volume, Faculty of Economics in Subotica Press).
Authors: Zoran Anđelić (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: Basel III; Loss Distribution Approach; capital allocation; compound distribution; Standardised Measurement Approach.
This book chapter provides a structured exposition of the Loss Distribution Approach as implemented under Basel III requirements, written for graduate students in banking and finance. It begins with the actuarial foundations of compound distributions, proceeds through parameter estimation and Monte Carlo aggregation, and concludes with capital allocation across business lines using the Euler principle. Worked numerical examples use publicly available ORX consortium summary statistics. The chapter also covers the Standardised Measurement Approach introduced in the 2017 Basel Committee consultative document and discusses the tension between model complexity and supervisory comparability. An appendix provides annotated R code for a complete LDA workflow including fitting, simulation, and sensitivity analysis. The chapter is intended as course material for advanced risk management modules.

SYN-PUB-05078.title: A Scenario-Based Impact Estimation Framework for Ransomware Attacks on Small and Medium Enterprises
SYN-PUB-05078.text:
A Scenario-Based Impact Estimation Framework for Ransomware Attacks on Small and Medium Enterprises (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 12th Symposium on Risk and Insurance, Novi Sad).
Authors: Gábor Széles (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: ransomware; scenario analysis; SHELF protocol; SME; impact estimation.
Small and medium enterprises have limited actuarial loss history to parameterise LDA models for ransomware risk. This paper proposes a structured scenario elicitation and quantification framework in which expert judgements are converted into truncated lognormal severity distributions using the SHELF protocol. Six scenario categories are defined—file encryption, operational downtime, recovery costs, reputational damage, regulatory fines, and third-party liability—and combined into a total impact distribution via Monte Carlo simulation with 500 000 trials. The framework is illustrated using data from 14 scenario workshops conducted with risk managers and IT security personnel at SMEs in the Vojvodina region, with total scenario coverage of 38 firms. The resulting aggregate loss distribution has a median of EUR 47 000 and a 95th percentile of EUR 310 000. Sensitivity analysis identifies operational downtime as the dominant contributor to tail risk, accounting for 58% of 99th-percentile loss variance. The framework is designed to be implementable without specialist software.

SYN-PUB-05079.title: Bayesian Updating of Operational Loss Severity Parameters Using External Consortium Data
SYN-PUB-05079.text:
Bayesian Updating of Operational Loss Severity Parameters Using External Consortium Data (2019, journal, Annals of Operations Risk and Insurance Mathematics).
Authors: Ivana Lukić (outside co-author); Mária Kováčová (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: Bayesian updating; MCMC; severity estimation; consortium data; parameter uncertainty.
Institutions with short internal loss histories face the problem of sparse data in the tail, leading to high parameter uncertainty in fitted severity distributions. This paper develops a Bayesian framework that uses external consortium loss statistics as a prior and updates it with institution-specific internal data. The prior is elicited from ORX-style summary statistics (mean, standard deviation, and selected quantiles of annual aggregate loss by event category) using moment matching onto a lognormal hyperprior for the scale parameter. The posterior is approximated by Markov Chain Monte Carlo using a Metropolis–Hastings algorithm with 200 000 draws after a 50 000 draw burn-in. The framework is applied to a dataset from a Serbian savings bank with only 87 IT security loss observations over six years. Posterior predictive 99.9th-percentile estimates are compared to MLE-based estimates; the Bayesian approach reduces the coefficient of variation of the capital estimate from 0.61 to 0.29. The paper provides R code for all computations.

SYN-PUB-05081.title: Comparing the Standardised Measurement Approach and the Loss Distribution Approach for Cyber Risk Capital: A Simulation Study for Balkan Banking Sectors
SYN-PUB-05081.text:
Comparing the Standardised Measurement Approach and the Loss Distribution Approach for Cyber Risk Capital: A Simulation Study for Balkan Banking Sectors (2021, journal, Review of Eastern European Banking Studies).
Authors: Ana Vinković (outside co-author); Gábor Széles (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: Standardised Measurement Approach; Basel; cyber risk capital; simulation study; Balkan banking.
The Basel Committee's 2017 decision to replace internal models with the Standardised Measurement Approach (SMA) for operational risk capital was contested by practitioners who argued it would disconnect capital from actual risk profiles. This paper uses a simulation study to compare SMA and LDA capital estimates for cyber risk specifically, using calibrated loss scenarios representative of banking sectors in Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia. For each of 50 simulated bank profiles varying in size and cyber loss history, both methods are applied and results compared at the 99.9% confidence level. The SMA consistently overestimates capital for small banks (median ratio SMA/LDA = 1.43) and underestimates for large banks (median ratio = 0.86), consistent with its size-driven formula. The paper argues that a hybrid approach retaining internal frequency modelling within an SMA-compatible framework is feasible and quantifies the potential capital savings.

SYN-PUB-05082.title: Frequency–Severity Decomposition of Phishing-Related Losses in Serbian Banks: A Zero-Inflated Compound Model
SYN-PUB-05082.text:
Frequency–Severity Decomposition of Phishing-Related Losses in Serbian Banks: A Zero-Inflated Compound Model (2022, journal, Economic Annals – Faculty of Economics in Subotica).
Authors: Bojana Trivunović (outside co-author); Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: phishing losses; zero-inflated model; truncation correction; Serbian banks; compound loss model.
Many Serbian banks report zero phishing-related losses in a given quarter not because phishing attacks do not occur but because losses fall below internal reporting thresholds or are absorbed without formal recording. This paper addresses the resulting excess zeros in the frequency distribution by fitting a zero-inflated negative binomial model to quarterly event counts from 11 banks over 2015–2021 (308 bank–quarter observations). The probability of structural zero is modelled as a logistic function of the bank's cyber insurance indicator and its IT security expenditure per employee. The mixing probability is estimated at 0.34, meaning roughly one third of zero-count observations are structural. Severity is fitted with a lognormal distribution truncated below a EUR 1 000 reporting threshold; truncation correction raises the estimated mean severity by 18%. The paper is the first to apply zero-inflated frequency models specifically to phishing loss data from the Serbian banking sector.

SYN-PUB-05083.title: Aggregate Loss Distribution Approximation Methods for Cyber Risk: Panjer Recursion, Fast Fourier Transform, and Monte Carlo Compared
SYN-PUB-05083.text:
Aggregate Loss Distribution Approximation Methods for Cyber Risk: Panjer Recursion, Fast Fourier Transform, and Monte Carlo Compared (2024, journal, Journal of Computational Risk and Finance).
Authors: Annika Lindström (outside co-author); László Farkas (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: aggregate loss distribution; Panjer recursion; Fast Fourier Transform; Monte Carlo; heavy tail.
Three numerical methods for computing aggregate loss distributions—Panjer recursion, Fast Fourier Transform inversion, and direct Monte Carlo simulation—are compared in terms of accuracy and computational cost for cyber risk applications characterised by heavy-tailed severities and overdispersed frequency distributions. The comparison is conducted on a standardised test battery of 24 frequency–severity combinations covering Poisson and negative binomial counts paired with lognormal, Pareto, and GPD severities, with tail parameters spanning from light to very heavy. Accuracy is measured relative to a high-precision reference obtained with 10 million Monte Carlo draws. FFT with discretisation step 100 EUR and grid size 2^20 achieves relative errors below 0.5% at the 99th percentile across all test cases in median CPU time of 0.8 seconds. Panjer recursion is accurate for Poisson–lognormal but fails to converge for heavy GPD tails. Monte Carlo with 100 000 draws achieves acceptable accuracy only above the 95th percentile. Practical guidance for practitioners choosing among methods is provided.

SYN-PUB-05084.title: Operational Risk Disclosure and Cyber Incident Reporting Under the DORA Framework: Implications for Loss Data Quality in EU Banks
SYN-PUB-05084.text:
Operational Risk Disclosure and Cyber Incident Reporting Under the DORA Framework: Implications for Loss Data Quality in EU Banks (2025, journal, Regulation and Risk in European Banking).
Authors: Ana Vinković (outside co-author); Radovan Petrović (outside co-author); Tamás Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422).
Keywords: DORA; ICT incident reporting; loss data quality; cyber risk taxonomy; EU regulatory compliance.
The EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) introduces mandatory ICT-related incident reporting for financial entities from January 2025. This paper analyses the expected impact of DORA reporting requirements on the quality and coverage of cyber loss datasets used to parameterise LDA models. Drawing on a survey of 31 risk and compliance officers at banks in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Croatia conducted in late 2023, the paper documents current internal classification and reporting practices and identifies misalignments with DORA's taxonomy of significant cyber incidents. Simulation experiments show that under DORA-compliant reporting, the number of recordable cyber loss events per bank is expected to increase by a median factor of 2.7 relative to current Basel AMA/SMA thresholds, substantially reducing the excess-zero problem documented in earlier literature. The paper discusses transition challenges for non-EU countries with close financial links to the EU, including Serbia, and recommends adoption of compatible reporting standards by the National Bank of Serbia.

SYN-PUB-05085.title: Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms
SYN-PUB-05085.text:
Tail Risk Estimation for Cloud Service Outage Losses: A Spliced Distribution Approach with Application to Serbian Fintech Firms (2026, preprint, Preprint, SSRN Working Paper Series).
Authors: Nikola Savić (outside co-author); Milica Đorđević (outside co-author); Attila Bálint (R0422); Rita Bálint (R0970); Emilija Ostojić (R0671).
Keywords: spliced distribution; cloud outage; generalised Pareto; fintech; business interruption.
Cloud service outages generate bimodal loss profiles: a large mass of short, low-cost interruptions and a thin tail of prolonged outages with severe financial consequences. This paper fits spliced distributions combining a gamma body with a generalised Pareto tail to hourly downtime cost data collected from 19 fintech firms operating in Serbia between 2021 and 2024, yielding 2 641 outage episodes. The splice point is selected by minimising the integrated squared error between the empirical CDF and the fitted spliced distribution, resulting in an optimal threshold at the 87th empirical percentile. The GPD shape parameter governing the tail is estimated at 0.38 (95% CI: 0.21–0.55), confirming heavy-tail behaviour. Annual aggregate loss distributions are constructed via compound Poisson simulation. The 99th-percentile annual outage loss for a median-sized firm is estimated at EUR 180 000, with high sensitivity to the GPD shape parameter. Results inform cloud resilience investment decisions and business interruption insurance structuring for the fintech sector.

SYN-PUB-05322.title: A rule-based controller for wire feed speed adjustment driven by real-time pool width feedback in robotic GMAW
SYN-PUB-05322.text:
A rule-based controller for wire feed speed adjustment driven by real-time pool width feedback in robotic GMAW (2013, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Valentina Simić (R0445); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Bojan Tanasić (outside co-author).
Keywords: adaptive control; wire feed speed; structured light; weld pool width; robotic GMAW; rule-based controller.
A rule-based adaptive controller is presented that adjusts wire feed speed (WFS) in real-time based on weld pool width measurements obtained from a structured-light stripe projected ahead of the arc. The controller uses 11 if-then rules relating measured pool width deviation from a target value to incremental WFS changes, with anti-windup logic to prevent oscillation during gap variations. Experiments on 6 mm fillet welds on S235 steel demonstrated that, compared to constant-parameter welding, the controller reduced width standard deviation from 0.83 mm to 0.31 mm and underfill defect frequency from 14 % to 3 % across a 200-run trial. The structured-light projector and camera assembly added 210 ms of processing latency, which is discussed in the context of travel speed limits for practical deployment on a six-axis manipulator.

SYN-PUB-05325.title: Structured-light sensing of weld pool geometry: accuracy assessment on moving arc applications
SYN-PUB-05325.text:
Structured-light sensing of weld pool geometry: accuracy assessment on moving arc applications (2017, conference, Measurement Science and Engineering Proceedings (Central European Manufacturing Conference, Brno)).
Authors: Valentina Simić (R0445); Luboš Hrubý (outside co-author); Katarina Belić (outside co-author).
Keywords: structured light; weld pool geometry; optical sensing; GMAW; accuracy assessment.
Structured-light triangulation is a candidate sensing technique for closed-loop weld pool geometry control, but its accuracy in the dynamic environment of a moving arc has not been thoroughly characterised. This paper presents a dedicated accuracy assessment using a high-speed camera (2000 fps) to track a laser stripe projected onto the pool surface during GMAW at travel speeds of 3–8 mm/s. A reference weld pool geometry was established by interrupted-arc cross-sections. Pool width was estimated within ±0.4 mm and length within ±0.6 mm under conditions where arc flash was adequately filtered by a 660 nm bandpass filter. At travel speeds above 6 mm/s, periodic arc instability introduced dropout events in 7 % of frames, for which a linear interpolation recovery strategy is described. The paper includes a practical guide to filter selection and stripe wavelength choice.

SYN-PUB-05326.title: Adaptive control of GMAW for thin-walled aluminium assemblies subject to progressive fixture compliance loss
SYN-PUB-05326.text:
Adaptive control of GMAW for thin-walled aluminium assemblies subject to progressive fixture compliance loss (2018, journal, Journal of Materials Processing Technology).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Đuro Simić (R0593); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author); Valentina Simić (R0445).
Keywords: aluminium welding; GMAW; adaptive control; thin-walled structures; fixture compliance; arc voltage.
Thin-walled aluminium structures lose clamping force progressively during welding due to thermal expansion, which alters fit-up gap and contact with the fixture heat sink. This study develops an adaptive control strategy in which arc voltage and WFS are adjusted every 0.5 s based on measured changes in pool width and arc electrical signatures. Twelve test assemblies made from 2 mm AA6082-T4 sheets were welded under controlled compliance loss simulated by calibrated spring-loaded fixtures. Under constant-parameter welding, 38 % of assemblies showed burn-through or incomplete fusion in the later portions of the seam. With the adaptive controller active, the defect rate dropped to 8 %. Electrical signal features, specifically arc voltage variance over 50 ms windows, were found to be early indicators of gap increase, with a 120 ms lead time relative to visible pool width change.

SYN-PUB-05331.title: Thermal boundary condition estimation from weld electrical signals: a Kalman filter approach
SYN-PUB-05331.text:
Thermal boundary condition estimation from weld electrical signals: a Kalman filter approach (2025, journal, International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer).
Authors: Valentina Simić (R0445); Ivana Đorđević (outside co-author); Radu Munteanu (outside co-author); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: Kalman filter; thermal boundary condition; heat-transfer coefficient; GMAW; state estimation; adaptive control.
Knowledge of the effective thermal boundary condition at the workpiece—determined by fixture contact, clamping force, and underlying structure—is rarely available directly in production but strongly influences weld quality. This paper presents a Kalman filter-based observer that estimates an effective heat-transfer coefficient at the workpiece underside from arc voltage, current, and wire feed rate measurements recorded during welding, using a reduced-order thermal model as the process model. The observer was validated on 48 welds where ground-truth heat-transfer coefficients were set by controlled air-gap fixtures with known thermal resistance. Estimated coefficients fell within 12 % of ground truth in 40 of 48 cases. The observer converged within the first 80 mm of weld length. Integration with a travel-speed adaptive controller demonstrated a 31 % reduction in penetration variability compared to a controller operating without boundary condition estimates.

SYN-PUB-05425.title: Latency and Throughput of ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in a Constrained TLS 1.3 Handshake Over LoRaWAN
SYN-PUB-05425.text:
Latency and Throughput of ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in a Constrained TLS 1.3 Handshake Over LoRaWAN (2026, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Stefan Gruber (outside co-author); Aleksandar Popović (outside co-author); Nebojša Ristić (R0454); Svetlana Kapor (R1033); Luca Bonfiglio (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: ML-DSA; SLH-DSA; TLS 1.3; LoRaWAN; IoT handshake latency.
LoRaWAN networks impose strict duty-cycle limits and maximum payload sizes (typically 51–242 bytes depending on spreading factor), making a standard TLS 1.3 handshake with post-quantum signatures highly problematic. We prototype a fragment-reassembly layer that segments ML-DSA-44 and SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s certificates and signature payloads across multiple LoRaWAN frames and measure end-to-end handshake completion time and energy on an STM32WL55 running at SF9 with BW125. ML-DSA-44 requires 38 uplink frames for a full handshake (certificate chain of one leaf and one intermediate), completing in 112 seconds under EU868 duty-cycle regulations; SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s requires 61 frames and 181 seconds. For comparison, a classical ECDSA P-256 handshake requires 9 frames and 26 seconds. We quantify the trade-off between quantum security and network overhead and propose a certificate compression scheme that reduces ML-DSA-44 frame count to 27 with no loss of security. Results are validated on a physical three-node LoRaWAN testbed using a Semtech SX1262 gateway.

SYN-PUB-05474.title: Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates
SYN-PUB-05474.text:
Combining CRF Sequence Labelling with Spatial Context Features for Field Extraction in Inspection Certificates (2016, journal, Journal of Information Science and Engineering).
Authors: Tatjana Sremčević (outside co-author); Predrag Ljubojević (R0460); Nikola Grujičić (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484).
Keywords: conditional random fields; sequence labelling; field extraction; inspection certificates; spatial features.
Inspection certificates issued by accredited testing laboratories follow loose conventions but no single fixed template. This work treats field extraction as a sequence labelling problem over sorted text tokens, augmented with spatial features derived from each token's bounding box and its nearest neighbours. A conditional random field model is trained on 1,100 annotated inspection certificates and evaluated on a held-out set of 275 certificates from laboratories not represented in training. The feature set includes token geometry, font-size estimates from bounding-box height, relative page position, left-margin alignment, and the label of the spatially closest token. Adding spatial context features raised per-field extraction accuracy from 72.3 % to 83.7 % compared with a purely sequential baseline. Error analysis identified measurement units as the most frequently mislabelled token class. The trained model is integrated into a prototype pipeline, and processing throughput of 8.4 certificates per second is reported on a standard 2014-era server.

SYN-PUB-05533.title: Adequacy of EN 50160 flicker compatibility levels for high-utilisation arc furnace industrial parks: a data-driven review
SYN-PUB-05533.text:
Adequacy of EN 50160 flicker compatibility levels for high-utilisation arc furnace industrial parks: a data-driven review (2026, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Jovana Nikolić (outside co-author); Andrei Moldovan (outside co-author); Ágnes Varró (outside co-author); Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Vesna Malešević (R0465); Nenad Ćirić (outside co-author).
Keywords: EN 50160; compatibility levels; Plt; industrial parks; arc furnace; grid code review.
EN 50160 sets a compatibility level of Plt ≤ 1.0 at medium-voltage public supply points, but industrial parks with dense arc furnace installation may structurally exceed this level during peak production periods. This paper assembles a database of 37 site-years of class-A power quality monitoring data from seven industrial medium-voltage networks in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, all characterised by arc furnace loads with utilisation factors above 0.6. The database is used to evaluate the exceedance frequency of the Plt = 1.0 limit under current operating conditions and to estimate how tightening or relaxing the limit would change the fraction of compliant sites. The analysis shows that 5 of 7 sites exceed Plt = 1.0 for more than 5% of weekly observation periods, making compliance formally unachievable without mitigation investment. The paper discusses the appropriateness of the single compatibility level for mixed public–industrial networks and proposes a differentiated limit framework analogous to the approach used in IEC 61000-3-7.

SYN-PUB-05579.title: A dynamic payback model for industrial symbiosis investments subject to tenant turnover in manufacturing parks
SYN-PUB-05579.text:
A dynamic payback model for industrial symbiosis investments subject to tenant turnover in manufacturing parks (2026, journal, International Journal of Production Economics and Industrial Systems).
Authors: Ivana Despotović (R0471); Aleksandra Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Sabo (R0859); Bence Varga (outside co-author); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: dynamic payback model; tenant turnover; discrete-event simulation; contract length; manufacturing park management.
Manufacturing parks experience tenant turnover — firms leaving or entering — that can alter the economic basis of symbiosis configurations mid-project. Standard static payback models do not capture this dynamic. This paper proposes a discrete-event simulation model in which tenant arrivals and departures are modelled as stochastic processes calibrated to observed turnover rates in 12 Serbian and Hungarian manufacturing parks over a 10-year period. The simulation generates distributions of payback periods under different turnover rate assumptions and contract length scenarios. Median payback periods under observed turnover rates are 1.4 to 2.8 years longer than static model estimates. The model identifies a critical contract length — the minimum binding term required to maintain positive NPV in 90% of simulated scenarios — which ranges from 5 to 9 years depending on the exchange type and number of participating firms. Practical guidance for park management on lease structuring is provided.

SYN-PUB-05667.title: High-Resolution Frost Risk Index for Vineyards in the Srem and Fruška Gora Wine Region
SYN-PUB-05667.text:
High-Resolution Frost Risk Index for Vineyards in the Srem and Fruška Gora Wine Region (2016, journal, Journal of Viticulture and Precision Agriculture).
Authors: Predrag Stojanović (outside co-author); Milena Nedić (R1023); Ingrid Mezei (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Anna Turčanová (R0480).
Keywords: frost risk; viticulture; cold-air drainage; MODIS; Fruška Gora.
Late spring frost events (April–May) are a primary yield-limiting factor for viticulture in the Srem and Fruška Gora region. A spatial frost risk index (FRI) was developed by combining downscaled minimum temperature grids at 250 m resolution, topographic cold-air drainage indices derived from a 25 m DEM, and 22 years of phenological records from 14 commercial vineyards. Minimum temperature was downscaled from a 2 km gridded product using a local lapse-rate correction and a cold-air-pooling factor estimated from nighttime MODIS LST anomalies. FRI was defined as the probability that minimum temperature falls below −1 °C during the period 15 April–20 May. Maps produced at the parcel scale (0.5 ha) showed risk differentiation of up to 35 percentage points across elevation bands as narrow as 40 m, consistent with growers' empirical observations. The index was validated against three independent frost event records with an accuracy of 81 %.

SYN-PUB-05706.title: Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study
SYN-PUB-05706.text:
Class Imbalance in Serbian Administrative Court Decisions: A Baseline Study (2014, journal, Journal of Information and Organizational Sciences).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: class imbalance; administrative courts; Serbian legal corpus; text classification; baseline.
Administrative court rulings in Serbia exhibit a pronounced class imbalance: approximately 78% of decisions in a collected corpus of 3,400 documents belong to a single outcome category. This paper documents the construction of that corpus, covering rulings from 2005 to 2012, and evaluates five standard classifiers—naive Bayes, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, and SVM—under original class distributions. F1-scores for minority classes fall below 0.21 across all methods when no resampling is applied. The paper analyses the linguistic and structural features most predictive of outcome, including citation patterns and procedural section length. Results serve as a reproducible baseline for subsequent resampling and augmentation experiments. All preprocessing code and anonymised metadata are released alongside the paper. The study intentionally avoids resampling or cost-sensitive learning so that future work can quantify gains relative to a clean reference point.

SYN-PUB-05707.title: Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification
SYN-PUB-05707.text:
Back-Translation as Data Augmentation for Low-Resource Legal Sentence Classification (2018, conference, Proceedings of the Language Technologies and Digital Humanities Conference).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Petra Horvat (outside co-author); Gregor Vidmar (outside co-author).
Keywords: back-translation; data augmentation; legal NLP; multilingual BERT; low-resource.
Legal sentence classification in low-resource Slavic languages is constrained by the scarcity of annotated data and the domain specificity of vocabulary. This paper investigates back-translation—translating Serbian sentences to English and back—as an augmentation strategy for a sentence-level dataset of 1,120 annotated clauses from civil procedure documents. Three translation pipelines are tested using freely available neural machine translation models, and the round-trip fidelity of legal terminology is measured against a manually curated glossary of 340 terms. Back-translation preserves legal term identity in 74% of cases for the best pipeline. Augmented training sets are used with a fine-tuned multilingual BERT model, yielding a macro F1 of 0.68 compared to 0.59 on the original data. Error analysis reveals that procedural verbs suffer the highest mistranslation rate, suggesting domain-adaptive fine-tuning of the translation component as a future direction. The dataset and annotation guidelines are publicly available.

SYN-PUB-05708.title: Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus
SYN-PUB-05708.text:
Transfer Learning from General Croatian–Serbian Legal Texts to a Specialised Serbian Labour-Law Corpus (2020, journal, Informatica: An International Journal of Computing and Informatics).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Nikola Supić (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; domain adaptation; labour law; intermediate pretraining; Croatian Serbian.
Transformer-based language models pretrained on large general corpora require substantial fine-tuning data to adapt to specialised legal domains. This paper examines whether intermediate pretraining on a moderately sized Croatian–Serbian legal text collection (approximately 120,000 sentences from publicly accessible legislation and court decisions) improves downstream performance on a Serbian labour-law classification task with only 640 training examples. Four model variants are compared: multilingual BERT with no intermediate pretraining, the same model with intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus, and two models pretrained on each national subset separately. Intermediate pretraining on the combined corpus achieves the best macro F1 (0.72) on a held-out test set of 160 examples, surpassing the no-pretraining baseline by 0.11. Differences between the Croatian-only and Serbian-only intermediate pretraining conditions are modest, suggesting that vocabulary overlap rather than syntactic similarity drives the gain. Computational cost and practical guidance for reproducing the pipeline on limited hardware are discussed.

SYN-PUB-05709.title: Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models
SYN-PUB-05709.text:
Predicting Sequences of Procedural Outcomes in Serbian Civil Litigation Using Recurrent Models (2021, journal, Expert Systems with Applications).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author); Eszter Fábián (outside co-author).
Keywords: judicial sequence prediction; LSTM; GRU; focal loss; civil litigation.
Civil litigation in Serbia often involves multiple procedural stages, and the outcome of each stage influences the distribution of subsequent outcomes. This paper frames judicial decision sequences as a temporal classification problem and evaluates three recurrent architectures—vanilla RNN, LSTM, and GRU—on a dataset of 2,180 complete case trajectories spanning first instance, appeal, and revision stages. Each stage is represented by a combination of extracted text features and structured metadata (case type, duration, court tier). The dataset is severely imbalanced at the revision stage, where case types eligible for revision constitute only 9% of trajectories. Weighted cross-entropy and focal loss are compared as training objectives. The GRU with focal loss achieves a macro F1 of 0.61 at the revision stage, compared to 0.43 for weighted cross-entropy. Sequence length and court tier are identified as the strongest non-textual predictors via ablation. Limitations related to data availability outside the University's legal informatics collaboration are discussed.

SYN-PUB-05710.title: A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets
SYN-PUB-05710.text:
A Survey of Synthetic Data Generation Methods for Small Legal Datasets (2022, book chapter, Advances in Legal Informatics: Methods, Systems, and Applications (edited volume, Springer)).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Ruxandra Ionescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: synthetic data; data generation; legal NLP; survey; evaluation.
The application of machine learning to legal tasks is frequently limited by small annotated corpora and ethical constraints on data sharing. This chapter surveys methods for generating synthetic legal data, covering rule-based paraphrasing, conditional language model generation, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks adapted to text. For each method the chapter describes the underlying mechanism, summarises reported performance on legal benchmarks from the literature, and lists known failure modes, such as hallucinated case citations and vocabulary drift in conditional generation. Special attention is given to evaluation protocols, since standard NLP metrics such as BLEU and perplexity do not capture the legal validity of generated texts. The chapter concludes with a decision framework helping practitioners choose a generation strategy based on available corpus size, annotation type, and downstream task. Thirty-seven papers published between 2015 and 2022 are reviewed.

SYN-PUB-05711.title: Conditional GPT-2 Fine-Tuning for Minority-Class Augmentation in a Small Serbian Court Decision Dataset
SYN-PUB-05711.text:
Conditional GPT-2 Fine-Tuning for Minority-Class Augmentation in a Small Serbian Court Decision Dataset (2023, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Science).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ana Lukić (outside co-author); Slobodan Krstić (outside co-author).
Keywords: GPT-2; conditional generation; augmentation; administrative courts; expert evaluation.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-05712.title: Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks
SYN-PUB-05712.text:
Cost-Sensitive Learning vs. Resampling: A Controlled Comparison on Four Serbian Legal Classification Tasks (2024, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems).
Authors: Jovan Puzović (R0484); Ognjen Malešević (R0987); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Eszter Fábián (outside co-author); Ruxandra Ionescu (outside co-author); Nikola Supić (outside co-author).
Keywords: cost-sensitive learning; resampling; focal loss; imbalance ratio; benchmarking.
Practitioners addressing class imbalance must choose between modifying the training objective and modifying the training set, but systematic comparisons on legal text data are rare. This paper applies seven resampling strategies (random oversampling, random undersampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and two hybrid methods) and four cost-sensitive objectives (weighted cross-entropy, focal loss, asymmetric loss, and class-balanced softmax) to four Serbian legal classification tasks drawn from administrative, civil, criminal, and labour law subdomains. Corpus sizes range from 412 to 2,180 documents and imbalance ratios from 1:4 to 1:19. Results show no single strategy dominates across tasks; cost-sensitive objectives outperform resampling on the two smallest datasets, while hybrid resampling performs better on the two larger corpora. Statistical significance is assessed with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across cross-validation folds. The paper provides a reproducible experimental framework and releases all task-specific evaluation scripts.

SYN-PUB-05713.title: Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics
SYN-PUB-05713.text:
Annotated corpus of Serbian electrical maintenance texts: construction methodology and baseline statistics (2016, conference, Language Resources and Evaluation Conference for South-East European Languages (LREC-SEEL)).
Authors: Maja Ristić (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Jovan Puzović (R0484); Vukica Ognjanov (R0979); Andrei Popescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: corpus construction; named entity recognition; annotation; Serbian NLP; maintenance texts.
Reliable named entity recognition and relation extraction in the power-systems maintenance domain require annotated corpora that reflect the vocabulary and writing style of field personnel. This paper describes the construction of a 9,800-sentence corpus drawn from work orders, inspection reports, and incident summaries produced by two Serbian electricity distribution companies between 2008 and 2014. Annotation guidelines were defined to cover four entity types—equipment identifier, fault descriptor, location reference, and repair action—and two relation types: fault-equipment and action-equipment. A team of four annotators, including two electrical engineers and two computational linguists, performed the labelling using the BRAT annotation tool. Final inter-annotator kappa values ranged from 0.68 to 0.79 depending on entity type. The corpus contains 47,000 entity mentions and 31,000 labelled relation instances. Baseline results using a CRF tagger are reported, with an F1 of 0.73 for fault descriptors, which proved the most variable category. The corpus is released under a restricted-access licence pending operator approval.

SYN-PUB-05914.title: Side-Channel Leakage in AES Implementations on 8-Bit AVR Microcontrollers: A Comparative Power Analysis Study
SYN-PUB-05914.text:
Side-Channel Leakage in AES Implementations on 8-Bit AVR Microcontrollers: A Comparative Power Analysis Study (2011, journal, Journal of Embedded Systems and Security Research).
Authors: Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: AES; differential power analysis; AVR microcontroller; side-channel attack; masking.
This paper evaluates the susceptibility of three publicly available AES-128 software implementations to simple and differential power analysis on an 8-bit AVR ATmega328P microcontroller. We collected 50,000 power traces per implementation using a 1 GHz digital oscilloscope and a 1-ohm shunt resistor, then applied standard DPA with a Hamming-weight model. All three implementations leaked the full 128-bit key within 10,000 traces; the fastest implementation (executing in 4,112 clock cycles) proved most vulnerable, with a signal-to-noise ratio 2.3 times higher than the most compact one. Countermeasures including boolean masking and shuffled S-box lookups were applied and re-evaluated; masking reduced the distinguishability metric by 87% at the cost of a 34% increase in execution time. The results provide a quantitative baseline for hardening AES on severely constrained nodes, directly informing subsequent work on post-quantum primitives for similar platforms.

SYN-PUB-05915.title: Benchmarking SHA-3 Candidates on ARM Cortex-M3: Cycle Counts, Stack Usage, and Energy Consumption
SYN-PUB-05915.text:
Benchmarking SHA-3 Candidates on ARM Cortex-M3: Cycle Counts, Stack Usage, and Energy Consumption (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Cryptology and Information Security (CECCIS)).
Authors: Aleksandar Popović (outside co-author); Ivana Žugić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: SHA-3; hash functions; ARM Cortex-M3; energy measurement; embedded benchmarking.
We ported and benchmarked five finalist and alternate candidates from the NIST SHA-3 competition—Keccak, Skein-512, Grøstl, BLAKE, and JH—on an ARM Cortex-M3 running at 72 MHz with 20 kB of SRAM. For each candidate we measured clock cycles per byte for message lengths of 64, 256, and 4096 bytes, peak stack consumption, and energy drawn from a 3.3 V supply using a precision current sensor. Keccak achieved the lowest energy per byte (1.14 µJ for 256-byte messages) but consumed the most stack (3,584 bytes). BLAKE offered the best throughput at 15.2 cycles/byte for long messages. Grøstl was slowest on this architecture due to poor utilisation of 32-bit word operations. The dataset is publicly archived and intended to serve as a reference for designers selecting hash functions for sensor node firmware, and as a comparison point for future post-quantum scheme evaluations that rely on these primitives.

SYN-PUB-05916.title: Memory-Efficient Polynomial Multiplication for NTRU on a 32-Bit Microcontroller
SYN-PUB-05916.text:
Memory-Efficient Polynomial Multiplication for NTRU on a 32-Bit Microcontroller (2015, journal, Journal of Embedded Systems and Security Research).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Petr Novotný (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: NTRU; polynomial multiplication; NTT; Cortex-M3; post-quantum cryptography.
NTRU encryption requires repeated polynomial multiplication in truncated polynomial rings, and naïve convolution is prohibitively slow on constrained hardware. This work implements and compares three multiplication strategies—schoolbook convolution, Karatsuba decomposition, and a Number Theoretic Transform adapted to NTRU parameters—on an STM32F103 Cortex-M3 running at 72 MHz with 20 kB RAM. The NTT approach requires 512 bytes of working memory for degree-509 polynomials and achieves 148,000 clock cycles per multiplication, compared to 1.92 million for schoolbook convolution. Karatsuba occupies a middle ground at 340,000 cycles with minimal stack overhead. Code size across all three variants was kept below 8 kB of flash. We profile the full NTRU-HPS key-generation and encapsulation routines and show that NTT-based multiplication reduces total encapsulation time from 28.4 ms to 4.1 ms at 72 MHz. The implementation is validated against known test vectors from the NTRU reference package.

SYN-PUB-05917.title: Practical Fault Injection Attacks Against a Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism on a Smart Card
SYN-PUB-05917.text:
Practical Fault Injection Attacks Against a Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism on a Smart Card (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Attacks and Solutions in Hardware Security (WASH)).
Authors: Luca Bonfiglio (outside co-author); Srđan Matić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: Kyber; fault injection; smart card; voltage glitching; key encapsulation.
We investigate the fault resilience of a software implementation of Kyber-512 running on a Java Card 3.0.4 smart card with an ARM SC300 security core. Using a voltage glitching station with sub-microsecond pulse resolution, we injected faults during the decapsulation procedure and collected 6,800 faulty ciphertexts over three days of automated testing. By applying a variant of the decryption failure attack, we recovered 128-bit session keys from 42% of successful fault injections within a single-bit error model. We further show that a simple instruction-count check at the end of the decapsulation loop detects 91% of our glitch attempts with zero false positives in 5,000 benign runs. The results indicate that Kyber implementations on real smart card hardware need explicit fault countermeasures beyond those assumed in the formal security proofs, and we propose a concrete software hardening checklist derived from our observations.

SYN-PUB-05919.title: Comparing CRYSTALS-Dilithium and Falcon Signature Verification Speed on ARM Cortex-M4
SYN-PUB-05919.text:
Comparing CRYSTALS-Dilithium and Falcon Signature Verification Speed on ARM Cortex-M4 (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Cryptology and Information Security (CECCIS)).
Authors: Bogdan Petrescu (outside co-author); Jelena Vasić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: CRYSTALS-Dilithium; Falcon; ARM Cortex-M4; signature verification; benchmarking.
We implement the NIST post-quantum signature finalists CRYSTALS-Dilithium (security levels 2 and 3) and Falcon-512 in C with platform-specific assembly optimisations for the ARM Cortex-M4 FPU on an STM32F407 board running at 168 MHz. Dilithium-2 verification takes 1.37 ms and requires 13.2 kB of stack; Dilithium-3 requires 1.89 ms and 16.8 kB. Falcon-512 verification takes 2.11 ms but requires only 7.4 kB of stack, making it preferable for devices with less than 10 kB SRAM. Signing is substantially more expensive for Falcon due to the discrete Gaussian sampler: 14.8 ms versus 3.2 ms for Dilithium-2. We also measure flash footprint and provide a side-by-side energy profile collected with a USB power monitor. All source code and raw trace data are released under a permissive open-source licence. The findings inform a practical selection guide for firmware engineers choosing between the two schemes.

SYN-PUB-05920.title: A Hardware Security Module Architecture Supporting Hybrid Classical/Post-Quantum Key Exchange for Industrial Controllers
SYN-PUB-05920.text:
A Hardware Security Module Architecture Supporting Hybrid Classical/Post-Quantum Key Exchange for Industrial Controllers (2020, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics – Special Section on Industrial Cyber-Physical Security).
Authors: Igor Lukač (outside co-author); Florian Krieger (outside co-author); Zoran Antonić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: hardware security module; Kyber; hybrid key exchange; industrial control systems; FPGA.
This paper describes the design and prototyping of a hardware security module intended for attachment to programmable logic controllers in industrial automation environments. The HSM combines an Infineon SLE97 secure microcontroller for classical ECDH key agreement with a separate FPGA fabric (Lattice iCE40UP5K) dedicated to Kyber-768 key encapsulation. The hybrid design ensures backward compatibility while adding quantum resistance. We detail the inter-chip communication protocol, a SPI-based command interface with authenticated encryption, and the key storage layout. Full key exchange (hybrid ECDH + Kyber-768) completes in 38 ms end-to-end. The FPGA implementation of Kyber uses 3,200 LUTs and 12 kB of embedded block RAM. Power consumption during key exchange peaks at 210 mW and averages 42 mW at idle. We evaluate the design against the IEC 62443-4-2 security level 2 requirements and identify three areas requiring further hardening before production deployment.

SYN-PUB-05921.title: Stack and Heap Memory Profiling of SPHINCS+ on RISC-V RV32IMC Without Hardware Multiplier
SYN-PUB-05921.text:
Stack and Heap Memory Profiling of SPHINCS+ on RISC-V RV32IMC Without Hardware Multiplier (2021, journal, Journal of Cryptographic Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: SPHINCS+; hash-based signatures; RISC-V; memory profiling; stack optimisation.
SPHINCS+ is a stateless hash-based signature scheme selected for standardisation by NIST, but its relatively large signature sizes and tree traversal operations raise questions about feasibility on severely memory-constrained RISC-V cores lacking the M (multiply) extension. We port all three SPHINCS+-SHA2 and SPHINCS+-SHAKE parameter sets to bare-metal RISC-V RV32I (without M extension) on a 32 kB RAM, 256 kB flash target and measure peak stack depth, heap allocation, code size, and cycle counts. Without a multiplier, SHA-256 compression function throughput drops by 6.1x compared to RV32IM. Signing with SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s (the smallest parameter set) requires 28.4 kB of stack and 1.84 billion cycles, which is infeasible for latency-sensitive applications at typical MHz clock rates but acceptable for infrequent firmware update signing. We propose a streaming tree-node computation that reduces peak stack to 11.2 kB at a 9% cycle overhead, and validate correctness against the NIST Known Answer Tests.

SYN-PUB-05922.title: Timing Variability in Constant-Time Dilithium Implementations Across Different Compiler Optimisation Levels
SYN-PUB-05922.text:
Timing Variability in Constant-Time Dilithium Implementations Across Different Compiler Optimisation Levels (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Attacks and Solutions in Hardware Security (WASH)).
Authors: Karolina Wójcik (outside co-author); Jelena Vasić (outside co-author); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: CRYSTALS-Dilithium; constant-time; timing leakage; TVLA; compiler optimisation.
Lattice-based signature schemes such as CRYSTALS-Dilithium are typically written to be constant-time, but compiler optimisations can inadvertently introduce data-dependent timing variation by reordering or eliminating branchless constructs. We compile a reference Dilithium-2 implementation using GCC 11 and Clang 14 at optimisation levels O0 through O3 and Os on ARM Cortex-M4 and x86-64, then measure timing distributions for 100,000 signing operations with message inputs sampled uniformly at random. At O3 with GCC on x86-64, we observe a 14-cycle bimodal spread in the rejection sampling loop that correlates weakly (Pearson r = 0.19) with the norm of the signing randomness. Leakage detection using Welch's t-test and TVLA methodology crosses the threshold of |t| = 4.5 in three of eight compiler/architecture combinations. We trace each instance to specific compiler transformations visible in the generated assembly and propose source-level annotations (using the volatile barrier idiom) that suppress the leakage in all tested configurations.

SYN-PUB-05923.title: Towards a Standardised Benchmarking Suite for Post-Quantum Cryptography on Embedded Targets
SYN-PUB-05923.text:
Towards a Standardised Benchmarking Suite for Post-Quantum Cryptography on Embedded Targets (2023, journal, ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems).
Authors: Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author); Thibault Marin (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Bogdan Petrescu (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: benchmarking suite; post-quantum cryptography; embedded targets; reproducibility; methodology.
Comparing published implementation results for post-quantum schemes is difficult because researchers use different clock frequencies, compiler flags, measurement methods, and reporting conventions. This paper proposes a minimal benchmarking suite—PQBench-Embed—that specifies four representative hardware targets (ARM Cortex-M0+, Cortex-M4, RISC-V RV32IMC, and ESP32), a fixed GCC toolchain version and flag set, a cycle-counting harness based on hardware performance counters, and a structured JSON output format for result reporting. We validate the suite by collecting results for Kyber-512, Dilithium-2, Falcon-512, SPHINCS+-SHA2-128s, and Classic McEliece 348864 across all four targets. Results show that cross-architecture speedup ratios for the same algorithm vary by up to 3.1x depending on benchmarking methodology, confirming the need for standardisation. The suite and all collected data are released as a public repository. We also provide a discussion of what metrics matter most for different deployment scenarios such as TLS handshake, firmware signing, and device attestation.

SYN-PUB-05924.title: Power Consumption of ML-DSA (FIPS 204) Across Dilithium Security Levels on a Common Criteria EAL5+ Secure Element
SYN-PUB-05924.text:
Power Consumption of ML-DSA (FIPS 204) Across Dilithium Security Levels on a Common Criteria EAL5+ Secure Element (2024, journal, Journal of Cryptographic Engineering).
Authors: Igor Lukač (outside co-author); Valentina Greco (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: ML-DSA; FIPS 204; secure element; power analysis; PQC migration.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-05925.title: Cache-Timing Attacks on ML-KEM (FIPS 203) in a Shared-Memory Embedded RTOS Environment
SYN-PUB-05925.text:
Cache-Timing Attacks on ML-KEM (FIPS 203) in a Shared-Memory Embedded RTOS Environment (2025, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Secure Computing Systems (ISCS)).
Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Karolina Wójcik (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503).
Keywords: ML-KEM; cache-timing; FreeRTOS; side-channel; Cortex-M7.
Embedded real-time operating systems increasingly run multiple isolated tasks sharing a common data cache, creating conditions for cache-timing side channels even on microcontrollers. We study ML-KEM (FIPS 203, formerly Kyber) running as a FreeRTOS task on an STM32H743 Cortex-M7 with a 16 kB 4-way set-associative L1 data cache and a co-resident adversarial task with unprivileged access. Using a Prime+Probe variant adapted for the Cortex-M7 cache geometry, the adversary task collects 250,000 cache access measurements and applies a correlation distinguisher to the modular reduction tables. We recover 4 bits of the decapsulation secret with probability greater than 0.8, demonstrating a practical (though partial) leakage channel. We then evaluate three mitigations: cache-line aligned constant-time modular arithmetic, OS-level cache flushing between task switches, and disabling the data cache entirely. The last option increases ML-KEM decapsulation time from 0.31 ms to 1.87 ms and is impractical for most deployments, while aligned arithmetic eliminates the observed leakage with a 4% cycle overhead.

SYN-PUB-05927.title: Reinforcement Learning for Joint Offloading and Beam Selection in mmWave-Assisted IoT Edge Nodes
SYN-PUB-05927.text:
Reinforcement Learning for Joint Offloading and Beam Selection in mmWave-Assisted IoT Edge Nodes (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Wireless Communications and Networking (EWCN)).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Reinhilde Claes (outside co-author); Milica Nikolić (R0503); Ondřej Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: deep reinforcement learning; mmWave; beam selection; joint optimisation; edge IoT.
This paper investigates the use of a deep Q-network to simultaneously select beam directions and offloading fractions at mmWave-equipped edge nodes serving dense IoT clusters. A custom simulation environment is constructed in Python using ray tracing channel models parameterised for an indoor factory scenario at 28 GHz with 64-element ULA antennas. The agent observes local queue length, residual energy, and a coarse channel quality indicator quantised to four levels. Training uses 200,000 environment steps with an experience replay buffer of 10,000 transitions. The learned policy achieves a 28% reduction in energy-per-bit compared to a heuristic that handles beam selection and offloading independently, and maintains queue stability at arrival rates up to 85% of channel capacity. Ablation experiments show that joint optimisation accounts for most of the gain over independent control.

SYN-PUB-05935.title: Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach
SYN-PUB-05935.text:
Optimising corona-discharge parameters for heterogeneous recycled packaging boards using a response-surface approach (2017, journal, Progress in Organic Coatings).
Authors: Miroslav Vujić (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Tomáš Novák (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504).
Keywords: response surface methodology; corona discharge; recycled board; process optimisation; ink adhesion variability.
Recycled packaging boards sourced from three European mills exhibited substantial variability in initial surface energy (28–37 mJ/m²) due to differing furnish compositions and coating histories. A central composite response-surface design with four factors (electrode gap 1–3 mm, line speed 50–150 m/min, power density 5–20 W·min/m², ambient humidity 30–65 % RH) was used to model total surface energy and polar component as responses. Forty-three experimental runs were performed. The quadratic model explained 88 % of variance in total surface energy; power density and electrode gap were the dominant factors, with a statistically significant interaction. A validated optimal treatment window (gap 1.5 mm, 12 W·min/m², 40–55 % RH) yielded total surface energy ≥ 50 mJ/m² across all three board grades, reducing within-batch variability in ink adhesion peel force from ± 0.9 N/cm to ± 0.3 N/cm.

SYN-PUB-05944.title: Residence time effects on fixed-bed pyrolysis of corn stover: product distribution and energy balance
SYN-PUB-05944.text:
Residence time effects on fixed-bed pyrolysis of corn stover: product distribution and energy balance (2015, journal, Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis).
Authors: Nemanja Ilić (outside co-author); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author); Péter Balogh (outside co-author); Sanja Lukić (R0504); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992).
Keywords: corn stover; residence time; fixed-bed pyrolysis; bio-oil; energy balance.
A parametric study was conducted in a bench-scale fixed-bed reactor using milled corn stover (particle size 0.5–1.0 mm, moisture 8.3 wt%) at 500 °C with residence times of 15, 30, 60, and 120 minutes. Gas, liquid (bio-oil), and solid (biochar) product fractions were gravimetrically quantified. At 15 min, biochar yield was 32.4% and bio-oil 38.1%; extending residence time to 120 min reduced biochar yield marginally to 29.6% while increasing non-condensable gas fraction from 18.2 to 24.5 wt%. Bio-oil higher heating value ranged from 16.8 to 18.3 MJ kg⁻¹. An energy balance across the reactor showed that the char fraction retained 38–44% of feedstock energy regardless of residence time, whereas extended holding increased secondary cracking of bio-oil vapours. Recommendations for process optimisation targeting simultaneous biochar and syngas valorisation are presented.
