SYN-PUB-06094.title: Influence of Residual Stress on the Natural Frequencies of Welded Steel Frame Members
SYN-PUB-06094.text:
Influence of Residual Stress on the Natural Frequencies of Welded Steel Frame Members (2021, journal, Journal of Constructional Steel Research and Diagnostics).
Authors: Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Zoran Aćimović (outside co-author); Borislav Bogdanović (R0518).
Keywords: residual stress; hole-drilling; stress relief annealing; geometric stiffness; FE model.
Residual stresses induced by welding alter geometric stiffness and thereby affect natural frequencies of frame members. This study quantifies the relationship using a combined experimental and finite-element approach. Residual stress profiles in twelve S355 steel beam specimens were measured by the hole-drilling method at five cross-sections per specimen; specimens were then tested for natural frequencies using impact hammer excitation before and after stress-relief annealing at 600 °C for two hours. Frequency increases of 0.8–2.3% were observed after annealing, depending on weld sequence and heat input. A 3D FE model incorporating measured residual stress fields as initial conditions reproduced the pre-annealing frequencies with a mean error of 1.1%. Parametric sensitivity analysis showed that longitudinal compressive residual stress near the weld toe exerted the strongest influence on the first bending frequency. The results imply that residual stress state should be accounted for when establishing SHM baselines for newly fabricated or repaired steel structures.

SYN-PUB-06151.title: A Comparative Study of Bilingual Lexicon Induction Methods for Serbian–Hungarian Word Pairs in Technical Domains
SYN-PUB-06151.text:
A Comparative Study of Bilingual Lexicon Induction Methods for Serbian–Hungarian Word Pairs in Technical Domains (2013, journal, Journal of Computational and Applied Linguistics (JCAL)).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Eszter Varga (outside co-author); Branislav Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: bilingual lexicon induction; word embeddings; Serbian; Hungarian; technical terminology.
Bilingual lexicon induction (BLI) without parallel corpora is particularly challenging for morphologically rich, closely situated language pairs. This study evaluates four BLI approaches—cross-lingual word embedding projection, iterative Procrustes alignment, VecMap, and a graph-based method—on Serbian–Hungarian word pairs sampled from three technical domains: civil engineering, agriculture, and information technology. Evaluation dictionaries containing 2,100 pairs per domain were assembled from terminological databases and validated by domain experts. Results show that iterative Procrustes alignment achieves the highest precision@1 (42.3%) on the IT domain, while graph-based methods perform better on agriculture (38.7% precision@1), where morphological regularity is lower. All methods degrade substantially on out-of-vocabulary compound terms. We release the three domain dictionaries and pre-trained fastText vectors fine-tuned on a 600 M token Serbian–Hungarian corpus.

SYN-PUB-06152.title: Cross-Lingual Named-Entity Linking Between Serbian and English News Corpora Using Wikipedia Anchors
SYN-PUB-06152.text:
Cross-Lingual Named-Entity Linking Between Serbian and English News Corpora Using Wikipedia Anchors (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Language Resources and Technologies Conference (BLRTC)).
Authors: Dragana Mirković (outside co-author); Mónika Papp (R0524); Tamás Fehér (outside co-author); Orsolya Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: named-entity linking; cross-lingual; Wikipedia; Serbian; news corpora.
Named-entity linking (NEL) across languages is complicated by transliteration variation, partial name translations, and entity ambiguity. We describe a system that links named entities in Serbian news articles to English Wikipedia entries using a combination of anchor text statistics, Wikidata cross-reference mappings, and string similarity features. We evaluated on a manually annotated dataset of 3,800 entity mentions drawn from four Serbian news portals, covering persons, organisations, and locations. The proposed system achieved a linking accuracy of 74.2% on persons and 68.9% on organisations, compared to 61.4% and 55.7% for a transliteration-only baseline. We analyse error categories and find that local public figures with sparse Wikipedia coverage account for roughly 40% of failures. The annotated mention dataset is made publicly available.

SYN-PUB-06153.title: Reconciling Duplicate Patient Records Across Hospital Systems: A Cross-Lingual Entity Matching Approach
SYN-PUB-06153.text:
Reconciling Duplicate Patient Records Across Hospital Systems: A Cross-Lingual Entity Matching Approach (2017, book chapter, Multilingual Data Management in Healthcare Information Systems, edited volume, IOS Press).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Zoran Petrović (outside co-author); Anita Hajdú (outside co-author).
Keywords: entity matching; health records; cross-lingual; data reconciliation; Serbian; Hungarian.
Electronic health record systems in multilingual regions often store patient and diagnostic data in different languages, leading to duplicate and conflicting records. This chapter presents a framework for cross-lingual entity matching of patient records in Serbian and Hungarian administrative data, using a combination of phonetic normalisation, transliteration, and fuzzy attribute matching. A prototype was developed and tested on a synthetic dataset of 10,000 record pairs generated from anonymised templates provided by a regional hospital administration. We define five match categories ranging from definite match to definite non-match and report precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.86 for the definite match category. The chapter discusses practical barriers including inconsistent date formats, name order conventions, and missing-field patterns common in legacy systems.

SYN-PUB-06154.title: Evaluating Multilingual Sentence Encoders on a Diverse Cross-Lingual Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark for South Slavic Languages
SYN-PUB-06154.text:
Evaluating Multilingual Sentence Encoders on a Diverse Cross-Lingual Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark for South Slavic Languages (2019, journal, Language Resources and Evaluation for Slavic Languages (LRESL), Special Issue, Journal of Slavic Computational Linguistics).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Marija Stjepanović (outside co-author); Luka Šimić (outside co-author); Tamás Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: semantic textual similarity; South Slavic languages; sentence encoders; benchmark; multilingual NLP.
Publicly available semantic textual similarity (STS) benchmarks rarely include South Slavic languages, making it difficult to evaluate multilingual encoder models in this region. We construct STS-SlaVoSe, a benchmark of 5,400 sentence pairs in Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, and Bosnian, covering six domains: news, legal texts, social media, scientific abstracts, product descriptions, and conversational transcripts. Each pair was annotated by three annotators on a 0–5 scale; inter-annotator Pearson correlation averaged 0.83. We evaluate eight publicly available multilingual sentence encoders including mBERT, XLM-R, LaBSE, and four smaller distilled variants. LaBSE achieves the highest average Pearson correlation (0.79) across all language–domain combinations, though performance varies markedly by domain: legal text pairs yield the lowest scores (0.61) across all models. We release the full benchmark under CC-BY-SA.

SYN-PUB-06155.title: Fine-Tuning Multilingual Transformers for Cross-Lingual Document Matching in Public Procurement
SYN-PUB-06155.text:
Fine-Tuning Multilingual Transformers for Cross-Lingual Document Matching in Public Procurement (2020, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Language Technologies and Digital Humanities (LanguageTech)).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Stefan Đorđević (outside co-author); Ivana Bojanić (outside co-author).
Keywords: document matching; public procurement; multilingual transformers; siamese networks; Balkans.
Public procurement databases in the Western Balkans are maintained in multiple national languages, making cross-border tender matching difficult without manual translation. We investigate whether fine-tuned multilingual transformer models can identify semantically equivalent tender notices across Serbian, Croatian, and Macedonian without explicit translation. Using a dataset of 12,400 tender notice pairs (6,200 positive, 6,200 negative) derived from the Open Tenders Balkans portal, we fine-tune XLM-R and mBERT with a siamese network objective and compare against a TF-IDF baseline and a machine-translation-then-monolingual-SBERT pipeline. The fine-tuned XLM-R siamese model achieves an average precision of 0.88 on the held-out test set, compared to 0.73 for TF-IDF and 0.85 for the translation pipeline, while running approximately 3.4× faster at inference time. We discuss domain-specific vocabulary challenges and release fine-tuning code.

SYN-PUB-06156.title: Structured Table Reconciliation Across Multilingual Financial Reports Using Column-Header Alignment and Cell-Level Semantic Similarity
SYN-PUB-06156.text:
Structured Table Reconciliation Across Multilingual Financial Reports Using Column-Header Alignment and Cell-Level Semantic Similarity (2021, journal, Journal of Information Science and Engineering (JISE)).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Réka Molnár (outside co-author); Dragana Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: table alignment; structured document reconciliation; multilingual; financial reports; semantic similarity.
Annual financial reports published by companies operating across multiple Central and Eastern European jurisdictions often contain the same underlying data structured in tables with headers in different languages and with variable column ordering. This paper presents a pipeline for aligning and reconciling such tables automatically. Column headers are aligned using cross-lingual sentence embeddings (LaBSE and XLM-R) combined with a type-inference module that classifies cells as numeric, date, currency, or free text. Cell-level reconciliation uses a combination of normalised numeric comparison and semantic similarity for textual cells. We evaluate on a corpus of 840 paired tables from 210 annual reports covering Serbian, Hungarian, and Romanian. Column alignment achieves an F1 of 0.92; full-row reconciliation with conflict detection reaches a precision of 0.87. The pipeline reduces manual review time by an estimated 65% in a controlled user study with eight financial analysts.

SYN-PUB-06157.title: Named-Entity Span Transfer for Low-Resource Languages via Cross-Lingual Projection from Serbian Annotations
SYN-PUB-06157.text:
Named-Entity Span Transfer for Low-Resource Languages via Cross-Lingual Projection from Serbian Annotations (2022, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on NLP for Low-Resource and Endangered Languages (NLPLRE), co-located with EACL 2022).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Miroslav Tymko (outside co-author); Stefan Đorđević (outside co-author); Anita Hajdú (outside co-author).
Keywords: named-entity recognition; annotation projection; low-resource NLP; Rusyn; cross-lingual transfer.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06158.title: A Modular Framework for Cross-Lingual Reconciliation of Structured Administrative Documents: Architecture and Case Studies
SYN-PUB-06158.text:
A Modular Framework for Cross-Lingual Reconciliation of Structured Administrative Documents: Architecture and Case Studies (2023, journal, ACM Transactions on Information Systems (TOIS)).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Tamás Fehér (outside co-author); Siniša Bošković (R0717); Claudia Niță (outside co-author); Luka Šimić (outside co-author); Nada Dobanovački (R0732).
Keywords: document reconciliation; schema mapping; multilingual NLP; administrative documents; XLM-R.
Administrative bodies in multilingual regions routinely exchange structured documents—forms, certificates, registrations—whose fields are defined by different national schema vocabularies. This paper describes DocAlign-ML, a modular software framework that combines schema-level field mapping, cross-lingual semantic similarity scoring, and value normalisation to reconcile such documents automatically. The framework consists of four interchangeable modules: a field-label encoder based on fine-tuned XLM-R, a type-aware value normaliser, a conflict resolver, and an explainability layer that generates natural-language justifications for each mapping decision. We present three case studies: business registration documents in Serbian and Romanian, land cadastre records in Serbian and Hungarian, and birth certificate data in Serbian and German. Average field-mapping accuracy across the three cases is 0.89. The framework is implemented in Python and the core components are released as open-source libraries.

SYN-PUB-06159.title: Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Sentence Encoders on Small Domain-Specific Parallel Corpora: A Study on Legal and Medical Subdomains
SYN-PUB-06159.text:
Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Sentence Encoders on Small Domain-Specific Parallel Corpora: A Study on Legal and Medical Subdomains (2024, journal, Natural Language Engineering (NLE)).
Authors: Mónika Papp (R0524); Petra Szabó (outside co-author); Dragana Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: contrastive learning; sentence encoders; fine-tuning; legal NLP; medical NLP; low-resource.
Large multilingual sentence encoders trained on general web data often perform poorly on specialised domains where vocabulary and sentence structure differ substantially from general text. We investigate the effectiveness of contrastive fine-tuning—using in-domain positive pairs and hard negatives mined from the same corpus—when the available domain-specific parallel corpus is small (2,000–8,000 sentence pairs). Experiments cover two subdomains (legal and medical) and three language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, EN–RO). We compare full fine-tuning, adapter-based fine-tuning, and prompt-based fine-tuning on top of LaBSE and XLM-R-large. Adapter-based fine-tuning with hard-negative mining matches or exceeds full fine-tuning on all six subdomain–language-pair combinations while using 7% of the trainable parameters. Performance gains are most pronounced on the medical subdomain (average Pearson correlation improvement of +0.11 over the base model). We provide a systematic analysis of hard-negative quality and its impact on final performance.

SYN-PUB-06160.title: Evaluating Hallucination and Semantic Drift in Cross-Lingual Summaries Generated by Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Structured Documents
SYN-PUB-06160.text:
Evaluating Hallucination and Semantic Drift in Cross-Lingual Summaries Generated by Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Structured Documents (2026, conference, Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL 2026)).
Authors: Petra Szabó (outside co-author); Stefan Đorđević (outside co-author); Mónika Papp (R0524); Claudia Niță (outside co-author); Orsolya Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: hallucination evaluation; cross-lingual summarisation; LLMs; structured documents; named-entity recall.
Instruction-tuned large language models are increasingly used to generate cross-lingual summaries of structured documents such as regulatory filings and procurement notices. However, it remains unclear how reliably these models preserve factual content and named-entity references when summarising across language pairs. We design an evaluation protocol using 1,200 structured document pairs in four language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, SR–RO, HU–RO) and three document types: regulatory filings, procurement notices, and scientific project abstracts. Three instruction-tuned models are evaluated: a 7B and a 13B open-weight model, and a proprietary API model. We measure hallucination rate (entity-level and numerical), semantic similarity between source and summary (using cross-lingual STS), and named-entity recall. The 13B open-weight model hallucinates named entities in 18.4% of generated summaries; the proprietary model reduces this to 9.1% but still introduces numeric errors in 6.7% of cases. We release the evaluation protocol, annotation guidelines, and test set.

SYN-PUB-06192.title: Parametric Skeleton Models for Rusyn Cyrillic Glyphs: Construction Rules and Interpolation Axes
SYN-PUB-06192.text:
Parametric Skeleton Models for Rusyn Cyrillic Glyphs: Construction Rules and Interpolation Axes (2023, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Typography Conference (CETC)).
Authors: Goran Radović (R0528); Milena Vukčević (outside co-author); Darko Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: Rusyn Cyrillic; parametric glyph design; skeleton model; UFO workflow; minority typeface.
Rusyn, a minority language officially recognised in Serbia and Croatia, uses a Cyrillic orthography that includes several characters absent from standard Serbian Cyrillic encodings. Existing digital fonts either omit these glyphs or render them through ad-hoc workarounds that break OpenType shaping. This paper proposes a parametric skeleton model for 14 Rusyn-specific glyphs, defining five interpolation axes—weight, contrast, x-height ratio, serif style, and counter aperture—using RoboFab-based Python scripting within a Unified Font Object (UFO) workflow. Skeleton nodes and handles are expressed as proportional functions of a master unit-per-em value, allowing consistent scaling across optical sizes. The model was validated by generating 48 instance fonts across axis combinations and subjecting them to readability assessments with 23 Rusyn-speaking participants recruited through the National Council of the Rusyn Minority in Novi Sad. Agreement scores measured on a five-point typographic naturalness scale reached a mean of 3.9 for serif instances and 3.6 for sans-serif instances, with the lowest scores associated with extreme contrast settings. The skeleton tables and UFO source files are released under a SIL Open Font License.

SYN-PUB-06193.title: OpenType GSUB Lookup Coverage for Southern Slavic Diacritics: A Cross-Renderer Audit
SYN-PUB-06193.text:
OpenType GSUB Lookup Coverage for Southern Slavic Diacritics: A Cross-Renderer Audit (2024, journal, Journal of Typographic Research and Practice).
Authors: Goran Radović (R0528); Milena Vukčević (outside co-author); Anita Horváth-Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: OpenType GSUB; GPOS; diacritics rendering; Southern Slavic; font quality assurance.
Southern Slavic writing systems—Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, and Macedonian—rely on a set of diacritical characters whose correct typographic rendering depends on Glyph Substitution (GSUB) and Glyph Positioning (GPOS) lookups defined in OpenType Layout tables. Inconsistencies between rendering engines (HarfBuzz, DirectWrite, CoreText, and the Adobe shaping stack) lead to mark attachment failures and incorrect contextual substitutions, particularly for the characters š, č, ž, ć, đ, and their uppercase counterparts when composed with quotation marks or following capital letters. This study conducted a systematic audit of 37 commercial and open-source fonts claiming Southern Slavic language support, testing each against a corpus of 2 400 word-level shaping sequences extracted from digitised newspaper text. Failures were classified into four categories: missing mark-to-base anchors, incomplete calt chain contexts, absent loclSRB or loclMKD features, and erroneous kern class assignments. Fourteen fonts exhibited at least one category-one failure. The paper provides a structured checklist and a freely downloadable test font containing deliberate failure cases for quality-assurance pipelines.

SYN-PUB-06194.title: Variable Font Axis Design for a Unified Latin–Cyrillic Type Family Serving Serbian Bilingual Publishing
SYN-PUB-06194.text:
Variable Font Axis Design for a Unified Latin–Cyrillic Type Family Serving Serbian Bilingual Publishing (2024, journal, Typographica Balcanica).
Authors: Goran Radović (R0528); Milena Vukčević (outside co-author); Tamara Đorđević (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: variable fonts; Latin–Cyrillic type family; bilingual typography; Vojvodina; fvar axis design.
Bilingual Latin–Cyrillic publications in Serbia—covering Serbian written in both scripts as mandated by official bilingual policies in Vojvodina—require type families that maintain consistent rhythm and colour across both scripts at identical optical sizes. This paper documents the design process of a variable font family, named Ravnica, created to serve bilingual administrative and editorial contexts. The family defines four axes: weight (100–900), width (75–125), optical size (8–36 pt), and a script-blend axis that continuously interpolates shared design parameters between the Latin and Cyrillic masters. Interpolation compatibility was achieved through a 312-step node-count harmonisation procedure across 64 master glyphs. The resulting variable font was tested in simulated bilingual page layouts representing municipal gazette formats used in three Vojvodina municipalities. Colour uniformity—measured as standard deviation of per-line optical density across mixed-script paragraphs—improved by 18 % compared to a matched non-variable control family. The paper also discusses axis naming conventions in the fvar table and their interaction with CSS font-variation-settings in web contexts.

SYN-PUB-06195.title: Automated Contour Quality Metrics for Interpolation-Ready Glyph Masters: A Benchmark Dataset for Southern Slavic Characters
SYN-PUB-06195.text:
Automated Contour Quality Metrics for Interpolation-Ready Glyph Masters: A Benchmark Dataset for Southern Slavic Characters (2025, journal, International Journal of Graphic Technology and Communication).
Authors: Goran Radović (R0528); Ildikó Papp (R0626); Milena Vukčević (outside co-author); Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: contour quality; glyph benchmark; interpolation compatibility; FontBakery; Southern Slavic glyphs.
Interpolation-based font production requires that glyph masters share compatible contour structures, but no standardised benchmark exists for evaluating contour quality specifically in Southern Slavic character sets, which include both Latin extended and Cyrillic blocks. This paper introduces the SlavoContour-109 benchmark dataset, comprising 109 glyphs drawn from Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, Macedonian, and Rusyn orthographies, each annotated with a reference contour and a set of deliberately introduced quality defects—direction errors, stray points, open paths, and incompatible node counts. Four automated checking tools (FontBakery, FoundryFabriek QC, a custom Python script, and a commercial proofing plugin) were evaluated against the dataset. Precision and recall were computed per defect category across all 109 glyphs. The custom Python script achieved the highest F1 score for direction errors (0.91) but performed poorly on stray-point detection (0.54). The dataset is published in UFO and Glyphs 3 format and is intended for use in type-design pedagogy and automated font production pipelines.

SYN-PUB-06196.title: Encoding Bunjevac Latin Orthography in OpenType: Character Set Recommendations and Font Engineering Notes
SYN-PUB-06196.text:
Encoding Bunjevac Latin Orthography in OpenType: Character Set Recommendations and Font Engineering Notes (2026, book chapter, Script Engineering and Minority Languages in Digital Environments (edited volume, Springer Typographic Studies series)).
Authors: Goran Radović (R0528); Milena Vukčević (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Katarina Bogdanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: Bunjevac; minority language encoding; Private Use Area; Unicode proposal; OpenType liga.
Bunjevac, a minority language spoken in the Subotica region of Vojvodina, uses a Latin-based orthography that was formally standardised in 2020. The standardised orthography introduces three digraph representations and two diacritical characters not present in any existing Unicode block, requiring a decision between Private Use Area encoding and a formal Unicode proposal. This book chapter reviews the encoding options in detail, evaluates six prior minority-language encoding case studies from Central and Southeastern Europe, and proposes an interim PUA-based OpenType implementation strategy pending a Unicode proposal submission. The chapter describes how liga and ccmp features can be used to compose digraphs from base characters and provides annotated OpenType feature code for the four most critical contextual cases. A proof-of-concept font, Subotička, is provided as a supplementary download. The chapter also outlines the Unicode proposal process and identifies the technical documentation gaps that currently prevent a submission.

SYN-PUB-06388.title: Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts
SYN-PUB-06388.text:
Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Vision).
Authors: Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Tamara Đurić (outside co-author).
Detecting surface defects on highly reflective metal components remains a significant challenge for automated visual inspection systems, primarily because specular reflections obscure subtle anomalies and corrupt standard feature representations. This paper presents a few-shot learning framework tailored specifically to reflective surfaces, combining a reflection-aware preprocessing pipeline with a prototypical network backbone trained on a curated set of metallic defect categories. A novel data augmentation strategy simulates varying illumination angles and reflection intensities, substantially increasing intra-class diversity without requiring large annotated datasets. The proposed method is evaluated on a newly introduced benchmark—ReflectDefect-M—comprising five metallic material types and twelve defect classes, collected in cooperation with regional SME manufacturing partners. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves a mean average precision of 87.3% using only five support examples per defect class, outperforming seven competitive baselines by margins ranging from 4.1 to 11.6 percentage points. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each pipeline stage. The work establishes a practical pathway for deploying few-shot defect detectors in small-batch production settings where collecting large labeled datasets is economically infeasible.

SYN-PUB-06396.title: Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines
SYN-PUB-06396.text:
Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines (2021, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author).
Keywords: active learning; annotation efficiency; defect detection; model uncertainty; industrial inspection.
Labeling defect images in industrial settings is expensive and requires domain expertise, making the efficient allocation of annotation effort a critical practical concern. This paper proposes an active learning framework for industrial defect detection that uses ensemble-based model uncertainty to prioritize the most informative unlabeled samples for expert annotation. A Monte Carlo dropout ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty at the instance and region levels, and a diversity-aware sampling strategy prevents the selection of redundant near-duplicate crops from the same production batch. The framework is integrated into a realistic annotation pipeline validated with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-molded plastic components. Across both domains, the active learning approach achieves 90% of fully supervised baseline performance using only 35% of the total available labeled data, reducing annotation cost by an estimated 58% in practitioner time. A user study with three quality control engineers confirms that the uncertainty-guided sample ordering significantly reduces the cognitive load of the labeling process compared to random sample presentation.

SYN-PUB-06500.title: Quantisation Effects on Recall and Storage in Billion-Scale ANN Search
SYN-PUB-06500.text:
Quantisation Effects on Recall and Storage in Billion-Scale ANN Search (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Database and Information Systems (ICDIS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author); Sara Despotović (R0559); Nikola Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: product quantisation; ANN search; HNSW; billion-scale; vector compression.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06501.title: Index Routing Policies for Multi-Tenant Search Services: A Simulation Study
SYN-PUB-06501.text:
Index Routing Policies for Multi-Tenant Search Services: A Simulation Study (2023, journal, Journal of Distributed Computing Systems (JDCS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Sara Despotović (R0559); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-tenant search; index routing; cluster simulation; load balancing.
Multi-tenant search services host thousands of independent indexes on shared infrastructure. Routing decisions—which node handles each index shard—affect both query latency and hardware utilisation. We simulate a 20-node cluster hosting 3,200 index shards with heterogeneous sizes and query-rate profiles drawn from anonymised access logs of a mid-sized document management platform. Four routing policies are compared: random placement, size-balanced bin packing, query-rate-aware placement, and a combined policy that jointly optimises for size and rate. The combined policy reduces 99th-percentile latency by 27% and lowers peak CPU utilisation by 19% relative to random placement under realistic diurnal load patterns. Simulation is implemented in a purpose-built discrete-event framework to allow reproducible experimentation without requiring access to production hardware. Sensitivity analyses show the gains hold across a range of shard-size distributions.

SYN-PUB-06563.title: Comparing generalised extreme value and log-normal tail models for Serbian flood damage records, 1980–2014
SYN-PUB-06563.text:
Comparing generalised extreme value and log-normal tail models for Serbian flood damage records, 1980–2014 (2017, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Dragana Stjepanović (outside co-author); Ildikó Virág (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842); Andrej Kokol Bukovšek (outside co-author); Nenad Fejsa (R0565).
Keywords: GEV distribution; flood losses; block maxima; return levels; L-moments.
Annual maximum insured flood losses from 14 Serbian counties over 35 years are modelled with the block maxima generalised extreme value (GEV) distribution and, as a benchmark, a log-normal upper tail. Maximum likelihood, L-moment, and Bayesian (non-informative Jeffreys prior) parameter estimates are compared for the GEV shape, location, and scale. In ten of the 14 counties the posterior shape parameter credible interval includes zero, suggesting Gumbel behaviour; three counties show positive shape consistent with heavy-tail Fréchet behaviour. Return-level estimates for 50- and 100-year events differ substantially between GEV and log-normal models when the shape is positive. The practical implication for regional reinsurance pricing is discussed. Data were obtained from the Serbian Flood Insurance Pool archive.

SYN-PUB-06577.title: Selective Harmonic Elimination PWM for a Three-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Inverter Using Newton–Raphson Iteration
SYN-PUB-06577.text:
Selective Harmonic Elimination PWM for a Three-Level Neutral-Point-Clamped Inverter Using Newton–Raphson Iteration (2011, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Dragan Milić (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: NPC inverter; SHE-PWM; Newton–Raphson; harmonic elimination; switching angles.
This paper addresses the computation of switching angles for selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation (SHE-PWM) applied to a three-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) inverter. The transcendental equations governing harmonic cancellation were solved using the Newton–Raphson iterative method initialised with angles derived from Fourier series analysis of the target waveform. Solutions were obtained for modulation indices ranging from 0.5 to 1.15 in steps of 0.05, targeting elimination of the 5th, 7th, 11th, and 13th harmonics while controlling the fundamental output. Simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink showed that the 5th and 7th harmonic magnitudes were reduced to below 0.3% of the fundamental for all tested modulation indices. Laboratory validation on a 2 kVA NPC prototype confirmed simulation predictions, with measured total harmonic distortion (THD) at the inverter output below 4.1% across the full modulation index range. The paper also discusses convergence sensitivity to initial angle estimates and provides pre-computed angle look-up tables for practical implementation on embedded control hardware.

SYN-PUB-06578.title: Comparison of Carrier-Based and Space-Vector PWM Strategies for Five-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters in Variable-Speed Induction Motor Drives
SYN-PUB-06578.text:
Comparison of Carrier-Based and Space-Vector PWM Strategies for Five-Level Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters in Variable-Speed Induction Motor Drives (2013, conference, Proceedings of the 11th International Symposium on Industrial Electronics and Applications (ISEA-2013), Timișoara).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Teodora Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: cascaded H-bridge; SVPWM; carrier-based PWM; induction motor; THD comparison.
A systematic comparison of phase-disposition carrier-based PWM (PD-CBPWM), phase-opposition-disposition PWM (POD-CBPWM), and space-vector PWM (SVPWM) is presented for a five-level cascaded H-bridge (CHB) inverter supplying a 15 kW induction motor. Each modulation strategy was implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and validated on a scaled laboratory prototype. Performance was evaluated across switching frequencies of 450 Hz, 900 Hz, and 1350 Hz and load conditions from 25% to 100% rated torque. Key metrics included output voltage THD, current ripple, DC-link capacitor voltage balance, and inverter losses estimated via a Plexim PLECS thermal model using IGBT datasheet parameters. PD-CBPWM achieved the lowest voltage THD (3.8% at 1350 Hz, full load) but exhibited a 6% DC-link voltage imbalance at light loads. SVPWM showed the best voltage balance across all conditions. The paper provides a decision framework linking switching frequency constraints typical of medium-voltage industrial drives to the preferred modulation strategy.

SYN-PUB-06579.title: Genetic Algorithm Optimisation of Switching Angles for Selective Harmonic Elimination in a Seven-Level CHB Inverter
SYN-PUB-06579.text:
Genetic Algorithm Optimisation of Switching Angles for Selective Harmonic Elimination in a Seven-Level CHB Inverter (2015, journal, Electrical Engineering and Drives – Transactions of the South-East European Power Engineering Forum).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Milan Pantelić (R0698); Dragan Milić (outside co-author); Nikola Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: genetic algorithm; SHE; seven-level inverter; harmonic elimination; optimisation.
Selective harmonic elimination for a seven-level cascaded H-bridge inverter requires solving a system of twelve nonlinear transcendental equations per modulation index. Classical iterative solvers are sensitive to initial conditions and frequently fail to find all solution families. This paper presents a real-coded genetic algorithm (GA) approach with tournament selection, arithmetic crossover, and adaptive mutation rate to compute globally optimal switching angle sets. The GA was run 200 times per modulation index point on a grid of 61 values from 0.4 to 1.2. Solutions targeting simultaneous elimination of the 5th, 7th, 11th, 13th, 17th, and 19th harmonics were obtained with convergence reliability above 97%. Experimental tests were conducted on a 5-level downscaled prototype (due to laboratory constraints) with the switching angles scaled accordingly. Measured output voltage spectra confirmed harmonic cancellation consistent with computed results. Computation time per modulation index point averaged 14 seconds on a standard desktop, making the GA suitable for offline look-up table generation but not real-time recalculation.

SYN-PUB-06580.title: Thermal Stress Estimation in IGBT Modules of Medium-Voltage CHB Inverters Under Non-Sinusoidal Load Conditions
SYN-PUB-06580.text:
Thermal Stress Estimation in IGBT Modules of Medium-Voltage CHB Inverters Under Non-Sinusoidal Load Conditions (2016, journal, Journal of Power Electronics and Energy Conversion).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Maja Horvat (outside co-author); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: IGBT thermal model; CHB inverter; power losses; thermal cycling; reliability.
Medium-voltage cascaded H-bridge inverters driving motors with significant harmonic content in the load current experience uneven thermal cycling across IGBT modules. This paper combines a PLECS-based electrothermal simulation with analytical loss models derived from manufacturer datasheets for 3.3 kV IGBT modules to estimate junction temperature swing and mean junction temperature across a full operating cycle representing a variable-speed compressor profile. The load profile covers start-up, ramp to 60% speed, steady-state operation, and deceleration over 180 seconds. Simulations show that outer phase modules in a seven-level CHB topology exhibit peak junction temperature swings 12–18°C higher than inner modules due to unbalanced harmonic currents. A simple balancing strategy based on rotating the switching angle assignment among modules is proposed and evaluated, reducing the maximum inter-module junction temperature difference from 21°C to under 7°C. The approach requires no additional sensors and is compatible with standard dSPACE-based control implementations.

SYN-PUB-06581.title: Harmonic Distortion Limits Compliance for Variable-Speed Pump Drives: A Case Study in the Water Treatment Sector
SYN-PUB-06581.text:
Harmonic Distortion Limits Compliance for Variable-Speed Pump Drives: A Case Study in the Water Treatment Sector (2020, journal, Acta Electrotechnica et Informatica).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Slobodan Rašić (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: harmonic limits; IEC 61000-3-6; passive filters; pump drive; power quality measurement.
This paper analyses total harmonic distortion levels produced by a medium-voltage multi-level inverter-fed pump drive installation at a water treatment facility in northern Serbia and evaluates compliance with the IEC 61000-3-6 harmonic emission limits for medium-voltage networks. Measurements were performed over seven consecutive days using a class A power quality analyser at the point of common coupling (PCC) of the 6 kV distribution network. The measured 95th percentile of voltage THD reached 4.7%, exceeding the 4% indicative planning level. Passive harmonic filters were designed for the 5th and 7th harmonic frequencies and evaluated through network simulations built in PSCAD. The proposed filter configuration reduced 95th percentile voltage THD at the PCC to 2.9%. Filter sizing, cost, and physical footprint constraints specific to pump station installations are discussed. The paper provides a practical procedure applicable to other industrial motor drive installations connected to medium-voltage networks with limited short-circuit power.

SYN-PUB-06582.title: Deadband Compensation Methods for Multi-Level Inverters and Their Effect on Output Voltage Distortion at Low Modulation Index
SYN-PUB-06582.text:
Deadband Compensation Methods for Multi-Level Inverters and Their Effect on Output Voltage Distortion at Low Modulation Index (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Power Conversion).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Jelena Komazec (outside co-author); Roberto Mancini (outside co-author); Dragan Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: deadband compensation; NPC inverter; low modulation index; voltage distortion; Luenberger observer.
Deadband intervals inserted to prevent IGBT shoot-through cause systematic output voltage errors that become proportionally more significant at low modulation indices. In three-level and five-level NPC inverters, the polarity of the phase current determines the direction of the voltage error, complicating compensation compared to the two-level case. This paper analyses deadband-induced distortion patterns for three-level and five-level NPC topologies and derives compensation formulas applicable to both SVPWM and SHE-PWM modulation. Four compensation strategies are compared: feed-forward voltage injection, current polarity detection with average voltage correction, observer-based estimation using a discrete Luenberger observer, and no compensation (baseline). Tests were conducted on a 400 V laboratory prototype across modulation indices from 0.15 to 0.55 at deadband times of 2 µs, 4 µs, and 6 µs. Observer-based compensation reduced low-order harmonic content (3rd, 5th, 7th) by 60–75% compared to baseline at a 4 µs deadband, with similar accuracy to the feed-forward method but without requiring explicit current polarity sensors.

SYN-PUB-06583.title: Multi-Level Inverters in Industrial Drive Applications: Modulation, Harmonic Control, and Practical Constraints
SYN-PUB-06583.text:
Multi-Level Inverters in Industrial Drive Applications: Modulation, Harmonic Control, and Practical Constraints (2022, book chapter, Power Electronics for Industrial Systems: Topologies and Control Methods, Springer).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Predrag Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-level inverter topologies; PWM methods; harmonic control; industrial drives; medium voltage.
This book chapter provides a structured overview of multi-level inverter topologies—diode-clamped, flying capacitor, and cascaded H-bridge—from the perspective of their deployment in medium-voltage industrial motor drive systems. The chapter covers the theoretical foundations of carrier-based and space-vector PWM methods adapted for levels three through nine, selective harmonic elimination formulations and solution strategies, and capacitor voltage balancing requirements for clamped topologies. A section is dedicated to practical constraints encountered in industrial environments, including thermal management of power modules, electromagnetic compatibility requirements under IEC standards, and commissioning considerations for retrofit installations. Numerical examples are drawn from documented laboratory results obtained on a 5-level CHB testbed. The chapter also discusses trade-offs between switching frequency, output harmonic performance, and semiconductor stress that arise when selecting modulation strategies for specific load profiles such as fans, compressors, and conveyors.

SYN-PUB-06584.title: Embedded Implementation of SHE-PWM Angle Look-Up Tables on a Low-Cost FPGA for Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters
SYN-PUB-06584.text:
Embedded Implementation of SHE-PWM Angle Look-Up Tables on a Low-Cost FPGA for Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Power Electronics and Motion Control (PEMC-2024), Novi Sad).
Authors: Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Jelena Komazec (outside co-author); Zorica Jovanović (R0567).
Keywords: FPGA implementation; SHE-PWM; look-up table compression; cascaded H-bridge; embedded control.
Pre-computed switching angle tables for selective harmonic elimination pulse-width modulation occupy significant memory when resolution over modulation index is fine and the number of target harmonics is large. This paper describes the implementation of a compressed look-up table on a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA, using piecewise linear interpolation between stored angle sets to reduce memory footprint while maintaining angular accuracy within 0.02°. The implementation targets a five-level cascaded H-bridge inverter eliminating the 5th, 7th, 11th, and 13th output voltage harmonics. Resource utilisation, interpolation latency (measured at 1.4 µs from modulation index update to angle output), and sensitivity of harmonic cancellation quality to interpolation error are reported. Hardware testing on a 2 kVA laboratory inverter confirmed that output voltage THD with the interpolated table differed by at most 0.15 percentage points from the THD achieved using the full-resolution table, across 61 modulation index points from 0.5 to 1.1. The design targets inverter control cards in cost-sensitive retrofit applications.

SYN-PUB-06585.title: Selective Harmonic Elimination Under Unbalanced DC-Link Voltages in Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters: Reformulation and Experimental Validation
SYN-PUB-06585.text:
Selective Harmonic Elimination Under Unbalanced DC-Link Voltages in Cascaded H-Bridge Inverters: Reformulation and Experimental Validation (2026, journal, IET Power Electronics).
Authors: Zorica Jovanović (R0567); Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Claudia Ferrero (outside co-author); Dragan Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: unbalanced DC link; SHE-PWM reformulation; cascaded H-bridge; harmonic correction; photovoltaic drive.
Standard SHE-PWM formulations assume equal DC-link voltages across all H-bridge cells. In practice, unequal charging of isolated DC sources—common in photovoltaic-fed or battery-buffered CHB drives—distorts the output voltage spectrum and invalidates pre-computed angle tables. This paper reformulates the SHE-PWM equations to account for arbitrary, known DC-link voltage imbalances across a seven-level (three-cell) CHB inverter. The reformulated system is solved using a trust-region algorithm with multiple random starting points to locate all physically meaningful solution branches. Angle correction maps were constructed for DC-link voltage deviations of up to ±15% relative to nominal. Experimental tests on a laboratory CHB prototype with deliberately unbalanced DC supplies (220 V, 208 V, 234 V nominal 220 V per cell) showed that corrected angles reduced the 5th harmonic from 4.1% to below 0.5% of the fundamental and the 7th harmonic from 3.7% to below 0.6%. The paper discusses update latency requirements if the correction is applied dynamically during operation.

SYN-PUB-06614.title: A Rule-Based Framework for Detecting Structural Inconsistencies in REST API Responses
SYN-PUB-06614.text:
A Rule-Based Framework for Detecting Structural Inconsistencies in REST API Responses (2015, journal, Journal of Information and Software Engineering (JISE)).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Jelena Stojčić (outside co-author); Mirjana Malešević (R0571).
Keywords: REST API; schema validation; rule-based monitoring; JSON; data quality.
Web service APIs frequently change their response schemas without formal versioning, causing downstream data consumers to silently ingest malformed or incomplete records. This paper presents a lightweight rule-based framework that continuously inspects JSON payloads returned by REST endpoints and flags deviations from a registered baseline schema. The framework encodes expected field types, cardinality constraints, and value-range rules in a declarative specification file. Violations are classified into four severity tiers and surfaced through an alerting interface. The approach was evaluated against a corpus of 14 publicly accessible APIs monitored over six months, capturing 38 distinct schema-change events. Detection latency averaged 1.4 seconds from the first non-conforming response. False-positive rates remained below 2.1% across all monitored endpoints. The paper also discusses how rule sets can be partially auto-generated from historical response samples using frequency-based field inference. The implementation is provided as a self-contained Java library with a configuration-file interface.

SYN-PUB-06615.title: Baseline Profiling of Temporal API Data Streams for Anomaly Threshold Calibration
SYN-PUB-06615.text:
Baseline Profiling of Temporal API Data Streams for Anomaly Threshold Calibration (2017, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Balkan Conference on Informatics (BCI 2017)).
Authors: Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Tamás Fehér (outside co-author); Mirjana Malešević (R0571).
Keywords: streaming data; anomaly threshold; STL decomposition; temporal profiling; e-commerce.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06616.title: Cross-Source Consistency Validation for Event-Triggered Business Logic in Distributed Retail Systems
SYN-PUB-06616.text:
Cross-Source Consistency Validation for Event-Triggered Business Logic in Distributed Retail Systems (2018, journal, International Journal of Distributed and Parallel Systems (IJDPS)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Nikola Lazić (outside co-author); Cornelia Munteanu (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-source consistency; event-driven systems; distributed retail; conflict detection; business logic.
When a single business event—such as a purchase confirmation—must be reflected consistently across inventory, billing, and logistics APIs, inconsistencies arising from partial failures or race conditions can corrupt downstream decision logic. This paper formalises a consistency validation model that reconciles event records from multiple independent API sources by aligning them on a shared transaction identifier and a configurable time window. A conflict detection module compares field-level values across sources and produces a structured discrepancy report. The approach was tested on a synthetic dataset of 500,000 simulated purchase events with injected inconsistencies at rates of 0.5%, 2%, and 5%. Precision exceeded 97% in all three scenarios; recall dropped to 91% at 0.5% injection rate due to borderline timestamp ambiguities. The paper proposes a tie-breaking heuristic based on source-reliability weights that partially recovers recall in low-rate conditions. Runtime overhead on a four-core commodity server was under 8% of total pipeline throughput.

SYN-PUB-06617.title: Schema Drift in Production API Pipelines: A Classification and Empirical Frequency Study
SYN-PUB-06617.text:
Schema Drift in Production API Pipelines: A Classification and Empirical Frequency Study (2020, journal, Journal of Data and Information Quality (JDIQ Supplement)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Bojana Đurić (outside co-author); Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592); Miroslav Kratochvíl (outside co-author); Stefan Ognjanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: schema drift; API monitoring; taxonomy; empirical study; pipeline reliability.
Schema drift—the unannounced alteration of data structures returned by APIs—is a recurring but poorly documented source of pipeline failures in practice. This paper presents a taxonomy of drift types encountered in production environments, distinguishing field addition, field removal, type coercion, key renaming, and structural nesting changes. An automated monitoring agent was deployed against 31 internal API endpoints operated by four partner organisations over 12 months, logging all response payloads in a versioned data store. Analysis of 9.7 million captured responses identified 74 drift events. Field addition was the most frequent type (41%), followed by type coercion (27%). Drift events clustered around software release dates, with 68% occurring within 48 hours of a detected version tag change in response headers. The paper derives practical design guidelines for pipeline engineers and discusses the feasibility of proactive drift prediction using release-calendar metadata.

SYN-PUB-06618.title: Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry
SYN-PUB-06618.text:
Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Data Quality in Engineering Systems (DQES 2021)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Péter Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: Isolation Forest; multivariate anomaly detection; IoT telemetry; streaming data; unsupervised learning.
High-frequency telemetry streams produced by IoT gateways and industrial APIs exhibit multivariate numeric patterns that rule-based detectors handle poorly when anomalies involve correlated deviations across several fields simultaneously. This paper investigates the use of the Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection in such streams, focusing on tuning the contamination parameter and the number of estimators under streaming constraints. Experiments used telemetry data from a factory automation pilot comprising six sensor channels sampled at 10 Hz over 30 days, yielding approximately 15.5 million records. Isolation Forest outperformed a univariate z-score baseline by 18 percentage points in F1 score on held-out labelled anomaly windows. The paper also reports the effect of sub-sampling strategies on detection quality when full-stream processing is not feasible, and provides a reference configuration table for practitioners operating within defined memory budgets. No labelled training data was required beyond the held-out evaluation set.

SYN-PUB-06619.title: Data Quality Monitoring in Apache Kafka Pipelines: Design Patterns and Operational Trade-offs
SYN-PUB-06619.text:
Data Quality Monitoring in Apache Kafka Pipelines: Design Patterns and Operational Trade-offs (2022, book chapter, Advances in Distributed Data Engineering (Springer LNCS volume, invented)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Dragana Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Apache Kafka; design patterns; data quality; stream processing; schema registry.
Apache Kafka has become a standard backbone for real-time data integration, yet integrating data quality checks directly into Kafka-based pipelines introduces non-trivial design decisions around consumer group placement, serialisation overhead, and back-pressure handling. This book chapter surveys and categorises design patterns for embedding schema validation, completeness checks, and anomaly scoring into Kafka consumer and Kafka Streams topologies. Four patterns are described in detail: inline validator consumers, side-car quality topics, quality-aware stream processors, and batch reconciliation jobs reading from compacted topics. Each pattern is evaluated against five criteria: latency impact, fault isolation, replayability, operational complexity, and suitability for schema drift detection. The chapter draws on deployment experience from three pilot integrations and provides worked configuration examples for each pattern using the Confluent Schema Registry and custom Avro schemas. Intended audience is data engineers and architects with working Kafka experience.

SYN-PUB-06620.title: Detecting Silent Data Corruption Caused by API Middleware Caching in Event-Driven Microservices
SYN-PUB-06620.text:
Detecting Silent Data Corruption Caused by API Middleware Caching in Event-Driven Microservices (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Services Computing (fictional sub-venue: Special Issue on Data Integrity in Microservices)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Ivan Marković (outside co-author); Hana Blažević (outside co-author); Stefan Ognjanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: caching; stale data; microservices; consistency audit; event-driven architecture.
Middleware caching layers in microservice architectures can serve stale data to downstream consumers long after the source record has been updated, producing a form of silent data corruption that is difficult to detect because individual responses remain schema-valid. This paper describes a consistency audit mechanism that periodically issues cache-bypass probe requests and compares their payloads against the most recently cached versions stored in a pipeline audit log. Discrepancies are scored by field-level severity weights reflecting business criticality. The mechanism was deployed in a logistics integration scenario comprising 11 microservices and approximately 200,000 event transactions per day. Over a four-week observation window, 312 stale-cache discrepancy instances were identified, of which 29 affected fields classified as high-criticality. The paper analyses the relationship between cache TTL settings and discrepancy frequency and proposes an adaptive TTL reduction policy triggered by elevated discrepancy scores. End-to-end detection latency averaged 3.1 seconds.

SYN-PUB-06621.title: Benchmarking Schema-Drift Detectors Under Controlled Injection: A Reproducible Evaluation Protocol
SYN-PUB-06621.text:
Benchmarking Schema-Drift Detectors Under Controlled Injection: A Reproducible Evaluation Protocol (2025, journal, Journal of Systems and Software — Data Engineering Track (fictional sub-venue)).
Authors: Emőke Varga (outside co-author); Radovan Jovanović (outside co-author); Luisa Ferreira (outside co-author); Mirjana Malešević (R0571).
Keywords: benchmarking; schema drift; reproducibility; evaluation protocol; JSON streams.
Comparing schema-drift detection methods across published papers is hampered by incompatible datasets, inconsistent drift injection procedures, and unreported hyperparameter choices. This paper proposes a reproducible benchmarking protocol for schema-drift detectors operating on JSON API streams. The protocol defines six canonical drift injection categories, each with three severity levels, applied to a synthetic baseline dataset generated by a configurable data generator released alongside the paper. Five existing detection approaches—including two rule-based and three statistical methods—were re-implemented and evaluated under the protocol. Results show that rule-based methods achieve higher precision on structural drift (type coercion, key removal) but fail entirely on distributional value drift, whereas statistical detectors show the inverse pattern. No single evaluated method scored above 0.80 F1 across all six categories simultaneously. The paper concludes with a discussion of hybrid architectures and releases all code and datasets under an open licence to facilitate future comparisons.

SYN-PUB-06622.title: Incremental Schema Inference for Long-Running API Integrations Using Probabilistic Field Tracking
SYN-PUB-06622.text:
Incremental Schema Inference for Long-Running API Integrations Using Probabilistic Field Tracking (2026, conference, Proceedings of the 18th European Conference on Data Engineering Practices (ECDEP 2026)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Anita Schwarz (outside co-author).
Keywords: schema inference; probabilistic models; API integration; incremental learning; data governance.
Maintaining accurate schema documentation for APIs that evolve continuously over years is impractical when done manually. This paper presents an incremental schema inference engine that updates a probabilistic field model after each observed API response, tracking field presence probability, dominant type, value entropy, and co-occurrence correlations with other fields. The engine distinguishes transient field appearances (sparse presence below a configurable threshold) from stable schema additions, reducing noise in drift alerts. It was evaluated on a 26-month archive of responses from seven APIs in a supply chain integration platform, comprising 31 million records. The inferred schemas at month 26 matched manually audited ground-truth schemas with 94.2% field-level precision and 96.8% recall. Incremental update cost per response averaged 0.9 milliseconds on a mid-range server. The paper discusses integration with existing Kafka-based pipeline monitoring and provides configuration guidance for organisations with limited schema governance resources.

SYN-PUB-06623.title: One-Class SVM for Detection of Scripted Clients in a Massively Multiplayer Online Environment
SYN-PUB-06623.text:
One-Class SVM for Detection of Scripted Clients in a Massively Multiplayer Online Environment (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information and Intelligent Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author); Mirjana Vidaković (R0948); Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Dragana Tadić (R0856); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; scripted clients; bot detection; anomaly detection; online games.
Scripted clients—programs that automate repetitive in-game actions—undermine economy balance in online games and are difficult to identify using rule-based filters alone. This paper applies one-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) to a labelled telemetry dataset of 48,000 sessions drawn from a game server log archive, of which 3,200 sessions were confirmed scripted via ban records. Training used only the majority legitimate-player class. Feature vectors were constructed from 22 behavioural metrics including action entropy, movement path straightness, click interval coefficient of variation, and resource acquisition rate. Radial basis function kernel parameters were tuned via cross-validation on a held-out clean subset. The resulting model achieved an F1 score of 0.81 on the contaminated test split, with a false-positive rate of 4.3%. Results were compared against isolation forest and local outlier factor baselines. The paper also discusses the effect of class contamination levels during training on downstream detection performance.

SYN-PUB-06624.title: Knowledge distillation from transformer-based activity recognisers to microcontroller-deployable CNNs
SYN-PUB-06624.text:
Knowledge distillation from transformer-based activity recognisers to microcontroller-deployable CNNs (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Embedded and Wearable Systems).
Authors: Svetlana Kapor (R1033); Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Cvejić (outside co-author); Kristina Ilić (R0960); Radovan Ðorić (outside co-author); Marek Svoboda (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge distillation; transformer; lightweight CNN; Cortex-M33; microcontroller deployment.
Transformer architectures operating on raw IMU sequences achieve high recognition accuracy but are impractical for wearable hardware due to their parameter count and memory footprint. This paper applies offline knowledge distillation to transfer prediction behaviour from a six-layer temporal self-attention teacher (1.4 M parameters, F1 = 0.927 on the benchmark set) to a student 1-D CNN with 45 000 parameters. Training uses the standard KL-divergence soft-target loss with temperature sweeping from 2 to 8 on a combined dataset drawn from three public wrist-IMU corpora totalling 112 hours. The distilled student achieves F1 = 0.911, narrowing the gap from direct-training F1 = 0.893 by 18 percentage points of the teacher–student gap. Deployment on a Cortex-M33 device at 64 MHz consumes 8.4 mW during inference on a 1 s window, measured with a hardware power monitor. Flash footprint after quantisation is 182 KB.

SYN-PUB-06646.title: Formal Verification Methods for Concurrent Software: An Introductory Perspective
SYN-PUB-06646.text:
Formal Verification Methods for Concurrent Software: An Introductory Perspective (2020, book chapter, Advances in Software Correctness (edited volume, Springer Academic Press)).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Miroslav Takáč (outside co-author); Nenad Lalić (R0573).
Keywords: model checking survey; LTL; CTL; CEGAR; SPIN; concurrent software.
This book chapter surveys model checking, deductive verification, and type-based approaches to concurrent software correctness, aimed at graduate students and practitioners unfamiliar with formal methods. The chapter covers the theoretical foundations of Kripke structures, LTL and CTL semantics, and Büchi automata, then walks through worked examples in SPIN and NuSMV with annotated Promela and SMV code fragments. A section on scalability discusses the state-space explosion problem and mitigation strategies: symmetry reduction, abstraction, and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR). The chapter closes with a structured comparison of tool capabilities and a guide to selecting an approach based on system size, property type, and available expertise. The text draws on material developed for a master's-level course at the University of Novi Sad over three academic years and has been classroom-tested with approximately 90 students.

SYN-PUB-06789.title: Supraharmonic emissions (2–150 kHz) from grid-connected photovoltaic inverters: field measurements and spectral characterisation
SYN-PUB-06789.text:
Supraharmonic emissions (2–150 kHz) from grid-connected photovoltaic inverters: field measurements and spectral characterisation (2017, journal, Renewable Energy and Power Quality Journal).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Rossella Fantozzi (outside co-author); Martin Bartoš (R0587); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: supraharmonics; photovoltaic inverter; grid-connected; spectral characterisation; 2–150 kHz.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-06833.title: Latency Profiling of Multi-Source Data Reconciliation Pipelines Across WAN-Linked Data Centres
SYN-PUB-06833.text:
Latency Profiling of Multi-Source Data Reconciliation Pipelines Across WAN-Linked Data Centres (2025, journal, IEEE Transactions on Distributed Data Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Tošić (outside co-author); Anita Vojvodić (outside co-author); Václav Horák (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020); Nenad Dimitrijević (R0592).
Keywords: WAN latency; multi-data-centre; reconciliation pipeline; latency profiling; operator co-location.
Organisations that operate data centres in multiple cities face non-trivial latency when reconciling data streams that originate in geographically separate locations. We deployed a five-source reconciliation pipeline across three data centres separated by WAN links with measured round-trip times of 8 ms, 47 ms, and 112 ms, reflecting intra-regional and cross-border scenarios relevant to European deployments. The pipeline reconciled structured records from simulated ERP, MES, and sensor historian systems at a combined rate of 35 000 events per second. We profiled latency contributions from network transfer, deserialization, entity matching, join state lookup, and sink write across 14 operator stages. Network transfer accounted for 61% of end-to-end latency on the 112 ms link but only 18% on the 8 ms link, shifting the optimisation priority from algorithmic to infrastructure concerns. Co-locating matching-heavy operators with the highest-volume source reduced median end-to-end latency by 29% without altering join semantics.

SYN-PUB-06838.title: Weld Process Parameter Optimisation for Low-Spatter MIG/MAG Joining of Thin Mild-Steel Sheet
SYN-PUB-06838.text:
Weld Process Parameter Optimisation for Low-Spatter MIG/MAG Joining of Thin Mild-Steel Sheet (2017, book chapter, PhD Thesis, University of Novi Sad).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593).
Keywords: MIG/MAG; spatter; response surface methodology; thin sheet; shielding gas.
This doctoral thesis presents a systematic investigation of process variable interactions governing spatter formation in short-arc and globular-to-spray-transition MIG/MAG welding of S235JR and DC01 sheet in thicknesses of 1.0–2.5 mm. Response surface methodology with a central composite design covering five factors — arc voltage, wire feed speed, travel speed, contact-tip-to-work distance, and shielding gas composition (Ar/CO₂ ratio 75/25 to 92/8) — was used to build regression models for spatter mass rate, bead width deviation, and tensile efficiency. Optimised conditions were validated on 120 weld specimens; spatter mass rates below 0.08 g/m were achieved on 1.2 mm sheet with a mixed gas of Ar/CO₂ 82/18 at 17.8 V, 5.8 m/min, and 45 cm/min travel speed. Mechanical testing confirmed all welds met EN ISO 15614-1 requirements. A simplified decision chart translating sheet thickness and joint configuration into parameter windows is provided as a practical outcome for production engineers.

SYN-PUB-06839.title: Alkaline Degreasing Bath Concentration and Temperature Effects on Residual Carbon and Wettability of Mild-Steel Sheet Before Powder Coating
SYN-PUB-06839.text:
Alkaline Degreasing Bath Concentration and Temperature Effects on Residual Carbon and Wettability of Mild-Steel Sheet Before Powder Coating (2019, journal, Surface Treatment and Finishing — European Journal).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Mirjana Vukčević (outside co-author); Nikola Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: alkaline degreasing; surface cleanliness; wettability; powder coating; pre-treatment.
Alkaline spray degreasing is the first stage in most powder coating pre-treatment lines. This study investigates how bath concentration (10–40 g/L of a commercial alkaline degreaser, Alkoclean 720) and temperature (45–70 °C) affect the residual total organic carbon (TOC) on the sheet surface and the resulting water contact angle. A 3² factorial design was applied to DC01 cold-rolled panels (100 × 150 mm) at a fixed spray pressure of 1.2 bar and 60 s exposure. Residual TOC was measured by combustion analysis of surface swabs. Contact angle was measured by sessile drop with deionised water. Bath concentration was the more influential factor: raising concentration from 10 to 40 g/L reduced median TOC from 48 to 9 µg/dm² and contact angle from 62° to 14°. Temperature above 60 °C provided marginal additional improvement. Cross-cut adhesion testing (EN ISO 2409) of subsequently phosphated and powder-coated panels showed a direct correlation between contact angle after degreasing and final coating adhesion class, with all panels degreased at ≥ 20 g/L achieving class 0.

SYN-PUB-06840.title: Measurement Uncertainty in Contact Angle Determination as a Process Control Indicator in Powder Coating Pre-Treatment
SYN-PUB-06840.text:
Measurement Uncertainty in Contact Angle Determination as a Process Control Indicator in Powder Coating Pre-Treatment (2020, journal, Measurement Science and Quality Assurance).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: contact angle; measurement uncertainty; GUM; powder coating; quality control.
Contact angle measurement by the sessile drop method is increasingly used as an inline or near-line indicator of surface cleanliness in powder coating pre-treatment lines. However, its measurement uncertainty under industrial conditions has not been systematically characterised. This study applies the GUM framework to quantify uncertainty contributions from drop volume (1–5 µL), image acquisition angle, baseline detection algorithm, and surface roughness for DC01 panels at various stages of a five-stage pre-treatment line (degrease, rinse, zinc phosphate, rinse, passivation). Expanded uncertainty (k = 2) ranged from ±1.8° on smooth panels after rinsing to ±6.4° on phosphated panels with Ra ≈ 1.8 µm. Operator-to-operator reproducibility, evaluated across four operators on identical panels, contributed 18–31 % of total variance depending on stage. Practical control limits accounting for these uncertainties are proposed for each pre-treatment stage, offering a statistically defensible accept/reject criterion for production quality control.

SYN-PUB-06841.title: Phosphate Coat Weight Uniformity Across a Conveyor-Fed Spray Phosphating Line: A Multi-Point Sampling Study
SYN-PUB-06841.text:
Phosphate Coat Weight Uniformity Across a Conveyor-Fed Spray Phosphating Line: A Multi-Point Sampling Study (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Central European Conference on Surface Engineering, Graz).
Authors: Nikola Radovanović (outside co-author); Đuro Simić (R0593); Katarina Mađarević (outside co-author); Péter Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: zinc phosphating; coat weight; process control; spray line; powder coating.
Zinc phosphate pre-treatment is critical to adhesion and corrosion resistance in electrostatic powder coating. This paper reports a multi-point sampling campaign at a medium-sized contract coating shop operating a seven-stage spray line with a throughput of 1800 m²/day. Coat weight was determined gravimetrically (strip-and-weigh per EN ISO 9717) at nine positions across the conveyor width and three longitudinal positions per batch, over 14 production days. Mean coat weight was 2.4 g/m² with a within-batch coefficient of variation of 11–19 % and a between-day coefficient of variation of 8 %. Edge zones (within 80 mm of conveyor rail) showed systematically 22 % lower coat weights, attributable to spray shadow effects characterised by flow visualisation with tracer dye. Bath chemistry (Zn²⁺, total acid, free acid, accelerator concentration) was logged concurrently; free acid point emerged as the strongest predictor of coat weight in a multiple regression model (R² = 0.71). Adjusting free acid set-point from 0.8 to 1.1 points reduced between-position variance by 31 % over a two-week trial.

SYN-PUB-06842.title: Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input
SYN-PUB-06842.text:
Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input (2023, journal, International Journal of Welding Science and Practice).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: shielding gas; Ar/CO₂; thin sheet; heat input; bead geometry.
Very thin mild-steel sheet (1.0 mm DC01) presents a narrow operating window in MIG welding because heat input must be minimised to avoid burn-through while maintaining fusion. This paper reports the effect of Ar/CO₂ mixture ratios (75/25, 82/18, 90/10, and 97/3 vol%) on spatter mass, bead width, dilution, and distortion in bead-on-plate welds at a fixed heat input of 85 J/mm. Forty-eight specimens were welded and measured. Ar/CO₂ 90/10 produced the lowest spatter mass (0.06 g/m) and the most consistent bead width (coefficient of variation 4.2 %), while 75/25 produced 0.21 g/m spatter. Hardness traverses across the heat-affected zone showed a maximum of 198 HV1 for all gas compositions, indicating no detrimental microstructural change. Distortion, measured by three-point deflection, was lowest at 97/3 but accompanied by an irregular bead profile with 14 % of runs showing incomplete fusion. The 90/10 ratio is recommended as the practical optimum for this thickness.

SYN-PUB-06843.title: Statistical Process Control Implementation for a Four-Stage Pre-Treatment Line Feeding an Electrostatic Powder Coating Operation
SYN-PUB-06843.text:
Statistical Process Control Implementation for a Four-Stage Pre-Treatment Line Feeding an Electrostatic Powder Coating Operation (2025, journal, Quality Engineering and Industrial Metrology).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Dragana Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPC; control charts; powder coating; pre-treatment; process capability.
This paper describes the design and pilot implementation of a statistical process control (SPC) scheme for a four-stage pre-treatment line (alkaline degrease, rinse, iron phosphate, rinse) at a small powder coating contractor in Novi Sad. Control variables selected for Shewhart chart monitoring were degreaser bath concentration, bath temperature, phosphate bath conductivity, and rinse-water conductivity at the final rinse stage. A three-month baseline data collection phase (n = 312 shift-level observations) established control limits. Capability indices (Cpk) were computed for each variable against supplier-specified bath chemistry windows; initial Cpk values ranged from 0.71 to 1.18. After operator training and the introduction of twice-daily titration checks replacing the previous once-daily practice, Cpk for degreaser concentration improved to 1.41 and phosphate conductivity to 1.29 over the subsequent three months. Coating adhesion cross-cut failures dropped from 4.1 % to 1.2 % of panels in the same period. The paper discusses the practical barriers to SPC adoption in small coating shops and proposes a minimal-instrument monitoring protocol.

SYN-PUB-06844.title: Pulsed MIG Welding of 1.2 mm Mild-Steel Sheet: Parameter Window Mapping for Spatter-Free Operation at 150–300 A Mean Current
SYN-PUB-06844.text:
Pulsed MIG Welding of 1.2 mm Mild-Steel Sheet: Parameter Window Mapping for Spatter-Free Operation at 150–300 A Mean Current (2026, journal, Welding in Production Engineering).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Ladislav Horváth (outside co-author); Milica Jovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: pulsed MIG; parameter optimisation; spatter-free; D-optimal design; response surface.
Pulsed MIG welding offers the potential for spatter-free operation across a wider thickness range than conventional short-arc transfer, but the interaction between peak current, pulse duration, background current, and frequency creates a large parameter space. This study applies a D-optimal design with 41 experimental runs to map the spatter-free operating window for 1.2 mm S235JR sheet using an inverter source with independent pulse parameter control (Varkon PulseMaster 400). Spatter was classified as zero, low (< 0.03 g/m), or unacceptable (≥ 0.03 g/m) based on production-line cleanliness targets. The response surface model identified a feasible zero-spatter region centred on peak current 320 A, pulse duration 2.1 ms, background current 42 A, and frequency 95 Hz for Ar/CO₂ 90/10 shielding gas. Travel speed and contact-tip-to-work distance were fixed at 48 cm/min and 14 mm respectively. Bead-on-plate and T-fillet specimens welded at the optimum point showed tensile shear strengths of 390–408 MPa and no radiographic indications above EN ISO 5817 level B. The mapped window boundaries are presented as a contour chart suitable for direct use in parameter card preparation.

SYN-PUB-06872.title: Competency Outcome Modelling in Mathematics Education: A Mixed-Effects Survival Analysis of Time-to-Mastery
SYN-PUB-06872.text:
Competency Outcome Modelling in Mathematics Education: A Mixed-Effects Survival Analysis of Time-to-Mastery (2019, journal, Statistics and Education Review).
Authors: Jelena Bosnić (outside co-author); Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author); Zuzana Kmeťová (R0595).
Keywords: survival analysis; time-to-mastery; mixed-effects models; competency; mathematics education.
This paper frames competency attainment in undergraduate mathematics as a time-to-event outcome and applies mixed-effects parametric survival models to longitudinal assessment data. Records from 2,240 students completing a multi-module calculus sequence over five academic years were analysed. The outcome was defined as the week in which a student first demonstrated sustained mastery on adaptive quizzes, operationalised as three consecutive passing scores above 80 %. A log-logistic accelerated failure time model with random student and instructor intercepts provided the best fit (log-likelihood ratio test against Weibull, p < 0.001).
