Time-to-mastery was significantly shortened by higher prior achievement scores and by weekly formative quiz completion, and was lengthened by patterns of concentrated last-minute access. The paper contributes a reusable feature engineering pipeline for Moodle log data and provides worked R code as a supplementary appendix.

SYN-PUB-06916.title: How teachers in Serbian vocational schools design screencasts: a survey of practices and stated rationales
SYN-PUB-06916.text:
How teachers in Serbian vocational schools design screencasts: a survey of practices and stated rationales (2020, journal, Pedagogy and Education in Serbia).
Authors: Dragan Subotić (outside co-author); Olivera Milanović (outside co-author); Sara Dobanovački (R0600); Boris Krstić (R0872); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: teacher practices; screencast design; vocational schools; Vojvodina; multimedia learning principles.
Despite the growing use of teacher-produced screencasts in Serbian secondary vocational education, little is known about how teachers make design decisions. This study surveyed 214 vocational teachers across 37 schools in Vojvodina regarding their screencast production practices, tools used, awareness of multimedia learning principles, and self-reported rationales for design choices. Eighty-one per cent used default settings in their recording software without consulting instructional design guidelines. Awareness of the redundancy effect was low (14% correct identification on a scenario-based item). Teachers with prior ICT training were more likely to use segmentation and to limit on-screen text. Open-ended responses revealed that perceived student preference drove many decisions, including the widespread inclusion of full narration transcripts as captions. The findings indicate a gap between research-derived guidance and classroom practice, informing the design of teacher professional development programmes.

SYN-PUB-06922.title: Does Physical Manipulation Add Value to Digital Math Games? A Comparative Study in Grades Four and Five
SYN-PUB-06922.text:
Does Physical Manipulation Add Value to Digital Math Games? A Comparative Study in Grades Four and Five (2014, journal, Computers & Education Research Quarterly).
Authors: Zoran Popović (outside co-author); Sara Dobanovački (R0600); Kristina Varga (outside co-author); Nenad Novaković (R1043); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: digital games; physical manipulatives; hybrid learning; transfer; grades four and five.
A between-subjects experiment compared three conditions: purely digital tablet-based number games, physical manipulative tasks, and a hybrid condition combining both within the same activity. Participants were 127 students in grades four and five from three schools in Novi Sad. Each condition ran for six weeks with two 30-minute sessions per week. Outcome measures included a curriculum-aligned arithmetic test, a near-transfer task involving number patterns, and a far-transfer task involving measurement word problems. On the arithmetic test, all three conditions improved significantly from pre- to post-test; however, the hybrid condition outperformed the digital-only condition on the near-transfer task (p = 0.03, d = 0.48) but not on the far-transfer task. Physical-only students scored lower than hybrid students on the digital post-test, suggesting interface familiarity effects. Findings support hybrid designs for near-transfer benefits while questioning claims of broad cognitive transfer.

SYN-PUB-06923.title: Designing Assessments Embedded in Educational Card Games: Challenges and a Proposed Framework
SYN-PUB-06923.text:
Designing Assessments Embedded in Educational Card Games: Challenges and a Proposed Framework (2020, book chapter, Handbook of Game-Based Approaches in Primary Mathematics Education).
Authors: Olivier Renard (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837); Sara Dobanovački (R0600).
Keywords: embedded assessment; card game; assessment framework; performance indicators; game design.
Assessing learning within a game without disrupting gameplay is a persistent design challenge. This book chapter reviews 22 published studies on embedded assessment in card and board games used for mathematics instruction at primary level and proposes a three-layer framework distinguishing performance indicators (observable in-game actions), inferential indicators (patterns requiring data aggregation), and post-game probes (brief structured questions administered after a session). The chapter argues that most existing designs rely exclusively on post-game probes, leaving real-time performance data unused. A worked example applying the framework to a fraction card game is provided, showing how rule-compliance errors, self-correction frequency, and help-seeking behaviour can serve as performance indicators without interrupting game flow. Limitations of the framework in low-technology settings and in classrooms without trained observers are discussed. The chapter concludes with a checklist for practitioners developing embedded assessment in game-based math instruction.

SYN-PUB-06924.title: Instrument validation: the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale for adult distance learners
SYN-PUB-06924.text:
Instrument validation: the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale for adult distance learners (2020, journal, Istraživanja u pedagogiji — Research in Pedagogy).
Authors: Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Simona Florescu (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837); Nenad Novaković (R1043); Sara Dobanovački (R0600).
Keywords: scale development; validation; metacognitive regulation; confirmatory factor analysis; psychometrics.
This paper reports the development and psychometric validation of the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale (SMRS), a 24-item instrument designed for use with adult distance learners. Item generation drew on existing frameworks and qualitative pilot data from 38 adult learners. The instrument was administered to 312 distance students across four universities in Serbia. Exploratory factor analysis on a random split-half (n = 156) yielded a three-factor structure corresponding to planning, monitoring, and evaluation, accounting for 54 % of total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis on the second half showed acceptable fit (CFI = 0.93, RMSEA = 0.061, SRMR = 0.057). Internal consistency was satisfactory for all three sub-scales (α = 0.81, 0.78, 0.76 respectively). Test-retest reliability over six weeks was r = 0.74. Convergent validity with the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire monitoring sub-scale was r = 0.63. The instrument is freely available in Serbian and English and is intended for use in research and programme evaluation.

SYN-PUB-07001.title: Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks
SYN-PUB-07001.text:
Time-domain simulation of conducted disturbances generated by single-phase rectifiers in low-voltage residential networks (2010, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Đorđe Petrović (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: conducted emissions; time-domain simulation; single-phase rectifier; LISN; low-voltage network.
A time-domain simulation framework is developed to predict conducted emissions from single-phase uncontrolled rectifiers connected to a simplified residential low-voltage network. The network is represented by a ladder model with frequency-dependent line parameters derived from measurements on a 230 V, 50 Hz test feeder of approximately 120 m length. Rectifier loads ranging from 100 W to 2 kW are modelled as nonlinear voltage-dependent current sources parameterised from laboratory measurements. Simulated disturbance voltages at the mains terminal are compared against LISN-based measurements following CISPR 16-1-1 procedures over the 9 kHz to 30 MHz range. Agreement within 4 dB is achieved across the 150 kHz to 2 MHz sub-band, with larger deviations at higher frequencies attributed to parasitic capacitances not included in the ladder model. The study identifies the 450 kHz to 600 kHz interval as the most sensitive to load power level, with peak quasi-peak levels increasing by up to 11 dB when aggregate load increases from 500 W to 2 kW. The results suggest that existing CISPR limits may be approached under dense residential loading conditions.

SYN-PUB-07002.title: Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks
SYN-PUB-07002.text:
Frequency-dependent impedance characterisation of low-voltage cable types used in Serbian urban distribution networks (2011, conference, Proceedings of the 8th International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility and Electromagnetic Ecology (EMCEE), Belgrade).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Luca Marchetti (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: cable impedance; frequency-dependent parameters; transmission-line model; SPICE; conducted emission.
The per-unit-length impedance and admittance parameters of four cable types commonly deployed in Serbian urban low-voltage distribution networks are characterised over the 10 kHz to 30 MHz frequency range using a two-port vector network analyser. Cable lengths between 10 m and 80 m are measured in open-circuit and short-circuit configurations, and results are fitted to a standard transmission-line model augmented with a skin-effect correction term. Measured propagation constants are compared to values predicted by IEC 60228-based geometric calculations, revealing deviations of up to 18% in the attenuation constant above 1 MHz for flat-conductor aluminium cables. The characterised parameters are incorporated into a SPICE-compatible model library intended for conducted emission simulations. Sensitivity analysis shows that uncertainty in conductor geometry translates to a maximum 6 dB uncertainty in predicted disturbance voltage at a 30 m cable termination at 10 MHz. The data set covers NYY, NAYY, NYM and NYFGbY cable types in cross-sections from 1.5 mm² to 25 mm².

SYN-PUB-07003.title: Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars
SYN-PUB-07003.text:
Impact of variable-speed drives on harmonic voltage distortion in industrial low-voltage busbars (2013, journal, Electrical Power Systems Research).
Authors: Aleksandar Simić (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611); Bojan Ristić (outside co-author).
Keywords: harmonic distortion; variable-speed drives; power quality; harmonic load flow; EN 50160.
Harmonic voltage measurements are carried out on three low-voltage industrial busbars (400 V, 50 Hz) in a metalworking facility over a seven-day continuous recording period using a class A power quality analyser. Variable-speed drives of 5.5 kW to 90 kW nameplate ratings account for between 40% and 70% of connected load depending on the shift schedule. Total harmonic distortion of voltage (THDV) consistently exceeds the EN 50160 indicative limit of 8% during peak production hours, reaching up to 12.3%. The fifth and seventh voltage harmonics dominate, with average magnitudes of 4.1% and 3.6% of fundamental respectively. Measured current spectra from individual drives are used to construct aggregated injection models following IEC 61000-3-6 guidelines, and harmonic load flow calculations are performed on a network model validated against field measurements. Simulations reproduce measured THDV values within 1.5 percentage points. Mitigation options including passive fifth-harmonic filters and increased feeder conductor cross-section are evaluated, with the former reducing THDV to below 6% under peak load.

SYN-PUB-07004.title: Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation
SYN-PUB-07004.text:
Conducted emission test reproducibility for switch-mode power supplies: influence of LISN topology and mains impedance variation (2014, journal, IEEE Transactions on Electromagnetic Compatibility).
Authors: Klaus Hoffmeister (outside co-author); Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: LISN; CISPR 32; switch-mode power supply; test reproducibility; mains impedance.
Switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are tested for conducted emissions according to CISPR 32 using three commercially available line impedance stabilisation networks (LISNs) of nominally identical 50 Ω/50 µH topology but from different manufacturers. Tests are performed on five SMPS samples with rated power between 30 W and 250 W. Measured quasi-peak levels at the same SMPS unit differ by up to 7.2 dB across LISNs in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band, exceeding the 3 dB reproducibility figure often cited in the literature. The observed discrepancies are traced to differences in the LISN high-frequency impedance characteristic, particularly a self-resonance near 1.4 MHz in one unit. An additional test campaign varies the mains source impedance from 0.05 Ω to 0.8 Ω at 50 Hz by inserting series inductors, demonstrating that SMPS peak emission levels shift by up to 5 dB due to changes in rectifier operating point. These findings have implications for compliance margins and for the interpretation of borderline-pass test results.

SYN-PUB-07005.title: Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study
SYN-PUB-07005.text:
Interference between ripple control signals and supraharmonic emissions in distribution networks: a time-domain case study (2018, journal, International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: ripple control; supraharmonics; interference; time-domain model; distribution network.
Ripple control systems operating at 316.7 Hz and 750 Hz are widely used by distribution system operators in central Europe for remote load switching. This study investigates the extent to which supraharmonic emissions from switch-mode loads corrupt ripple control telegram reception in a 400 V test feeder modelled from parameters measured in a suburban distribution area near Novi Sad. A full time-domain model is built in MATLAB/Simulink incorporating a ripple control transmitter, feeder impedance, and four classes of switching loads: SMPS, LED drivers, PV micro-inverters, and EV on-board chargers. At 15% feeder loading with mixed loads, signal-to-interference ratio at the receiver input drops below the 20 dB design threshold assumed in EN 61000-5-1 for ripple control. Worst-case degradation of 28 dB is observed when multiple PV micro-inverters synchronise their switching near the ripple control frequency. Temporal correlation between load power cycles and interference bursts is demonstrated. The model is validated against a 4-hour measurement record from the test feeder with 4.5% mean absolute error in receiver input voltage.

SYN-PUB-07006.title: Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis
SYN-PUB-07006.text:
Common-mode and differential-mode separation of conducted emissions: measurement method comparison and uncertainty analysis (2019, journal, Metrology and Measurement Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Čabarkapa (outside co-author); Ida Lerch (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: common mode; differential mode; conducted emissions; measurement uncertainty; LISN.
Four methods for separating common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) conducted emissions from single-phase equipment are compared: a commercial CM/DM separator, a home-built balun-based separator, a two-LISN simultaneous measurement approach, and a post-processing technique applied to standard LISN recordings. Measurements are performed on five reference loads including a 100 W SMPS, a 40 W LED driver array, and a 1.5 kW motor controller in the 150 kHz to 30 MHz band. Separator insertion loss and balance-to-unbalance conversion ratio are characterised by network analyser, revealing that the commercial unit maintains 40 dB mode separation only below 5 MHz. Uncertainty budgets are constructed according to JCGM 100:2008 for each method. Total standard uncertainty ranges from 1.1 dB to 3.8 dB depending on method and frequency, with the two-LISN method providing the lowest uncertainty above 10 MHz. Practical guidance is provided on method selection depending on available equipment and required accuracy.

SYN-PUB-07008.title: Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling
SYN-PUB-07008.text:
Conducted disturbance propagation from EV on-board chargers: network impedance dependency and phase-to-phase coupling (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Jasmina Jokić (R0769); Marta Johansson (outside co-author); Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: EV charger; conducted emissions; three-phase feeder; phase coupling; charging infrastructure.
Three-phase low-voltage feeders serving residential parking areas with electric vehicle charging infrastructure are studied using a combination of laboratory measurements and network simulation. On-board chargers of 3.3 kW, 7.4 kW and 11 kW rated power are characterised individually on a LISN test bench, and their emission spectra exported as Norton equivalent sources. A three-phase feeder model of 60 m length is parameterised from field impedance measurements and loaded with up to 12 simultaneous charger connections distributed across phases. Phase-to-phase coupling via the neutral conductor and earth return path is analysed and shown to introduce cross-phase disturbance voltages up to 8 dB below the directly driven phase in the 150 kHz to 500 kHz band. Feeder impedance variation due to the connection of reactive compensation capacitors shifts dominant emission peaks by up to 40 kHz. Compliance margins relative to EN 61000-3-11 group emission limits shrink by 6 dB when six or more chargers of the same type operate simultaneously. Results are discussed in the context of planned charging hub deployments.

SYN-PUB-07009.title: Real-time hardware-in-the-loop emulation of conducted disturbances for testing distribution automation equipment
SYN-PUB-07009.text:
Real-time hardware-in-the-loop emulation of conducted disturbances for testing distribution automation equipment (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Renewable Energies and Power Quality (ICREPQ), Vigo).
Authors: Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Zdravko Milovanović (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: hardware-in-the-loop; conducted immunity; distribution automation; real-time simulation; power amplifier.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07010.title: Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign
SYN-PUB-07010.text:
Statistical characterisation of supraharmonic emission levels in a low-voltage feeder over a 12-month monitoring campaign (2023, journal, Electric Power Systems Research).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Rossella Fantozzi (outside co-author); Gábor Fekete (outside co-author); Danijela Ninkov (R0611).
Keywords: supraharmonics; long-term monitoring; statistical characterisation; low-voltage feeder; lognormal distribution.
Continuous monitoring of supraharmonic current and voltage emissions at the 400 V low-voltage busbar of a suburban distribution substation near Novi Sad is carried out over twelve consecutive months using a purpose-built acquisition system with 1 MS/s sampling and 90 dB dynamic range. The feeder supplies a mixture of residential and small commercial loads. Emission spectra are computed in 200 Hz bins from 2 kHz to 150 kHz on a ten-minute aggregation basis in accordance with the draft measurement protocol of IEC/TR 61000-2-1-2 Ed.2. Statistical distributions of emission levels are fitted to lognormal models at selected spectral bins; the 95th percentile levels at 16 kHz and 40 kHz are 12.1% and 6.3% of the fundamental current respectively. Clear diurnal and weekly patterns are observed, with evening peaks 4 to 9 dB above overnight minima. Seasonal variation is modest (less than 2 dB) except at 16 kHz, where a 5 dB increase in winter is attributed to increased LED and SMPS loading. The data set is made available as a supplementary repository and is intended for validation of aggregation models.

SYN-PUB-07161.title: Factorial structure of a Serbian-language matrix reasoning battery in primary school children
SYN-PUB-07161.text:
Factorial structure of a Serbian-language matrix reasoning battery in primary school children (2010, journal, Psihologija: Časopis Srpskog Psihološkog Društva).
Authors: Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Miroslav Ilić (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: matrix reasoning; Rasch model; factorial structure; primary school.
This study examined the latent factor structure of a newly constructed matrix reasoning battery administered to 412 children aged 8–11 from eight primary schools in Novi Sad and Subotica. Exploratory factor analysis followed by confirmatory factor analysis indicated a single dominant general factor accounting for 54% of common variance, with two residual group factors corresponding to item set complexity. Item response theory Rasch modelling showed adequate fit for 38 of 48 items; 10 items were removed due to local dependence or misfit. Differential item functioning by gender was absent for all retained items. The battery demonstrated good internal consistency (α = .88) and four-week test–retest reliability (r = .82, n = 94). Age-differentiated raw-to-standard-score conversion tables are provided. The results support the battery's use as a screening instrument within the Serbian educational context, pending broader national norming.

SYN-PUB-07162.title: Standardisation of working memory span tasks for Serbian children aged 7–15: percentile norms and reliability estimates
SYN-PUB-07162.text:
Standardisation of working memory span tasks for Serbian children aged 7–15: percentile norms and reliability estimates (2012, journal, Primenjena Psihologija).
Authors: Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Luka Kovačević (outside co-author); Ana Marković (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: working memory; digit span; normative data; Serbian children; developmental norms.
Normative data are reported for three working memory tasks—digit span forward, digit span backward, and a newly developed sentence span task—administered to a stratified sample of 1,186 Serbian children from Vojvodina. Stratification variables included age (seven one-year bands), school type, settlement size, and parental education. Digit span forward and backward showed monotonic age-related increases through age 13, with a plateau thereafter. The sentence span task showed a steeper developmental trajectory and higher correlation with reading comprehension (r = .46) than either digit span measure. Internal consistency ranged from .73 to .84 across tasks and age bands. Split-half reliability corrected by the Spearman–Brown formula ranged from .70 to .80. Age- and task-specific percentile tables are provided alongside standard scores (M = 10, SD = 3). Implications for clinical assessment of children with suspected working memory difficulties are discussed.

SYN-PUB-07163.title: Comparing classical test theory and two-parameter logistic IRT estimates in a short vocabulary test for school-age children
SYN-PUB-07163.text:
Comparing classical test theory and two-parameter logistic IRT estimates in a short vocabulary test for school-age children (2013, journal, Educational and Psychological Measurement).
Authors: Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: IRT; classical test theory; vocabulary; 2PL model; item discrimination.
The study compared item parameter estimates derived from classical test theory (CTT) and a two-parameter logistic item response theory (2PL IRT) model for a 40-item multiple-choice vocabulary test administered to 784 children aged 9–12. CTT item difficulty correlated .95 with IRT b-parameters and CTT item-total correlations correlated .88 with IRT a-parameters, replicating findings from Western language contexts. However, the rank ordering of items by discrimination diverged notably (Kendall's τ = .61) in the upper range of difficulty, suggesting that CTT discrimination indices underestimate differentiation for hard items in this sample. Information functions showed that the test measured most precisely at ability levels slightly below the sample mean (θ ≈ −0.4), indicating the test is better suited for identifying below-average vocabulary than for differentiating high performers. Recommendations for item revision and adaptive test construction are outlined.

SYN-PUB-07164.title: Cross-cultural measurement equivalence of a non-verbal cognitive battery between Serbian and Hungarian primary school children in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-07164.text:
Cross-cultural measurement equivalence of a non-verbal cognitive battery between Serbian and Hungarian primary school children in Vojvodina (2015, journal, European Journal of Psychological Assessment).
Authors: Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Kristina Balogh (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: measurement invariance; minority children; non-verbal ability; multi-group CFA; Vojvodina.
Vojvodina hosts a substantial Hungarian-speaking minority whose assessment in Serbian-language instruments may introduce cultural measurement bias. This study applied multi-group confirmatory factor analysis to test measurement invariance of a five-subtest non-verbal cognitive battery across Serbian-speaking (n = 511) and Hungarian-speaking (n = 248) primary school children in grades 3–5. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance models were estimated, with the Satorra–Bentler scaled chi-square difference test used to compare nested models. Metric invariance held for all five subtests (ΔCFI = .006), but scalar invariance failed for one block design subtest (modification indices > 10 for two intercepts), suggesting partial scalar invariance. Latent mean comparisons corrected for non-invariant intercepts indicated no statistically significant group differences in general non-verbal ability (d = 0.09, p = .41). These findings support cautious use of the battery across both groups with appropriate intercept corrections.

SYN-PUB-07165.title: A pilot study of computerised adaptive testing for general cognitive ability in Serbian secondary school students
SYN-PUB-07165.text:
A pilot study of computerised adaptive testing for general cognitive ability in Serbian secondary school students (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 9th Conference of the European Association of Psychological Assessment, Zurich).
Authors: Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author); Marek Doležal (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: computerised adaptive testing; item bank; 3PL IRT; secondary school; test efficiency.
Computerised adaptive testing (CAT) offers efficiency gains over fixed-form paper tests by selecting items calibrated to the examinee's estimated ability level after each response. This pilot evaluated a CAT implementation for general cognitive ability using a bank of 96 items previously calibrated with a 3PL IRT model in a sample of 1,340 Serbian secondary school students. Forty students aged 15–17 completed both a fixed 40-item form and the CAT version on separate occasions. The CAT reached comparable precision (mean standard error of measurement 0.31) using on average 18.4 items compared with 40 items for the fixed form. Ability estimates correlated .92 across administrations. Administration time was reduced by approximately 43%. Students' self-reported engagement ratings were higher for the CAT format (M = 4.1 vs. 3.6 on a 5-point scale). Limitations related to item bank depth and exposure control are discussed.

SYN-PUB-07166.title: Item exposure control strategies in adaptive cognitive testing: a simulation study using Serbian item bank parameters
SYN-PUB-07166.text:
Item exposure control strategies in adaptive cognitive testing: a simulation study using Serbian item bank parameters (2017, journal, Psihologijska Istraživanja).
Authors: Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: item exposure; adaptive testing; simulation; Sympson-Hetter; item bank.
Uncontrolled item exposure in computerised adaptive testing inflates the risk of item compromise and score inflation over repeated administrations. This simulation study evaluated five exposure control methods—maximum information, randomesque, Sympson–Hetter, Stocking–Lewis, and a modified fade-away algorithm—using real item parameters from a calibrated 96-item Serbian cognitive ability bank. Simulations were conducted with 10,000 simulated examinees drawn from a standard normal ability distribution. Outcome criteria were measurement precision (RMSE of ability estimates), test overlap rate, and item pool usage. Maximum information yielded the lowest RMSE (0.29) but the highest overlap rate (61%). The modified fade-away algorithm achieved a balance, with RMSE of 0.33 and overlap rate of 28% while using 89% of the item pool. Sympson–Hetter performed comparably but required lengthy constraint calibration. Practical recommendations for adaptive test administration in Serbian educational settings are provided.

SYN-PUB-07167.title: Psychometric properties of a short fluid intelligence scale for preschool children aged 5–7
SYN-PUB-07167.text:
Psychometric properties of a short fluid intelligence scale for preschool children aged 5–7 (2018, journal, Early Child Development and Care).
Authors: Jelena Savić (outside co-author); Mirjana Đorđević (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: preschool; fluid intelligence; analogical reasoning; Rasch; non-verbal assessment.
Cognitive assessment of preschool-aged children is complicated by short attention spans, verbal demands, and examiner–child rapport factors. This study reports the development and initial validation of a 24-item picture-based fluid intelligence scale for Serbian children aged 5–7 (n = 318, recruited from kindergartens in Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Sombor). Items required analogical reasoning using pictorial stimuli with no verbal response required. Rasch analysis indicated acceptable fit (infit MNSQ 0.82–1.21) for 21 items; three items were revised. Test–retest reliability over three weeks was r = .78 (n = 62). Convergent validity with an established non-verbal reasoning measure was r = .64. Normative data stratified by age in six-month bands are presented. Results confirm that analogical reasoning at an age-appropriate level can be assessed reliably without verbal mediation, supporting use in multilingual and low-verbal populations.

SYN-PUB-07168.title: Test norming with continuous norming methods: an application to a Serbian reading speed and comprehension battery
SYN-PUB-07168.text:
Test norming with continuous norming methods: an application to a Serbian reading speed and comprehension battery (2019, journal, Journal of Psychoeducational Assessment).
Authors: Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Jana Vukojičić (outside co-author); Wolfgang Lenhard (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: continuous norming; cNORM; reading assessment; percentile norms; Serbian.
Traditional normative approaches group scores by discrete age bands, discarding information on age as a continuous predictor. This paper applies continuous norming using the cNORM method to a reading speed and comprehension battery administered to 1,842 Serbian children aged 7–14. The battery comprised three timed passages and 30 comprehension questions. Using Taylor polynomial regression within the cNORM framework, smooth percentile trajectories were estimated across the full age range. Compared with conventional norming, continuous norming reduced standard error of score estimates by 12–18% at age boundaries and eliminated the step artefacts observable when adjacent norm groups were compared. Cross-validation using a 20% hold-out sample confirmed predictive accuracy (R² = .91 for reading speed, .87 for comprehension). Normalised T-score and percentile tables derived from the continuous model are provided, along with the R code and anonymised dataset as supplementary materials.

SYN-PUB-07169.title: Psychometric assessment in Serbian schools: a review of available instruments, norming quality, and gaps in coverage
SYN-PUB-07169.text:
Psychometric assessment in Serbian schools: a review of available instruments, norming quality, and gaps in coverage (2020, book chapter, Handbook of Psychological Assessment in Southeast Europe (edited volume, University of Sarajevo Press)).
Authors: Luka Kovačević (outside co-author); Bojana Mihajlović (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: test review; Serbia; norming quality; Flynn effect; educational assessment.
This chapter reviews cognitive and scholastic ability instruments available in Serbian for school-age populations, evaluating each against criteria of norming sample adequacy, publication date, standardisation transparency, and psychometric reporting quality. Forty-one instruments were identified through database searches and publisher catalogues; 19 had been normed on Serbian samples, of which only 11 reported sample stratification procedures. Norms older than 15 years were flagged as likely outdated given documented Flynn effect trends in neighbouring Balkan countries. Critical gaps identified include the absence of nationally representative adaptive testing platforms, limited instruments for children under age 6, and scant coverage of children with hearing impairment. The chapter summarises recommendations for test publishers and policymakers, including minimum reporting standards, mandatory restandardisation cycles, and investment in digital test delivery infrastructure for schools.

SYN-PUB-07170.title: Differential item functioning by socioeconomic status in a national cognitive screening battery: findings from a Vojvodina stratified sample
SYN-PUB-07170.text:
Differential item functioning by socioeconomic status in a national cognitive screening battery: findings from a Vojvodina stratified sample (2021, journal, Assessment).
Authors: Jana Vukojičić (outside co-author); Milena Cvejić (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: differential item functioning; socioeconomic status; cognitive screening; DIF; measurement bias.
Cognitive screening batteries used for educational placement may carry systematic item bias against children from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. Using ordinal logistic regression DIF analysis, this study examined 54 items from a cognitive screening battery administered to 2,106 children in grades 1–4 across Vojvodina schools. Socioeconomic status (SES) was operationalised as a composite of parental education and occupational prestige. Fifteen items showed non-negligible DIF (effect size Δ > 0.43 on the McFadden scale), with 12 favouring high-SES children. Item content analysis revealed that SES-biased items more frequently included culturally loaded vocabulary in instructions or relied on familiarity with printed books and library materials. After removal of these 15 items, latent mean differences by SES were reduced by 31% compared with the full battery, suggesting that part of the observed group difference was attributable to item bias rather than true ability differences.

SYN-PUB-07171.title: Short-form derivation and validation of the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children using automated item selection algorithms
SYN-PUB-07171.text:
Short-form derivation and validation of the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children using automated item selection algorithms (2022, journal, Psychological Assessment).
Authors: Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author); Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Jelena Savić (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: short form; item selection; cognitive battery; reliability; validity.
Long cognitive test batteries are impractical in school and clinical settings with limited testing time. This study derived short forms of the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children (VCBC), a 90-item instrument normed on 2,106 children, using three automated selection algorithms: maximum battery reliability, maximum validity against an external criterion, and a combined information–coverage algorithm. The full calibration dataset (n = 2,106, grades 1–4) was split into derivation (n = 1,404) and validation (n = 702) halves. A 25-item short form selected by the combined algorithm achieved composite reliability of .84 and correlated .91 with the full battery score in the validation sample. External validity against teacher ratings of academic performance was r = .47 for the short form versus r = .50 for the full battery. Administration time was reduced from approximately 65 to 22 minutes. Norm tables for the short form are provided.

SYN-PUB-07172.title: Test–retest stability and practice effects in repeated cognitive testing of Serbian children: a six-month longitudinal study
SYN-PUB-07172.text:
Test–retest stability and practice effects in repeated cognitive testing of Serbian children: a six-month longitudinal study (2023, journal, Primenjena Psihologija).
Authors: Jana Vukojičić (outside co-author); Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627).
Keywords: practice effects; test-retest reliability; reliable change index; longitudinal; cognitive battery.
Reliable interpretation of cognitive re-assessment requires knowledge of expected score changes attributable to practice rather than genuine ability development. This study administered the Vojvodina Cognitive Battery for Children short form twice, six months apart, to 381 children aged 8–12 from four Novi Sad primary schools. Practice effect magnitudes (Cohen's d) ranged from 0.14 (block design) to 0.38 (matrix reasoning) across subtests. A regression-based reliable change index was computed for each subtest and the composite, enabling clinicians to identify changes exceeding practice effects at 80%, 90%, and 95% confidence thresholds. Younger children (ages 8–9) showed larger practice effects than older children (ages 11–12) for three of five subtests. Intraclass correlation coefficients for test–retest reliability ranged from .76 to .84 across subtests. Tables of reliable change indices are provided for clinical and school psychologists.

SYN-PUB-07174.title: Updating norms for a Serbian general ability screening test: secular score changes over 15 years and implications for the Flynn effect in Serbia
SYN-PUB-07174.text:
Updating norms for a Serbian general ability screening test: secular score changes over 15 years and implications for the Flynn effect in Serbia (2026, journal, Intelligence).
Authors: Dragana Petrović (outside co-author); Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author); Nikola Ranković (R0627); Jan Vermeersch (outside co-author).
Keywords: Flynn effect; secular IQ change; restandardisation; Serbia; matrix reasoning.
National cognitive test norms become outdated as population ability distributions shift over time. This study restandardised a general ability screening test originally normed in 2007–2009 using a new stratified sample of 1,614 Serbian children aged 7–14 collected in 2022–2024. Mean IQ-equivalent scores in the current sample exceeded the original normative sample by 3.1 points (95% CI: 2.3–3.9), corresponding to a rate of gain of approximately 0.21 points per year, consistent with the lower end of Flynn effect estimates from comparable European countries. Gains were larger for matrix reasoning (d = 0.29) than for vocabulary (d = 0.08), a pattern matching the predominantly abstract reasoning component of the Flynn effect. Regression discontinuity analyses ruled out school curriculum changes as the main explanation. Updated norm tables rendering 2007–2009 norms obsolete are presented alongside the original tables for historical comparison.

SYN-PUB-07201.title: Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh
SYN-PUB-07201.text:
Thermal gradient mapping inside refrigerated road trailers using a 16-node wireless mesh (2012, conference, Proceedings of the 4th European Conference on Sensor Networks in Transport and Logistics).
Authors: Miroslav Pejić (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Dragana Tomić (outside co-author); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Ivan Zec (R0903).
Keywords: refrigerated trailer; spatial temperature mapping; ZigBee mesh; ATP regulations; cold chain.
Spatial temperature heterogeneity inside refrigerated semi-trailers was characterised using a 16-node ZigBee mesh network mounted at three heights and four longitudinal positions. Measurements were conducted over 22 journeys between Novi Sad and Vienna covering a total of 14,300 km under summer and winter conditions. Nodes sampled at 1-minute intervals, producing approximately 1.1 million temperature records. Analysis identified a persistent warm zone near the rear doors, averaging 2.1 °C above the set-point of +4 °C during door-open events lasting more than 90 seconds. A principal component decomposition of the spatial profiles revealed that the first two components explain 81% of within-trailer variance. These findings were used to propose three alternative sensor placement strategies that reduce the probability of undetected warm zones by a factor of 2.4 compared to the single-probe standard practice currently mandated by ATP regulations.

SYN-PUB-07294.title: Piecewise Linear Approximation for Sensor Data Reduction on 8-bit Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-07294.text:
Piecewise Linear Approximation for Sensor Data Reduction on 8-bit Microcontrollers (2010, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Embedded Computing Systems (ICECS-ECS), Ohrid).
Authors: Miroslav Tanasić (outside co-author); Dragana Lučić (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: piecewise linear approximation; sensor data reduction; ATmega; building automation.
This paper presents a piecewise linear approximation (PLA) scheme implemented on an ATmega328P microcontroller targeting temperature and humidity sensor streams in building automation scenarios. The algorithm segments incoming data into variable-length intervals whose endpoints are stored, discarding intermediate samples when the reconstruction error stays below a user-defined threshold. We evaluated performance on 72 hours of real sensor logs sampled at 1 Hz, achieving compression ratios between 8:1 and 14:1 at a maximum absolute reconstruction error of 0.4 °C. Flash footprint was kept below 3.2 kB and average processing time per sample was 11 µs at 16 MHz. The scheme is compared against a fixed-rate decimation baseline and a simple dead-band filter; PLA consistently produces smaller payloads while maintaining tighter error bounds. Energy consumption during the compression stage was measured at 1.7 µJ per sample using a shunt-resistor current monitor. The results suggest that PLA is a practical first-stage compression step before MQTT transmission in low-power mesh networks.

SYN-PUB-07295.title: A Comparative Study of Delta Encoding Variants for Industrial Vibration Signals on ARM Cortex-M3
SYN-PUB-07295.text:
A Comparative Study of Delta Encoding Variants for Industrial Vibration Signals on ARM Cortex-M3 (2012, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Nenad Vuković (outside co-author); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: delta encoding; vibration monitoring; Cortex-M3; Golomb-Rice coding; bearing fault.
Industrial vibration monitoring generates high-rate accelerometer data that must often be stored or transmitted by nodes with limited SRAM. We implemented five delta-encoding variants — first-order delta, second-order delta, delta with Golomb-Rice coding, delta with run-length extension, and an adaptive-threshold delta — on an STM32F103 microcontroller and tested them against a 48-hour dataset of bearing vibration signals sampled at 4 kHz from a conveyor drive unit. Each algorithm was profiled for compression ratio, signal-to-noise ratio of reconstructed waveforms, processing cycles per sample, and peak SRAM usage. Adaptive-threshold delta achieved the best compression ratio of 3.8:1 while retaining impact-event peaks within 2.1 dB SNR of the original. SRAM overhead across all variants ranged from 128 bytes to 640 bytes. Cycle counts varied from 6 to 41 per sample. The paper provides decision guidelines for selecting a variant based on spectral content and memory budget.

SYN-PUB-07296.title: Adaptive Nyquist-Rate Reduction Using Signal Variance Tracking for Low-Power Acoustic Sensors
SYN-PUB-07296.text:
Adaptive Nyquist-Rate Reduction Using Signal Variance Tracking for Low-Power Acoustic Sensors (2013, journal, IET Wireless Sensor Systems).
Authors: Bojana Milošević (outside co-author); Goran Peić (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: adaptive sampling; acoustic sensing; MSP430; energy harvesting; wildlife monitoring.
This work addresses the energy cost of continuous acoustic sensing in wildlife monitoring nodes powered by solar-harvesting supercapacitors. We propose a variance-tracking scheduler that estimates short-time variance in 20 ms windows and dynamically reduces the effective sampling rate from 16 kHz to as low as 2 kHz during low-activity periods, restoring full rate when variance exceeds a learned threshold. The threshold is updated via an exponential moving average with a decay constant tuned to avoid false rate reductions during transient silence. Experiments were conducted with a custom node based on an MSP430FR5969 microcontroller and a MEMS microphone deployed in a mixed forest environment for 14 days. Compared to continuous 16 kHz sampling, the adaptive scheme reduced flash write volume by 73% and cut average current draw from 4.1 mA to 1.4 mA, extending estimated node lifetime from 11 days to 31 days without missing a single detected bird call event. Spectral fidelity during active periods was indistinguishable from the full-rate baseline.

SYN-PUB-07297.title: Anomaly-Preserving Lossy Compression: Retaining Fault Signatures Under High Compression Ratios
SYN-PUB-07297.text:
Anomaly-Preserving Lossy Compression: Retaining Fault Signatures Under High Compression Ratios (2016, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Miroslav Tanasić (outside co-author); Radovan Obradović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: anomaly-preserving compression; CUSUM; DPCM; fault detection; industrial IoT; bit allocation.
Standard rate-distortion optimisation treats all signal samples equally, which can erase rare fault-indicative spikes at high compression ratios. This paper formalises the concept of anomaly-preserving compression (APC) for industrial sensor streams and proposes a two-stage pipeline: an online anomaly scorer based on a lightweight CUSUM detector flags candidate segments, and a segment-aware bit allocator assigns additional bits to flagged regions. The allocator operates within a fixed total bit budget so that overall compression ratio is unchanged. We tested APC on synthetic bearing-fault accelerometer traces (1000 trials per fault type) and on 60 hours of real motor current signals from a pump station. At a 12:1 target compression ratio, standard DPCM missed 31% of injected fault events, whereas APC missed 4.2% under identical bit constraints. The computational overhead of the anomaly scorer was 9 CPU cycles per sample on a Cortex-M4 at 168 MHz. The paper also provides an analytical bound relating CUSUM detection lag to false-anomaly rate.

SYN-PUB-07298.title: Fixed-Point FFT Optimisation for Spectral Feature Extraction on Cortex-M4 Without FPU
SYN-PUB-07298.text:
Fixed-Point FFT Optimisation for Spectral Feature Extraction on Cortex-M4 Without FPU (2017, conference, Proceedings of the Regional Conference on Signal Processing and Embedded Intelligence (RCSPEI), Belgrade).
Authors: Branislav Stojanović (R0641); Nikola Bezbradica (outside co-author).
Keywords: FFT; fixed-point arithmetic; Cortex-M4; tool wear; spectral features.
Many mid-range microcontrollers include an FPU-equipped Cortex-M4, yet FPU use in battery-constrained nodes is often disabled to save power. This paper details the design of a 256-point radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FFT using Q15 fixed-point arithmetic without FPU instructions. We compare three twiddle-factor storage strategies — full table, quarter-wave compression, and on-the-fly CORDIC — for their trade-offs between SRAM, ROM, and cycle count. Full-table FFT executes in 4,912 cycles at negligible numerical error (SNR 78 dB); CORDIC reduces ROM by 2 kB but costs 9,340 cycles. The implementation was used in a vibration-based tool-wear classifier where six spectral band energies serve as features. Classification accuracy on a 400-sample dataset of milling operations was 91.3% using a lookup-table nearest-centroid classifier consuming 1.2 kB RAM. Total feature extraction and classification latency was 0.31 ms, making real-time 1 kHz inference feasible.

SYN-PUB-07299.title: Lightweight Dictionary Coding for Repetitive Telemetry Payloads in LPWAN Networks
SYN-PUB-07299.text:
Lightweight Dictionary Coding for Repetitive Telemetry Payloads in LPWAN Networks (2018, journal, Sensors and Actuators: Physical and Cyber Systems).
Authors: Tatjana Kovačević (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Dragana Lučić (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: dictionary coding; LZ78; LoRaWAN; agricultural IoT; soil sensing; LPWAN.
Low-power wide-area networks such as LoRaWAN impose strict payload size limits (typically 51 bytes in Europe at SF12) that force aggressive data reduction. Many agricultural IoT deployments generate highly repetitive soil-sensor payloads where values change slowly. We exploit this repetitiveness by implementing an LZ78-inspired dictionary coder with a bounded dictionary of 64 entries stored in 512 bytes of SRAM on an ATtiny3217. Across a 90-day deployment monitoring soil moisture, temperature, and electrical conductivity at four depths in a maize field, the coder achieved a mean payload reduction of 58% relative to raw quantised integers, enabling SF9 transmission and reducing time-on-air from 1.48 s to 0.62 s per burst. Monthly energy consumption fell by 34% compared to uncompressed transmission, extending estimated battery life from 14 months to 21 months. Decoding is performed server-side with negligible latency. The paper includes a simulation study covering payload entropy conditions where the scheme degrades gracefully to near-uncompressed size.

SYN-PUB-07300.title: On the Use of Haar Filterbanks for Compressive Aggregation in Wireless Sensor Trees
SYN-PUB-07300.text:
On the Use of Haar Filterbanks for Compressive Aggregation in Wireless Sensor Trees (2019, journal, Ad Hoc Networks).
Authors: Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Marco Bertolini (outside co-author); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: Haar filterbank; in-network compression; wireless sensor network; energy optimisation; tree topology.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07301.title: Resource Budget Modelling for Co-located Compression and Inference Tasks on RISC-V MCUs
SYN-PUB-07301.text:
Resource Budget Modelling for Co-located Compression and Inference Tasks on RISC-V MCUs (2021, journal, Journal of Systems Architecture).
Authors: Miroslav Tanasić (outside co-author); Lukas Hofer (outside co-author); Nikola Bezbradica (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: RISC-V; resource budget; co-located inference; compression; Pareto frontier; air quality.
When a sensor node must run both a data compressor and a machine-learning inference engine simultaneously, their memory and compute demands interact in non-obvious ways. This paper proposes a static resource budget model that takes as inputs the compressor's working-set size, the inference model's layer dimensions, and the microcontroller's SRAM/flash/cycle budget, and outputs a Pareto frontier of achievable compression ratio versus inference accuracy trade-offs. We instantiate the model for four compressor types (DPCM, PLA, Haar, dictionary) and three classifier sizes (16, 64, 256 parameters) on two RISC-V targets: GD32VF103 and ESP32-C3. Empirical validation on an air-quality monitoring workload (6 sensors, 1 Hz) shows the model predicts achieved compression ratio within ±7% and classification accuracy within ±2 percentage points across 48 configuration combinations. The paper also discusses memory-bank partitioning strategies that reduce SRAM contention between the two tasks by 23% without hardware modification.

SYN-PUB-07302.title: Quantisation Error Propagation in Cascaded Lossy Compression Stages for Multi-Hop IoT Pipelines
SYN-PUB-07302.text:
Quantisation Error Propagation in Cascaded Lossy Compression Stages for Multi-Hop IoT Pipelines (2022, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Stefan Lukić (outside co-author); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author); Radovan Obradović (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: quantisation error propagation; multi-hop; cascade compression; vector quantisation; transform coding.
In multi-hop sensor networks, data may be compressed at the originating node, partially decompressed and re-compressed at relay nodes, and finally decoded at a gateway. This paper analyses quantisation error accumulation across up to five cascade stages for three compressor families: scalar quantisation, vector quantisation, and transform coding. We derive recurrence relations for mean-square error under additive quantisation noise assumptions and validate these analytically against Monte Carlo simulations (10 000 runs per configuration) using synthetic AR(2) sensor traces. For scalar quantisation with uniform step size, error after five stages reaches 4.7 times the single-stage distortion; the proposed stage-aware bit-rate allocation, which front-loads precision to early hops, caps the same metric at 2.1 times. Practical guidelines are given for selecting per-hop quantisation step sizes given a gateway reconstruction target and a network energy budget. The paper includes a worked example for a three-hop soil moisture network consistent with LoRa hardware constraints.

SYN-PUB-07303.title: TENT: A Tiny Entropy-Coded Transform for Ultra-Low-Power Sub-Threshold Microcontrollers
SYN-PUB-07303.text:
TENT: A Tiny Entropy-Coded Transform for Ultra-Low-Power Sub-Threshold Microcontrollers (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs).
Authors: Lukas Hofer (outside co-author); Bojana Milošević (outside co-author); Branislav Stojanović (R0641).
Keywords: sub-threshold; integer DCT; Huffman coding; ASIC; ultra-low power; 65 nm CMOS.
Sub-threshold microcontrollers operating at supply voltages below 0.5 V achieve pico-joule-per-cycle energy figures but impose extreme constraints on code size and arithmetic complexity. This paper introduces TENT, a lightweight integer transform followed by a two-symbol static Huffman coder, implemented entirely within 1.4 kB of flash and 256 bytes of SRAM on a custom ASIC test chip fabricated in 65 nm CMOS running at 50 kHz and 0.4 V. TENT applies a 4-point integer approximation to a discrete cosine transform using only additions and one-bit shifts, quantises coefficients with a three-level dead-zone quantiser, and encodes symbols using a precomputed 16-entry Huffman table stored in ROM. On temperature, pressure, and light sensor streams sampled at 0.1 Hz, TENT achieves compression ratios of 3.1:1 to 5.8:1 at per-sample energy of 48 pJ. The paper presents silicon measurement results alongside a software reference implementation validated on an ARM Cortex-M0+.

SYN-PUB-07502.title: Goodness-of-fit testing for bivariate extreme value copulas via the Pickands dependence function
SYN-PUB-07502.text:
Goodness-of-fit testing for bivariate extreme value copulas via the Pickands dependence function (2010, conference, Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics — Balkans Region Workshop Proceedings).
Authors: Miroslav Jevtić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: Pickands dependence function; extreme value copulas; goodness-of-fit; parametric bootstrap; Hüsler–Reiss model.
Bivariate extreme value copulas are characterised by their Pickands dependence function A, which must satisfy convexity and boundary constraints. Several nonparametric estimators of A have been proposed in the literature, but their use in formal goodness-of-fit testing has received limited attention. This paper derives a Cramér–von Mises test statistic based on the distance between a parametric estimate of A under the logistic, negative logistic and Hüsler–Reiss models and a boundary-corrected nonparametric estimate. The finite-sample distribution of the statistic under the null hypothesis is approximated by a parametric bootstrap procedure with B = 9999 replicates. A simulation study covering sample sizes n = 50, 100, 250 and 500 shows that the test achieves nominal size and competitive power against misspecified models. The procedure is applied to annual maximum daily precipitation and wind speed at three weather stations in the Western Balkans, where the Hüsler–Reiss model is selected at two of the three sites.

SYN-PUB-07503.title: Estimating bivariate return periods for compound drought–heat events using an elliptical copula approach
SYN-PUB-07503.text:
Estimating bivariate return periods for compound drought–heat events using an elliptical copula approach (2012, journal, International Journal of Climatology and Risk).
Authors: Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Konstantin Balog (outside co-author); Rolf Seeberg (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: compound events; SPI; Student-t copula; bivariate return period; Pannonian Plain.
Compound drought–heat events cause disproportionate impacts on agriculture and human health relative to either hazard individually. Using monthly standardised precipitation index (SPI-3) and maximum temperature anomaly data from 1960 to 2009 for 14 stations across the Pannonian Plain, this study fits Gaussian and Student-t copulas to model the dependence between drought severity and concurrent heat intensity. The Student-t copula with estimated degrees-of-freedom parameter ν̂ = 4.1 fits better than the Gaussian copula at the majority of stations, indicating heavier joint tail behaviour. Bivariate return periods in the Kendall sense and in the survival copula sense are computed and compared. Results indicate that Kendall return periods exceed univariate return periods by a factor of 1.3 to 2.1 for moderate events but converge toward univariate values for very rare events. A regionalisation using hierarchical clustering identifies three coherent zones across the domain.

SYN-PUB-07504.title: Vine copula models for multivariate dependence in a network of Danube basin river gauges
SYN-PUB-07504.text:
Vine copula models for multivariate dependence in a network of Danube basin river gauges (2014, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Bojan Đurić (outside co-author); Ingrid Håkon (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: vine copulas; R-vine; river discharge; multivariate flood risk; Danube.
Multivariate flood risk assessment requires joint models for discharge at several gauging stations simultaneously. Regular vine copulae (R-vines) decompose a multivariate distribution into a cascade of bivariate pair copulae and offer flexibility that no single parametric family can match. Discharge records from nine stations along the Danube corridor and its main tributaries within Serbia (1970–2010) were standardised to unit Fréchet margins. An R-vine structure was selected using the minimum spanning tree algorithm applied to pairwise empirical Kendall τ values. Each pair copula family was chosen from a candidate set of twelve families by the Akaike information criterion. Out-of-sample predictive performance was evaluated using a conditional probability scoring rule on withheld data from 2000–2010. The fitted vine model assigned non-negligible probability to simultaneous high-discharge events across all nine stations, whereas a meta-Gaussian model underestimated this probability by a factor of approximately three. Simulated 10 000-year realisations from the fitted vine are provided for use in hydraulic engineering design.

SYN-PUB-07505.title: Extreme value copulas
SYN-PUB-07505.text:
Extreme value copulas (2016, book chapter, Handbook of Statistical Methods in Environmental Sciences, Chapter 8, Edited by T. Bartha and K. Szabó, Pécs University Press).
Authors: Miroslav Jevtić (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: extreme value copulas; Pickands representation; max-stable processes; parametric estimation; spatial extremes.
This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of the class of extreme value copulas arising as the limiting dependence structures of componentwise block maxima. The Pickands representation theorem is stated and proved, and its implications for the parametric subfamilies — logistic, asymmetric logistic, Galambos and Hüsler–Reiss — are derived. Estimation methods including maximum likelihood, the method of moments via Kendall's tau, and nonparametric estimators of the Pickands function are compared with respect to bias and variance in a comprehensive simulation study. The chapter includes a treatment of the connection between extreme value copulas and max-stable random fields, which is relevant for spatial modelling of environmental extremes. Three worked examples using Balkan precipitation and temperature data illustrate the methods. The chapter is intended for graduate students and researchers with a background in mathematical statistics.

SYN-PUB-07506.title: Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of compound flood–wind events at the Serbian Danube reach
SYN-PUB-07506.text:
Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of compound flood–wind events at the Serbian Danube reach (2017, journal, Extremes: Statistical Theory and Applications in Science, Engineering and Economics).
Authors: Nataša Todorović (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Carlo Ventura (outside co-author).
Keywords: peaks-over-threshold; generalised Pareto distribution; bivariate extremes; threshold selection; Galambos copula.
The peaks-over-threshold (POT) method requires selection of a threshold above which observations are modelled by the generalised Pareto distribution. In the bivariate context, both variables must exceed respective thresholds simultaneously or separately depending on the risk definition. This paper evaluates five threshold selection diagnostics — mean residual life plots, parameter stability plots, and three automated criteria based on goodness-of-fit — applied to concurrent records of river discharge and mean daily wind speed at five stations on the Serbian Danube reach (1980–2015). The copula of the bivariate exceedances is modelled with a censored-likelihood approach that accounts for observations exceeding only one threshold. Results show that the Galambos copula fits the bivariate extremes well (upper tail dependence coefficient 0.22–0.35) and that threshold choice materially affects estimated joint return levels: a 10 percent increase in threshold reduces the estimated 200-year joint quantile by up to 18 percent. Guidance for practitioners is provided.

SYN-PUB-07507.title: Comparing parametric and nonparametric multivariate quantile contour estimation under copula misspecification
SYN-PUB-07507.text:
Comparing parametric and nonparametric multivariate quantile contour estimation under copula misspecification (2021, journal, Statistical Papers).
Authors: Miroslav Jevtić (outside co-author); Ondřej Hlávka (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: multivariate quantile contours; return period analysis; depth functions; copula misspecification; nonparametric estimation.
Multivariate quantile contours — level sets of a joint distribution at a given probability level — are central to multivariate return period analysis but sensitive to model misspecification. This simulation study compares five estimators: the Kendall quantile contour under three parametric copula families (Gaussian, Clayton, Gumbel–Hougaard), the geometric quantile estimator of Chaudhuri and the depth-based Tukey median contour estimated by the Donoho–Gasko algorithm. Data are generated from six dependence structures at sample sizes n = 100, 300, 500, 1000, with standard Gumbel margins. Performance is measured by the integrated squared Hausdorff distance between estimated and true contours. Parametric estimators outperform nonparametric competitors when the model is correctly specified, but nonparametric depth-based contours exhibit substantially lower worst-case error across misspecified scenarios. A data-driven selection rule combining a copula goodness-of-fit test with a nonparametric fallback is proposed and evaluated on a subset of Serbian environmental monitoring data.

SYN-PUB-07508.title: Modelling the joint distribution of extreme wildfire weather indices in Serbia using time-varying copulas
SYN-PUB-07508.text:
Modelling the joint distribution of extreme wildfire weather indices in Serbia using time-varying copulas (2022, journal, International Journal of Wildland Fire).
Authors: Milena Radović (outside co-author); Sanja Konjević (outside co-author); Hanna Lehtonen (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: wildfire weather indices; non-stationary copulas; time-varying dependence; GEV; climate change.
Climate change is shifting the distributional properties of wildfire weather indices, so static copula models fitted over long historical periods may be inadequate for current risk assessments. Daily records of the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) components — Fine Fuel Moisture Code and Drought Code — from 18 stations in Serbia for 1961–2020 were used to investigate non-stationarity in both marginal distributions and dependence structure. Marginal parameters of the fitted GEV distributions were allowed to vary as smooth functions of a global temperature covariate using penalised spline regression. The copula dependence parameter was then estimated conditional on the same covariate using a local-likelihood approach with a Gaussian kernel. Estimated Kendall τ increased from approximately 0.31 in the 1960s to 0.48 in the 2010s, indicating strengthening co-occurrence of the two fire risk indicators. This trend implies that joint exceedance probabilities have roughly doubled over the observational record.

SYN-PUB-07509.title: Sensitivity of infrastructure failure probability to tail dependence assumptions: a case study for bridge foundations on the Sava River
SYN-PUB-07509.text:
Sensitivity of infrastructure failure probability to tail dependence assumptions: a case study for bridge foundations on the Sava River (2023, journal, Reliability Engineering and System Safety).
Authors: Predrag Nikolić (outside co-author); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: structural reliability; tail dependence sensitivity; bridge foundations; Sava River; limit-state function.
The structural reliability of bridge foundations in alluvial reaches depends jointly on peak discharge, scour depth and ice loading, three variables whose dependence in the extreme tails is poorly constrained by available data. This paper quantifies the sensitivity of estimated annual failure probability to the choice of tail dependence structure. A structural limit-state function for a simplified foundation model is combined with a joint hazard model in which the copula family is varied across six candidates spanning tail independence to strong upper tail dependence. The difference between the failure probability under the independence copula and under the upper-tail-dependent Gumbel–Hougaard copula with τ = 0.4 is approximately one order of magnitude at annual exceedance probability 10⁻⁴, a difference that is practically significant for design. A robust upper bound is obtained by taking the maximum over a class of copulas with matching Kendall τ.

SYN-PUB-07510.title: Bayesian estimation of C-vine copula parameters for high-dimensional environmental hazard vectors
SYN-PUB-07510.text:
Bayesian estimation of C-vine copula parameters for high-dimensional environmental hazard vectors (2024, preprint, arXiv preprint (submitted to Computational Statistics and Data Analysis)).
Authors: Vesna Stanković (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664); Pieter Van den Berg (outside co-author).
Keywords: C-vine copula; Bayesian inference; reversible-jump MCMC; high-dimensional dependence; Vojvodina.
C-vine copulas reduce the dimensionality problem in multivariate dependence modelling by expressing the joint density as a product of bivariate pair copulas arranged in a tree structure. When the dimension is moderate to high (here d = 8), maximum likelihood estimation of the full parameter vector becomes computationally burdensome and confidence intervals are poorly calibrated. This preprint proposes a blocked Gibbs sampler for posterior inference over C-vine structures and bivariate copula family indicators jointly, using a reversible-jump extension. Experiments on simulated data with n = 500 show that credible intervals for tail dependence coefficients have nominal coverage 3 to 8 percentage points closer to 95 percent than profile likelihood intervals. The method is applied to an eight-dimensional vector of hydrometeorological hazard indicators — discharge, precipitation intensity, wind speed, temperature anomaly, and four soil moisture metrics — observed simultaneously at a single representative site in the Bačka subregion of Vojvodina.

SYN-PUB-07511.title: A regional frequency analysis framework for multivariate compound events using spatial pooling and copula aggregation
SYN-PUB-07511.text:
A regional frequency analysis framework for multivariate compound events using spatial pooling and copula aggregation (2025, journal, Water Resources Research).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Éva Molnár (outside co-author); Radu Cojocaru (outside co-author); Tomáš Blaho (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: regional frequency analysis; compound events; Wasserstein barycenter; Danube basin; L-moments.
Regional frequency analysis (RFA) extends the information base for rare event estimation by pooling data from hydrologically homogeneous stations. Classical RFA applies to univariate distributions; this paper extends the L-moments approach to multivariate compound events by fitting station-specific copulas and aggregating them into a regional dependence structure using a weighted Wasserstein barycenter. Sixty-three stations in the middle Danube basin (Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia) contribute 40 to 95 years of simultaneous discharge and precipitation records. Homogeneity is assessed using a multivariate extension of the Hosking–Wallis H statistic. The regional copula reduces estimation uncertainty for joint return levels at ungauged locations compared to at-site estimation; the reduction in root-mean-square error for the 100-year bivariate quantile ranges from 23 to 41 percent depending on the region. The method is implemented in an open-source R package deposited at the University of Novi Sad data repository.

SYN-PUB-07512.title: Quantile regression forests for marginal standardisation in nonparametric multivariate extreme value analysis
SYN-PUB-07512.text:
Quantile regression forests for marginal standardisation in nonparametric multivariate extreme value analysis (2026, journal, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society — Series C (Applied Statistics)).
Authors: Sanja Konjević (outside co-author); Ondřej Hlávka (outside co-author); Jasmina Arsić (R0664).
Keywords: quantile regression forests; marginal standardisation; max-stable processes; discharge modelling; machine learning in extremes.
Transforming raw observations to uniform or Fréchet margins is a necessary preprocessing step in most copula-based extreme value analyses, and the quality of this transformation influences downstream inference. Standard empirical probability integral transforms perform poorly in sparse tails. This paper proposes using quantile regression forests to estimate marginal conditional distribution functions that adapt to covariate information — elevation, land use, catchment area — thereby improving tail standardisation at environmental monitoring stations. The approach is evaluated in a leave-one-out cross-validation on 44 discharge stations in Serbia and Croatia. After forest-based standardisation, the residual dependence structure is more stable across stations and seasons than after empirical-transform standardisation: the interquartile range of estimated pairwise Kendall τ values shrinks by 19 percent. The standardised residuals are then used as input to a Brown–Resnick max-stable model fitted by pairwise composite likelihood, which yields a 12 percent reduction in the composite likelihood information criterion relative to the baseline approach.

SYN-PUB-07520.title: Modal Parameter Extraction from Welded Steel Portal Frames Under Ambient Excitation
SYN-PUB-07520.text:
Modal Parameter Extraction from Welded Steel Portal Frames Under Ambient Excitation (2012, journal, Journal of Mechanical Engineering Research and Applications).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: operational modal analysis; SSI; weld defect; ambient vibration; portal frame.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07522.title: Comparison of Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Stochastic Subspace Identification for Damage Localization in Multi-Bay Steel Frames
SYN-PUB-07522.text:
Comparison of Frequency-Domain Decomposition and Stochastic Subspace Identification for Damage Localization in Multi-Bay Steel Frames (2015, journal, Journal of Vibration Diagnostics and Structural Integrity).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Attila Varga (outside co-author).
Keywords: FDD; SSI-COV; damage index; multi-bay frame; damage localization.
Two widely used OMA algorithms—frequency-domain decomposition (FDD) and stochastic subspace identification (SSI-COV)—are compared for their ability to localize damage in a three-bay, two-storey welded steel frame model. Damage was simulated by progressively cutting a weld in the lower right column-beam connection in three stages, reducing net throat area by 20%, 40%, and 60%. Ambient excitation was provided by pedestrian-like loading applied at the floor levels. Both algorithms identified natural frequencies within 0.15 Hz of each other for the first six modes. Damage localization was assessed via the modal strain energy damage index (MSEDI). SSI-COV achieved correct panel identification at 20% damage in 7 of 10 repeated trials, while FDD achieved correct localization in only 4 of 10 at the same damage level. At 40% and 60% damage, both methods localized correctly in all trials. The study recommends SSI-COV for early-stage damage detection when signal-to-noise conditions are moderate.

SYN-PUB-07523.title: Temperature Effects on Modal Parameters of Welded Steel Frame Structures: A Seasonal Monitoring Study
SYN-PUB-07523.text:
Temperature Effects on Modal Parameters of Welded Steel Frame Structures: A Seasonal Monitoring Study (2017, journal, Structural Monitoring and Maintenance).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author); Svetlana Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: temperature compensation; continuous monitoring; industrial rack structure; environmental variability; OMA.
Environmental temperature variation is a known source of false alarms in vibration-based structural health monitoring systems. This paper reports a 14-month continuous monitoring campaign on a full-scale welded steel storage rack structure at an industrial facility in Zrenjanin, during which ambient temperature ranged from −14 °C to +38 °C. Twelve accelerometers and four temperature sensors were installed. OMA was performed on 30-minute data windows using SSI-COV. The first natural frequency varied by up to 4.3% over the monitoring period, primarily correlated with temperature (Pearson r = −0.81). A linear regression model was fitted to remove temperature effects from frequency trends; residuals were examined for anomalies. No structural damage occurred during the campaign, confirming the temperature model captured the dominant environmental influence. The study provides a temperature-compensation baseline that can support future damage detection in similar industrial steel structures in the Pannonian climate zone.

SYN-PUB-07524.title: Laser Vibrometry Measurements of Weld-Zone Mode Shapes in Thin-Walled Steel Box Sections
SYN-PUB-07524.text:
Laser Vibrometry Measurements of Weld-Zone Mode Shapes in Thin-Walled Steel Box Sections (2018, conference, Proceedings of the 14th European Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation, Prague).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Radovan Stupar (outside co-author).
Keywords: laser Doppler vibrometry; thin-walled box section; lack of fusion; operational deflection shape; wavelet energy.
Conventional accelerometer grids cannot resolve high-spatial-resolution mode shapes in thin-walled welded box sections without adding significant mass. This paper uses a scanning laser Doppler vibrometer (SLDV) to measure operational deflection shapes at 320 scan points on three box-section specimens (wall thickness 4 mm, 6 mm, and 8 mm) under harmonic excitation at frequencies corresponding to the first five bending and torsional modes. Specimens were fabricated with identical nominal welds; one specimen per thickness group contained an artificial internal lack-of-fusion defect of 12 mm length introduced by inserting a 0.3 mm Teflon insert during fabrication. The SLDV measurements revealed localized amplitude anomalies of 8–23% at the defect location for the 4 mm and 6 mm specimens at modes 3 and 4, while the 8 mm specimen showed no detectable anomaly. Mass loading from a hypothetical 4-accelerometer grid would have shifted frequencies by up to 2.1%, justifying the non-contact approach. Fractional wavelet energy maps derived from the velocity fields improved defect contrast over raw mode shape images.

SYN-PUB-07525.title: Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring of Steel Structures: Methods and Practical Considerations
SYN-PUB-07525.text:
Vibration-Based Structural Health Monitoring of Steel Structures: Methods and Practical Considerations (2019, book chapter, Handbook of Structural Integrity Assessment for Industrial Facilities, TechPress Bratislava).
Authors: Miroslav Kovačević (outside co-author); Attila Varga (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Petra Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: SHM review; steel structures; sensor placement; damage index; long-term monitoring.
