This book chapter reviews the application of vibration-based SHM to steel civil and industrial structures, with emphasis on welded connections. The chapter covers the theoretical basis of modal analysis, sensor placement strategies, algorithm selection criteria, and the practical challenges of long-term monitoring including power supply, data transmission, and environmental compensation. Case studies drawn from laboratory and field experience in the Western Balkans region illustrate typical damage scenarios (weld cracking, corrosion-induced stiffness loss, fatigue-related loosening) and the sensitivity of common damage indices to each. Particular attention is given to structures with irregular geometry or asymmetric boundary conditions, where standard damage localization indices can give misleading results. The chapter concludes with a discussion of open problems, including the scarcity of labeled field damage datasets and the difficulty of transferring laboratory-calibrated models to field conditions.

SYN-PUB-07526.title: Detection of Fatigue Crack Initiation in Fillet-Welded T-Joints Using Damping Ratio Tracking
SYN-PUB-07526.text:
Detection of Fatigue Crack Initiation in Fillet-Welded T-Joints Using Damping Ratio Tracking (2020, journal, International Journal of Fatigue and Structural Diagnostics).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Svetlana Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: damping ratio; fatigue crack; T-joint; fillet weld; half-power bandwidth.
Changes in damping ratio are hypothesized to be more sensitive to early-stage crack initiation than frequency shifts, but damping estimation is highly variable. This paper investigates the feasibility of tracking damping ratios as a damage indicator in fillet-welded T-joint specimens subjected to cyclic three-point bending fatigue loading. Eight specimens of S275 steel were cycled at 60% and 75% of their static failure load. OMA data were collected at intervals of 5,000 load cycles. Damping ratios for the first bending mode, estimated by the half-power bandwidth method and by SSI-COV, were compared. SSI-COV estimates showed standard deviations approximately 40% lower than half-power bandwidth estimates. Damping ratios increased detectably (>2σ above baseline) at approximately 35–40% of total fatigue life at 75% load, preceding a measurable frequency drop by roughly 8,000 cycles. At 60% load, no consistent damping increase was detected prior to visible crack formation. Results suggest that damping tracking may provide early warning in moderate-to-high stress fatigue scenarios.

SYN-PUB-07527.title: Baseline-Free Damage Detection in Welded Steel Trusses Using Transmissibility Functions
SYN-PUB-07527.text:
Baseline-Free Damage Detection in Welded Steel Trusses Using Transmissibility Functions (2022, journal, Mechanical Systems and Structural Diagnostics).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Radovan Stupar (outside co-author); Marko Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: transmissibility function; baseline-free; Pratt truss; damage localization; transmissibility damage index.
Transmissibility-based methods do not require a pristine baseline measurement, making them attractive for structures where an undamaged reference state was never recorded. This paper evaluates a transmissibility-function damage indicator on three laboratory-scale welded Pratt-type steel truss specimens. Each truss had 11 joints; damage was introduced at single joints by partially cutting the weld of one diagonal member to depths of 1, 2, and 3 mm. Transmissibility functions were computed between all sensor-pair combinations (15 pairs from 6 accelerometers) under broadband random excitation. A transmissibility damage index (TDI) based on the Euclidean norm of transmissibility differences between two arbitrary operating conditions was computed. Correct damage localization was achieved in 18 of 21 test cases (86%) across all damage levels and joint positions. Failed cases were concentrated at joints near the support conditions. Comparison with the modal strain energy method showed similar localization accuracy but lower computational demand for TDI. The approach requires no FE model and no undamaged reference.

SYN-PUB-07528.title: Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Continuous Vibration Monitoring of a Welded Steel Overhead Crane Girder
SYN-PUB-07528.text:
Low-Cost Wireless Sensor Network for Continuous Vibration Monitoring of a Welded Steel Overhead Crane Girder (2023, journal, Sensors and Structural Monitoring Letters).
Authors: Nemanja Tešić (outside co-author); Branislav Nikolić (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Maja Ristić (R0939); Petra Novák (outside co-author).
Keywords: wireless sensor network; MEMS accelerometer; crane girder; weld fatigue crack; automated OMA.
Overhead crane girders in production halls undergo repetitive dynamic loading from hoisting operations and are susceptible to weld fatigue at rail attachment points. This paper describes the design, installation, and 18-month operation of a low-cost wireless accelerometer network (8 nodes, MEMS sensors, 1 kHz sampling) installed on a 22-metre span welded box-girder crane at a metalworking company in Zrenjanin. Data were transmitted to a local edge device and processed using automated SSI-COV at each hoisting event. Over 3,400 events were recorded. The first bending frequency showed a gradual decrease of 0.9% over the monitoring period; post-campaign visual inspection revealed a 28 mm weld fatigue crack at one rail attachment. Frequency changes tracked the estimated crack length progression using a fracture mechanics model calibrated to the geometry. System power consumption averaged 220 mW per node. The study demonstrates that MEMS-based wireless networks can detect slow-growing weld fatigue cracks in crane girders under purely operational loading.

SYN-PUB-07529.title: Principal Component Analysis of Long-Term Modal Data for Anomaly Detection in an Industrial Steel Frame: Influence of Operational Load Patterns
SYN-PUB-07529.text:
Principal Component Analysis of Long-Term Modal Data for Anomaly Detection in an Industrial Steel Frame: Influence of Operational Load Patterns (2024, journal, Journal of Structural Health Monitoring and Condition Assessment).
Authors: Radovan Stupar (outside co-author); Jelena Jokić (R0666); Attila Varga (outside co-author); Nemanja Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: PCA; statistical process control; long-term monitoring; mezzanine frame; anomaly detection.
Statistical process control methods applied to long-term SHM data must account not only for environmental variability but also for systematic changes in operational loads such as storage fill levels or production-line traffic. This paper applies principal component analysis (PCA) to a 22-month dataset of modal parameters (12 frequency and 8 damping estimates per measurement epoch) collected from a welded steel mezzanine frame in a logistics warehouse in the Novi Sad industrial zone. Ambient excitation was provided by forklift traffic. Temperature, humidity, and floor load (estimated from a weigh-bridge log) were recorded simultaneously. A PCA model trained on the first 6 months of data reduced the feature vector to 3 principal components explaining 87% of variance. Control charts on the residuals flagged three anomalous periods; two corresponded to planned maintenance (bolt retightening), and one corresponded to a previously unreported localized weld crack found during the subsequent annual inspection. False alarm rate over the remaining 16 months was 3.1%, comparable to the 5% control limit set.

SYN-PUB-07530.title: Modal Testing Protocol for Welded Steel Frame Structures in Active Industrial Environments: Repeatability and Interference Assessment
SYN-PUB-07530.text:
Modal Testing Protocol for Welded Steel Frame Structures in Active Industrial Environments: Repeatability and Interference Assessment (2026, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Structural Health Monitoring and Integrity Assessment, Ljubljana).
Authors: Jelena Jokić (R0666); Siniša Petrov (outside co-author); Theodora Ionescu (outside co-author).
Keywords: testing protocol; repeatability; effective independence; industrial environment; standardization.
Performing modal tests in operating industrial environments introduces variability from background machinery noise, temperature gradients, and measurement interruptions. This paper proposes and evaluates a standardized testing protocol designed to maximize repeatability under such conditions. The protocol specifies sensor placement rules based on effective independence (EFI) criteria, a minimum recording duration formula as a function of the target frequency resolution and lowest expected natural frequency, and a quality-control step using automated pole stabilization diagrams with human-review triggers. The protocol was validated on five distinct welded steel frame types at three industrial sites in Vojvodina over a period of two years, with two operators per site performing independent tests within 48 hours of each other. Inter-operator repeatability of estimated natural frequencies was within 0.4% for all structures and all modes up to the sixth. Damping ratio repeatability was within 12% of the mean value for 89% of identified modes. The protocol is described in sufficient detail to be reproducible without specialized training beyond standard OMA software familiarity.

SYN-PUB-07783.title: Partition-Aware Inverted Index Construction for Heterogeneous Document Streams
SYN-PUB-07783.text:
Partition-Aware Inverted Index Construction for Heterogeneous Document Streams (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Information Retrieval (CECIR)).
Authors: Miroslav Bjelogrlić (outside co-author); Darko Vukelić (outside co-author); Radovan Radulović (R0694); Snežana Todorović (R0741).
Keywords: inverted index; stream indexing; index partitioning; multilingual.
This paper addresses the challenge of building inverted indexes over document streams that vary widely in language, length, and encoding. We propose a partition-aware construction algorithm that assigns incoming documents to index shards based on a lightweight language-and-length feature hash, reducing cross-shard query fan-out by approximately 34% compared to round-robin partitioning on a corpus of 12 million news articles drawn from four Balkan-language feeds. Index build time on a six-node cluster decreased by 18% while median query latency fell from 47 ms to 31 ms at the 50th percentile. The approach requires no prior knowledge of the full corpus distribution and adapts incrementally as stream statistics shift. Experiments use Apache Lucene as the underlying segment engine, with a custom coordinator layer implemented in Java. Recall at rank 10 remains within 0.4% of a monolithic baseline.

SYN-PUB-07802.title: Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity
SYN-PUB-07802.text:
Wake-up receiver circuit for asynchronous event-driven body-area networks: design and measured sensitivity (2021, journal, Microelectronics Journal).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Aleksandar Jeremić (R0696).
Keywords: wake-up receiver; asynchronous MAC; envelope detector; 868 MHz; event-driven sensing.
Polling-based duty cycling requires a node to activate its main radio at fixed intervals regardless of whether data are ready, wasting energy between physiological events. A wake-up receiver (WuRx) circuit that remains continuously active at very low power can replace this periodic wakeup. This paper presents a WuRx designed in 130 nm CMOS consuming 4.2 µW from a 1.0 V supply. The circuit uses an envelope detector followed by a three-stage comparator with hysteresis to decode an amplitude-shift-keyed wake-up beacon at 868 MHz. Measured sensitivity was −62 dBm at a target false-alarm rate of one per hour. Selectivity to adjacent channels was verified in a shielded box with an interferer 3 MHz offset at levels up to −20 dBm. Die area was 0.19 mm². When integrated into a complete sensor node alongside a CC1310 main radio, the WuRx reduced mean idle-state current from 18.4 µA (timer-based duty cycle at 1% duty) to 6.7 µA under a traffic model representative of a cardiac event monitor with bursts averaging twice per hour.

SYN-PUB-07834.title: Geostatistical merging of rain-gauge and C-band radar data over the Pannonian Plain: a variogram-based approach
SYN-PUB-07834.text:
Geostatistical merging of rain-gauge and C-band radar data over the Pannonian Plain: a variogram-based approach (2012, journal, Journal of Hydrometeorology and Remote Sensing).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Mirjana Vuković (outside co-author); Klaus Steiner (outside co-author).
Keywords: kriging with external drift; C-band radar; rain-gauge merging; Pannonian Plain; flash flood.
Accurate precipitation estimates over flat terrain such as the Pannonian Plain are constrained by the low density of surface rain-gauge networks and the range-dependent errors of single-polarisation C-band radars. This study applies ordinary kriging with external drift (KED) to merge hourly rain-gauge observations from 47 stations in Vojvodina with composited reflectivity data from the Serbian RHMSS radar network during the summer convective seasons of 2007–2009. Empirical variograms were fitted using an exponential model after systematic bias correction of the radar field via mean-field adjustment. Cross-validation against withheld gauge stations showed a reduction in root-mean-square error of 31% compared to radar-only estimates and 18% compared to gauge-only kriging. Spatial correlation ranges of 35–60 km were identified for convective events, substantially shorter than for stratiform precipitation. The merged product was tested against an independent flash-flood inventory for the Fruška Gora foothills, showing improved hit rates for events exceeding 20 mm h⁻¹. Results confirm that KED merging is viable operationally even with sparse station networks typical of the western Balkans.

SYN-PUB-07835.title: Просторна варијабилност интензитета конвективних олуја у Војводини на основу мреже дистрометара
SYN-PUB-07835.text:
Просторна варијабилност интензитета конвективних олуја у Војводини на основу мреже дистрометара (2013, journal, Гласник Географског друштва Републике Српске).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Бојана Лазић (outside co-author); Немања Чуп (outside co-author).
Keywords: дистрометар; DSD; Z–R релација; конвективне олује; Војводина.
У раду је анализирана просторна варијабилност интензитета падавина током девет конвективних епизода у Војводини у периоду 2010–2011. на основу мреже од шеснаест оптичких дистрометара типа ОТТ Парсивел размештених на растојању 5–40 км. Измерени параметри расподеле капљица (DSD) коришћени су за проверу Z–R релација добијених за радарске снимке РХМЗС мреже. Утврђено је да стандардна Маршал–Палмерова релација потцењује акумулацију за 15–28% у највећим ћелијама организованих мезоскалних конвективних система. Предложена је регионално калибрисана релација Z = 270R¹·⁵², чијом применом је RMSE смањен на 2,4 mm у поређењу са 4,1 mm код стандардне релације. Резултати указују на значај регионалне калибрације за оперативну хидрологију.

SYN-PUB-07836.title: Detection of hail-bearing convective cells using dual-polarisation radar signatures and MSG SEVIRI infrared channels
SYN-PUB-07836.text:
Detection of hail-bearing convective cells using dual-polarisation radar signatures and MSG SEVIRI infrared channels (2015, journal, Atmospheric Measurement Techniques and Applications).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Andrea Marchetti (outside co-author); Немања Чуп (outside co-author); Тамара Јовановић (outside co-author).
Keywords: dual-polarisation radar; hail detection; SEVIRI; cell tracking; Balkans.
This study presents a cell-tracking algorithm that fuses dual-polarisation C-band radar parameters with Meteosat Second Generation SEVIRI brightness temperatures to identify hail-bearing convective cells over Serbia and northern Bosnia-Herzegovina. Radar-derived variables — differential reflectivity ZDR, co-polar correlation coefficient ρHV, and specific differential phase KDP — were combined with 10.8 µm and 6.2 µm channel data at 15-minute temporal resolution. A decision-tree classifier trained on 78 hail reports collected during 2011–2014 achieved a probability of detection of 0.81 and a false alarm ratio of 0.23 in leave-one-season-out validation. Detected cells were tracked using a modified TITAN algorithm over a 400 × 400 km domain. The resulting dataset of 312 hail-cell trajectories reveals a pronounced SW–NE advection corridor across the Pannonian sector, consistent with regional synoptic climatology. Cell life spans ranged from 18 to 94 minutes, with median maximum reflectivity of 58 dBZ. The fused approach outperformed single-source detection in both probability of detection and cell continuity.

SYN-PUB-07839.title: Integrating Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter and rain-gauge data for post-event surface inundation mapping in the Sava River floodplain
SYN-PUB-07839.text:
Integrating Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter and rain-gauge data for post-event surface inundation mapping in the Sava River floodplain (2019, journal, Remote Sensing of Environment and Hydrology).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Bojana Stajić (outside co-author); Péter Halász (outside co-author).
Keywords: Sentinel-1; SAR; flood mapping; Sava River; backscatter change detection.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07840.title: Fusion of multi-frequency passive microwave and infrared satellite retrievals for sub-daily precipitation estimation over the Dinaric–Pannonian transition zone
SYN-PUB-07840.text:
Fusion of multi-frequency passive microwave and infrared satellite retrievals for sub-daily precipitation estimation over the Dinaric–Pannonian transition zone (2020, journal, Journal of Applied Remote Sensing and Meteorology).
Authors: Florin Moldovan (outside co-author); Тамара Јовановић (outside co-author); Бојана Стајић (outside co-author); Jasmina Jakovljević (R0898); Дарко Тошић (R0700).
Keywords: GPM IMERG; passive microwave; SEVIRI; blending; convection.
Passive microwave (PMW) precipitation retrievals from the GPM constellation provide physically meaningful rain-rate estimates but suffer from low revisit frequency (2–4 h) over mid-latitudes. This paper presents a weighted blending scheme that combines half-hourly IMERG Late Run precipitation fields with SEVIRI infrared-based motion-vector extrapolations to produce 15-minute precipitation estimates over a 600 × 600 km domain spanning the Dinaric–Pannonian transition. Blending weights were determined by a spatially varying skill score derived from three years of gauge verification data. Against an independent 2020 verification dataset, the blended product reduced false alarm rates for events above 10 mm h⁻¹ by 22% relative to IMERG alone, while maintaining the spatial coherence of large-scale precipitation features. Systematic underestimation of deep convective cores, documented in earlier IMERG studies, was partially corrected by incorporating column-maximum reflectivity from operational radars as a secondary predictor. Seasonal analysis shows the largest skill gains in June–August, when fast-evolving supercell storms constitute a majority of extreme events in the study domain.

SYN-PUB-07841.title: Probabilistic hail hazard maps for agricultural insurance: a radar-based approach for Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-07841.text:
Probabilistic hail hazard maps for agricultural insurance: a radar-based approach for Vojvodina (2021, journal, Natural Hazards and Agricultural Risk Assessment).
Authors: Небојша Поповић (outside co-author); Claudia Hörner (outside co-author); Дарко Тошић (R0700).
Keywords: hail hazard; MESH; agricultural insurance; kernel density; Vojvodina.
Agricultural losses from convective hail in Vojvodina represent a recurrent economic hazard affecting the region's dominant cereal and vegetable production. This study develops probabilistic hail hazard maps at 1 km resolution using a 15-year (2005–2019) archive of dual-polarisation radar data processed with the cell-tracking algorithm described in earlier work. For each identified hail trajectory, kinetic energy proxies were derived from maximum expected size of hail (MESH) estimates. Kernel density estimation was applied to produce continuous hail frequency surfaces. GEV distribution fitting at pixel level yielded 10-, 25-, and 50-year return-period MESH maps. The maps were validated against parcel-level crop loss reports provided by the insurance cooperative Vojvodina Agro-Protect covering 14,000 parcels over 2015–2019. Concordance between high-hazard zones and observed loss frequencies was evaluated with the Spearman rank correlation (ρ = 0.67, p < 0.001). Spatial clustering of high-hazard areas is statistically significant (Moran's I = 0.43), supporting the use of these maps for zone-based premium differentiation rather than uniform province-wide rates.

SYN-PUB-07842.title: Evaluation of a random forest downscaling model for daily precipitation from ERA5 reanalysis over the Carpathian–Pannonian region
SYN-PUB-07842.text:
Evaluation of a random forest downscaling model for daily precipitation from ERA5 reanalysis over the Carpathian–Pannonian region (2022, journal, Geoscientific Model Development and Evaluation).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Ágnes Kovács-Varga (outside co-author); Бојана Стајић (outside co-author); Milán Tóth (outside co-author).
Keywords: statistical downscaling; random forest; ERA5; precipitation; Pannonian region.
ERA5 reanalysis provides spatially complete precipitation fields at 31 km resolution, but this coarseness is insufficient for catchment-scale hazard assessment. This paper evaluates a random forest (RF) model that statistically downscales ERA5 daily precipitation to a 5 km grid using terrain elevation, land cover, distance to major water bodies, and upper-air predictors as features. Training used 780 station-days from a dense network in Hungary, Romania, and Serbia (2000–2015), with spatial cross-validation across five geographic blocks. In the validation period (2016–2020) the RF model achieved a continuous rank probability score 18% lower than bilinear interpolation and correctly reproduced 91% of the spatial pattern variance for events exceeding the 95th percentile. However, peak intensities in convective grid cells were systematically underestimated by 12–19%, a limitation attributed to the representativeness mismatch between point gauge observations and ERA5 large-scale fields. The model is made available as a Python package with pre-trained weights for the study domain.

SYN-PUB-07843.title: Резултати примене производа мреже метеоролошких радара РХМЗС у систему за рано упозорење на поплаве у Сремском округу
SYN-PUB-07843.text:
Резултати примене производа мреже метеоролошких радара РХМЗС у систему за рано упозорење на поплаве у Сремском округу (2023, conference, Конференција о водама Србије — Зборник радова).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Горан Обрадовић (outside co-author); Srđan Korolija (outside co-author).
Keywords: QPE; систем за рано упозорење; хидролошки модел; Сремски округ; оперативна хидрологија.
У раду су приказани резултати двогодишњег тестирања система за рано упозорење на изненадне поплаве у Сремском округу заснованог на оперативним производима радарске мреже Републичког хидрометеоролошког завода Србије. Систем комбинује QPE (quantitative precipitation estimation) производе у реалном времену са хидролошким моделом ТОПМОДЕЛ прилагођеним за шест малих сливова брдске Посавине. Прагови упозорења дефинисани су на основу фреквентне анализе падавина из дугогодишњег архивског низа. У периоду тестирања (2021–2022) систем је генерисао 23 упозорења, од чега је 19 коресподирало са забележеним надлевањима водотокова или пријавама штете. Средње предупређујуће време износило је 47 минута. Лажне узбуне везују се претежно за рефлективност из прелетних конвективних ћелија ниске основе облака које нису дале значајне падавине на тлу. Предложено је увођење дополнске верификације путем мреже нисконошћних сензора влажности тла.

SYN-PUB-07844.title: A benchmark dataset and baseline models for convective storm cell segmentation from composite radar reflectivity in South-East Europe
SYN-PUB-07844.text:
A benchmark dataset and baseline models for convective storm cell segmentation from composite radar reflectivity in South-East Europe (2025, journal, Earth System Science Data).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Бојана Стајић (outside co-author); Stefan Weidemann (outside co-author); Тамара Јовановић (outside co-author).
Keywords: storm cell segmentation; radar composite; U-Net; benchmark dataset; South-East Europe.
Automated segmentation of convective storm cells from composite radar reflectivity is a prerequisite for downstream hazard mapping workflows, yet no publicly available labelled dataset exists for the South-East European radar domain. This paper describes the construction of CONVBALK-2800, a dataset of 2,800 manually annotated composite reflectivity images from three operational C-band radars in Serbia covering 2010–2023, with polygonal labels for 14,620 individual convective cells. Three baseline segmentation approaches — watershed transform, U-Net, and an ensemble of watershed with a gradient-boosting cell-property classifier — are evaluated in five-fold cross-validation. The U-Net achieves the highest intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.74 for cells with equivalent radar reflectivity factor ≥ 45 dBZ but degrades to IoU = 0.51 for weak-cell fringe areas. Processing time per composite frame is 1.2 s on a single GPU, suitable for near-real-time use. The dataset and training scripts are released under an open licence to facilitate reproducible research. Known limitations include temporal clustering of labels and under-representation of nocturnal events.

SYN-PUB-07845.title: Temporal trends in convective precipitation intensity over the Pannonian Basin inferred from a homogenised multi-radar archive, 1998–2023
SYN-PUB-07845.text:
Temporal trends in convective precipitation intensity over the Pannonian Basin inferred from a homogenised multi-radar archive, 1998–2023 (2026, journal, Climate Dynamics and Extreme Weather).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Claudia Hörner (outside co-author); Florin Moldovan (outside co-author); Милош Ристић (outside co-author).
Keywords: trend analysis; radar homogenisation; Mann–Kendall; CAPE; Pannonian Basin.
Detection of long-term trends in convective precipitation intensity from radar archives is hampered by hardware upgrades, site relocations, and calibration discontinuities. This study applies a homogenisation procedure to the 25-year (1998–2023) Serbian composite radar archive using parallel rain-gauge records and reanalysis data as reference series. After correction for six identified inhomogeneity breaks, Mann–Kendall trend tests were applied to annual 99th-percentile hourly rain-rate series at each 4 × 4 km grid cell. Statistically significant increasing trends (p < 0.05) in hourly extremes are found over 34% of the Pannonian domain, concentrated in the northern and eastern sectors, with median Sen's slope of +0.18 mm h⁻¹ per decade. No significant trend was detected in event frequency, suggesting intensification rather than increased occurrence. Comparison with ERA5-derived convective available potential energy (CAPE) trends shows spatial correspondence (Pearson r = 0.61), supporting a thermodynamic interpretation. These findings have direct implications for updating the probabilistic hazard maps produced in earlier work.

SYN-PUB-07846.title: Estimating Soil Surface Temperature at 10 m Resolution Over Agricultural Fields by Fusing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices with Landsat-9 Thermal Band
SYN-PUB-07846.text:
Estimating Soil Surface Temperature at 10 m Resolution Over Agricultural Fields by Fusing Sentinel-2 Spectral Indices with Landsat-9 Thermal Band (2024, journal, IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations).
Authors: Nataša Brkić (outside co-author); Petra Varga (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Дарко Тошић (R0700).
Keywords: Landsat-9; Sentinel-2; data fusion; soil surface temperature; thermal sharpening.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-07944.title: Drought trends in Vojvodina, 1961–2023
SYN-PUB-07944.text:
Drought trends in Vojvodina, 1961–2023 (2024, journal, Climate Research Letters).
Authors: Milena Drašković (outside co-author); Branko Telebak (outside co-author); Lidija Vujović (outside co-author); Uroš Kecman (R0710).
This study presents a comprehensive analysis of drought trends across the Vojvodina region of northern Serbia for the period 1961–2023, utilizing a network of 14 meteorological stations and monthly precipitation and temperature records obtained from the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. Three standardized drought indices—the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI)—were computed at multiple timescales to characterize drought frequency, duration, and intensity. Results indicate a statistically significant increase in the frequency of moderate-to-severe drought episodes since the mid-1980s, with the most pronounced drying trend observed during summer months. Spatial analysis conducted in a GIS environment reveals that the northeastern and eastern sub-regions of Vojvodina exhibit greater drought vulnerability compared to the western areas adjacent to the Danube floodplain. The study further identifies a decadal oscillation in drought recurrence linked to large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns over the Euro-Atlantic sector. These findings carry direct implications for agricultural planning and water resource management in one of Serbia's most economically significant farming regions.

SYN-PUB-07945.title: Spatial interpolation of precipitation anomalies in the Pannonian Plain using geostatistical methods
SYN-PUB-07945.text:
Spatial interpolation of precipitation anomalies in the Pannonian Plain using geostatistical methods (2022, journal, Journal of Spatial Climatology and Geoinformatics).
Authors: Milena Drašković (outside co-author); Uroš Kecman (R0710); Darko Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: geostatistical interpolation; kriging; precipitation anomalies; Pannonian Plain; GIS.
Accurate spatial representation of precipitation anomalies is fundamental to regional climate assessments and agricultural risk modeling. This study evaluates the performance of five geostatistical interpolation techniques—ordinary kriging, universal kriging, co-kriging with elevation as a covariate, radial basis function interpolation, and inverse distance weighting—applied to monthly precipitation anomaly data from 27 meteorological stations distributed across the Pannonian Plain in Serbia and Croatia for the period 1971–2010. Cross-validation was employed to assess interpolation accuracy using root mean square error and mean absolute error metrics. Results demonstrate that ordinary kriging and co-kriging consistently outperform simpler deterministic methods, particularly in areas with complex microclimatic gradients near the Fruška Gora massif. Seasonal differences in interpolation performance are documented, with winter months showing markedly higher predictability than the convection-dominated summer season. All analyses were performed within an open-source GIS framework, and the resulting interpolated raster layers were integrated into a multi-temporal geodatabase for downstream drought and climate trend analysis. The methodology presented here is directly transferable to operational agro-meteorological monitoring systems.

SYN-PUB-07946.title: Assessment of the SPEI drought index under projected climate scenarios for northern Serbia to 2050
SYN-PUB-07946.text:
Assessment of the SPEI drought index under projected climate scenarios for northern Serbia to 2050 (2023, journal, Regional Environmental Change).
Authors: Uroš Kecman (R0710); Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Nemanja Perić (outside co-author); Ana Korolija (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPEI; climate projections; EURO-CORDEX; drought frequency; northern Serbia.
This paper investigates projected changes in drought conditions across northern Serbia using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) derived from statistically downscaled outputs of three regional climate models participating in the EURO-CORDEX initiative under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 emission scenarios. Baseline statistics were established from observed station data for 1981–2010, and future projections were analyzed for two time horizons: 2021–2040 and 2041–2060. Spatial analysis in a GIS environment was used to map drought frequency, mean duration, and peak intensity across a 5 km resolution grid covering the Vojvodina administrative province. Results indicate that under the high-emission scenario, the probability of summer drought events exceeding SPEI −1.5 doubles by the 2041–2060 period relative to the baseline. Intermodel uncertainty is quantified and discussed in relation to regional teleconnections and model biases in simulating summer precipitation. The findings have direct relevance to climate adaptation strategies for the agricultural sector, particularly irrigated maize and sunflower cultivation in the Bačka and Banat plains. Recommendations for integrating these projections into spatial planning decision support tools are outlined.

SYN-PUB-07947.title: GIS-based delineation of agro-climatic zones in Vojvodina using cluster analysis of drought and temperature indicators
SYN-PUB-07947.text:
GIS-based delineation of agro-climatic zones in Vojvodina using cluster analysis of drought and temperature indicators (2021, journal, Applied Geography).
Authors: Uroš Kecman (R0710); Snežana Marković (outside co-author); Goran Lazar (outside co-author).
Keywords: agro-climatic zoning; cluster analysis; drought indices; Vojvodina; spatial planning.
The spatial delineation of agro-climatic zones is a prerequisite for precision agricultural management and land-use planning. This study proposes a GIS-based methodology for classifying the Vojvodina region into homogeneous agro-climatic zones by applying hierarchical and k-means cluster analysis to a composite dataset of drought indices (SPI-3, SPI-12, SPEI-3), mean growing-season temperature, thermal amplitude, and frequency of late spring frosts, computed from 18 meteorological stations over 1981–2020. Cluster solutions were evaluated using the silhouette coefficient and Calinski-Harabasz index to determine the optimal number of zones. Five distinct agro-climatic zones were identified, each characterized by a unique drought risk profile and thermal regime. The resulting zone map was produced in vector GIS format and overlaid with existing land-cover and soil-type data to assess zone-specific agricultural vulnerability. The methodology is reproducible and scalable, making it suitable for integration into regional agricultural information systems or decision support platforms operated by agri-tech companies. This work represents a contribution to the spatial planning literature for post-socialist transitional economies facing accelerated climate change.

SYN-PUB-07948.title: Remote sensing integration with ground-based drought monitoring: a case study of the Bačka lowland
SYN-PUB-07948.text:
Remote sensing integration with ground-based drought monitoring: a case study of the Bačka lowland (2023, journal, International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation).
Authors: Jelena Savić (outside co-author); Mirko Stanić (outside co-author); Uroš Kecman (R0710).
Keywords: remote sensing; NDVI; SMAP; drought monitoring; Bačka.
Ground-based drought monitoring networks in the Western Balkans suffer from sparse station coverage and data gaps, motivating the integration of satellite-derived vegetation and soil moisture indices as complementary observational sources. This paper presents a multi-source drought monitoring framework for the Bačka lowland in northern Serbia, combining the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) anomaly derived from MODIS Terra 16-day composites, and the Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Level-3 product for the period 2015–2022. Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were used to quantify the relationship between SPI timescales and satellite-derived stress indicators across four land-use classes: arable land, orchards, pastures, and wetlands. Results show that NDVI anomalies lag SPI-3 by approximately four to six weeks on arable land, while SMAP soil moisture correlates most strongly with SPI-1 and SPI-2. The integrated framework is implemented as a semi-automated workflow in an open-source GIS environment, enabling near-real-time drought condition mapping. Practical implications for operational early-warning systems are discussed, with reference to data requirements relevant to agri-tech and environmental monitoring enterprises.

SYN-PUB-07949.title: Temporal variability of the SPI and PDSI over the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal network zone and implications for water management
SYN-PUB-07949.text:
Temporal variability of the SPI and PDSI over the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal network zone and implications for water management (2020, journal, Water Resources Management).
Authors: Uroš Kecman (R0710); Branko Telebak (outside co-author); Petar Zorić (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPI; PDSI; Mann-Kendall trend; DTD canal; water management.
The Danube–Tisa–Danube (DTD) hydro-amelioration system in Vojvodina is central to the region's agricultural water balance, yet its management is increasingly challenged by hydro-climatic variability. This study examines temporal variability in the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) for meteorological stations situated in the DTD zone over the period 1961–2020, using Mann-Kendall trend tests and Sen's slope estimator to detect monotonic changes in drought index time series. Wavelet coherence analysis is applied to identify cyclical signals and their evolution through time. Results reveal statistically significant drying trends in summer PDSI since the late 1990s, while SPI at the 12-month timescale indicates increasingly prolonged dry spells in the hydrological year. These trends are corroborated by independent streamflow records from DTD canal monitoring stations. The GIS visualization of trend magnitudes highlights spatial heterogeneity within the seemingly flat agricultural plain, pointing to the role of local soils and land cover in modulating drought expression. The study provides actionable inputs for revising canal operation protocols and dimensioning future irrigation infrastructure under climate change.

SYN-PUB-07950.title: Climatological atlas of drought indices for the Balkans: methodology and pilot application
SYN-PUB-07950.text:
Climatological atlas of drought indices for the Balkans: methodology and pilot application (2022, book chapter, Advances in Balkan Climatology (Edited Volume, Springer Geography Series)).
Authors: Uroš Kecman (R0710); Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Hrvoje Kovačić (outside co-author); Selma Muratović (outside co-author).
Keywords: climatological atlas; drought index; Balkans; cartography; climate services.
Standardized climatological atlases serve as foundational reference products for climate services, yet no comprehensive drought index atlas exists for the Balkan Peninsula at the national or regional scale. This book chapter describes the methodology developed for a pilot climatological atlas covering Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on the computation, validation, and cartographic representation of four drought indices: SPI, SPEI, PDSI, and the Reconnaissance Drought Index (RDI). Input data were sourced from national hydrometeorological services and subjected to quality control procedures including homogeneity testing using the standard normal homogeneity test (SNHT) and Pettitt test. All indices were computed for multiple reference periods and timescales using a harmonized Python-based processing pipeline. Results are represented as a series of GIS-derived thematic maps showing climatological means, percentile ranks, and trend directions at 10 km spatial resolution. The chapter discusses challenges specific to the Balkan data environment, including station network sparsity, political fragmentation of data archives, and diverging national data standards, and proposes a collaborative transboundary data-sharing framework as a prerequisite for operational regional climate services.

SYN-PUB-07951.title: WebGIS prototype for real-time drought index visualization in the Vojvodina region
SYN-PUB-07951.text:
WebGIS prototype for real-time drought index visualization in the Vojvodina region (2024, conference, Proceedings of the GeoICT Balkans Conference, Novi Sad).
Authors: Uroš Kecman (R0710); Vladimir Čolić (outside co-author); Milena Drašković (outside co-author).
Keywords: WebGIS; drought visualization; SPI; PostGIS; agricultural decision support.
Effective dissemination of drought information to agricultural stakeholders requires interactive, web-accessible spatial tools that transcend the limitations of static map products. This paper presents the design, implementation, and user evaluation of a WebGIS prototype developed for near-real-time visualization of SPI and SPEI across the Vojvodina region. The system ingests daily precipitation and temperature data from 14 automated meteorological stations via an open API provided by the national hydrometeorological service, computes drought indices on a rolling basis using a server-side Python module, and renders output layers as Web Map Service (WMS) tiles accessible through a Leaflet.js front end. The database back end uses PostGIS for spatial querying and time-series storage. A user evaluation study involving 22 participants from the agricultural advisory service confirmed that the prototype significantly improved the perceived accessibility and timeliness of drought information compared to conventional bulletin-based delivery. Key challenges related to data latency, index uncertainty communication, and mobile responsiveness are discussed. The prototype architecture is documented in sufficient detail to facilitate adaptation by environmental technology companies or public agencies seeking to deploy operational versions. Directions for expanding the system to include forecast-based drought outlooks are outlined.

SYN-PUB-08026.title: Slow Strain Rate Testing of Grade 10.9 Fastener Steel in Simulated Industrial Atmospheric Condensate
SYN-PUB-08026.text:
Slow Strain Rate Testing of Grade 10.9 Fastener Steel in Simulated Industrial Atmospheric Condensate (2023, journal, Journal of Corrosion Science and Engineering (Central European Edition)).
Authors: Miloš Ivanović (R0719); Dragana Vučković (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: slow strain rate testing; stress corrosion cracking; 42CrMo4; hydrogen embrittlement; fractography.
Stress corrosion cracking susceptibility of a commercially produced grade 10.9 bolt steel (42CrMo4) was evaluated using slow strain rate testing (SSRT) in a synthetic condensate solution representative of moderately polluted industrial atmospheric environments (pH 4.2, 150 mg/L Cl⁻, 80 mg/L SO₄²⁻). Tests were conducted at a strain rate of 1×10⁻⁶ s⁻¹ at 25 °C. Susceptibility indices based on reduction in area (ISCC = 0.31) and time-to-fracture (ISCC = 0.27) indicated moderate but clearly measurable susceptibility compared to inert mineral oil baseline tests. Fracture surfaces were examined by scanning electron microscopy, revealing a transition from predominantly ductile dimple morphology in the reference specimens to a mixed intergranular and quasi-cleavage morphology in the corroding specimens, consistent with hydrogen-assisted cracking. The fraction of intergranular fracture area increased with applied cathodic pre-charging time, suggesting hydrogen diffusion into grain boundaries as a primary embrittlement mechanism. Results are discussed in relation to microstructural features including prior austenite grain size and carbide distribution along grain boundaries.

SYN-PUB-08027.title: Influence of Surface Coating Defects on Hydrogen Uptake in High-Strength Bolts Under Cyclic Wet–Dry Exposure
SYN-PUB-08027.text:
Influence of Surface Coating Defects on Hydrogen Uptake in High-Strength Bolts Under Cyclic Wet–Dry Exposure (2024, conference, Proceedings of the 12th European Symposium on Corrosion and Protection of Metals (ESCPM 2024), Budapest).
Authors: Miloš Ivanović (R0719); Dragana Vučković (outside co-author); Tamara Horváth (outside co-author); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: hydrogen uptake; coating defects; zinc–nickel coating; electrochemical permeation; high-strength steel.
High-strength fasteners installed in outdoor industrial structures are routinely protected by zinc–nickel or phosphate coatings, yet localised coating defects are unavoidable in service. This study examined how artificial defect size (0.5 mm, 2 mm, and 5 mm diameter scribes) in a zinc–nickel electrodeposited coating affected hydrogen uptake in grade 12.9 steel substrates during cyclic wet–dry exposure to a 0.5 M NaCl solution over 240 hours. Absorbed hydrogen content was measured by vacuum hot extraction at 400 °C and confirmed by electrochemical permeation experiments using a Devanathan–Stachurski cell. Specimens with 5 mm scribes accumulated 2.8 times more diffusible hydrogen than intact coated specimens. Subsequent tensile testing demonstrated a reduction in notched tensile strength of up to 14% relative to uncharged controls. Cross-sectional metallography combined with energy-dispersive X-ray analysis showed preferential zinc dissolution and local acidification at scribe edges, consistent with an active dissolution-driven hydrogen generation mechanism. The findings indicate that defect size thresholds should be considered in maintenance inspection protocols for fasteners in corrosive atmospheres.

SYN-PUB-08028.title: Fractographic Classification of Stress Corrosion Fracture Modes in Quenched-and-Tempered Bolt Steels: A Comparative SEM Study
SYN-PUB-08028.text:
Fractographic Classification of Stress Corrosion Fracture Modes in Quenched-and-Tempered Bolt Steels: A Comparative SEM Study (2026, journal, Materials Characterisation and Testing).
Authors: Miloš Ivanović (R0719); Dragana Vučković (outside co-author); Zoran Mitrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: fractography; SEM; quenched-and-tempered steel; intergranular cracking; SCC fracture modes.
Fracture surface morphologies arising from stress corrosion cracking in three quenched-and-tempered steels used in structural fastener production (42CrMo4, 34CrNiMo6, and 30CrNiMo8) were systematically characterised by scanning electron microscopy following slow strain rate tests in acidic chloride solution (pH 3.5, 0.1 M NaCl, 1×10⁻⁶ s⁻¹). Each steel was tested at two tempering temperatures (450 °C and 550 °C) to produce ultimate tensile strengths ranging from approximately 1050 MPa to 1350 MPa. A total of 36 fracture surfaces were imaged and classified according to the proportion of intergranular, transgranular quasi-cleavage, and ductile dimple areas using image analysis software. The 34CrNiMo6 steel at the higher strength level showed the largest intergranular fraction (41%), while 42CrMo4 tempered at 550 °C exhibited the lowest susceptibility index and predominantly ductile fracture. Crack initiation sites were associated with inclusions and prior austenite grain boundary triple junctions. The dataset provides a reference classification framework for in-service failure analysis of fasteners retrieved from industrial facilities.

SYN-PUB-08093.title: Downscaling Monthly Air Temperature Over the Vojvodina Plain Using MODIS Land Surface Temperature and Regression-Kriging
SYN-PUB-08093.text:
Downscaling Monthly Air Temperature Over the Vojvodina Plain Using MODIS Land Surface Temperature and Regression-Kriging (2011, journal, Journal of Applied Geoinformatics and Earth Observation).
Authors: Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Zsolt Horváth (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: MODIS LST; regression-kriging; air temperature; Vojvodina; downscaling.
Monthly mean air temperature fields at 1 km resolution were produced for the Vojvodina plain by combining MODIS Terra LST composites (MOD11A2, 2003–2008) with ground observations from 34 meteorological stations operated by the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia. A regression-kriging framework was adopted in which daytime and night-time LST, elevation, and distance to water bodies served as covariates in an ordinary least-squares pre-regression step, with residuals subsequently interpolated by ordinary kriging. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded a mean absolute error of 0.62 °C averaged across all months, improving on straight inverse-distance weighting by 31 %. Spatial patterns of cold air pooling in topographic depressions and urban heat islands around Novi Sad and Subotica were captured more faithfully than in the national 10 km gridded product. Seasonal decomposition showed the strongest LST-to-air-temperature coupling in July and weakest in December, a result attributed to soil moisture and snow cover masking effects.

SYN-PUB-08094.title: Mapping Growing Degree Days at Sub-Kilometre Scale Across the Middle Danube Basin
SYN-PUB-08094.text:
Mapping Growing Degree Days at Sub-Kilometre Scale Across the Middle Danube Basin (2013, journal, International Journal of Biometeorology and Spatial Sciences).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Mirela Ostojić (outside co-author); Anca Păun (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: growing degree days; ERA-Interim; geographically weighted regression; Danube basin; agroclimatic indices.
Growing degree days (GDD, base 10 °C) were computed at 500 m resolution for the 2005–2010 growing seasons across a 180 000 km² domain spanning Hungary, Serbia, Croatia and Romania. Temperature surfaces were produced by spatially downscaling ERA-Interim reanalysis fields using a statistical transfer function fitted to surface station data and MODIS LST anomalies. The transfer function was a geographically weighted regression model, separately calibrated for spring and summer sub-periods to account for differing advection regimes. Validation against 51 held-out stations showed RMSE in cumulative GDD below 120 GDD-days for the April–September period. The resulting maps revealed consistent positive anomalies along the Fruška Gora slopes relative to flat Vojvodina, with implications for early-harvest crop variety selection. The dataset was made available as a 12-band GeoTIFF archive through a regional agrometeorological data portal.

SYN-PUB-08095.title: Estimating Reference Evapotranspiration in Data-Sparse Regions by Fusing SEVIRI and MODIS Thermal Imagery
SYN-PUB-08095.text:
Estimating Reference Evapotranspiration in Data-Sparse Regions by Fusing SEVIRI and MODIS Thermal Imagery (2015, journal, Agricultural and Forest Meteorology Letters).
Authors: Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Fabrizio Moretti (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: reference evapotranspiration; MSG SEVIRI; Penman-Monteith; data fusion; Serbia.
Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀, Penman–Monteith FAO-56) requires net radiation and humidity inputs that are often measured only at sparse synoptic stations. This study fused instantaneous surface radiation estimates from the MSG/SEVIRI satellite (3 km, 15-minute) with daytime MODIS LST (1 km, daily) to reconstruct diurnal temperature and radiation cycles at 1 km resolution over Serbia for 2008–2011. A temporal interpolation scheme based on sinusoidal fitting between two daily MODIS overpasses was applied to fill the radiometric gap left by SEVIRI's coarser spatial detail. Daily ET₀ estimated from the downscaled inputs agreed with FAO Penman–Monteith computed from station data to within 0.38 mm day⁻¹ (RMSE, n = 28 stations). Spatial maps revealed a systematic ET₀ gradient from the Pannonian lowland to the Šar Mountains exceeding 1.1 mm day⁻¹ in July, consistent with independent eddy covariance records at two sites.

SYN-PUB-08096.title: Kriging Interpolation Variants for Daily Precipitation in Complex Terrain: A Comparative Assessment Over the Dinaric Alps Fringe
SYN-PUB-08096.text:
Kriging Interpolation Variants for Daily Precipitation in Complex Terrain: A Comparative Assessment Over the Dinaric Alps Fringe (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 4th Balkan Conference on Geomatics and Geoinformatics).
Authors: Dragan Vujović (outside co-author); Marija Lazić (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: kriging; daily precipitation; Dinaric Alps; variogram; geostatistics.
Four kriging variants — ordinary kriging (OK), kriging with external drift (KED), co-kriging with elevation, and indicator kriging of wet-day occurrence — were evaluated for daily precipitation interpolation using a 62-station network across a 55 000 km² domain covering the Dinaric fringe of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. The 2009–2013 wet-season record was used, with 15 % of stations withheld for validation in each of 200 bootstrap iterations. KED using terrain-exposed elevation as the external drift variable outperformed OK in 73 % of daily cases, with mean RMSE reductions of 12 % in autumn and 8 % in spring. Indicator kriging proved most accurate for binary wet-day mapping, reducing false wet-cell fractions by 18 percentage points compared with deterministic methods. Variogram range parameters varied seasonally between 28 km in convective summer and 110 km in frontal winter regimes.

SYN-PUB-08097.title: Spatiotemporal Drought Monitoring Over the Pannonian Basin Using the SPEI at Multiple Time Scales Derived from Downscaled Gridded Climate Data
SYN-PUB-08097.text:
Spatiotemporal Drought Monitoring Over the Pannonian Basin Using the SPEI at Multiple Time Scales Derived from Downscaled Gridded Climate Data (2018, journal, International Journal of Climatology and Remote Sensing Applications).
Authors: Tamás Bodnár (outside co-author); Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Loredana Constantin (outside co-author); Milena Nedić (R1023); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: SPEI; drought monitoring; Pannonian Basin; NDVI; trend analysis.
The Standardised Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month accumulation periods was computed at 1 km resolution over the Pannonian Basin for 1991–2015 using monthly precipitation and ET₀ grids produced by the author's regression-kriging pipeline. The resulting 25-year, 288-layer dataset allowed continuous spatial tracking of drought onset, intensity and recovery without relying on station interpolation alone. Trend analysis using the Mann–Kendall test identified statistically significant (p < 0.05) drying trends in 34 % of the study area at the 12-month SPEI, concentrated in the eastern Hungarian and western Romanian sectors. Correlation of 3-month SPEI with satellite NDVI composites (MODIS MOD13Q1) reached 0.71 for rainfed maize areas, confirming utility for near-real-time agricultural drought early warning. Comparison with the European Drought Observatory CCI SM product showed spatial agreement of 78 % for severe drought flags.

SYN-PUB-08098.title: Comparison of Machine Learning Regressors and Geostatistical Models for 1 km Daily Minimum Temperature Mapping Over Serbia
SYN-PUB-08098.text:
Comparison of Machine Learning Regressors and Geostatistical Models for 1 km Daily Minimum Temperature Mapping Over Serbia (2020, journal, Computers and Geosciences – Environmental Applications).
Authors: Marija Lazić (outside co-author); Bojan Đorđević (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: random forest; regression-kriging; minimum temperature; machine learning; ensemble.
Random forest (RF), gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost), and artificial neural networks were compared against regression-kriging and co-kriging for the task of producing daily minimum temperature grids at 1 km over Serbia. Inputs common to all methods included MODIS LST, DEM-derived topographic variables, distance to major water bodies, and calendar-day encoding. Training used station data from 67 automatic weather stations for 2013–2017; testing was performed on 2018–2019 withheld data. Random forest achieved the lowest test RMSE (0.88 °C) compared with regression-kriging (0.97 °C), XGBoost (0.91 °C), and co-kriging (1.03 °C). However, regression-kriging produced better-calibrated prediction intervals and smoother spatial fields in data-sparse mountain regions. An ensemble blending RF predictions with kriging residuals achieved RMSE of 0.81 °C while retaining spatial coherence. Computational cost for the ensemble was approximately 4× that of standalone RF.

SYN-PUB-08099.title: Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Agroclimatic Grids for the Carpathian–Pannonian Region Using Historical Station Records and Spatial Reanalysis
SYN-PUB-08099.text:
Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Agroclimatic Grids for the Carpathian–Pannonian Region Using Historical Station Records and Spatial Reanalysis (2021, journal, Climate Dynamics – Regional Studies).
Authors: Tamás Bodnár (outside co-author); Anca Păun (outside co-author); Srđan Krstić (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: historical climate reconstruction; ERA-20C; growing season; Carpathian-Pannonian; bias correction.
High-resolution gridded records of growing season length, heat accumulation, and aridity index were reconstructed for the 1961–2000 period over the Carpathian–Pannonian region by downscaling the ERA-20C centennial reanalysis to 2 km using transfer functions calibrated on the 2001–2015 overlap period with MODIS LST data. Station data from 148 surface synoptic stations in five countries were used to bias-correct the ERA-20C baseline. Trend testing showed a 14-day advance in start-of-growing-season dates between 1961 and 2000 in the lowland zone, consistent with independent phenological records for winter wheat. The reconstruction fills a critical gap for long-term impact assessments that require spatial data prior to the MODIS era. Uncertainty was quantified by propagating station observation errors and ERA-20C ensemble spread through the downscaling chain, yielding 90 % confidence intervals of ±3 days for growing season start.

SYN-PUB-08100.title: Agroclimatic Zoning of Soybean Cultivation Potential in the Western Balkans Under Present and Near-Term (2030–2040) Climate Projections
SYN-PUB-08100.text:
Agroclimatic Zoning of Soybean Cultivation Potential in the Western Balkans Under Present and Near-Term (2030–2040) Climate Projections (2022, journal, Field Crops Research and Spatial Modelling).
Authors: Snežana Branković (outside co-author); Claudiu Nistor (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: soybean; agroclimatic zoning; EURO-CORDEX; Western Balkans; RCP scenarios.
Soybean cultivation in the Western Balkans is expanding but spatially under-characterised. This study applied a set of agroclimatic indices — growing season length, sum of active temperatures above 10 °C, number of dry spells exceeding 10 days in July–August, and mean diurnal temperature range during pod fill — computed from high-resolution (1 km) historical grids and from dynamically downscaled EURO-CORDEX RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 projections for 2030–2040. Under RCP4.5, the area classified as highly suitable for soybean is projected to increase by 11 % relative to the 1991–2020 baseline, driven primarily by warming in the mountainous interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro. Under RCP8.5, suitability decreases in the Vojvodina core zone due to increased drought stress frequency. Results were delivered as Web Map Service layers and as 1 km GeoTIFF products.

SYN-PUB-08101.title: A Benchmark Dataset for Sub-Kilometre Agroclimatic Index Mapping in the Pannonian Zone
SYN-PUB-08101.text:
A Benchmark Dataset for Sub-Kilometre Agroclimatic Index Mapping in the Pannonian Zone (2023, journal, Earth System Science Data – Regional Contributions).
Authors: Jovana Tešanović (outside co-author); Goran Filipović (outside co-author); Mirela Ostojić (outside co-author); Darko Mirković (R0877); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Sara Šijački (R0828).
Keywords: benchmark dataset; agroclimatic indices; Pannonian zone; GDD; Huglin index.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-08102.title: Sensitivity of Spatial Downscaling Performance to Variogram Estimation Sample Size in Sparse Station Networks
SYN-PUB-08102.text:
Sensitivity of Spatial Downscaling Performance to Variogram Estimation Sample Size in Sparse Station Networks (2026, journal, Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment).
Authors: Bojan Đorđević (outside co-author); Milutin Đukić (R0727).
Keywords: variogram estimation; REML; kriging; sparse networks; Monte Carlo simulation.
Variogram estimation is a fundamental step in geostatistical downscaling, but its reliability degrades when fewer than 30–40 stations are available — a common situation in developing countries. Using a sub-sampling simulation study on the 72-station Serbian agrometeorological network, this work examined how kriging interpolation error grows as the estimation sample is reduced from 72 to 8 stations for monthly mean temperature, total precipitation, and reference ET₀. Variograms were estimated by the method-of-moments and by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). REML maintained acceptable nugget-to-sill ratios down to 15 stations where the method-of-moments failed, yielding 18 % lower RMSE on average. Below 12 stations, both estimators produced unreliable range parameters. The study provides practical guidance for selecting estimation method and minimum station density thresholds for each variable type, expressed as a function of spatial autocorrelation range.

SYN-PUB-08103.title: Detecting inter-annual change in softwood floodplain forest extent using dense Sentinel-2 time-series and a change vector approach
SYN-PUB-08103.text:
Detecting inter-annual change in softwood floodplain forest extent using dense Sentinel-2 time-series and a change vector approach (2020, journal, Remote Sensing of Riparian and Wetland Environments).
Authors: Aleksandra Đorđević (outside co-author); Predrag Vuković (outside co-author); Marina Malešević (R0730); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Jasmina Jakovljević (R0898); Helena Novak (outside co-author).
Keywords: Sentinel-2; change vector analysis; softwood forest; Sava River; phenological composites.
Softwood gallery forests dominated by Salix alba and Populus nigra are among the most flood-disturbance-adapted habitats in Pannonian river floodplains, but their spatial extent can fluctuate substantially between years in response to flood frequency and timber harvesting. This study applied a change vector analysis framework to annual phenological composites derived from Sentinel-2 MSI 10 m imagery for the period 2016–2021 across a 210 km reach of the Sava River floodplain in Serbia. Annual composites were constructed using the 20th percentile NIR and the maximum NDRE over a 60-day spring window. Change magnitudes exceeding one standard deviation above the multi-year mean were flagged and attributed to four process categories (flood disturbance, harvest clearance, natural regeneration, encroachment) using auxiliary topographic wetness index and forest management registry data. Over the six-year period, 2,140 ha of softwood forest underwent detectable canopy-layer change, with flood-related losses concentrated in the 2019 and 2021 high-water years. Accuracy of change attribution reached 82% against independent field verification of 160 change patches. The approach requires no training data beyond the composite stack and is applicable at the scale of an entire national river network.

SYN-PUB-08104.title: Bounded Model Checking for Mutual Exclusion Protocols: A Comparative Study of Four Classical Algorithms
SYN-PUB-08104.text:
Bounded Model Checking for Mutual Exclusion Protocols: A Comparative Study of Four Classical Algorithms (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Formal Methods (CEWFM)).
Authors: Miroslav Takáč (outside co-author); Anna Čániová (R0728).
Keywords: bounded model checking; mutual exclusion; SPIN; partial-order reduction; Promela.
This paper applies bounded model checking (BMC) to four classical mutual exclusion algorithms — Peterson's, Dekker's, Lamport's Bakery, and a ticket-based protocol — encoded in Promela and analysed with SPIN 6.2. The study systematically evaluates reachability of deadlock states and violation of the critical-section property under varying thread counts from 2 to 8. State spaces grow from roughly 10^4 to over 10^9 states, making exhaustive verification infeasible beyond five threads without abstraction. We apply partial-order reduction and bitstate hashing, documenting the precision loss and the corresponding reduction in memory consumption. Results confirm that Lamport's Bakery generates the largest state space but maintains the strongest fairness guarantees; the ticket protocol is most amenable to partial-order reduction, retaining full verification up to seven threads within 4 GB memory. The comparison provides quantitative guidance for choosing mutual exclusion mechanisms in resource-constrained embedded contexts.

SYN-PUB-08105.title: Specifying Progress Properties of Multi-Threaded Java Programs with LTL Annotations
SYN-PUB-08105.text:
Specifying Progress Properties of Multi-Threaded Java Programs with LTL Annotations (2014, journal, Journal of Formal Software Engineering (JFSE)).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Miroslav Takáč (outside co-author); Petra Vargová (outside co-author).
Keywords: LTL annotations; Java verification; liveness; starvation-freedom; SPIN.
We describe a lightweight annotation framework that maps LTL progress properties onto Java bytecode, enabling automatic extraction of finite-state models suitable for SPIN-based verification. Annotations capture liveness constraints such as starvation-freedom and eventual consistency at the method level. The extracted Promela models are conservative abstractions that preserve counterexample traces traceable back to source locations. We evaluated the approach on six open-source Java libraries containing a total of 43 annotated thread interaction points. Of eleven liveness properties specified, SPIN confirmed eight and produced counterexample traces for three, two of which corresponded to genuine bugs subsequently patched upstream. Abstraction overhead was measured: on average, the extracted model is 97% smaller in state count than a naive direct encoding. The paper discusses soundness limits of the abstraction and outlines conditions under which the approach is both sound and complete for safety sub-properties.

SYN-PUB-08106.title: Assume-Guarantee Reasoning for Lock-Free Data Structures
SYN-PUB-08106.text:
Assume-Guarantee Reasoning for Lock-Free Data Structures (2016, journal, Formal Methods in System Design Letters).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Dušan Grujić (outside co-author); Tobias Frenzel (outside co-author).
Keywords: assume-guarantee; lock-free; linearisability; CTL*; NuSMV.
Lock-free data structures avoid mutual exclusion by exploiting hardware compare-and-swap (CAS) operations, but their correctness proofs are notoriously difficult. This work applies assume-guarantee compositional reasoning to verify linearisability of three lock-free queue implementations: Michael–Scott, Kogan–Petrank, and a single-producer single-consumer ring buffer. Each component (enqueue and dequeue operations) is modelled as a labelled transition system and verified in isolation against assumptions about its environment, then composed. We formalise the composition rule in CTL* and implement verification using NuSMV 2.6. The full parallel composition of Michael–Scott with four threads and a 32-entry queue has 2.1 × 10^7 states; the compositional approach reduces per-component verification to at most 1.4 × 10^5 states. All three structures were verified correct; one latent ABA-problem scenario in the ring buffer was exposed under relaxed memory model assumptions and documented as a known limitation.

SYN-PUB-08107.title: Timed Automata Models for Real-Time Task Scheduling in Embedded Controllers
SYN-PUB-08107.text:
Timed Automata Models for Real-Time Task Scheduling in Embedded Controllers (2018, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Real-Time and Embedded Systems Verification (SRTESV)).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author); Miroslav Takáč (outside co-author); Ioana Drăghici (outside co-author).
Keywords: timed automata; UPPAAL; real-time scheduling; embedded systems; deadline verification.
Real-time embedded controllers must satisfy hard deadlines whose violation can cause physical harm. This paper develops a library of timed automata templates for common scheduling policies — fixed-priority preemptive, earliest-deadline-first, and cyclic-executive — and verifies schedulability and absence of deadline misses using UPPAAL 4.1. We model a case study drawn from an automotive body-control module with 12 periodic tasks and three aperiodic interrupt handlers. UPPAAL's symbolic reachability analysis with difference-bound matrices completes within 180 seconds on a 16-core workstation. Properties checked include absence of deadline misses, mutual exclusion of shared-bus access, and bounded end-to-end latency. The templates are parameterised and distributed as an open UPPAAL library. We compare verification times with those of a direct Promela encoding and find a 3× speedup attributable to UPPAAL's native clock semantics.

SYN-PUB-08108.title: Detecting Data Races in Rust Programs via Model Extraction and SPIN Verification
SYN-PUB-08108.text:
Detecting Data Races in Rust Programs via Model Extraction and SPIN Verification (2022, journal, International Journal of Software Tools for Technology Transfer).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Tomáš Beneš (outside co-author); Nemanja Ostojić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Rust; data race detection; MIR; SPIN; unsafe code; concurrency.
Although Rust's ownership type system prevents most data races at compile time, programs using unsafe blocks or foreign-function interfaces can still exhibit race conditions. This paper proposes a pipeline that extracts a Promela model from Rust's MIR (mid-level intermediate representation) for functions marked unsafe, preserving thread-interleaving semantics and shared-reference patterns. The extraction handles raw pointers and atomic intrinsics. We evaluate the approach on 27 crates from the Rust package registry that contain unsafe blocks and have known concurrency issues listed in public issue trackers. SPIN found confirmed race conditions in 9 of 27 crates; 4 were previously unreported. State spaces for individual crates range from 8 × 10^3 to 6 × 10^6 states. False-negative analysis shows that our MIR abstraction misses races mediated by interior mutability through reference-counted types in 6 additional crates, a limitation we characterise formally.

SYN-PUB-08109.title: Verifying Distributed Consensus Protocols with Parameterised Model Checking
SYN-PUB-08109.text:
Verifying Distributed Consensus Protocols with Parameterised Model Checking (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Automated Verification of Critical Systems (AVoCS 2023)).
Authors: Anna Čániová (R0728); Nemanja Ostojić (outside co-author); Klára Horváthová (outside co-author); Ioana Drăghici (outside co-author).
Keywords: parameterised model checking; Paxos; Raft; consensus protocols; Cubicle; distributed systems.
Distributed consensus protocols such as Paxos and Raft are difficult to verify because correctness must hold for an arbitrary number of participants. We apply parameterised model checking, using the indexed predicate abstraction technique implemented in the Cubicle tool, to a Promela-level encoding of single-decree Paxos and a simplified version of Raft's leader election phase. For Paxos with up to n proposers and n acceptors (n treated as a parameter), we verify agreement and validity automatically for all n ≥ 3; liveness under weak fairness is verified up to n = 6 before state-space limits are reached. For Raft leader election, safety is verified for arbitrary n but liveness requires a bound n ≤ 5. We additionally identify an abstraction gap between the Raft TLA+ specification and our Promela encoding and document which properties are preserved across the gap. Verification times on a 32-core server range from 4 minutes (n = 3) to 11 hours (n = 6).

SYN-PUB-08138.title: Sensitivity of Solvency II SCR estimates to extreme-value model choice for motor third-party liability tail risk
SYN-PUB-08138.text:
Sensitivity of Solvency II SCR estimates to extreme-value model choice for motor third-party liability tail risk (2025, journal, Journal of Risk and Insurance Modelling).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Tijana Vučković (outside co-author); Andrej Kokol Bukovšek (outside co-author); Nada Dobanovački (R0732); Gordana Todorović-Simić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Solvency II; SCR; MTPL; tail risk; model uncertainty.
Under Solvency II, the solvency capital requirement (SCR) for reserve risk in motor third-party liability (MTPL) lines depends on assumptions about the tail of the claim severity distribution. Regulators permit internal models if adequately validated. We analyse a synthetic MTPL portfolio calibrated to match aggregate statistics from the Serbian Insurance Supervision Agency's public reports: 4,200 closed claims over eight years, of which 38 exceed the 95th percentile. Five severity tail models (GPD, log-normal tail, Burr, Weibull, and a spliced log-normal–GPD) are fitted by maximum likelihood and by MCMC with weakly informative priors. The resulting one-year 99.5th-percentile VaR estimates—the SCR basis—range from 1.41 to 1.87 times the mean reserve. Bayes factors weakly favour the spliced model but the SCR uncertainty from model choice dwarfs parameter uncertainty in all cases.

SYN-PUB-08203.title: Evaluating Compression Schemes for Posting Lists in Low-Resource Server Environments
SYN-PUB-08203.text:
Evaluating Compression Schemes for Posting Lists in Low-Resource Server Environments (2015, journal, Journal of Data and Information Engineering (JDIE)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Miroslav Bjelogrlić (outside co-author).
Keywords: posting list compression; codec comparison; full-text search; low-resource deployment.
Posting-list compression directly affects both the memory footprint and decode throughput of full-text search engines. We systematically compare seven integer-compression codecs—including FOR-delta, PForDelta, Simple-8b, and a bitpacking variant—across three corpora of 1 million, 10 million, and 50 million documents sourced from Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian web crawls. Experiments are conducted on commodity hardware with 16 GB RAM to reflect the constraints typical of small research or company deployments. PForDelta achieves the best decode throughput at 1.1 billion integers per second on the largest corpus, while a tuned FOR-delta variant yields the smallest on-disk footprint at 2.3 bits per integer. We also report how codec choice interacts with query selectivity: high-frequency terms favour block-oriented codecs, whereas rare-term queries are insensitive to codec selection. Practical guidance is provided for operators choosing codecs without exhaustive tuning budgets.

SYN-PUB-08204.title: A Sharded Query Broker for Sub-100 ms Retrieval over Fifty Index Partitions
SYN-PUB-08204.text:
A Sharded Query Broker for Sub-100 ms Retrieval over Fifty Index Partitions (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Symposium on Scalable Data Management Systems (SSDMS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Tomáš Hradil (outside co-author); Darko Vukelić (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: query brokering; scatter-gather; distributed search; latency.
Scaling a search service beyond a single machine introduces coordinator overhead that can dominate end-to-end latency when shard count is large. We design and evaluate a sharded query broker that uses a two-phase scatter–gather protocol with early termination: in the first phase, each shard returns only top-k document identifiers and their scores; in the second phase, only shards holding documents that could affect the global top-k are asked for full postings. Tested on a 50-shard cluster indexing 200 million documents (a synthetic web corpus generated from Common Crawl metadata), the broker keeps 95th-percentile latency below 94 ms for single-term queries and below 140 ms for three-term Boolean conjunctions at 500 queries per second. A comparison with a naïve full-scatter baseline shows a 41% latency reduction with less than 0.1% loss in NDCG@10.

SYN-PUB-08205.title: Distributed Full-Text Indexing for Heterogeneous Document Collections: Architectures and Trade-offs
SYN-PUB-08205.text:
Distributed Full-Text Indexing for Heterogeneous Document Collections: Architectures and Trade-offs (2018, book chapter, Advances in Large-Scale Text Processing, edited volume, IOS Press Academic).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Jelena Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: distributed indexing; survey; document partitioning; index architecture.
This book chapter surveys architectures for distributed full-text indexing, focusing on the trade-offs between document-partitioned and term-partitioned layouts when collections are heterogeneous in language, format, and update frequency. We categorise existing systems along four axes: partitioning strategy, merge policy, fault tolerance mechanism, and query routing logic. For each axis we review the academic literature from 2005 to 2016 and relate design choices to measurable outcomes: index freshness, query latency distribution, and hardware utilisation. A recurring finding is that document-partitioned layouts tolerate heterogeneous update rates better, while term-partitioned layouts reduce per-query network traffic for vocabulary-rich corpora. The chapter closes with a discussion of open problems, including the integration of real-time segment merging with batch reindexing and the impact of multilingual tokenisation on partition balance.

SYN-PUB-08206.title: Incremental HNSW Index Updates Under Concurrent Write Load
SYN-PUB-08206.text:
Incremental HNSW Index Updates Under Concurrent Write Load (2020, conference, Proceedings of the European Workshop on Vector and Similarity Search (EVSS)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Rade Milošević (outside co-author); Petra Novotná (outside co-author).
Keywords: HNSW; ANN search; index updates; vector search; compaction.
Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs provide high recall and low query latency for approximate nearest-neighbour search but were originally designed for static datasets. We study how concurrent insertions and deletions affect graph connectivity and search quality when updates arrive at rates between 500 and 10,000 vectors per second.
