Using a 768-dimensional sentence-embedding corpus of 8 million documents (generated with an open encoder trained on multilingual Wikipedia), we measure recall@10 degradation as a function of the fraction of deleted nodes not yet compacted. At 15% uncompacted deletions, recall falls by 3.1 percentage points. We propose a lightweight background compaction scheduler that monitors the deleted-node ratio and triggers partial graph reconstruction during low-traffic windows, recovering recall to within 0.6 points of the static baseline without pausing query serving. Experiments run on a single 40-core server with 256 GB RAM.

SYN-PUB-08207.title: Hybrid Sparse–Dense Retrieval: Combining BM25 and Vector Indexes Without Score Normalisation Heuristics
SYN-PUB-08207.text:
Hybrid Sparse–Dense Retrieval: Combining BM25 and Vector Indexes Without Score Normalisation Heuristics (2021, journal, Journal of Information Retrieval Research (JIRR)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Rade Milošević (outside co-author); Marco Dellarocca (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: hybrid retrieval; BM25; dense retrieval; reciprocal rank fusion; multilingual.
Combining a lexical BM25 index with a dense vector index requires merging scores from incompatible distributions. Most practical systems rely on hand-tuned linear interpolation weights or min–max normalisation, both of which are sensitive to corpus and query distribution shifts. We propose a rank-based fusion approach grounded in reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) that requires no score normalisation and is calibrated using a small set of 500 labelled query–document pairs. Evaluation on two corpora—a 3-million-document Serbian legal archive and a 7-million-document multilingual news collection—shows that the proposed method matches or exceeds the best normalisation baseline on NDCG@10 (gains of 1.8 and 2.4 points respectively) while being robust to out-of-distribution query sets. Latency overhead compared to BM25 alone is 22 ms at the 95th percentile on the larger corpus when vector retrieval runs on GPU.

SYN-PUB-08208.title: Learned Sparse Retrieval for Low-Resource South Slavic Languages
SYN-PUB-08208.text:
Learned Sparse Retrieval for Low-Resource South Slavic Languages (2025, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Language Technologies and Information Access (BALTIA)).
Authors: Snežana Todorović (R0741); Milica Savić (outside co-author); Marco Dellarocca (outside co-author).
Keywords: learned sparse retrieval; SPLADE; South Slavic languages; low-resource NLP; multilingual IR.
Learned sparse retrieval models such as SPLADE expand query and document terms using transformer-derived weights, producing sparse vectors that are indexed in a standard inverted index. Their effectiveness on languages other than English is less studied. We fine-tune a multilingual base transformer on Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian document–query pairs assembled from publicly available court decisions and parliamentary records, producing a total of 280,000 training triples. The resulting model is evaluated on three held-out test sets. MRR@10 improves by 6.1, 4.8, and 5.3 points over BM25 on the Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian sets respectively. Index size is 2.1× that of BM25, and query latency at the 95th percentile is 38 ms on a CPU-only server. We also report the effect of training set size, showing useful gains above approximately 40,000 triples.

SYN-PUB-08209.title: Tiered Vector Storage: Exploiting NVMe and DRAM Hierarchies for ANN Index Serving
SYN-PUB-08209.text:
Tiered Vector Storage: Exploiting NVMe and DRAM Hierarchies for ANN Index Serving (2026, conference, Proceedings of the International Symposium on Data Storage and Retrieval Systems (DATSYS)).
Authors: Milica Savić (outside co-author); Nikola Stanković (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Jürgen Albrecht (outside co-author).
Keywords: tiered storage; NVMe; ANN search; HNSW; memory hierarchy.
Dense vector indexes for ANN search are memory-intensive; billion-scale deployments frequently exceed available DRAM. We design a tiered storage manager that partitions HNSW graph layers across DRAM and NVMe, keeping upper graph layers and frequently accessed vectors in DRAM while spilling lower layers to NVMe. Access patterns are tracked with a lightweight frequency counter and a decay factor that deprioritises temporally stale vectors. On a 1.5-billion-vector index (768 dimensions, float16) requiring 2.2 TB uncompressed, the tiered system achieves 89.1% recall@10 using 128 GB DRAM plus 2 TB NVMe, compared to 94.3% recall with full DRAM loading. Query throughput at this recall level is 1,340 queries per second, a 4.2× improvement over a pure NVMe baseline. The implementation builds on an open-source ANN library with a custom I/O scheduler.

SYN-PUB-08210.title: Distributed Stream Processing: Architectures, Algorithms, and Deployment
SYN-PUB-08210.text:
Distributed Stream Processing: Architectures, Algorithms, and Deployment (2022, book chapter, Handbook of Big Data Systems Engineering, Springer).
Authors: Miroslav Tošić (outside co-author); Snežana Todorović (R0741); Balázs Fekete (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: stream processing survey; operator graph; exactly-once semantics; fault tolerance; textbook.
This book chapter surveys the architectural space of distributed stream processing systems, covering foundational data models (data streams, continuous queries, operator graphs), core algorithmic challenges (join algorithms, windowing, state management, fault tolerance), and deployment considerations on both on-premises clusters and cloud-native infrastructure. The chapter is structured in three parts. The first part establishes formal definitions and a taxonomy of processing guarantees (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once). The second part surveys algorithms for the main operator classes—filters, aggregations, joins, and enrichments—with emphasis on complexity trade-offs under varying data distributions. The third part addresses operational concerns: resource allocation, monitoring, schema management, and integration with batch systems. Representative open-source and commercial systems are discussed as illustrative examples without prescriptive endorsement. Annotated references guide readers toward primary literature for each subtopic. The chapter is intended for graduate students and practitioners with prior exposure to database systems and parallel computing.

SYN-PUB-08279.title: Demand Uncertainty Modelling in Supplier Contracts Using Scenario-Based Stochastic Programming
SYN-PUB-08279.text:
Demand Uncertainty Modelling in Supplier Contracts Using Scenario-Based Stochastic Programming (2023, conference, Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Production Engineering and Management (ICPEM), Ljubljana).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Dragan Ćurčić (outside co-author).
Keywords: stochastic programming; two-stage model; order allocation; demand uncertainty; scenario generation.
This study formulates a two-stage stochastic programming model for supplier order allocation when end-customer demand is uncertain. The first stage determines contract quantities with each of six candidate suppliers before demand is realised; the second stage adjusts order volumes after a demand scenario is observed. Fifty discrete demand scenarios are generated from three years of historical shipment data provided by a food processing company in Bačka Palanka, fitted to a mixture of normal distributions. The objective function minimises total expected procurement and penalty costs, including holding, shortage, and over-order costs. The model is implemented in Python using the PuLP library and solved with the CBC solver. Compared to a deterministic baseline using average demand, the stochastic solution reduces expected total cost by 8.3% and decreases the standard deviation of total cost by 22.1% across out-of-sample test scenarios. The paper also examines how varying the shortage-to-holding cost ratio shifts the optimal supplier mix, finding that above a ratio of 4:1, dual sourcing from the two top-ranked suppliers becomes consistently preferable to single sourcing.

SYN-PUB-08280.title: Quantifying Supply Chain Disruption Risk with a Combined Failure Mode and Stochastic Simulation Framework
SYN-PUB-08280.text:
Quantifying Supply Chain Disruption Risk with a Combined Failure Mode and Stochastic Simulation Framework (2024, journal, European Journal of Industrial Engineering and Operations).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Péter Németh (outside co-author); Aleksandra Kostić (outside co-author).
Keywords: supply chain risk; FMEA; Monte Carlo simulation; disruption cost; risk quantification.
Supply chain disruption events such as supplier insolvency, transport delays, and quality failures are difficult to capture with deterministic risk scores alone. This paper presents a hybrid framework that combines a modified Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) with Monte Carlo simulation to estimate the distribution of annual disruption costs for a multi-tier supply network. The case study involves a plastics processing manufacturer in Novi Sad with 11 first-tier suppliers and three second-tier nodes. FMEA severity, occurrence, and detectability scores are collected from 12 supply chain managers using structured questionnaires. These scores seed the probability distributions for individual failure events, and 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations generate an empirical cost distribution. The 95th percentile of simulated annual disruption cost is 18.4% higher than the deterministic point estimate used in the company's existing risk register. The framework identifies three suppliers whose individual contribution to tail risk exceeds their share of purchase volume, suggesting targeted mitigation actions such as dual qualification and safety stock increases. Limitations regarding the subjective basis of FMEA scores and their correlation structure are discussed.

SYN-PUB-08281.title: Robust Supplier Selection under Interval-Valued Criteria Weights: A Min-Max Regret Formulation
SYN-PUB-08281.text:
Robust Supplier Selection under Interval-Valued Criteria Weights: A Min-Max Regret Formulation (2025, journal, International Journal of Production and Logistics Research).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Cristina Moldovan (outside co-author).
Keywords: robust optimisation; min-max regret; interval weights; supplier selection; mixed-integer programming.
When decision-makers cannot precisely specify the relative importance of evaluation criteria, using exact weights in multi-criteria supplier selection models can lead to solutions that perform poorly under alternative weight settings. This paper proposes a min-max regret model for supplier selection in which criteria weights are only known to lie within specified intervals, derived from a group of eight procurement professionals via an interactive questioning protocol. The model selects the supplier portfolio that minimises the maximum deviation from the optimal solution across all weight vectors within the defined intervals. The approach is applied to a dataset of 10 candidate suppliers for an agri-food company in Sombor, evaluated across six criteria. The robust solution differs from the deterministic weighted-sum solution in two out of five selected suppliers. Computational experiments show that the min-max regret formulation can be solved exactly for problems of this size within a few seconds using standard mixed-integer programming solvers. The paper includes a comparison with a minimax regret approach based on sampled weight vectors and discusses conditions under which the exact and approximate solutions agree.

SYN-PUB-08282.title: Integrating Carbon Emission Penalties into Stochastic Supplier Selection: Evidence from the Serbian Food Processing Sector
SYN-PUB-08282.text:
Integrating Carbon Emission Penalties into Stochastic Supplier Selection: Evidence from the Serbian Food Processing Sector (2026, conference, Proceedings of the 12th International Symposium on Sustainable Manufacturing and Supply Chains (ISMSC), Timișoara).
Authors: István Lukács (R0750); Jelena Borozan (outside co-author); Zoran Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: carbon emissions; sustainable procurement; stochastic optimisation; Pareto frontier; food processing.
Growing regulatory pressure on greenhouse gas emissions is beginning to affect procurement decisions in Serbian manufacturing. This paper extends a two-stage stochastic supplier selection model to incorporate a carbon emission penalty cost term, allowing procurement planners to evaluate the trade-off between economic and emission-related objectives under demand uncertainty. Emission factors per unit shipped are estimated for each supplier based on transport distance, modal split, and energy intensity data gathered through supplier questionnaires. Demand scenarios are constructed from 24 months of sales data for a pasta production company based near Novi Sad. The extended model is solved for 30, 50, and 100 scenario sets to assess solution stability. Results indicate that including a carbon penalty equivalent to 25 EUR per tonne of CO2 changes the preferred supplier in one out of four sourcing categories and increases expected total procurement cost by 2.1%. The paper also presents a Pareto frontier between expected cost and expected total emissions, computed by parametric variation of the carbon penalty, and identifies a range of penalty values within which the supplier portfolio remains unchanged, providing guidance for sensitivity to future carbon pricing.

SYN-PUB-08283.title: Evaluating buffer sizing policies in unbalanced mixed-model lines through designed simulation experiments
SYN-PUB-08283.text:
Evaluating buffer sizing policies in unbalanced mixed-model lines through designed simulation experiments (2021, journal, Simulation Modelling Practice and Theory – Regional Series).
Authors: Lazar Marković (R0763); Péter Varga (outside co-author); Katarina Malešević (R0835); István Lukács (R0750); Ivan Subotić (outside co-author).
Keywords: buffer sizing; mixed-model line; designed experiments; work-in-process; throughput.
Buffer sizing is a key design decision in mixed-model assembly that is often addressed heuristically. This paper uses a full-factorial simulation experiment to quantify the effect of buffer capacity, line imbalance level, and product-mix ratio on throughput and work-in-process inventory simultaneously. Experiments were conducted on a parameterised simulation model representing a six-station line with configurable imbalance (coefficient of variation of station workloads ranging from 0.05 to 0.35) and three product-mix scenarios. In total, 648 experimental conditions were evaluated, each replicated 30 times to achieve 95% confidence intervals of width below 2% of mean throughput. The results show that for imbalance levels above 0.20, buffer insertion at the first identified bottleneck upstream neighbour delivers more than 80% of the throughput gain achievable with unconstrained buffering, with a WIP cost two to three times lower than full buffering.

SYN-PUB-08314.title: A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments
SYN-PUB-08314.text:
A watchdog-based self-recovery scheme for 802.15.4 sensor nodes in unattended deployments (2013, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Sensor Systems).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: watchdog timer; fault recovery; wireless sensor node; soil monitoring; ATmega.
Unattended wireless sensor nodes in field deployments frequently enter irrecoverable software states due to memory corruption, peripheral lockup, or stack overflow caused by transient power events. This paper presents a layered watchdog architecture implemented on an ATmega128RFA1 platform in which three independent timers supervise the operating system scheduler, the radio driver, and the analog front-end sequencer separately. When any tier detects a violation of its expected heartbeat window, a graduated recovery procedure is executed that avoids full device reset in roughly 74 percent of observed fault cases, thereby preserving the sensor's runtime context. The scheme was evaluated over a 90-day outdoor deployment of 18 nodes sampling soil moisture at 10-minute intervals. Mean time between unrecoverable resets increased from 11.3 days in the baseline configuration to 61.7 days with the proposed architecture. Current overhead introduced by the additional supervision circuitry was measured at 38 µA in active mode, representing less than 2 percent of total node consumption. The design is described in sufficient detail to be reproduced on comparable 8-bit and 16-bit microcontroller families.

SYN-PUB-08315.title: On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring
SYN-PUB-08315.text:
On-node detection of resistive humidity sensor drift using recursive least-squares residual monitoring (2018, journal, Sensors and Actuators: Methods and Applications).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ivan Zec (R0903); Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author).
Keywords: sensor drift; humidity sensor; recursive least squares; edge diagnostics; anomaly detection.
Capacitive and resistive humidity sensors used in long-term field deployments exhibit systematic drift attributable to membrane contamination, mechanical stress, and UV degradation of the sensing polymer. This study examines drift detection using a recursive least-squares estimator running on a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontroller with 64 kB RAM. The estimator maintains a sliding 72-hour model of sensor behaviour and raises a diagnostic flag when the standardised prediction residual exceeds a threshold calibrated to yield a 5 percent false-alarm rate under clean operating conditions. The method was validated against a controlled ageing experiment in which 24 SHT31-compatible sensors were exposed to accelerated UV and humidity cycling; 21 of 22 drift events exceeding 3 percent RH offset were detected within 8 hours of onset. Computational cost was benchmarked at 1.2 ms per update cycle at 48 MHz, consuming negligible battery capacity relative to the radio subsystem. The paper includes a discussion of threshold sensitivity as a function of sampling interval and recommends a minimum of 15-minute sampling for reliable operation.

SYN-PUB-08316.title: Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions
SYN-PUB-08316.text:
Energy-aware retransmission scheduling for IoT nodes operating on solar-harvested power under partial shading conditions (2020, book chapter, Handbook of Low-Power Sensing Systems for Environmental Applications (TechPress Academic, Vienna)).
Authors: Gordana Simić (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Ralf Brünner (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting; solar power; transmission scheduling; supercapacitor; duty cycle control.
Solar energy harvesting for IoT nodes in temperate climates is complicated by persistent partial shading from vegetation, cloud cover, and seasonal sun angle variation. This chapter reviews energy buffering and transmission scheduling strategies applicable to nodes where the harvester output drops to 10–40 percent of rated capacity for multi-hour periods. A discrete-time predictive controller is presented that adjusts the uplink reporting interval and transmission power based on a rolling 24-hour energy budget estimated from a small supercapacitor voltage sensor. Simulations using one-year solar irradiance data from three sites in the Pannonian Plain show that the controller maintains the reporting duty cycle above 85 percent of the target rate throughout the year compared with 61 percent for a fixed-interval baseline. The chapter also covers hardware design guidelines for solar panel placement and MPPT circuit selection, and discusses the trade-off between supercapacitor capacity, leakage current, and cold-start reliability in sub-zero conditions.

SYN-PUB-08317.title: Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments
SYN-PUB-08317.text:
Multi-metric data quality scoring at the gateway for heterogeneous agricultural IoT deployments (2021, conference, IEEE International Conference on Agricultural IoT and Precision Farming (AIPF)).
Authors: Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Marija Đurić (outside co-author); Konstantinos Papadimitriou (outside co-author).
Keywords: data quality; gateway processing; agricultural IoT; anomaly flagging; heterogeneous networks.
Aggregation gateways in agricultural IoT networks receive streams from sensors operating under different power regimes, communication protocols, and environmental exposures. This paper proposes a gateway-side data quality scoring framework that assigns each incoming measurement a composite score based on four sub-metrics: timeliness (elapsed time since last message relative to expected interval), signal plausibility (z-score against a rolling peer-group distribution), battery state estimate, and historical reliability index derived from 30-day uptime statistics. The framework was implemented in Python 3.9 on a Raspberry Pi 4 gateway serving 61 nodes in a test vineyard in Fruška Gora, processing approximately 8,700 messages per day. Over a 5-month evaluation period, the composite score correctly flagged 93 of 97 manually confirmed measurement anomalies and produced 11 false positives. Score computation added a mean latency of 4.1 ms per message at gateway level. The scoring metadata is forwarded alongside raw measurements to a central time-series database, enabling downstream analytics to weight observations accordingly. Integration steps for two commercial farm management platforms are documented.

SYN-PUB-08318.title: Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study
SYN-PUB-08318.text:
Firmware update reliability over NB-IoT in low-signal rural environments: a field study (2022, journal, Embedded Systems and Wireless Communications Letters).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Aleksandra Ninković (outside co-author); Tibor Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: FOTA; firmware update; NB-IoT; rural deployment; link quality.
Over-the-air firmware updates (FOTA) are essential for maintaining security and functionality of deployed IoT nodes but are poorly characterised in weak-signal rural cellular conditions. This study documents 1,840 FOTA sessions conducted across 46 NB-IoT nodes installed at distances of 8–22 km from the nearest base station in the southern Bačka region of Serbia. Update payloads ranged from 48 to 192 kB and were delivered using a block-based transfer protocol with configurable block size and retry budget. Session success rate was 81.4 percent without adaptive configuration and rose to 94.6 percent when block size was reduced from 512 to 128 bytes and the retry budget was tripled. Failed sessions were traced primarily to receive-window mismatches during peak network load periods. Energy cost per successful update was measured between 0.9 and 3.4 mAh depending on retry overhead. The paper quantifies the dependency of success rate on RSRP and presents a simple heuristic for selecting block size based on a short link probe transmitted before each update session.

SYN-PUB-08319.title: Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study
SYN-PUB-08319.text:
Characterising the interaction between cellular network congestion and duty-cycle regulation in dense IoT deployments: a simulation and measurement study (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.NI)).
Authors: Žarko Jakovljević (R0754); Luka Horvatović (outside co-author); Florian Kersting (outside co-author).
Keywords: NB-IoT congestion; duty cycle; dense IoT; network simulation; transmission scheduling.
When hundreds of IoT nodes sharing a single NB-IoT cell simultaneously enter their reporting window, uplink congestion increases packet delay and loss in ways that interact nonlinearly with node-level duty-cycle power management. This preprint reports a combined simulation and measurement study: a system-level LTE-M/NB-IoT simulator was configured to match the topology of a 312-node crop monitoring network in Srem, and its congestion behaviour was cross-validated against 8 weeks of gateway-side timestamps showing mean delay growth from 1.2 s to 14.7 s during morning reporting peaks. The simulator was then used to evaluate four transmission-window randomisation strategies across node densities from 50 to 500 nodes per cell. A jitter-and-backoff strategy combining a randomised initial delay drawn from a 0–300 s uniform window with an exponential backoff on contention reduced 99th-percentile delay from 41 s to 8 s and cut failed transmissions by 63 percent at 400 nodes per cell. Interaction effects with solar harvesting schedules are discussed and a recommended configuration table is provided for deployment engineers.

SYN-PUB-08545.title: Characterising Interference Patterns in Dense 2.4 GHz IoT Deployments: A Measurement Study
SYN-PUB-08545.text:
Characterising Interference Patterns in Dense 2.4 GHz IoT Deployments: A Measurement Study (2016, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Wireless Sensor and IoT Systems (CEWSIS)).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Aleksandra Petrović (outside co-author); Norbert Farkas (outside co-author).
Keywords: interference measurement; IEEE 802.15.4; dense IoT; spectrum occupancy.
Dense IEEE 802.15.4 and IEEE 802.11 co-existence is studied through a structured measurement campaign conducted across three office floors totalling 1,200 square metres at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Novi Sad. Forty-two sensor nodes and eight Wi-Fi access points were deployed simultaneously, and spectrum occupancy was logged over 72 hours using USRP B210 radios. Packet reception rates, channel busy times, and inter-arrival jitter are reported across 16 non-overlapping and overlapping channel configurations. Results show that the median packet loss rate in the densest configuration reaches 18% on channel 11 when Wi-Fi traffic exceeds 4 Mbps aggregate. A simple empirical interference model is fitted to the data and validated against a held-out 24-hour trace. The dataset and measurement scripts are released publicly. The model is intended as an input layer for scheduling algorithms in subsequent work.

SYN-PUB-08546.title: Energy Neutral Operation Bounds for Solar-Harvesting Sensor Nodes With On-Board Inference Workloads
SYN-PUB-08546.text:
Energy Neutral Operation Bounds for Solar-Harvesting Sensor Nodes With On-Board Inference Workloads (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Embedded Systems).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Jovana Lazić (outside co-author); Tomáš Bureš (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting; energy-neutral operation; supercapacitor; embedded inference.
The paper derives analytical bounds on the maximum sustainable computation rate for sensor nodes powered exclusively by small-area photovoltaic panels under Central European solar irradiance profiles. A finite-capacity supercapacitor energy buffer is modelled, and the tradeoff between inference task complexity and buffer underflow probability is characterised using a Markov chain formulation. Irradiance traces from Novi Sad (2014–2018, hourly resolution) sourced from the national meteorological service are used as the stochastic input. Results show that a node with a 1 F supercapacitor and a 2 cm² panel can sustain a 30 ms inference task every 4.2 seconds at a 99% non-interruption probability in summer, falling to one task every 14.7 seconds in December. A lookup-table controller is designed and validated on STM32L4-based hardware. Code is made available as open source.

SYN-PUB-08547.title: Comparative Evaluation of Offloading Granularity Strategies in Multi-Tier Edge Architectures
SYN-PUB-08547.text:
Comparative Evaluation of Offloading Granularity Strategies in Multi-Tier Edge Architectures (2020, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Edge and Fog Computing Systems (EFCS)).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Sonja Bošković (R0923); Stefan Nikolić (outside co-author); Reinhilde Claes (outside co-author).
Keywords: task offloading granularity; multi-tier edge; OMNeT++ simulation; latency.
Three offloading granularity models—binary, fractional, and subtask-level—are compared in a simulated three-tier architecture consisting of end devices, a local edge server, and a regional cloudlet. Simulation is implemented in OMNeT++ 5.6 using the INET framework extended with a custom task queue module. Workload traces are derived from a smart-factory IoT pilot involving 120 temperature, vibration, and current sensors sampled at 100 Hz. Energy consumption, end-to-end latency, and server CPU utilisation are measured over simulated intervals of 3,600 seconds under low, medium, and high congestion conditions. Subtask-level offloading reduces 95th-percentile latency by 22% over binary offloading at the cost of a 9% increase in signalling overhead. Fractional offloading provides a middle ground with lower implementation complexity. Results suggest that subtask decomposition is worthwhile only when task graphs contain at least five parallelisable branches.

SYN-PUB-08548.title: Scheduling Harvested-Energy Allocation Across Concurrent Sensing and Communication Tasks on a Single MCU
SYN-PUB-08548.text:
Scheduling Harvested-Energy Allocation Across Concurrent Sensing and Communication Tasks on a Single MCU (2022, journal, Journal of Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Ana Radu (outside co-author).
Keywords: real-time scheduling; energy harvesting; EDF; microcontroller; duty cycle.
This work addresses the problem of allocating harvested energy between concurrent sensing and wireless transmission tasks executing on a single microcontroller. A priority-inversion-free earliest-deadline-first variant is adapted to account for a stochastically replenished energy budget. The scheduler is implemented on a Nordic nRF9160 system-in-package device. A hardware emulator injects synthetic energy traces derived from piezoelectric and RF energy harvesting measurements taken from a vibrating industrial pipe fixture. Over 48-hour continuous operation tests, the proposed scheduler reduces task deadline miss rate from 11.3% to 3.7% compared to an energy-oblivious EDF baseline, while maintaining average radio duty cycle below 4%. The paper also provides a worst-case energy consumption analysis that supports offline dimensioning of the storage element.

SYN-PUB-08549.title: A Congestion Index for Heterogeneous IoT Access Networks and Its Use in Offloading Triggers
SYN-PUB-08549.text:
A Congestion Index for Heterogeneous IoT Access Networks and Its Use in Offloading Triggers (2023, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Dragan Vukić (outside co-author); Valentina Kovač (outside co-author); Ognjen Malešević (R0987); Péter Molnár (outside co-author).
Keywords: congestion index; heterogeneous IoT; offloading trigger; LoRaWAN; NB-IoT.
The paper proposes a lightweight congestion index computed from three observable quantities—channel busy ratio, queue occupancy at the edge node, and per-flow retransmission rate—that can be calculated on resource-constrained hardware without packet inspection. The index is calibrated against ground-truth throughput measurements on a 35-node testbed spanning IEEE 802.15.4, LoRaWAN, and NB-IoT access segments. Calibration uses a ridge regression fit on 48 hours of labelled traffic. The index is then embedded as a trigger condition in an offloading policy: offloading is initiated only when the index exceeds a threshold tuned per access technology. Field evaluation over 14 days shows that trigger-based offloading reduces unnecessary offload invocations by 41% compared to a fixed-interval policy, with negligible increase in peak latency. The index computation requires under 0.8 ms on a Cortex-M4 core.

SYN-PUB-08550.title: Energy Harvesting for Mobile Edge Nodes: Survey of Sources, Storage Technologies, and Scheduling Approaches
SYN-PUB-08550.text:
Energy Harvesting for Mobile Edge Nodes: Survey of Sources, Storage Technologies, and Scheduling Approaches (2023, book chapter, Handbook of Mobile Edge Computing: Architectures and Applications, Springer).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Jovana Lazić (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy harvesting survey; edge computing; storage technologies; scheduling.
This book chapter surveys energy harvesting modalities applicable to mobile and fixed edge computing nodes in IoT deployments, covering solar, vibration-based piezoelectric, RF ambient, and thermal gradient sources. Typical harvested power ranges and temporal variability are tabulated for each source based on literature values and the authors' own measurements. Storage technologies—lithium polymer batteries, supercapacitors, and hybrid cells—are compared on capacity, leakage rate, and cycle lifetime. The chapter then surveys scheduling frameworks published between 2012 and 2022, categorising them by optimisation objective (energy neutrality, latency minimisation, reliability) and solution method (Lyapunov, dynamic programming, reinforcement learning, heuristic). A comparison table of 34 reviewed systems is provided. Open research directions highlighted include multi-source harvesting coordination and predictive models trained on locally collected irradiance data.

SYN-PUB-08551.title: Deadline-Aware Partial Offloading Under Shared Uplink Congestion: A Fluid Model Analysis
SYN-PUB-08551.text:
Deadline-Aware Partial Offloading Under Shared Uplink Congestion: A Fluid Model Analysis (2026, journal, Performance Evaluation: An International Journal).
Authors: Ivona Ostojić (R0779); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Ana Radu (outside co-author); Zsolt Horváth (outside co-author).
Keywords: partial offloading; fluid model; shared uplink; deadline; coordination.
A fluid model is developed to analyse the interaction between multiple IoT devices sharing a single uplink channel when each device independently applies a partial offloading policy with hard task deadlines. The model captures the feedback loop in which individual offloading decisions increase aggregate channel load, which in turn degrades the transmission time for all devices. Fixed-point analysis yields conditions on device count and arrival rate under which deadline satisfaction probability exceeds 95%. Numerical results for populations of 10, 20, and 40 devices show that without coordination, deadline miss rate grows superlinearly beyond 28 devices for the tested parameter set. A simple token-bucket coordination mechanism is proposed that restores near-linear scaling. The analysis is validated against event-driven simulations in NS-3 with relative error below 6% across all tested configurations.

SYN-PUB-08788.title: A Practical Framework for ISO 14064-1 Organisational GHG Inventories in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs
SYN-PUB-08788.text:
A Practical Framework for ISO 14064-1 Organisational GHG Inventories in Serbian Manufacturing SMEs (2018, journal, Environmental and Industrial Management Review).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Aleksandar Tomić (outside co-author); Bojana Stanković (outside co-author); Stefan Dimitrijević (R0805).
Keywords: ISO 14064; organisational GHG inventory; SME; Scope 1 and 2; Serbia.
Small and medium-sized manufacturers in Serbia increasingly face requests from export customers and public procurement bodies to document greenhouse gas emissions at the organisational level. ISO 14064-1 provides a recognised framework, but its implementation guidance assumes resource levels not typical of Serbian SMEs. This paper develops and tests a simplified but standard-conformant procedure for Scope 1 and Scope 2 inventory compilation, applied to four manufacturing companies in the Novi Sad industrial zone with between 45 and 210 employees. The procedure uses default emission factors from the national energy balance supplemented by supplier-specific electricity grid data from EPS. Data collection time at each company was recorded; the full inventory was completed in an average of 14 working days per company. Verification readiness was assessed against ISO 14064-3 criteria. Two companies achieved documentation sufficient for third-party verification without additional consultancy. Barriers identified include inconsistent utility metering and lack of internal ownership of environmental data. The paper provides a checklist and data collection template adapted to Serbian regulatory and utility contexts.

SYN-PUB-08820.title: Empirical Path-Loss Characterisation for 868 MHz Signals in a Mixed Residential and Commercial District
SYN-PUB-08820.text:
Empirical Path-Loss Characterisation for 868 MHz Signals in a Mixed Residential and Commercial District (2010, journal, Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computing – Serbia).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: path-loss model; 868 MHz; measurement campaign; COST 231 Hata; shadowing.
This paper presents a measurement-based path-loss study conducted in the Liman district of Novi Sad at 868 MHz during autumn 2009. A total of 4 800 received signal strength indicator samples were collected along 22 transects using a calibrated test transmitter and a portable receiver mounted on a bicycle. The log-distance model with a dual-slope breakpoint at 120 m was fitted to the data, yielding path-loss exponents of 2.1 and 3.6 for the near and far zones, respectively. Shadowing standard deviation was estimated at 7.2 dB. Results are compared against the COST 231 Hata model, which overestimates median loss by 4.8 dB in this environment. The fitted model parameters are provided as a baseline for subsequent LoRa link budget calculations in the region. Measurement methodology, equipment calibration procedure, and statistical goodness-of-fit tests are described in detail.

SYN-PUB-08822.title: Effect of Seasonal Foliage on LoRa Received Signal Strength in a Suburban Environment
SYN-PUB-08822.text:
Effect of Seasonal Foliage on LoRa Received Signal Strength in a Suburban Environment (2016, journal, Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computing – Serbia).
Authors: Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: vegetation attenuation; seasonal variability; RSSI; LoRa testbed; suburban.
Vegetation attenuation is a well-known propagation impairment but its seasonal variability at 868 MHz has not been systematically quantified for LoRa links in a continental European climate. This study used a fixed LoRa testbed with five static end nodes deployed in a mixed residential and park area in Novi Sad to record RSSI and SNR continuously over a 14-month period from March 2015 to April 2016. Three nodes had line-of-sight paths through deciduous trees; two served as reference nodes with unobstructed paths. A mean additional attenuation of 8.4 dB was observed during full-leaf season (June–September) compared with the dormant season, with a standard deviation across links of 2.1 dB. The results suggest that link budget calculations for year-round deployments in this climate should incorporate a seasonal margin of at least 11 dB when tree-lined paths are unavoidable.

SYN-PUB-08826.title: LoRa Link Budget Analysis for Water Meter Telemetry in a Dense Urban Area: A Case Study
SYN-PUB-08826.text:
LoRa Link Budget Analysis for Water Meter Telemetry in a Dense Urban Area: A Case Study (2020, book chapter, IoT Deployment Strategies for Smart Cities – Edited Volume, TechPress Balkan).
Authors: Ljiljana Stanković (outside co-author); Danilo Uzelac (R0962); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: water metering; AMR; link budget; basement deployment; LoRaWAN.
This chapter examines the practical link budget constraints encountered when deploying LoRaWAN-based automatic meter reading for water utilities in a densely built urban district. The case study is based on a pilot deployment of 340 end nodes in the Stari Grad neighbourhood of Novi Sad, where meter boxes are located in basement utility cupboards 1.5–2.5 m below street level. The chapter first derives an extended link budget model that accounts for: outdoor urban path loss (measured empirically), building wall penetration loss (14–28 dB depending on construction type), and meter-box cavity shielding (estimated 6–10 dB additional loss). The model is validated against measured delivery rates from the pilot. Results show that SF10 was sufficient for 87% of nodes, while the remaining 13% required SF12 and in some cases external antenna cables. Network dimensioning guidelines are provided for practitioners.

SYN-PUB-08828.title: Three-Dimensional Ray-Tracing Validation Against Large-Scale LoRa RSSI Measurements in Novi Sad
SYN-PUB-08828.text:
Three-Dimensional Ray-Tracing Validation Against Large-Scale LoRa RSSI Measurements in Novi Sad (2023, journal, Radio Science and Propagation – European Journal).
Authors: Marija Vučković (outside co-author); Ana Marković (outside co-author); Christoph Weidner (outside co-author); Branislava Janković (R0811).
Keywords: ray tracing; validation; RSSI; LoRa; building geometry.
Ray-tracing models require careful validation before use in network planning tools. This paper presents a systematic comparison of a 3-D ray-tracing simulator, developed in-house in C++, against 18 500 georeferenced RSSI measurements collected from a 12-gateway LoRaWAN network operating continuously over Novi Sad. Building data were obtained from the geodetic authority of the Republic of Serbia at a cadastral level, supplemented by height estimates derived from a 2020 aerial photogrammetry survey. The simulator considers up to four specular reflections and one diffraction per ray. Over the full dataset, the simulator achieved a root mean square error of 5.8 dB and a mean error of −0.4 dB. Errors were highest in areas with large construction sites where building models lagged physical reality by up to 18 months. A correction procedure using recent satellite imagery to flag stale geometry is described and shown to reduce RMSE by 0.9 dB in affected zones.

SYN-PUB-09075.title: Cognitive Load During Digital-Physical Hybrid Math Tasks: Eye-Tracking Evidence from Nine-Year-Olds
SYN-PUB-09075.text:
Cognitive Load During Digital-Physical Hybrid Math Tasks: Eye-Tracking Evidence from Nine-Year-Olds (2016, journal, Journal of Cognitive and Educational Technology).
Authors: Nemanja Đurić (outside co-author); Boris Krstić (R0872); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837); Nenad Novaković (R1043).
Keywords: eye-tracking; cognitive load; fraction learning; hybrid tasks; nine-year-olds.
This study used eye-tracking to assess cognitive load while 34 nine-year-old students completed a hybrid math task combining a tablet-based game with physical fraction tiles. Fixation duration, saccade length, and pupil dilation were recorded using a remote eye-tracker mounted on a desk. Tasks required students to match digital fraction representations to physical tile arrangements of varying complexity. Linear mixed-effects models showed that pupil dilation increased significantly with task complexity level (β = 0.14 mm per level, 95% CI [0.08, 0.20]), while longer fixations on the physical tile area were associated with higher accuracy on subsequent written fraction problems (r = 0.43). Students who frequently switched gaze between screen and tiles made fewer procedural errors. Results suggest that coordinated dual-channel engagement, rather than one medium alone, supports fraction comprehension. Practical implications for task sequencing in hybrid game design are discussed.

SYN-PUB-09076.title: Game Mechanics and Fraction Misconceptions: A Quasi-Experimental Classroom Study
SYN-PUB-09076.text:
Game Mechanics and Fraction Misconceptions: A Quasi-Experimental Classroom Study (2017, journal, European Journal of Mathematics Education).
Authors: Vukica Arsić (R0837); Tatjana Lukić (outside co-author); Gábor Mérei (outside co-author).
Keywords: fraction misconceptions; card game; quasi-experimental; part-whole model; implementation fidelity.
Persistent misconceptions about fractions, such as treating numerator and denominator as independent whole numbers, are well documented but poorly addressed by conventional drill practice. This quasi-experimental study tested whether a physical card game designed around part-whole fraction models could reduce four specific misconceptions identified in a 186-student diagnostic pre-test drawn from grades four and five in five Vojvodina schools. Game sessions replaced one of three weekly arithmetic lessons over eight weeks. Post-test data showed statistically significant reductions in two of the four targeted misconceptions: the independent-whole-number error fell from 54% to 31% of responses, and the larger-denominator-means-larger-fraction error fell from 41% to 22%. The other two misconceptions showed non-significant trends. Teacher implementation fidelity, measured via observation checklists, was moderately correlated with misconception reduction rates (r = 0.52). The study highlights implementation quality as a key moderator of game-based outcomes.

SYN-PUB-09077.title: Teachers' Preparedness to Facilitate Game-Based Mathematics Lessons: Survey Evidence from Primary Schools in Serbia
SYN-PUB-09077.text:
Teachers' Preparedness to Facilitate Game-Based Mathematics Lessons: Survey Evidence from Primary Schools in Serbia (2018, journal, Teaching and Teacher Education in the Balkans).
Authors: Snežana Bogdanović (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837); Ivana Stevanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: teacher preparedness; professional development; game facilitation; survey; primary mathematics.
Effective integration of game-based learning in primary mathematics depends substantially on teacher knowledge and confidence. This cross-sectional survey reached 203 primary school mathematics teachers across Serbia through a self-administered online questionnaire measuring four constructs: technological competence, game-facilitation confidence, beliefs about play in learning, and reported barriers. Exploratory factor analysis confirmed a four-factor solution accounting for 61% of variance. Teachers in urban schools reported significantly higher technological competence than those in rural schools (t(201) = 3.87, p < 0.001), while beliefs about play did not differ by location. Only 28% of respondents reported having received any in-service training on game-based methods. Regression analysis showed that game-facilitation confidence was the strongest predictor of self-reported frequency of game use in class, above technological competence and beliefs. Findings point to a need for structured professional development programmes targeting facilitation skills specifically.

SYN-PUB-09078.title: Spatial Reasoning and Number Line Understanding: Can a Hybrid Sliding-Tile Game Bridge the Two?
SYN-PUB-09078.text:
Spatial Reasoning and Number Line Understanding: Can a Hybrid Sliding-Tile Game Bridge the Two? (2021, journal, Spatial Cognition and Education).
Authors: Bojan Radivojević (outside co-author); Nenad Novaković (R1043); Maja Tomić (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837); Renáta Fehér (outside co-author).
Keywords: spatial reasoning; number line; hybrid game; grade three; mediation analysis.
Research suggests that spatial reasoning and number line understanding share cognitive resources in late childhood, but few interventions have targeted both simultaneously. This study evaluated a hybrid game in which students physically repositioned numbered tiles on a floor-mounted number line while receiving feedback from a paired tablet application. Eighty-one students in grade three from four schools participated in a six-week intervention. Spatial reasoning was measured with a mental rotation task and a block-pattern completion task; number line understanding was measured with a computerised number placement task. Compared to a business-as-usual control group, the intervention group showed significant improvement on the number placement task (d = 0.67) and on the block-pattern task (d = 0.44), but not on mental rotation (d = 0.18, p = 0.19). Mediation analysis suggested that number line gains partially mediated improvements on block-pattern completion, though causal interpretation is limited by study design.

SYN-PUB-09079.title: Socioeconomic Moderation of Game-Based Learning Effects on Arithmetic in Grade Four: Evidence from Rural and Urban Schools in Vojvodina
SYN-PUB-09079.text:
Socioeconomic Moderation of Game-Based Learning Effects on Arithmetic in Grade Four: Evidence from Rural and Urban Schools in Vojvodina (2022, journal, Journal of Educational Equity and Technology).
Authors: Aleksandra Petković (outside co-author); Dragiša Cvejić (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: socioeconomic moderation; multilevel modelling; Vojvodina; achievement gap; arithmetic.
Whether game-based learning benefits are equally distributed across socioeconomic groups is underexplored in the regional literature. This study used multilevel modelling to analyse data from a six-week hybrid game intervention conducted across 14 primary schools in Vojvodina, covering 312 fourth-grade students. Schools were classified as urban, peri-urban, and rural; student socioeconomic status was estimated using a parental education composite score. The main effect of the intervention on arithmetic post-test scores was significant (β = 5.1 points, SE = 1.2). A significant interaction between intervention condition and socioeconomic status (β = 1.8, SE = 0.7, p = 0.01) indicated that students from lower socioeconomic backgrounds benefited somewhat more from the game condition than higher-SES peers, though both groups improved. School location did not moderate the intervention effect after controlling for socioeconomic status. These findings tentatively support the use of hybrid games as a tool for reducing within-classroom arithmetic achievement gaps.

SYN-PUB-09080.title: Using Tablet-Logged Interaction Data to Predict Mathematics Post-Test Scores in a Game-Based Intervention
SYN-PUB-09080.text:
Using Tablet-Logged Interaction Data to Predict Mathematics Post-Test Scores in a Game-Based Intervention (2023, conference, Educational Data Mining and Learning Analytics Conference Proceedings).
Authors: Stefan Janković (outside co-author); Milena Grujičić (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: interaction logs; predictive modelling; ridge regression; formative assessment; tablet games.
Tablet-based educational games generate interaction logs that can, in principle, serve as formative signals during an intervention. This study examined whether log data collected during a four-week hybrid game intervention predicted end-of-intervention post-test scores in 88 grade-four and grade-five students. Nine log features were extracted per student per session: session duration, number of attempts per item, error rate, help-request frequency, inter-attempt latency, game-level progression rate, voluntary replay frequency, score volatility, and session abandonment count. Ridge regression with leave-one-out cross-validation explained 41% of post-test variance using log features alone, compared with 38% for the arithmetic pre-test score alone. A combined model including both pre-test score and log features explained 53% of variance. Error rate and inter-attempt latency were the most influential log features. The study suggests that interaction logs carry predictive information beyond baseline ability, but effect sizes indicate that log-based prediction should complement, not replace, conventional assessment.

SYN-PUB-09081.title: A Registered Replication of the Hybrid Game Advantage for Fraction Near-Transfer: Preregistered Study in Three Countries
SYN-PUB-09081.text:
A Registered Replication of the Hybrid Game Advantage for Fraction Near-Transfer: Preregistered Study in Three Countries (2024, journal, Journal of Experimental Education).
Authors: Kristina Varga (outside co-author); Renáta Fehér (outside co-author); Tatjana Lukić (outside co-author); Olivier Renard (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: registered replication; hybrid game; fraction transfer; multi-country; prior knowledge.
A 2014 study by the first author reported a near-transfer advantage for hybrid over digital-only fraction game instruction. This registered replication tested the same hypothesis across schools in Serbia, Croatia, and Hungary, enrolling 341 grade-four students in a three-arm design (hybrid game, digital-only game, curriculum-as-usual control). Preregistration was lodged on the Open Science Framework before data collection. The arithmetic test and near-transfer fraction task were identical to the original study; a new far-transfer measurement task was added. Replication of the near-transfer advantage was successful in two of three countries: standardised effect sizes were d = 0.44 (Serbia), d = 0.39 (Croatia), and d = 0.11 (Hungary, non-significant). A moderation analysis found that the Hungarian null result was associated with significantly higher baseline fraction knowledge in those students. Far-transfer effects were small and non-significant across all sites. The study supports the original finding with important boundary conditions related to prior knowledge levels.

SYN-PUB-09082.title: Effects of Game Session Length on Arithmetic Learning and Fatigue in Nine-to-Eleven-Year-Olds: A Within-Subject Crossover Study
SYN-PUB-09082.text:
Effects of Game Session Length on Arithmetic Learning and Fatigue in Nine-to-Eleven-Year-Olds: A Within-Subject Crossover Study (2026, journal, British Journal of Educational Psychology).
Authors: Milena Grujičić (outside co-author); Stefan Janković (outside co-author); Vukica Arsić (R0837).
Keywords: session length; fatigue; crossover design; arithmetic; nine-to-eleven-year-olds.
Optimal session length for game-based arithmetic practice remains empirically underdetermined. This within-subject crossover study assigned 62 students aged nine to eleven to three session lengths (15, 30, and 45 minutes) using a counterbalanced schedule over nine weeks. Each session length was repeated twice per student. Outcomes measured immediately after each session included a ten-item arithmetic probe, a five-item attention check, and a self-report fatigue rating on a visual analogue scale adapted for children. Linear mixed-effects models treating student as a random effect showed that arithmetic probe scores peaked after 30-minute sessions and were significantly lower after 45-minute sessions (β = −1.8 items, 95% CI [−3.1, −0.5]). Fatigue ratings increased monotonically with session length. Attentiveness scores did not differ between 15- and 30-minute sessions but were lower after 45 minutes. Order effects were not significant. Results recommend 30-minute game sessions as a practical default for this age group in classroom settings.

SYN-PUB-09109.title: Bayesian estimation of the Bühlmann credibility factor under sparse claim records
SYN-PUB-09109.text:
Bayesian estimation of the Bühlmann credibility factor under sparse claim records (2013, journal, Acta Mathematica et Informatica Universitatis Ostraviensis).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Andrej Kokol Bukovšek (outside co-author).
Keywords: credibility theory; Bühlmann model; hierarchical Bayes; sparse data; prior specification.
Classical Bühlmann credibility assumes sufficient within-risk observations to reliably estimate the within-risk variance. When individual risk histories contain fewer than five annual observations—common in industrial liability and agricultural lines—the naive credibility weight is severely biased. This paper reformulates the Bühlmann parameter estimation problem as a hierarchical Bayesian model with weakly informative priors on the between- and within-risk variance components. Using a synthetic portfolio of 120 risks with histories of one to four years, generated from a shifted log-normal collective, we show that the posterior mean credibility factor reduces mean squared prediction error by 18–31 percent relative to the empirical Bühlmann estimate across three prior specifications. A leave-one-risk-out validation on a real agricultural hail portfolio from a regional insurer confirms a 22 percent improvement in out-of-sample squared loss. Computational implementation relies on Hamiltonian Monte Carlo via Stan.

SYN-PUB-09110.title: Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of operational risk losses
SYN-PUB-09110.text:
Threshold selection for peaks-over-threshold modelling of operational risk losses (2015, journal, Journal of Applied Statistical Methods).
Authors: Mirko Janković (outside co-author); Tijana Vučković (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842).
Keywords: peaks-over-threshold; generalised Pareto distribution; threshold selection; operational risk; extreme-value theory.
The peaks-over-threshold (POT) method fits a generalised Pareto distribution (GPD) to exceedances above a chosen threshold. In operational risk datasets the effective sample above any reasonable threshold is small—often 30 to 80 events in a ten-year window—making threshold choice critical. We compare four automated threshold selection rules (mean residual life plot heuristic, Wadsworth's spacings estimator, the Northrop–Coleman profile likelihood, and a Bayes factor approach) on 16 publicly available operational loss event collections and six simulated GPD samples with shape parameters ranging from 0.1 to 0.7. The Bayes factor approach and the Northrop–Coleman rule give the lowest bias in tail quantile estimation when the true shape exceeds 0.3. For lighter tails the spacings estimator is competitive. We provide an open R implementation of all four methods.

SYN-PUB-09111.title: Posterior predictive distributions for aggregate annual loss with few historical years
SYN-PUB-09111.text:
Posterior predictive distributions for aggregate annual loss with few historical years (2016, conference, Insurance: Mathematics and Risk Analysis — Central European Symposium Proceedings).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Katalin Balogh-Fehér (outside co-author); Mirko Janković (outside co-author).
Keywords: collective risk model; Bayesian inference; aggregate loss; posterior predictive; MCMC.
Many small insurance portfolios and corporate self-insurance programmes have at most three to seven years of aggregate annual loss experience, rendering frequentist collective risk model fitting unreliable. We construct a fully Bayesian collective risk model in which claim frequency follows a negative binomial and severity follows a log-normal, with conjugate-like prior elicitation guided by industry benchmark data from reinsurance market surveys. Posterior predictive distributions for next-year aggregate loss are derived by Markov chain Monte Carlo for three case studies: a Serbian municipal fleet programme, a regional hospital professional liability programme, and a crop hail programme in Vojvodina. Value-at-risk at the 99th percentile is estimated with credible intervals. Coverage probability of 95 percent posterior predictive intervals is assessed via a simulation study with 500 synthetic portfolios, yielding empirical coverage of 93.1 to 94.8 percent.

SYN-PUB-09112.title: A credibility-weighted extreme-value estimator for heterogeneous risk groups
SYN-PUB-09112.text:
A credibility-weighted extreme-value estimator for heterogeneous risk groups (2019, journal, Scandinavian Actuarial Journal).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Mirko Janković (outside co-author).
Keywords: credibility theory; GPD; empirical Bayes; tail estimation; heterogeneous risks.
When an insurer groups risks by a covariate (e.g., region or industry class) and each group has a small extreme-loss history, neither a fully pooled GPD fit nor a group-specific fit is satisfactory. We propose a two-stage estimator in which group-level GPD shape parameters are shrunk toward a common mean via empirical Bayes, borrowing the formal structure of Bühlmann–Straub credibility. The shrinkage intensity is estimated by method of moments from the cross-sectional dispersion of group shape estimates. In a Monte Carlo study with 20 groups of 15 to 50 tail observations each, the credibility-weighted estimator reduces root mean squared error of 99.5th-percentile quantile estimates by 14 to 28 percent compared to separate group fits, across shape parameter values of 0.0, 0.2, and 0.4. An application to liability loss triangles from five Central European markets is presented.

SYN-PUB-09113.title: Prior elicitation for Bayesian GPD models using reinsurance treaty data
SYN-PUB-09113.text:
Prior elicitation for Bayesian GPD models using reinsurance treaty data (2020, journal, ASTIN Bulletin: The Journal of the International Actuarial Association).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Nóra Hegedűs (outside co-author); Tijana Vučković (outside co-author).
Keywords: prior elicitation; GPD; Bayesian analysis; reinsurance; small sample.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-09114.title: Ruin probability approximations for compound Poisson risk processes with Pareto claim severities under small portfolio assumptions
SYN-PUB-09114.text:
Ruin probability approximations for compound Poisson risk processes with Pareto claim severities under small portfolio assumptions (2021, journal, European Journal of Actuarial Science and Finance).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842).
Keywords: ruin probability; compound Poisson; heavy-tailed severity; Pareto distribution; saddlepoint approximation.
Classical Cramér–Lundberg ruin probability bounds assume exponential or at most phase-type claim severity distributions. For heavy-tailed Pareto severities with shape parameter below 2, the classical adjustment coefficient does not exist. We examine three approximation approaches—the Pollaczek–Khinchine formula truncated to a finite number of convolutions, a saddlepoint approximation adapted for heavy tails, and a simulation-based estimator with importance sampling—applied to synthetic portfolios of 200 to 1000 annual claims. Relative errors against exact ruin probabilities (available for Pareto via integral equations) are reported for initial surpluses corresponding to 50th, 80th, and 95th percentile reserve levels. The saddlepoint approach performs well for shape parameters above 1.5; below 1.5 the simulation estimator is preferred. Results are relevant for capital adequacy assessment of small non-life insurers.

SYN-PUB-09115.title: Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo
SYN-PUB-09115.text:
Bayesian updating of catastrophe loss models using sequential Monte Carlo (2023, journal, Computational Statistics and Data Analysis).
Authors: Marija Ivanović-Pešić (outside co-author); László Varga (outside co-author); Péter Szabó (R0842).
Keywords: sequential Monte Carlo; Bayesian updating; catastrophe modelling; GPD; hailstorm losses.
Catastrophe risk models for pricing and reserving are typically calibrated on datasets that are augmented by a new large event every several years. Re-running full MCMC after each such update is computationally costly. We adapt a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to propagate posterior distributions over GPD parameters as new catastrophe event observations arrive. Tempering schedules and resampling strategies are tuned for the low-event-count regime typical of natural catastrophe lines: 8 to 30 historical events. We apply the SMC scheme to a stylised hailstorm loss series for the Pannonian Plain region, simulating sequential arrival of one to three new events. Posterior contraction and shifts in 99th-percentile return-level estimates are documented. Computation time is compared with fresh MCMC runs. The approach is implemented in Stan with custom R wrappers.

SYN-PUB-09116.title: Finite-sample performance of credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimators: a simulation study with implications for agricultural insurance
SYN-PUB-09116.text:
Finite-sample performance of credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimators: a simulation study with implications for agricultural insurance (2026, preprint, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics).
Authors: Péter Szabó (R0842); Marija Ivanović-Pešić (outside co-author); Nóra Hegedűs (outside co-author).
Keywords: simulation study; credibility estimators; agricultural insurance; tail quantile; Vojvodina.
Agricultural insurance portfolios in South-East Europe frequently span fewer than fifteen seasons per region, making individual-region tail quantile estimation unreliable. We design a factorial simulation study varying four factors: true GPD shape (0.1, 0.3, 0.5), number of regions (5, 10, 20), observations per region (8, 15, 25), and strength of between-region heterogeneity (low, medium, high). Three credibility-adjusted estimators—empirical Bayes shrinkage on the shape parameter, full hierarchical Bayes, and a simple equal-weight pooled estimator—are compared against individual-region MLE on root mean squared error of the 99th-percentile quantile. Hierarchical Bayes is best in 74 percent of the 108 simulation cells; the gap over empirical Bayes shrinkage is modest (median 4 percent RMSE reduction). Both dominate MLE when within-region sample size is below 15. A brief application to grape hail losses in three Vojvodina districts is included.

SYN-PUB-09246.title: Energy Consumption Mapping in a Small-Batch Metal-Stamping Line: A Bottom-Up Measurement Approach
SYN-PUB-09246.text:
Energy Consumption Mapping in a Small-Batch Metal-Stamping Line: A Bottom-Up Measurement Approach (2013, journal, Journal of Production Engineering).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Dragoslav Petrović (outside co-author); Nataša Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: energy measurement; metal stamping; sub-metering; idle-state losses; small-batch manufacturing.
This paper presents a bottom-up methodology for measuring electricity consumption in a small-batch metal-stamping facility located in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. Thirteen individual machine tools and auxiliary systems were sub-metered continuously over a 12-week production period using clamp-on current loggers at 1-second sampling intervals. The collected data were aggregated by part family and compared with top-down invoice-based estimates from the same period. Results showed that auxiliary systems—compressed air, lighting, and HVAC—accounted for 38% of total consumption, a share consistently underestimated in prior invoice-based analyses at the same site. Specific energy consumption per stamped part ranged from 0.11 to 0.43 kWh depending on batch size, with smaller batches exhibiting disproportionately high idle-state losses. The methodology is reproducible with commercially available metering hardware costing under €800 per measurement point. Findings inform both process scheduling decisions and the energy inventory phase of subsequent LCA studies conducted at the facility.

SYN-PUB-09248.title: Comparative Carbon Footprint of Conventional and Powder-Coated Surface Finishing on Mild Steel Components
SYN-PUB-09248.text:
Comparative Carbon Footprint of Conventional and Powder-Coated Surface Finishing on Mild Steel Components (2016, conference, Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Environmental Protection (IIZS)).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Milena Đorđević (outside co-author); Ljubomir Marković (R0988).
Keywords: surface finishing; powder coating; ISO 14067; VOC emissions; gate-to-gate LCA.
Surface finishing is often omitted or simplified in product-level carbon footprint studies despite its material contribution to overall greenhouse gas emissions. This conference paper reports a comparative LCA of two finishing routes—liquid solvent-based paint and thermosetting powder coating—applied to mild steel enclosures manufactured at a contract coater in Novi Sad. System boundaries followed ISO 14067, covering raw material extraction through gate-to-gate production. Functional unit was defined as one square metre of finished surface meeting a specified salt-spray corrosion class. Primary data on energy and chemical consumption were collected from production logs over six months; background data were sourced from ecoinvent 3.6. Powder coating showed a 22% lower global warming potential per functional unit, primarily due to elimination of VOC-containing solvents and higher transfer efficiency. Waste treatment contributed 18% of total emissions in the solvent-paint route. Results are presented with uncertainty ranges and discussed in the context of regulatory reporting under the EU Industrial Emissions Directive.

SYN-PUB-09249.title: Life-Cycle Assessment of an Injection-Moulded Polymer Automotive Bracket: From Granulate to End of Life
SYN-PUB-09249.text:
Life-Cycle Assessment of an Injection-Moulded Polymer Automotive Bracket: From Granulate to End of Life (2019, journal, Journal of Cleaner Production and Industrial Ecology).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Zoran Horvat (outside co-author); Katharina Brenner (outside co-author); Srđan Nikolić (outside co-author).
Keywords: LCA; injection moulding; automotive; polyamide; end of life; PEFCR.
This study presents a cradle-to-grave LCA of a glass-fibre-reinforced polyamide bracket used in passenger vehicle underbody applications, manufactured by a Tier 2 supplier in the Vojvodina automotive cluster. The functional unit is one bracket with a 200 000-cycle mechanical durability specification. Life-cycle stages covered include polymer granulate production, compounding, injection moulding, assembly, vehicle use-phase weight contribution, and end-of-life shredder processing. Primary data were collected during a three-month factory audit; use-phase modelling applied EUCAR fuel consumption methodology scaled to a 150 000 km vehicle lifetime. The use phase dominated the global warming potential at 58% of the total, driven by vehicle weight contribution. Material production accounted for 29%. Substituting 30% of virgin PA66 with post-industrial recyclate reduced cradle-to-gate GWP by 11% with no change in use-phase performance. Sensitivity to end-of-life recycling credit allocation was examined. The study is consistent with the methodology of the PEFCR for high-performance plastics, facilitating future benchmarking.

SYN-PUB-09250.title: Scope 3 Emission Estimation for a Metal Furniture Manufacturer: Purchased Goods and Freight Contribution
SYN-PUB-09250.text:
Scope 3 Emission Estimation for a Metal Furniture Manufacturer: Purchased Goods and Freight Contribution (2021, journal, Sustainable Production and Consumption Letters).
Authors: Jovana Račić (outside co-author); Péter Varga (outside co-author); Milan Sabo (R0859).
Keywords: Scope 3; GHG accounting; value chain emissions; metal furniture; purchased goods.
Scope 3 categories remain the least reported part of organisational GHG inventories in Serbian manufacturing, partly due to data availability constraints. This paper documents a Scope 3 Category 1 (purchased goods and services) and Category 4 (upstream transportation) assessment for a metal office furniture manufacturer with annual revenues of approximately €12 million and 130 employees. Spend-based and activity-based hybrid methods were compared. For steel sheet and tube—which constitute 71% of material spend—supplier-specific carbon intensity data were obtainable from two of seven suppliers; the remaining five required industry-average ecoinvent factors. Freight data were reconstructed from transport management records covering 48 weeks. Results indicate that purchased goods alone contribute 4.1 times the Scope 1 and 2 combined emissions. The paper evaluates the uncertainty introduced by using spend-based proxies and proposes a tiered engagement strategy for supplier data collection that can be implemented without dedicated environmental staff.

SYN-PUB-09251.title: Dynamic LCA for Batch Chemical Milling: Accounting for Temporal Variation in Electricity Grid Carbon Intensity
SYN-PUB-09251.text:
Dynamic LCA for Batch Chemical Milling: Accounting for Temporal Variation in Electricity Grid Carbon Intensity (2022, journal, Journal of Industrial Ecology and Engineering).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Nataša Vuković (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: dynamic LCA; time-differentiated emission factors; electricity grid; chemical milling; ISO 14067.
Standard attributional LCA uses annual-average grid emission factors, which can misrepresent the actual carbon intensity of energy-intensive industrial processes whose operation is concentrated in particular hours or seasons. This study applies an hourly time-differentiated electricity emission factor to a batch chemical milling process at an aerospace subcontractor in Serbia, using publicly available half-hourly grid dispatch data from ACER and EMS Serbia for a full calendar year. The chemical milling process runs in three-hour cycles and can be partially time-shifted within a ±6-hour window. Replacing the annual-average grid factor with hourly factors changed the Scope 2 emission estimate by between −18% and +23% depending on the day and shift. Time-shifting production cycles toward high-renewable-penetration hours reduced the annual electricity-related GHG figure by 9.4% with no capital investment. The paper discusses the implications for product carbon footprint declarations under ISO 14067 and for contractual reporting to aerospace OEM customers requiring hourly matching of renewable electricity.

SYN-PUB-09252.title: Environmental Benchmarking of Wire Harness Assembly: A Multi-Site Study Across Three Balkan Countries
SYN-PUB-09252.text:
Environmental Benchmarking of Wire Harness Assembly: A Multi-Site Study Across Three Balkan Countries (2024, journal, International Journal of Sustainable Manufacturing).
Authors: Milan Sabo (R0859); Aleksandar Tomić (outside co-author); Emina Hadžimuratović (outside co-author); Stefan Risteski (outside co-author).
Keywords: wire harness; benchmarking; automotive supply chain; multi-site LCA; Western Balkans.
Wire harness assembly is a labour-intensive but not energy-trivial process found extensively in the automotive supply chain across the Western Balkans. This paper presents a comparative LCA and energy-intensity benchmarking study of wire harness assembly at six production sites located in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, all supplying the same OEM platform. The functional unit is one complete harness set for a B-segment passenger car. Inventory data were collected through standardised audit protocols developed jointly with the OEM sustainability team. Electricity consumption per harness set ranged from 3.8 to 7.1 kWh across sites, with the largest single driver being building HVAC per unit of floor area. Material waste ratios for wire and connector housings varied between 2.1% and 5.6%. The study identifies equipment maintenance scheduling and building thermal performance as the two highest-leverage intervention points. Cross-site variability in secondary packaging material was also quantified. The OEM used results to set supplier-specific carbon reduction targets for 2025.

SYN-PUB-09253.title: Carbon Footprint Reporting Under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: Implications for Serbian Steel Product Exporters
SYN-PUB-09253.text:
Carbon Footprint Reporting Under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: Implications for Serbian Steel Product Exporters (2025, journal, European Journal of Environmental and Industrial Policy).
Authors: Jovana Račić (outside co-author); Milan Sabo (R0859); Dragan Ćosić (outside co-author).
Keywords: CBAM; carbon border adjustment; steel exports; ISO 14067; Serbia; GHG reporting.
The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), entering its transitional phase in October 2023, requires non-EU exporters of covered products—including iron, steel, and aluminium goods—to report embedded carbon emissions using EU-equivalent methodologies. This paper examines the preparedness of Serbian steel product exporters, based on structured interviews with 22 companies and a document review of their current GHG reporting practices. Seventeen of 22 companies had no existing product-level carbon footprint data. The gap between current reporting and CBAM methodology requirements is analysed, including differences in system boundary definition, emission factor sources, and verification requirements. A roadmap is proposed for companies to transition from no reporting to CBAM-compliant disclosure within 18 months using existing ISO 14067 infrastructure. Cost estimates for data collection and third-party verification are provided based on quotes obtained from three accredited verification bodies active in Serbia. Policy recommendations address the role of the Serbian Environmental Protection Agency in providing default emission factors.

SYN-PUB-09629.title: A sub-threshold OTA topology for ECG front-ends in 180 nm CMOS with 320 nA supply current
SYN-PUB-09629.text:
A sub-threshold OTA topology for ECG front-ends in 180 nm CMOS with 320 nA supply current (2013, journal, Serbian Journal of Electrical Engineering).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: sub-threshold OTA; ECG front-end; biopotential amplifier; CMOS 180 nm; low-power analogue.
This paper describes an operational transconductance amplifier designed to operate entirely in the sub-threshold region for use in single-lead ECG acquisition systems. The circuit was implemented in a 180 nm standard CMOS process. Biasing was set to achieve a quiescent current of 320 nA from a 1.2 V supply while maintaining an input-referred noise of 42 nV/√Hz at 100 Hz, sufficient for R-wave detection. The common-mode rejection ratio measured 78 dB across 20 fabricated dies. Electrode offset cancellation was addressed with a pseudo-resistor network whose impedance exceeded 10 GΩ at dc. Bandwidth could be digitally trimmed between 0.5 Hz and 150 Hz using a 3-bit switched-capacitor load. Measured results from twelve prototype boards equipped with dry Ag/AgCl electrodes showed SNR of 51 dB for a resting adult subject. Power consumption of the complete analogue chain, including a first-order high-pass filter, was 890 nW. The design occupies 0.041 mm² of active silicon area.

SYN-PUB-09630.title: Characterisation of packet collision statistics in IEEE 802.15.4 networks under periodic biomedical traffic patterns
SYN-PUB-09630.text:
Characterisation of packet collision statistics in IEEE 802.15.4 networks under periodic biomedical traffic patterns (2015, conference, Proceedings of the 22nd Telecommunications Forum TELFOR, Belgrade).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEEE 802.15.4; body-area network; CSMA/CA; packet delivery ratio; biomedical traffic.
