Biomedical body-area networks impose deterministic, quasi-periodic traffic from multiple sensor nodes sampling at fixed physiological rates such as 250 Hz for EMG or 500 Hz for EEG. Standard CSMA/CA back-off procedures in IEEE 802.15.4 were evaluated through a combination of analytical modelling using a two-dimensional Markov chain and hardware experiments with fifteen custom nodes based on a CC2520 transceiver. Traffic was generated to emulate simultaneous ECG at 250 samples/s, SpO2 at 50 samples/s, and skin temperature at 1 sample/s. Packet delivery ratio dropped from 98.7% with a single node to 83.2% with six co-located nodes at the default back-off exponent settings. Adjusting the minimum back-off exponent from 3 to 5 and reducing the maximum number of back-offs from 5 to 3 recovered delivery ratio to 96.1% for six nodes, at the cost of a mean latency increase of 4.1 ms. The paper provides a lookup table of recommended parameter combinations for clinically relevant node counts.

SYN-PUB-09632.title: Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes
SYN-PUB-09632.text:
Duty-cycled MAC scheduling with deadline-aware slot allocation for implantable sensor nodes (2018, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author).
Keywords: MAC scheduling; deadline-aware; duty cycling; implantable sensor; IEEE 802.15.4.
This work, developed as part of the author's doctoral research, proposes a beacon-enabled superframe structure derived from IEEE 802.15.4 in which guaranteed time slots are assigned according to each sensor stream's sampling deadline rather than priority class alone. The scheduler runs on a body hub modelled as a 32-bit ARM Cortex-M3 at 4 MHz and accepts registration messages carrying a sampling period, payload size, and maximum tolerable latency for each node. A first-fit decreasing bin-packing heuristic assigns contiguous slots within each superframe. Simulation across 10,000 randomly generated workloads with 2–8 nodes showed that deadline miss rates remained below 0.3% for workloads at up to 80% superframe utilisation. Radio duty cycle for a six-node ECG plus EMG scenario was reduced to 1.8% compared with 6.4% under a fixed-slot baseline, yielding a projected 3.5-fold increase in node battery lifetime. The protocol was prototyped on a Cortex-M0 hub with four slave nodes and validated against simulated data.

SYN-PUB-09633.title: Low-power multi-electrode bioimpedance spectroscopy front-end for wearable fluid monitoring
SYN-PUB-09633.text:
Low-power multi-electrode bioimpedance spectroscopy front-end for wearable fluid monitoring (2019, journal, Sensors and Actuators A: Physical Circuits and Systems).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Jelena Marković (outside co-author); Tobias Weigand (outside co-author).
Keywords: bioimpedance spectroscopy; Howland current source; lock-in amplification; wearable; oedema.
Bioimpedance spectroscopy between 1 kHz and 1 MHz can track extracellular fluid shifts relevant to oedema management in heart failure patients. This paper describes a four-electrode analogue front-end implemented in discrete components on a flexible PCB targeting wrist-worn use. A current source based on a Howland pump injected 50 µA peak sinusoidal current; the driving waveform was generated by a DDS peripheral on a low-power ARM microcontroller. Voltage was sensed by an instrumentation amplifier with a gain-bandwidth product of 10 MHz and an input impedance exceeding 100 MΩ. Phase and magnitude were extracted by a hardware lock-in approach sampling at 50 kSa/s and performing 16-point coherent averaging on the microcontroller. Average system current consumption was 1.4 mA during a 200 ms measurement burst and 3.8 µA in sleep. Accuracy of extracted resistance and reactance was within 1.2% of values measured with a laboratory impedance analyser across a 30-sample tissue-equivalent phantom set covering the physiological range of 20–800 Ω.

SYN-PUB-09634.title: Retransmission strategies for reliable ECG streaming over Bluetooth Low Energy in clinical environments with co-channel interference
SYN-PUB-09634.text:
Retransmission strategies for reliable ECG streaming over Bluetooth Low Energy in clinical environments with co-channel interference (2022, conference, Wireless Communications in Healthcare — Proceedings of the 4th Balkan Biomedical Engineering Symposium).
Authors: Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Filip Mijatović (R0905); Marija Đurić (outside co-author).
Keywords: Bluetooth Low Energy; ECG streaming; ARQ retransmission; co-channel interference; clinical environment.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-09635.title: Energy harvesting from body heat for wearable ECG patches: thermoelectric generator characterisation and power management circuit
SYN-PUB-09635.text:
Energy harvesting from body heat for wearable ECG patches: thermoelectric generator characterisation and power management circuit (2023, journal, Journal of Power Sources Electronics).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Radovan Ilić (outside co-author).
Keywords: thermoelectric harvesting; wearable ECG; boost converter; MPPT; body heat.
Wearable ECG patches worn continuously on the thorax can harvest energy from the skin-to-air temperature gradient, which typically spans 3–8 K in indoor environments. This work characterises six commercial thermoelectric generator (TEG) modules with active areas of 10–40 mm² under a simulated skin load using a temperature-controlled copper plate and forced convection at 0.5 m/s. Open-circuit voltages ranged from 18 mV to 74 mV at a 5 K gradient. A boost converter based on the BQ25504 integrated circuit with an impedance-matching network achieved maximum power point tracking efficiency of 82% across the characterised voltage range. Harvested power delivered to a 4.7 µF storage capacitor reached 48 µW at 5 K gradient for the 30 mm² module. A duty-cycle controller using a comparator and a timer allowed the ECG front-end described in a previous paper to operate from the harvested supply alone when the gradient exceeded 4.2 K, as verified over 48-hour benchtop trials. Implications for electrode placement and garment integration are discussed.

SYN-PUB-09636.title: Compressed sensing reconstruction for sparse EEG signals acquired by sub-mW wireless nodes: a comparison of three recovery algorithms
SYN-PUB-09636.text:
Compressed sensing reconstruction for sparse EEG signals acquired by sub-mW wireless nodes: a comparison of three recovery algorithms (2025, journal, Biomedical Signal Processing and Circuits).
Authors: Filip Mijatović (R0905); Stefan Horvat (outside co-author); Milena Savić (outside co-author); Paweł Nowak (outside co-author).
Keywords: compressed sensing; EEG; sparse recovery; OMP; BPDN; wireless BAN.
EEG signals exhibit sparsity in the wavelet domain; compressed sensing (CS) can therefore reduce the number of samples transmitted over a wireless link, cutting radio energy. This paper evaluates three recovery algorithms — basis pursuit denoising (BPDN), orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), and iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) — applied to EEG segments recorded from eight healthy subjects performing an eyes-open resting task. Compression ratios of 2×, 4×, and 8× were tested by randomly sub-sampling a 256 Hz, 16-channel stream at the sensor node simulated in MATLAB. At a 4× ratio, BPDN achieved a mean per-channel SNR of 28.3 dB, OMP 24.7 dB, and IRLS 27.9 dB. Clinical-grade feature detection for alpha-band power (8–13 Hz) was preserved with less than 5% relative error for BPDN and IRLS at 4× but degraded sharply at 8×. Transmission energy savings estimated from a Cortex-M0 radio model were 61% at 4× compression after accounting for the reconstruction overhead run on the hub.

SYN-PUB-09637.title: A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS
SYN-PUB-09637.text:
A 0.6 V, 210 nW instrumentation amplifier with reconfigurable gain for multi-modal biopotential acquisition in 65 nm CMOS (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers).
Authors: Milena Savić (outside co-author); Filip Mijatović (R0905); Christoph Brandner (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author).
Keywords: instrumentation amplifier; CCIA; 65 nm CMOS; biopotential; sub-volt supply; reconfigurable gain.
This paper presents a capacitively-coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) fabricated in a 65 nm low-power CMOS process and intended to serve both ECG (gain 40 dB, bandwidth 0.5–150 Hz) and EEG (gain 52 dB, bandwidth 0.5–80 Hz) acquisition modes selectable at run time via a 1-bit digital input. Supply voltage is 0.6 V drawn from an energy-harvesting rail. Total quiescent current across both amplifier stages is 350 nA. Input-referred noise integrated over the ECG band is 0.41 µVrms, and over the EEG band is 0.37 µVrms. The mid-band CMRR measured 91 dB for ECG mode and 88 dB for EEG mode. Electrode offset rejection was verified with offsets up to ±300 mV applied via a dc servo loop consuming 18 nA. The circuit was characterised on 20 dies; gain spread across dies was ±0.4 dB. Post-layout simulations and measured data are compared and show less than 6% discrepancy in noise and 3% in bandwidth.

SYN-PUB-09638.title: Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering
SYN-PUB-09638.text:
Cutting false atrial fibrillation alarms in patch ECG with motion-aware filtering (2024, journal, Journal of Biomedical Signal Analysis).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Luka Horvat (outside co-author).
Patch-based ECG monitors are increasingly deployed for continuous ambulatory cardiac surveillance, yet their clinical utility is severely limited by high false-positive rates for atrial fibrillation (AF) alarms, largely attributable to motion artifacts. This paper presents a motion-aware filtering framework that fuses single-lead ECG signals with three-axis accelerometer data recorded simultaneously by the same wearable patch. The proposed method employs an adaptive notch filter whose coefficients are dynamically updated according to a motion-intensity index derived from accelerometer magnitude. A subsequent AF detector based on RR-interval irregularity metrics is applied to the cleaned signal. The system was evaluated on a dataset of 312 twenty-four-hour recordings collected from 89 volunteers performing standardized daily activities including walking, stair climbing, and cycling. Compared with a baseline detector operating on raw ECG, the proposed approach reduced false AF alarms by 61% while maintaining sensitivity above 94% on confirmed AF episodes verified by a board-certified cardiologist. Processing latency was benchmarked on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, confirming real-time feasibility. The results demonstrate that tightly coupled motion-aware signal conditioning is essential for trustworthy AF screening in free-living conditions.

SYN-PUB-09639.title: Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller
SYN-PUB-09639.text:
Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller (2022, conference, Conference on Medical Devices Engineering).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906); Tijana Marković (outside co-author).
Arrhythmia classification in wearable cardiac monitors demands algorithms compact enough to execute entirely on the sensor node, eliminating reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. This paper describes the design and validation of a single-lead ECG arrhythmia classifier implemented on a low-power 32-bit microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M0+, 48 MHz, 32 kB RAM). The classifier distinguishes five rhythm classes—normal sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation, premature ventricular contractions, supraventricular tachycardia, and noise—using a lightweight feature set comprising RR-interval statistics, QRS morphology descriptors, and a three-stage decision-tree ensemble. Memory-efficient quantization reduces all floating-point parameters to 8-bit fixed-point representations without measurable accuracy loss. Evaluated on a held-out split of 4,200 annotated 30-second segments, the on-device model achieved a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.87 and consumed an average of 1.4 mW during inference, enabling operation for more than 72 hours on a 180 mAh coin cell. The work demonstrates a practical pathway toward fully autonomous, battery-powered cardiac monitors suitable for remote patient monitoring in resource-limited settings.

SYN-PUB-09640.title: Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers
SYN-PUB-09640.text:
Activity recognition from chest-worn accelerometers (2021, journal, Wearable Sensing Review).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Ana Stevanović (outside co-author); Miloš Radović (outside co-author).
Accurate activity recognition from chest-worn inertial measurement units is a prerequisite for context-aware physiological monitoring, yet most published benchmarks rely on wrist or hip placements. This study investigates the suitability of a single chest-mounted accelerometer for recognizing twelve daily-life activities including rest, walking, jogging, stair ascent and descent, cycling, and six sedentary postures. Features extracted in the time and frequency domains from three-axis acceleration signals were used to train and compare a k-nearest neighbor classifier, a random forest, and a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel. Data were collected from 45 healthy adults across a structured protocol lasting approximately 90 minutes per participant. The random forest achieved the highest overall accuracy of 92.3% in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. A confusion analysis revealed that the chest location provides particularly strong discrimination between static postures, outperforming wrist placement on that sub-task. The findings support the integration of chest-worn accelerometers into ECG patch monitors for simultaneous cardiac and activity monitoring without additional sensor hardware.

SYN-PUB-09641.title: Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults
SYN-PUB-09641.text:
Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults (2023, journal, Data in Biomedical Engineering (Open Access Journal)).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Petra Kovač (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark dataset; patch ECG; accelerometry; atrial fibrillation; motion artifact; open data.
High-quality annotated datasets pairing ambulatory ECG recordings with synchronised inertial data from the same wearable patch remain scarce, hampering reproducible research on motion-artifact suppression and context-aware cardiac monitoring. This paper describes the NovaSAD-PatchECG dataset: 128 recordings of 48 hours each, collected from 64 healthy volunteers and 64 patients with known arrhythmia history. Each recording includes single-lead ECG sampled at 500 Hz, three-axis accelerometer data at 100 Hz, and ground-truth rhythm annotations produced by two independent cardiologists with inter-annotator agreement reported via Cohen's kappa. Participants performed a standardized protocol encompassing controlled laboratory activities and unrestricted daily life. The dataset captures a diverse range of motion intensities, electrode contact qualities, and arrhythmia types. Baseline performance figures for three published AF detectors are reported to facilitate fair future comparisons. The dataset is released under an open-access licence and accompanied by Python-based loading utilities. We anticipate that this resource will accelerate development and fair benchmarking of wearable cardiac monitoring algorithms, particularly those addressing false-alarm reduction and real-time on-device inference.

SYN-PUB-09642.title: Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices
SYN-PUB-09642.text:
Federated learning for atrial fibrillation detection across heterogeneous wearable ECG devices (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906); Radovan Bešlin (outside co-author); Elena Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: federated learning; atrial fibrillation; ECG; wearable; privacy-preserving; domain adaptation.
Training robust atrial fibrillation detectors on data pooled from multiple clinical sites raises significant patient privacy concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative by training shared model parameters without centralizing raw recordings. This work presents a federated AF detection framework tailored to the heterogeneous signal characteristics encountered when aggregating data from four distinct wearable ECG patch platforms with differing sampling rates, electrode configurations, and noise profiles. A domain-adaptive normalization layer is inserted before each local model head to compensate for device-specific distributional shifts. Communication efficiency is improved through gradient sparsification with a threshold calibrated per round. Experiments conducted on data partitioned across five simulated client nodes demonstrate that the federated model achieves within 2.1 percentage points of a centrally trained oracle in terms of F1 score for AF detection, while keeping raw data entirely local. Convergence analysis shows stable training within 35 communication rounds. The proposed approach is directly applicable to collaborative model development between hospitals and medical device manufacturers operating under strict data governance constraints.

SYN-PUB-09643.title: Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches
SYN-PUB-09643.text:
Energy-efficient QRS detection on ultra-low-power microcontrollers for long-term cardiac patches (2022, journal, Biomedical Microdevices and Embedded Systems Journal).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Marko Tešić (outside co-author).
Keywords: QRS detection; ultra-low-power; microcontroller; wearable ECG; integer arithmetic; cardiac patch.
Battery life is the dominant constraint for wearable cardiac patches intended for multi-week arrhythmia screening. This paper presents an ultra-low-power QRS detection algorithm specifically designed for deployment on a 16-bit microcontroller operating at 8 MHz with 4 kB of available SRAM. The algorithm adapts the classical Pan–Tompkins pipeline by replacing floating-point operations with integer arithmetic and replacing the bandpass filter with a computationally cheaper differentiator-squarer cascade whose coefficients are pre-quantized to powers of two, enabling shift-based multiplication. Threshold adaptation is reformulated as a recursive integer update requiring no division. The implementation is benchmarked on five publicly available ECG databases totalling over 120,000 annotated beats, achieving a detection sensitivity of 99.1% and positive predictivity of 98.9%. On the target microcontroller, the algorithm consumes 87 μW at 500 Hz input, extending projected patch lifetime from 9 to 21 days compared with a floating-point baseline at equivalent sampling rate. The source code is released openly to support reproducibility and adoption in resource-constrained medical device development.

SYN-PUB-09644.title: Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions
SYN-PUB-09644.text:
Combining heart rate variability and accelerometer features for stress detection in free-living conditions (2023, conference, Sensors and Wearable Systems Conference).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Ana Stevanović (outside co-author); Katarina Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: stress detection; heart rate variability; accelerometer; wearable; free-living; multimodal.
Continuous stress monitoring in everyday life has attracted growing interest as a tool for preventive mental health management, yet most validated methods require laboratory-controlled conditions. This paper investigates a multimodal approach that fuses heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from a chest-worn ECG patch with accelerometer-based activity features to infer subjective stress levels in free-living adults. Thirty-six participants wore the sensor system continuously for five days while self-reporting stress events via a smartphone application. A total of 41 time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features were extracted over non-overlapping five-minute windows and combined with six activity context features capturing posture and movement intensity. A random forest classifier trained with leave-one-day-out cross-validation achieved a binary stress/non-stress accuracy of 76.4%, improving by 8.3 percentage points over HRV-only baselines. Analysis of feature importance revealed that low-frequency HRV power and accelerometer-derived posture class were the two most discriminative predictors. The study highlights that activity context is an important confound in wearable stress detection and should be accounted for in algorithm design.

SYN-PUB-09645.title: Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study
SYN-PUB-09645.text:
Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study (2021, journal, Biomedical Signal Processing and Control).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Milena Vujović (outside co-author).
Keywords: signal quality assessment; wearable ECG; single-lead; arrhythmia detection; survey; embedded systems.
Reliable automatic interpretation of single-lead wearable ECG recordings is contingent upon accurate signal quality assessment (SQA), yet no consensus exists on the best methodology for this task. This survey reviews 38 SQA algorithms published between 2010 and 2022, categorizing them by feature type (statistical, spectral, template-based, and learned), classification strategy, and target application domain. We implement and comparatively evaluate nine representative approaches on two independent ECG datasets collected with chest-worn patches under both controlled and free-living conditions. Evaluation metrics include per-segment quality classification accuracy, computational cost on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, and downstream impact on AF detector performance when SQA-based segment rejection is applied as a pre-processing gate. Results show that lightweight spectral flatness combined with kurtosis achieves the best accuracy-to-cost trade-off for real-time embedded use, while deep-learning approaches yield superior accuracy at much higher computational expense. The survey concludes with a discussion of open challenges including cross-device generalization and labelling inconsistencies across public datasets.

SYN-PUB-09646.title: Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation
SYN-PUB-09646.text:
Wearable biomedical systems: signal acquisition, processing and clinical translation (2023, book chapter, Advances in Wearable Health Technology (Springer)).
Authors: Maja Popović (R0906); Dragan Ilić (outside co-author); Petra Kovač (outside co-author); Sonja Vukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: wearable systems; biomedical signal processing; ECG; clinical translation; medical device regulation; embedded algorithms.
This book chapter provides a comprehensive overview of the engineering challenges involved in translating wearable biomedical sensing systems from laboratory prototypes to clinically validated devices. The chapter covers the full signal chain from electrode–skin interface physics and analog front-end design through digital signal processing pipelines to clinical validation methodology. Particular attention is paid to the interplay between hardware constraints—power budget, memory, communication bandwidth—and algorithm design choices for cardiac and motion signals. The ECG acquisition and arrhythmia detection pipeline is used as a running example throughout, illustrating how design decisions at each layer propagate to end-to-end system performance. A dedicated section addresses regulatory considerations under the European Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745) relevant to software-as-a-medical-device classification of on-device diagnostic algorithms. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for future research directions including personalized adaptive algorithms, multi-sensor fusion, and privacy-preserving distributed learning. It is intended as a graduate-level reference for students and practitioners entering the field of wearable medical technology.

SYN-PUB-09647.title: Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring
SYN-PUB-09647.text:
Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring (2020, conference, International Conference on Biomedical Signal and Image Processing).
Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Radovan Bešlin (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906).
Keywords: adaptive thresholds; arrhythmia detection; personalization; atrial fibrillation; wearable ECG; Bayesian update.
Fixed detection thresholds in ambulatory arrhythmia monitors fail to account for inter-individual variability in cardiac electrophysiology and body habitus, leading to systematically elevated false-positive rates in certain patient subgroups. This paper proposes a patient-adaptive threshold framework for wearable ECG arrhythmia detectors in which detection parameters are continuously updated using an online Bayesian update rule applied to a rolling window of high-confidence rhythm annotations from the preceding monitoring period. The method requires no pre-training on patient-specific data and is therefore directly applicable from the first hour of monitoring. Computational overhead is bounded to allow deployment alongside an existing QRS detector on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The framework is evaluated on long-term recordings from 58 patients with documented paroxysmal AF. Compared with fixed-threshold detectors, the adaptive approach reduces the per-patient median false-alarm rate by 47% while maintaining sensitivity above 91% across all subgroups stratified by age, sex, and body mass index. The results support patient-adaptive personalization as a practical and computationally tractable strategy for improving specificity in clinical-grade wearable cardiac monitors.

SYN-PUB-09754.title: Adhesion strength of PVD TiAlN coatings on cemented carbide substrates with varying surface roughness preparation
SYN-PUB-09754.text:
Adhesion strength of PVD TiAlN coatings on cemented carbide substrates with varying surface roughness preparation (2012, journal, Surface and Coating Technology Letters).
Authors: Predrag Janković (outside co-author); Svetlana Kopač (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: TiAlN; PVD adhesion; scratch test; Rockwell indentation; substrate roughness.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-09755.title: Crater wear characterisation of TiAlN-coated carbide inserts in turning of AISI 4340 hardened steel
SYN-PUB-09755.text:
Crater wear characterisation of TiAlN-coated carbide inserts in turning of AISI 4340 hardened steel (2013, journal, Tribology International).
Authors: Nebojša Radović (outside co-author); Ivan Kovačević (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: crater wear; TiAlN; hardened steel; FIB-TEM; tribolayer.
Crater wear on the rake face of TiAlN-coated WC-Co inserts was characterised during turning of AISI 4340 steel hardened to 52 HRC, at cutting speeds 120 and 160 m/min, feed 0.10 mm/rev, depth 0.5 mm, under strictly dry conditions. Crater depth and area were measured at intervals of 200 m by confocal laser scanning microscopy. At 160 m/min, crater depth reached 12 µm after 800 m, while at 120 m/min the same depth was not exceeded before 1400 m. Cross-sectional TEM foils prepared by FIB from the crater floor revealed a 40–80 nm amorphous tribolayer enriched in Fe and O. Raman spectroscopy identified alumina clusters in the tribolayer, suggesting partial oxidative transformation of the TiAlN coating. Abrasive wear dominated the crater floor, with diffusion wear becoming significant above 160 m/min. The data support a transition from predominantly mechanical to thermally assisted wear between 140 and 160 m/min for this coating–workpiece combination.

SYN-PUB-09756.title: Comparative study of TiAlN and TiSiN PVD coatings on cemented carbide in high-speed dry turning of compacted graphite iron
SYN-PUB-09756.text:
Comparative study of TiAlN and TiSiN PVD coatings on cemented carbide in high-speed dry turning of compacted graphite iron (2015, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Andrej Perović (outside co-author); Krzysztof Czyżewski (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: TiSiN; TiAlN; compacted graphite iron; high-speed turning; oxidative wear.
TiAlN and TiSiN coatings, each deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering to 3.2 µm thickness on identical WC-10%Co substrates, were evaluated when turning compacted graphite iron (CGI, 4 vol% graphite nodularity) at 250, 320 and 400 m/min, feed 0.20 mm/rev, depth 1.0 mm. Flank wear was monitored at 200 m intervals; tests ended at VB = 0.35 mm or 2000 m. TiSiN-coated inserts outlasted TiAlN by 22 % at 320 m/min and 31 % at 400 m/min, while differences were within measurement uncertainty at 250 m/min. EDS line scans across worn flanks showed higher oxygen content in TiAlN wear scars, consistent with faster oxidative wear. Nanoindentation hardness of TiSiN was 38 GPa versus 31 GPa for TiAlN before testing. Surface temperature was estimated from secondary electron contrast variation following a calibrated emissivity approach. The study identifies TiSiN as the preferred coating for CGI turning above 300 m/min.

SYN-PUB-09758.title: Pin-on-disc tribological screening of CrAlN and TiAlN PVD coatings against hardened steel counterfaces at elevated temperature
SYN-PUB-09758.text:
Pin-on-disc tribological screening of CrAlN and TiAlN PVD coatings against hardened steel counterfaces at elevated temperature (2017, journal, Tribology Transactions).
Authors: Miroslav Plančak (outside co-author); Tamara Vukić (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: CrAlN; TiAlN; pin-on-disc; elevated temperature; tribo-oxide.
CrAlN and TiAlN coatings deposited by cathodic arc PVD on cemented carbide discs were tested against AISI D2 steel pins (62 HRC) in a pin-on-disc tribometer at temperatures of 25, 200, 400 and 600 °C, normal load 10 N, sliding speed 0.2 m/s, total sliding distance 2000 m. Coefficient of friction (COF) and specific wear rate were recorded continuously. At 25 °C, mean COF was 0.52 for CrAlN and 0.49 for TiAlN with comparable wear rates (~4 × 10⁻⁶ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹). At 600 °C, TiAlN wear rate increased fourfold while CrAlN remained within a factor of 1.8 of room-temperature values. Cr₂O₃ tribo-oxide formation, confirmed by XPS, was identified as the protective mechanism for CrAlN at 600 °C. These findings support the selection of CrAlN for turning operations where high sustained interface temperatures are expected.

SYN-PUB-09759.title: Acoustic emission signatures associated with coating delamination events during turning of hardened bearing steel
SYN-PUB-09759.text:
Acoustic emission signatures associated with coating delamination events during turning of hardened bearing steel (2018, journal, Journal of Manufacturing Processes).
Authors: Ákos Horvát (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Petar Vranić (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: acoustic emission; coating delamination; in-process monitoring; bearing steel; TiAlN.
An acoustic emission (AE) sensor was mounted directly on the tool holder during external turning of 100Cr6 bearing steel (60 HRC) with TiAlN-coated carbide inserts at 140 m/min, feed 0.08 mm/rev, depth 0.3 mm. Continuous AE root-mean-square voltage and frequency spectrum were logged at 1 MHz sampling. Eleven individual tests were run to pre-defined cumulative cutting distances; inserts were then examined by SEM. Bursts in the 100–200 kHz band with amplitudes exceeding 2.5 times the background level were correlated with delamination patches of ≥ 0.02 mm² identified in post-test SEM images with 87 % precision and 79 % recall. False positives were predominantly caused by chip jamming events. A simple threshold-based detection criterion is proposed and validated on a hold-out set of six additional tests. The approach allows in-process discrimination between progressive abrasive wear and catastrophic delamination without additional instrumentation beyond a standard AE sensor.

SYN-PUB-09760.title: Influence of WC grain size in substrate on wear resistance of TiAlN-coated inserts in dry turning of nodular cast iron
SYN-PUB-09760.text:
Influence of WC grain size in substrate on wear resistance of TiAlN-coated inserts in dry turning of nodular cast iron (2019, journal, International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials).
Authors: Andrej Perović (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: WC grain size; substrate; TiAlN; nodular cast iron; notch wear.
Three grades of cemented carbide substrate—fine grain (0.6 µm WC), medium grain (1.2 µm) and coarse grain (3.0 µm), all with 10 wt% Co—were coated with TiAlN by magnetron sputtering and tested in dry turning of nodular cast iron (Grade 500, 170 HB) at 220 m/min, feed 0.18 mm/rev, depth 1.5 mm. Flank and notch wear were measured every 400 m until VB = 0.3 mm. Fine-grain substrates yielded 40 % longer tool life than coarse-grain at this condition, attributed to reduced substrate pull-out that exposes coating edges. Notch wear at depth-of-cut boundaries was 28 % lower on fine-grain substrates. Hardness of fine-grain carbide was 1720 HV10 versus 1540 HV10 for coarse-grain. Fracture toughness KIc estimated by Palmqvist method was 8.4 MPa√m for fine and 11.6 MPa√m for coarse, indicating the expected toughness–hardness trade-off. The paper provides quantitative guidance for substrate grade selection in cast iron turning at moderate speeds.

SYN-PUB-09761.title: Tool life modelling for CrAlN-coated inserts in high-speed dry turning using a modified Taylor equation
SYN-PUB-09761.text:
Tool life modelling for CrAlN-coated inserts in high-speed dry turning using a modified Taylor equation (2021, journal, CIRP Journal of Manufacturing Science and Technology).
Authors: Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920); Gordana Zorić (R1041); Ákos Horvát (outside co-author).
Keywords: Taylor tool life; CrAlN; dry turning; tool life model; hardened steel.
Tool life data for CrAlN-coated WC-Co inserts turning AISI 4340 steel (48 HRC) were collected at six cutting speeds (120–320 m/min) and three feed rates (0.08, 0.12 and 0.16 mm/rev), depth fixed at 0.5 mm, in strictly dry conditions. VB = 0.3 mm was used as the failure criterion. Ninety-six complete tool life tests were conducted with three replicates per condition. A modified Taylor equation incorporating feed rate as a secondary variable was fitted by nonlinear least squares; the exponents were n = 0.31 and m = 0.48 for speed and feed, respectively, with standard errors below 5 %. A validation set of 12 tests at intermediate conditions gave mean absolute percentage error of 9.2 %. The model was also compared against a response surface regression (second-order); both achieved similar predictive accuracy, but the Taylor-based form offers better extrapolation behaviour outside the experimental range.

SYN-PUB-09762.title: Wear mechanisms in multilayer TiAlN/TiN PVD coatings on carbide inserts: effect of bilayer period on performance in turning of austempered ductile iron
SYN-PUB-09762.text:
Wear mechanisms in multilayer TiAlN/TiN PVD coatings on carbide inserts: effect of bilayer period on performance in turning of austempered ductile iron (2022, journal, Wear).
Authors: Krzysztof Czyżewski (outside co-author); Petar Vranić (outside co-author); Miroslav Plančak (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: multilayer coating; TiAlN/TiN; bilayer period; ADI; crack propagation.
Multilayer TiAlN/TiN coatings with three bilayer periods—8 nm, 20 nm and 60 nm—were deposited by cathodic arc PVD on WC-6%Co inserts. Total coating thickness was maintained at 3.5 µm for all architectures. Turning of austempered ductile iron (ADI, Grade 800, 280 HB) was carried out at 180 m/min, feed 0.14 mm/rev, depth 1.2 mm, in dry conditions. Flank wear, notch wear and cutting force components (Fc, Ff, Fp) were monitored at 300 m intervals. Inserts with the 20 nm period showed 19 % lower flank wear rate than the 8 nm period and 34 % lower than the 60 nm period at 900 m cumulative distance. Nanoindentation hardness was highest for the 8 nm period (42 GPa) but this did not translate to the best wear performance. SEM of worn flanks revealed that the 20 nm architecture delayed crack propagation across interfaces more effectively. Cutting forces were within 8 % across all three architectures throughout testing.

SYN-PUB-09763.title: PVD coatings for cemented carbide cutting tools: deposition methods, wear mechanisms and characterisation techniques
SYN-PUB-09763.text:
PVD coatings for cemented carbide cutting tools: deposition methods, wear mechanisms and characterisation techniques (2023, book chapter, Advanced Tool Materials for Machining (Edited Volume, Springer Nature)).
Authors: Andrej Perović (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: PVD coatings; cutting tools; wear mechanisms; characterisation; review.
This chapter provides a systematic review of physical vapour deposition methods applied to cemented carbide cutting tool inserts, with emphasis on cathodic arc evaporation and magnetron sputtering. Deposition parameters, resulting coating microstructures, and typical mechanical property ranges (hardness, elastic modulus, residual stress) are tabulated for the TiN, TiAlN, TiSiN, CrAlN and AlCrN coating families. Wear mechanisms encountered during dry turning—abrasion, adhesion, oxidation, diffusion, and delamination—are described and linked to specific coating properties. Characterisation methods covered include XRD phase analysis and residual stress measurement, nanoindentation, scratch and Rockwell adhesion tests, SEM/EDS and TEM analysis of wear surfaces, and acoustic emission monitoring. Case studies from the author's laboratory data illustrate selected topics. The chapter is intended for postgraduate students and engineers selecting coatings for high-speed dry turning applications.

SYN-PUB-09764.title: Thermomechanical wear modelling of PVD-coated inserts combining finite element heat flux estimation with empirical wear rate data
SYN-PUB-09764.text:
Thermomechanical wear modelling of PVD-coated inserts combining finite element heat flux estimation with empirical wear rate data (2025, journal, International Journal of Machine Tools and Manufacture).
Authors: Petar Vranić (outside co-author); Dragan Milošević (outside co-author); Ákos Horvát (outside co-author); Roberto Sannino (outside co-author); Filip Urošević (R0920).
Keywords: thermomechanical model; FEM; PVD coating; wear prediction; dry turning.
A combined modelling approach for predicting wear of PVD-coated cemented carbide inserts in dry turning is presented. A 2D finite element thermal model of the tool–chip interface was used to estimate heat flux and temperature distribution on the rake and flank faces for AISI 4340 (48 HRC) turning at 120–280 m/min, feed 0.10 mm/rev, depth 0.5 mm. Boundary conditions were set using experimentally measured cutting forces from a three-component dynamometer. Interface temperature estimates were validated against thermocouple measurements embedded 0.5 mm below the cutting edge (mean error 7 %). Wear rate coefficients for TiAlN and CrAlN coatings were calibrated from 24 turning tests. The coupled model predicted flank wear at 600 m cutting distance with a mean absolute error of 0.021 mm across 18 validation conditions, compared with 0.035 mm for a purely empirical Taylor-type model. The approach reduces the number of calibration experiments required for a new coating–workpiece combination by approximately 40 %.

SYN-PUB-09804.title: A transformer model pre-trained on Serbian web text
SYN-PUB-09804.text:
A transformer model pre-trained on Serbian web text (2024, conference, Workshop on Slavic Language Technology).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author); Katarina Horvat (outside co-author).
This paper presents SrbBERT-Web, a transformer language model pre-trained from scratch on a large-scale crawl of Serbian web text comprising approximately 14 billion tokens. We describe the data collection and cleaning pipeline, which addresses noise specific to Serbian web content, including mixed-script documents, informal spelling variations, and code-switched passages. The model adopts a RoBERTa-style architecture and is trained with dynamic masking on deduplicated data. We evaluate SrbBERT-Web on four downstream tasks: named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, morphological tagging, and extractive question answering, comparing it against multilingual baselines such as mBERT and XLM-R, as well as against smaller domain-specific Serbian models. SrbBERT-Web consistently outperforms all baselines on three of the four tasks, with especially pronounced gains on question answering and sentiment analysis. We release the model weights, tokenizer, and pre-training corpus metadata under open licenses to support further research on Serbian language technology. We also provide a detailed analysis of tokenization efficiency, showing that a vocabulary trained specifically on Serbian text significantly reduces token-per-word ratios compared to multilingual vocabularies.

SYN-PUB-09805.title: Dense retrieval for Serbian customer-support questions
SYN-PUB-09805.text:
Dense retrieval for Serbian customer-support questions (2023, journal, Journal of Language Engineering).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Luka Đorđević (outside co-author).
This paper investigates dense passage retrieval (DPR) for Serbian customer-support question answering. Customer-support interactions in Serbian present unique challenges: queries are short and colloquial, answers are embedded in lengthy policy documents, and the corpus contains both Latin and Cyrillic script. We construct a new benchmark dataset, SrbCSQA, containing 4,200 question–passage pairs collected from publicly available support portals and annotated by native speakers. We fine-tune a bi-encoder retrieval model initialised from a Serbian transformer checkpoint and compare it against BM25, a multilingual DPR baseline, and a cross-encoder re-ranker. Experiments show that our fine-tuned bi-encoder achieves a mean reciprocal rank of 0.73, outperforming BM25 by 18 percentage points and the multilingual baseline by 11 points. We further study the effect of script normalisation as a preprocessing step and show that it consistently improves retrieval quality. Error analysis reveals that lexical gaps between formal policy language and informal user queries remain the primary failure mode. We release the SrbCSQA benchmark and fine-tuned model under open licenses.

SYN-PUB-09806.title: Handling Latin and Cyrillic script in one embedding space
SYN-PUB-09806.text:
Handling Latin and Cyrillic script in one embedding space (2022, conference, Conference on Computational Linguistics in the Balkans).
Authors: Ana Mirković (outside co-author); Bojan Savić (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925); Tijana Relić (outside co-author).
Texts in Serbian are written in both the Latin and Cyrillic scripts, often within the same corpus or even the same document. Existing multilingual embedding models treat these as largely separate character sequences, resulting in poor cross-script semantic alignment. This paper proposes a script-unified embedding approach that maps Latin-script and Cyrillic-script Serbian sentences to a shared vector space. We achieve this through a three-stage training procedure: (1) initialisation from a multilingual sentence encoder, (2) contrastive fine-tuning on automatically generated Latin–Cyrillic parallel pairs obtained by deterministic transliteration, and (3) hard-negative mining using nearest-neighbour retrieval. We evaluate semantic textual similarity and cross-script retrieval on newly constructed Serbian benchmarks and on a subset of the XSTS evaluation suite. Our model closes 84% of the cosine-similarity gap between same-script and cross-script sentence pairs while maintaining competitive performance on standard STS tasks. We release the model, training data, and evaluation scripts. The approach is lightweight, requiring no manual annotation of cross-script pairs, and can be extended to other language communities with dual-script traditions.

SYN-PUB-09807.title: SrbNER: a named entity recognition corpus and baseline models for Serbian
SYN-PUB-09807.text:
SrbNER: a named entity recognition corpus and baseline models for Serbian (2023, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation for South-East European Languages).
Authors: Jovana Ilić (outside co-author); Tijana Relić (outside co-author); Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: named entity recognition; Serbian NLP; annotation; transformer fine-tuning; sequence labelling.
Named entity recognition (NER) is a foundational NLP task, yet Serbian has lacked a large, openly licensed NER corpus with consistent annotation guidelines. This paper introduces SrbNER, a corpus of 120,000 tokens drawn from news, social media, and administrative text, manually annotated with seven entity categories: person, organisation, location, event, product, law, and date. We describe the annotation scheme, adjudication process, and inter-annotator agreement, which reached a Cohen's kappa of 0.87. We train and evaluate several baseline models: a CRF tagger with hand-crafted features, a BiLSTM-CRF model, and three transformer-based sequence labellers fine-tuned from mBERT, XLM-R, and SrbBERT-Web respectively. The transformer baselines substantially outperform the CRF and BiLSTM approaches, with SrbBERT-Web achieving an F1 of 89.4 on the test set. We analyse per-category performance and find that product and law entities are the most difficult, largely due to inconsistent surface forms and low frequency in the training data. SrbNER and all baseline model weights are released publicly to accelerate Serbian NLP research.

SYN-PUB-09808.title: Extractive question answering for Serbian: dataset construction and model evaluation
SYN-PUB-09808.text:
Extractive question answering for Serbian: dataset construction and model evaluation (2024, conference, ACL Findings).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author); Marta Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: question answering; extractive QA; Serbian NLP; span extraction; dataset construction.
We present SrbQA-Ext, the first large-scale extractive question answering dataset for Serbian, containing 11,400 question–answer pairs grounded in Wikipedia-derived passages. Questions were elicited from native-speaker annotators who read a passage and formulated answerable questions; each answer is a contiguous span within the passage. We additionally include 1,200 unanswerable questions to test model abstention. The dataset covers eight topic domains and is balanced across Latin and Cyrillic script versions to prevent script-specific overfitting. We establish baselines using mBERT, XLM-R-large, and our in-house SrbBERT-Web model fine-tuned with the standard span-extraction objective. SrbBERT-Web achieves an exact match of 62.1 and an F1 of 78.4 on the development set, surpassing XLM-R-large by 3.2 F1 points despite having fewer parameters. We analyse common error types, showing that multi-sentence reasoning and numerical inference are the leading sources of error. We also conduct a cross-lingual transfer experiment in which models trained on translated SQuAD data are compared against our natively constructed dataset, demonstrating the importance of domain-appropriate, language-native training data. All resources are publicly available.

SYN-PUB-09809.title: Cross-lingual transfer learning for low-resource South Slavic languages using shared subword vocabularies
SYN-PUB-09809.text:
Cross-lingual transfer learning for low-resource South Slavic languages using shared subword vocabularies (2022, journal, Transactions on Slavic Language Processing).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Ana Mirković (outside co-author); Bojan Savić (outside co-author); Irena Pejović (outside co-author).
Keywords: cross-lingual transfer; South Slavic languages; subword vocabulary; low-resource NLP; multilingual models.
Transfer learning from high-resource to low-resource languages has shown strong results when languages share linguistic or orthographic properties. South Slavic languages — Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Slovenian, and Macedonian — form a cluster with shared grammatical structures and partially overlapping vocabulary, making them ideal candidates for cross-lingual transfer. In this paper we examine the effect of vocabulary design on transfer performance. Specifically, we train three transformer models with different tokenisation strategies: a vocabulary trained on Serbian only, a joint vocabulary trained on all five South Slavic languages, and the multilingual SentencePiece vocabulary of XLM-R. We evaluate downstream performance on NER, part-of-speech tagging, and dependency parsing for each language using the same fine-tuning budget. Results show that the joint South Slavic vocabulary reduces out-of-vocabulary rates by 31% on average and improves NER F1 by up to 4.7 points for Macedonian compared with the Serbian-only vocabulary. We release the joint vocabulary and pre-trained model checkpoints under an open license and provide a detailed analysis of vocabulary overlap across the five languages.

SYN-PUB-09810.title: Retrieval-augmented generation for Serbian: adapting RAG pipelines to a morphologically rich language
SYN-PUB-09810.text:
Retrieval-augmented generation for Serbian: adapting RAG pipelines to a morphologically rich language (2024, conference, EMNLP 2024 Workshop on Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP).
Authors: Luka Đorđević (outside co-author); Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: retrieval-augmented generation; Serbian NLP; morphological richness; dense retrieval; generative models.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a retrieval component with a generative language model to produce factual, grounded responses. Most RAG research targets English, where morphological simplicity makes keyword and dense retrieval effective. Serbian, as a morphologically rich language with six grammatical cases and free word order, poses distinctive challenges: inflected query terms may not match base forms in the index, and sentence boundary detection is complicated by enclitic clitics. This paper adapts a full RAG pipeline to Serbian by integrating our dense retrieval model with a multilingual generative model fine-tuned on Serbian instruction data. We introduce lemma-expanded dense retrieval, in which query embeddings are averaged over all inflected forms of content words as predicted by a morphological analyser. On the SrbCSQA benchmark, this approach improves ROUGE-L by 6.1 points over a vanilla bi-encoder retrieval baseline and reduces hallucination rate as measured by automatic factual consistency scoring. We also release a small test set of 400 long-form generation examples with human-annotated factuality labels to support future evaluation of Serbian generative NLP systems.

SYN-PUB-09811.title: Sentence embeddings for Serbian: benchmark construction and model comparison
SYN-PUB-09811.text:
Sentence embeddings for Serbian: benchmark construction and model comparison (2023, journal, Journal of Language Engineering).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Katarina Horvat (outside co-author); Ana Mirković (outside co-author); Vladislav Knežević (outside co-author).
Keywords: sentence embeddings; semantic textual similarity; Serbian NLP; contrastive learning; benchmark.
High-quality sentence embeddings are a prerequisite for semantic search, clustering, and question answering in any language. For Serbian, no systematic sentence-embedding benchmark has previously existed, leaving practitioners without a reliable way to compare models. This paper makes three contributions. First, we construct SrbSTS-22, a semantic textual similarity benchmark of 3,500 sentence pairs drawn from news headlines, online reviews, and conversational transcripts, scored by five native-speaker annotators on a 0–5 scale. Second, we adapt the NLI-based contrastive training paradigm to Serbian by automatically translating MultiNLI and SNLI into Serbian and fine-tuning sentence encoders from multiple base checkpoints. Third, we perform a systematic comparison of twelve sentence encoder variants—covering multilingual off-the-shelf models, cross-lingual knowledge distillation, and our natively trained models—on SrbSTS-22 and cross-script retrieval tasks. Our best model, fine-tuned from SrbBERT-Web using NLI pre-training followed by STS fine-tuning, achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.88 on SrbSTS-22. We release the benchmark, trained models, and evaluation toolkit.

SYN-PUB-09812.title: Morphology-aware tokenisation strategies for Serbian transformer models
SYN-PUB-09812.text:
Morphology-aware tokenisation strategies for Serbian transformer models (2021, conference, Proceedings of the Workshop on Computational Morphology for Under-Resourced Languages).
Authors: Milan Petrović (R0925); Tijana Relić (outside co-author); Dragan Vasiljević (outside co-author).
Keywords: tokenisation; morphology; Serbian NLP; subword segmentation; transformer pre-training.
Standard subword tokenisation algorithms such as BPE and WordPiece are optimised for frequent character sequences but are agnostic to morphological structure. For a highly inflected language like Serbian, this can lead to segmentations that split across morpheme boundaries in linguistically arbitrary ways, potentially harming model generalisation across inflectional paradigms. This paper systematically evaluates five tokenisation strategies for Serbian: standard BPE, Unigram language model tokenisation, morpheme-boundary-aware BPE initialised with morphological analyses, syllable-based tokenisation, and character-level tokenisation. For each strategy we pre-train a small transformer model with identical hyperparameters and evaluate on NER, POS tagging, and STS tasks. We find that morpheme-boundary-aware BPE reduces the average number of split morphemes by 28% and yields consistent downstream gains on NER (+1.9 F1) and POS tagging (+0.8 accuracy) compared with standard BPE, while remaining computationally competitive. Syllable-based tokenisation performs competitively on STS but lags on structured prediction tasks. We provide guidance for practitioners choosing tokenisation strategies for morphologically rich Slavic languages.

SYN-PUB-09813.title: Zero-shot intent detection for Serbian chatbots using multilingual sentence encoders
SYN-PUB-09813.text:
Zero-shot intent detection for Serbian chatbots using multilingual sentence encoders (2022, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Spoken Language Processing and Dialogue Systems).
Authors: Stefan Novaković (outside co-author); Nevena Stanković (outside co-author); Radoslav Pejić (outside co-author); Milan Petrović (R0925).
Keywords: intent detection; zero-shot learning; chatbot; Serbian NLP; sentence encoders.
Intent detection is a core component of task-oriented dialogue systems. Deploying such systems for Serbian is hampered by the scarcity of labelled intent data; collecting annotated examples for every new domain is expensive and slow. This paper explores zero-shot intent detection, in which a model trained on seen intents in one or more high-resource languages is applied directly to Serbian without any Serbian-language training examples. We frame intent detection as nearest-neighbour classification in an embedding space and compare five multilingual sentence encoders, including our SrbBERT-Web-based sentence model, on a new Serbian intent detection benchmark covering four domains: banking, travel, e-commerce, and healthcare. Our Serbian sentence encoder, despite never seeing intent labels during training, achieves an accuracy of 71.3% in a zero-shot setting, outperforming the best general multilingual encoder by 8.4 points. We further show that adding as few as ten Serbian examples per intent in a few-shot extension pushes accuracy to 84.1%. We release the benchmark and all experimental code to support research on conversational Serbian NLP.

SYN-PUB-09851.title: Contrastive Learning of Audio Description Embeddings Using Weak Supervision from Listener Behaviour
SYN-PUB-09851.text:
Contrastive Learning of Audio Description Embeddings Using Weak Supervision from Listener Behaviour (2024, journal, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Information Systems).
Authors: Jana Zahorecová (R0931); Dragan Horvat (outside co-author); Lukas Obermaier (outside co-author); Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Aleksandra Tomić (outside co-author).
Keywords: contrastive learning; weak supervision; listener behaviour; audio embeddings; recommendation.
We propose a contrastive training objective for learning audio description embeddings that incorporates weak supervision signals derived from listener co-engagement patterns — specifically, pairs of audio items listened to in the same session by the same user. A dataset of 4.2 million session records from a fictional regional streaming platform was provided under a data processing agreement. Positive pairs are defined by co-occurrence within a session window of ten consecutive plays; negatives are sampled from across the catalogue. The resulting embeddings are evaluated on three downstream tasks: genre classification, mood tagging, and nearest-neighbour retrieval as judged by human assessors. On retrieval, the contrastive model achieves NDCG@10 = 0.74, exceeding a supervised sentence-transformer baseline by 3.1 points. Ablation studies confirm that session-derived weak supervision contributes meaningfully beyond text-only training, particularly for instrumental and ambient content where descriptive text is sparse.

SYN-PUB-10238.title: Dynamic Race Detection at Runtime for Embedded Systems Using Shadow Memory with Fixed Overhead
SYN-PUB-10238.text:
Dynamic Race Detection at Runtime for Embedded Systems Using Shadow Memory with Fixed Overhead (2016, conference, ACM Sigplan Workshop on Languages, Compilers, and Tools for Embedded Systems (LCTES Companion)).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Ivan Rajković (outside co-author); Vukica Ognjanov (R0979).
Keywords: dynamic analysis; shadow memory; race detection; runtime overhead; microcontroller.
Dynamic data-race detectors based on shadow memory, such as those following the ThreadSanitizer design, impose memory overhead proportional to the monitored address space. On microcontrollers with 8–256 kB of RAM this overhead is generally unacceptable. This paper proposes a fixed-overhead shadow-memory scheme that maintains race-detection state only for a configurable set of shared variables explicitly declared by the developer, reducing RAM overhead to a user-tuned constant. A prototype is implemented as a set of C macros and a lightweight runtime library occupying 1.4 kB of flash and 48 bytes of RAM. The approach is evaluated in simulation using QEMU emulating an STM32F4 target. On 14 benchmark programs containing injected races the tool detected 11 of 14 injected races at runtime with no false positives during a two-hour test run per program. The paper discusses the trade-off between coverage and overhead, and compares coverage against two static tools on the same benchmarks.

SYN-PUB-10239.title: Lightweight Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained ICS Gateways: A Quantisation and Pruning Study
SYN-PUB-10239.text:
Lightweight Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained ICS Gateways: A Quantisation and Pruning Study (2025, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Industrial Automation and Security (ECIAS)).
Authors: Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Dávid Szabó (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Andrea Jovanović (R0983); Vukica Ognjanov (R0979).
Keywords: model compression; quantisation; pruning; embedded deployment; autoencoder.
Many ICS sites route traffic through ARM-based gateways with 256 MB RAM and single-core processors. This paper evaluates the effect of weight quantisation (32-bit to 8-bit and 4-bit floating point) and structured pruning (removing 10%, 25%, 50% of autoencoder units) on detection performance and inference latency for traffic-based anomaly detectors. Experiments used three autoencoder architectures differing in depth (2, 4, 6 hidden layers) trained on Modbus/TCP and DNP3 captures. 8-bit quantisation reduced model size by 3.7× and inference time by 2.1× with an average AUROC reduction of 0.012. 4-bit quantisation introduced a 0.041 AUROC drop. Structured pruning at 25% improved inference speed by 1.4× with negligible performance loss; at 50%, AUROC declined by 0.028. A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target, fitting within a 10 ms cycle budget, making real-time deployment feasible without dedicated hardware accelerators.

SYN-PUB-10346.title: Thermal decomposition kinetics of sunflower husk under nitrogen atmosphere: a non-isothermal TGA study
SYN-PUB-10346.text:
Thermal decomposition kinetics of sunflower husk under nitrogen atmosphere: a non-isothermal TGA study (2011, journal, Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry of South-East Europe).
Authors: Mirjana Stojković (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Aleksandar Petrović (outside co-author).
Keywords: sunflower husk; TGA; isoconversional methods; pyrolysis kinetics; activation energy.
Sunflower husks sampled from three processing sites in Vojvodina were subjected to non-isothermal thermogravimetric analysis at heating rates of 5, 10, 20, and 40 K min⁻¹ under nitrogen flow (50 mL min⁻¹). Three isoconversional methods—Ozawa–Flynn–Wall, Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose, and Friedman—were applied to conversion degrees from 0.1 to 0.9. Apparent activation energies ranged from 148 to 213 kJ mol⁻¹ across the conversion range, with a pronounced compensation effect observed between 0.4 and 0.6. The three-stage decomposition profile (hemicellulose, cellulose, lignin) was deconvoluted using Fraser–Suzuki peak fitting, yielding individual component contributions consistent with proximate analysis data. Kinetic triplets were determined and compared across sites; moisture and ash content influenced the pre-exponential factor but not activation energy substantially. The results provide a baseline kinetic dataset for process modelling of sunflower residue pyrolysis reactors in the region.

SYN-PUB-10348.title: Distributed activation energy model applied to co-pyrolysis of wheat straw and lignite from the Kovin deposit
SYN-PUB-10348.text:
Distributed activation energy model applied to co-pyrolysis of wheat straw and lignite from the Kovin deposit (2016, journal, Fuel Processing Technology).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Slobodan Đurić (outside co-author); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author).
Keywords: DAEM; co-pyrolysis; wheat straw; lignite; synergistic effects.
The distributed activation energy model (DAEM) was fitted to TGA data for wheat straw, Kovin lignite, and three blending ratios (25:75, 50:50, 75:25 straw:lignite by mass) at heating rates of 10 and 20 K min⁻¹. For pure wheat straw, the Gaussian activation energy distribution yielded a mean of 204 kJ mol⁻¹ with a standard deviation of 21 kJ mol⁻¹. Lignite exhibited a broader distribution (mean 231 kJ mol⁻¹, σ = 34 kJ mol⁻¹). Blending produced negative synergistic deviations from linearly interpolated values in the 350–450 °C range, interpreted as catalytic effects of inorganic matter in the lignite ash on cellulose decomposition. The model reproduced experimental mass loss curves with root-mean-square errors below 0.8% for all cases. Interactions between alkali metals in biomass ash and the organic matrix of lignite are proposed as the primary interaction mechanism.

SYN-PUB-10349.title: Characterisation of biochars from Vojvodina agricultural residues against European Biochar Certificate criteria
SYN-PUB-10349.text:
Characterisation of biochars from Vojvodina agricultural residues against European Biochar Certificate criteria (2018, journal, Agronomy and Soil Science Reports).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Tamara Horvat (outside co-author); Ivana Rađenović (outside co-author); Lukas Brandt (outside co-author).
Keywords: biochar certification; EBC; PAH; heavy metals; Vojvodina.
Six biochar samples were produced from sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover at 500 and 650 °C using identical slow pyrolysis conditions and subjected to full physicochemical characterisation aligned with European Biochar Certificate (EBC) version 9 criteria. Analyses included elemental composition (C, H, N, S, O), BET surface area, pore size distribution (Barrett–Joyner–Halenda method), pH and electrical conductivity in water extract, plant-available phosphorus, cation exchange capacity, and 16 EPA priority PAH congeners by GC-MS. All samples produced at 650 °C met EBC Basic grade for stable carbon (minimum 50% Corg). PAH totals ranged from 1.2 to 4.7 mg kg⁻¹ dry matter, below the EBC premium threshold of 6 mg kg⁻¹ for all samples. Heavy metal concentrations (Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb, Zn) remained well within limits. A scoring matrix comparing regional feedstocks is presented to guide commercial producers in Vojvodina.

SYN-PUB-10351.title: Influence of feedstock particle size on pyrolysis kinetics and biochar surface area: a systematic TGA and reactor study
SYN-PUB-10351.text:
Influence of feedstock particle size on pyrolysis kinetics and biochar surface area: a systematic TGA and reactor study (2020, journal, Chemical Engineering and Processing: Process Intensification).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Ivana Rađenović (outside co-author); Zoran Petković (outside co-author).
Keywords: particle size; heat transfer; TGA; BET surface area; effectiveness factor.
Wheat straw was milled and sieved to four particle size fractions: <0.25, 0.25–0.5, 0.5–1.0, and 1.0–2.0 mm. Non-isothermal TGA at 10 K min⁻¹ revealed that apparent activation energy (KAS method) varied from 192 to 218 kJ mol⁻¹ across size fractions, with the finest fraction exhibiting the highest values, attributed to reduced heat and mass transfer limitations revealing true chemical kinetics. Reactor experiments at 550 °C and 60 min residence time showed biochar yield differences of 2.1 percentage points between the smallest and largest fractions. BET surface area decreased from 210 to 143 m² g⁻¹ as particle size increased, linked to restricted volatile escape and re-condensation in larger particles blocking pores. A simple effectiveness factor model, adapted from heterogeneous catalysis, described the particle size–surface area relationship with R² = 0.94. Practical implications for biochar quality control in hammer-mill pre-processing are discussed.

SYN-PUB-10352.title: Biochar amendment effects on sandy loam soils of Vojvodina: a two-season pot experiment with maize
SYN-PUB-10352.text:
Biochar amendment effects on sandy loam soils of Vojvodina: a two-season pot experiment with maize (2021, journal, Soil Use and Management).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Tamara Horvat (outside co-author); Jelena Krstić (outside co-author); Lukas Brandt (outside co-author).
Keywords: biochar amendment; sandy loam; maize; soil water retention; pot experiment.
This study bridges thermochemical production of biochar with its agronomic performance. Wheat straw biochars produced at 450 and 600 °C (characterised in prior work by the same group) were applied to sandy loam soil collected from the Bačka region at rates of 0, 10, 20, and 40 t ha⁻¹ equivalent. A pot experiment over two growing seasons (2018 and 2019) used maize (cv. Zlatni Jubilar) as the test crop. Plant dry biomass increased by 12–18% at 20 t ha⁻¹ for the 600 °C char in the first season, but differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05, Tukey HSD) by the second season. Soil water retention improved significantly (p < 0.01) for all amended treatments. Soil pH rose by 0.3–0.8 units. Available phosphorus and potassium showed modest but consistent increases at higher application rates. The experiment underlines that production temperature affects agronomic response as strongly as application rate.

SYN-PUB-10353.title: Py-GC/MS fingerprinting of biochars from three Vojvodina lignocellulosic feedstocks at two carbonisation temperatures
SYN-PUB-10353.text:
Py-GC/MS fingerprinting of biochars from three Vojvodina lignocellulosic feedstocks at two carbonisation temperatures (2022, journal, Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Marko Cvejić (outside co-author); Andrea Fabbri (outside co-author).
Keywords: Py-GC/MS; biochar fingerprinting; recalcitrance; PAH; principal component analysis.
Analytical pyrolysis coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) at 500 °C was applied to biochars previously produced from sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover at 450 and 650 °C in a fixed-bed reactor. The objective was to identify residual volatile organic compounds indicative of incomplete carbonisation and to compare aromatic cluster formation as a function of feedstock and production temperature. Levoglucosan, furfural, and guaiacol derivatives were prominent in 450 °C chars and nearly absent in 650 °C samples, confirming greater thermal recalcitrance of the latter. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (fluorene, phenanthrene, pyrene) were detected in all 650 °C chars at concentrations consistent with EBC limits. A principal component analysis of 47 identified compounds separated samples primarily by production temperature (PC1, 61% variance) and secondarily by feedstock lignin/cellulose ratio (PC2, 19% variance). The dataset supports using Py-GC/MS as a rapid screening tool in biochar quality workflows.

SYN-PUB-10354.title: Torrefaction pre-treatment of sunflower husks: mass and energy yields, grindability and subsequent pyrolysis kinetics
SYN-PUB-10354.text:
Torrefaction pre-treatment of sunflower husks: mass and energy yields, grindability and subsequent pyrolysis kinetics (2023, journal, Bioresource Technology).
Authors: Ivana Rađenović (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Péter Balogh (outside co-author); Marko Cvejić (outside co-author).
Keywords: torrefaction; sunflower husk; grindability; energy densification; pyrolysis kinetics.
Sunflower husks were torrefied at 230, 260, and 290 °C for 30 minutes in a rotary tube furnace under nitrogen. Solid mass yields were 91.4, 82.7, and 71.3 wt% respectively. Energy densification ratios reached 1.08, 1.15, and 1.24. Grindability was assessed by measuring particle size distribution after standardised hammer milling; the Hardgrove Grindability Index analogue improved by 38% at 290 °C relative to raw husks. Non-isothermal TGA of torrefied samples at 10 K min⁻¹ showed that the hemicellulose decomposition shoulder (typically 250–320 °C) was suppressed proportionally to torrefaction severity. Apparent activation energy of the cellulose decomposition step increased from 198 kJ mol⁻¹ (raw) to 217 kJ mol⁻¹ (290 °C torrefied), attributed to reduced structural disorder and removal of easily decomposable fractions. A two-step torrefaction–pyrolysis process simulation using collected data predicted a 9% gain in biochar fixed-carbon content relative to single-step pyrolysis of raw husks.

SYN-PUB-10355.title: Raman spectroscopic assessment of structural order in biochars: correlation with BET surface area and agronomic stability index
SYN-PUB-10355.text:
Raman spectroscopic assessment of structural order in biochars: correlation with BET surface area and agronomic stability index (2025, journal, Carbon).
Authors: Andrea Fabbri (outside co-author); Milica Novaković (outside co-author); Đorđe Vukelić (R0992).
Keywords: Raman spectroscopy; biochar structure; ID/IG ratio; graphitic ordering; stability index.
Fifteen biochar samples spanning four feedstocks and production temperatures from 350 to 750 °C were characterised by Raman spectroscopy (532 nm excitation). The D and G band parameters (position, full width at half maximum, and integrated intensity ratio ID/IG) were extracted from curve-fitted spectra. ID/IG decreased from 1.41 ± 0.08 at 350 °C to 0.87 ± 0.06 at 750 °C, reflecting increasing graphitic ordering. A linear correlation (R² = 0.86) was found between ID/IG and the H/C molar ratio from ultimate analysis, supporting Raman spectroscopy as a rapid structural proxy. BET surface area showed a non-monotonic relationship with ID/IG, peaking at intermediate disorder corresponding to 550–600 °C chars. An agronomic stability index, defined as the ratio of recalcitrant carbon (R50 method) to total organic carbon, correlated moderately with Raman D-band FWHM (R² = 0.74). The dataset supports integration of Raman spectroscopy into biochar certification screening workflows to reduce reliance on lengthy carbon stability incubation tests.

SYN-PUB-10356.title: Temperature–residence-time response surface for biochar yield, fixed carbon and BET surface area: a central composite design study with corn stover
SYN-PUB-10356.text:
Temperature–residence-time response surface for biochar yield, fixed carbon and BET surface area: a central composite design study with corn stover (2026, journal, Industrial Crops and Products).
Authors: Đorđe Vukelić (R0992); Marko Cvejić (outside co-author); Dragana Vasić (outside co-author).
Keywords: response surface methodology; central composite design; biochar optimisation; fixed carbon; BET surface area.
A central composite design with two factors—pyrolysis temperature (450–700 °C) and residence time (20–120 min)—was applied to fixed-bed slow pyrolysis of corn stover in a nitrogen atmosphere to map responses including biochar yield, fixed carbon content, volatile matter, BET surface area, and pH. Thirteen experimental runs (including five centre points) were executed. Response surface models were fitted using least-squares regression; lack-of-fit tests confirmed adequacy for all five responses (p > 0.1). Temperature was the dominant factor for all responses; residence time showed significant interaction with temperature for BET surface area (p = 0.023) and volatile matter (p = 0.041). Optimal conditions maximising a composite desirability function combining high fixed carbon (≥60 wt%) and high BET surface area (≥180 m² g⁻¹) while maintaining biochar yield above 28% were identified at 615 °C and 75 min. The validated optimum was confirmed experimentally with deviations below 4% for all predicted values. Design-of-experiment data are provided as supplementary material.

SYN-PUB-10372.title: A Metamodel for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text: Design Rationale and Conformance Checking
SYN-PUB-10372.text:
A Metamodel for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text: Design Rationale and Conformance Checking (2015, journal, Journal of Systems and Control Engineering Research).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author).
Keywords: IEC 61131-3; Structured Text; metamodeling; Ecore; OCL; conformance checking.
IEC 61131-3 defines five programming languages for programmable logic controllers, yet no widely adopted formal metamodel exists for its Structured Text variant. This paper presents a metamodel covering the full grammar of Structured Text as defined in the third edition of the standard, implemented in Ecore within the Eclipse Modeling Framework. The metamodel comprises 47 metaclasses and 112 structural features. Conformance checking is realized through 34 OCL constraints covering type compatibility, scope resolution, and temporal execution order. The metamodel was validated against a corpus of 18 publicly available PLC project archives totalling approximately 120,000 lines of Structured Text, extracted from open automation repositories. Constraint violations found in the corpus are categorized by severity and related to common programming errors. The paper discusses design decisions around POUs, data types, and sequential function chart interoperability. The resulting artifact serves as a foundation for model-to-model and model-to-text transformation chains described in subsequent work.

SYN-PUB-10373.title: Mapping UML Class Diagrams to IEC 61131-3 Function Blocks via ATL Transformations
SYN-PUB-10373.text:
Mapping UML Class Diagrams to IEC 61131-3 Function Blocks via ATL Transformations (2017, conference, International Conference on Industrial Informatics and Automation (ICIIA)).
Authors: Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author); Katarzyna Wiśniewska (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995).
Keywords: UML; ATL; model transformation; function blocks; IEC 61131-3; code generation.
Function blocks in IEC 61131-3 exhibit structural similarity to classes in object-oriented formalisms, yet practitioners lack automated tooling to carry designs expressed in UML into executable PLC artifacts. This paper defines an ATL transformation that maps a restricted profile of UML class diagrams—covering classes, associations, aggregations, and a subset of stereotypes—to IEC 61131-3 Function Block Declaration bodies in Structured Text. The transformation handles inheritance by flattening class hierarchies into self-contained function block bodies, preserving interface semantics through input and output variable mappings. An evaluation was conducted on five industrial-style case studies ranging from conveyor-belt sequencing to batch-reactor control, each containing between 8 and 31 classes. Generated code was compiled and executed on Beckhoff CX5130 hardware. Cyclic execution times of generated programs stayed within 5% of manually written equivalents. The paper also reports on maintainability metrics comparing generated and hand-written code using McCabe complexity and comment density.

SYN-PUB-10374.title: Variability Modelling in PLC Software Families Using Feature Models and Configuration Constraints
SYN-PUB-10374.text:
Variability Modelling in PLC Software Families Using Feature Models and Configuration Constraints (2018, conference, European Workshop on Software Product Lines for Industrial Systems (EWSPLIS)).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Miroslav Đorđević (outside co-author).
