Keywords: software product lines; feature models; variability management; PLC; code generation; FeatureIDE.
Automation equipment manufacturers frequently produce families of machines that share a large fraction of control logic but differ in optional subsystems such as sensor types, drive configurations, or safety interlocks. Managing such variability through copy-paste code leads to maintenance burdens quantified here on a dataset of 14 PLC projects from a partner manufacturing firm. This paper proposes using FODA-style feature models, extended with numerical attributes for timing parameters, to represent the configuration space of a PLC software product line. A binding-time model distinguishes features configured at project generation time from those configured at runtime through parameter tables. A prototype implementation uses FeatureIDE for feature model editing and a Xtend-based generator to produce Structured Text artefacts for selected configurations. The approach was applied to a filling-machine product line with 23 optional features, yielding a single-source model from which 8 valid configurations were derived and verified against a test harness of 310 unit tests. Lines of code under manual maintenance were reduced by 61% compared to the previous fork-based approach.

SYN-PUB-10375.title: An Xtext Grammar and IDE Support for a Subset of IEC 61131-3 Structured Text
SYN-PUB-10375.text:
An Xtext Grammar and IDE Support for a Subset of IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (2019, journal, Journal of Automation Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: Xtext; IEC 61131-3; Structured Text; parser; IDE; domain-specific languages.
Development of domain-specific tools for PLC programming is hampered by the absence of reusable, open parser infrastructure. This paper describes an Xtext grammar covering approximately 92% of the Structured Text syntax defined in IEC 61131-3 third edition, excluding only deprecated GOTO constructs and certain vendor extensions. The grammar is accompanied by scope provider rules for cross-reference resolution across compilation units, a type-inference engine handling implicit numeric widening, and formatter and outline view implementations for Eclipse IDE integration. Error recovery strategies are documented, as PLC source files from industrial environments frequently contain partial programs during edit sessions. A user study involving 11 automation engineers from three companies measured error detection time for introduced syntax and type errors; the IDE reduced median detection time from 14.3 minutes to under 2 minutes compared to a plain text editor workflow. The tooling is released under an open-source license and has been adopted in three subsequent research projects at partner institutions.

SYN-PUB-10377.title: Integrating Safety Requirements into PLC Product-Line Models Using SysML Parametric Diagrams
SYN-PUB-10377.text:
Integrating Safety Requirements into PLC Product-Line Models Using SysML Parametric Diagrams (2021, conference, International Conference on Model-Driven Engineering and Industrial Automation (MDEIA)).
Authors: Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Stefano Cremonesi (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995).
Keywords: safety requirements; SysML; product lines; IEC 62061; traceability; PLC.
Safety-critical PLC applications require that timing and operational constraints derived from hazard analyses be traceable through to implementation. This paper proposes a model-based workflow in which SysML parametric diagrams capture quantitative safety constraints—maximum response times, watchdog periods, and safe-state transition conditions—derived from a HAZOP analysis artefact. A model-to-model transformation maps parametric constraint blocks to annotations on a feature model, and a subsequent model-to-text step embeds the constraints as pragma comments and runtime assertion code in generated Structured Text. The approach was demonstrated on a palletizer control application with 17 identified safety functions. All 17 functions produced traceable artefacts from HAZOP table rows to compiled PLC code. A traceability matrix was generated automatically and verified by a safety assessor against IEC 62061 SIL 2 requirements. The paper discusses limitations arising from the restricted expressiveness of IEC 61131-3 assertions and proposes extensions.

SYN-PUB-10378.title: DSL Design for Conveyor Routing Logic: A Case Study in Abstraction Level Calibration
SYN-PUB-10378.text:
DSL Design for Conveyor Routing Logic: A Case Study in Abstraction Level Calibration (2024, conference, European Conference on Software Language Engineering (ECSLE)).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Péter Szalai (outside co-author); Dragana Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: domain-specific languages; abstraction level; Xtext; conveyor control; user study; code generation.
Choosing the right abstraction level for a domain-specific language is a practical design problem with limited empirical guidance. This paper reports a case study in which three successive DSL versions were designed, implemented, and evaluated for expressing conveyor routing logic in a logistics automation context. The first version mirrored the structure of IEC 61131-3 function block networks closely; the second introduced a graph-based topology language with implicit signal routing; the third added a declarative routing-rule layer. Each version was implemented as an Xtext grammar with an Xtend code generator producing Structured Text. Evaluation involved six automation programmers who completed identical routing tasks under a think-aloud protocol. Task completion time, error rate, and post-task questionnaire scores were recorded. The graph-based version produced the lowest error rate at 0.8 errors per task; the declarative version had the shortest median task time at 11.4 minutes but required the longest learning period. The paper derives three abstraction-level heuristics for industrial DSL design.

SYN-PUB-10379.title: Towards Round-Trip Engineering for IEC 61131-3: Extracting Feature Models from Legacy PLC Codebases
SYN-PUB-10379.text:
Towards Round-Trip Engineering for IEC 61131-3: Extracting Feature Models from Legacy PLC Codebases (2025, journal, Journal of Systems and Software).
Authors: Ana Kovačević (outside co-author); Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Radu Constantin (outside co-author); Dragana Milić (outside co-author).
Keywords: round-trip engineering; feature extraction; clone detection; legacy code; PLC; product lines.
Many manufacturing firms operate legacy PLC codebases developed without explicit variability management. Migrating such code to a product-line architecture requires recovering implicit variation points from existing programs. This paper presents a semi-automated extraction approach that applies clone detection to a corpus of related PLC projects to identify recurring code patterns, clusters patterns by structural similarity using a tree-edit distance metric, and maps clusters to candidate features in a FODA feature model. The approach was applied to a set of 11 related projects from an anonymised food-processing equipment manufacturer totalling 84,000 lines of Structured Text. Extraction identified 38 candidate features, of which domain experts validated 29 as genuine variation points. Six features required manual refinement. The recovered feature model was used to derive a product-line architecture, and one configuration was re-generated and compared against the original project using cyclomatic complexity and test pass rate as metrics. Results indicate functional equivalence for the regenerated configuration on the existing test suite.

SYN-PUB-10380.title: A Benchmark Suite for PLC Code Generators: Construction, Metrics, and Baseline Results
SYN-PUB-10380.text:
A Benchmark Suite for PLC Code Generators: Construction, Metrics, and Baseline Results (2026, journal, Empirical Software Engineering).
Authors: Veljko Pantelić (R0995); Dragana Milić (outside co-author); Péter Szalai (outside co-author); Radu Constantin (outside co-author); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark; code generation; PLC; IEC 61131-3; empirical evaluation; hardware-in-the-loop.
Reproducible evaluation of PLC code generators is difficult because published studies use heterogeneous, proprietary case studies. This paper describes the construction of an open benchmark suite comprising 24 PLC control scenarios spanning motion control, process automation, and safety interlock domains. Each scenario is specified at three levels: a natural-language requirements document, a structured functional specification, and a reference implementation in Structured Text manually written by two authors independently and reconciled. Benchmark metrics include correctness (pass rate on a hardware-in-the-loop test harness using Wago PFC200 controllers), code size ratio to reference, cyclomatic complexity ratio, and compilation time. Baseline results are reported for three existing open-source code generators and for the authors' own generator. No generator achieves above 81% correctness across all scenarios; motion control scenarios prove most difficult. The benchmark suite and harness scripts are released under an open licence to enable comparative evaluation in future work.

SYN-PUB-10454.title: Predicting Course Dropout from Early Moodle Activity Logs Using Logistic Regression
SYN-PUB-10454.text:
Predicting Course Dropout from Early Moodle Activity Logs Using Logistic Regression (2013, journal, Journal of Educational Informatics).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Vesna Đorđević (outside co-author); Miroslav Stanić (outside co-author).
Keywords: dropout prediction; logistic regression; Moodle; clickstream; early warning.
This study examined whether student dropout in an introductory programming course could be predicted from the first three weeks of Moodle activity logs. Log data from 412 students enrolled over two academic years were used. Features included weekly login frequency, time-on-task estimates derived from session timestamps, and quiz attempt counts. A logistic regression model trained on weeks one to three achieved an AUC of 0.71 on a held-out semester cohort, outperforming a baseline model using only prior academic grades (AUC 0.58). Precision at a 30 % recall threshold was sufficient to support early adviser notification. The study also identified that late-evening access patterns in week two were among the strongest predictors of dropout, a finding discussed in relation to work-study conflicts common among part-time students at the faculty. Limitations regarding class imbalance and cross-course generalisability are addressed.

SYN-PUB-10455.title: Temporal Patterns in Student Engagement: A Sequence Clustering Approach
SYN-PUB-10455.text:
Temporal Patterns in Student Engagement: A Sequence Clustering Approach (2015, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Conference on Learning Technologies).
Authors: Aleksandra Kovač (outside co-author); Tibor Fehér (outside co-author); Danilo Mitrović (R1006).
Keywords: sequence clustering; student engagement; dynamic time warping; trajectory analysis; k-medoids.
Engagement patterns in online course materials were analysed using sequence clustering applied to week-level activity vectors from 1,840 students across six undergraduate courses. Each student's 14-week activity profile was encoded as a categorical sequence over four engagement states (high, moderate, low, absent) derived by discretising composite activity scores. Sequences were clustered using a k-medoids procedure with a dynamic time warping distance metric. Five robust clusters emerged, labelled by dominant trajectory shape: consistently active, late starters, early decliners, sporadic engagers, and persistently absent. Cluster membership at week four was a significant predictor of final examination grade in a subsequent multinomial regression (pseudo-R² = 0.34). The paper discusses how cluster assignments could feed into adaptive course notifications. Data were drawn from three consecutive academic years (2010–2013) at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.

SYN-PUB-10456.title: Applying Hidden Markov Models to Detect Shifts in Student Learning States from Clickstream Data
SYN-PUB-10456.text:
Applying Hidden Markov Models to Detect Shifts in Student Learning States from Clickstream Data (2017, journal, Journal of Learning Analytics Research).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Nataša Popović (outside co-author); Christoph Baumann (outside co-author).
Keywords: hidden Markov model; learning states; clickstream; Baum-Welch; engagement dynamics.
Hidden Markov models (HMMs) were fitted to weekly clickstream summaries of 620 students enrolled in a statistics course over one academic year, with the aim of identifying latent learning states and their transition dynamics. Observations consisted of five aggregated behavioural features per week: resource views, forum posts, quiz attempts, assignment submissions, and session duration. A three-state HMM, selected by BIC, was estimated using the Baum–Welch algorithm. The inferred states corresponded interpretably to disengaged, routine, and intensive study behaviours. Transition matrices indicated that recovery from the disengaged state became increasingly improbable after week seven. Students who spent more than four consecutive weeks in the disengaged state had a pass rate of 23 %, versus 81 % for those who did not. The paper examines model stability across two replication cohorts and discusses annotation validity through think-aloud interviews with a subsample of 18 students.

SYN-PUB-10457.title: Cross-Course Generalisation of Clickstream-Based Performance Predictors: An Empirical Evaluation
SYN-PUB-10457.text:
Cross-Course Generalisation of Clickstream-Based Performance Predictors: An Empirical Evaluation (2020, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Educational Data Mining).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Stefan Vuković (outside co-author); Ivana Petrović (outside co-author); Marc Delacroix (outside co-author).
Keywords: transfer learning; cross-course prediction; random forest; LSTM; model evaluation.
Most clickstream-based prediction models are trained and tested within a single course, leaving their cross-course generalisability unclear. This paper reports a systematic evaluation in which six predictive models (logistic regression, random forest, gradient-boosted trees, an LSTM, a naive Bayes baseline, and a rules-based expert model) were trained on data from one course and evaluated on 11 other courses at the Faculty of Sciences. Data covered 3,100 unique students and 14 courses over three academic years. AUC values dropped by an average of 0.11 when models were applied without retraining to new courses, but transfer performance recovered to within 0.04 of in-course performance after fine-tuning on as few as 50 labelled instances from the target course. Feature importance was markedly inconsistent across courses, with quiz-attempt features being the most portable. The paper provides recommendations for practitioners deploying predictive analytics in heterogeneous institutional contexts.

SYN-PUB-10458.title: Feature Importance Stability in Gradient-Boosted Models for Student Performance Prediction
SYN-PUB-10458.text:
Feature Importance Stability in Gradient-Boosted Models for Student Performance Prediction (2021, journal, Journal of Educational Informatics).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Nataša Popović (outside co-author).
Keywords: gradient boosting; feature importance; stability analysis; bootstrap; educational data mining.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-10459.title: Longitudinal Latent Profile Analysis of Learning Behaviours Across a Three-Year Study Programme
SYN-PUB-10459.text:
Longitudinal Latent Profile Analysis of Learning Behaviours Across a Three-Year Study Programme (2023, journal, Computers & Learning Research).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Bojana Marinković (outside co-author); Andrej Horváth (outside co-author); Christoph Baumann (outside co-author).
Keywords: latent profile analysis; longitudinal; study programme; learning behaviour; early warning system.
Most learning analytics studies examine single courses; this paper follows 890 students through an entire three-year bachelor's programme, applying longitudinal latent profile analysis (LLPA) to semester-aggregated behavioural indicators derived from Moodle logs. Six behavioural indicators per semester were used: mean weekly logins, resource coverage ratio, discussion board participation, assessment completion timeliness, peer review engagement, and estimated reading time. LLPA identified four latent profiles that were stable in composition but varied in prevalence across years. Profile membership at the end of year one predicted programme completion with an accuracy of 74 % (balanced accuracy 0.69). Transitions between profiles were more common at the boundary between year one and year two, coinciding with a curriculum redesign. The paper discusses implications for longitudinal early warning systems and presents an online Shiny dashboard prototype used to communicate risk scores to academic advisers.

SYN-PUB-10460.title: Modelling Competency Decay: Estimating Knowledge Retention Rates from Repeated Assessment Logs
SYN-PUB-10460.text:
Modelling Competency Decay: Estimating Knowledge Retention Rates from Repeated Assessment Logs (2024, journal, Journal of Learning Analytics Research).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Jelena Bosnić (outside co-author); Luca Ferrarini (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge retention; competency decay; exponential decay model; empirical Bayes; spaced practice.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-10461.title: Evaluating Fairness Properties of Clickstream-Based Grade Prediction Models Across Student Demographic Groups
SYN-PUB-10461.text:
Evaluating Fairness Properties of Clickstream-Based Grade Prediction Models Across Student Demographic Groups (2026, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Educational Data Mining).
Authors: Danilo Mitrović (R1006); Stefan Vuković (outside co-author); Milica Stanojević (outside co-author); Marta Czajkowska (outside co-author).
Keywords: algorithmic fairness; equalised odds; demographic parity; grade prediction; bias mitigation.
Predictive models in learning analytics risk encoding historical inequities if their accuracy varies systematically across demographic groups. This paper audits six previously published and three newly trained clickstream-based grade prediction models using a dataset of 5,600 students from two Serbian universities, with demographic variables including gender, whether the student is the first in their family to attend university, and regional origin. Equalised odds differences across gender exceeded 0.08 in four of nine models, driven primarily by differing patterns of after-hours access between groups rather than differential academic performance. First-generation students were identified as a higher-risk group by models at a rate 1.4 times that of continuing-generation students at the same actual grade distribution. Reweighting training instances by demographic group membership reduced equalised odds gaps to below 0.03 with less than 1 % loss in overall AUC. The paper calls for routine fairness reporting as part of learning analytics deployments.

SYN-PUB-10472.title: Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network
SYN-PUB-10472.text:
Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network (2010, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: Modbus/TCP; statistical baseline; Mahalanobis distance; substation automation; one-class detection.
This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed. For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation with a Gaussian kernel and bandwidth selected by cross-validation. A one-class detector based on Mahalanobis distance thresholding over a 20-feature vector was evaluated against 14 manually injected attack scenarios, including replay, coil-write injection, and scan sweeps. At a false positive rate of 0.5%, the detector achieved a true positive rate of 91.4% across all attack types. The paper also quantifies the effect of seasonal load variation on baseline drift and proposes a sliding-window recalibration schedule with a 72-hour update period that maintains detection performance without human intervention. Results are compared with a fixed-threshold rule-based baseline, which achieved 67% TPR at the same FPR. The testbed comprised three Siemens-compatible PLCs connected over a deterministic switched Ethernet fabric.

SYN-PUB-10473.title: One-Class SVM for Detecting Anomalous DNP3 Command Sequences in Water Treatment Control Systems
SYN-PUB-10473.text:
One-Class SVM for Detecting Anomalous DNP3 Command Sequences in Water Treatment Control Systems (2012, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Industrial Communication Security (CEWICS)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Ágnes Varga (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: DNP3; one-class SVM; SCADA; n-gram features; water treatment.
One-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) were applied to detect anomalous DNP3 application-layer command sequences in a water treatment SCADA testbed. Feature vectors were constructed from 15-second sliding windows using n-gram frequency histograms of function code and object group pairs, yielding 128-dimensional vectors after principal component analysis retaining 95% of variance. The OC-SVM used an RBF kernel; the nu hyperparameter was swept from 0.01 to 0.20 and selected via leave-one-out cross-validation on a 90-day normal-operation capture (approximately 4.2 million packets). Attack scenarios—unauthorised control block writes, time-sync spoofing, and application-layer flooding—were injected during a separate 14-day test period. The detector achieved an F1 score of 0.87 for unseen attack types not represented during training. Computational overhead was measured at under 3% CPU utilisation on an ARM Cortex-A9 industrial gateway, supporting inline deployment feasibility.

SYN-PUB-10474.title: Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study
SYN-PUB-10474.text:
Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study (2013, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: traffic characterisation; industrial Ethernet; long-range dependence; measurement study; Hurst parameter.
This measurement study presents a 12-month passive capture of traffic from four industrial sites—two discrete manufacturing lines, one water utility, and one district heating plant—totalling approximately 680 GB of raw packet data. The study characterises normal traffic behaviour through 22 statistical descriptors per flow, including coefficient of variation of inter-packet gaps, entropy of destination port distributions, and autocorrelation structure of payload-length time series. Results show that industrial Ethernet traffic exhibits strong periodicity at scales of seconds to hours, with Hurst parameter estimates between 0.61 and 0.79 across sites, indicating long-range dependence. The study documents characteristic differences between Modbus, EtherNet/IP, and proprietary vendor protocols and quantifies seasonal variation. The dataset and feature extraction code are described in sufficient detail to support reproducibility. Findings inform design choices for unsupervised detectors and highlight risks of training on short captures.

SYN-PUB-10475.title: Isolation Forest Applied to ICS Protocol Traffic: Sensitivity to Contamination Fraction and Window Length
SYN-PUB-10475.text:
Isolation Forest Applied to ICS Protocol Traffic: Sensitivity to Contamination Fraction and Window Length (2015, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: Isolation Forest; hyperparameter sensitivity; Modbus; contamination fraction; window length.
Isolation Forest was evaluated as a detector for ICS protocol traffic anomalies under controlled variation of two critical hyperparameters: the contamination fraction estimate (ranging from 0.001 to 0.10) and the sliding-window aggregation length (1 s to 300 s). Experiments used a publicly described Modbus/TCP dataset generated on the authors' testbed across five attack classes. Detection rate and false alarm rate were measured at each combination using a 5×2 nested cross-validation design. The contamination fraction had a stronger effect on precision than recall; a mismatch of one order of magnitude reduced average precision from 0.91 to 0.63. Window length affected recall for short-burst attacks more than for persistent anomalies. An empirical calibration procedure based on unlabelled holdout data is proposed and benchmarked. The paper provides a practical guide for practitioners deploying tree-based anomaly detectors in environments where ground-truth labels are unavailable.

SYN-PUB-10476.title: Autoencoder-Based Reconstruction Error for Anomaly Scoring in PROFINET IO Traffic
SYN-PUB-10476.text:
Autoencoder-Based Reconstruction Error for Anomaly Scoring in PROFINET IO Traffic (2016, conference, Proceedings of the European Conference on Industrial Automation and Security (ECIAS)).
Authors: Dávid Szabó (outside co-author); Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: autoencoder; PROFINET IO; reconstruction error; anomaly scoring; automotive.
A shallow fully-connected autoencoder with a 48-32-16-32-48 architecture was trained on PROFINET IO cyclic data exchange traffic captured from an automotive body-assembly line. The encoder compressed 48-dimensional per-cycle feature vectors—including cycle time jitter, alarm status byte distributions, and data record checksum statistics—into a 16-dimensional bottleneck. Reconstruction error was used as an anomaly score. The network was trained on 30 days of normal operation (approximately 2.1 million cycles) using stochastic gradient descent with batch size 256. Anomaly scoring was tested against seven fault conditions introduced by a cooperating maintenance team, including sensor dropout, network congestion injection, and controller firmware substitution. The autoencoder achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.94 across all fault types, compared with 0.81 for a PCA-based reconstruction baseline. Inference latency was 0.4 ms per cycle on a standard x86 edge server, compatible with 10 ms scan cycle requirements.

SYN-PUB-10477.title: Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems
SYN-PUB-10477.text:
Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems (2017, book chapter, Handbook of Industrial Cybersecurity (Edited volume, Springer-Verlag Academic)).
Authors: Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Goran Milošević (outside co-author).
Keywords: survey; ICS security; statistical detection; protocol analysis; evaluation methodology.
This book chapter surveys statistical and machine-learning approaches to anomaly detection in ICS environments, focusing on network-level traffic analysis rather than host-based or physical-process monitoring. The chapter covers the statistical properties of ICS traffic that distinguish it from enterprise IT traffic—determinism, periodicity, limited state space—and how these properties can be exploited by unsupervised methods. Covered algorithms include univariate control charts, multivariate Gaussian models, kernel density estimators, one-class SVMs, Isolation Forest, and autoencoders, with discussion of their assumptions, computational requirements, and suitability for embedded deployment. Protocol-specific considerations are provided for Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, and PROFINET. The chapter closes with a discussion of evaluation methodology challenges, including the scarcity of labelled datasets, the difficulty of representative attack injection, and the trade-off between false alarm rate and response latency. Representative results from the published literature are tabulated.

SYN-PUB-10478.title: Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison
SYN-PUB-10478.text:
Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Workshop on Industrial Communication Security (CEWICS)).
Authors: Tibor Farkas (outside co-author); Marek Novotný (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: OPC UA; encryption; traffic features; one-class SVM; security mode.
OPC UA supports three security modes—None, Sign, and SignAndEncrypt—and this paper evaluates how each mode affects the discriminability of traffic features used in unsupervised anomaly detectors. Experiments were conducted on a testbed comprising an OPC UA server, two client applications, and an embedded data historian. Seventeen traffic features extractable from unencrypted traffic were assessed for their availability under Sign and SignAndEncrypt modes using packet capture before and after the application layer. Under SignAndEncrypt, 11 of 17 features became unavailable or uninformative at the packet level; however, timing, packet length distribution, and session-level handshake frequency remained discriminative. A reduced 6-feature one-class SVM trained on these surviving features achieved a detection rate of 0.83 against four attack scenarios, compared with 0.91 for the full 17-feature detector on unencrypted traffic. The paper discusses the implications for passive inline monitoring architectures and proposes a broker-based decryption approach for trusted network segments.

SYN-PUB-10479.title: A Labelled Packet-Level Dataset of Modbus/TCP Attacks for Evaluating Anomaly Detectors
SYN-PUB-10479.text:
A Labelled Packet-Level Dataset of Modbus/TCP Attacks for Evaluating Anomaly Detectors (2020, journal, IEEE Access).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Ágnes Varga (outside co-author); Bojan Perić (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: dataset; Modbus/TCP; benchmark; labelled traffic; attack scenarios.
This paper describes the collection, annotation, and release of a packet-level Modbus/TCP dataset captured on the ICS testbed at the University of Novi Sad. The dataset spans 21 days of normal operation and 6 days of controlled attack execution, comprising approximately 310 million packets. Eight attack scenarios were implemented: function code scanning, coil mass-write injection, replay with modified values, man-in-the-middle payload substitution, time-synchronisation offset injection, denial-of-service flooding, slow-rate polling exhaustion, and firmware update spoofing. Each packet is labelled with a binary normal/attack flag and a scenario identifier. The paper documents the testbed topology, PLC configuration, traffic generation scripts, and labelling methodology in sufficient detail for reproduction. Baseline results for five detectors—statistical process control, one-class SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM-based reconstruction—are reported to enable direct comparison by future researchers. The dataset is hosted on the university repository.

SYN-PUB-10480.title: Threshold Calibration for ICS Anomaly Detectors Under Imbalanced Operating Conditions
SYN-PUB-10480.text:
Threshold Calibration for ICS Anomaly Detectors Under Imbalanced Operating Conditions (2021, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: threshold calibration; false positive rate; beta mixture model; detector evaluation; ICS.
Anomaly detectors for ICS traffic are typically calibrated by fixing the decision threshold to achieve a target false positive rate estimated on a clean training set. This paper investigates the miscalibration that results when the actual false positive rate at deployment differs from the target, and proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data. The procedure fits a two-component beta mixture model to the empirical score distribution and uses the mixture weight of the anomalous component as a proxy for the contamination fraction. Experiments on four detectors (OC-SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and kernel density estimator) across three ICS protocol datasets show that the calibration procedure reduces the gap between nominal and actual FPR from a mean of 3.1 percentage points to 0.4 percentage points. The paper also quantifies sensitivity to the choice of beta mixture initialisation and provides practical recommendations for operators setting alert thresholds.

SYN-PUB-10481.title: Federated One-Class Classification for Distributed ICS Sites Without Sharing Raw Traffic
SYN-PUB-10481.text:
Federated One-Class Classification for Distributed ICS Sites Without Sharing Raw Traffic (2022, journal, International Journal of Critical Infrastructure Protection).
Authors: Dávid Szabó (outside co-author); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Mirjana Stošić (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: federated learning; one-class classification; privacy; energy distribution; ensemble.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-10482.title: Comparing Score Aggregation Strategies for Multi-Protocol ICS Anomaly Detection
SYN-PUB-10482.text:
Comparing Score Aggregation Strategies for Multi-Protocol ICS Anomaly Detection (2024, journal, Computers and Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: score aggregation; multi-protocol; Dempster-Shafer; EtherNet/IP; detection pipeline.
Industrial sites often run several ICS protocols concurrently; a single anomaly may manifest in traffic from multiple protocols or only one. This paper compares six score aggregation strategies—maximum, mean, product, Dempster-Shafer combination, learned linear combination, and a voting threshold rule—for combining per-protocol anomaly scores from Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP detectors deployed simultaneously on the same network segment. A testbed with all three protocol stacks was operated for 45 days, and 18 multi-protocol and single-protocol attack scenarios were injected over a 10-day evaluation period. The learned linear combination, trained on a 5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination, achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.91) but required labelled data for weight estimation. The Dempster-Shafer rule achieved 0.88 without labelled data. The maximum rule performed consistently below 0.80. Results provide concrete guidance for operators designing multi-sensor detection pipelines.

SYN-PUB-10483.title: Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads
SYN-PUB-10483.text:
Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads (2026, journal, Journal of Industrial Network Security).
Authors: Jelena Kovačević (outside co-author); Péter Horváth (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008); Milutin Paunović (R1022).
Keywords: protocol-agnostic; byte-level features; proprietary protocols; one-class SVM; heterogeneous ICS.
Most ICS anomaly detectors are designed for a specific protocol and rely on parsed field values. This paper investigates a protocol-agnostic approach in which raw application-layer payload bytes from the first 64 bytes of each PDU are used to construct feature vectors via byte-frequency histograms augmented with bigram entropy and mean absolute deviation of byte values. A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures from a testbed running Modbus, DNP3, and a proprietary vendor protocol for which no parser was available. The proprietary protocol represented 31% of traffic. Against seven attack scenarios including vendor-protocol-specific command injection, the protocol-agnostic detectors achieved AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, compared with 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector applied only to Modbus traffic. The paper discusses cases where protocol-agnostic features are sufficient and where parsed fields remain necessary, providing a decision framework for practitioners deploying detectors on heterogeneous industrial networks.

SYN-PUB-10523.title: Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic
SYN-PUB-10523.text:
Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragan Kovač (outside co-author).
Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

SYN-PUB-10524.title: Threat modelling for smart building controllers
SYN-PUB-10524.text:
Threat modelling for smart building controllers (2022, conference, Conference on Applied Cybersecurity).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Luka Stanković (outside co-author).
Smart building automation systems increasingly integrate heterogeneous controllers managing heating, ventilation, access control, and fire suppression, all connected over IP-based networks. This convergence introduces significant attack surfaces that are rarely addressed through systematic security engineering. This paper applies a structured threat modelling methodology—adapted from STRIDE and augmented with ICS-specific threat categories—to a representative smart building controller architecture. The analysis identifies seventeen distinct threat scenarios spanning spoofing of sensor inputs, tampering with actuator commands, and denial-of-service against building management gateways. For each threat, the paper proposes corresponding mitigations including cryptographic command authentication, rate-limiting policies, and network segmentation strategies. A comparative evaluation against an unmitigated baseline system is conducted using a simulation environment, demonstrating measurable risk reduction across all identified threat categories. The findings offer actionable security guidance for building automation vendors and facility managers deploying next-generation smart infrastructure.

SYN-PUB-10525.title: A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks
SYN-PUB-10525.text:
A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks (2023, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics Security).
Authors: Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015); Nemanja Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: SCADA security; intrusion detection; industrial control systems; anomaly detection; network security.
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) networks form the backbone of critical infrastructure sectors including energy distribution, water treatment, and transportation. Protecting these networks from cyber intrusions requires detection systems capable of operating on highly specialised industrial protocols while maintaining low false-positive rates in continuous operation. This paper conducts a systematic comparative evaluation of five intrusion detection architectures—signature-based, specification-based, statistical anomaly, deep learning, and hybrid approaches—applied to a common SCADA testbed. Each architecture is assessed across four attack categories: reconnaissance, command injection, man-in-the-middle, and denial-of-service. Performance is measured in terms of detection accuracy, latency, resource consumption, and adaptability to concept drift. Results show that hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance, while purely deep-learning-based systems exhibit higher sensitivity to protocol version variability. The paper concludes with a decision framework to guide practitioners in selecting appropriate detection strategies based on operational constraints.

SYN-PUB-10526.title: Federated learning for distributed intrusion detection across IoT edge nodes
SYN-PUB-10526.text:
Federated learning for distributed intrusion detection across IoT edge nodes (2023, journal, Computers & Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Rastko Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT security; federated learning; intrusion detection; edge computing; anomaly detection.
Internet of Things deployments in industrial and smart city environments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous network traffic across geographically distributed edge nodes. Centralising this data for intrusion detection raises significant privacy and bandwidth concerns, particularly in multi-stakeholder environments. This paper proposes a federated learning framework for distributed intrusion detection, wherein each edge node trains a local anomaly detection model on its own traffic and periodically shares only model gradient updates with a central aggregation server. The aggregated global model is then redistributed to participating nodes, enabling collective knowledge improvement without raw data exposure. The framework is evaluated on a purpose-built IoT testbed consisting of twenty-four heterogeneous edge devices simulating smart metering, environmental sensing, and industrial actuation scenarios. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves detection accuracy within 3% of a centralised baseline while reducing data transmission overhead by over 80%. The paper also investigates the robustness of the framework against poisoning attacks introduced by compromised edge nodes.

SYN-PUB-10527.title: Threat modelling in IIoT supply chains: identifying lateral movement pathways
SYN-PUB-10527.text:
Threat modelling in IIoT supply chains: identifying lateral movement pathways (2022, journal, Journal of Cybersecurity and Privacy).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Bojana Vuković (outside co-author); Luka Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: threat modelling; IIoT; supply chain security; lateral movement; industrial control systems.
Industrial Internet of Things supply chains encompass multiple layers of hardware vendors, firmware providers, system integrators, and end operators, each introducing potential vulnerabilities that adversaries may exploit for lateral movement across organisational boundaries. This paper presents a threat modelling methodology tailored to IIoT supply chain architectures, extending traditional STRIDE analysis with supply-chain-specific threat categories including firmware substitution, third-party library poisoning, and vendor credential reuse. A reference IIoT architecture involving a six-tier supply chain is modelled, and attack graphs are constructed to identify the most probable lateral movement pathways between tiers. Quantitative risk scores are assigned using a modified CVSS-based scoring system adapted for operational technology contexts. The analysis reveals that firmware update channels and remote maintenance interfaces constitute the highest-risk lateral movement vectors. Mitigation recommendations include cryptographic firmware signing, role-based access segmentation across supply chain tiers, and continuous behavioural monitoring of maintenance sessions. The framework is validated through a tabletop exercise with industrial practitioners.

SYN-PUB-10528.title: Network segmentation strategies for securing legacy OT environments
SYN-PUB-10528.text:
Network segmentation strategies for securing legacy OT environments (2021, conference, International Conference on Industrial Cybersecurity (ICICS 2021)).
Authors: Dragan Kovač (outside co-author); Ivana Jovanović (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015).
Keywords: network segmentation; OT security; industrial control systems; network security; legacy systems.
Operational technology environments in manufacturing and utility sectors frequently rely on decades-old equipment designed without cybersecurity considerations. Retrofitting strong security controls onto such systems is often impractical, making network segmentation one of the most effective available defences. This paper systematically evaluates five segmentation strategies—air-gapping, DMZ insertion, unidirectional gateways, micro-segmentation using software-defined networking, and VLAN-based isolation—across three representative legacy OT environments modelled after real-world process control architectures. Each strategy is assessed against a standardised threat catalogue derived from known ICS incident reports, covering scenarios such as ransomware propagation, historian server compromise, and remote access exploitation. The evaluation employs a simulation-driven methodology combining network topology modelling with attack path analysis. Results indicate that micro-segmentation combined with unidirectional gateways at critical zone boundaries provides the highest resilience against multi-stage attacks, though at significant configuration complexity. The paper provides a practical scoring matrix to assist security engineers in selecting segmentation approaches based on available resources and operational constraints.

SYN-PUB-10529.title: Detecting replay attacks on DNP3 protocol in smart grid communications
SYN-PUB-10529.text:
Detecting replay attacks on DNP3 protocol in smart grid communications (2020, conference, Workshop on Security of Cyber-Physical Systems (SCPS 2020)).
Authors: Nemanja Filipović (outside co-author); Stefan Lazić (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015).
Keywords: DNP3; replay attacks; smart grid; intrusion detection; network security.
DNP3 is a widely deployed communication protocol in smart grid environments, facilitating data exchange between substations, remote terminal units, and control centres. Despite extensions introduced in DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5, many deployments remain vulnerable to replay attacks due to misconfiguration or the use of older protocol variants. This paper presents a lightweight detection mechanism for DNP3 replay attacks based on temporal sequence analysis of application-layer message fields. The proposed detector monitors request-response timing patterns, sequence counter consistency, and message fragment ordering to identify anomalous retransmission behaviour indicative of replay activity. The mechanism is implemented as a passive network probe requiring no modifications to existing field devices. Evaluation on a hardware-in-the-loop smart grid testbed shows that the detector correctly identifies replay attacks with 97.3% precision and 95.8% recall, while maintaining a processing latency below 12 milliseconds per packet—well within operational requirements. The paper further discusses integration of the detector into existing security information and event management pipelines used in utility control centres.

SYN-PUB-10530.title: Cybersecurity frameworks for critical infrastructure protection: a survey and gap analysis
SYN-PUB-10530.text:
Cybersecurity frameworks for critical infrastructure protection: a survey and gap analysis (2021, journal, ACM Computing Surveys).
Authors: Ana Petrović (outside co-author); Vuk Đukić (R1015); Marija Đorđević (outside co-author); Luka Stanković (outside co-author).
Keywords: cybersecurity frameworks; critical infrastructure; ICS security; IoT security; threat modelling.
Critical infrastructure sectors—including energy, water, transportation, and telecommunications—face an evolving and increasingly sophisticated threat landscape. Numerous cybersecurity frameworks have been developed to guide operators in assessing and improving their security posture, including NIST CSF, IEC 62443, NERC CIP, and ISA/IEC standards. Despite their widespread adoption, significant gaps remain in how these frameworks address emerging challenges such as cloud-connected OT environments, AI-driven attacks, and supply chain interdependencies. This survey systematically reviews twelve major cybersecurity frameworks applicable to critical infrastructure, evaluating them across dimensions of scope, implementation guidance, assessment methodology, and adaptability to ICS-specific threats. A structured gap analysis reveals that most frameworks inadequately address real-time anomaly detection requirements, provide insufficient guidance on IoT integration, and lack concrete metrics for evaluating detection and response effectiveness. The paper proposes a consolidated gap taxonomy and outlines a research agenda addressing the most critical deficiencies. It is intended as a reference for both practitioners implementing security programmes and researchers developing next-generation framework components.

SYN-PUB-10531.title: Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models
SYN-PUB-10531.text:
Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models (2024, journal, IEEE Internet of Things Journal).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Rastko Mirković (outside co-author).
Keywords: IoT security; intrusion detection; recurrent neural networks; resource-constrained devices; anomaly detection.
Deploying intrusion detection directly on resource-constrained IoT devices such as microcontroller-based sensors and actuators presents fundamental challenges in terms of memory footprint, computational overhead, and energy consumption. This paper investigates the feasibility of implementing lightweight recurrent neural network models—specifically truncated LSTM and GRU variants—on devices with fewer than 256 KB of RAM. A model compression pipeline is developed that combines quantisation, pruning, and knowledge distillation to reduce model size by up to 94% relative to full-precision baselines, while preserving detection accuracy above 90% across standard IoT attack benchmarks. The compressed models are deployed on three representative IoT platforms and evaluated under realistic workload conditions. Power consumption measurements indicate that continuous on-device inference adds less than 4 mW overhead, making deployment feasible even on battery-powered nodes. The paper also proposes an adaptive inference strategy that dynamically reduces model complexity during high-load periods to prevent resource exhaustion. Results suggest that on-device intrusion detection is practically achievable for a broad class of constrained IoT deployments.

SYN-PUB-10561.title: Evaluating Windowing Semantics for Multi-Source Sensor Fusion in Industrial Monitoring Applications
SYN-PUB-10561.text:
Evaluating Windowing Semantics for Multi-Source Sensor Fusion in Industrial Monitoring Applications (2012, conference, Proceedings of the International Workshop on Real-Time Data Streams (RTDS)).
Authors: Anita Vojvodić (outside co-author); Balázs Fekete (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: windowing; sensor fusion; watermarks; clock skew; event-time semantics.
Sensor fusion across heterogeneous measurement sources requires careful alignment of time windows when source clocks differ or data arrives out of order. We compared tumbling, sliding, and session window semantics in a controlled testbed scenario representing an industrial temperature and vibration monitoring use case. Data from 12 simulated sensors was ingested at rates between 200 and 4 000 events per second per source, with artificially introduced clock skew ranging from 50 ms to 2 s. We measured join completeness, duplicate rate, and end-to-end latency for each windowing strategy across three watermark delay configurations. Session windows with adaptive watermarks achieved the highest join completeness (97.4%) at 500 ms skew but degraded sharply beyond 1 s. Sliding windows offered more predictable latency at the cost of a 12–18% duplicate rate before deduplication. The paper provides guidance on watermark delay selection as a function of observed skew variance in deployment environments.

SYN-PUB-10563.title: Operator Placement in Heterogeneous Cloud-Edge Stream Processing Topologies
SYN-PUB-10563.text:
Operator Placement in Heterogeneous Cloud-Edge Stream Processing Topologies (2016, journal, Journal of Cloud and Edge Computing Systems).
Authors: Dragana Petković (outside co-author); Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author); Anita Vojvodić (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: operator placement; edge computing; cloud-edge continuum; topology optimisation; stream graph.
When stream processing graphs span both edge devices and cloud nodes, operator placement decisions affect both latency and network cost. We modelled the placement problem as a variant of the weighted minimum-cut problem on a directed acyclic operator graph annotated with data rate estimates, processing cost per node type, and inter-node bandwidth. A greedy heuristic and an integer programming formulation were compared against a random baseline on 120 synthetically generated topologies of 10 to 80 operators each. The cloud-edge testbed comprised four Raspberry Pi 4 devices acting as edge nodes and eight virtual machines on a commercial cloud provider. The greedy heuristic reached within 11% of the integer programming optimum on average while running three orders of magnitude faster, making it suitable for online re-planning. End-to-end latency improvements of 34% over the random baseline were observed in the median case, with network egress cost reductions of up to 41%.

SYN-PUB-10565.title: Incremental Materialisation of Join Results Under Schema Evolution in Long-Running Stream Pipelines
SYN-PUB-10565.text:
Incremental Materialisation of Join Results Under Schema Evolution in Long-Running Stream Pipelines (2018, journal, Data Engineering and Management).
Authors: Predrag Nedić (R1020); Miroslav Tošić (outside co-author).
Keywords: schema evolution; state materialisation; pipeline maintenance; Flink; stream joins.
Long-running stream pipelines in production environments routinely encounter upstream schema changes—new fields, renamed attributes, or type modifications—that can invalidate materialised join state. We characterised four schema evolution patterns observed in three production deployments and proposed an incremental materialisation strategy that classifies changes as backward-compatible or breaking, applying partial re-materialisation only to affected state partitions. The strategy was implemented as a pluggable component for a Flink-based pipeline framework. Experiments used synthetic workloads with injected schema changes at 30-minute intervals over six-hour runs. For backward-compatible changes, the proposed approach completed state migration with zero pipeline restarts and a transient throughput reduction under 8%. For breaking changes, the approach reduced re-materialisation time by 53% compared with full-state recomputation by exploiting unchanged partitions. Correctness was verified by replaying historical event logs against the updated schema and comparing output checksums.

SYN-PUB-10566.title: Latency-Aware Scheduling of Stateful Operators on Kubernetes-Managed Stream Processing Clusters
SYN-PUB-10566.text:
Latency-Aware Scheduling of Stateful Operators on Kubernetes-Managed Stream Processing Clusters (2019, conference, Proceedings of the European Symposium on Cloud and Container Systems (ESCC)).
Authors: Dragana Petković (outside co-author); Václav Horák (outside co-author); Teodora Stanojević (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: Kubernetes; stateful operators; scheduling jitter; container orchestration; latency.
Container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes introduce variable scheduling delays that affect the latency guarantees of stateful stream processing operators. We instrumented a Flink cluster deployed on a 12-node Kubernetes cluster to measure pod scheduling jitter, network policy enforcement overhead, and storage volume attach latency across three Kubernetes versions and two container runtimes. Scheduling jitter reached up to 340 ms at the 99th percentile under concurrent pod churn, causing stateful operator timeouts in 2.1% of observed window completions. We propose a latency-aware scheduler extension that reserves priority scheduling slots for stateful operators and pre-warms persistent volume claims. The extension reduced operator timeout rate to 0.07% and improved end-to-end 95th-percentile latency by 28% across all tested workloads without increasing infrastructure cost measurably. Configuration recommendations derived from the experiments are provided for practitioners.

SYN-PUB-10567.title: Reconciling Conflicting Records from Heterogeneous Industrial Databases in Near-Real-Time
SYN-PUB-10567.text:
Reconciling Conflicting Records from Heterogeneous Industrial Databases in Near-Real-Time (2020, journal, Journal of Industrial Data Integration).
Authors: Sorin Moldovan (outside co-author); Anita Vojvodić (outside co-author); Nemanja Grujić (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: data reconciliation; entity resolution; change data capture; industrial databases; near-real-time.
Industrial environments often run multiple transactional databases that record overlapping facts about the same physical entities—machines, batches, or shipments—with differing update frequencies and inconsistent identifiers. We designed a reconciliation pipeline that ingests change-data-capture streams from three source databases simultaneously, performs entity resolution using a deterministic blocking scheme followed by probabilistic field matching, and produces a unified view updated with a median lag of 1.4 seconds. The system was evaluated on a dataset derived from a manufacturing scenario comprising approximately 2.1 million entity records and 11 months of change history, replayed at 5× real-time speed. Precision of entity matching reached 94.7% and recall 91.2% at a threshold tuned to minimise false merges. The pipeline processed peaks of 22 000 change events per second on a four-node cluster. We report failure modes under network partition between source systems and describe recovery procedures.

SYN-PUB-10568.title: Cost Modelling for Autoscaling Stateful Stream Processing Jobs in Public Cloud Environments
SYN-PUB-10568.text:
Cost Modelling for Autoscaling Stateful Stream Processing Jobs in Public Cloud Environments (2021, conference, ACM Symposium on Cloud Data Management (SCDM)).
Authors: Lena Wöhrstein (outside co-author); Teodora Stanojević (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: autoscaling; cost modelling; stateful streaming; cloud billing; predictive scaling.
Autoscaling stateful stream jobs in public clouds is complicated by the cost of state migration during scale-out and the billing granularity of cloud instances. We built a cost model that accounts for instance-hour billing boundaries, state migration data transfer fees, and throughput-dependent SLA penalty costs, then evaluated three autoscaling policies—reactive threshold, predictive using a seasonal ARIMA model of input rate, and a model-predictive controller—on workloads derived from two months of real anonymised clickstream data from a web analytics context. Experiments were run on a major European cloud provider using spot and on-demand instance mixes. The predictive policy reduced total cost by 19% compared with reactive threshold autoscaling while maintaining SLA compliance above 99.1%. The cost model's predictions deviated from actual bills by less than 4% in 90% of 15-minute billing windows tested. We discuss edge cases where spot interruptions invalidate predictions.

SYN-PUB-10569.title: Skew-Resilient Parallel Hash Joins for Real-Time Financial Transaction Matching
SYN-PUB-10569.text:
Skew-Resilient Parallel Hash Joins for Real-Time Financial Transaction Matching (2024, conference, Proceedings of the International Conference on Data Engineering and Applications (IDEA)).
Authors: Teodora Stanojević (outside co-author); Lena Wöhrstein (outside co-author); Predrag Nedić (R1020).
Keywords: key skew; parallel hash join; Count-Min Sketch; transaction matching; load balancing.
Key skew in financial transaction streams—where a small fraction of merchant or account identifiers account for a large fraction of events—causes severe load imbalance in standard parallel hash join implementations. We characterised key-frequency distributions in two anonymised transaction datasets totalling 8.3 billion records and found that the top 0.1% of keys accounted for 34–41% of events. We implemented three skew-handling strategies within a Flink pipeline: key splitting with partial aggregation, heavy-hitter replication, and a hybrid that switches strategy per key at runtime based on observed frequency estimates maintained with a Count-Min Sketch. The hybrid approach achieved the most consistent performance, reducing maximum task throughput imbalance from 7.3× to 1.4× under peak skew, with end-to-end matching latency at the 95th percentile improving by 46% compared with the baseline hash join. Memory overhead of the Count-Min Sketch was under 8 MB per task at the tested error bounds.

SYN-PUB-10581.title: Static Detection of Data Races in Interrupt-Driven C Firmware Using Lock-Set Analysis
SYN-PUB-10581.text:
Static Detection of Data Races in Interrupt-Driven C Firmware Using Lock-Set Analysis (2011, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Microelectronics).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Šešlija (outside co-author).
Keywords: data race detection; lock-set analysis; interrupt-driven firmware; static analysis; GCC plugin.
Interrupt-driven firmware written in C is prone to data races that are difficult to expose through testing because race conditions depend on precise interrupt timing. This paper adapts the classical lock-set algorithm to the interrupt-preemption model used in bare-metal microcontroller firmware, where mutual exclusion is typically enforced by disabling specific interrupt vectors rather than by acquiring locks. The analysis is implemented as a GCC plugin and evaluated on six open-source firmware projects ranging from 8 kB to 120 kB of source code. The tool identified 47 confirmed race conditions, of which 38 had been previously unknown to project maintainers. False-positive rate was 12% on average. The analysis completes in under four seconds for all evaluated projects on a standard workstation. Results suggest that interrupt-vector-aware lock-set analysis is practical for integration into continuous build pipelines for embedded projects, and the paper discusses configuration options that trade precision for analysis speed.

SYN-PUB-10582.title: Bounding Interrupt Latency in Deeply Nested ISR Hierarchies: A Worst-Case Execution Time Study
SYN-PUB-10582.text:
Bounding Interrupt Latency in Deeply Nested ISR Hierarchies: A Worst-Case Execution Time Study (2013, conference, Proceedings of the Central European Symposium on Embedded Real-Time Systems (CESERTS)).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Zoran Jovanović (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author).
Keywords: WCET; interrupt latency; nested interrupts; Cortex-M; timing analysis.
Nested interrupt service routines create complex preemption chains that make worst-case execution time (WCET) analysis substantially harder than in flat single-ISR models. This study examines four industrial-grade microcontroller families—two ARM Cortex-M3 parts and two legacy 8-bit AVR parts—and develops a graph-based preemption-chain enumeration method to bound the maximum latency experienced by the highest-priority interrupt. Timing measurements are collected using hardware cycle counters and compared against analytically derived upper bounds. Across 12 firmware configurations the analytical bound exceeded the measured maximum by no more than 9%, validating the tightness of the model. The paper also quantifies how enabling interrupt tail-chaining on Cortex-M3 hardware reduces the overhead of context switching and therefore narrows the gap between the analytical bound and measurement. Practical guidance is provided for firmware engineers selecting interrupt priority assignments.

SYN-PUB-10583.title: Applying SPIN Model Checking to Verify Mutual Exclusion in Bare-Metal RTOS Kernels
SYN-PUB-10583.text:
Applying SPIN Model Checking to Verify Mutual Exclusion in Bare-Metal RTOS Kernels (2014, conference, International Workshop on Formal Techniques for Embedded and Real-Time Systems (FTERS)).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Aleksandar Tešić (outside co-author); Lucie Bernardová (outside co-author).
Keywords: SPIN; Promela; model checking; RTOS; mutual exclusion; bare-metal.
Small real-time operating system kernels for microcontrollers commonly implement mutual exclusion through inline assembler critical sections rather than through portable primitives, making formal reasoning non-trivial. This paper describes a methodology for extracting a Promela model from a bare-metal RTOS kernel written in C, using a combination of manual abstraction and a purpose-built C-to-Promela translator for common critical-section idioms. The approach is applied to two open-source RTOS kernels with kernel sizes of roughly 2,000 and 5,400 lines of C respectively. SPIN verification reveals three previously undetected scenarios in which mutual exclusion can be violated under specific task activation sequences. The paper reports verification times, state-space sizes, and the impact of partial-order reduction. Verified configurations reached up to 18 million states within a 16 GB memory bound. The methodology requires approximately two person-days of manual model preparation per kernel.

SYN-PUB-10584.title: Refactoring Strategies for Safety-Relevant Legacy Firmware: A Catalogue and Case Study
SYN-PUB-10584.text:
Refactoring Strategies for Safety-Relevant Legacy Firmware: A Catalogue and Case Study (2015, book chapter, Advances in Embedded Software Quality Assurance (edited volume, Springer-Verlag imprint)).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Nataša Kovačević (outside co-author); Peter Wimmer (outside co-author).
Keywords: refactoring; legacy firmware; MISRA-C; safety-critical; static analysis.
Legacy firmware in safety-relevant products is often written in C dialects that predate modern safety standards such as MISRA-C:2012. Applying refactoring in this context requires care to preserve timing and memory behaviour as well as functional correctness. This book chapter presents a catalogue of 21 refactoring patterns derived from analysis of four industrial firmware codebases, each between 30 kB and 200 kB of C source. The patterns are grouped into three categories: eliminating undefined behaviour, introducing testability through dependency injection, and separating platform-specific code from application logic. For each pattern the chapter states preconditions, the transformation steps, and the classes of static analysis warnings it eliminates. A worked case study traces the full refactoring of a 47 kB motor-controller firmware through 14 applied patterns, documenting before-and-after metrics including cyclomatic complexity, MISRA-C violation count, and unit-test coverage. The chapter concludes with a discussion of risks specific to refactoring under real-time constraints.

SYN-PUB-10585.title: Formal Modelling of the Cortex-M NVIC Priority Scheme for Verification of Priority-Inversion Freedom
SYN-PUB-10585.text:
Formal Modelling of the Cortex-M NVIC Priority Scheme for Verification of Priority-Inversion Freedom (2017, journal, Microprocessors and Microsystems — Embedded Hardware Design).
Authors: Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Milutin Paunović (R1022); Marko Dimitrijević (outside co-author).
Keywords: NVIC; Cortex-M; priority inversion; Promela; LTL; SPIN.
Priority inversion in interrupt-driven firmware causes higher-priority interrupt handlers to be delayed by lower-priority activity for indeterminate periods, a potentially catastrophic condition in safety systems. The ARM Cortex-M Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller implements a priority scheme with configurable preemption and sub-priority bits whose interaction is subtle enough to cause inadvertent priority inversion during configuration changes. This paper presents a formal model of the NVIC priority resolution logic in Promela, parameterised over the number of active interrupt vectors and the width of the priority register. The model is verified with SPIN against a priority-inversion-freedom property expressed in linear temporal logic. Exhaustive verification for configurations with up to eight active vectors completes within practical time and memory limits. The model is used to identify three NVIC configuration patterns that violate priority-inversion freedom under specific pending-interrupt sequences. Corrections for each pattern are proposed and re-verified.

SYN-PUB-10586.title: A Comparative Study of Model Checkers for Real-Time Embedded Firmware Verification
SYN-PUB-10586.text:
A Comparative Study of Model Checkers for Real-Time Embedded Firmware Verification (2020, journal, Journal of Systems Architecture).
Authors: Aleksandar Tešić (outside co-author); Milutin Paunović (R1022); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author); Bojan Stojčić (outside co-author).
Keywords: model checking; SPIN; UPPAAL; firmware verification; comparative study.
Several mature model checkers are available for verifying concurrent systems, including SPIN, UPPAAL, NuSMV, and mCRL2. Their relative strengths for firmware verification tasks are not well characterised in the literature. This paper conducts a structured comparison across four verification tasks derived from real firmware defects: mutual exclusion correctness, absence of deadline misses, bounded response time for interrupt handlers, and absence of deadlock in cooperative scheduling. Each task is encoded in the input language of each tool by experienced users following documented modelling guidelines. The comparison measures verification time, peak memory consumption, expressiveness of the property language for each task, and the effort required to construct the model. UPPAAL outperforms alternatives on timed-automata tasks at the cost of requiring explicit clock modelling. SPIN handles untimed reachability tasks most efficiently. The paper provides a decision-support table to guide tool selection and highlights gaps where none of the tested tools performs adequately without significant manual state-space abstraction.

SYN-PUB-10587.title: Trace-Based Concurrency Testing for Microcontroller Firmware Using Instrumented Execution on QEMU
SYN-PUB-10587.text:
Trace-Based Concurrency Testing for Microcontroller Firmware Using Instrumented Execution on QEMU (2021, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Ivan Rajković (outside co-author); Marko Dimitrijević (outside co-author).
Keywords: concurrency testing; QEMU; instrumented execution; firmware bugs; scheduling injection.
(no abstract)

SYN-PUB-10588.title: Modular Verification of Firmware Components Using Assume-Guarantee Reasoning in SPIN
SYN-PUB-10588.text:
Modular Verification of Firmware Components Using Assume-Guarantee Reasoning in SPIN (2023, journal, Formal Methods in System Design).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Lucie Bernardová (outside co-author); Sonja Lukić (outside co-author).
Keywords: assume-guarantee; compositional verification; SPIN; Promela; state explosion; firmware.
Full-state-space verification of complete firmware images quickly becomes intractable due to state explosion. Assume-guarantee (A-G) reasoning decomposes a verification problem into per-component proofs that communicate through assumptions about the behaviour of the environment. This paper adapts the circular A-G rule to firmware components modelled in Promela, where the environment consists of hardware peripheral behaviour and other interrupt handlers. Assumptions are expressed as deterministic finite automata over sequences of shared-variable accesses. The methodology is demonstrated on a 14-component CAN-bus firmware stack. Full monolithic verification of the stack requires more than 32 GB of memory and does not terminate within 12 hours. The compositional approach verifies all 14 components within 2 hours and 6 GB combined memory, finding the same two genuine property violations as a targeted partial search. Challenges in constructing adequate assumptions without excessive manual effort are discussed, along with a heuristic for bootstrapping assumption candidates from execution traces.

SYN-PUB-10589.title: Characterising Refactoring Risk in Safety-Relevant Firmware Through Mutation Testing
SYN-PUB-10589.text:
Characterising Refactoring Risk in Safety-Relevant Firmware Through Mutation Testing (2024, journal, Empirical Software Engineering).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Bojan Stojčić (outside co-author); Renata Pflüger (outside co-author); Milena Đurđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: mutation testing; refactoring; firmware; test adequacy; interrupt handling; safety-critical.
Before refactoring safety-relevant firmware, practitioners need confidence that their test suite is sensitive enough to detect regressions introduced by the transformation. Mutation testing provides a systematic way to measure this sensitivity, but applying standard mutation operators to embedded C firmware raises practical difficulties: compilation and execution on actual hardware is slow, and coverage of interrupt-handling paths is poor under host-machine simulation. This paper proposes a firmware-specific mutation operator set of 19 operators targeting interrupt-enable/disable idioms, volatile qualifiers, bitfield manipulation, and register-mapped I/O accesses, and evaluates it on three refactoring subjects using QEMU-accelerated execution. Mutation scores before and after refactoring are compared for 12 refactoring transactions applied to 63 kB of safety-relevant motor control firmware. Results show that standard mutation operators yield mutation scores between 31% and 47% on interrupt-handling code, while the firmware-specific operators raise scores to between 61% and 78% for the same code paths. The paper argues for including firmware-specific operators in pre-refactoring test adequacy assessments.

SYN-PUB-10590.title: Incremental Model Extraction for Continuous Formal Verification of Evolving Embedded Firmware
SYN-PUB-10590.text:
Incremental Model Extraction for Continuous Formal Verification of Evolving Embedded Firmware (2026, journal, ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Ivan Rajković (outside co-author); Milena Đurđević (outside co-author); Tibor Farkaš (outside co-author).
Keywords: incremental verification; continuous integration; Promela extraction; firmware; model checking.
Formal verification of embedded firmware is typically performed as a one-off activity at a fixed project milestone rather than continuously throughout development. This paper presents an approach for incremental Promela model extraction integrated into a firmware build system, so that a reduced model capturing the changed components is re-extracted and re-verified on each commit. The extraction tool monitors which source files changed, re-extracts Promela processes only for affected interrupt handlers and shared-data regions, and replaces unchanged processes with previously verified stubs. The incremental approach is evaluated on a 22-module sensor-gateway firmware developed over 18 months, with verification triggered on 1,147 commits. Average verification time per commit is 38 seconds, compared to 94 minutes for full re-verification. Three property violations introduced during development were detected within the same day they were committed. The paper discusses conditions under which incremental re-use of stubs is sound and describes the fallback to full verification when structural changes affect the composition of modules.

W3005806384.title: The use of personal weather station observations to improve precipitation estimation and interpolation
W3005806384.text: Hydrology and earth system sciences, 2021. Abstract. The number of personal weather stations (PWS) with data available online through the internet is increasing gradually in many parts of the world. The purpose of this study is to investigate the applicability of these data for the spatial interpolation of precipitation for high intensity events of different durations. Due to unknown errors and biases of the observations rainfall amounts of the PWS network are not considered directly. Instead, only their temporal order is assumed to be correct. The crucial step is to find the stations with informative measurements. This is done in two steps, first by selecting the locations using time series of indicators of high precipitation amounts. The remaining stations are checked whether they fit into the spatial pattern of the other stations. Thus, it is assumed that the percentiles of the PWS network are accurate. These percentiles are then translated to precipitation amounts using the distribution functions which were interpolated using the information from German National Weather Service (DWD) data only. The suggested procedure was tested for the State of Baden-Württemberg in Germany. A detailed cross validation of the interpolation was carried out for aggregated precipitation amounts of 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 hours. For each aggregation nearly 200 intense events were evaluated. …

W3171699581.title: An Adaptive Cognitive Sensor Node for ECG Monitoring in the Internet of Medical Things
W3171699581.text: IEEE Access, 2021. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) paradigm is becoming mainstream in multiple clinical trials and healthcare procedures. Cardiovascular diseases monitoring, usually involving electrocardiogram (ECG) traces analysis, is one of the most promising and high-impact applications.
